title: Echo "was" a good brand years ago....just not anymore. Only buy if you are handy with parts and have spare cash!
text: The 5-year warranty and success of the brand for a 15-year old trimmer that just wouldn't die was enough for me to buy the Echo BP500T backpack blower. Unfortunately, like many other reviews mention, these newer blowers go downhill in a hurry. I bought my first one at H.D. as their "biggest and best" backpack blower on the shelf at the time, used it for 1 1/2 years, then the issues started. It started, but wouldn't run at full throttle, and you had to play with the choke just to keep it going at all. Took it back and exchanged it for an identical model which they still carried. Another 1 1/2 years pass okay, but then the same issues started occurred again. Same throttle issues, but this time you had to pull the chain at least 10-20 just to get some life out of it. I followed all of the troubleshooting methods you can find online. All say about the same thing. "They run good until they don't....then you have to replace the carburetor." What? New carburetor at 1 1/2 years? Took it back to H.D. to exchange again, only to find that they no longer actually exchange it on the spot. You had to send in the blower (which was a 3-week turn around time in off-season....but that's a different issue with HD) and wait to hear if the repairs were covered by warranty or not. I helped out the clerk by telling him I thought it was the carburetor based on what I was experiencing and all the online posts on the issue. The clerk helped me out by saying that carburetors aren't covered under the Echo 5-year warranty and it would cost at least $130 to get it repaired through HD. Needless to say, I didn't bother sending it out for 3-weeks for a part that costs $35 online and is relatively simple to change out myself. Considering that this Echo blower has very few parts, why one of the major parts isn't covered in the warranty, or why the exclusions aren't notably called out on the box, is beyond comprehension. There should be big disclaimer in stores like H.D. about stuff like this if they want to keep any semblance of a good reputation.

I had the opportunity to Test and Buy VitaFiber Basic Syrup. I will explain in detail why I gave them 1 Star "at this time." I will also provide Pros and Cons of this product along with some recipes for PROTEIN BARS, which is the reason I bought this in first place.

░░░░░First, WHAT IS THIS STUFF FOR░░░░░
❖ VitaFiber(tm) is a sweet natural fiber providing low calorie and soluble prebiotic fiber for human digestive health. VitaFiber(tm) is non-GMO, sugar-free and gluten-free. It's made with something called IMO, lots of info available on IMO study (someone on BB website gave a great description):
This is a moderately sweet carbohydrate that's special because it's largely "digestion-resistant," meaning that it functions as soluble fiber in your digestive tract. This greatly reduces both the caloric value and glycemic impact of things made with it relative to other ingredient selections.

Isomalto-oligosaccharides (IMOs) are also very useful because they have properties usually reserved for high-energy foods like sugar syrups and nut butters: they mix nicely when heated, and when cooled they "bind" extremely well, making things stick together. This makes them an absolutely ideal ingredient for a "low net carb" protein bar.

VitaFiberbis available as a syrup or powder on Amazon. On a dry basis, VitaFiber is greater than 90% soluble fiber. Based on published studies, the caloric value of VitaFiber is 1.5 kcal/g

░░░░░COST░░░░░
Well the company BioNeutra that makes VitaFiber is in Canada. On their website cost of 1kg is $14.00. I am pretty sure that is Canadian dollar which is around $17 us dollar. But the product is sold on Amazon for 1.2kg for $22.00. I think it's still expensive compare to other IMO products on Amazon. VitaFiber has a reputation for being the name brand so its famous.
I have ordered this stuff in past from China/other countries in past. Let me tell you, read the label to verify what's all in it. They all do same thing. It's made from same stuff. To me price in a big thing and it can be sold cheaper. I paid allot less from other manufactures on Amazon and even ordering from China with expensive shipping it was pretty reasonable price.

░░░░░CUSTOMER SERVICE ISSUE░░░░░
So one of my siblings ordered some of this stuff and I called the manufacture since the order had issue. The person that answered the call was not polite. She told me she cannot help me and I should call Amazon directly. She kept spinning the circle, I just told her have a good day and ended the call. I will give them NO STARS for their attitude when calling them. The product itself deserves 5 start. But not necessarily their brand. IMO itself was not available to consumers until recently, especially in the USA. Manufactures that make cookies and protein bar have had access for years, so my 5 Star will go to IMO only.

░░░░░PRO'S░░░░░
❖ This is how I make my Quest protein bars. I have provided some recipes below. Check in out
❖ Can be used for other things other than protein bars. There are lots of recipes out their already.
❖ Fiber - Good for Adults. IMO is essentially a fiber. I just wouldn't give a child under 10 yrs old too much of this stuff.

░░░░░CONS░░░░░
❖ Cost is way High, Almost not worth it, especially if I can buy Quest/Protein bars in Bulk on Amazon.

░░░░░BOTTOM-LINE░░░░░
I will buy IMO products, but not from this manufactory again. It's a really good product if you want to customize your protein bars/cookies/other sweets for healthy diet. If you know what's all going inside your food mix then it's allot safer to eat. I have provided some recipes for Protein bars and cookies below alone with some pictures. Hope this helps!

░░░░░RECIPES (These are not entirely mine. I customized them a little) ░░░░░

░░░░░Cookies░░░░░
*** Zero-Carb (Oreo) Protein Cookies Recipe from proteinpow - Picture below***

❖Ingredients for the cookies:
* 2 tbsp IMO syrup
* 4 tsps black onyx cocoa powder (I used onyx so my cookies would turn Oreo-like; if you don't care about this though, just use regular cocoa powder!)
* 2 tbsps of chocolate whey protein powder (could use vanilla too)

❖Ingredients for the Filling
* 1 big tbsp of mascarpone cheese (or quark or cream cheese)
* 1/8 - 1/4 cup of vanilla whey protein powder (depending on how thick you want your mix; I used 24g).

❖Directions
1. First, make your cookies by chucking all the above cookie ingredients in a bowl and mixing it up with a spoon until you get a soft dough that you can mold with your hands into `balls' (it's going to feel like play-dough!) If your dough is too sticky to allow you to do this, add a bit more cocoa powder to it until you get to the right consistency.
2. Shape 6-10 `balls' out of the mix (depending on how big you want your cookies) and, using your hands, flatten them and place them on a nonstick baking tray or a regular cookie tray lined with baking paper.
3. Bake at 200C (around 395 F) for no more than 6 minutes. Yes: NO MORE THAN SIX MINUTES. They often take 5 minutes to cook so please check them after five and if they're cooked through, take them out of the oven.
4. Make your filling by mixing all your filling ingredients together. If you want your mix to be creamier than mine was, feel free to use casein!
5. Fill the cookies with the filling and that's your cookie.

❖ Macros/Nutrition
* Per cookie, solo (out of the six I got from the mix above): 20kcals, 2g protein, 5g carbs (out of which 4.5g is fiber so net carbs 0.5), 0g fat.

* Per 2 cookie, to make a cookie sandwich with (out of the 3 I got from the mix above): 40kcals, 4g protein, 10g carbs (out of which 9g is fiber so net carbs 1) + the filling (which is 51kcals, 6g protein, 3g fat and 0 carbs per cookie): 91kcals, 10g protein, 10g carbs (out of which 9g is fiber so net carbs 1), and 6g fat.

░░░░░Protein Bars░░░░░
***Homemade Quest-Inspired Bars - Cookie Dough flavor from busybuthealthy***

❖Ingredients
* 2 Tbsp VitaFiber Syrup
* 1 scoop (30 grams or ¼ cup) whey protein, vanilla (I used Whey Gourmet Naturelle Vanilla)
* 2 tsp almond meal (just ground up almonds) 15 g (2 squares) no-sugar chocolate, chopped (I used Simply Lite No Sugar Added Milk Chocolate)

❖Directions
- For a firm bar:
1. Heat the 2 Tbsp of VitaFiber Syrup in a saucepan over medium heat. When its just starts to bubble, remove from heat and immediately add protein powder, almond meal.
2. Place mixture in a plastic bag and knead until it starts to cool down. It will form into a bar. I also sometimes had to make it in to a dough by using my hand + adding little water and then placing in non-sticky pan to refrigerate it.
3. Add in the chopped chocolate once its cooled a bit. Still might melt a little.

- For a softer bar:
1. In a small bowl, combine the VitaFiber syrup, whey protein, almond meal and chopped chocolate. Mixture will be slightly sticky to the touch.
2. From here, it can be stored in a plastic bag, or you could also bake it in a 350 degree F oven for 5 minutes, or microwave for 15-20 seconds, as you would to a regular Quest bar.

❖ Notes
* Nutrition (of a Quest bar Cookie Dough flavor) Calories: 210 Fat: 8 g Carbs: 21 g Fiber: 17 g Sugar 1 g Sodium: 290 mg Protein: 21 g

❖ Macros/Nutrition
* Serving size: Per bar (Cookie Dough flavor) Calories: 288 Fat: 10 g Saturated fat: 3.5 g Carbs: 33 g Sugar: 4 g Sodium: 131 mg Fiber: 27 g Protein: 22 g

***Graham cracker crust 9 Bars from BB user- Picture below***

❖Ingredients
* 22 tbsp IMO syrup or 330g
* 2 sheets of Graham Crackers
* 6 tbsps Nutella
* 6 scoops 30 grams Protein powder of your choice (I used Birthday Cake flavor here)

❖Directions
Heat the 22 Tbsp of VitaFiber Syrup in a saucepan over medium heat. When it's just starts to bubble, remove from heat and immediately add protein powder and other ingredients. Mix it all with wood spoon at first, then use hand to mix it more. I had to add a little water to make the mixing process little faster. You can also use coconut oil instead of water. Place it all in Non-sticky pan to refrigerate it, then cut in bars as seen in picture below.

❖ Macros/Nutrition
* 67g per bar

title: Good idea gone bad
text: At first when taking them off the roll they seem like other bags. One should be able to tell which is the top which opens, and which is the bottom. That is not the case! Part of the answer is that there is a perforated strip one can pull off at the top, and then begin to open it. But the plastic rips so easily that trying to open the bags up often creates holes. Next, the bottom of the bag is a gathering of all the plastic to a center point. Separating all the folds of a folded bag rarely opens it entirely to the bottom. And trying to achieve that often creates more holes.

title: Blocks light, helps with flickering sensation post-cataract surgery.
text:
Bought after reading reviews from others, agree, it was just what I needed post-cataract surgery. You are light sensitive after surgery, and this does the trick filtering light, but allowing you to see. In fact, slept in it for about a week, (bought some tape, too, at the time) even though doc said only need a shield for a day (the clear one they provided). Nurse said about 4 days, I went a week, just to make sure I didn't bonk my eye in my sleep.

Also, post-cataract surgery you can have a flickering sensation as your eye heals from the outer edge of your eye. As for my first eye a few weeks ago, that's mostly done with, but sometimes need still need it. At first, I just walked around with it half-taped on. Afterwards, just stuck it under my glasses while at home. Lol, look like a pirate space alien, but whatever. :)

The material around it (stretchy) is a nice addition. Can be removed to wash.

I even bought a second one for next surgery - just in case I need to look full-on alien at times. :)

title: Works perfectly without damaging button holes,
text:
I have used the this product for years with good results. If you forget and dry your favorite jeans on high and shrink them, this device will save your pants!
It is plastic so care has to be taken to not snap the plastic. Here is how to do it.
1) wet the waistband thoroughly, front and back, it should be fully wet throughout
2) attach device to button side of pants, do NOT over tighten, it does not have to be super tight
3) use the size adapters to get close to the waist size, you don't want to have to turn the green screw a long way
4) make sure the side opposite the screw is completely covered by the waistband, you want all the waistband to be stretched across the entire waistband
5) GENTLY tighten the green screw until all the slack is out of the waistband, hold for 20 seconds, the band will start to stretch
6) continue to use the screw to stretch the waistband GENTLY, if the screw is hard to turn, WAIT for 10 seconds.
7) if you have more than 8 turns on the screw threads showing, STOP and add an adapter rather than hyper extend the screw handle, yes you will have loosen what you have so far to use another short adapter
8) repeat to tighten, watch for a max of 8 turns and stop at your desired stretch point for the waistband
9) let the waistband dry completely! Leave the expander in until you want to use the pants. This will hold the stretch.
HTH

title: A Cool Idea
text:
I suffer from overheating at night where I come in contact with my pillow, which results in waking with a headache on the surface in contact with my pillow. This results in having to toss and turn all night. The idea of the pillow was to keep my head cool.

The pillow is cool when you first lay down (good). Over a period of half an hour it warms up quickly as it draws the heat from your head. Then it releases the heat back to you and I wake up at the same intervals as before having to turn the pillow over to get a cool surface again. (bad.)

Would I recommend this pillow to others? It is a comfortable pillow which holds its shape nicely, but if you suffer as I do, this pillow does not help and I do not recommend it for relief of overheating headaches.

Thumbs up for comfort. Thumbs down for cooling.

title: Great product and a good price
text:
I've only seen one other site that has these online cheaper, and by the time you add shipping, it's about the same.

If you've never had rations, then you need to consider taste. After all, this is something you might be eating a LOT of, if the need arises. I carry three days worth in my go-bag, another three days in my hunting bag, and I have another two cases in the pantry.

Taste: Each serving of 400 calories is a "brick" of cream-colored powder that resembles a really thick sugar cookie. The taste is almost the same as that as well. They have a semi-sweet flavor. They're dry, but they're supposed to be.. and the advertising is correct.. they don't leave you thirsty either. I'm not really sure how they accomplish that, but they do it nicely.

The taste is good and they do the job.

Keep in mind if you're purchasing these for survival or camping, a normal human adult at rest needs about 1200 calories in a day, so three bars are sufficient. Three bars won't "fill you up." You'll still FEEL hungry, but they do the job of providing your body everything it needs to remain healthy for an extended period of time. If you're like me, a man who is "working" in the woods, they say you'll need 2500-3000 calories per day if you're working all day doing something like splitting wood or extreme hiking. If that's what you're doing, then you can just double or triple your intake for those days. If you had to work outside from sunup to sundown, you'd need a whole pack of 9, but that still equates to about 3 dollars for a day's meal. Compare that to MRE's which are about $6 per meal, and it's still an awesome savings.

When we got these, we opened them up and tried them and I intentionally left the pack opened and placed it in a ziploc bag just to see how they'd last once opened. I've eaten the same pack over a month's time and they're still good and still do the job.

My wife even started taking them like a protein bar for breakfast on her workouts (so I had to buy more!).

So I bought this due to my getting a little older (fabulous 47)... I'm noticing some very sudden changes in my hair, in the fact that it just doesn't have the luster it used to... It seems to be dulling and even feels thinner (I have very baby fine hair to begin with)... I haven't noticed any hair loss and I want to keep it that way... I started taking Luscious 7 about a week ago and the very first dose I noticed a really warm sensation throughout my skin and scalp, I began feeling hot and flushed, skin turned red and I started itching a bit (symptoms began about 20 minutes of taking and lasted about 15 minutes)... Well being a nurse, I know that Niacin B3 may cause "niacin flush" if taken on an empty stomach (I was so excited to start taking them when it arrived at my door, I just took them before I realized I hadn't had lunch yet)... It is a harmless side effect but it is best that you not take on an empty stomach (as I did and i got the "niacin flush")... I haven't had another episode since I started taking with food...Just a little heads, so you don't freak out that something is wrong if you get "niacin flush"... Three major changes I've noticed since I started taking this supplement:
**My hair is more supple/softer/SHINY (I haven't changed my routine with daily hair rituals) but most of all, my ends feel stronger...
**My energy level is through the roof... I am not as fatigued after work/exercise as I would get before using... I didn't expect that at all...
**I feel less sore and achy after a long day at work or a good yoga session... I also feel more limber in my joints... Could it be that I have more energy, who knows??? I am definitely going to continue taking this as part of my oral supplements... If any changes (positive/negative) occur, I will update with that info... I am satisfied with the quick results I'm experiencing thus far and hope they continue... FINGERS CROSSED!!!

I went from getting worse to better, it still took a few weeks but I got there and it was tolerable with a week for me, your milage may vary but you'll like this for your office chair, tv chair, or even in the car but don't keep it there in the summer according to the instructions and other reviews.

It's weird squishy and kind of weird but fun to sit on without the cover, but I was worried about my cat eating it so I put the cover on anyways and then it doesn't squish around as much. I liked it better with no cover, but it still works great with it on.

The size is pretty big for this one but it will squish into a smaller chair if you get the wrong size or need to use around the house in different chairs. I even brought it to my sleep number bed to sit and watch tv during the first week.

Good quality, I'm a bigger guy and it's held up all summer great. I bring it in the car for longer trips. For regular driving I recommend Ergoseet (old or new model, if you can find them) because of the heat issue, but for temperature controlled areas this is the real deal.

title: A must have for kids!
text:
These protective knee, elbow, and wrist pads are a must for little ones! They are great quality and the wrist/palm guard is so important!

Likes
+ the hard wrist/palm guard is my favorite and not as common in these sets
+ nice size for my 3 and 4 year olds
+ adjustable to grow with the children
+ comfortable pads and straps
+ good protections from the hard plastic

Dislikes
- The only thing I can think of is that the white plastic is sure to get a bit dirty with some tumbles

These pads come in a mesh bag and seem to be a really great quality. The knee and elbow pads are a great size. They will fit my 3 and 4 year old pretty well now and give them plenty of room to grow with the adjustable velcro straps. The red stripe on the straps along with the black and white looks really nice. I LOVE the wrist/palm guards. Most of these protective sets that I've seen only include knee and elbow pads or they include just gloves. Palms are one of the first things to hit the pavement and these offer a lot of support for the wrist and protection for the palm. They also seem to offer enough flexibility and comfort.

title: Clean, nutritious, and flavorless (but that's a good thing!)
text: I eat a mostly vegetarian diet, so I bought this product to help boost my protein intake. I love that it's made from grass-fed dairy and includes oats for a huge punch of fiber with the protein. I'm also not a big fan of artificial sweeteners or other chemical additives, so the three ingredient list (whey, oat fiber and oat flour) is a major selling point for me. Because it doesn't have any added sweeteners, etc., it has a very bland taste. I think this is a good thing, because it's pretty much a blank canvas for you to add your own flavorings and sweeteners to it to create whatever kind of protein shake you want. I personally don't want to add too many extra calories when I drink this, so I just blend it with a cup of almond milk and a few ice cubes for thickness (No matter what you add to it, I definitely recommend using a blender and a couple of ice cubes to create a more drinkable texture). By itself, it's certainly palatable....tastes slightly oat-y, a touch chalky, and a little milky...not really much flavor, but not so terrible that it's undrinkable. Cheers to good health!

title: Medline Aluminum Forearm Crutches (B00083DFOW)
text:
I've tried several alternatives following a recent leg injury. A cane is too unstable to support much weight and full crutches are simply too cumbersome. These forearm crutches are the perfect solution. Indeed, a single one, used much like a cane, provides all the support I need. It provides more balance and stability than a cane, yet takes enough weight off my leg to eliminate pain while walking.

These crutches are well built. The frames are thick and highly polished. In fact, they truly look and feel far more like stainless steel than aluminum. On each crutch, the length from floor to hand grip is fully adjustable using a series of holes with spring loaded locking pins. The length above the grip to the forearm brace/cuff is adjustable in the same manner. Rotating locking nuts above and below the adjustable sections eliminate any noise during use, and provides an even more solid feel overall. There is no play in the hand grip, the forearm brace/cuff is well padded, and the rubber foot offers reliable traction.

I would prefer more padding on the handgrip, perhaps a softer rubber instead of hard vinyl. The handgrips are not really uncomfortable. Instead, it would be more accurate to say the handgrips are not as comfortable as they could be. However, there is little doubt these vinyl grips will last much longer than soft rubber ones.

Overall, I'm very satisfied with this purchase.

text:
Bought this shaver for the bald experiment. I didn't want to spend a lot on a shaver if I didn't like the look of bald.
After using a clipper to trim down hair amap…. I first tried dry shaving. That worked great but I found wetting the head and using barbasol works better for a closer shave and softer experience. The unit charges really fast and a charge lasts plenty long enough to buzz a head. I usually do two rounds of shaving which leaves the hair dam close to a blade shaver.
How does this compare to a Pit Bull Platinum? Since I liked the look the shaver gave I went ahead and ordered a more expensive unit for everyday use. I'll use the Vsmooth for travel and the pit bull at home. First the feel of the more expensive pit bull is much better as expected. The pro blades cut much easier. I still end up having to shave two rounds with barbasol to get the desired effect... all in all the results are pretty much the same but the shaving experience is much better with the pit bull. Not to mention other advanced features the pit bull offers. For the money tho… the Vsmooth is a solid unit providing a nice smooth shaved head for a fraction of the cost.

text: I'm always purchasing and receiving body wash as gifts, but I had been hesitant to use them without a bath shower pouf as I never feel completely clean just applying the soap with my hands.  My husband on the other hands, seems to prefer these method, despite my qualms.  I purchased this 2 pack of shower poufs to finally start to use up some of my supply of body wash, and to forgo purchasing the bars of soap I usually use.  So far, I've been super pleased with these poufs.  First, they are large, dense, and hardy feeling poufs.  I've purchased poufs from my local drugstores in the past, but they always feel kind of weak and not really "full".  What is nice about the size and density of these is that are good at creating a ton of soap foam with just a small amount of body wash (I usually use just about a tablespoon per shower), and their larger size makes them great at covering a lot of body surface area.  Second, these poufs are make of a good meshy material that is isn't too harsh on the skin, yet is able to effectively exfoliate my skin, so I always feel clean after every shower.  In fact, these poufs work so well, I've noticed an improvement in the skin on my arms and legs, which normally can become quite ashy and rough due to the colder winter weather.  I can attribute this improvement to the great exfoliation I am getting from using these poufs in the shower every day.  Overall, I feel these poufs are really well made, and will last me a long time without falling apart.  I highly recommend these to anyone looking for large and luxurious poufs in enhance the capabilities of their normal body washes. Disclaimer: I received this product for free or for a discount. All thoughts, ideas, and opinions are honest and my own, and I was NOT paid to leave a positive review.

title: You can have mine for free
text: Ignore any review that doesn't mention the taste of this product - in my opinion they must be "planted" reviews because anyone who has actually tasted this product would tell you about it's horrendous taste first and foremost. This stuff is absolutely the most vile concoction ever invented for human consumption. If I lost a pound a day (which I am not) I would not, physically could not, tolerate drinking this stuff more than the five times I already have - and each time it took me well over 10 minutes to drink four ounces - that's a half a cup people!! I don't believe a dehydrated starving person would drink this stuff after trying the first sip. I persevered that many times only because I spent $100 and didn't want to make my hubby mad for wasting so much money.  After five days I'm okay with him being mad about it. He can be mad for weeks, just don't make me drink any more PRUVIN!! I have managed five painful days of this stuff and tried mixing it with water and flavor drops, cranberry juice, orange juice and even grapefruit juice (hoping the acid and bitterness of grapefruit juice could mask the bitterness of the Pruvin, but I do not believe ANYTHING can mask the excessive sulphuric bitterness of this product.) The closest I can describe the taste is that of the pithe (the white part of the peel) of a lime or grapefruit that has been sprinkled heavily with some sort of industrial sulphur compound. People, I would love to tell you that this product works and maybe it does but I do not believe that anyone could actually tolerate the taste long enough to feel the benefits (they say it takes 2 months).  So those reviews that say they have? I don't believe them. It is my opinion that  those saying they have used it that long must be lying, or paid reviewers or must not have functional taste buds. I don't see how anyone could tolerate the taste long enough to find that out if it does what it claims to do. There certainly are no immediate effects except some sulphuric burps and an upset stomach along with revulsion. The science is based on Baylor research but from what little I could find about it on the Internet, it is not endorsed by those researchers. The only positive thing I have to say about this product is that the packaging is nice and fancy. However, in my opinion they should spend far less money on the box they send it to you in and more on developing a product that is palatable. How about a pill form if they can't make it taste decent?! I would rather give myself a shot every day to administer this stuff than drink it. It is THAT BAD. I have quite a bit left and I'd be happy to give it away for free, but I don't think I could find any takers. I hate being fat. I hate it a LOT, but I hate this product more.

title: Beautiful scale, but fluctuating readings.
text:
This product looks expensive and is great quality. I really like the digital reader and the design. However, this scale is inaccurate. I find that it fluctuates by the pound, not in increments of .2lbs. My husband and I were active, and are trying to get back into it. We have two scales; a basic white one where you have to step on it to activate it, and this one. When I step on the Mosiso scale, I get a reading. I step on the basic scale, and it is a pound higher. I get back on the Misiso scale, and it now matches the basic scale. I step on the basic scale and it still has the same reading. Then, I step on the Misiso scale, and I am now a pound lighter! I would understand if this is a fluke, but this pretty much happens every other time I step on the scales.

Now, maybe I am just crazy, but I do not like how much it fluctuates. My husband brought this to work because they were doing a weight loss challenge, and they experienced the same issue. I found that the scale has a "sweet spot". if you stand at the top edge of it, you get the most accurate reading, which is now .2lbs within the other scale. If not for the other scale to compare it to, I would have retired this scale a long time ago. But because I like comparing things like a crazy person (on top of weighing my food and counting calories), I am keeping the scale around.

title: Prepare to see a drop in total cholesterol, specifically triglycerides
text:
I absolutely hate taking pills, especially fish oil, because it's generally 2 pills/dose. Liquid form is definitely the best, and Carlson makes great tasting fish oil that is pleasant and does not leave a nasty fish aftertaste. The instructions say 1 tsp (or maybe tbsp)/dose, however, I would just recommend taking a swig and be done with it. Just remember you need a 2:1 ratio between inflammatory EFA to antiinflammatory EFA (omega 6 versus 3).

After drinking this for one month, you will see a MASSIVE drop in your cholesterol. If you take this with Konsyl (the only laxative that is safe for long term use), you will feel better. My triglycerides were a staggering 40 on the last labs that I had done. I was afraid I was going to have hypotrygliceridemia!

I personally have not tried the orange flavor. I recall reading someone mentioning the lemon flavor was better so I purchased it. I do like it and don't find the taste to be unappetizing. Get your omega 3s through a solution rather than a pill. Make it easy for yourself!

title: Excellent for sensitive and oily skin
text:
I live in a house without central air, and as this has been one of the most humid, hottest summers my area has seen in quite a while, this product had a LOT to live up to. Thankfully, it passed with flying colors.

I'm one of those lucky people who have both sensitive AND oily, acne-prone skin. YAY ME. So it's very, very hard for me to find products that adequately address both issues: the ones for sensitive skin tend not to help with my acne, and the acne-targeted products dry out and irritate my skin.

First impressions: the bottle came with the clay separated, so I had doubts. There is no strong scent, which I really appreciate; you can detect a little bit of the clay and some of the lavender, but only barely, and once on the skin, any hint of scent disappeared. It went on easily, did not make my skin feel tight or dry, didn't irritate my skin. I was able to put my regular makeup on over it easily; even without an added moisturizer, my foundation seemed to go on more smoothly than normal. And after a day both in and outside (tbh, there wasn't really a difference for me, thanks to my lack of A/C), I managed to avoid the usual oil slick across my face. There were times when I was sweating quite a bit on my face; I did not notice any stinging in my eyes or streaking on my face. After washing my face at the end of the day with my usual cleanser, my skin was still soft, not irritated.

The only drawback (and not worth taking away a star) was the actual application method: the instructions indicate you squirt into your hands and pat on your face. Doing it that way, I felt like more product ended up between my fingers and on my hands instead of my face. I tried it with a cotton pad instead, using the patting method, and it appeared to work just as well and saved more of the product for my face instead of my hands.

Overall, this is an excellent product, does what it says it will (and very well), and though I received this as a complimentary product, I would most certainly pay money to get it again.

I was sent a complimentary sample of this product for reviewing purposes. Any option expressed is mine alone, based on my personal experience with the product.

title: Much better design
text:
Disclosure: I bought this product directly from the distributor--did not realize it was available on Amazon.

Really like this product. The design of this unit is SO much better than the traditional tank gauge! The traditional gauge has this long, articulated rod with a float on one end. But when the tank is more than half full, a good portion of the rod is below the surface of the oil in the tank. And that means the rod and the hinge get "gunked up" with residue causing the gauge to fail.

This product has a float attached to a string which goes up/down to register the amount of oil in the tank. In other words, the only thing touching the oil is the bottom half of the float. Nothing to gunk up and cause failure. Plus, the gauge itself is so easy to read--very much like a bedside alarm clock.

Very easy install and works like a charm. I would highly recommend this product to others.

title: Three years as my favorite conditioner ever!
text:
My favorite conditioner! I've been using this product for about three years, and it's the best product I've found to make it possible to get a brush through my very thick, wavy, tangly hair after shampooing. It leaves my hair with a soft texture once it dries, and I don't feel the need to use any additional products. I read one review about hair falling out. I certainly haven't had that experience, and in fact because there's less breakage fighting tangles, my hair is definitely healthier. When I run out of it and have to use something else, I'm always motivated to get in another order. Once . You could describe the texture of this as "waxy", but frankly that works best for me. I would not recommend it for thin or fine hair, but nothing's a perfect fit for every type of hair.

The packaging is treacherous, so I suggest sitting down with a good pair of scissors, some protective gloves to protect from being sliced up, and a large dose of patience. Free all of the ampules at once time and carefully dispose of the It's well worth it once you fight your way through to the actual ampules.

While the manufacturer suggests using an entire ampule per treatment, I don't find that to be necessary. I have a lot of hair, and one ampule lasts for three or four treatments as a little goes a long way. I leave it in for a couple of minutes like a typical deep conditioner, and I use it every time I shampoo rather than as a special treatment.

I just looked at my order history (I was just about to reorder when I thought to submit this review), and each order has lasted about 16 months, so it's a good value as well.

This does the job, but the curl is definitely not as dramatic as using a curler, but lasts longer given the heat function ( you can do it manually first with a standard curler, top it with mascara, then use this heated one to stick it in place). Since I have trouble even getting waterproof mascaras to hold my curl and refuse to double-clamp with a traditional curler, this turned out to be the perfect combo. I like that is doesn't take up too much space, it's the size of a bulky marker, and the charge has lasted a full week thus far.

title: Great little pump!
text: Recently, while on vacation I misplaced the membranes for my Medela Pump In Style Breastpump, which are vital for operation. The spare parts were safe at home, and with a hungry boy on my hands I was in a predicament.  Unable to nurse, I have provided my son with breastmilk by pumping three times a day since birth.  I was concerned about maintaining my milk supply, not to mention the discomfort of very full breasts, so I purchased the Isis Breastpump because I use Avent products and like the idea of being able to pump right into the feeding bottle, 4 oz, 9 oz or disposable. I am amazed by the comfort, control and power this little hand pump provides.  In addition, I enjoy the convenience of not having to be "plugged in" and the reduced amount of bottles to wash.  I found this pump to be great in a pinch, or for a weekend away.  However, for my particular situation having to express 30 ounces a day in order to keep up with my little guy, the Pump In Style is superior to the Isis both in speed and quantity of milk expressed.

title: love these virtue code masks
text:
i adore these virtue code masks. they are so pretty and feel so nice. that said, i only wear this brand mask in "safe" places like with my friend after she and i each self isolate for two weeks so we can then safely visit since we live in separate cities, or if i'm going to get drive up orders, and now outdoors since the national usa no mask outdoors for fully vaccinated people has been enacted.

to be honest these maske are normally nice feeling lightweight fabric. one layer! don't be fooled by the 3 layers listed. the second two layers are very open weave apparently inferior grade. they provide no protection whatsoever. however they do have a filter pocket and i always wear them with a filter. ALWAYS! otherwise you might as well not wear a mask at all.

i have both the virtue code pleated and this style mask in fabric. the pleated ones are one lightweight layer with a very similar weight filter pocket and come with one filter. so order a package of filters also. the little flat ones. i have none of their neoprine masks. i have a smallish face. the earloops make it adjustable so it fits nicely. i just feel good and happy wearing these masks. thanks to virtue code for making pretty masks at a sensible price but please please use two true layers at least in the masks then the filter pockets.

my friend and i ( her mostly) made over a thousand quilting fabric 2 layer masks, some with filters and some with the heavy filters sold at better fabric stores. those are all my workhorse masks. but if i just want to smile while choosing my daily masks, i always smile when i see the virtue code ones.

title: It worked well for about 11 months! Now it is in the trash, except for the battery!
text:
Final Update: A ring seal slipped out of alignment, creating an air leak, causing the water in the reservoir to spray out the sides. When I opened up the device I noticed several very cheap plastic tabs, responsible for maintaining the seal and stabilizing the attachments, were broken, being held in place only by a corresponding screw. An item with, supposedly, a five year warranty did not even last a year! The company no longer advertises this device on its web site, and has not responded to a complaint email.

Update: After less than a year of use, the reservoir now develops a vacuum during use. If the vacuum is released, it leaks all over the place the remaining water. This started a few days ago. No idea how to get warranty service, since the company does not even mention its irrigator on its web site any more! There seems to be no way to take it apart to service without breaking something. Disappointing. More Chinese junk!

The high speed is quite forceful, so you have to move quickly. The water reservoir is ample to do the whole job. It is light weight and the on/off button is conveniently located. The LED control lights are bright, so there is a bit of bleed between option indicators. The reservoir is fixed to the unit, but it does not appear to be difficult to clean or disinfect occasionally. Lots of attachments, most of which you probably will not use, contained in a convenient case. It looks like it will travel well, but time will tell.

title: Beware! Caused our pipe to break!
text:
We bought this for our little girl to get used to taking showers and for that purpose, it worked well. We had been using it the same way - which is with the flow about halfway open (maybe more), and generally without the 'tray' attachment. One evening I had just pulled the shower doohickey on the tub to divert the water to the showerhead. It made some funny sounds for a moment, the water didn't come, it made some more sounds and right when I was about to give up and turn the water off, the front of the showerhead exploded off! The whole front part detached from the showerhead and blew across the tub. Thank goodness it was pointed away from the kiddo or it would have caused serious injury. Luckily we avoided physical injury, but after bathtime was over and we went back downstairs, we saw our ceiling beneath the upstairs bath was wet. The pressure from the showerhead caused the pipe in the wall to burst. It seemed ok at first but now we have a leak in our ceiling that the plumber has to cut into and repair. All due to this showerhead. The plumber said it was certainly from the pressure of the exploding showerhead - you could see clearly what happened since the showerhead was in pieces.

Don't buy this. You could damage your property at best and damage yourself or your kids at worst.

title: Buy It.  It Works!
text:
Over the years I've tried multiple callus removers: various liquid varieties, the ped egg, files, scrapers, battery powered, wet / dry, and the chargeable type. You name it and I've probably tried it. I was almost to the point of making an appointment with a podiatrist to them surgically removed until I found the Emjoi. None of that stop and start if you press too hard. This thing is powerful enough to actually remove calluses!!! You must follow directions though (2-3 seconds in one spot) and not try to remove them in one sitting or you'll end up with sore feet. I've been using it twice weekly for the past couple of months and my calluses are practically gone. I wish I had taken some before and after photos. The only negative I can think of would be the fact that it is corded and I had to use and extension cord in order to reach with comfort but that's a small negative considering that IT WORKS!!! It comes with a one year warranty but if anything ever happens it, I would not hesitate to buy other one.

Note: I did not receive this item at a reduced price for my "unbiased" opinion. I wished to make that clear because I generally read a glowing review and somewhere down towards the end is the disclaimer that the reviewer got the item for free or at a reduced price. I try to skip those types of reviews for obvious reasons.

title: Comfortable on the feet
text:
I suffer from lower back pain and have been seeing a chiropractor for my condition. I purchased the HappyFeet Massaging Insoles as part of my treatment plan for my lower back pain. I wear a size 9.5 in shoes. I trimmed these down only a tad bit. Here's my feedback on the product since using them:
-The insoles are clearly labeled which made using them a breeze. The insole is labeled for the left/right foot and the size of the shoe is labeled so you know where to trim if needed.
-I put these in my casual lace up shoes that I wear to work. I did remove the existing insole as my shoe didn't fit comfortably with both insoles in.
-When you remove the plastic cover from the insoles, the gel side is a little sticky. This allowed the insole to stay in place and not move when I walked.
-The upside of the insole felt nice on my feet. Didn't get any blisters from my sock rubbing on the insole. I could wear my shoes with or without socks with these insoles.
-The gel arch was a nice touch and gave my flat feet some arch support.
-The gel insert was pleasing for my feet and lower back. However, the insoles didn't completely alleviate my lower back pain, but I did notice it was not as pronounced.
-I did notice a positive difference when I used these insoles in comparison to the ones that came with the shoes.
Final recap: All in all, these are comfortable insoles and they felt pleasant to my feet when I wore them. However, my lower back pain was still present.
I did receive this product for free in exchange for my honest and unbiased review. I have not been compensated in any way. Any questions please ask.

text:
I’ll be honest, I was worried about trying this item out. I’ve always been curious about epilating, but I’ve only known one other person to do it, and they said it was incredibly painful, but the results were great. As someone who is always looking for a shaving method that won’t leave me prickly after a few hours, I really wanted to try it.
I will say, I chickened out with the epilator after a few meek passes over my ankle. It does indeed hurt, as it obviously will, since the very nature of the thing is tons of tiny tweezers literally ripping the hair out. However, my hair HAD grown pretty long due to my putting off trying this for a while, so that may not have helped. But I’m unsure.
Either way, I ultimately just ended up using the electric razor attachment, and that worked wonderfully. Quick and easy, a lot easier than a manual razor. So that is a major plus. It may take some working up to the epilator attachment, and trial and error.
I will make sure to update if I figure out an easier way to use it.

text:
What I liked:
1. Nice build, feels solid enough.
2. Liked simple lamp feature - button to turn lamp on/off and a wheel knob on the right side to make the light brighter or dimmer. Bright enough to read by.
3. Liked that they taped printed instructions for main features on the sides so you don't have to keep referring to the booklet.
4. Amazon's return/customer service policy gets 2 thumbs up.

What I didn't like:
1. The sunset part where the lamp dims and then turns off is only 3 minutes long. While you can set the lamp to dim at 15, 30, 45, 60, 95 minutes long, etc., it dims at the last 3 minutes of the time you set it, not the entire time. E.g., set it to dim at 30 minutes, will begin dimming at 27 minutes. I got stressed that I only had 3 minutes to relax and fall asleep. Didn't work for me and didn't find out about this feature until read instructions. This was the deal breaker for me more than the sunrise which I slept through.
2. The sunset also dimmed in fixed increments, not a smooth or true dimming transition from bright to off.
3. The nature sounds were only 3-5 seconds of recording which were repeated in a loop. Not long enough to really capture a good sense of nature before repeating.
4. The backlight of display panel was too bright even though you could turn it off.

title: Do not expect a Beauty Blender
text:
Three pack is awesome, it comes with more than what you'll need. But do not expect this to be comparable to a beauty blender.
I use this for putting on liquid foundation. Unlike a beauty blender, it doesn't have a very natural finish, so you'll have to get used to blending the product more than before. BUT, what I love about it, is that it doesn't absorb any product and it's really easy to clean. I use less than half of the liquid foundation that I would use in comparison to a blender sponge, and it takes a few seconds to rinse off.

Would I use it? Yes, I currently do.
Do I recommend it? Yes
Would I buy it again? Yeah, but it's pretty sturdy, and it comes with three, so I don't think I'll be needing to buy it again unless I lost it.

text: I am relatively new to using a straightener to curl my hair, but so far I've been successful with this handly little straightner! It's small and easy to take with you when you're traveling. The small size also makes this product ideal for short hair. Another major pro is how quickly it'll heat up. And as so many other reviewers have stated, the box it comes in is pretty darn cute. My only complaint about this product is the smell that it produces... it gives off a really funky, almost tangy smell when it is being used . I know it isn't the products I am using in my hair because I use the same stuff with my curling iron and I've never had the smell with that. I think it's just the material that the straightener is made with. I'm not sure if anyone else has noticed this, and I'd be interested to hear if others have had the same problem. Fortunately, it works so well that I can look past the smell, but it is something that I would rather do without.

title: These are very small and seem firmer than Hapads
text:
I've been using hapads, but since they are pretty expensive, I thought I would try these. Based on some product reviews here I went against my instinct to buy medium and bought the small. I wear size 8 1/2-9 shoes.

Since the product info doesn't tell us the actual size of these, I'll do it here (I'll put my Hapad dimensions in parentheses for comparison so you can check these relative to whatever you are using now):

Approx length: 2" (hapad: 2 3/8)
Approx width: 1 3/8" (hapad: 2")
Approx depth at center: 1/4" (hapad 3/8")

The good news is that I can wear these on top of the insoles that came with my shoes. Then when I put the extra cushion insoles I use in my athletic shoes on top, the insoles make it a little higher and bigger. With hapads I had to use the pad on the top of the extra insoles because it would have been to high with them over it, but putting my foot in and out tended to catch on the hapads and wrinkle up the insoles to the point of worthlessness. Then when I went to replace the insoles, I couldn't get the hapads off...ack!

I think the extra firmness might not be so much from the pads being stiffer, but from the fact that the highest point is closer to the front of my shoe than a comparably-placed hapad. I tried moving the pad farther back, but that didn't give enough support.

title: Very nice massager, very crappy User Manual
text:
Nice massager, especially for the price. My neck problem is at C5 and C6, and this is the only massager I've found that gets low enough on my neck to do some good. As others have said, the heat function is very, very lukewarm: it doesn't really get hot, but that's OK with me.

I love this thing and would have given 5 stars, except for one big flaw: The printed instructions that come with the massager are worse than useless -- they are a joke. For example: "Please don't use this produce when drunken or bad." (Trust me, I made no typos; I copied it exactly as written.) OK, I realize that operation is pretty simple, but still, I wanted some basic info sheet to tell me how to set different massage modes using the single control button. There is no answer in the instructions that come with the massager; you'll have to rely on Amazon reviews, as I did. :-)

Still, as I said at the outset, it's a great massager, especially at this price point. Another feature I like: It will turn itself off after 15 minutes. The thing is so comfortable and relaxing, it's easy to fall asleep -- so the timer is smart. Of course, if you want more than 15 minute, all you have to do is push the button again. Overall, highly recommended.

title: Not durable and of questionable use. NOT a substitute for an N95.
text: Ok I get that they say "reusable for up to 24 hours" but why do the straps keep breaking? The box also says "not recommended for use in a clinical setting where there is significant risk level through inhalation". So basically its as KN95 that doesn't really work like a KN95. Actually, KN95 is supposed to be the equivalent of the US standard N95. An N95 FFR is a type of respirator which removes particles from the air that are breathed through it. These respirators filter out at least 95% of very small (0.3 micron) particles. N95 FFRs are capable of filtering out all types of particles, including bacteria and viruses. THIS KN95 doesn't do that!

title: Nicely built, but not powerful enough
text:
Pretty, hefty, solidly built, from wonderful materials, but it's missing some juice. Vibrations are not the tinniest, but they aren't particularly powerful either. They're passable.
Despite its looks, the big button is not a rocker, it's just a button, cycling through three speeds followed by two patterns of the main shaft. The small button cycles through three speeds for the bunny. Long press on each of the buttons is required to turn it off, and each part remembers the last setting when you turn it back on. The ears are very long. Unless you're very sensitive, they're not going to be as useful as inserting all the way in and applying pressure with the bunny's nose instead.

Charging port is covered by a somewhat difficult to remove rubber plug (need to use a nail), and has a red/green LED charge level light. When charging, the vibrator does not turn on. It arrives mostly discharged. It's splash resistant and very easy to clean. The seam running along the entire thing as the result of the molding process is a bit unseemly, if you're really picky.
Comes in a big, nice storage box (too big if you don't have ample storage at your home) and a black silk storage pouch.
Overall I feel it's overpriced.

title: Why you need a different brace, and how to heal faster & prevent re-injury
text:
The BandIt (or one like the BandIt) is a better brace for me and will be for most who need one. Here is a link to it on Amazon: [[ASIN:B000FML7SW BandIT Therapeutic Forearm Band]] It actually compresses the tendon, where the
Bracoo brace provides uniform pressure around the arm. That is better than nothing & does offer a little support to help in healing. But it doesn't support the tendon nearly as well. And to work effectively the Bracoo brace needs to be tight enough to restrict circulation, which obviously won't help it heal.

And for those who prefer to heal faster and solve the problem on a more permanent basis buy a brace & also buy a Thera-Band FlexBar. Here is the Amazon link: [[ASIN:B000KGOMBC Thera-Band Flexbar, Green, Medium]] Depending on how bad your injury is start slow with your hands on the outside of the green (medium) FlexBar (like five reps a day) and work up to ten or fifteen reps with your hands on the inside (where it is harder to use so the muscles get a harder workout). It will take a week to a month (depending on the severity of the damage to the tendon) to see results but it works for almost everyone.

The reason is simple: The tendon is damaged because the muscles on the "other side" of the arm are weak. I'm talking about the small muscles that get big stress only when we do things like play golf/tennis/etc. Using the FlexBar every day will target and slowly but surely strengthen these small weak muscles. This will keep the tendon from continually being stressed too far, allow it to heal much quicker, and in almost all cases prevent re-injury (if the FlexBar is used a couple of times a week to maintain muscle strength).

text:
I hate committing to a huge tub of protein powder, so I was glad to see Promix offering a sample pack of their whey protein flavors. The 6 different powders come in individual-use packets (equivalent of 2 scoops). I blend mine with 1 cup of milk and a few ice cubes (and add a banana for extra carbs on workout days). The powder is very light and will get foamy if you blend it too long. I thought all the flavors were good - they aren't overpowering so if you are used to artificially sweetened protein mixes, you probably will find these very subtle in comparison.

I find Promix whey protein to be a healthful way to increase my protein intake with few carbs and no soy. I appreciate their lack of artificial sweeteners and non-GMO ingredients. I ended up buying a large container of the chocolate PB, although the unflavored (surprisingly) was a second runner up!

title: Simple and economical
text:
I only recently started using a can to help me walk with a bout of sciatica. Desperate for something, I purchased my first cane from the local supermarket's pharmacy. It provided what I needed, but its solid handle got uncomfortable over long distances. Adjustment meant loosening the locking nut, moving the lower piece to a new incremental location, then re-tightening the nut. Nothing wrong with a $20 cane if it's only going to be used infrequently. But it turns out this affliction will accompany me for longer and more frequent periods. So I started looking for something more ergonomic.
The Ergocane looked and sounded like it would fit the bill and its price is substantially less than some of the other canes I found. When it arrived I found that, as described, it's infinitely adjustable in one step. I can get an exact length while holding my hand where I want the handle to be, not a 'near enough' location. And it feels rock-solid when I release the adjusting pin. The handle took a bit of getting used to, but, unlike the solid one on my first cane, this one is cushioned and feels better in my hand - I don't feel like I'm spending effort to grip it. The texture of the handle holds the cane in place when I lean it against a wall or rest it beside the counter.
The design of the handle puts my hand over the cane itself, not behind it like my first one. That, in addition to the pivoting tip, gives me a better sense that the cane isn't going to slip out from under me.
I hope I only need to use this occasionally, but I feel like the Ergocane is going to last a good long time even if I ultimately use it all day and every day.

title: The Case of the Missing Fish Oil
text:
I noticed a lot of fogginess going on at work; I felt my cognitive health deteriorating; my focus was just not what it used to be.

So I decided to order fish oil.

The bottle came and I was excited. I was hopeful. But I'm just not good at taking supplements - a personal problem, I know. It's not the fish oils fault. But upon cracking open the seal, I realized this only will last 90 days. The first couple days of my fish oil experience was good, but the taste was gag worthy. I would have honestly preferred it without the lemon.

After a month of taking it on and off, I decided to bring it to a camp I was staffing. During camps I tried to keep taking it, and I kept it in the staff fridge. Everyone knew it was mine and none seemed to want to steal it. No blame is being passed.

But after camps ended, the fish oil disappeared. Maybe it's because I just haven't gone searching for it, maybe deep down I don't want to find it, whatever the case, it's gone and well passed the 90 days and 20 dollars is now wasted.

All in all, buy the capsules.

title: OMG! It smells like Chocolate!
text:
Now that Spring has officially arrived & the weather is starting to get warmer, we will be spending a lot more time outdoors. This means a lot more time in the sun. And even if it's a cloudy day, we still need to be protected with a good sunscreen. But getting kids to want to stand still long enough to apply sunscreen can sometimes be frustrating, so I was very interested to try this Fun'n'Sun Broad Spectrum SPF30 Sunscreen for Kids.
When I opened the top of the tube, I could smell the chocolate scent. Now, this is supposed to be for kids but I admit that this is a sunscreen that I will use too! It is a light brown color when it comes out of the tube but, once it is applied to the skin, it disappears & doesn't leave that white film like some sunscreen products. It doesn't feel greasy after it is absorbed, just soft & dry. It doesn't take a lot of this sunscreen so be careful how much you squeeze out because a little bit does go a long way.
We have not yet had a chance to test this sunscreen after swimming because it's not warm enough for a trip to the lake yet. But the tube indicates that it is water-resistant for 80 minutes which means that it should be reapplied after 80 minutes of swimming or sweating or immediately after towel drying.
Why didn't someone think to make sunscreen smell like chocolate a long time ago?? It's such a good idea to make kids WANT to wear their sunscreen all the time!
I received this product for the purpose of testing & review. I was not required to write a positive review & the opinions expressed above are 100% my own.

title: Compact but Jerky - Updated
text:
Just received this today. It's fully assembled, minus the electronic pad on the front which just snaps on. Before putting it on I peered inside to get a look at it.

Gobs of grease everywhere practically dripping from the gears. Well lubed, so I figured it would be smooth.

However, it is not. While it fits perfectly under my desk, and gives me room to move my legs, it's still very jerky. Nowhere near as smooth as an exercise bike you'd find at a gym. I decreased the resistance all the way and it was just as jerky so I increased it to the max... didn't feel a lick of a difference.

The foot straps also snag on the pedals and bars with each rotation, making the jerky movement even more annoying.

I'll be keeping this and using it, but very disappointed with the flow and really wish I knew why it jerked around so much while peddling.

Edit: After two days of owning this and using it daily, the electronic pad on the front stopped recording or responding. I pried it off to see if the batteries came loose but discovered that the wire that easily connects to the control panel had -ripped the connection clean off-. I looked closely and noticed that it was only held on by two dabs of glue. It's fixable but it's absurd how shoddy this thing was built. I can still use it without the panel, but I'm very disappointed with this product.

title: Difficult assembly - functional, but leaves a lot to be desired.
text: This table - once you get it together - is fair. It is a cheaply built table, but it serves its purpose. The problems started on arrival. The box it was packed in was too insubstantial to handle an item of this weight. It had several holes ripped in it. Along the way, the little formed-plastic sheet they had where all the small parts (nuts, bolts, washers, etc.) were itemized by number, came loose. It was secured to the paper behind it with ONE staple - nearly in the middle. Two bolts and two washers were missing, and the rest were all loose and would have fallen out if the package had had one more good jar along the delivery route. The instructions just... weren't. There was a numbered diagram, but none of the large parts had any numbers on the physical items, and the diagram was so tiny, it was difficult to determine exactly what the items were supposed to look like in several cases. The diagram didn't even look like it was for the same table. The diagram did not show a two-part top. It took some ingenuity and trial-and-error to get the parts we received together and working as they should. It is pretty flimsy, but I don't have time to exchange or return. It was needed NOW. That's why I paid for one-day shipping. The concept is great. My problem with tilt-tables appeared to be answered when I saw this item. The stable portion that doesn't tilt was the answer... text:
This is a keeper for my needs. To be fair, this is NOT for every battery in your collection, but for the ones it will charge, it is going to do the job.

PROs:
1. Compact. It does not take up a large space for storage or on my desk when I am using it.
2. Simple to use. The instructions that came with it are straight to the point.
3. I have put 4 C-Cell batteries in it with no success. To be fair, they had been pretty much used up in trail cameras and had nothing left to build a charge upon. However, I put 6 AA batteries out of remotes, and in about 2-3 hours, they had new life. If I can do this 5 or 6 times until these batteries no longer have life, then I have gotten my money back on battery savings. Everything else will be "icing on the cake."

CONs:
1. If a battery is very heavily drained, then it will NOT recharge
2. The cover can pop off easily
3. The LED screen looks like all batteries are fully charged if you look at it from much more of an angle than directly above.
4. The plastic of the body feels kinda cheap, but if this is handled without too much horse play, then it should be okay.

The best way to remove them is to pull them down to the floor, let the patient step out of them and then try to pull them apart a bit at a time starting with a corner and working towards the middle. Believe it or not, this takes a few minutes and a lot of effort. The first time I used it on a patient I tried to take it off as I usually would by undoing the velcro while it was still on the patient so I could remove the pads and ice pack before standing the patient up. After pulling and pulling on the velcro and finding that it wasn't coming off at all, I pulled out the pads and Ice pack, asked the patient to stand, pulled the belt down to the floor and let the patient leave before wrestling with the velcro. Unlike the Nylex Wraps I have previously bought that were easy to put on and remove, this one required way too much effort to remove and so I sent it back. Either I received a strap with defective velcro fasteners that were way to tight or the company needs to replace the velcro fasteners they are currently using.

title: Great relief for my knee...
text:
I purchased this because I recently injured my knee and am now experiencing arthritis. Upon opening the package, I checked it for leaks and defects. There were none, construction was good. The fit was nice and adjustable too so it was pretty comfortable. My only initial disappointment was that no instructions or guides came with it. Was just a wrapped product in a box.
The first test was done with freezing. Everything was great. The gel stayed consistent and didn't harden. It did stay cold for a very long time. Be sure to wear it above clothes due to extreme temperatures and condensation.
It performed to my expectations.
Second, it is advertised as a hot pack as well. The problem is that there are no instructions not a temperature guide on the product like most hot packs have. Having experience with hot packs, I had to use the info provided on Amazon description along with my sense of how to microwave hot packs. I put it for 30 secs at a time. I noticed that the area hearing was inconsistent due to the gel squeezing from one section to another. I took it out, let it cool and then laid it flat to evenly distribute the gel. Tried again and this worked for better distribution of heating. Again , you must apply this over thicker clothing or you will burn yourself. It was very soothing radiant heat and held up fine to the test. Keep in mind though, if you are in the middle of hot/ cold therapy you need to be able to switch quickly. You'll have to have two devices, whether it's two of these or another device. Switching this over will not happen instantaneously as needed obviously.
I was able to receive this product at a steeply reduced price in exchange for my honest and unbiased review. The reason that I'm unable to give this 5 star is because there were no instructions included, which could be harmful to those who don't take time and caution using the hot pack. Also, I think they can improve the pack design to prevent cold spots with a proper quilting design. That would have kept the gel evenly distributed. Otherwise, the product has held up well and performed as advertised. My knee appreciates it.

Update: the item instructions were emailed out shortly after purchase, however was caught in my spam filter. Instructions are provided but not with the product.

title: Like a mini-loofah for the face, only softer.
text:
I'm borderline obsessive with my skin care routines, especially when it comes to obtaining only natural, organic products. We live in a world filled with chemicals, BPAs and PCBS, and all other manner of toxins, and so when attempting to rid my body of these inorganic influences, the last thing I want is to use more chemicals and plastics to "cleanse" myself from them.

Konjac is a root-based vegetable that is found on the Jeju island. It is naturally alkaline and balances the acidity of the skin’s impurities and oils while being enriched with protein, carbohydrate, iron, phosphorus, copper, zinc, vitamin A, vitamin E, vitamin D, vitamin B1, vitamin B2, vitamin B6, vitamin B12, vitamin C, and folic acid. It's naturally deep-cleaning and pH balanced, and contains no chemicals, Some of my favorite beauty bloggers swear by it, and so I thought I'd try it to see if it rose up to all of the hype surrounding it.

These sponges came three to the package - and I loved the eco-friendly, well-designed cardboard packaging that it came in. It includes a small silicone scrub brush - a nice touch, but something I personally won't use on my face. They are surprisingly hard in the package, not unlike a dry loofah, and must first be moistened to soften. Although the back of the package states that can take up to 15 minutes, that seemed greatly exaggerated - it takes a little under a minute to fully saturate and soften, and the texture is quite soft and even slippery. A thoughtful touch: Each sponge has a small string that you can hang it on, and an accompanying suction cup hook is provided, and this keeps it absolutely clean and off of your germy counter or soap dish.

So, I am sold. What I loved about it is that it takes virtually one drop of cleanser to foam up far beyond anything you'll need to completely cleanse both skin and neck - it produced a crazy amount of foam, and I found myself wringing it out several times to get rid of it. Not a bad thing as I spend a lot of money on cleansers and previously used a turkish washcloth which, believe me, required a good squirt to get even half as much foam. These are good sized sponges as well - not body sized, certainly, but more than adequate for your face and neck. Each one fits nicely in the palm of my hand.

There was some residual redness after using - that is attributed to my being vigorous with it to obtain the exfoliating benefits. It does exactly what it says - it gives you beautiful, glowing clean skin, and is definitely a part of my daily skin care regime. The sponges should be discarded after about a month, so this three pack gives you an easy three months of use.

I did not detect any noticeable difference between the three sponges aside from the color.

I received this at a discounted price for my review, but I don't mince criticisms. This was just something I really loved.

title: Broke In Less Than 6 Months
text:
I purchased this scooter for my 75yr old mom in Oct of 2017 and it quit working a few days ago. The motor will die randomly and won't move, all while beeping at her. It has a full charge and this is her 3rd Go-Go scooter over the last decade and she is well accustomed to operating it. It died on me as well while I was trying to see if there was anything obviously wrong..... It will eventually go again after removing the key multiple times, and then eventually die. I am dealing with the original vendor now which is Bargain Blast and if I don't get any help I will then go through amazon...... I will update this review with the outcome so you know if Bargain Blast and/or Amazon stood by their very expensive product.

UPDATE #1 3/22/18: My mom called Bargain Blast via the customer service phone number that is listed on their store front and she got right through to the owner named Eric. He said he would jump on getting her scooter repaired first thing tomorrow morning and apologized for her inconvenience. She said he couldn't have been any nicer or more helpful...... so far so good, and I will continue to update this review with the ultimate outcome.

UPDATE #2 4/5/18: Eric stayed in touch with my mom and had the repair people out to her house exactly 1 week after she first contacted him. After a lengthy visit, they finally figured out what the issue was but needed to special order the part and would have to come back to install it once it came in. As of this update, my mom is still without her scooter.

UPDATE #3 4/11/18 The part came in and they promptly came and repaired the scooter, and so far, so good. I have raised my rating to 4 stars because of Bargain Blast's prompt service. If there are no further updates by me, figure no news is good news and the scooter is running like it should........

title: Not likely to work like you expect.
text:
Not powerful enough, slow, takes many “shots” to do anything, targets skin as well as hair, did very little on my hair unless I colored the surface hair black.

There are a number claims in the advertising of this device that are doubtful or plain incorrect. When advertising is exaggerated or erroneous, I start to doubt all of the claims. Here is my observations and test results:

This laser hair remover is NOT a laser. IPL Technology is not laser hair removal. IPL based systems use xenon flash lamps that emit full spectrum light. You can see the xenon lamp in the treatment window. Even one of the ad photos and the body text says it uses a quartz lamp. So obviously, it is not Laser Hair Removal even though it says so in the title.

No type of IPL or Laser hair reduction techniques have been found that result in permanent hair removal. At best hair regrowth is slowed and limited for 6 months to several years.

The primary principle behind laser hair removal is selective matching of a specific light wavelength and pulse duration to obtain optimal effect on Melanin in the hair follicle with minimal effect on surrounding tissue.

There is no information provided on the pulse duration or output power. The window on the device is rather large while the claimed treatment spot size is 3 square cm.

There is no FDA certification for this device. There is only FDA certification for the general process of using high intensity light for hair removal

Not enough power to do much of anything on my hair color and skin color. Even after 8 shots at maximum power on the exact same spot the surface hair was untouched. If it can’t damage surface hair on top of the skin there is no way it is going to do anything on hair follicles under the skin. It did make my skin slightly red after 8 shots and it started to sting on the last two shots. It burnt my skin about the same time as it burnt my hair.

I ran various tests on several different areas. It was most effective on my darkest arm hair. I circled an area to use as demonstration with a black magic marker before I realized that the black color was the thing that made it work. Hair I colored with the black “sharpie: vaporized after several shots, even the marker on my skin vaporized and disappeared after several shots.

Other experience:
The LED display is not evenly lite. The center section is quite dim compared to the outside edges. This makes it difficult to read.

The tool is very slick. Whatever I set it on it wants to slide off. It will not stand up on its face because of the curve, you can’t lay it down because the cord comes out of the side it is stable on.

The instructions are confusing and not clear. You must hold down the “fire” button to get “automatic” repeat shot mode. On low power, shoots one shot every 1.5 seconds. On max power, it is 1 shot every 3 seconds. Very slow to treat a large area like my thigh.

Overall, makes bright light flashes that are highly unlikely to result in permanent hair removal. Doesn’t work on me. I won’t buy again.

title: It;s great to have both hands free, but there are design flaws.
text:
I had been using the tote bag with a shoulder strap that came with my G3 for about two weeks and was having trouble doing tasks like cleaning the pool and just about anything else that requires two hands. Even with the shoulder strap the unit seemed bulky, heavy and in the way.
I was delighted to see this backpack and even though the price was very high, I could see how this would help me to be more active and mobile. I received it today, and took it to the gym to walk on the treadmill and was pretty pleased.

The G3 fits snugly in this bp and took some effort to pull the material around the top of the unit. Once in it's in though! Some reviewers have stated that the unit slides down into the space below, but I found that the square support sides and the "shelf" with heavy duty velcro to hold it in place worked fine. The zipper to access the storage compartment gets stuck, really stuck and I'm afraid I'm going to have to send it back for a replacement I dont want to be needing my replacement battery and having to fight a zipper as I'm running out of oxygen!
I used it only with the double battery attached to the unit and left the storage space empty and although it was easier to carry and the weight was distributed properly, it got pretty heavy after about 15 minutes walking on the treadmill. Can't imagine toting around another double battery AND charger.

Pros
Much easier to carry than the shoulder bag
Backpack straps are easy to adjust and are wide and nicely padded
Comes with a sturdy rubberized handle to use when not on your back
Mesh pocket on the sides for easy access to a water bottle

Cons
Storage area zipper is defective
Chest strap and waist strap are not removable. Waist strap is big and bulky
Seems like it will take some doing to swap batteries. The unit either has to come out or the velcro shelf has to be removed and repositioned

I love Soylent. I am the type of person that is still waiting for science to invent a once-a-day pill for total nutrition, eliminating the need to eat. But for now there’s Soylent. It is so unbelievably convenient.

Reviewers mostly talk about how lumpy and grainy it is, but it’s all in the preparation. The key is to add water in three steps. If you gradually add water to the powder it will turn into a paste, then thick batter, then a soup-like liquid, zero lumps. I normally make four one-scoop 200 calorie servings at a time, which makes two meals. The water to powder ratio is 3/4 cup to 1 scoop. In my case the ratio of water to powder is 3 cups to 4 scoops. I add one cup at a time, stirring for a minute in between each addition.
