So when these reading glasses became available for review, I wanted to see if they could work for her crazy life. She was excited about the style and color options. Immediately, after trying the first pair, she commented how clear they were and noticed great improvement in her reading vision for both hardcopy papers and books, as well as endless hours on her laptop. As a school teacher, her eyes are constantly strained by reading, grading and uploading performance reports on her computer. She noted that her eyes felt relaxed using these glasses, as the particular magnification for reading was spot on. She switches between colors to match whatever I was wearing: red, for bright and energizing outfits; grey for muted pastels and black for accenting her dark hair and emboldening her scholarly teacher look. The glasses have remained comfortable throughout the day. Perhaps one of the most important benefits of these reading glasses is their durability. Flexible plastic frames, scratch resistant lenses and spring-loaded arms withstood the torture of her overfilled teacher bag, dropping on the floor, sitting on them, kids grabbing the glasses off her face and the normal on-off-on-again-off-again wear and tear a teacher's reading glasses must endure. In our Amazon review of these glasses, my wife gave them five stars for style, durability, function, clarity and comfort.  We received these for a reduced price in exchange for our unbiased opinion.

title: Amazing quick results
text:
[[VIDEOID:59ba0aa0c2e5ff10ae54ca774c4b1be7]] This curler is like nothing I’ve ever seen before! I was really amazed with results!

To set up, all you do is plug it in, set the desired temperature and time setting, and wait for just a few moments until it heats up. It only takes a minute or so. You can also choose to have the curls face one way or the other depending on which wide of your head you are curling. I just keep mine on “alternate” because it looks more natural.

I do want to mention that I wish this came with the ability to show Fahrenheit instead of just Celsius but I will get used to that and it’s a very minor inconvenience compared to how well this works!

Once heated up, take a section of hair, pull it taught and place the section inside of the curler. Once you press down, release the hair. Don’t worry, if you don’t do it correctly or if it starts to get tangled, it will stop and beep to let you know. (I have used this over and over again and have never gotten my hair tangled in it which is what my main fear was in the beginning.)

Once you press the curler down, it will automatically roll up the rest of your hair inside and over the ceramic plates. Once it is complete (depends on what timer setting you have it on) it will beep and stop. Release the curler and gently pull it away from your head. The result is a perfect ringlet curl!

Just watch the video to see this work in real time. And trust me, I have little experience with any type of curler, straightener etc. so if I can do this, anyone can.

If you’re looking for a quick and easy way to curl your hair perfectly, this would be a great choice! I received this product for free in exchange for my honest review.

title: Easy to use and easy to read
text:
[[VIDEOID:903f04fe6e7da024c043ec994772fbd2]] I usually have pretty good blood pressure readings at all my checkups but there are times at home where I swear it’s going through the roof! So whether you need to keep track of your blood pressure for health reasons or just because you’re curious, this would be a great thing to have.

It comes in a convenient carrying case along with a set of instructions with all the features it provides including multiple users, recording of information over a period of time and averaging.

As you can see in my short video, this is extremely easy to use and because of the long velcro strip, it will fit a wide range of sized wrists.

The sturdy piece goes around your wrist and you wrap the rest around the remainder of your wrist. Rest your elbow on a table and have your palm facing upwards. The display should be on the underside (palmside) of your wrist.

Press the button and it does the rest. You will feel it getting tighter and will hear slight beeps as it is working. When it is done, your results will flash in large and easy to read numbers.

It really is as simple as that. During the video, I must have been a little nervous and/or talking to much because it read my BP a little higher than normal. Once off camera, I took it a couple of times and it was definitely accurate as to what mine normally is at the doctor’s.

If you’re looking for an easy way to keep track of your blood pressure while still at home, this would be a great thing to have! I received this item for free in exchange for my honest review.

title: A one year update . . .
text:
I gave these rechargeable hearing amplifiers a great review almost a year ago when I first bought them. One still works well, the other doesn't. Considering the low cost of these, I'm buying another set. They've been worth every penny. NOTHING will restore your hearing to what it was when you were younger, but these are very good. I tried a $3,000 BTE hearing aid last year and brought it back to the hearing specialist, because these Banglijian hearing aids worked just as good! The BTE combined with eyeglasses & face mask was a huge hassle.

This is the 5th or 6th set of hearing aids I bought through Amazon. Most have been very good. These are actually the 3rd that fit in the canal (ITC) rather than behind the ear I'm very happy with them. One thing I've noticed with ITC digital hearing aids, they react to microwave ovens, or the plug in anti-pest signal things that put out a super high frequency that keeps mice or bugs away. They produce a loud static with these hearing devices. I just unplugged the anti pest things, and the interference stopped.
These hearing devices come with a tiny wax filter that does get plugged with ear wax, and must be replaced. So it also comes with a small pack of 8 new filters with a removal tool that will remove the clogged filter and insert a new one. The instruction book goes over this in great detail. In fact, the booklet is very comprehensive & easy to understand. I can't afford thousands for a hearing aid, so these are great. They work, and I'd recommend them to anyone who's hard of hearing.

This is hands down, the best sleep mask I have ever used. Seriously. I typically prefer the 3d masks over ones like this, but this is so comfortable, I just absolutely love it. It's the only one I've ever had that I wake up with it still on my face in the morning. Other ones make me too hot and sweaty, and I'll end up taking them off in my sleep. This mask really is breathable and keeps my face cool. The material is very soft, and doesn't annoy me like other non 3d masks do. My only complaint is that the velcro isn't very strong, and after just a little over a month, I'm going to have to add some new velcro to it, because I have a big head, and it keeps popping off :(
That is pretty typical regular wear and tear, I'm sure. It's completely worth the hassle to be able to enjoy a good night of sleep without sweating so much. It blocks out the light great and doesn't put pressure on my nose. I definitely, DEFINITELY recommend this mask!

title: Light-duty percussion massager
text:
I've had other Homemedics percussion massagers before and this one is (model HHP300) is somewhat of a disappointment.
Pros ---
-- The handle extends so you have some extended reach
-- Two speed (low and "high")
Cons ---
-- SPEEDS - The 2speeds should be labeled as "low" and "medium". I have a previous Homemedics model (Model # PA-1HWA) and the "high" speed on this one is really about 1/2 of the RPM's of the older models. I would call the massage level "adequate" for those that can't use a "high-speed", but when you're really in pain, it sure is nice to have a true high speed.
-- HEAT - Again, I judge it to be about half the heat of the previous model I reference above.

If you're looking for an "average" massager, then I guess this one might work for you. But if you're looking for a massager that has a true high speed and generates a fair amount of heat, I would look elsewhere (not to mention that you can find this model at Target for much less).

text: I just received my scooter, never having or needing one before, these are just my first impressions. It was easy to set up, it’s mostly put together out of the box. It feels very sturdy and my weight (195 lbs) shouldn’t be an issue. The brakes work well, although I think I’d feel more comfortable with a locking feature. I’m still pretty fresh from surgery and not in a cast yet so I feel every bump, there is no shock absorbing other than the padded seat. The included basket is a nice feature. I ordered the two color blue and white, the paint and welds all look good. It’s not as easy to use as you might think, so give yourself some practice time. If I raise the seat to the higher positions, I’d feel comfortable sitting on it and scooting around the house like that too. It’s very stable. It’s nice to be able to go to the kitchen in an upright position and get into the cupboards. After I get a cast, I’ll venture outside with it. By then I should be accustomed to walking with it.  I didn’t really want to spend $300 for one with more features and this one seems like it will be more than adequate for my needs. I’ll be using it for 12 to 18 months so if anything changes, I’ll let you know. Unless it falls apart, and I don’t think it will, I don’t see any problem with it. Thank you.

text:
I didn’t buy this product for its flavor/smell so I find that it’s not entirely worth mentioning that both left me wanting. But there it is. It smell and tastes on its own like it is exactly what it is. BUT by making a simple smoothy with it to cut and mask the natural flavor, you get the best of both. Amazing health benefits and a yummy drink!

I cut caffeine out of my diet a few weeks ago with the hope of gaining more mental clarity and longer lasting energy and alertness by switching to healthier approaches to combatting motherhood...er, I mean exhaustion. I ordered this powdered wheatgrass as well as powdered spirulina, mixing both into my yummy little smoothy each morning (even the kids like it!) It’s been over a week now and the health benefits are extremely evident.

My digestion is mom regular, my energy level is higher and lasts all day, my mental clarity is crisper and my mood feels overall elevated. When I was cutting coffee/caffeine out of my diet, the first few days of withdrawal were rough. Headaches and crazy fatigue, but once that subsided I noticed that I was really seeing results in my overall health.

I highly recommend this product and I highly recommend making a similar shake as the one I do. I can’t say if the spirulina or wheatgrass on their own would each work as effectively, but for me having both seems to be a great combination!

title: Better with than without it
text:
I love kill cliffs. My Gym sells them and I was more familiar with fit aids but I felt these helped me in recovery better than fit aids. They’re both excellent drinks. I’ve been drinking them consistently for about a month. All I can say is that when I don’t drink them I don’t recover well from workouts. There was actually a week where I went without drinking them and I was way more achy and sore than when I was drinking them. I’m 37 years old. I’m not old but entropy is taking place and I’m aging for sure. That being said I have some joint problems and inflammation is always an issue and this certainly helps with that. I was going to order a case of fit aid and was torn between the two but the decision came down to which one makes me feel better when I feel my worse (and the price was more feasible). As I get older I’m focusing way more on recovery than how I actually perform. I’m finding that if I take care of myself on the back end I can not only keep up and put more out in workouts but I’ll have enough to enjoy the more important things like family time. Kill cliff is becoming a staple in helping maintain that.

Packaging was nice and pretty too.

title: Information on the mouth film from Crest
text:
It took me a really long time to determine that this toothpaste is what causes the mouth slime/scum/film in my mouth. But, I didn't want to just speculate. So, I located some information on Crest's own website:

"Q: Since using Pro-Health toothpaste, I've noticed a "shedding" of the lining of my mouth. It is like a layer peels off each time I use it. My mouth feels cleaner than ever, but I'm not sure if this is normal."

"A: The shedding that you have noticed in your mouth is not unsafe and is a result of the natural process to remove dead cells from the skin surfaces in your mouth. The cleaning action of both Crest Pro-Health Toothpaste and Crest Pro-Health Rinse can accelerate this process and often results in the skin coming off in sheets, making the removal of dead skin cells more noticeable."

[...]

I've been using Crest for the majority of my life and have had almost zero cavities. So, I'll continue buying Crest, but I will NOT be buying 'Pro Health' any longer.

title: Fantastic flavor
text:
I’ve tried a lot of pre-workouts over the years and it’s an area I’m fairly critical in as a result. This pre-workout did not disappoint. Here are my thoughts:

- Flavor: 5/5
With most pre-workouts, I either hate the flavor right away, or I start to get tired of it after a couple of servings. That has not happened with this flavor so far, and it’s honestly one of the most delicious pre-workouts I’ve ever tasted. Literally tastes like a mojito (Raspberry Lime Mojito flavor)

- Energy Effects: 4/5
I’m quite sensitive to caffeine, so I almost never take a full serving of pre-workout. In fact, I usually half it. Even with a half dose, I definitely feel the energy and it makes me want to shred weights. It’s not so much that I get jittery though. However, and I’ve noticed this on different occasions, I do seem to crash a few hours later. It’s not a hard crash, I just get a little bit tired.

I also don’t feel any of the tingling or itching from the beta-alanine, but that’s probably because I halve the serving.

So overall happy with the effect, just not super thrilled about the crash at the end.

- Ingredients: 4/5
This pre-workout is one of the best mixers I’ve tried. Usually there’s a bunch of residue at the bottom of my shaker from the creatine or other ingredients, but this one mixes very well…that might be a bit of a con though because it’s missing ingredients you tend to see in other pre-workouts.

As an example, it doesn’t have any creatine in it, and for the price, it really is lacking ingredients you can find in competing products at the same or lower price point.

- Value: 4/5
I almost gave this a 3 because the cost to ingredients to servings ratio is not great. You can get other pre workouts at the same or cheaper price for more servings and more ingredients per serving. However, I tend to purchase those other ingredients individually (like creatine) so it doesn’t matter too much to me. Also, the taste is so delicious that it makes up for it, at least for me personally. Up to you whether that’s enough to pay the extra $$ though.

Hope this review helps, and happy lifting

title: An Effective Clean, At Home or On the Road
text:
This product is comparable to putting a capful of Woolite into a sink to hand-wash your clothes. It’s pure detergent, without any water in it, but water-soluble, so you can just drop one or two sheets into the sink, swish the water around until the detergent dissolves, then you can scrub your clothes by hand. It uses less water, isn’t laden with unnecessary perfumes, and doesn’t leave a heavy soapy residue. It’s just pure, compressed cleaning.

Notice, this is a detergent, not a soap. This means you don’t have to use hot water to maximize cleaning; you can achieve best results with cold water. (Though if you’re hand-washing, you may want to use lukewarm water for comfort.) If you have a conventional double kitchen sink, you can wash in one, rinse in the other, and hang your laundry up to dry. It requires very little water, and no electricity, to do your laundry with this product.

Chances are, if you’re considering buying this product, you’re probably considering it for its travel qualities. I’ve used this detergent in the kinds of washbags or hand-cranked washing machines that many people take camping with them, and had equal success. Of course, camping washers do develop an odor over time, and this detergent doesn’t eliminate that odor; you need to use the recommended washing agents that will remove odor from high-efficiency machines.

I’ve read a few people complaining that you need a large amount of this detergent to produce suds. But I respond that this isn’t accidental: manufacturers put lathering agents into many soaps simply because customers associate suds with clean. If you’ve ever watched your laundry in a glass-door washing machine, you already know that most commercial detergents don’t create suds, because suds don’t actually clean. They’re ornamental, nothing more.

You still need to take the usual prewash steps, such as pretreating stubborn stains. This product won’t remove anything set-in or persistent, just like a standard washing machine won’t. Sad to say, I failed to do this with a couple of shirts, which now have their stains set for life. If you want to use this product for maximum efficiency, you need to remain just as diligent about prewashing and stain-treating as you would if using an electric washing machine.

That said, if you travel or camp frequently, or if you prefer a low-electricity lifestyle that favors hand-washing clothes, this detergent should work well for you. I’ve used it for some time, both at home and on the road, with consistent success. As long as you treat the product as seriously as you would with the detergent you’d put into a conventional electric washer, you’ll get clothes that are clean, minimally faded, and comfy to wear.

title: Cool stuff, a little tricky to set up
text:
The scale is a bit tricky to set up. In a nutshell, the way it works is that the setup application guides you by gathering your Wi-Fi information, disconnects your PC/Tablet/Phone from your Wi-Fi, connects to you to the scale's wi-fi which acts as an access point, sends the connection information, then the scale connects to your wi-fi, you connect back to your wi-fi, and it's all done. The windows app didn't work for me, so I used the web-based app for phones on an android tablet and it worked.

Now the tricky part is to get your weight to show up as yours, not as a guest. For that, you need to go to your fitbit account on the web site (the fitbit app doesn't do this). Then you claim the measurements as yours by selecting yourself on the dropdown box. From now on the scale will "recognize" you.

The rationale for buying this scale and why I would recommend it when it costs 7-8 times what a standard digital scale would is that getting a single measurement is insignificant. When you weigh yourself, you want to know the trends over a period of time, whether you're going up or down or steady, and some days fluctuate. You can do it on any scale by logging the data into excel and that's how I did it in the past, but this is so much more convenient, as the data just pops up on the fitbit dashboard!

title: Setup harder than necessary and has some surprising limitations
text:
I have a Fitbit Charge 2 and decided to add the Aria scale. I really like the Charge 2 and would give that a 4 out of 5 rating.
The Aria Scale only gets a 2 out of 5 star rating in my book. It works but has some issues which are enumerated below:
1. Scale is significantly harder than it should be to set up. If you want to change what router its paired with, that is also a more difficult than it has any right to be. In general, you are better off using a PC/laptop setting this thing up than using a phone. However, the PC/laptop must have a wireless network card. Also, you have to download the setup program and on my laptop, the program window is much smaller than it should be making it a unnecessarily difficult challenge to navigate through the screens and complete the setup process.
2. Unlike the Fitbit watches, the scale doesn't use Bluetooth. Instead, it relies solely on Wifi. This means that you can't have your scale too far away from your router/wireless access point. The last thing I want to have to do is install a wireless access point in my bathroom for a scale.
3. The scale takes longer to determine and display your weight than a normal scale. The delay isn't enormous but once again it seems like unnecessary, though small, inconvenience.

If none of the above issues is a major concern and you want a scale that sync up with your Fitbit then go ahead and purchase. Otherwise, I'd wait for version 2.0 of the scale. It seems like they will definitely have to improve the setup process and hopefully the speed which the scale will display your weight. I'm not sure newer versions of the Aria scale will support blue tooth but who knows, we can always hope that this feature will someday see the light of day. I suspect that one of the challenges with adding blue tooth in the future is the power consumption - it would either eat through batteries or need to be plugged in.

Comparison
I was testing two scales at once, the Aria($120) and RedRock Multi-Function Body Digital Weigh Scale($20). The redrock although complicated to work with had the two main functions I wanted weight and body fat. The Aria certainly looks sleeker and works with an app to sync your weight and body fat trends but that's just not worth an extra $100 to me.

The main reason i bought the scale was to checkout the awesome Fitbit app tracking features. The app for the band is amazing allowing you to make goals, look at trends and encouraging your along the way with smiles, tips and achievements. I was dissapointed to see the data tracked for the Aria does not have the same nice display it's just pure data without the fun Fitbit pluses.

If the price were dropped by $70 and app functionality improved i would buy one for me and all my friends but as for now there are scales with much better value out there.

title: This is going in my 3D printer enclosure.
text:
Kinda big, but worth the peace of mind for my 3D printer. I'm putting one of these in my 3D printer enclosure just for peace of mind, in case of failure of electronic safeguards. The fuses are activated by combustion, which is good for me because it gets quite warm inside the enclosure. The minimum clearance is also good because the enclosure is somewhat small, too small for the original STFS rangehood device.

Keep in mind, this is technically a pyrotechnic device inside a fire extinguisher, so it's going to make a loud "BANG!" if it activates and spreads its powder.

One last thing about the size of this--my stove has a microwave range hood, and this is too bulky to fit under there. Unfortunate, but maybe there will be a long, slim version at some point for customers with this kind of setup in their kitchen.

For those wondering about freshness, I ordered on Oct 3rd and the product I received is labeled "replace by August 2025"

After 15 months of use, the scale would intermittently read out, "step off, step on, thinking, ect.," but never give me a weight readout.  I would remove the battery and replace with fresh ones weekly for one month before contacting Fitbit.  This is an expensive scale that is virtually disposable. title: I was very excited...but ended up being disappointed
text:
I was very excited to get this massager and all the great reviews, however I ended up being disappointed. I'm going to rate my experience and machine in parts:

Build quality: 3 stars (the equipment looks good but when you look closer, it's mostly cheap plastic)
Remote: 1 star (this thing is complete junk, you have to twist your wrist in every way possible to get it to work)
Side compression: 4 stars (this is the best part of the machine, however the padding should be a little more firm)
Bottom rollers: 2 stars (they are too hard and too sharp and dig into the bottom of the foot, and could cause injury)
Ergonomics: 3 stars (the bottom rollers does not get the inner part pf the foot and puts pressure on the outer sides, completely missing an arch of the foot) I recommend positioning the rollers in the angle. I tried repositioning the foot but still could not get it in the right spot.
Toes: 1 star (This machine does not massage the front of the foot at all)
Shipping: 2 stars (The box was damaged because it was too large)
Seller: 5 stars (because they emailed me right away and asked fr 5 star review)

Over all I can only give this machine 2 stars because the only thing I liked are the side compressions.

title: Extra-hard bristles misrepresented as "sensitive"
text:
I received a package of these super-hard bristled toothbrush heads for Philips Sonicare handles misrepresented as "sensitive," both on the package and in the Amazon listing. My wife tried one and it hurt her gums. I tried it after her and had to agree that this head has the hardest bristles I've ever experienced, too hard even for me.

There's a note in the box indicating that I should contact the seller directly if not satisfied and get a refund directly.

When a company lies about a product on Amazon, it's being pretty optimistic to hope it can keep Amazon and shoppers from learning the truth. Here's how it actually works: we return the product to Amazon with a note about why, and then post a review. I do hope Amazon pays attention and these guys are kicked of the site, at least eventually, but anyway, reader please be forewarned.

Instead: I just received MorningGo soft bristled brushes to replace the scam brushes, and they are not only as soft as the Philips Sensitive heads were, but also very well made, looking nicer than the originals from Philips, and fitting the handle just as well. My wife is pleased. Honesty and attention to detail are where it's supposed to be at.

I hoped to find an easy and effective chemical solution but not an acid.  Speedy Clean did the job.  It sprays on foamy and needs to sit on the hardened concrete for a full 10 minutes.  I then used a 4 inch scraper to easily remove the splatter.  Anything that didn't want to easily come off (super thick concrete blob) received a second treatment. Be sure to wash the area well to neutralize the cleaner and lay down a tarp before starting if working on a concrete floor so you don't damage the floor.

title: Best Model Tested Thus Far
text:
As someone who has purchased five other bottles for comparison purposes, I can say that I prefer this bottle to the others for a couple of reasons. First, the part that screws onto the bottle is better made so that the bottle does not leak. Lest this sound simplistic, the problems experienced with other bottles is that the moment the bottle is tipped over, it begins to leak. The amount of leakage increases as one squeezes. However, the rigidity of the screw top of this unit is such that leakage has not occurred.

Secondly, the spray is a bit more subtle. Some bottles have a single outlet for the water so there is one stream. This is sometimes desirable but not always. The Leka Travel Bidet has several smaller holes which allows for wider distribution of the water and probably an overall cleaner experience.

Since I am the first to review this particular model, I will repeat what I have written elsewhere about portable bidets. The word "portable" suggests the bidets are mainly useful when traveling, especially perhaps to countries that either do not routinely supply toilet tissue or where the tissue might not seem hygienic. However, it goes without saying that anyone who is sensitive to chemicals in the paper would probably like to consider such a bottle as an alternative to paper. Likewise, if one is concerned about the environment or using a composting toilet, these bottles have a real niche. They are also useful for people with motion issues, such as those recovering from surgery or whose infirmities or lack of agility interfere with good hygiene.

There are additional reasons to use such bottles. One can bring one's own water and perhaps reduce the risks associated with potentially contaminated water. It is also possible to medicate the water with essential oils or herbs to reduce risks of various types of microbial and fungal infections. As someone who travels a lot, I find these bottles very useful and I like the fact that this one has a cap for the nozzle. It seems like an extra touch to prevent both leakage and contamination. However, unlike the other models I have bought, this one does not have a carrying bag. Having never used the bags supplied, I do not regard this is a shortcoming.

For those who are concerned about where things are made, it would seem this is made in China. The print on the box is mostly in Chinese, but the suggestions for use include various medical conditions such as hemorrhoids and itchiness. The advice is aimed at ladies, but there is no reason that gents would not also find this very useful.

Update after long use:

A few ago, the little blue tip to the nozzle fell off. There are no threads and no sign of glue. It might therefore have simply been pushed into place. I cannot get it to stay in place. The bottle will still work but without as much control over the water flow and without the ability to direct the water. I think this is a design flaw and could easily be corrected with threads. In the meantime, I will try glue.

title: Room for Improvement
text:
This is my second unit so the three-star rating has to be taken in that context. The first unit was sent to a clinic in a third world country. It was greatly appreciated so I bought another one for the clinic but decided to test it before shipping. My sense is that it does, in fact, do a rather good job of cleaning the air and it works considerably faster than expected. However, and this is unfortunately quite important, it does emit ozone. It seems to improve the air quality up to a point and then the ozone is quite unbearable and probably not particularly safe either. It does not seem to have any on/off switch nor settings so the only way I see to stop it is to unplug it. This is not difficult, but it is a tad inefficient and awkward.

For its price and tiny footprint, it does a remarkable job, but there is significant room for improvement. That is the reason for knocking off two stars, but even if features were added, the ozone would still justify some reduction in praise. If one were not going to use the unit on a continuous basis, this type of air purifier would have a place in any situation in which odor or germs were occasionally introduced. However, for continuous use, I think a higher quality and perhaps more expensive purifier would be better. The unit is not silent at all. It actually makes quite a bit of noise, enough to prevent me from sleeping.

title: Heavy tablets / on larger side
text: I decided to try this Cervello Brain and memory supplement because I experience some brain fog as I age into my 40s. Since having kids a few years ago, I'll come into a room and forget what I went in there for, little things like that, as I get older. I want to try to keep my brain healthy and functioning well, and this product seems to contain a lot of good vitamins and nutrients that can be beneficial to brain health, so I decided it was worth a try. Always check with your doctor to make sure a supplement is safe for you and won't interact with any medications you take. This product is a rather large tablet, in my opinion, that might be slightly difficult to swallow for those with swallowing difficulties. The suggested dose is to take 2 tablets once a day about 20 minutes before a meal. It smells kind of like alfalfa or rabbit food. On the plus side, the label says it contains Ginseng, Ashwagandha, and Ginko biloba, among other vitamins and nutrients, which I have heard positive things about in the past. I can say, after opening the bottle I received my bottle was 75 percent cotton ball stuffing, with about 1/4 the bottle full of tablets, but I'm hopeful this is just bc it was a free sample bottle for vine reviewers, so maybe they give us less of them as a sample, which is fine. Taking it short term for a few days, personally I have not experienced any negative side effects, other than slight indigestion after swallowing kind of a bitter horse pill. I like that it is stimulant free! Pregnant or nursing mothers should probably avoid this product though because of some of the herbal supplements it contains. For those without sensitivities or allergies, who do not have difficulty with larger pills, this might be worth a try to boost brain health, because there are a lot of vitamins and good things in it! 🧠

title: Great all-purpose earplugs.
text: I use earplugs a lot.  It seems like I'm the first one to be bothered by loud sounds, like bands that overplay or blaring movie theater speakers.  These stay on my key chain and I'm never caught without them.  I'm also a musician.  So, trying to reduce damage to my hearing is a big deal.  The problem is that most earplugs aim to block all sound from entering your ear.  This creates a problem if, like me, you play a wind instrument, because the sound reverberates in your head and you end up not being able to hear anything BUT yourself.  The DownBeats earplugs let some sound safely through, which helps this problem.  In a movie for example, these don't muffle the sound, but rather helps take the "edge" off so that it's not painful.  In musical performances, they don't totally solve the issue I described, but it's better than other types I've used.  If I pull them out just a little (so that my ear isn't totally plugged) I can hear my own playing normally and the rest of the orchestra, but the volume of the other instruments is reduced to a comfortable level.  I went to a hearing specialist to see if there were better options and he said that more expensive "musician's earplugs" would block more sound and make the reverberation problem worse.  I showed him these earplugs and explained how I used them, and he he agreed that that was probably the best solution.  I think these are great.  Comfortable too.

title: Ongoing Relief from Female Issues
text: I have suffered from recurrent BV for a couple of years now and have tried all of the antibiotics and creams from my doctor. Nothing worked for long, and I'd alternate between yeast infections and BV from medication side effects. I did a lot of research online and found that a 50/50 combination of 3% hydrogen peroxide and distilled water douche was a popular "cure". It does work to refresh yourself after your menstrual cycle or sex, but it only gives temporary relief for about a day. I also read about the boric acid suppositories but was scared they would be too harsh for my system. I finally gathered the nerve to try these and I'm so glad I did! This also isn't a "cure", but it keeps me fresh for days after I use it. I use one every 3-5 days and haven't had a problem with itching or odor since I started. I also use these for a couple days in a row after my cycle, as your pH changes at that time, so you're more likely to have a BV flare up. You can also buy empty capsules and boric acid, which I tried since it's a little cheaper, but it's pretty sketchy. You have to wear gloves because boric acid will burn your skin, as the skin's pH is a lot different than your vaginal pH. The powder floats around in the air when you're making the capsules and my eyes started to burn, so I tossed it all in the trash. I'd rather pay a little more and have the convenience of the pre-made pills! I strongly recommend these to anyone suffering from "female issues".

I will now be known for taking my purple cushion everywhere now. I cannot sit comfortably anywhere without it.  And now that I have something that can help make the pain go away even if it's just due to this cushion I will do it. title: TL;DR "Is Dece."
text:
I don't normally write reviews, but the company offered me $10 to do so, so here I am. While these opinions are still my own and uninfluenced in that regard, I would likely not bother writing otherwise.

Took a bit to get the item reoriented due to the internal sleeve becoming misaligned from shipping, but afterwards it seemed to work fine.

I went for this model style (the 2 way type) thinking it would be easier to clean, and for the most part it is, though I worry about getting water and such between the sleeve and the plastic since as far as I can tell there isn't a way to separate the two.

The hard case seems pretty decent, as it allows for a sufficient amount of leverage and control when in use.

The TPE is pretty soft, though I can already tell that it will likely not hold up under use long term and it has already started showing signs of deformation from one use. Still, for the price ($16.58 at time of purchase) it seems like it will be worth the cost.

My biggest concern is that if one is to leave both sides open and is to use it, a misplaced climax could lead to a very sticky situation. While I would assume this will not be an issue for most users, it is something to consider.

I do like how the product is basically self contained with its own storage unit. While the semi transparent lids may lead me to not have this openly displayed, it is otherwise mostly inconspicuous . And seems of decent quality too. I find its heft to be quite useful in keeping things where they should be. It is likely that after it has been torn to shreds, that the case itself could be easily repurposed and I will likely hold onto it long after it is as dead inside as I am.

Overall, I would say that it is pretty good.

So, while this product appears to work, you must exercise extreme caution when using it. According to the product page, they are made of boron trioxide glass, which should make them resistant to chips and cracks, but one encounter between them caused one to shatter. After it worked so well in the bedroom I tried it in the living area, but since they have a large open concept it didn't do much of anything.

As far as noise goes, yes you can hear it. But it's quiet so it sounds more like a small fan at low speed. Mist of the time I don't even hear it.

There is a blue light around the top of it, but it's not very bright or distracting.

title: Updated Review Based On First Use, Pictures Included :)
text:
Pictures only for now, will update with product review very soon!

Super cute hair dryer with accessories & carrying bag!
Hopefully it will work as good as it looks because it looks super sleek!

Update:
Used this the night before last to blow dry my daughters THICK hair, it smelled a little weird (hopefully just to using for the first time, not like a fire or anything just an smell that wasn’t there before using it, nothing bothersome or anything like that.. I just have a really good sense of smell)!
Anyway, we didn’t use the included brush yet, my daughter grabbed her wet brush & later I grabbed a different lightweight paddle brush that I actually got off here & finished with that. It took awhile due to my daughter having literally the thickest head of hair I have ever felt in anyone in my life (my hair used to be thick, but when I get hers in a ponytail I don’t think my fingers can touch if I put them around it, it’s thick thick!
Even though she kept trying to lay her head on me because we laid in bed while drying it, or complained most of the time we finally got it as dry as she would let me. The turntable nozzle was a nice use to direct the air where it needed to go (didn’t even try it without that to be honest) & her hair was SUPER smooth once done. She asked why her hair can’t always look like that, she is 13 so she has had her hair blown dry quite a few times but we mainly just let it air dry! It was super easy to change the temp (I do wish they were in Fahrenheit, not Celsius because we just don’t use that type of measurement much in the US)!
I would like to use it a few more times before saying I completely recommend, but for now it is a nice addition & I am glad we have it to try & hopefully fall utterly in love with in the next few uses :)

title: Great idea, poor performance
text:
Commercial dental floss products are typically made with plastic that doesn't degrade, ends up killing animals, and is sometimes coated with resins that make it slippery--but which are carcinogenic.

Finally, how wonderful to have a dental floss that's made of natural substances, tastes fine, and uses minimal packaging. So what's not to like?

First, the Dental Lace container has only one cutting edge, not two. This means that after I cut off the floss, it keeps popping back into the container. To remedy this, I must wrap the floss around my finger a few times before cutting it above where I wrapped it, thus allowing enough string to be on the outside so it doesn't migrate back into the container. This can waste a lot of floss.

Even so, I'd go to the additional trouble if the floss worked. The silk fiber is very poorly made and keeps breaking as I use it. This completely negates any advantages of buying, having and using it!

Don't waste your money on this brand. Instead, buy the far superior floss made of bamboo fibers from Terra & Co (also available at Amazon).

text: I don't know why it works, but it does and quickly.  I first purchased a single bottle and it was so effective that now I buy the three-pack.  For many years I have been woken up by painful cramps in my legs.  Until the last year or so, I could "walk them off." I don't remember how I came across this product, but I was desperate enough to try it despite thinking that the ingredients were too simple to have any effect. The words "snake oil" occurred to me.  I'm glad I was wrong.  I keep one bottle by my bedside at all times.  As soon as I feel the start of a cramp, I take a few swallows.  I don't find a mere capful or two effective.  I usually need the equivalent of a quarter-cup.  The instructions state you can apply the liquid externally; I haven't tried that.  But drinking it works very well.  I couldn't recommend it more.

title: Night light is the best function
text:
I actually really like this sound machine, but there are some things that would make me like it more.

The good:
1. The night light function is the best part of this. It projects a cute moon and stars and is perfect as a nightlight.

2. I like that it runs on batteries rather than being plugged into the wall so that I can move it around where needed.

The bad:
1. I really wish this had a timer function. I don't like leaving it on all night (because I can hear it from my son's nursery) so I end up sneaking in to turn it off after I'm sure he's asleep.

2. The volume button on mine stopped working about the second week. So it's full volume, which is pretty loud.

3. I really wish the creators of this would have made the sound loop a little longer. For example, after listening to the running water option for a few seconds, there is a clear sound where it resets. It's just kind of unnerving and I wish the loop ran longer.

Overall - this thing is pretty cheaply made, but it works for what it's supposed to. Keep in mind, this item is quite small. (I had been expecting something much larger.)

title: Love/Hate this machine
text:
I had the EXACT same problem as S. Franklin (see review of August 29, 2011). I bought my Yogourmet in January 2009 and had great success--for awhile. Then I noticed a sloshing sound in the body of the appliance which I'd not remembered before. After this, I noticed the same leaking from the cord area. Still, I shook out most of the water andI kept using it, thinking (stupidly) maybe there's a little moisture getting trapped in the walls somehow (imperfect seal on top edge, "sweating"?) TODAY I finally noticed a hairline crack inside and a very low level of water as I took out the inner yogurt container. I shudder to think that I might have easily electrocuted myself over the several months I've used this item with this (increasing) leak. I'm sure the warmth of the container opens that crack enough when in operation to allow water to seep inside.
Still, the yogurt came out great! And I NEED a batch yogurt maker. I really do not want to go back to laboriously filling those little jars. In addition, our family wipes out yogurt really fast.
Since someone else has had the exact same hairline crack leakage problem, I really do not want to invest another (nearly) $50 in this yogurt maker. I have two nice 2-quart containers left over, so I'm thinking I'll take the advice of Commenter "jim_nc" and try to mix up my culture and warm it some other way, either in a crock pot set on warm (which I'll need to calibrate somehow) or with an insulated "ice" chest, or ... ? Would these methods hold the warmth for 24 hours (rather than just a few hours as in most yogurt-making? Ideas, anyone?
Perhaps there's a market out there for an enterprising inventor to make a simple, quality warmer for 24-hour yogurt making.

title: Wonderful item, heavy duty, works well
text:
I have owned about a dozen shoe stretchers - from Target - over the years. The Target shoe stretchers look similar to this one - albeit with a shorter handle and without the angled last. The target stretchers have a plastic end on the screw and a plastic plug. I break a Target shoe stretcher every few years - the plastic plastic end separates from the screw or the screw device becomes stripped and inoperable. I continue to repurchase only because I need it and it never dawned on me I had other options.

The problem is that my Target shoe stretcher never worked with my high heels. It has no angle, so it would not go in deeply enough or create the tension that is necessary for it to actually stretch a high heel well. After wearing a pair of expensive and agonizingly tight high heels over the holidays, I searched for a specific "high heel stretcher." I bought this one - really because it had the best reviews. It looked remarkably similar to the Target version I own, so I expected it to be a similar stretcher with an angle that works for high heels.

I was very pleasantly surprised. This stretcher is incredibly well made, the handle turns smoothly and the bunion plug and screw mechanism are metal - not plastic. It was easy to operate. At first glance, it may look like my cheapy target version - but it is FAR SUPERIOR to it! There is nothing flimsy about it and it works really well. I am sure it will last for many, many years. Do not hesitate to buy it!

I love them, slip four panels in and off you go. Unless you just really want wet paintings rubbing together, I would not put more than four in a case.  You can, in the 12 by 16 case, put 8 x 16 panels stacked into one slot.  Word of warning: the holders that separate the panels are glued in, and leaving the case in a very hot car can make the glue fail.  It can be fixed with E-6000 glue.  Be sure to put your name on the outside, because everyone who paints outside seems to have one of these!

title: Almost crunchy
text:
I've had the bottled Soylent before. It was all right, neutral flavor, very smooth, with an aftertaste like graham crackers. So I figured, hey, maybe I can make a coffee shake that's nutritious. I could save on shipping by not buying something online that includes water, or buying into one of the originators of the recent subscription product boom.

Here's the thing about Soylent powder: It's gritty. Even when it's blended for a minute in a Vitamix, it feels like there are tiny sugar crystals that weren't bashed to bits by the blender blades, except they're not sweet. It's like ice crystals that are room temperature. So every shake and smoothie I made with this stuff ended up slightly crunchy, which was weird enough for me to not buy it anymore.

I'll probably have some bottles on hand for those rare occasions when I need a full meal and there are no tasty alternatives, but I don't think I'll be buying the powder again.

title: Not user friendly at all
text:
I’ve never used a heated eyelash curler. I’m used to the traditional clamp curlers so I was excited to try this. Oh boy is it not user friendly. First of all, if it’s sold in the US I would prefer to see temperatures in Fahrenheit. It’s not a huge deal, it’s fine just to think of it as 4 heat settings I guess. But I’d rather see the temperature in a format I understand or not need to pull out a calculator to figure out. That being said, it is incredibly simple to turn on and switch through temps. The biggest issue comes with the instructions. From what I can tell you’re just supposed to hold it against your lash line from the outside. But then the instructions tell you to do this for a “few seconds.” Such a highly subjective number. Is it 5 seconds? 10? 30? I don’t know. Given that if you hold a curling iron on your hair too long you can end up with a burned off section of hair, I don’t want to take chances here. Eyelashes are fragile as heck and you don’t have a whole bunch of them. If you burn them off, it will be noticeable. So I ask again, how long should I be holding this on my lashes? I’ve tried it up to 10 seconds (the most amount of time I’d keep a curling iron in my hair). Didn’t notice a difference. It’s just such an awkward system. I’d much rather just have a heated clamp curler.
Besides the glaring issues with use and instructions, it’s a really cheap looking tool. This mascara sized wand comes looking more like cheap metallic plastic than the sleek chrome color shown in the photos from the seller.
I’d pass this on this one. I personally haven’t been able to get it to do anything and don’t want to continue to experiment and risk losing my lashes.

title: It’s cool, but HOW DO I USE IT?!??
text:
[[VIDEOID:cd8757ffae0e7a2cf1d476813a516b79]] I was quite excited for this product but I’m really confused by the instructions, especially the clean mode (green). It mentions applying cleanser prior to using it but then in the warnings it says not to co-use it with cleanser or cleansing oil. It can be used with makeup remover or cleaning makeup water? It also mentions not to use “too thick cotton pads.” What cotton pads? Am I using them with the machine somehow? It is mentioned again in safety precaution again: “cotton pad fixing ring…”
What ring? Where is this ring? Am I supposed to be using this with cotton pads somehow?! There’s certainly not one included. I do not know, it’s very confusing. I’m also not clear on how many passes I should be doing on my skin. Additionally, it mentions using it on the eyes but doesn’t really show that in its directions or say if it’s cool on any function or just one. One thing it is pretty clear on is that you DO NOT want to use more than one function per day. It’s best to use them in succession (one on Monday, the next on Tuesday, the last on Wednesday and so on…). But apparently you should only use it once a week if you have allergic skin (?).
Aside from the confusing instructions, it’s also a little bit difficult to get it to work. You have to hold it with two fingers on the edges to get it to vibrate which doesn’t seem to always work. Also, holding it like this creates an awkward usage. It’s tough to hold it that way and maneuver to both sides of the face.
Another really annoying thing is the charging port! It took I long to figure it out. You really have to shove the thing in there! At first I thought I had it the wrong way. After turning it several times I finally pushed harder than I would like and it went in. Not a great experience.
It’s a neat little device, but the confusion in exactly how to use it really detracts from its appeal! That paired with the awkwardness created by how it needs to be held and the difficulty placing the charger take this from a pretty good device to a mediocre experience.
Oh and I almost forgot, don’t keep this device that you will undoubtedly be using in the bathroom, IN THE BATHROOM. It’s too sensitive to humidity and it might break. What? I get not running it under water, but it cannot take the humidity from a shower? Could you imagine if all your electronic bathroom supplies needed to be kept on another room? Not a fan of that discovery!

title: A Noticeable Difference In Someone with Severe ADD
text: Since I suffer from an extreme form of ADD and depression/anxiety it is important that you consider those things as I review this product.  I am on adderall for my ADD which is a habit forming amphetamine, and I was hoping that I could reduce my dose & substitute the Area 10 for it.  However, that was not the case.  This herbal remedy takes at least 2-3 weeks before you notice any difference.  So, if you're looking for an immediate "fix" this is not the solution for you.  However, on a positive note, for someone like me to notice any difference at all is short of a miracle.  Nevertheless, after about 3 weeks on this supplement I noticed slightly better concentration/focus, and a slight but noticeable increase in my energy levels.  Since I have severe deficits in these departments, I am willing to bet that someone with a less severe condition would notice a marked effect in their cognitive abilities after taking AREA 10 for a few weeks.  So I gave this product 4/5 stars because for someone like me a noticeable difference is, in fact, very impressive.  I would say that this product is definitely worth a try especially if your condition is not as severe as mine.

title: I Completed 30 Days & Was Thrilled
text:
I took the 30 day challenge with Exaltria and incorporated the one-a-day pill into a healthy daily routine with 8 glasses of water, a healthy breakfast, 30 minutes of exercise daily, and washing my face twice daily. At 36 I have started to notice the fine lines, enlarged pores and general age of my skin. Taking the pill was a great reminder to do other healthy things to keep my body at its best, from the inside out.

The first two weeks of taking Exaltria I experienced more skin peeling than usual and my skin was drier. I kept drinking my 8 glasses of water a day and washing and moisturizing my face and by the 3rd week my skin was more hydrated than before using the product and looked better. I took weekly photos without make-up to track my progress.

Overall I was pleased with the results. It was a simple enough step to add to my daily life that resulted in my skin feeling and looking better.

I received a sample in order to complete my 30 day challenge with #CollectiveBias, Inc and the advertiser but all experiences and opinions are my own. #shop

It was easy to transport discreetly (I liked the handle) but really wasn't as cushy as I had hoped. After some minutes I may as well be sitting on the hard seat itself.

It did work well to keep the coldness of the seats from getting to me and I like the fleece. I guess there's a trade off here. To get more thickness, then I'd have to get a cushion that is not so easy to transport. But who wants to drag a bulky cushion around a stadium?
It's also doesn't grip to non-cloth surfaces so it will tend to "travel" if you are a wriggler. I am and had to keep pulling it back under me.
It may work very well in an office chair as shown in the photo but not for stadium seating.

title: Works well; arrived super quickly; needs better description
text:
I was looking for one-way straws for my mother, who is quadriplegic, so that when she drinks the liquid will stay in the straw. However, every one-way straw I found had a diameter too wide for her preference. These select flow valves were our best shot at being able to have our desired effect on the straws she presently uses. I saw these first on the ARK website. There, they have the option to buy in packs of 3 and up. However, this listing on amazon does not outline how many you will receive for the price. I needed them quickly; so, I bit the bullet and purchased them, as a prime member, not knowing how many would arrive for the price. I was pleasantly surprised to find 3 were sent for my purchase price (which I believe was just under $8, including shipping). I was also pleasantly surprised by how quickly they arrived. I selected two-day shipping, but these arrived at my door the next day - and early in the morning! Kudos!

In order to fit well on a straw, the straws diameter should be at least 3/16" wide. My mother uses a more narrow straw (1/8"), and as such these valves to do not fit well. Again, how they are used and how large the device is is not outlined in the product description. Instructions for use are provided in the packaging, but it would be nice to see in the product's description before buying.

Having said all of that, they do work well and for their intended purpose provided the straw is large enough, and again, the shipping was super fast!

title: Just okay
text:
This tin of brush soap arrived quickly. I use small brushes for egg tempera painting and, because I mix my own paints, I find that some pigments wash out easily while others need a bit more work to get the brush really clean. I found that, especially with small brushes, it was hard to get this soap to lather up at all. (In all fairness, when I purchased a similar product some years ago, it got better at this with repeated use.) However, my brushes do appear clean and are easy to reshape when I use the product. Hence, 4 stars because it does what it claims to do.

One star was lost because the tin was packaged in a completely unnecessary plastic container that cannot be recycled. I am concerned enough about the environment that I feel there should be consequences to such practices. The other issue is that I believe this product, like most of its type, is overpriced. Take a mild bar soap, cut a piece off, put it in that jar lid that you can't recycle, and you have a brush soap that works as well or better. You will save money and have kept the jar lid out of the landfill.

I appreciate the opportunity to try this product and review it. I know I'm opinionated about the environment and, if you need this type of product, I think this one does a fair enough job.

title: Conversational lamp
text:
My interest in the lamp stems from sleep issues, including circadian rhythm. I knew ahead of time that research indicates the amount of light put off by the Per2 lamp isn't likely to have a physical clinical effect. Compare this one with the lumens of their other lamps. But if use of the lamp can help me establish good sleep habits, routine awake/sleep time, then it will be worth the purchase.

Let me talk about what the lamp does. My misconception of how it was supposed to work, probably added to my frustration with programming the device. The programming can be tedious as mentioned in other reviews. A video would be great.

a) As a desktop lamp, it provides bright, adjustable light for reading. It also includes a digital clock.
b) As a dawn simulator, you program what time you want the light to come on. The light turns on and stays on for an hour or so, gradually increasing in brightness. Then it turns off. It doesn't stay on all day with the light automatically adjusting to the time of day. If you want it back on, you turn it on. Adjust it to the brightness level manually or use the autoshift feature discussed next. The dawn activation only has to be activated once. Going forward, it will begin the gradual brightness everyday at whatever time you set. If you get up at the same time every day, less programming..
c) You can have the lamp automatically adjust corresponding to the time of day. No programming is involved, like for the dawn, dusk and alarm settings. Turn the light on, then click a specific button to automatically shift between three discrete stages of light: dawn (5 am - 1 pm), daylight (1 pm - 9 pm), dusk (9 pm - 5 am). These stages are factory set, meaning you can't change them. An easy to use feature, but less flexible. As mentioned above, you can always adjust the brightness up and down manually.
d) As an alarm clock, you program the start time just like you do the dawn simulator. If the gradual brightness of the light does not wake you up, you have a fail safe with the alarm.
e) As a dusk simulator, you don't set what time the light will go off, you just program the activation. You can then start the dusk simulator any time you want. Once activated, the first click of the power button gradually dims the light off over a 30 minute period, until it is turned completely off. If for some reason, you want to turn the light off right away, press the power button a second time. You only have to activate the dusk simulator once. Going forward, whenever the light is on, the first click of the power button will start the 30 minute power down, the second click an immediate shut off.

You can tell when a feature is activated, because its symbol will continually blink. Good.

Since I often read and fall asleep with the light on, the dusk simulator with its automatic power off, is the most useful feature. If you are more interested in an adjustable reading lamp, which puts out similar types of light and has an auto shut off option, but not the dusk/dawn timings, I suggest another purchase I made [[ASIN:B00KSQ8ZNA LAMPAT Dimmable LED Desk Lamp, Black]].

text:
This ginger grater works well for both garlic and ginger. I use a lot of both in my cooking, and have kids in the kitchen who also like to use this product. First, it is STURDY. I actually tried to use this aggressively to see if I could get it to bend..and there was not a chance of that happening. This is is one of those kitchen tools that will last years. When grating garlic, we preferred the press and rock method. But sure you start with peeled garlic! I found that with ginger, it was best to grate it as opposed to pressing and rocking.

One thing I like a great deal about this product is that if you want your item to be chopped finer, you can just press and rock it a few more times...easy and really gets to what you want for your recipe. It is also really safe if you have kids helping you in your kitchen. Both my 9 and 12 year olds were able to use this with ease and found it fun. There are no truly sharp edges to cut any little fingers. This is simple, and no fuss..does what it should and appears built to last.

I would love to see some instructions added to this product. It is pretty straightforward, yes, but asking around, not many people in my region would know what this is or how to use it. I think instructions would be very helpful. This uses minimal packaging, which is a plus, but a short instruction sheet added would be great!

title: Absolutely amazing. I have my life back from itchy hives!
text:
Edited: November 6th, 2014 -- I replied to a comment today, so thought I would give quick update on how Daosin is working for me.

I still love this stuff!! I take it every day still and probably will until they figure out a way to fix the histamine intolerance permanently.

As I stated in original review I use a lot, I still do, but it works for me and I am worth it. My sanity is worth it. It does not work on food allergies, it works on histamine intolerance.

I'll state again, the best advice I can give is to check with your doctor first. They may not narrow it down immediately, but they can eliminate some things. I got lucky in that my doctor has the same problem and she told me to try this. I wouldn't have if she hadn't told me to.

-------------------------

Love this stuff! As I've gotten older, I've found that foods I have eaten all my life, are now causing problems. My problems were hives. Chocolate, tomatoes, bananas, peanut butter, hot dogs, parmesan cheese, and so much more. I didn't know what the heck was going on. I knew I had latex allergies, but these new problems had me stymied. I was at the doctor for an unrelated problem, and casually asked could I now be allergic to certain foods, because I had done some home testing because of hives I started getting. My doctor recommended Daosin to try, it was something she herself took for the same problem. Told me to read up on histomine intolerance. She takes 3 before bedtime, and it works for her. I tried that, didn't have great result. So, I tried per instructions on bottle. A little better, but still had problems. So I tested. For me, I have found taking 1 in the morning when I wake up, and then 1-2 each meal, depending on what I am eating (if tomato based- I always take 2), sometimes nothing. It's not cheap, but for me it is absolutely worth every penny. I got hives on a daily basis. I am ecstatic to say I have been hive free for 3 months now. It took me about a solid week and half to notice any difference. This seems to be a good balance for me. And if I want a Mountain Dew or to eat a handful of peanuts, or maybe grab a tomato just picked off the vine to snack on, I take an extra pill (they are actually capsules) and I am good to go. Absolutely, being able to eat the foods I want to is awesome. But I can do that by taking Benedryl (dye-free). The greatest difference is, with Daosin, I don't go to sleep. One Benedryl knocks me out. I am thrilled my doctor told me about Daosin, I just wish I had asked sooner, could have saved myself a couple of years of misery. As I said, it's not cheap, I go through anywhere between 2-3 bottles a month. But I am worth it and my sanity is worth it. No more hives, no more wanting to skin myself with my fingernails because of the itching. Amazing. I'll be honest, no way would I have even tried this if my Doctor hadn't recommended as well as told me she herself took it. Natural or not, I am biggest weanie when it comes to taking medicines, especially if I've never heard of it before. ;-) Talk to your doctor, get their advice. That's my tip before you try anything.

title: Life changer for this overwhelmed Mom
text: I have two kids a 3-year-old and an infant. I also have a husband that wants to talk to me while said children are yelling crying you know doing what kids do. I tend to get really overwhelmed with all the sound. Especially bad when I'm trying to cook or pay the bills or just think deeply about something. It's one of the things that makes me feel like a bad Mom. I blow up way too often just because of too much sound. When I saw these advertised on facebook I decided to get them even though I thought they were just overpriced ear plugs. I got them on sale and paid like $14 for them. They come with multiple different ear hole adapters (probably not the correct term). I've used the ear hole adapters for other things too like my bluetooth ear buds so that's a perk. As far as the sound reduction goes. One concern is I did need to be able to actually hear my children. As long as they're in the same room as me I can definitely still do that. I can also watch TV with them in with subtitles. It's hard to hold a conversation at times because when I'm talking all I can hear is my own voice. I definitely cannot eat while using these as the sound of my crunching drowns out everything else. I will definitely purchase these again if the time comes because they've definitely made me a calmer nicer mom. I only use them once or twice a day when I feel my blood boiling from the sound and it instantly makes me more at peace. I keep them pinned on my clothes at all times with a diaper pin. They come with a tiny pouch that I can slide a pin through the zipper.

title: . Small  for the tall( 5’11 and over . Sturdy, stable, lightweight and easy to use.
text:
I love my Elevens knee scooter I am an active 66 yr old woman. .Broke my foot. I am 5’8” 120 Lbs After a couple days using I found the highest placement of handle bar and seat about midway to be the most comfortable. If you are a very tall man this will be short for you. I started with both seat and handle too low and my back started hurting so hope this fixes that. Just make sure hips are Parallel when standing in place for a seat adjustment. Make sure your knee is completely rested on the seat or you will end up with it too low as I did to begin with. That said, It is lightweight, easy to maneuver, the front wheels are wide enough to be stable yet narrow enough to allow me to get through spaces other scooters would not. The break is nice for parking and being hand free in the kitchen. The basket is great for transporting items including drinks .It makes quite tight turns. It is easy to back up and turn through tight spots also. The seat is comfy. No seat cover needed. The instructions say you need nuts for basket placement. You won’t find any in the equipment but don’t freak out. You really don’t need them. Misprint! . The screws thread right through a plate and tighten nicely. There is only one break lever on the right hand side but it works fine even for a lefty like me.
Seems to be very sturdy.. well-built. To the woman who feel over the handle bars I have only two words... Slow down!!!

At the end of March 2021 it cost $2.79/1.5 oz.  so I thought it was a bargain over Aquaphor and Cerave (which is particularly THIN and requires a LOT or reapplication).  In fact, it does a MUCH longer lasting job than both Aquaphor and Cerave with much less product per application because it is a thicker consistency.  Ultimately this leads to less greasy mess where elasticized garment edges tend to hit - this is an important point because who likes to feel greasy, gooey, and in need of a bath?  A thinner application of this is much more healing and protective of these sensitive areas meaning I can go more days without ever applying it in the first place as my skin feels stronger from the active ingredients doing their job. title: A health drink that actually tastes good...make that DELICIOUS!
text:
Wow! I was stunned the first time I tried this energy shake. The most I hoped for was that it might taste half-way decent, but to my very pleasant surprise, it tasted wonderful! It was not a feat of iron-willpower at all to drink. I wasn't stopping to gag a little every few seconds, like I have with other health drinks. I think it tastes like an oatmeal cookie, but creamy, and when I looked at the can's label, the product was described as having a "creamy granola flavor", so I was pleased that the description was true to the product, unlike other shake powders that tout yumminess and taste like something you wouldn't feed your dog! In addition to delicious flavor, I find that it is very filling, which has been helpful to my dieting efforts, and it definitely boosts my energy. I have always struggled with getting an adequate workout, because I would tire too easily, but after drinking this energy shake, I can really push myself hard and burn significant calories - a first for me! Finally, I feel good about all the vitamins, minerals, and whole food concentrates I am getting with this product, especially since everything is all-natural.

I have used this shake powder with Dole's Peach-Orange-Mango juice, which is really good, but my favorite way to drink it is: 1 scoop energy shake powder; 8 oz. Odwalla Superfood drink; 8 oz. Mountain High all-natural yoghurt (vanilla or lemon); 1 banana. (Actually, this recipe makes enough for me to drink half, and refrigerate the rest for later.) This product mixes well with a blender or salad dressing shaker, but I don't recommend mixing it with a spoon (stays kind of clumpy). Also, I have never used more than 1 scoop in my drinks, and the flavor and consistency have been perfect for me (I think 2 scoops would be too much, but I think 2 scoops are recommended only if you will be mixing it with water, and not something thicker, like juice or milk).

Try this product - it is SO good! I will definitely be re-ordering it when I run out.

First and foremost, my hair is a little over 4 ft long, fine and straight. The curls shown in the photos that are voluptuous is definitely not from this product.

1. It doesn't warm up high enough to hold a perfect cirl
2. Definitely will not curl pass a few inch of hair before it gets scared and start beeping for a redo. As you can see in the customer photos, if its long hair, it doesnt hold a curl or its a tiny spiral. I did notice a photo of someone with short hair. That might work because its short.

I only decided to purchase the product because I want to work on my hair vquickly. If i use a regular wand or rod, it will take about 2 hours. Yes, my hair is that long. And straight. I am a beauticians favorite client if they charge by the hour to style.

This device? Probably would take me 4 hours to complete my whole head. Everytime it takes an inch of my strand, it stops and beeps.

Once it does that, it frizzes the end so if you try to redo without straightening the hair, youll continue to frizz out your hair. Just imagine a paperjam. More than likely, it wont straighten itself.

text: This is a great concept, it just doesn't deliver like you'd hope. It's not completely useless though. The problem is that the removable tips just don't get hot enough. If it was one solid piece rather than removable silicone tips I think the heat would transfer a lot better. Also, the entire thing is plastic versus metal heating elements on standard heated curlers. The plastic doesn't transmit heat well and doesn't retain it AT ALL. You spend so much time on one eye that it shuts off and gets cold before you can start on the other so you have to start all over and let it heat up again and even that takes way longer than with standard curlers. It's a good thing it's rechargeable too because you might get 3 uses before it has to be charged again, or at least it's that way for me because it has to go through multiple heat ups with each use so maybe someone else would get more uses. If this thing had the heat retention and distribution of a metal heating coil it would be nearly perfect. Adding a battery and temp display would make it 100%. All that said, I have straight, long lashes so I need a tool that is really going to curl. If you already have mildly curled lashes, or at least ones that don't point down (like mine) you might have better luck. It would probably work better on shorter lashes too. I really, really like the design of this curler, I just wish it worked better for me.

title: ... didn't have any issues with the softgels sticking together like other reviewers
text:
I didn't have any issues with the softgels sticking together like other reviewers. The pills look about identical to what I've bought at Walmart and Target in the past.

I'm docking two stars though because the product images are obviously computer renderings instead of photos of the actual product. The actual bottle is a thin, cheap feeling plastic with a white lid and a label sticker slapped on it.

Why is this a big deal? A few reasons:

1) Amazon doesn't allow renderings for product images. Companies are required to use REAL photos of their products. I don't like rule breakers.

2) I absolutely hate not getting exactly what I ordered. The product images show a premium looking vitamin bottle, something you'd feel comfortable giving to a health nut as a gift. Instead of getting that bottle, I got a junky bottle that is lower quality than the locally available store brands.

3) A vitamin is a vitamin. It is unlikely that Brand A is going to be substantially different than Brand B. The only things that make one vitamin product stand out from another are the price and the packaging. I can get vitamin D3 cheaper locally and in a better bottle.

This product was provided at a discounted price in exchange for my honest review.

text:
Preface, I haven't tried any other handsfree wireless pumps so I cannot compare to others. I need to have mammograms more frequently due to monitoring of a mass, but I'm also still lactating. These are far from discreet. I wasn't expecting them to be sleek or discreet, but they are BULKY. Also when washing them before use, you'll notice that you're not going to be able to get all your breastmilk out. I wasn't able to get every last drop of water out of the collection container. There's a flat part near the opening where the water collects and won't pour out. I know many value every last drop of breastmilk, so this could be an issue for many. May not be as big of an issue if the collection containers can double as a bottle, but that's not an option. How do you get every last drop of milk out? Is there a trick?

Anyhow, for this reason, and because I really meant to buy the ones that you can attach a wide mouth bottle to, I've returned them.

As for the when it's turned on, it's not quiet, but again, didn't expect it to be for the price. My Baby Buddha is also not quiet so the noise isn't an issue for me, but it may be for others who would like to pump more discreetly.

title: Good as a breastfeeding supplement
text:
I got this as a breastfeeding supplement, since the reason barley and oats are supposed to help is because they contain beta glucan, especially barley. I found it here in a concentrated form while looking for different ingredients to make lactation cookies. Buying this was ultimately easier and cheaper than buying the ingredients for lactation snacks.
This supplement, along with pumping a little extra here and there, more than doubled my milk supply. I went from barely pumping enough to feed my baby to pumping 16-20 ounces extra daily after about 10-14 days. Also, the milk I made began to look different, the fat rose to the surface when stored in the fridge but the color of the milk stayed the same, whereas now that I have not used this supplement for a week to see what would happen, my milk looks much clearer after the fat rises.
The reason I'm not giving this five stars is because of the texture. It wants to settle at the bottom of the glass, and it changes the consistency of everything. One person in the reviews mentioned putting it in their coffee- it sat at the bottom and made the consistency of the coffee itself very thick. I found it best in juice, after letting it sit for a minute it absorbed a lot of the juice and thickened to a smoothie texture. Would definitely be best in an actual smoothie, but as it stands I hate washing blenders.
Overall, it worked for what I wanted. Would recommend to mothers who want to boost the supply and quality of their milk.

These are okay to use in a pinch (when you have no paper towels) or maybe to clean with, but if you need them for anything food-related, they are a little too hairy. If they were more of a chamois texture, they'd be great, but they are absolutely hairy and fuzzy no matter how you handle them. Also, the tube they come on doesn't fit standard paper towel holders (nice and sturdy, but too skinny). Kind of annoying.

Pro tip: after washing, you can put them back on the roll by overlapping the sheets and rolling. I see people talking about how to store these and wonder why nobody thinks of that. Do it on a regular paper towel roll, though, if this one doesn't fit your holder.

Edit: I am upgrading my star rating on this since the seller reached out to apologize and offer a refund. They have also said that they will be updating the product info to make it clear that these are not intended for food use. Good customer service wins me over every time. I'm only doing 4 stars because I don't 100% love them, but the product is not all bad, and the customer service is great.
