The package had already been opened, and the gel part of the tablets didn't look like the original tablets (tablet on left is new, on right is old). The new tablets smell like a mix of weeds, vinegar, and and melted plastic. The old tablets smell like... lemon and clean soap. I haven't used the new ones yet, but I suspect they won't be as effective (or safe) as the old ones.

Perhaps this was a bad batch, or maybe they went bad because of the damaged package (can detergent even go bad?) But I am not impressed with this product. Other people have fantastic reviews and experiences with this product, so I don't know if it's maybe an issue with just this one batch, this one pack, the seller, or some other cosmic misfortune. I won't say "DON'T BUY THESE THEY'RE HORRIBLE BLARGH!!!!", but I will say be prepared for a potentially unpleasant experience.

text: I use sunblock 365 days a year or else my lips will blister around the edges from sunburns.  I've been using Z Blok for about a year, and I am very pleased with the sun protection.  The label claims "clear zinc," "fragrance free," "chemical free," and "SPF30."  My lips have never burned or blistered or reacted to the ingredients, so it works great for me.  Even though the label says it is clear zinc, it is actually an off-white color that goes on almost clear.  Sometimes my lips will look a little pale just after application and in that case I smack my lips together and slide them around a bit to evenly distribute the balm and then the product is clear.  The texture (or lip feel) of Z Block makes lips a tad too waxy and thus too tacky for my taste, so I apply a thin coat of Neosporin's Overnight Renewal Therapy over the Z Blok to achieve that perfectly hydrated, moist (but not shiny or slippery), wax-free lip feeling.  Typically, I just use this once a day, but if I'm outdoors for an extended period, I will reapply it just to make sure I won't burn...just as I would for SPF30 sunscreen. It's nice that it comes in a 3-pack so that you can keep them on hand wherever you are and it's nice that it is applied directly to the lips...you don't need to clean your finger before dipping it in a tiny tub of lip balm or wipe product out from under your fingernail. In sum, it is effective, convenient, and fairly priced.

title: Great traveling bag!  Maybe not for hiking in rainy areas...
text:
I'll be traveling to a couple of different states and a few towns, starting next week. I've been looking for a good travel bag to take with me. Since we'll be in a new town every week, I definitely did not want to lug around a large suitcase. Also, we didn't want to have to pay for sending our luggage beneath the plane each time we fly.

I'm really happy with the size and shape of this bag. Because it's a "barrel" bag, it fits a lot of items and/or clothes. I was specifically looking for a backpack or something that can convert. This was perfect! I doubt that I'll be using any of the other carrying methods, but it's nice to have options. Good front pocket on the outside of the bag for all of my cords and charges. The back and separating liner are padded and fit my 17" laptop and/or 10.1 tablet. There's another small inner pocket for maybe a phone, id, mouse or other small items such as those.

There are buckles that help cinch down "fluffy" things like clothes which will be a big help in not carrying a big bulky bag on your back!

This bag is a good size for travel but it will also hold all of my son's school books and other "junk" he just has to pack around with him.

The canvas is pliable and not stiff like a lot of canvas bags you find. It would make a great pillow while waiting at the airport for two hours! It's sewn really well and even if the back straps are not very padded, they are padded enough to be comfortable.

Being that I live in a state that rains constantly, I don't think I'd use this bag for hiking. The canvas would get soaked through since it's not lined with waterproof fabric. Otherwise, this bag is perfect for my travels!

I think this is a great bag and a good size for what I intend it for. If you're looking for a good travel bag or night out bag, this would be a great choice!

title: Highly recommended. Slightly larger than a pen, but very convenient
text:
I bought this product for myself in the hopes that it would make traveling simpler for me, and I am very pleased with the outcome.
This product is simple and does what it claims. Loading toothpaste is easy (all you do is rotate the bottom to fill the syringe inside) and the fact that it dispenses from the center of the brush is pretty nifty in my opinion. It's larger than your average pen, but it does have a clip that helps keep it in place in your jacket. Most of all, everything you need is in one hand, so it's easy to keep track of.
I often end up brushing my teeth in bathrooms when I travel, and I hated putting anything other than the water I bring on those dirty counters. I'll wash my hands, but when it comes to brushing my teeth, I'm just there to spit in the sink and use the mirrors. With this, I never have to put my toothbrush/toothpaste on those wet, dirty counters because it's in one hand. On top of that, it's much simpler to just take out of my jacket than somewhere in my bag when I have luggage.

title: It does a great job and so far as been a much better ...
text:
This is the first hair straightener brush I've ever purchased and I was pleasantly surprised! It does a great job and so far as been a much better experience than a traditional flat iron. First of all it's really difficult to burn yourself since the heating elements are behind the combs of the brush. Second of all I don't have to stand in front of a mirror to straighten my hair any more. Since it's almost as easy as brushing your hair, sometimes I'll throw on a TV show and before I know it my hair is nice and straight! The brush also comes with a couple large hair clips that make it super easy to separate hair into sections and a storage bag that keeps the cord from getting in the way when I'm not using it.

The only negative I have is that the way the buttons are placed, it's easy to turn the straightener off while you're using it. Just need to keep an eye on it so it doesn't turn off without you realizing it!

title: A very good brush for a while.
text:
I’ve had to edit my review. I liked this brush, but after using it for a year it has started to shed its hair drastically. I have to clean hairs out of my shaving soap or mug after every use. It is shedding more than my old Everready brush that I used for years before I started electric shaving. I guess for the price, a year’s use isn’t bad, but I’ve reduced my rating from 5 stars to 3. Going to try a more expensive brush,

I guess. Over many years I've shaved with double edge blade, straight razor, rotating electric, reciprocating electric, the current crop of multi blade razors. I've shaved dry and wet, in the shower and out. I've used brush and soap, various canned or tubed lathers and creams and gels. And for years I wore a full face beard so I didn't have to shave so much.

Recently, exploring razor reviews, I decided to go back to shaving with a double edged razor with soap and lather. I couldn't find my last DE razor. Although I found my granddad's straight razor I used to shave with, I don't have the strop anymore.

I bought a brand new Mercur DE razor and a bunch of blades. I found my Old Spice shaving mug and my old Ever Ready shaving brush. Using some Castile soap, I had the best shave I've had in years.

Alas, my 60 year old Ever Ready brush started shedding badly. Back to Amazon to study shaving brushes.

I settled on the Latherwhip Badger Hair shaving brush. I liked the reviews and the personal responses of the manufacturer to questions. As soon as I ordered the brush, I got email with advice on breaking in the brush, and using it. I think I'm too old to take any advice on how to use it, but I appreciate the thought. And I'm too impatient to take advice on breaking it in.

Actually, the brush arrived in a soft enough condition to use immediately and there was no odor at all. I proceeded to lather up with it, out of the box.

I've been using it for about a week now. It is very nice, and makes a great lather. There has been no shedding of the long bristles, but a couple of half length bristles came out on the second or third day.

I like this brush, a very good brush for a reasonable price.

text:
I bought the first one for my wife-to-be because she said she was having trouble sleeping and the fan helped. Bingo! This simple device is in constant use and I, too, like the effect.

My mother has had trouble sleeping for years. She would use the TV to put her to sleep (which I could never understand). She was up at all hours and she never got a good night's sleep. So I bought the second one and had it shipped to her. Bingo! She's now sleeping better than ever. In fact, she recently told me that she forgot to turn it on the other night and still slept well. (I have to believe that's because she is sleeping regularly now.)

If you have trouble sleeping for whatever reason, this seems to do the trick. $40 is a small price to pay for a consistent and good night's sleep.

Hint: since the device should be across the room, I also got an extension cord that has a switch that extends off of it (it's like a T configuration) so my wife can turn it on and off from the bedside.

Update: we just had our first baby four months ago. I immediately got another one for the baby's room. Seems to help her fall and stay asleep. (She's been a good sleeper from the beginning, though, so I can't say it is some miracle cure for babies that don't sleep well.)

text:
We love this. 13-yr old son's acne was out of control, retin-a products were drying him out and weren't helping, ProActive and Acne.org products also didn't help.

I'm a 30-something mom who also has acne from time to time, resulting in temporary acne scarring.

This stuff is great. Here's what we've been doing:

Once per week, we each do a Lactic Acid 70% peel for a minute or two.

Each night (except the Lactic Acid night) we cleanse and then swipe with this skin prep toner.

Then we use the 100% pure Hyaluronic acid, once that soaks in we top it with a few drops of 100% pure Moroccan Argan oil.

We use an extraction tool a few nights week to help dislodge the clogs that are ready to come out (and they are purging quickly, he had some of the biggest, most stubborn blackheads and petrified waxy whiteheads I'd ever seen) and they are little by little all coming out of his face without trauma, bleeding, or scarring.

Honestly, he looks great (and since I'm doing it too, it's helping me, too) and I'm so happy for him that his acne is getting under control.

title: Great Product and Service, Just a Slow Delivery Time
text: I needed to find a way to refill fountain pen cartridges as the converter was hard-to-find or was not available. This was well described and seemed to be a good workaround for what I needed. The delivery was slow, (about 7 days) even though it is an Amazon Prime product, hence losing 1 start point. However, when I received it I couldn't wait to try it out! There are three components to each syringe: the ink reservoir, the needle and the plastic connector. Note: The narrow end of the connector is inserted into the needle. Once done, you can press down on the syringe's piston and then place the tip of the needle into a bottle of fresh fountain pen ink (I use special one that does not clog the pen tip); gently release the spring  of the piston and you get a full chamber of ink. From there you can insert the tip of the syringe into your empty cartrige, fill it up by pressing down on the piston. I then got a piece of paper towel just the clean up a bit,  inserted the now full cartridge into the pen, connect everything back up again, and it writes perfectly, without any spillage! It's really amazing and a great way to be able to use your favourite ink colours where an ink converter is not available.

title: Something works, I woke up pain-free for the first time in over a year
text:
Got a free pair of the low intensity rings (not neodymium) over 10 years ago. I was pretty sure he was a scam artist, but just wanted to get my free rings. When they didn't arrive quickly, I fired off an email to him complaining. To my surprise, the rings really did come a little while later after a nice apology from Alex.

I didn't notice much out of the free rings, but I did notice a little something and since he had instructions on how to build your OWN rings right on his website, I decided to do a little test. Still skeptical and not wanting to give a scammer any of my money, I found a website which sold neodymium magnets in the range his website suggested and created 2 rings according to his instructions, with a compass to determine which side should face up. Once I had it all figured out, I wrote a big R on one ring to indicate it should be worn on my Right pinky and an L on the other to indicate it should be worn on the left just to make sure I always wore the rings correctly.

I wore the rings a couple times back then but noticed they gave me really bizarre energy spikes and seemed to almost give me anxiety or something. I was in my late 20s or early 30s and I was just worried they were doing something unhealthy, so I stopped using them and wrote Alex off as a quack.

Fast forward to last night. I am now almost 42 and I have had increasing pains in my legs, joints and especially problems with my feet. It's really weird when you start developing pain for apparently no reason. I have to make an appointment with the doctor soon, but at first I attributed the pains to low magnesium, ill-fitting shoes, and straining my body with starting a new yoga and walking routine too forcefully. However, the more time that has gone by (over a year now), I began to suspect it's some underlying health issue, which is why I need to see the doctor for a complete checkup again.

For the past year, I have had what I believe is plantar fasciitis. The yoga helped for over a year until I sprained my big toe and had to stop. Still, when I would wake up in the morning, my heel and hamstring were tight and sore and required stretching, which is the basic symptom of plantar fasciitis. The bottoms of my feet begin to hurt if I stand too long or walk too much. My ankles and knees also hurt if I exert myself too much running. My lower back often is a bit sore because I have swayback and if I do not do abdominal exercise regularly, it starts to LOOK like swayback and also gets sore. Again, the yoga greatly fixed this problem: I had a straighter stance without belly tipping forward and butt sticking out (makes you look 20 pounds lighter and about 2 inches taller) and this also meant I had no pain in my lower back, not even if I slept too long on a bad mattress. Yoga was the answer to most of my prayers until I had to stop doing it. I am very much looking forward to the day my toe heals up so I can begin again!

ANYWAY, with all these pains increasing and not being able to do yoga or run, I bought night splints to stretch out my feet while I sleep so that hopefully my plantar fasciitis will be healed eventually. And I bought several supplements which I have been taking for over 6 months now trying to address any deficiencies which may be the cause of this apparent degeneration. Nothing has really helped much as far as I can tell.

LAST NIGHT, on a whim, I got up from the couch and found my homemade "Alex Chiu" neodymium rings and put them on before I went to sleep. I did not put on my night splint for plantar fasciitis. I woke up today with no pain in my feet or back and feeling well-rested after just 5 hours of sleep. I went back to bed for another 3 hours, which borders on too much sleep for me (especially after doing nothing but lay on the couch the previous evening) and still woke up with no lower back pain.

I have no idea what the rings did, but it is obvious they did something. My guess is they improved circulation which may have in turn moved something carried in the blood that may settle in the extremities of legs and feet, but that doesn't explain why my lower back doesn't hurt.

I can honestly say that I wish I had worn these rings when I first made them now. I will definitely be wearing them every night for the foreseeable future and if anything interesting happens, I will update this review.

These are homemade rings, but if I feel they really start to improve my health, I might just buy the very expensive (and most powerful) foot bar magnets as a way to say thank you to Alex. He certainly has received a lot of negative attention for his website and I was one of the people who made fun of the site back then, too. I got a free pair of rings from him, learned how to make my own, and never gave him a penny or even thanked him. Instead, I continued to joke about the website with people online until I forgot about it. Now I feel like a complete jerk because there is no way my pain-free body is a result of anything but these rings. I have woken up daily with these pains for over a year now, there is simply not a day that I get out of bed and don't stumble immediately to the wall to stretch out my hamstrings due to pain. Today I did not. Last night I wore the rings. End of story.

title: Super easy set up and well worth it!
text:
I love this scale. I know it is expensive, but I figure if it helps keep me motivated then it is worth it! I first bought the Fitbit HR after decided that I would commit to losing weight. It was the motivation I needed. For some reason when I spend my hard earned money on something I really try a lot harder. I set a goal. I told myself If I lost 15 pounds I would buy new jeans...20 and I would buy the scale. I have lost 40 pounds now. so for me this has been really helpful along with the apps I use and eating better.

I read that people had problem setting it up so I was a bit worried about that, but I literally turned it on, opened the app and with 3 steps it was done. It took me maybe 5 minutes. I am not sure why others had problems, my just did everything to set itself up with very little effort from me. I turned it on and hooked it to my wireless..and wallah, synced and ready to use. That was it! I will admit that the body fat % may not be the most accurate out there, I have had mine measured and this was 4 percent off. I don't really care about that. I step on and it loads to my dashboard and my Lose it app in a flash. If you use fit1bit everyday it is awesome. If you use Lose it ( TRY the app is SO helpful!) you will love the step on and instantly logged feature. Sure I could write it down and then log it. But I know myself, and seeing it up on my dashboard daily is real motivation for me and I don't forget to do it! The scale is very accurate for weight. I can step off and on 3 times in a row and it will say the same thing. I don't know about you but my other scale was always a "Lets do it 3 times" scale. It was really annoying! It is nice to have it accurate and consistent!
So, for what it is worth, I wanted to write this review so you could read another opinion. I would buy this again and I recommend it if you are looking for a new fit bit product to add, a wireless scale that is accuarate or motivation to keep you going.

Best to have a battery tester on hand if you use these in combination, because if the toy/appliance dies after you put in all 'new' ones, it's probably just one or two of the batteries. Since then, I tried switching to a different seller (batteries that come in original blister packs), and my Arlos now last for about 4 months, so much longer! So it's pretty clear that these batteries are not new ones. Unless you enjoy swapping out batteries a lot, I would avoid these.

title: Too firm for me
text:
I would just like to start out saying that Purple's customer service has been amazing! Jeni specifically was the representative that helped me and she was very attentive and responsive to my concerns. I ended up keeping the double cushion and it came with some splitting so she quickly sent me a replacement!

I purchased the Double cushion, Ultimate, and Royal cushion to all try out. I am around 125lbs and petite, so unfortunately I found the ultimate and royal cushion too firm for me, both felt like i was sitting on a wooden chair. For the double cushion, it was the only one that made me feel a difference! It is plush and actually DID something. I am using it on a office chair handed down to me that has lost its cushioning so it was like sitting on cement, I needed something to hold me over before i can buy another office chair, and for me the double cushion sufficed. Now it didnt change my life and take away the pain completely, as I unfortunately still feel pain in my lower back/tailbone (but that could also be because of no lumbar support from my office chair so i don't want to put the blame completely on the cushion) and after 30 minutes to an hour of sitting i do have to reposition myself or stand up from my chair as I still do feel pain. That being said, it is usually recommended to get up and move around every 20 minutes or so of sitting so with that in mind it may actually be helping me! Using the cushion with an office chair that has more cushioning than my current chair may improve its efficacy though. Our bodies are all so different, and there are a lot of factors to consider when it comes to cushions/comfortably so this may be comfier for you than it was for me or it may do nothing, so I would suggest trying it and then deciding! Hope this helps!

title: Comfiest I've found
text:
I would just like to start out saying that Purple's customer service has been amazing! Jeni specifically was the representative that helped me and she was very attentive and responsive to my concerns. When the cushion arrived there seemed to be a few splitting marks at the edge of each side and when I showed photos she went ahead and sent me a replacement. I also did not need to go through the hassle of returning the defective one.

I've used this cushion now for about two months and I've tested two other cushions from amazon (knock off's) as well as the ultimate and royal cushion from Purple, both of which weren't for me since they were extremely too firm. I am around 125lbs and petite, so unfortunately they both felt like i was sitting on a wooden chair. The knock off's were extremely thin and it was like i was using nothing so i returned those as well (learned that not all gel cushions are made the same). For the double cushion, it was the only one that made me feel a difference! It is plush and actually DID something. I am using it on a office chair handed down to me that has lost its cushioning so it was like sitting on cement, I needed something to hold me over before i can buy another office chair, and for me the double cushion sufficed. Now it didnt change my life and take away the pain completely, as I unfortunately still feel pain in my lower back/tailbone (but that could also be because of no lumbar support from my office chair so i don't want to put the blame completely on the cushion) and after 30 minutes to an hour of sitting i do have to reposition myself or stand up from my chair as I still do feel pain. That being said, it is usually recommended to get up and move around every 20 minutes or so of sitting so with that in mind it may actually be helping me! Using the cushion with an office chair that has more cushioning than my current chair may improve its efficacy though. I am using the smaller waffle side up and the larger side down, I believe they state for harder surfaces you should be using the smaller squares on the bottom but i felt more cushion with it facing upwards. Our bodies are all so different, so this may be comfier for you than it was for me or it may do nothing, so I would suggest trying it and then deciding! Hope this helps!

title: Very overpriced, but it provides solid protection and survives the test of time
text:
Tanita scales are super accurate for measuring weight. They also are expensive, at least Tanita is. I have owned a Tanita scale for about 5 years I believe, and I needed to order another one. I laughed, but found that scale prices haven't dropped one bit. I figured over time this would get cheaper. Nope!

What does this rant have to do with this case? Well this case also hasn't lost any value, and is ridiculously over priced. But when you buy a $400+ scale, you don't want to damage it during transport. And these scales are quite heavy and very sensitive.

So they got you by the short and curlies. I will say that my scale has survived the test of time and has continued to be accurate throughout the year. I use it for myself and my athletes for MMA, kickboxing, and grappling weigh-ins, so even a .2 of a pound accuracy is vital.

I attribute that survival primarily to the case. It is rock solid on the outside, and inside is well padded. Even after 5 years, everything has held together, mostly. The padding is started to give-in a bit too much, but it hasn't effected it's protection yet.

So yes it is a quality carry case for the scale, but way over priced. If you have handy man like skills, I would recommend you measure out the scale and make your own. If you don't, or can't be bothered to do this yourself, find someone to do it for you. And if you have no such person in your life, then bite the bullet and get this overpriced case. You will feel stupid paying so much for a plastic case, but you won't have to worry about damaging your scale.

M

title: Love this
text:
I've had a BioBrite for about 6 years now, and it is finally giving up it's last breath (clock completely blacks out occasionally, and the light flickers.) Anyway, I'm in the market for a new one and have been reading the reviews. This model does take up a lot of real estate, something I've never liked. The buttons/functions are a bit difficult to figure out the first couple of times you use it, but really, just read the directions, it's not that hard. My current model does not have nature sounds or white noise -- it makes a soft ticking noise as the audible alarm. It can be set to either 15 or 30 min to reach full brightness, I like 30, but that drives my husband nuts, so I use the 15. The sunset/dusk feature is nice too, but I usually just leave it bright while reading before bed.

With that said, my recommendation is for anyone who has a hatred for waking up and feels like destroying their regular alarm clock in an extremely violent manner when that awful noise goes off (that's me), using a sunrise light is a much more relaxed, peaceful, calming way to wake up in the morning! I can't imagine that it's healthy to wake up startled and angry everyday, and this peaceful method is so worth it. I will never go back to another type of alarm, and have recommended these to many people.

title: Great for Sensitive Skin!
text:
My SIL has been telling me for over a year that I have to try the Konjac sponge. Recently, the opportunity came up to purchase this one for a discounted price in exchange for an honest review and I jumped at the opportunity. I had just gotten over being sick which had left my skin in terrible shape, sensitive and broken out, and I thought it would be a great chance to really see what the Konjac could do. I used it exclusively, without additional cleansers, twice a day for one week and overall I'm happy with it. The packaging says this sponge can be used on face and body but I only used it on my face. I would get a second sponge to use on my body if I wanted to use it for both and I'm planning to do that.

PROS:
--It's super soft, gentle doesn't even begin to describe how soft this is on the skin. It's even gentle enough to use on the sensitive skin right around the eyes.
--It's easy! The instructions are simple and you don't even need to use any additional cleansers (but you can use your favorite cleanser if you want to).
--It comes with a built-in hanging string so you can hang it up and allow it to dry well in between uses.
--It's the perfect size for face or body and fits well in your hand; not too big so that it's awkward and not too small so you can't get a good grip on it.
--It does not irritate sensitive skin. (Yes, I would know!)
--Is not drying.

CONS:
--By day 3 and 4, I felt like I needed a bit more exfoliation in typical areas such as around the chin and nose. (I usually use a linen cloth with a gentle cleanser and that does the job well). I felt like the Konjac needed a bit more if it were going to the sole product for cleansing.

When the week was up, my face had really settled down and was much improved with a decrease in redness. Success! I'm going to keep it in the rotation with my other products but I won't continue using it exclusively. My next step is to use it with my regular cleansing products and see how that goes. I'll also continue to use it at times when my ultra-sensitive skin needs a break from products or medications.

title: Good Roadside Emergency Bag
text:
First let me manage your expectations... This is not a professional quality bag. If you are purchasing for an EMS/LE/rescue agency, I have no idea why you are looking on Amazon. If you aren't, you probably don't need a super high-speed bag anyways.

This bag is able to fit everything you need to render first aid or BLS care while waiting for an ambulance to arrive. The internal adjustable dividers were extremely useful and seem like they will hold up very well. The bag seems fairly sturdy and will probably tolerate light to moderate use.

The downside is that, while the construction is generally okay, they skipped on the shoulder strap. It has cheap metal hardware that makes it not well suited for regular use. Additionally, the cheap zippers are attached with single stitching, which will rip with repeated stress.

The bag looks pretty good and is definitely functional as an emergency kit for the trunk, but as I mentioned previously, it's not a professional grade item. That being said, the size is perfect and it will serve it's purpose, so overall I am happy with the purchase and would recommend it to others.

title: No more policeman's heel!
text:
My BFF was diagnosed with plantar fasciitis, aka policeman's heel. Plantar fasciitis is one of the most common causes of heel pain. It causes pain and inflammation that runs across the bottom of your foot and connects your heel bone to your toes. It's aggravated by long periods of standing or after getting up from a seated position. It is also common in runners and overweight people.

My BFF is a runner, part-time photographer that walks around A LOT, in addition to working at a desk job. He complained of constant heel pain while we went out on our runs. So as a BFF, I did some research and find several foot compresses that help alleviate the pain caused by plantar fasciitis. I came across the Plantar Fasciitis Therapy Wrap by Neo Compress and was impressed by the description online. I immediately ordered them so he could give them a try.

Upon receiving them, I noted they looked very small out of the packaging. I was concerned they may not fit him. However, they stretch to fit. He immediately tried them on and kept them on throughout the day. He even went on a run using them.

According to my BFF, the Plantar Fasciitis Therapy Wrap by Neo Compress felt really nice on the feet. They were easy to put on and comfortable. They have a perfect amount of tightness while providing tons of support. The material feels breathable. He really liked that his toes were open. He said his feet don't get hot because his toes aren't covered up. He pretty much forgot he had them on.

His feet do not swell like they used to and don't feel achy. They helped keep the arch supported reducing the pain on his feet. The nice thing about these compression sleeves is that they can be worn alone while at home or under socks while running or just out and about.

Benefits of wearing the Plantar Fasciitis Therapy Wrap by Neo Compress:
* Alleviates foot pain, while providing ankle and heel arch support
* Provides the perfect level of support to every region of the foot
* Offers sturdiness and stability to your foot with a snug fit, while still allowing for full range of motion.
* Improves flexibility and endurance for runners and athletes
* Promotes quicker muscle recovery, better oxygen circulation helps reduce lactic acid build up.
* With shock absorbent support, these heel protection prevents heel spurs and plantar fasciitis.
* Comfortable design, providing open toes to keep sweat away and feet dry and cool
* Versatile, can be worn alone or under socks
* Breathable, produced with anti bacterial material to reduce odor and itch
* Machine washable
* Great value

The compression foot sleeves seem to be made from good quality material and appear to be durable.

Although I received these Plantar Fasciitis Therapy Wrap by Neo Compress at a discounted rate in exchange for an unbiased honest review, this doesn't affect my five star rating for it. I rely heavily on reviews before buying products so I personally like to be honest when reviewing items myself! Given the review provided by my BFF, I would recommend it to family and friends. My BFF also gives it two FEET up!!! ;)

If at any time I find the product does not live up to the initial review, I will update my review to reflect my findings.

title: Great choice! Comfy, clean, environmentally conscious.
text:
I love the smalls. Originally I ordered the small and the large because I figured I needed medium but those were the sizes that had prime shipping so I figured what did I have to lose. When I received them I immediately returned the large because they were too big for me, personally (likely wouldn't even fit in my underwear) and I found the smalls to be roughly the same size as the Always Radiant flex foam pads I was using prior. I washed them without fabric softener and dried them on low. Used them for my period without any leaking and they were extremely comfortable, so I decided to just order another package of smalls instead of bothering with mediums because the smalls seemed perfect. I received mediums instead :/ I'm gonna keep them on the off chance I have an unusually (more so) heavy period than usual, but REALLY wish I had received the smalls I ordered. **I said that I'd keep the mediums, then tried to place the pad in clean underwear (to make sure it would fit properly before I ever needed it) and it was too big. It bunched the underwear up and seemed like it would slide around, I will actually be returning them.**
Overall I'm loving the switch to reusable cloth pads, super comfortable, feel dry like soft underwear (not like sitting in a pad/diaper), no smells (didn't have any before but I guess worth mentioning?), not irritating (I was beginning to get irritation from disposables), easy to wash, discreet, and you can personalize your pads for your personality if you want. You will likely want to purchase a wet/dry bag (like one for cloth diapers) for your purse/bag/backpack for when you need to change a pad in public. I found a cute 3 pack (various sizes) of Jack skellington that have 2 pockets, works for my pads, swimming, gym cloths if you get super sweaty etc, but this way your pads stay separate from everything else in your bag.

title: Requires more skill than it should
text:
The big question, does it work? Yes, it does the job. Question #2, is it easy? On that I would have to say not initially, this tool will require a little practice, you need to develop a sense of “touch” to use this one to its full potential, though not nearly the level of skill needed to use a 3-corner file.
The file’s shank is round, so it is easy to let the tool roll side to side on the fret. The previous model had a squared shank that gave a better sense of the correct orientation, when the flat side of the shank is is flat and level, the file groove will be properly oriented on the fret. With this file, you have to feel for the proper orientation.
The wide groove can be used to flatten a single tall fret, or 3 or 4, much more than that you will want the leveling beam. To level a fret takes a bit of pressure, but to actually crown the fret, you need to use a lighter touch. Overpressure will definitely chew up the frets a bit.
I would like to see Baroque go back to the initial design, squared shank, fractionally deeper grooves, and milled safe edges on all the corners. If I could get that tool for the same price, I would order one today. At $28, I would consider looking around for other alternatives.

I have gone through more custom-made orthotics than I want to admit to, but none of them were as good as these right out of the box. I have plantar fasciitis and the heel cradle definitely hits my foot in the right place to help with the heel pain. The instep height seems perfect. And the inserts do not pick up foot or shoe smells so I've never been tempted to toss a pair for that reason. (They can be spot cleaned but are not recommended to be immersed in water.)

Best part, to me, you can slip them right into your shoes and start walking. There's not a horrendously long break-in time. Just a few hours a day for the first few days, and then full-time. As far as I was concerned, I forgot I even had them in the shoes after the second day. Although if you're not used to having orthotics at all, I suppose it might take longer.

title: What makes it worse is our lifestyle
text:
I weightlift 5 days a week and do cardio as well so for me trigger point been a constant battle for me. Tbh, when you lift you are going to contract your muscle and you need to release it. Looking around the gym you will see plenty of guys with same issues. What makes it worse is our lifestyle, i.e sitting in the car, lying in bed, long office hours makes it even tighter. So I have been through deep tissue massage therapy, dry needling etc. temporary relief only.
What's working for me now is I do I do about 10 mins of trigger point therapy daily now before workouts using foam rollers and backnobber. along with 10 mins of stretching the fascia. For the backnobber, you need to apply pressure on the trigger points, hold it there without moving for 15-20 secs and move on to another trigger point, very simple really. Also, it would help if you add a hot/cold shower therapy, sauna. It's just a routine for me now that I'm used to it.

title: Great addition to my other fitness technology.
text:
I already had a Fitbit Flex so I wanted to just add to my fitness stuff. I'm the kind of person where the more money I spend on something, the more serious I take it. I wouldn't want to waste money on something expensive, so even though this is a glorified scale, I get a lot of use out of it. I'm currently trying to track my food intake with My Fitness Pal, and my exercise and whatnot with my Flex, and now this is helping me identify my weight and body fat %. I find it best to weigh myself at the same time every day. I usually weigh myself right after I wake up and then sometimes I'll weight myself in the afternoon or night as well. The afternoon or night weight is always higher, and the body fat % varies. I haven't done enough research to know why the body fat % fluctuates more than the weight, but it's not more than 1 or 2 numbers of difference.

Connecting the scale was actually easy for me. I was concerned after reading other reviews, but I had not problems with the initial connection steps. The only issue I did find was that it was logging my weight as a "Guest." All I needed to do was google "Fitbit Aria logging my weight as guest" and I found a solution. Basically I would manually mark the weight as mine online and then it told me to weigh myself like 3 or 4 more times and that should set it well enough to read me. That solution worked perfectly.

title: Affordable ultraviolet air purification for small spaces.
text:
I used to get these from Lowes until they stopped carrying them in store. Luckily, you can get them direct from the manufacturer through Amazon now. They are perfect for small spaces such as apartments, offices, classrooms etc. My wife uses one in her grade school classroom and we have two at home in our two bedroom apartment. They take up zero floor space so that makes them better than most air purifiers right there. You do want to avoid putting anything directly in front of it though, as you want good air flow going to it. You can swivel the plug-in so that it can be plugged in upright as shown in the pictures or upside down. It works equally well in either position and its handy for when there is something above the plug-in preventing you from plugging it in right side up. Also, if you have plug-ins that are getting worn out and heavier things won't stay plugged into them, I've found that plugging it in upside down helps it say plugged in better.

It does make a bit of noise due to the impeller fan inside the unit. This noise is very quiet when you first get it, but gets louder and more high pitched when the unit is about to quit working. But, usually, you can make it work again by buying just the inside bulb from the manufacturer's website and replacing that part. You can tell when it is about to go out also by the light on the front. It is usually blue but sometimes turns orange when it needs a new bulb. The bulbs last for 12 months to two years, sometimes even three depending on how much you keep it plugged in and on how dirty your air is. The unit uses about 6 watts per hour so it's pretty energy efficient.

It seems to really help, especially with airborne mold. I've had farmers lung or lung infections before I started using air purifiers like this so I tend to be rather sensitive to mold. Now that I'm using these, I've noticed that I have far less trouble with mold in my lungs. It also helps get rid of that musty smell that some places have (which is due to mold). My wife's classroom used to smell musty and she and the kids would have the sniffles often, even when they didn't have the flu but not anymore now that she's got one of these in her room.

As for odor reduction, I can't say that it really does a lot. It kind of depends on how strong the odor is and whether the thing that is producing the odor is still present after a while. If something makes a strong odor but is then removed, it does seem to make the smell go away sooner. If the item that is making the odor stays in the room, these things can't keep up with it. It doesn't release any smells of its own, so it won't mask the bad odor with anything like an air freshener does. If you do use air fresheners though, I recommend keeping the air freshener and this Germ Guardian as far apart as you can because I'd imagine that making the Germ Guardian try to clean the particles of air freshener chemical out of the air will wear the Germ Guardian out faster.

The best part is that it uses blue light technology to kill mold and germs with ultraviolet light rather than ozone production. Air purifiers that use ozone production actually wind up contributing to indoor air pollution and can make you just as sick as the stuff you are trying to clean out of the air. I've tried ozone producing air purifiers in the past, and they gave me terrible headaches. I don't have that problem with the Germ Guardian.

If you notice in a lot of restaurants and hospitals, this UV light technology is used there as well. With the Germ Guardian, the fan draws air towards the bottom of the unit, flows it past the UV light and back out the top of the unit. Though it makes the unit make a little noise, it's better than the passive UV filters since it processes the air in the room more efficiently and takes less time to clean the air column in the room. If you use it in conjunction with a fan (either on the ceiling or floor) it can work even faster, especially if it is a floor fan and you can blow the room's air towards the unit. This is especially helpful in rooms that are approaching the upper limit of the unit's capacity which I think is something like 50 - 70 square feet.

title: Researched: The Best Seat Cushion tech on the market
text:
I am a recent college graduate, and now full-time Web Designer in a large corporate environment. My job requires that I sit from 8:30am - 5pm everyday creating website mock-ups and coding them.

Though I have been provided with a pretty ergonomically-sound office chair, I wanted my sitting experience augmented without replacing the chair itself.

After conducting a couple hours of research, I concluded the Wondergel Extreme cushion was the best option on the market.

What makes the Wondergel Extreme worth it:

1) It really does make sitting for extended amounts of time more doable. I can sit the entire day, and only have to get up for bathroom breaks and lunch.

2) It won't cave in permanently from use like memory foam, or pop like air cushions.

3) The sleeve that comes with this cushion makes it that much easier to transport the cushion.

4) The gripping texture on the bottom of the sleeve actually does keep the cushion in place (doesn't slide around).

From my research, this type of cushion made the most sense logically.

I say go ahead and purchase this product!

text:

title: They work, but are too small and painful for me
text:
Yes, you will look ridiculous wearing these. However, if you suffer from severe motion sickness/vertigo, you won't mind.

I've been hospitalized more than once due to vertigo. Of course, motion sickness is a common occurrence for me as well. I used to be a gamer, but now looking at a moving screen makes me instantly sick.

After my last hospitalization, I purchased these. They help with working on a computer when scrolling, and help significantly when looking at my phone. They aren't a miracle cure, the motion sickness doesn't go away, but it lessens it more effectively than OTC medication.

Unfortunately, they seem to be designed for someone with a much smaller head than I. I wear XL size baseball hats, and these glasses don't reach from my ears to my nose without stretching. The part of the glasses that sit on my nose has ZERO padding, it is hard, pointed plastic. As a result, it becomes painful after 10+ minutes of wearing. It leaves deep, painful imprints. A soft rubber coating or longer temple/earpieces would improve this product significantly. I'm currently trying out a few ideas to see if I can fix it myself.

title: Heat is too weak to matter
text:
Quick Review:

Wearing these gloves set to high is equal to wearing unheated gloves from the discount bin at Target. The gloves are thick and make using anything such as turn signals or keys too difficult.

Long Review:

I hooked these gloves up to my Anker 26800mAh power bank I tested these gloves on a cool night on a motorcycle. I set them to high for 10 minutes before trying them out. These gloves only warmed up to 82 degrees when the room temperature was 75 degrees. Yes, I used a thermometer to measure the warmth after closing off the open end and pressing both sides of the glove against the thermometer. My infrared thermometer, which I used to double check, read 81.

I then wore them on my motorcycle, at which time the 50 degree temperature outside sapped the heat immediately. Wearing glove liners with a decent glove provides significantly more warmth. These will be useless in Chicago during the winter.

My Volt 12V heated gloves heat up to the point that keeping them on high had led to a mild burn. I wear them with no issues at -20 degrees, going 80+ mph.

title: Lightweight and runs large - REVIEW UPDATED
text:
UPDATE: I wore this belt for 3 weeks to support a broken rib. I was on a vacation with long airplane flights, carried backpacks, and walked miles daily. The belt helped to support my rib and back. I had to wrap the belt tight occasionally and that necessitated the Velcro being attached directly to the belt fabric, not the other Velcro tab. I was worried that this would shred the fabric but it did not! it was nice to be able to adjust the tightness of the belt easily. I was hesitant to buy this because of the negative reviews but it has been a great little rib belt. And it is still elastic and in great shape to use again (I hope not though!). I updated my stars from 3 to 4. It is a very comfortable belt.

I've worn the rib belt for two days now with no tearing or shredding as reported by other users. However, the big flaw is that there are velcro tabs on either end that should match up to secure the belt. Unless you are the exact size of the belt, the female velcro is useless. I have to wrap the belt halfway again around my torso to get any kind of compression. The male velcro does attach to the belt material securely but I can see the lightweight material eventually shredding from adjusting and removing the belt on a daily basis. The belt material is lightweight and elasticity holds once you get the belt positioned.

It is comfortable to wear and it does help secure my broken rib while allowing me to breathe. it stays in place and doesn't roll. But if you need a heavier (tighter) compression, you might want to get something sturdier.

Overall, it is a comfortable belt to wear when you need light compression. It fits nicely under the girls so there is no pinching there either. I will use this until it wears out but I also ordered a heavier belt to wear (with two straps) when I am lifting or need a heavier compression factor.

title: Great for a science project, not for reducing carbon footprint
text:
I just moved into a new place and have a lot of packing styrofoam stored up. I was hoping to find a cheap way to reduce the density so it wouldn't take up so much room in a landfill somewhere and I found an article about using D-Limonene to dissolve it down to a thick, rubbery substance. The D-Limonene DEFINITELY works for that, but it doesn't dissolve as much as I needed it to. I estimate I'd need to spend another 100$ to effectively dissolve down all the styrofoam I have, so I'll just look for another option to dispose of it - or find a craft project to use it on... a really big craft project.

All that said - it's super cool to pour this stuff on a block of styrofoam and see it get eaten away, so if you want to impress your kids with a science project - 100% recommend.

If the seller provided a different solution that was specifically targeted at dissolving styrofoam in a safe, home-friendly, eco-friendly manner - that would be awesome.

I've been buying, testing and reviewing "massagers" for quite some time now since my old favorite finally went to massager heaven much to my chagrin. So, I know a thing or two about them by now.. This one just gets a C grade from me. She's a pretty thing, not too big but not dainty like a mini..yet not ginormous like that all time favorite of so many. As for power I like to say they feel like either a high intensity dragon fly or a rumbling horse. This one, like many, can buzz at one speed or do a little dance of all sorts for you, but it's a horse. It's not as strong a rumble as many but a horse is a horse is a horse. I'm more of a strong dragon fly kinda gal (and those seem to be hard to find) so it won't ever be my favorite. For some it might be fine.

The reason I gave it two stars only, because I realize that the horse ride is awesome for some-just not for me-, is the charging cord. The magnets are a bit of a joke.. I mean really people, these things fall off if a strong breeze passes over them. That's not gonna work. Fix that and you'll have at least a B product. Up the intensity to a strong, buzzing dragon fly and you might be looking at an A. Or you might just have an entirely different product.

title: Believe it or not, this stuff works
text:
I started suffering from migraines in my teens. They became debilitating in my 40s. I was prescribed every drug in the book, including Cafergot injections, and most of them worked for awhile but then stopped. I developed rebound headaches with OTC analgesics and Cafergot. Antidepressants, seizure meds - tried 'em all.

I was given MigreLief in a 6-month clinical trial at Kaiser Permanente in the early 2000s. Although the results were hugely promising, the placebo effect couldn't be eliminated - a frequent problem with migraine meds - so Kaiser didn't prescribe it. I stopped taking it because at the time it was quite a bit more expensive.

Then I heard from an old friend to whom I'd recommended MigreLief during the Kaiser trial. She told me I'd saved her life, that she'd taken the supplement for the last 10 years and her headaches had stopped. That's all the endorsement I needed. I now order a 6-month supply directly from the manufacturer and take it twice a day, religiously. The number of headaches I experience has dropped by 90%.

Akeso isn't paying me to write this. It's an unsolicited appreciation. Thank you, MigreLief.

title: More than just a diaper bag!
text:
Holy diaper bag Batman! I thought my old diaper bag was big and held a lot, but then I saw this bad boy. When I opened the Amazon box I immediately could tell that this thing was monsterous. So for fun, I thought, let me see just how much I can fit into this thing. I started gathering up things I usually have to leave behind from my current diaper bag. So I was able to fit 1 thirty one medium size zip bag filled with toys, 1 thirty one thermal bag filled with snacks, 1 thirty one small thermal bag filled with feminine products band aids and lotion, 1 reusable grocery bag, 1 small makeup case, 1 skip hop changing pad (it comes with a changing pad but I like this one better), 1 Apple iPad, 1 gallon size Baggie of coupons, 1 coveredgoods nursing cover, 1, burp cloth, 3 cloth diapers (which I don't usually use but wanted to show how much it fit, 1 set of clothes (shirt, pants, and heavy socks), 1 plastic Baggie holder for dirty diapers, 1 sippy cup, 1 bottle, 1 cell phone. I fit all this and had room for more. The diaper bag measures 16 inches tall and 21 inches wide. It comes with 2 handle straps and 1 shoulder strap. I really love that it has 2 zippers on the top. Because if the zipper gets pulled apart, which it already has, then it is easier to zip back together and get back on track.
But that is not all. I actually let my son use this bag to carry around his giant 3 ring binder to school. It not just any binder though. It is one of those fabric zip up binders by case it. It was too big to fit into a normal jansport backpack and he has been carrying it around by hand. So when I saw how big this bag is I asked hi if he wanted to try it. He said sure. He wasn't sure it would fit though. But it did. And the side pockets still had room for two of his text books.
A few things that I found as cons to the diaper bag were that once it was full, it seemed too heavy. It no longer sit straight and didn't look as nice. That to me is the biggest con. Another con is that after letting my son use it for a week, he made the zipper pull apart as mentioned above, and he also has put two holes in the diaper bag, one on each side. I wouldn't normally put this as a con, but as rough as he is on his bags, he hasn't managed to do this much damage to his backpacks.
I received this product for free in exchange for my honest and unbiased review. All opinions are my own.

title: Problems, Problems, Problems
text:
Review of the FootSmart Carepeutic Foot and Calf Beauty Massager with Infrared Heated Therapy, model Kh383I, Black, purchased directly from FootSmart 26Nov2010 for $119.99.

Received this foot & calf massager as a Christmas present (2010).

First Problem:
The silver placard "instrument panel" had come off and was stuck on the side of the unit instead of over the lights on top of the middle section. When placard was replaced to its proper position, it would again become unstuck after a day or so.

Second Problem:
The unit has a receptacle with two jack pins that the power cord plugs into. The bases of the two jacks were not seated properly and prevented the power cord from being entirely inserted such that the plug itself would not seat properly. When the unit was being used the vibration would cause the plug to fall out.

Third Problem:
When using the unit on my feet, the unit eventually damaged my left foot (rollers inside the unit squeeze the feet in an effort to massage them) causing pain for about a week. A month later my left foot still feels sore on occasion.

For the above three reasons I cannot recommend this product. I am returning unit to FootSmart 18Jan2011 in hopes of getting a refund.

title: A Guide To Choosing the Best Foam Roller Foam roller’s have continued to gain wide ...
text:
Triathlete here and this thing is a life saver. If you're any sort of athlete or just have sore muscles that have knots which are difficult to roll out this is the toy for you. The beauty of this thing is that it allows you to torture yourself three different ways. The outter portion is smooth and hard so you can start with it to roll out your ITB issues, then just whip out the middle slightly softer but pointy roller and roll out your butt, hamstrings and quads and finally get the stick roller inside to do your calfs. This thing does it all. Honestly I wouldn't settle for a single when you can buy a three in one for the same price. Basically every coach and athlete will suggest you get one of these things. It's esp helpful for people with ITB or muscular injuries due to endurance sports. A Guide To Choosing the Best Foam Roller

Foam roller’s have continued to gain wide acceptance as more and more trainers help their clients understand all the benefits of using a foam roller.

I originally began to use a foam roller while I was training for a marathon. A close friend of mine who works with elite athletes recommended it after I complained of hip tightness. What I found is that it’s a little bit like any other healthy habit, you’re not going to love it at first but eventually you won’t be able to go a day without it. Don’t quote me on this, but I think the phrase “it hurts so good” was originally used to describe a relationship with a roller.

Since then, I've been using a foam roller during all of my training. I recently ran the BMO Marathon in Vancouver British Columbia and I can't express just how vital the Trigger Point Foam Roller was post-run. Anytime you run 5, 10 or 25 miles, stretching your muscles out with the best foam rollers is going to help your body the next day.

Now depending on your pain tolerance and how tight your muscles are you’re going to need a different roller. And while some experts recommend ditching a foam roller and going straight for the PVC pipe I caution against that. Again it depends on the type of muscles you'll be using your foam roller on. Throughout this site, we have a variety guides on foam rollers for back pain and lower body pain like shin splints.

Why You Shouldn't Start With The Most Intense Foam Roller?

You’re not going to make rolling out your muscles a habit. If you’re new to this, a PVC pipe is going to hurt. Sure, all foam rollers will be uncomfortable particularly when you first start. A PVC pipe won’t be uncomfortable, it will hurt. There is no easing into it, and as a result you won’t pause to let those trigger points dissipate, you’ll use it less frequently and for a shorter periods of time.

Both EVA rollers and high density foam rollers are very cheap and you may find that you actually enjoy the slight discomfort that these products inflict.

The Benefits of Using a Foam Roller

When my friend recommended I start using a foam roller the first thing I wanted to know is why. What is a foam roller going to do for me? Like many, I'm the type of person who will be more motivated to do something if I know the why.

He broke it down into two categories for me:
Warming up
Recovering
Warming Up
Best Foam Roller for Warm Up
Before any intense exercise you should always warm up. It doesn’t matter if you’re going into a yoga class, running a marathon or weight lifting. A foam roller has become a vital part of my warm up. Kneading your muscles with a roller will help improve blood flow to prime your muscles for whatever you’re about to do. This in turn helps to reduce injuries.

The only reason I gave it 4 stars and not 5 isn't even the fault of the product per se. Depending on how cold your refrigerator is, the oil fat can congeal and separate from the rest of the product. This can be solved by letting it sit for a few minutes and a good shake, but still it's a minor complaint I had.

If you're looking for good quality fish oil look no further, I've been buying this stuff for about a year now (ie brand loyal).

title: Perfect for my little bedroom!
text:
I have a larger humidifier that works great, but is too much for my rather small bedroom with limited ventilation. My walls were getting soggy with my old one, and I was a bit scared of mold. I went looking around for a smaller humidifier, and this one seemed like the best bet.

It works great! We turn it on for about an hour or two at night before going to sleep, and it keeps things very comfortable. Because the room is small, we don't have to leave it running all night, but I like that it's just big enough to do so if I DID want to. Very little noise (the small desk fan behind it drowns it out entirely), and it puts out a good amount of steam. When we get up in the morning, we click it on for about 30 minutes to "top off" the humidity in the room. It's perfect.

The room I have it in is about 10' x 8', possibly 9'. It has a slant wall on one side, so the dimensions aren't exact. It always bothers me when people say "It works great in my small room" but don't ever give dimensions on the room. So there you have it. In a 10x8 room, it works fine and my walls are dry as a bone in the morning after using it at night. :)

title: Excellent and easy - if you figure it out
text:
I read a lot of the other reviews that talked about extreme scrubbing. The first time I used this, 15ish years ago, I had the same issue, it was an amazing amount of hands and knees scrubbing.

The second time, I allowed it to sit on the surface much longer before attempting to remove the wax. The problem is that it tends to dry out too quickly. So, I waited a few minutes until it started drying and obviously wrinkling up the old wax, then sprinkled/poured a lot of additional water on it.

The difference between leaving it for 2 minutes and leaving it for 15 minutes is remarkable. Very light scrubbing removed all wax very easily. The second big problem is removing it the resulting mess. Using towels or paper towels to sop it up is *brutal* and takes forever. I used my Bissell Spot Clean Pro wet/dry vac with just plain water in the tank, and it was remarkably easy. It's a good thing to have around, but if you don't, you can rent similar systems for one-time use. DO NOT put the remover directly in the tank, that's entirely unnecssary. The cleaner can spray the keep-alive water, but just use it for rinsing and sucking up the residue. My recommendation is to pour out the extraction tank without looking at it too closely, because it's disturbing how filthy that floor was and how much crud the wax has grabbed.

So - work in small sections (I did about 4x4 feet at a time)
let it sit on the surface for as long as you can
if it starts to dry prematurely, add water to keep it moist
Scrub lightly with a stiff brush
buy/rent a wet-dru vac and rinse with lots of clear water

Do this, and it is a very low-impact and easy operation.

The results (both previously and now) are rather amazing and alarming. My floor did not look that bad - until I did the first section. The difference was astonishing, that thing was *filthy* after even normal cleaning and occasional mop n' glo. It was rather alarming, cleaning it made a huge difference in the appearance, and also in the brightness of the kitchen. I had put off doing this for a long time because it was such a pain the first time, but now, this is going to be once/year, just to keep it from building up like that again.

text: My fiance got me this for Christmas and I LOVE shaving with it!  I was going to go with a Dovo but I wanted a truly old fashioned style razor (solid steel).  I have a Boker automatic knife and I love it so I figured a straight razor made by Boker will be just as good.  This type of shaving does have quite a large learning curve that range from the angle of shaving, pressure, direction of how your hair grows, how to shave with both hands, etc.  I purchased a nice strop to go with this and after I stropped it for the first time, it was a very smooth shave.  It did not come without a few nicks (which I absolutely expected).  After the first few shaves do not get discouraged if the results were not as expected.  During my first few shaves, my face was sensitive, I did cut myself a few times, and I missed a few patches of hair on my chin and had rough "5 o clock shadow" areas.  The more you use the straight razor, the better you will be, the better you will learn how your facial hair grows, and the more in control you will be of the straight razor.  I spend about 20 minutes to shave and it has now become an activity to shave (which admittedly is fun) and not a burden.

title: Most aggravating product ever developed yet I love it when it works
text:
I've had this cussed thing for almost five years and I can say without any hesitation that it is the most aggravating piece of technology I own. I can also say that when it works (which is almost all of the time), I love it.

Pros: It weighs accurately and syncs with your Fitbit dashboard so that you can get a big picture of your weight over the week, months and years. I think even the body fat part is accurate and it is certainly consistent. The thing I like most is that on days when I don't want to weigh, I can get on the scale, not look at it, and go off into the day in blissful ignorance. When I'm feeling brave I can look at it later in the week and see how I'm doing. Hopefully, I have gotten back on track and the news is all good.

Cons: Two things: The first is that it will get into endless "sensing" or "thinking" mode and burn through batteries. You can sometimes stage an intervention and take the battery out, reposition it, do something and it will stop. If you don't, you will get to the next aggravating thing:

Setting up--and setting up some more. Why oh why do you have to set this thing up again and again? I can understand if you change your Internet provider or router or password, but sometimes just changing the batteries will make it forget everything and you have to set it up again. (Note: It might forget everything, but your Fitbit dashboard does not so all your data is still there and once you get set up again it will work fine.) It seems like every time I've had to set it up I've had to do it a different way, and it is not convenient in the least. They really need to fix it.

I do recommend it but it ought to be a better product. It will aggravate you but eventually you will get it back online. I have yet to throw it out of the window but I have come close.

I do rely on it and it does keep me motivated. Seeing several years of history of my weight and body fat helps me see my progress (and my slip ups) and I think is a health benefit. If only it wasn't so quirky!

My blood pressure has also dropped and is more stable and I feel less anxious (calmer). I have now been dosing consistently for about 6 weeks and will be a ReMag customer for life. I really like how clean my face feels after I use this. I also noticed my pores were noticeably smaller, which never happens when I just use my hands to wash my face. The bristles are really soft and not at all harsh on my skin. There are two speeds: For my face I prefer to use the slower setting and for the body I use the second, faster setting. If you press the brush down too hard against your skin, the head stops rotating, so just keeps it lightly pressed against your skin.

One thing you should definitely watch out for though, is getting your hair caught behind the brush. I have really long hair and I was using this in the shower to wash my face. A couple strands of hair got caught on the rotating axis behind the brush and ripped right off my head. I'm always sure to tuck my hair behind my ears when I use it now.

title: "Gospel-Centered" says it all
text:
Sara Wallace does a fantastic job remaining biblically accurate and gospel-focused in this "mom's guide." There are several things about this book that I really appreciate:

1. The way the book is structured is very intelligent as Sara moves from ensuring that we have a proper understanding of the true and unadulterated gospel before moving into applications of this gospel in the life of being a mother.
2. The chapters that explain the true gospel and detail false gospels (gospels of legalism) are done so very clearly and the content is much needed truth in today's church. As parents, we need a true understanding of salvation by grace alone through faith alone and we need to teach it clearly to our children.
3. The way the book is broken into 14 concise but thoughtful chapters makes reading through it as a busy mother more feasible. Each chapter left me with thoughts to dwell on and prepared me theologically for the following chapter. The review questions are great for private reflection or a group setting.
4. The content on teaching children the importance of looking to Christ for grace and forgiveness instead of hammering rote behaviorism was very relieving to me as a mother. We aren’t aiming for Pharisees who obey out of self-righteousness, we are aiming for believers who worship Christ and obey through a changed heart that only God can provide.

I will definitely be recommending this book to many mothers of all ages. I think the gospel focus that this book maintains is beautiful and vitally needed in the church in America today, where we are more apt to entertain goats than to feed sheep. This is not a book on how to be the perfect mom. It’s a book on how to look to Christ and the beauty of the gospel, and let the gospel flow out of us as mothers.

title: Really expensive, but really works
text:
I was extremely skeptical at first, especially with the hefty price tag, but after just a few weeks I noticed a HUGE difference. I'm 5', yet I still ate the same amount as my 6' husband. Not only was I overeating, but I was tired all the time-- I used to drink several cups of coffee and take naps throughout the day. After I started TT, my appetite was cut in half and I had a lot more energy.

TT is not a chalky powder like so many other similar products. This is more like a crystallized lemonade mix, so it blends really easily with fruit or vegetable juice (I like beet-carrot juice or some fruit blend with sparkling water). With my appetite cut in half, I noticed the weight loss. It has only been a few pounds, but for someone my height, it's a big difference. If I keep eating this little, I'll be at my goal weight in no time.

When I ran out, I looked for alternatives since TT is so expensive. Most things I found were of comparable price, and the cheaper ones were completely off (chalky, not blending, tasting terrible). I didn't get far with the others, but I certainly realized how much energy I got from TT. Now that I'm tired again, I decided to go back to TT. It's really expensive, but how much time, money, and health do I waste on coffee, naps, and that extra helping of food?

text: I have wanted to try one of these posture correctors for quite some time and I finally found one that seemed simple to use at a reasonable price. The adjustments are made with quick changes in two Velcro enclosures so you get the exact fit that is appropriate for you. I’ve always felt like my posture was better than most people’s but I’ve had chronic back pain for years. When I put this on and got it adjusted properly, I was surprised at how much it changed my stance. I must admit, after wearing it for a few hours, my back was hurting in places that it normally does not. title: Great product if used as directed.
text:
When I started to need bifocals, I had to give up my daily disposables for monthly lenses. However, the monthlies were becoming so uncomfortable within a few days that I was ready to give them up. My doctor noticed deposits on my 1-day old lenses and suggested Clear Care. He warned me to follow the directions on the box as it cleans with Hydrogen Peroxide. I soak them overnight in the case provided (with the little metal thing) and rinse them with water or saline in the morning before putting them in. The results have been phenomenal. I can comfortably wear my lenses for 24 hrs.

To those that complain of burning eyes, they tell you burning eyes will result if you don't follow directions. The directions say "Do not use flat lens case. Clear Care only works with the special lens case provided" and "Do not rinse lenses with Clear Care prior to inserting lenses into your eyes." in a BIG RED BOX! How much clearer can they make it? If you choose not to read or to disregard the instruction your burning eyes are your own fault not the products.

This solution works amazingly well when used as directed.

title: Poor quality control
text:
This scale works fairly well as a bathroom scale to send weight data to FitBit.

The scale is a little frustrating to set up. It can go smoothly the first time, or it can take an hour for it to stay connected to your phone or to the Wifi network you program in. After it had been working for several months, mine lost Wifi connectivity and had to be coaxed into reconnecting through a battery replacement, five hours of repeatedly trying to configure it one night, and a couple hours the next morning.

As well, there are constant and continuous reports of body fat percentage measurement not working. The ultimate resolution appears to be getting a replacement from FitBit: many of the Aria units simply cannot measure body fat percentage. Extremely poor quality control in that respect. Even functional units can be finicky about body fat measurement, so you can't tell until you've tried troubleshooting for a while to no resolution. Support responds largely by blaming the user, but will readily replace the scale eventually.

title: Only sling that worked well in our situation.
text: I used this with a motorized lift to move my father (94 years old) around the house.  I transferred him to a small wheel wheelchair because my house is too small to move him in the Hoyer Lift.  This was the only sling I could easily put around him while he was sitting on the sofa.  I didn't have to lift him to put him in the sling.  My father was just too heavy to lift without the Hoyer so this sling made it practical to move him safely and relatively easily.  I got two slings with the Hoyer but I had to lift him physically to get him into them.  I'm in my late 60s so that just wasn't going to work.  This one was much more useful.  If you follow the directions that come with it, and watch some of the (many) videos on Youtube on how to use a Hoyer lift you should do OK.  None of this is fun or simple but in some cases it is necessary.  How did he like it?  Well, not so much at first, but my sister pointed out that it was't much different from the Coney Island parachute ride of his childhood and he actually got to like it.  The transfer to and from the chair took some practice, but it got to be a routine.  You are lucky if you have a big house and NO carpets!

text:
I am currently using this toothpaste exclusively, and I really like it.
Before, due to many and painful sensitive "spots", I was pretty much confined to Sensodyne and similar products. Also, since I am a moderate coffee and tea drinker, I was also looking for something that can help remove the stains without causing excruciating pain, like the common over-the-counter whitening products do when you have sensitive teeth.
I am also nearly 60, so the days of pearly whites are sadly gone, and the teeth need all the help they can get (without spending ridiculously high amounts on veneers) to get remineralized the most natural and affordable way I can find.

After doing some reading on the product, and many, many reviews from all over the web, I purchased this toothpaste.
I have put it to immediate use, usually three times per day after meals and, after about three weeks, I can already see some subtle results. Many discolorations are becoming much less visible, and my teeth actually look and feel clean. Best of all, the plaque is gone, and I no longer need the customary twice-yearly dental cleaning!
Even my dentist made a remark that my "teeth are being taken excellent care of". I mentioned the Apagard toothpaste, and he was very impressed with it.

Since then, I have bought three more tubes of this wonderful toothpaste, and keep one at work so I can brush after lunch. Apagard is expensive but, I believe, it is money well spent. Peanuts, comparing to the dentist' fees.

title: Makes crappy shoes awesome!
text:
I was in Zimbabwe last summer doing a combination of vacationing and relief work. I only brought a pair of tennis shoes and loafers with me. We were going hiking, and I didn't have boots or anything to get muddy in. So I bought a pair of boots from the only place nearby at the time. The place was rather shady. It was more of a shack than an actual store. None of the shoes had insoles. They'd been removed, and no explanation was offered. I reluctantly bought a pair of Champion boots as they were the cheapest pair the man would sell me.

Many miles and blisters later, I ended up back in the United States with these pain in the foot boots. I didn't wear them again for close to a year. I decided it was time to buy some insoles and give them another shot considering the amount of money I'd already sunk into them. I did my usual Amazon search for a highly rated and well priced product. These Powerstep insoles came up, and I'm so glad I bought them. I wear size 11, so I bought the 11-11 1/2 Men's. I now love the boots. I wish I had these insoles back when I really needed them in Zimb. O well. Now I'm happy :)

title: One of the best, but be forewarned, 90% chance of breaking in under 1 year!! Avoid if you can...
text: I purchased this thru Folica admittedly but wanted to come to Amazon and provide fair warning. I have sworn by the SEDU line of flat irons for the last 15 years, but at this point I am looking at other brands. The Sedu Revolution broke not once, not twice, not three times, but 4 - all in under a year. Folica had to keep sending me replacements because it kept breaking within their warranty, after only a few months of somewhat regular use. The same thing would happen: the flashing blue and red lights (indicating it has reached your temperature setting and is ready for use) started showing only solid blue or solid red. The flat iron MAYBE heats up halfway to the current setting (450 degrees), and I need the maximum temperature for my super-thick, super-frizzy, wavy, curly hair. Every last one of them did the same thing, and now the 4th replacement is on the way out after only a year. For the price point, this should NOT be happening!! My SEDU classics also broke, but those at least lasted a full 2 years a pop. I WILL tell you that SEDU does perform better than every single other flat iron brand I've tried yet, but be forewarned, they break way too quickly for the price you will pay :(
