title: Seems okay, but I remain skeptical of some claims
text:
This product is packaged by AmerMed. Upon emailing AmerMed, I was informed that it is sold to them by a supplier in New Jersey. I have consumed six or even twelve pills of this product twice daily. On some days it gave me a mild headache, but I guess I should expect that for consuming so much of it.

I was skeptical about the claim of 10% theobromine, because most cocoa extracts contain only about 2% of it. I was informed by AmerMed that their supplier has provided them with a COA (certificate of authenticity) claiming results from a HPLC (high performance liquid chromatography) test, stating that it contains 11% theobromine. I asked to be emailed the COA, but AmerMed denied my request saying that their supplier disallows sharing the COA. Baloney, I say, and for this I deduct one star from my rating. I then asked if an independent COA was performed by AmerMed to confirm the theobromine findings by HPLC, but AmerMed said they didn't deem it necessary. In my opinion, as a general policy, it is wise to be skeptical of claims made by suppliers, and only independent third-party tests can be relied upon to confirm nutrient and product safety (lead, mercury, etc.) levels.

Despite consuming up to 24 pills a day amounting to over one gram of theobromine, I really did not notice any of theobromine's claimed mood enhancing effects. Could it be because this product contains much less thebromine than advertised? I don't know.

Cocoa extracts contain caffeine, and so I also inquired with AmerMed about the quantity of caffeine contained in this extract. I was informed it contains 0.18% caffeine, which is nothing to worry about.

Two commonly used processes exist for the extraction of cocoa from cacao beans, namely the Broma process and the Dutch process. The Dutch process is intended and known to make cocoa taste milder and remove some of its natural bitterness. Unfortunately, the Dutch process destroys the beneficial flavonols contained in cocoa. Consuming cocoa extract processed using the Dutch process is therefore largely useless from a health perspective. I inquired with AmerMed about which process is used, but despite two emails, I was not provided the answer to this question. Due to this, I deduct one more star from my rating here. Nonetheless, I tasted the powder, and it does taste somewhat bitter, and so I still have reason to believe that the process may still be the Broma process.

Be very skeptical of consuming this product for weight loss. While there is some evidence that theobromine may reduce hunger (perhaps due to the claim that it inhibits vagus nerve activity), as per my knowledge, it is not entirely certain whether those claims are solid, nor is it certain whether this product contains the suggested amounts of that chemical. In any event, I suppose there is little risk of harm in trying it in order to see if it reduces hunger; it didn't for me.

title: Very impressed
text: I have been in the market for a long time for a yoga mat cleaner that meets all my requirements: not full of toxic ingredients that will hurt my skin, pleasant smelling (or even unscented), inexpensive, long-lasting, and something that actually works! This checked off each of them. The ingredient list is short, and I recognize the names of all the ingredients (I use some of them on a regular basis too), not to mention that there are only 9 of them in this mat cleaner. None are toxic, and all the ingredients are natural. I ordered the sweet rose scent, and it is has a light and pleasant aroma. I have tried other cleaners with little to no success lifting much of the dirt on my mat, and there were some stains that frankly I didn't think would lift. I sprayed those areas liberally, left the cleaner to soak in for 5 minutes, came back to wipe it down with the microfiber towel... and a lot of the stains lifted right up! I didn't expect them to be completely gone, as I have had my yoga mat for about 5 years now, but it looks much newer than it did before. I didn't have to scrub very much and the remaining ones are a lot lighter! I hate feeling like I have to deep clean my mat, and a decent mat cleaning spray shouldn't take so much energy to efficiently use. The cleaner doesn't leave my mat sticky or slimy, and I love that not only is the scent pleasant, I can also tell that it isn't full of harsh chemicals. I have very sensitive skin, and have had no reaction to the product after using it for a couple months. If I had any pets or children I wouldn't be paranoid about this cleaner being in their reach (obviously I wouldn't want them eating it, but I wouldn't have to worry about it damaging their skin or anything else it came in contact with if it were accidentally sprayed). A yoga mat cleaner should be able to contact your skin directly without discomfort, because your skin contacts the mat it cleans directly, and this one has my vote!

title: Miracle product for odors and stains, affordable, effective
text:
I had to buy this product for a laundry crisis a few months ago, and I wrote a review back then, but I am updating to list some of the other magic this product has done for me. I am continually impressed and ever more reliant on this product, I wish I could give it 10 stars.

Odor Removal: My shirts weren't getting clean with cheap detergent so eventually they all smelled very strongly of burnt body odor. I made a paste with the powder and let that work for 30-minutes and it worked. I soaked blankets that had been in the garage for a year and smelled like rubber and oil, as well as some sheets that just always smelled kind of funky, it worked. Dog blankets, smelly shoes, mildewy towels, jackets that smell like smoke, clothes that smell like fried food - all not a problem.

Stains I've used this for: Puppy peed and pooped on a white blanket, old blood stains in dark colored undies, new blood stains in very light colored jeans, raw hide crisped to a blanket, dingy white hand towels, the orange powder from cheetos and doritos - all came out.

Again, could not be happier with how well this works on all of the crazy stuff I'm up against when I'm battling laundry. The price for this (especially compared to high-end laundry detergents and additives) does seem reasonable. Also, I have sensitive skin and this doesn't give me any problems.

title: now my favorite organic chyavanprash
text: Like spicy, warm, exotically fruity molasses, leaning more towards a honeylike base flavor than a fruit preserve fruitiness. Not tart, but rather rootsy, botanical and warming. I had tried one other organic chyawanprash, from Organic India, and had reviewed that one as having a tougher texture but also a higher quantity of medicinal roots, fruits, herbs, and botanicals, and also had originally found it less sweet, and so had preferred it. I purchased about a dozen jars direct from Organic India after first ordering here, but as I worked my way through the first couple of jars, I found the texture in each progressive jar becoming tougher and tougher to work out (apparently, they dry rather quickly), until I finally unsealed a fresh jar to find a solid mass my spoon could not push or break through. I recently placed another order with Banyan Botanicals and included a few jars of their chyavanprash, and was very pleased, again, to find its consistency so spreadable and easy. I just finished one jar of this chyavanprash and will have to get back to my Organic India stock and do my best with those jars, but I wanted to come back and share my reconsidered review. These are still my two favorite chyawanprashes (sp?), but I now feel that Banyan is probably the better of the two. It does contain fewer botanicals, but that may even be by design (how many of those things can possibly be compatible all at once to our human system? after all, these ingredients are all potent!). I also had originally thought it was much sweeter than the Organic India chyawanprash, but, on second thought, I may have had that other chyawanprash after eating a piece of fruit or something, because I find them almost equal in sweetness now. If you are interested in trying both, please do. If you get a fresh jar of Organic India chyawanprash, it will be a nice treat too. If you are only looking for one, though, maybe Banyan Botanicals would be your best bet. The product is more consistent and smooth in texture, there is nothing grainy or gritty in it, it is delicious, and it is easy to spoon out from the jar. After one jar, I am sure you will return for more. Please contact your seller and request care in shipping, though, as these jars are glass and fragile, and can break in transit (it happened to me once). Enjoy!

title: Warning: Read their Disclaimer about Deflation!
text:
Size: LargeColor: Cappuccino

Be sure to read their disclaimer, "Inflatable Lounge Doctors may lose some air after time and usage." The manufacturer doesn't specify how much time or usage before it starts to lose air, but for me it was after 3 1/2 weeks of nightly use. It started deflating slowly on its own despite absence of holes or punctures. I'd wake up in the morning and the pillow had deflated to the point that my leg/foot was not elevated. I went back to Amazon.com to read its description and that's when I discovered the disclaimer that the leg pillow "...may lose some air after time and usage." This disclaimer means buyers cannot seek a refund. Bottomline - in my opinion - : If you are looking for something that stores flat and you only plan to use it a few times, this inflatable leg rest will be fine. But if you're recovering from an injury that requires heavy use, consider the possibility that this could deflate.

title: Terribly disappointing. BEWARE!
text:
This was /almost/ complete waste of $6. Almost only because I /was/ eventually able to trim my nails, so I can't justifiably say it was actually a /complete/ waste... but it was pretty darn close.

These clippers do not cut. You have to squeeze with all your might, and then it still only leaves an impression and you're forced to tear off the rest of the nail. I don't have a weak grip, either; these are just /that/ difficult to use. I do not understand all of the positive reviews; sure, the things don't slip in your hands... but how many people actually have an issue with that normally? I mean, I don't consider myself a nail clipper snob or anything, and I've only ever really used cheap ones from the store, but I have never in my life had as much difficulty clipping my nails as I did when using these clippers. Perhaps all of the positive reviews are just because people received the clippers for free... I don't know.

Regardless, don't waste your money. If it wasn't such a hassle to deal with return shipping, you can bet I'd be getting a full refund. But, at $6, it's just not worth it to me. I'll eat the loss and grab a better pair from the store next time I'm there.

If you're anything like me, I hate that my glasses slide down my face All. The. Time. It's frustrating. So when I saw this product, I wanted to give it a try. It couldn't hurt! title: Fair Buy. Great For Sensitive Skin.
text:
Delivery / Packaging

I purchased the travel size to test it out, as I need specialty detergent for a small set of silk, and cotton fabrics.

Being a small item, this was item was placed with several others in a communal box. The delivery was on-time and hassel free. The box arrived undamaged. Shutout to the delivery team for doing such a good job.

The item itself was placed in a medium-thick plastic bag with an advertisement and a coupon. The top of the bottle leaked a bit.

Overall, 6/10 for packaging. I would have preferred to not have recieved any additional advertisements or offers. As a millenial, I do everything electronically. An email or text with an offer would have been better. Simply to elimate paper waste and make using a coupon more efficient for online or in-person purchased.

I also disliked the use of a plastic bag. Obviously, it's to act as a barrier in case of spills. My suggestion to the company is to create a stronger seal and cap instead. Also, using a wax-lined, recycled, unbleached cardboard box instead of a plastic bag would have been better. At least that way the packaging can be compostable.

Basically, 3 pieces (1 plastic bag and 2 pieces of paper) ended up in a landfill for nothing. So I would like to see the company making improvements to change this dynamic.

Contents:

The detergent itself is fairly decent. It has a very faint smell that's hardly noticeable. The soap is not concentrated, and somewhat thin. A few drops does not lather particularly well. It takes roughly a third of the bottle to create any foam.

I used this to handwash vintage kimono silk. In a separate batch, I also washed a set of pure cotton fabrics (printed and dyed). I didn't notice any damages to the silk or brocade. The cotton remained intact, no visible shrinkage. No color fade. None of the items had any visible residue left over. I was a bit disappointed that there wasn't any scent remaining after drying. I don't have any allergies or skin sensitivity, so I enjoy a vibrant fragrance.

Overall, the detergent gets 7/10. It does the job. However, I think it's over-hyped. The website and the presentation make the product seem more high-end than it actually is. I feel like the price is less to do with the quality of the product itself, but more to do with keeping up with production costs. Since the product is made in the United States, the operation costs are greater. The consistency was also a bit disappointing. It's marketed as being concentrated, but it has very little viscosity.

However, it gets a 10/10 for being cruelty free. Absolutely no animal testing. They get my respect and my thanks for that one.

Another 10/10 for not using caustic chemicals, or having a heavy fragrance. I may be disappointed, but they do market themselves as being good for people with allergies and sensitivities. So if you're someone who can't handle fragrance, this detergent is for you.

Final Thoughts:

Honestly, I don't know if I like it or not. I appreciate the thought and care the company has put into certain things. I think it's just okay. Not the best, not the worst. If I had to use it again, it would be only for specialty items. I don't think I would purchase this for my everyday needs.

I do think this is a good option for people who are really struggling to find a detergent that won't make them break out or sneeze or cause some kind of reaction.

title: I don't regret getting this scale one bit.
text: It took me several months to decide to get this scale, because it's a lot of money for a scale. I already had another scale that would show me my weight and body fat %. My old scale's interface wasn't very intuitive and I'd have to manually set myself as the user all the time, and then I'd have to remember to actually record the results, which wasn't always convenient because I don't normally carry my phone into the bathroom, and my computer is not nearby either. So there's a lot of steps there to do on a daily basis, if I were to weigh myself everyday. I had resigned myself to just weighing myself once a week. A lot of weight loss books/sites advise you to only weigh yourself once a week anyway. I don't think this is great though, because what if you weigh yourself on a bad day and it seems like you didn't make any progress (easy for this to happen when you're trying to lose 1-2 lbs a week.) The end result is weighing myself wasn't a very effective motivator because I often felt I wasn't making any progress. So I finally got the Aria. I weigh myself every morning. It automatically recognizes who is standing on the scale, whether it's me or my boyfriend and then uploads the data to the website. Then there's wonderful graphs on their website or phone app where you can see how much weight you lost over the course of a week (or a month, or a year.) It also integrates with Lose It! (if you have a premium account on lose it.) Currently I am using a FitBit One, FitBit Aria, and Lose It! premium and seeing all the graphs and numbers on all of those things has been very motivating and my weight has been going down.

title: Certainly the 2 best forms of B12 and most effective delivery supplement available.
text: B12 is best absorbed with sublingual spray or drops, or dissolving tablets (or Deplin shots). If you're vegetarian or vegan, you need to take B12 supplementation seriously (probably shots as well). I like Black Bear Energy B12, which has both hydroxy and adenosylcobalamin along with B2, B3, B6, trace minerals, molybdenum, antioxidants. (Most supplements use the cheap/less effective cyanocobalamin). Methylcobalamin is the most effective form, but can be too much for some people. Haven't found anything to compare with BlackBear short of taking multiple supplements. Not to say you wouldn't benefit from more of the other B's, but the Black Bear spray is the best delivery method and form(s) of B12. If you had labwork to check B12 levels, plasma levels of B12 don't necessarily mean it's available. Plus, the reference range on plasma B12 indicated on lab results is lower than optimal. Mine is 4x the upper limit and the doc said that's a good thing. I keep a spray bottle in my car, gym bag, etc. The other ingredients/antioxidants help with transport and detox support. To ensure your body can use the B12, add a methylfolate like Thorne Methyl Guard to bypass common genetic mutations restricting the pathway. Supplementing B12 has to be done slowly as it does generate detox and can cause herxheimer reactions as the liver tries to keep up. Liver and Metal support supplements are also a good idea as detox depletes minerals like selenium, zinc, magnesium, lithium, etc. I like the Thorne formulations for those two supports as well. I was excited to try this after my dentist's recommendation and I ordered a pack with samples of multiple flavors directly from the cocofloss website.

I do prefer these flavors to mint, but not worth the price for me.
EFFECTIVENESS: This does work well,much better than the other floss I have on hand, but it wasn't as luxe feeling as I'd expected. I had a more comfortable and effective flossing experience in the past with the listerine woven floss that has been discontinued. Next time I'll try Dr Tungs for half the price.
BRAND: They advertise this as luxury floss. There are lots of other flavors and sample packs on the website. I haven't tried all the flavors yet, but will update if my opinions change. I think this might be worth it to help getting into the habit of flossing more consistently and to make flossing more enjoyable, but I'm thinking there are more affordable and good options out there. One of the other flavors might yet reel me in. I'll find out soon enough. title: Key to using properly
text:
This glove works well to pill up dead skin, but it only works if you use it properly. First, take a warm shower or bath and cleanse without any moisturizer. Towel dry your skin so it’s still damp but not wet. Wet the glove and wring out. Ensure that the glove is pulled taught on your hand, and with your hand flat, rub skin back and forth gently. It may take several passes for dead skin to start forming little balls. Keep gentle pressure and look closely, sometimes it is hard to see the balls of dead skin cells but they are there! Rinse skin with warm water and moisturize!

I have been very happy with this, I have very dry skin and keratosis pilaris as well. This really helps with both. Skin feels soft and smooth after using this glove! Totally recommend.

title: Good Pouches Well Made
text: These first aid Molle pouches are great. I inspected both pouches and have not been able to find any flaws in workmanship. The materials used are very strong and durable and I believe will last a long time. It is rip-away so that you dont have to unsnap to gain access and the center strap with buckle should hold it in place without fear that it may peel off the velcro when its not suppose to. Very difficult to tell in the advertised pictures but these pouches are perfectly sized for a first aid kit and should hold everything you need for a medical emergency. The only design flaw that it has is in the center strap that is sewn into to top of the pouch and velcros to the top to help keep the pouch closed if for some reason it unzips. The tab used to pull it from the velcro is backwards (in my opinion) and so you have to pull it apart as oppose to peeling it off making it a little more work to get to much needed medical supplies in a hurry. Not a deal breaker since I may just cut them off altogether. The buckled center strap should still perform that same function when its all attached. The shears are of decent quality and will easily cut through clothing. Dont see any need to purchase any other shears. The added bonus to these pouches is that they came with the rubberized velcro Red Cross patches.  Not knowing this initially I purchased one but it wasnt necessary. Overall these are great molle pouches. Not just as IFAK kits but any other use you may have.

title: Not actually a gel battery
text:
I ordered 6 of these for a project. They shipped promptly and were well packaged. Each one includes a little bag with bolts and washers for the terminals. The little charge meter on the top is nifty but will be worthless in my application.

One star because despite all of the information on the product page, and on the manufacturer's own web site, and even on the packaging, this is not a gel battery; it's an AGM battery. I don't know what "Gel Series" means (maybe it's a hybrid gel?) but it says it's an AGM battery, it sloshes if you shake it because there's liquid electrolyte, and it even comes with a handy little tool to pry the cover off so that you can top off the (non-gel) liquid electrolyte. It's not that they put the wrong battery in the box - 6 times - the battery is printed with the part number, this is what they're selling. It's not a gel battery, it's an AGM battery. If you want a gel battery, you need to buy a different one.

The blade design is very close to the same, but the covers are designed differently which may be the reason for the difference. In one of my photos you can see the original design has a curved cut pattern in the outer most ring while the Jovno has straight lines, this area does the initial beard cutting. The next inner ring on the original has fine holes and the Jovno has a mix of slots and holes, this covers the closer shave.

I particularly disliked that the photo on the listing page shows a different design for the covers than was delivered. The photos on the listing show a sort of attempt at the curved cuts in the outer ring.

title: Crazy Soft Right Out The Gate
text:
Disclosure: This was sent to me for free via the Vine program. I did not receive monetary compensation to write this review, just the product itself.

I have a lot of shaving brushes. At this point, it's kind of a collection but in reality, I do actually use them. All of them, however, required a breaking-in period. Boar bristles are the worst offenders because the come smelling like a vaguely washed pig and take forever to break in to be soft. Badger bristles are usually fairly good but still need a breaking-in. To break-in a shave brush, you do what you'd normally do to soften and condition hair: wash it with soap. I soak mine in hot water for 12 hours to loosen any stray strands that would normally come out, then hit it with a puck of shave soap and lather it up hard, then leave the soap in for 24 hours, or more, depending. But I was absolutely astounded by this brush. It was shave ready right from the box.

It's no mean feat to have something "shave ready" out of the box. I felt it and it was buttery smooth and perfectly worked in. I figured that it was a fluke and decided to do my standard break-in treatment. After the 12 hour hot water rinse, NO hairs came out. None. Not a single one. I figured "okay, but once I lather this bad boy then it'll start to shed". Nope. I hit it with a puck of soap so hard it could have turned the soap into diamonds...but no shed. Then, I left the soap in. I figured "well, the soap will loosen the glue holding it in, that'll make it shed."

No. No it did not.

This thing is ready to go right out the gate. I couldn't budge the badger hair knot to save my life. The handle it's attached to is gorgeous, also. It's large and provides a firm grip but is also light weight so you won't fatigue your hand. The brush, in overall size, is about 4-5" so it's definitely no travel brush. But what it is is a thing of beauty. A soft, sturdy brush that you can take out of the box and get right to shaving with. Lathering it is a treat and it holds heat well. My only wish is that the handle wasn't varnished, to improve grip, but that's the only gripe I could come up with and even that's a stretch. This brush is perfect. Sure, you're gonna spend a bit on it. $50 for a non-brand-name brush IS a lot but by gosh does it perform equally or better than brushes in its category. And it has the dopest name ever. Who wouldn't want to shave with a brush named "Professor Fuzzworthy"?!

title: My fingernails are so happy that I bought these files.
text:
As a little girl, I remember admiring my grandmother's long, elegant fingernails. Many an afternoon we spent together at the kitchen table, using old-fashioned emery boards to shape our nails together. Fast forward 30(!) years, and I finally decided to upgrade. Listen, if you're on the fence about whether or not a glass nail file is something you want to invest in, just do it. You wouldn't think they would be very different, or maybe not even work as well, but I think you'll be pleasantly surprised.

The thing that I really love about these files? They leave the edges of my nails so smooth. I can barely tell I've filed my nails at all. Apply more pressure and it behaves like a heavier grit, or use a light touch to finish up - no need for numerous grits anymore! I think this set of five is probably going to last me for the rest of my life, unless I manage to lose them all.

The carrying case they come in is nice, though it's a little bulky for carrying in a small purse. It does make a really nice presentation case, though.

All in all, I wish I had saved myself the headache and bought these sooner. Money well spent.

title: It Works
text:
In the age of COVID, I've been disinfecting just about everything that my hands touch. When I found the SNEGDO Portable Cleaner Bag with UVC, I decided to order it. I put a question mark after my title because I have no idea if this is actually working the way they say it will, because I have no way of testing its effectiveness. This is one time I have to trust that is working, and what I put in it is truly disinfected.

What I can say is, it's very simple to use, and that it cuts off after five minutes. However, I read a review for another item similar to this, and the reviewer was a microbiologist. He said that cotton masks should be left in one of these for about 11 minutes rather than five, so I do three iterations for masks.

Another nice thing is, it folds out, so if you don't use it that often, you can just collapse it and it won't take up much room.

I gave this five stars in hopes that it's doing what it's supposed to.

***UPDATE***

I just discovered that there's a card you can buy to test whether or not a sanitizer is working as it claims. title: Vitamin D3 tablets
text:
These tablets are 7mm wide and small enough to swallow easily. No side effects, and no aftertaste at all. I am taking two of these per day, the label recommends one per day. I always take 2 per day in the winter and I have not seen any negative effects from D3, only positive.

I personally believe everyone should take D3 each day. Even 5000iu will help boost immunity and enhance your mood. Those are easy to see in my life and I haven't been sick for a couple years now and I think vitamin D3 is one of the main reasons. No COVID, no flu, or even a cold. I also take zinc and vitamin C daily as well as a probiotic but that's all. Nothing expensive or complicated. D3 has other supposed health benefits and of course you can get D3 for free from the sun by being exposed to UVB rays. I can't do that during our cloudy winters working in an office all day and one of the first things I noticed when I started taking D3 softgels a couple years ago is that my mood was better after just a few days and it's been more stable ever since.

These tablets are not as small as other D3 doses I've taken, but they certainly aren't too large to swallow for anyone who takes any other pills. I suppose these could be crushed up and eaten with food if you are unable to swallow, I haven't tried it. I'm happy with this D3, there doesn't seem to be any toxic ingredients and nothing is genetically modified.

title: Works well for me

This formula is gluten/soy/chemical free and seems to be made by a reputable company in the USA. Happy with this product so far, I recommend probiotics to everyone and this seems to be a very good one based on my experience.

title: Taste is good, works well
text:
I haven't used a lot of non fluoride toothpastes but I've been wanting to switch and this brand seemed good because I am a fan of Tea Tree oil. The paste is translucent, almost clear and has a fresh minty taste to it. Abrasive particles are used to clean deposits off teeth and gums and it works well with my Sonicare brush.

The tube is a bit smaller than other brands I've used but you only need a small amount as it's very strong. I overwhelmed myself the first time I used it and was sneezing for a few minutes from one of the ingredients. I reduced the amount of paste I used and that didn't happen again so I have no side effects to report when used properly. Good product, and a nice alternative to fluoride toothpastes.

title: Very nice reusable storage containers
text:
These storage containers are fantastic and work just like the name brand ones we've all used. Clear bottom with a see through blue top, and a really nice 24 ounce size that can hold soups or a salad but it's also big enough to hold a sandwich to keep it from getting crushed in a backpack.

The lids seal fairly tight and don't leak under normal conditions. You can microwave these and they made from BPA free plastic. You can also freeze them. I think the best feature with these is they cost less than a dollar each so if you are in a situation where you need to throw one away or leave it at someone's house, it's fine. Or you can use them for years, since they don't really fall apart. They can get scratched up over time but they still work and I put mine in the dishwater with no issues.

It's hard to give these storage containers anything less than 5 stars. They work well, are inexpensive, and are a great size for a variety of foods. You can even use them as storage containers for crafts and hobbies since they stack fairly well. An all around great product, practical and useful for so many things.

It tastes better than expected to be honest, and seems to have the same antioxidants and other benefits of fresh juice. I use about 12 ounces of water, they recommend 8 but it's whatever you prefer.

title: Easy to use, easy to clean, works for pets
text:
Overall, these silicone scrubby straps are a gentle way to clean an area that's generally hard to reach. The side with the short silicone bristles is the side best for scrubbing, while the side with the little domes is better for a light massage. The short bristle side is also better at getting your body wash/soap to foam up than the little dome side.

Neither side is effective at a good, deep scrub like a bristle brush is, but the tradeoff is that you can easily clean and disinfect this strap versus needing to replace the bristle brush-type every couple of months or so. The bristles on these straps are also less harsh on your skin. If you have a problem like psoriasis that can flare up with excessive scrubbing or exfoliation, this product is the better way to go. Thanks to the design, you can also use this to clean the soles of your feet without having to bend down in the shower. For older folks, those who have back injuries, or those with medical conditions that prevent them from doing so (like vertigo), this strap is a safer method. And if you happen to drop this in the shower, the soft silicone isn't going to leave a bruise on your foot like the wooden or plastic handle of a scrub brush would.

This scrubby strap also does a great job at getting the undercarriage of our large breed dog. His coat is super short little eyelash hairs, and the bristles on this are plenty to get down to his skin. Using this to give his tummy a good scrub is SO much easier and faster, and it does a better job than we can do with bare hands. He seems to enjoy it, and will even stand still during these tummy scrub session.

title: Meh...doesn't last
text:
This is a nice vibrating facial cleansing brush, but only while it lasts. The bristles are soft and do a good job of helping your regular cleanser work harder to clean your skin. It's comfortable to use though the brush shape would be better if the end was tapered as right now the end is too large to easily get around your nose folds.

The biggest problem with this brush is that after only a couple weeks of use it completely stops charging. Unlike other rechargeable facial brushes, this one is NOT waterproof. You cannot use it in the shower, or submerge it in water. If any water gets into the charger port, that's it. You have to be extremely careful when using this to wash your face or when rinsing the soap off. Keep your finger tightly pressed down over the charging port, which helps greatly to keep everything dry. My brush didn't die from getting water in the charger. (I 'borrowed' a silicone plug from another facial brush I have and it kept any water or soap from getting into the port. I only removed it charge this brush.) The brush worked fine one day, the next day zip. I thought maybe the charge had run out, so I tried charging it, but nothing happened. Tried another outlet, nothing. Found another charger identical to the one that came with this one (my hubby keeps everything, I swear), and it didn't charge either. Checked to make sure there was nothing in the port, that it was bone dry, and it was clean and dry. This just stopped working. I have a similar brush from Foreo, but unlike this one it has a magnetic charger and the brush unit is completely sealed and waterproof. If this brush from JIANNZT were sealed and had a magnetic charger, it would have been as good as my Foreo and for a better price.

title: Utterly gross
text:
As these are aimed at kids, you think they would make them at least taste good. However, these chewable tablets are anything but. I imagined these would be more like the Emergen-C chewables, but the flavor of these was sour with the most horrid fake orange flavor I've ever come across. I tried one at the same time I gave one to my child, and almost immediately we both spit it out. Maybe if your child has a nose that is so stuffed up they cannot smell a thing and therefore can't really taste anything you could get them to take these, but otherwise I highly doubt it.

Another problem I encountered was how these reacted once the seal was broken. With most chewable vitamins and supplements, a moisture absorbing pack is included in the jar to keep the tablets from clumping together. This particular brand did not, and within a week inside an air conditioned house all of the tablets were clumped into one big ball at the bottom of the container. I had decided to try taking these myself by swallowing like a regular pill instead of chewing, but when I opened the bottle, I knew immediately that the lack of absorbent had come back to bite me in the rear. Since they were tightly sealed and humidity wasn't an issue at the time, I didn't think I would need to go ahead and add an absorbent pack myself (I bought a bag off of Amazon just for this situation), mostly because the manufacturer didn't think the product needed one.

These chewables were a disaster all around, and I can't recommend them.

title: They do work mostly
text:
Since I've started using these my dental hygienist has raved about the condition of my gums. So I'm going to say the technology works. Unfortunately the execution of this particular device leaves something to be desired.

I can't comment on these devices crapping out after one or two uses, but I have found that not all apparently dead ones are in fact done for. I've found that some will come back to life if they're charged correctly.

The little metal pieces must be lined up just so and stay that way during the entire charge cycle. Unfortunately it's very easy to misalign the parts or to jostle them out of alignment. A pair of magnifying eyeglasses and a very steady charging station are invaluable here.

Although this has been a (temporary?) solution for me, this company is crazy to sell a consumer item whose maintenance is so exacting. They could at least warn people to take care when setting up the device for recharge.

Please note that Starlight Smile also sells a corded device. I haven't used one so can't comment, but if recharging this one continues to be a nightmare, I'll probably try it. My gums and my hygienist are happy, and it's worth some trouble to keep that going.

I have never owned a robotic vacuum, so I can only compare this to my experience with what I own which are traditional vacuums.

Pros:

title: Seems to aid elimination and regularity
text: There are many, perhaps most supplements that frankly are just not necessary. If you eat a healthy, mostly plant based diet with quality grown foods, you're probably supplying your nutritional needs already. I like to experiment, though to see if I notice any tangible results in a product, so I gave chlorophyll a go. I like using liquid suppliments because I don't like swallowing pills or tablets and if I have several products, I can add them all to a small amount of water in the morning. But in the constant rush they sometimes are not taken. Gummies seem to be all the rage now and I'm seeing everything now available in gummy form. If you take multiple gummy products you  might be overloading on sugar, so that's a factor. First a note on chlorophyll. Is it necessary? It's said to offer a host of purported benefits, many related to help keep your system clean and detoxified. None of those claims are scientifically substantiated though some studies with animals seem to support that chlorophyll has aided in shrinking some forms of tumor. I don't consume enough plants rich in chlorophyll, like say, spinach because of fear of the oxyllic acid that can have negative effects like kidney stone formation. I tried wheatgrass which is 70% chlorophyll, but I couldn't handle the taste. I've been using these gummies about 2 weeks and have noticed they do seem to help with regularity, which is hugely positive. It causes a strange phenomenon where the bowel movement has the appearance of a moss cover log from a tropical Forrest; sorry if that's too graphic. But that tells me it really is having some effects. As for the gummies themselves, the consistency is firm and easy to chew. I'm not a fan of the taste but it's easily tolerable. The cost per day seems reasonable as well. It this a must have supplement? Probably not if you eat lots of green plants. But I will probably reorder when this order is exhausted. Recommended.

title: Huge fan of Magnesium, BUT this is undrinkable!
text: I've tried several magnesium products over time primarily due to its purported benefits in regard to sound sleeping. As a frequent problem sleeper I was extremely hopeful, and it didn't disappoint. Always experimenting to find effective natural products, I agreed to receive this magnesium to compare it's efficacy. I mixed it in the usual way but noticed particles of various sizes that refused to disolve at all. I took a first sip and had to spew it out into the sink. I checked the glass wondering if it had been used or tainted with something. Nope. The product tastes horrific. I easily consume things like Black Seed Oil that have strong tastes without issue. I could not have a single serving of this. It's that bad. I imagined perhaps my batch might be an outlier, but see at least one other reviewer expressing similar sentiments. So yes, depending on your particular needs and issues you're trying to address, by all means try a magnesium powder product. So sorry, but I cannot recommend this one at all. My package has been disposed of.

title: DHEA has a definite and profound effect, if you are deficient as you grow older.
text: I've gone from a cupful of supplements every day person to the conservative naturalist I am today, believing that your nutrition should come from natural sources, i.e., a healthy diet, primarily plant based. That being said, there are times when, due to age or circumstance, you can be deficient in certain nutrients that might require outside help. Case in point is Vitamin D, which it is said, most of us are deficient in due to modern lifestyles that have us indoors working under artificial lighting most of our waking hours. DHEA is a hormone our bodies naturally produce that is a precursor to both testosterone and estrogen, hormones that produce profound effects on our health, muscle mass, energy level, skin tone, and even degree of passion. As we age, we naturally produce less of it. Nature it seems, believes that past a certain age, since we no longer will be producing offspring, presumably we have already attracted a mate and therefore don't need to have the vibrant glow of health that offers displays that theoretically attract a mate. That's a lame system, but the sad truth. DHEA is somewhat of a debated supplement that everyone should do their due diligence, as in anything before you chose to ingest it. In some circumstances, it can exacerbate or can put you at greater risk for serious health risks according to many health authorities. I personally weighed the evidence and have chosen to use it regularly and can say it has a noticeable and profound effect, being of the baby boomer generation, and accordingly in the testosterone depleted age group. It's very often difficult to know if a supplement is having any effect at all, since the benefits might be so subtle or need many weeks or months to influence our bodies in any noticeable way. Not so with DHEA, at least in my experience. It gives me more energy and feeling more youthful. It induces feelings of sensual interest that may have lapsed under the radar to the point that you did even realize it. As in all new supplements you're adding, its best to experiment to see how they are effecting you, and erring on the low side to begin with. As such, 25 mg might be high for many women or low for some men, depending on your age and circumstance. Again, do your homework. As for this brant, it is new to me but seems to be reputable and safe, so I gave it the full 5 stars. Don't expect anything to reverse aging or be miraculous. But if you want to retain energy, positive mood and muscle mass, especially as you get older, DHEA might be something to investigate and experiment with. Recommended.

title: I find Ashwaganda incredibly effective. This, however had no positive effect.
text: As soon as I read about Ashwaganda I wanted to give it a try so purchased some here on Amazon. Most supplements take time to display any difference in your health or feeling of well being, unless they are designed to combat a known deficiency in your system. But while driving on my long daily commute in hectic traffic one day some time ago, it dawned on me that I had just finished a 12 hour day but all that week I seemed abnormally calm and positive. The Ashwaganda had been the only alteration to my routine so I realized that had to be the factor. Now I recommend it to everyone. Thats why I was intrigued when I saw this product specifically marketing itself as an Ashwaganda replacement as a so called adaptogen. While simply a lay person without a medical background, I still always try to understand the basis for claims made and do my due diligence as much as possible. This product seems to be primarily geared to someone who might be lacking certain things in their metabolism specifically as it relates to the function of their adrenal glands. I included it in my routine hoping to discover another mood and energy enhancing product, but at least for me, failed to detect any difference in mood or energy level. I intentionally excluded Ashwaganda intake since I wanted to not have any beneficial benefits masked. But without medical tests revealing low levels of anything adrenal related I can only assume my body was already in balance at least in that arena. For those in need of a boost as revealed by medical tests, perhaps this will be effective. Especially if they have a negative reaction with Ashwaganda. As for me, I can't report any noticeable change.

title: There’s easier ways to mop than this
text:
I had to delay my review because I simply couldn’t get the top off this bucket and it doesn’t say anything about it in the instructions which is a huge oversight. Thankfully someone mentioned removing the red handle on here and I was able to finally get it so I could use this thing.
Here’s what I like about this mop and bucket set. It’s compact so it fits anywhere. I like the idea of keeping it near the toilet as shown in the photo. The microfiber pads work great. Really mops well and picks up any dirt along the way. It glides under baseboards and into corners like a champ. You can easily control how dry you want the pad so the floor will dry faster. You can even use it as a dust mop if you like. Just throw it in the washer when you’re done. Two pads are included so you can change them out.
Here’s what’s not to like. The pole handle goes together easily in metal sections, but it also loosens as you mop which is frustrating. I would need to tape the joints if I used it all the time. I also found the pole too short for me so I was constantly stooping while mopping. I had way too much trouble removing the top so that I could fill the bucket with water and then dump the dirty water. I practically broke the handle off trying. The bucket is too tall for standard sinks and you have to tip it to fill it. I looked, but could not find a fill line on the side or inside the bucket so I had no idea exactly how much water to put in. I discovered I didn’t put quite enough and part of my pad wasn’t even getting wet. Fitting the mop head into the bucket just right and tugging it up and down to wet and dry it takes more effort than I expected. Pull up too fast and you risk tipping the bucket.
This contraption makes mopping even more of a chore than it already is and I can’t recommend it especially at over thirty dollars. I would take my spin mop and bucket over this any day for the price.

title: Maltodextrin - not organic at all, heavily processed and potentially dangerous
text:
Red flags abound here. At 3.8 g carbs per teaspoon its not KETO or dieter friendly.

And elsewhere on the internet you will find warnings like this

"The high GI of maltodextrin means it can cause spikes in your blood sugar level, especially if it’s consumed in large amounts.

Because of this, you may want to avoid or limit it if you have diabetes or insulin resistance. It should also be avoided if you’re predisposed to developing diabetes. Another reason to limit maltodextrin is to keep your gut bacteria healthy.

According to a 2012 study published in PLoS ONE, maltodextrin can change your gut bacteria composition in a way that makes you more susceptible to disease. It can suppress the growth of probiotics in your digestive system, which are important for immune system function.

The same study showed that maltodextrin can increase the growth of bacteria such as E. coli, which is associated with autoimmune disorders like Crohn’s disease. If you’re at risk for developing an autoimmune or digestive disorder, then avoiding maltodextrin may be a good idea."

This product tastes really good, but you are better off with regular sugar if you don't mind carbs OR the much safer erythritol if you are KETO/reduced carbs

title: Buy the replacement plan!
text: I've used a variety of similar toppers for years and find them relaxing -- not deep massage but good for relaxation. This one is pretty well designed and works well -- when it works. But I have had three fail in less than a year. In each case it seems clear that it was a burnt-out resistor in the controller, a 5-cent part that the Chinese manufacturer probably bought from his crooked cousin. I'm sure that Brookstone is getting pretty tired of replacing them, and maybe someday they'll get tired enough to exercise some quality control (or buy from some place that does not specialize in junk and ripping off the customer). For my part, I paid for the two-year replacement policy, and plan to get my two years regardless of how many Brookstone has to send me.

title: Positive first impression, but could be improved with stirrups
text: I've only gotten this recently and cannot give a very thorough review yet, but since there are so few I thought it might be useful to say what I could. I got this because I have problems with lumbar stenosis and my doctor says I need to strengthen my core muscles. Riding is very good for core development, but the jarring is hard on the spine and of course there are some dangers. This machine provides exercise that seems pretty much like riding but without the jarring and without the danger -- albeit with less fun. I got the two-motor version that does a rocking motion and/or figure-eight motion, separately or in combination. The range of adjustmnent in speed seems adequate. There is also a simple program mode that I have not yet tried. There seems little doubt that I am getting core development from using it and have not experienced any pain. I feel pretty sure that aerobic benefit is very slgight at best. If you want more exercise for your laterals, they suggest sitting with both legs off one side so it rocks you side to side. The big question for me is where to put my feet when riding astride. They suggest holding them clear of the floor with knees bent, which is pretty tiring. Resting them on the floor (which is feasible as long as you are not especially short-legged) somewhat defeats the purpose of the exercise. There is no place to attach stirrup leathers. I am thinking I will connect a pair of stirrup leathers (the narrow English style) end-to-end and hang them across the saddle at the front, with a stirrup iron on each side.

title: A good convenient TENS unit with more straightforward intuitive control than most.
text: In a market full of similar products, one must differentiate oneself from the competition.  This unit does that very well.  The combination of the LCD display (which other units have), and buttons labeled with body parts that each define special programs for the particular areas is what sets it apart.  Instead of just dialing up numbers and programs that might work for an area, a designed program made for these is a good thing.  I can still try all of the programs, but (assuming they know what the medical needs are most common) the TENS programing should be more targeted.  Unit came with batteries, but they typically don't last long if you use high intensity, but programmable cells will work.  I don't see a lot of these that use rechargeable Lithium batteries, but that might just make it all the more confusing given you already have to deal with wires and plug-in pads.  I tried a few of the programmed area buttons, and the targeting seemed good.  Recommended.

title: My doctor suggested I take this kind of supplement, but I'm lazy taking the capsules.

title: Have to take at different times a day than my Thyroid meds, but it definately works for foot pain.
text:
I've only recently made in roads in reversing type 2 diabetes, getting a clean A1C for the first time in years. Neuropathy and pain in the feet still remain and vary in intensity on a daily basis. I've noticed that ALA is a major benefit in nearly eliminating that pain. Although I've taken in the past, it seemed only marginally effective, however this stabilized type seems much better. It the absorption numbers are true, that might explain the almost immediate effects of this supplement on foot pain from Neuropathy.

I take this just an hour or so before lunch, whereas I take my thyroid synthoid before bed. While they don't technically interact chemically, ALA is known to reduce the action of synthoid or natural thyroid hormone in the body, so do not overtake or take together if you use thyroid meds. Well sourced, and not stomach upsetting, especially important since should take on an empty stomach. The type here is "stabilized" which they assert is 40 times more viable to absorption over non-stabilized. Given how fast it relieves my foot pain, I believe it. Inexpensive as well, recommended.

title: With my girth I'm very glad they increased the length, I could probably use it longer still.
text:
Nice, easier to control than a back brush, and gentler on the skin as well. I used it two places I can't reach easily, my lower legs and my lower back area. I was without a shower for several months while they worked to convert my bathtub into one. I can't step over a tub wall without extreme difficulty, and getting out of a tub is near impossible so I don't take baths. This is easy to pass between hands with the dual handles and move in a back and forth scrubbing motion. There are two grades of bristles, some silicon mini nubs that are very very soft, and some stiffer larger nubs for an exfoliate action.

My lower leg skin on my shins started to flake off like shedding a snake skin. After a few showers unable to reach there I was peeling off pieces of dried skin about the size of a quarter. I poured on some body wash with the stiffer nubs and used this to shave off the rest of the dead skin. It did a nice job, my skin in sensitive there, most of the brushed I have will irritate that area rather than exfoliate. It reaches the small of my back rather well, an seems to allow enough body wash to lather up the area to clean properly. I don't have anyone to help me wash my back so this is a nice tool for the bath or shower. It's a little trickier to get the top of the back I have to use on cross angles to do that, but it's still works. I could use this at closer to 35 inches instead of the 29, but it's better than some of the sorter, rough brushes I've used. I get some cramping when trying to reach over the back to scrub the lower area with a brush, and there is no problem with this. The handles make it easy to hang on a hook when not in use and the light weight does not unbalance my shampoo caddy I have on the fixed shower head. Recommended.

title: Contents good, taste bad, not really awful, so you probably don't have to worry about kits overdose.
text: Funny taste, it was not bad enough to spit out, but it was not good either.  A danger many don't realize is if you give your kid some sort of gummy single or multi-vitamin, and they are too young to realize what it it, it becomes candy if they find the bottle. It may even have an effect with COVID19, but there is currently no data on that, but it is one of the few things that has an effect versus viruses.  Of course vitamin see just keeps your immunity strong and provides the building block to repair common cellular damage in the body, so it's a must.  Cold and Flu season are coming soon, so a good product to have even if you can't eat them like candy, fair price.  Recommended

title: A lot of benefits from Elderberry, not all can be integrated into gummies, but safe, easy to take.
text:
It would be nice if you could get a way to preserve all the benefits of the berries, but that's not possible. The berries themselves are coated with a poison that's not too dangerous in small mounts, but the other part of the plants are very bad. Some of the beneficial effects probably lost during the conversion to gummies are fiber for one, that may be an assumption on my part, but they don't list it on the bottle, so it's likely true. I'd say next a certain proportion of the antioxidants are not carried over. Fresh uncooked berries would retain a lot more antioxidants than processed ones. I know from my past history as a juicer, that once the fruit or veggie is juiced the concentration of antioxidants drops very quickly from hours to only a day or so depending on the method.

Still there are a lot of benefits left, from mood enhancing to digestion, to vitamin C, enough of the health benefits remain to want to use an easy way to take Elderberry. This particular version is somewhat unusual as most seem to use blueberry as a flavoring for Elderberry gummies, but this brand uses raspberry. I like that they are sugar coated on the outside as gummies can stick together and be a pain to dig out of the bottle that way. My usual caution is in effect because they taste good and can be harmful if you take too many. Adults should resist eating too many, and put away so your kids don't find a great new gummy candy that can hurt them if they consume the bottle. With these precautions in place. Recommended.

title: Gives decent support for those who have a problem with slouching and others with medical issues.
text:
I'm a bit big to try this out and have decent posture anyway, so I had my friend put it on today. I ordered it with her in mind as she'd been complaining of shoulder pain. She'd had rotator cuff surgery not too long ago, and the pain was back. She had problems sleeping on her side with the pain. I mentioned this to her and she said her doctor has told her about similar devices that helped maintain posture. I've ordered and used compression straps for my forearms to alleviate and allow healing for tennis elbow, so I know how a little support helps. Anyway, she tried it on and said she immediately felt two inches taller. The support was there and it helped with the pain immediately. The device came with two pads, but didn't have any explanation for them. I thought they might be shoulder pads, but later read on the product page they were for the arm pits. They wrap around and velcro the strap there so it doesn't make that area tender.

I think the best thing about this she thought besides the support and pain relieve was how light it is. She is still working and on her feet all day inspecting electronic components for a local firm with government contracts for critical plane parts. With this she can wear under her clothes and maintain good posture all day working while her muscles heal. Thus avoid the bad things of taking NSAID painkillers and other things that become chronic problems instead of solutions. Going on her experience, I recommend this device, it's inexpensive and does it's job well.

title: Feel good antioxident at decent price, a little goes a long way.
text: I sometimes don't know why I get on a healthy kick thats working then get off it and forget about it for too long.  In the 90's I used Spirulina a lot, usually in tomato juice or just plain water.  I got about four ounces from a health food bulk store, and a teaspoon per mix lasted nearly 50 servings.  Other than some coloring of my stools, it did nothing but make me feel better.  I used it for about six months and didn't have a stomach ache or upset the whole time.  The rest of my diet was much worse, but if the pipes work good the digestive system can handle a lot.  This is tolerable, nothing strong about the taste, and it blends well with vegetable oriented juices.  Not recommended for fruit juice, and milk is maybe a toss up.  If your juicing veggies it works well for those veggie blends as well.  Recommended for those who like veggie drinks.

title: Color me impressed, I expected not to like this thinking it would be cheap, but it was great.
text:
I have a shower filter by one of the more prominent makers. The problem was it restricted water flow a lot, and the filter replacements cost as much as this whole assembly. I couldn't believe the filtering tech going on here. Fifteen stages , really, and designed in an order to filter out the bad stuff and finish up the purification in the end. It probably doesn't filter our fluorine, bus that is something that some people like and others do not. It generally needs a reverse osmosis filter to remove it anyway.

Like my other shower filter, I thought this (especially with so many stages) would slow my waterflow in the shower to a trickle. It did not do that the flow although slightly restriced was nothing like my other filter. This one lasts longer too 4-6 months per filter cartridge and you get too. I didn't price them, but since the device and two filters cost more than one filter replacement from my old shower filter, I figured I could not go wrong here. The water even tasted good when I rinse my mouth (I usually brush my teeth and shave while showering). I love it, recommended. Frankly if they can get this much water flow for a shower filter, why not use these types for those passive filter pitchers I have in my fridge. It might take a bit longer to filter through, but the result would be worth it.

title: Great product as good as the name brand, and an inexpensive as you could get without being free.
text:
Seems to work as good or better than the leading brand, I use Petroleum Jelly for areas of my skin that gets chafed or irritated due to clothing or skin to skin contact. I use three things actually P Jelly, A&D Ointment, and an antibiotic cream, it all depends on what the redness seems to be caused by and if it's swelling. All three of those products have the effect of sealing the skin from air and moisture. I believe this inhibits bacterial growth on the skin and promoted healing. Amazon's brand here like the big V brand is basically a protectant, it's among the best to be used in areas just starting to chafe. If you are starting to be inflamed, then A&D will do some healing, and if the infection is bad, go with the antibiotic cream.

This earns its fifth star for the price the price Amazon is selling this for seems to me like it's below cost, so if you use the stuff, this is a huge supply for under 8 bucks on the current list price for 4 large jars of the stuff. If I had any complaint it would be that some of the product leached out a little in the shipping, and seeped into the cardboard, but it was little and no harm done except new stuff should be a bit better sealed. The four were sealed in plastic, but it still leaked through that. Recommended, great for covering burns, sores, any type of skin issue, with no chemical effects.

title: Fair price and a good cleansing and conditioning shampoo, not for everyone, don't recommend with children, or allergic.
text:
The odor takes a bit of getting used to, but all the aloes, oils, extracts and especially the activated charcoal, which since it's listed first meaning it's the most prevalent ingredient, do a nice job of cleaning and conditioning the hair. I have to use a dermatologist prescribe shampoo to take help take care of a scalp skin condition, and I like to follow it up with something, but my dandruff shampoo is a bit harsh for use after that. This is milder than you'd think and contains a number of things that act as a conditioner. Activated charcoal is often used with pets, and sometimes humans to negate and get rid of poison if swallowed. It works equally well as an outside purifier, often you find it in those Brita or other water purifying pitchers because of the cleansing effects.

This shampoo is gray and smells very much like medicine, but not as bad as lye soap, and the natural barks and other substances give some temper to the smell, it's no worse than a strong anti-dandruff shampoo, but milder and better for your hair. I think this would work better than my swim shampoo to take out the stiffness and effect of pool chlorine as well, so I'll try it next time I go swimming at a hotel. The cost is no bargain, but on the other hand, it's not much more than many dandruff shampoos. From what I can see a little goes a long way. title: The Beats are Back!
text:
I've used my Ion Tailgater a lot over the years, for picnics, events, even while working in the yard, and almost always on battery, so it was a great disappointment a few weeks ago when I turned it on and, after just a few minutes, got nothing but noises and distortion. Thankfully, it didn't take long to pin the problem down to a worn-out battery, and when I found the Unicell TL1245 F1 Replacement Battery on Amazon I ordered it immediately. In a few days - well ahead of the estimated delivery date - the new battery arrived; I installed it in a few minutes, plugged in the Tailgater to charge the new battery, and by that evening was rocking again.

The Unicell TL1245 F1 Replacement Battery is very slightly larger than the battery I took out; while the original came from the factory with strips of foam tape to keep it from rattling in the battery box, the Unicell replacement was a snug - but not too tight - fit and required no foam tape cushioning. Otherwise, the new battery seems to be a perfect replacement for the original, giving the same operating time and the same low-distortion volume levels. I had worried that a new battery might cost so much as to not be worth doing, but this was certainly not the case.

title: Easy, healthy whitening strips
text:
I shy away from most of the "heavy-duty" whitening strips/ gels because I prefer to use more natural products, so I was excited to try these whitening strips from Moon, which use hydrogen peroxide combined with a blend of health-promoting botanical ingredients. My teeth aren't badly stained, but I drink a lot of coffee and tea and they definitely aren't as white as they used to be! This package contains 56 strips, enough for 2 weeks of twice-daily use on top and bottom teeth. I'm about a week in, and seeing improvements already! Even more important, they're not causing any issues for my teeth, gums or mouth. I have sensitive gums, and experience some discomfort from certain brands of toothpaste, but these strips don't have any ill effects for me.

The strips are individually wrapped, and easy to position on your teeth. Once you've got them where you want them, they'll take about 15 minutes to dissolve, leaving a pleasant minty flavor behind with no residue. They do turn a bit tacky while they work, so I only use them when I can get away with not talking for 15 minutes, usually right before bed and after I've brushed my teeth in the morning. I feel reassured knowing that all the ingredients are safe to ingest.

My only complaint so far is that I wish the strips were a tiny bit longer - there are some stains on teeth they don't quite reach when I apply them front and center. Granted, I'm probably the only one who notices these, but I feel like they'll be more noticeable by contrast with my freshly whitened front teeth! It's a minor issue though, and I'd definitely use these again over other types of whitening products.

I'll update this review with progress photos once I've finished the full 2 weeks!

text:
So, I saw this advertised on TV and immediately thought of my slow bathroom sink. I'll admit, the phrase, "you are SO gullible" drifted through my mind, but I found it on Amazon and decided to give it a try. It arrived today.
After some wiggling, I got it into the drain, twisted it around, and tried to pull it back out. It got stuck. After a few more wiggles and several more refrains of "you are SO gullible and now you broke the sink," I found the proper angle and pulled out... THE THING. I'm quite certain the thing was sentient, and evil. It looks like it was nearly ready to either crawl from the drain and start eating my neighbors, or maybe run for Congress. I'm ever so grateful I didn't have to disentangle THE THING from the wand. Instead, I detached the wand, briefly considered killing THE THING with fire, then finally wrapped it in paper towel and threw it away. With luck, I destroyed it BEFORE it was able to bring our civilization to an end. And my sink drains again.
If you need to unclog your drain -- and possibly save the human race from THINGS -- I highly recommend this product.

title: It Half-Works
text:
Put in 3 "super heavy duty" AAA cells @ 1.32v. It charged them for a few minutes then said "Full". But they only increased to 1.37v. Useless.

Tried 3 other heavy duty AAAs @ 1.31v. Wouldn't charge them at all. Said "Exausted". Totally useless.

Tried several D "Alkaline" batteries @ 1 volt. It began charging any placed in the left side, but none in the right side. Two of them increased from 1.0v to 1.18v, the third one from 1,0v to 1.21v. Useless again.

This time needed 2 different name-brand AA alkalines charged. First one charged from 1.36v to 1.49v. Good. Second one went from 1.37v to 1.47v. Good.

A few weeks later after that one of them leaked in a flashlight. The other is still fine. This is why manufacturers say not to rechare them.

I've seen top-brand alkaline batteries recharged. Durracell Energizer Rayovac and the cheapo Super Heavy Duty brands. For each brand a few leaked and a few didn't.

Alkalines don't like being recharged, except the rechargable alkalines.

So this charger does poorly with batteries that are more than half dead, but works good with ones that haven't been drained much.

First, pull on the tape and circumvent your waistline; make it as loose as possible, leaving enough space to fit your hand between your stomach and the tape. In the product picture there is a pocket where you can hook the tape extremity you just pulled; insert it in the pocket. Once completed there is a button below the symbol "MYOTAPE". Press it. It will retract the tape, tightening it around your waist. Make sure the tape is nicely snugged around the outermost part of your stomach, and use a mirror in order to read the measurement.

I would recommend this tape to anyone who wants a fancy body tape. But on serious note, a singer tape measure is just as efficient in my opinion. $4 vs $10. You make the call.

text:
As my husband and I hit our 40's we started feeling the effects that we weren't as young as we thought we were in our heads! The aches and pains started creeping in, but we decided that we weren't going to let it take us sitting down. We've both been trying to work out together and have been getting some equipment that we can use at home. While we already have some bigger pieces, we also wanted to supplement them with things like a jump rope. I was very surprised at how lightweight this jump rope was when it arrived, but at the same time the weight didn't prevent its performance. It can go fast! Currently I have a jump rope at home that came free with a weighted ball and it was also very lightweight. However, that particular jump rope is very hard to use. The "rope" part of it is wrapped in rubber and doesn't straighten out all the way. It is also hard to get a fast rate going. I often felt like I was just skip jumping like a child. That wasn't the case with this jump rope. The cable stays straight and allows it to move fast. I also liked that it can be adjusted to size by sliding the screws down and cutting it (though it does require a hacksaw or wire cutter to cut through the cable) and they have included easy instructions to do that. The handles have a good grip and allow it to swing nicely. It coils up nice and small so it can easily be brought along to workout outside or at the gym.

text:
This product suffers from poor industrial design. In the first place when I first opened the box I was stunned at the need to have a usb to ac adapter in order to charge. Who charges their toothbrush from a usb outlet? Who plugs their toothbrush into a laptop.
But the real problem is the schizophrenic performance of the device. A little after two months of use, the water floss feature completely stopped working- most likely because I neglected to use it for sometime. The performance of the motor, which they explain needs to lubricated or some other such nonsense, only deteriorated from there.
First the brush would turn off while brushing, sporadically-causing me to reset it. And then it seemed to get stuck in one mode-the brush makes a noise like a broken jalopy now where once it produced a quiet hum. It seems the motion in the brush head has stopped altogether.
Yes they offer troubleshooting tips, filling it up with water didn’t seem to work.
All in all why did they make the decision to incorporate such a poor motor?
My device had a lifespan of 3 months-I’ve used 15 dollar electric toothbrushes that lasted twice as long-years even.
Let’s not even mention that the water floss feature before it stopped working was a serious hassle. You have to worry about tipping the cup over constantly or running out of water.
I hardly ever gripe. I always try to see the redeeming features in every product I use because I know at the end of the day, most companies are doing their best to make products that make their customers happy.
But this toothbrush simply doesn’t work as it’s supposed to-even with the inconvenience of water flossing Id probably have given them a five star rating.
All in all they need to go back to the drawing board with this on

text: I've seen these sponges in a few videos, a mom stripping off loads of dirt & dead skin from her kid in the bath just using a sponge on his skin. I was absolutely shocked that the cute little sponge removed so much dead skin from a clean arm & without any pain at all. Before using the sponge on the rest of me, I took a regular shower with body wash on a mesh body poof. Then I went all over with the sponge. title: I'm not wowed enough to eliminate razors + UPDATE
text:
First of all, let me say that this wasn't as painful as I had been expecting. Not comfortable but definitely tolerable. This took a while to ship to me, so I had plenty of time to grow out the hair on my legs to give it a test run. Perhaps I let my hair get a little too long because even though this definitely removed most of the hair on my ankles and calves, it didn't give me a smooth result at all. I think it broke some of the hairs close to the skin, causing some stubble that the epilator couldn't pull out with more passes.

It did come with directions but they were pretty basic. Nothing mentioning the desired starting length of hair before using. I did no preparation before using. Unboxed it and gave it a go.

My skin is pretty dry and flaky from the winter air. As I was using it, I could see my dry skin flaking off with the plucked hairs. It took many passes to get both legs (knee to ankle done). Took about 15 minutes. The after result was really ashy skin that was pretty itchy with some minor redness at some of the follicles.

I will attempt to use this again after a hot shower and good exfoliation to see if I achieve a better result. I did give my legs another pass over the stubble left behind with the shaver head and that didn't make anything any smoother. I did use it on my partner's back of neck and it did remove hair but he flinched a few times from the shaver head grabbing and pulling a few of the longer hairs. After a few passes, he ran and refused to allow me to test the product on him any further.

The product itself is not junk but it's not high quality either. The clear covers for each head don't fit snugly and fall off easily. The box it came in is really basic, nothing you would want to keep to store the device, attachments, brush and charging cable in. It did arrive already charged. I ran it for about 20-30 minutes and did not notice any slowing down or lag in the motor.

So far, I don't think that this will replace shaving for me but instead will be another tool in my hair removal arsenal. I have noticed that my legs have remained mostly hair free after using it. I haven't had to shave again in the week after using this.

I feel as this might be a cheaper, less effective epilator than other more expensive models, but can't say for certain as this is the first I've tried. Inexpensive way to see if you can tolerate this method of hair removal to see if purchasing a better unit is worth your time/expense. I don't have the nerve to try this on my bikini area but will attempt it on my armpits after a warm shower to see if I can tolerate it.

I will continue using this but when I come across a higher quality product, I will definitely be upgrading and passing this budget epilator along to my daughter for her to try before purchasing one for herself.

UPDATE: I attempted to use this on my armpits. While the pain factor was tolerable on my legs, I could not withstand the pain it caused while using it on my underarms. However, I came back to give this product one more star. Since using this product on my legs, I have not needed to shave my legs whatsoever. I'm due to give my legs a touch up soon, but I am tickled with how long my hairless legs have lasted. It took a while to do both legs the first time but with how long the results have lasted, I've saved myself so much time and effort in the long run. It's a very worthwhile investment.

title: My cats think this is a water dish...
text:
Pro:
Great packaging.
Awesome looking product.
Maneuverability, especially for small hands/children.
Pretty lights.
"big" tank.

Con:
Missing a lot of tips. This only comes with 2 basic tips and a tongue tip. No ortho, no brush, no varied sizes.
Open-top means my cats think this thing is a water dish for them with a string-toy on the side. Probably going to get chewed through at some point.
While you can flip the water tank over, you cannot secure it without unlocking and removing the hand unit/tubing.
When in travel pack mode I was unable to get the pick(s) to fit inside, and they were awkward lumps inside the travel bag.
Stiff cord makes it's length less lengthy. (hopefully it'll soften up a bit)

Verdict:
I can't say this is a bad unit, I just wanted so much to love it and it has quite a few drawbacks. I missed that it was open-topped (that's on me, it's clearly advertised) when I got it and thought it would be cool to have this thing ready to go at any moment, filled with water and a splash of germ-killing mouth wash to keep it from growing anything inside. That got dashed the second I realized it would be a water dish for my cats and would be ruined fast since one of my cats washes her paws (kitty litter mouth-wash anyone?) in the water dishes.
If the lid were flippable on the fly it would be great, but the cord attachment blocks the tank from sitting properly upside down.

It's still a nice unit, just less versatile than it seems. It is a little premium in price and certainly shines/looks premium but delivers average instead.

In the end ask yourself if this open top is for you. It's easier to fill for sure, and more maneuverable. Probably good for braces (but why no ortho-tip?) I think a simple lid and additional tips (perhaps they sell them, I'll have to look later) would make this well worth the money.
