title: Lets enjoy some TMI time...
text:
What you get is a box just like the one in their picture. Inside are 50 individually wrapped NOT CANDIES. I swear you could probably toss these in a bowl at halloween and kids would think (until they tasted it, I assume) that these are lemon candies of some sort. As you can see the individual pieces don't have any indication that they are NOT for consumption, or even what they are.

This is great for discretion I suppose, and the lemon smell doesn't smell like food lemon, but more like cleaning supply lemon, so hopefully no kids will eat these.

Anyway, you plop one into the toilet and it seems to kinda fizz a bit like a weak alka-seltzer and the smell of lemon is there. It's mild. Not overpowering at all, which gives concern for it's effectiveness after an Irritable Bowel meets Dairy Allergies evening of discomfort.

First, if you're in a rush (which I sometimes am due to having IBS) grabbing a pellet and ripping the (pretty sturdy plastic) packaging off and dropping it in the toilet might be the last thing on your mind.

Furthermore, it states if you get this on your skin to wash it off immediately. Easy enough at home, but why bother there? Isn't this for when you're at work and don't want to embarrass yourself after the company chili pot-luck takes it's revenge? I suppose if you're just at a friends house trying not to peel paint in their guest bathroom it's fine?

Anyway, it plop-fizzes before you plop-whiz and to it's credit I would say that I mostly smell just the faint aroma of lemon. Occasionally a whiff of my own brew would break through, but nothing too shocking.

Also to it's credit I allowed my last creature feature to stew for a solid 5 mins after I was done and came back to a still mostly lemon smelling bathroom. NOT BAD!

On the not so great side, is if you have ever used a Bidet, which I do, I'm assuming others have also noticed while it's spraying your dark side after a particularly unpleasant deuce-drop, the spray can kick up the smell as it splashes those particles off you and into the bowl. I can attest, these pellets being in the bowl and not up where the Bidet sprays, they do NOTHING to combat that aroma besides jazz it up with a hint of lemon.

At the time of writing this review the price is about 32 cents per potty break. I'm not convinced that this is something I'd use often, but perhaps if you're still young and dating and trying NOT to scare off a potential future spouse, or if you have exceptionally foul aromas.

title: First impression
text:
Pro - after a little more than an hour in -17°F freezer almost no frost build up on outside of mask and double layer mask also stayed almost completely dry inside. Works to keep face and nose warm.

Con - just barely able to get hook and loop sections of mask to grab on to hook/loop sections of thermal lined shoulder length hood I purchased to go with this. I'm not a very big person, and I don't have a jutting chin/larger nose, I can imagine it might be impossible for someone to make this mask stay attached to the head gear it's meant to go with. However, for the price it is pretty comfortable and might be worth adding either some hook/loop tabs on either side or perhaps stitching on an elastic band to go all the way around your head.
Also, I find that it does fit/feel a bit different right side up and upside down (RSU meaning with the tags on the upper part, USD with the tags down) I find it more comfortable for my face USD.

So, comfortable, warm, and keeps icy damp from building up, but you might need minor modifications to make it comfortable for you. Still worth the price point I paid (under $5 US)

title: Comfortable, easy to use, and clean. Great product
text: Since the pandemic, I have had to wear masks for a good part of my day. I was looking for a good option in order to protect the back of my ears from wear especially since I had surgery behind one of my ears. I found this product. The price point cannot be beat. You get FIVE straps/extended/ear protectors in the package.  They are fully adjustable with many knobs. I have a lot of hair and a big head and I use the last knob but the inner knob would be fabulous for a child's head. I definitely believe these would work well for kids through adults.  You simply place the elastic of your mask around the knobs and then slip it over your head. I have worn mine under my hair and over it. I also have worn mine under the ear completely or around the ear higher up. Either way has worked well. These are extremely comfortable to wear and to use and I have not had a problem with them tangling my long hair. I keep one in my purse. They are easy to sanitize as they are fully cleanable with wipes or disinfectant. They seem very durable and indestructible. They stretch well and very rubbery so I believe they will last forever.

title: Awesome Vibrating Massager for AROUND Your Eyes. GREATLY Helps Relieve Sinus Headaches and Migraines! Powerful & Soothing.
text:
Ok, I'll admit when I first saw this, I was a bit... frightened?! Hahaha. For some reason I pictured the little nodes moving in and out and was like, how is this safe? But they don't move. The whole thing just vibrates. It has 9 Programs (or variations of vibrations)

So, TO CLARIFY, this massages AROUND your eyes... not your eyes directly.. as that would just be dangerous.

I deal with sinus headaches a lot, so I'm always looking for devices that might provide some relief. THIS thing is awesome!

The vibrations are strong and it really just gets all the right spots around your eyes to loosen up all that tension!

It does put pressure around your eyes, so I could see some people not liking it for that if they're not used to it.

I am definitely used to it because pressure on these areas is one of the only things that seems to give me relief sometimes. (I discovered once after putting one of those long stretchy ice packs around my head that the tighter I wrapped the strap part around my brow bone, the better it felt... so sometimes my husband will come home to find me with... pretty much anything wrapped around my head trying to get rid of a migraine... headbands, sleep masks, long socks, bras... just whatever's on hand, lol. But THIS DEVICE IS FAR SUPERIOR!)

I'm so glad I took the leap and bought this! It's very relaxing. It IS loud because the vibration is pretty strong; but the loosening of the muscles achieved by the vibration makes it not really a thing. Basically, pop a couple ibuprofen or tylenol, put this on and relax. Your headache will melt away. At least mine do. (Or if you want to speed things along, take one of the migraine pills that have ibu, tylenol or aspirin WITH a bit of caffeine.) I think that JUST this around eye massager would work for someone really interested in not taking any pills; but I'm not a hero, haha. When I have a migraine I just want it gone.

Anyway, I hope this helps a fellow migraine sufferer somewhere. The other thing I do to get migraine relief is to actually use a back massager on my head... like a percussion massager. There is a technique to it... you have to ease into it or it IS jarring. The reason I do this is because for some crazy reason... the TOP of my head also holds a lot of tension (crazy, I know!). So if you get this around eye massager and you're still having trouble.. try to massage the rest of your head with your hands and see if the combination helps.

Bottom line: This is a GREAT TOOL for easing migraine or sinus headaches. Now that I have it, I would NOT want to be without it. It has a strong vibration that hits all the right spots for sinus issues.

I purchased this MLMSY Electric Eyes Massage Machine at a discounted price in order to test it out and provide my honest and unbiased review. I am not paid by nor am I affiliated with the company in any way. As with all my reviews, if something stops working, gives an adverse reaction or changes in any way with continued use I will absolutely update this review.

title: Struggled to Breath While Wearing This! Only Get This If You Are SUPER AWESOME at Breathing ONLY Through Your Nose!
text:
I have been struggling with what to rate this chin strap. I mean, the product does what it says in the sense that,, yeah, it holds your chin up so your mouth is closed. HOW that is supposed to help with snoring though... I just don't get it. Because it eliminates the ability to breath through your mouth entirely.

I don't mind my husband's snoring; but I'm concerned for his health because he definitely has sleep apnea. He won't see a doctor for it because he doesn't want to use a cpap machine. *sigh* So, I've got him a mouthpiece that lifts his jaw which he hated and says he can't sleep with it. So I was REALLY hoping this might work.

But it does NOT seem to help his breathing at all. And for people that would get this to make their snoring quieter... I don't think it works for that either because the sounds that were coming out of my husband when he wore this... were NOT quiet. As a matter of fact, I woke him up to take this strap off because I was afraid he might die without being able to breath through his mouth. (Maybe that's irrational; but he was really struggling to breath while he was sleeping which is what I was trying to FIX... not make worse.)

So, I don't know, maybe this might work for some people with incredibly clear nasal passages or something. But for us, it's just not helping. The only way we could use this is if somehow I could get him to wear this in combination with a snorkel, hahaha!

So, my search continues for something to help my stubborn but wonderful husband.

I received this DrSleepwell Chin Strap for free in order to test it out and provide my honest and unbiased review. I am not paid by nor am I affiliated with the company in any way. title: Toothpaste in Shaving Gel Form
text:
I saw this on sale when I was shopping one day and decided to try it since I was running low on regular tubed toothpaste. I typically am a fan of Aquafresh toothpaste in general.
After using this product for a few days, I am not impressed.
The first time I used it, it was tough to press the button to release the paste and ended up getting a good amount onto the sink rather than the toothbrush. It comes out as fast as shaving gel and it is tough to control it to land on the toothbrush. Also, similar to shaving gels, after you are done dispensing, there is a little bit of it that leaks out. If you use shaving gel from similar aerosol cans daily, you know what I'm talking about.

It was an okay brushing experience but this stuff FOAMS, A LOT.
You definitely need less with this toothpaste gel, but it's really hard to control how much goes on your toothbrush in the first place!
By the time I am done brushing, I look like I have rabies because it literally just foams in your mouth.

It does leave your mouth feeling minty and clean, but I do not think I would buy again unless they improved the dispensing mechanism and make it a bit less foamy.

title: Six Minute Solution
text:
I appreciate Palmer's as a brand, so when I saw this hair removal cream, I leapt at the chance to try it. While it does have a strong smell, the smell disappears once the cream is washed away. The instructions suggest leaving the cream to set for 3 minutes and adding an additional 2 minutes if needed. I find that 5-6 minutes works best for me, and then I remove it with a cloth dipped in warm water. All the hair is removed in one pass, and I have a very smooth finish afterward with no threat of irritation or the hyperpigmentation that using a razor can cause. Even in areas of varying sensitivity, I find this product to be an easy to use, easy to clean, easy to maintain, quick and painless method of hair removal. This is definitely my preferred depilatory cream now. I only withheld two stars from its rating because the formula is too strong to use on my face as well, but the product only promises hair removal for legs, bikini, and underarms, so technically it does exactly as promised.

*update to 5 stars*
I haven't gone back to razors, wax, or Nair and I probably never will. This is my holy grail now.

title: Good Value for what it is
text:
Pros:
Much more affordable than Waterpik
Smaller footprint in my small bathroom.
Comes with a base that holds brush, brush head, and flosser head
Replacement heads are comparable with original Waterpik replacement heads prices

Cons
You need to provide your own wall plug -not a big deal for me because I had extras
If you're rushing and don't put the brush in the stand correctly, it won't charge.
If the battery is too low, it won't do the deep clean at the high speed.
I often hit the mode button when I meant to press the power button which means I have to scroll through the modes to get back to my preferred setting.
Replacement heads are cheaper than Waterpik but more expensive than off brand replacement heads.
Only 1 tip. Less tip variety than Waterpik. Doesn't have tongue scraper, Plaque Seeker, Pik Pocket, or Orthodontic tip.
Even and high speed, it's much weaker than the Waterpik on the low speed.

I had a Waterpik Complete Care Water Flosser and Sonic Toothbrush, WP-900 since February 2016 because I was too lazy to floss. I wasn't good about using the water flosser. I mostly used the toothbrush because my dental hygienist said the water flosser was a good supplement, but shouldn't replace normal flossing. I really liked that brush even though it stopped holding a charge after a few years. My daughter needed a water flosser so I gave her mine, and I decided to get this combination. I almost bought a different brush because it was lavender instead of blue, but I bought this one because it came with a base that would house the brush, brush head, and flosser head.

title: MMMMMM....smooth, clean teeth :)
text:
Having been turned on to the anti-inflammatory properties of Neem I went looking for a natural toothpaste containing it.
This item caught my eye because I still recall the superior cleaning of baking soda/salt tooth powder back in the day.

I also recalled the gaggifying taste of that cleaning duo. Thankfully this tooth powder has all the gentle scrubbing properties and tastes a million times better.

It is cinnamon flavored. And not that sickly, chemical cinnamon you experience in most mainstream toothpastes. Instead it tastes like there is just enough honest- to- goodness cinnamon in it to flavor it without making it "hot".

Your teeth feel smooth and look whiter after just one use. After a few uses any little areas on my gums that had looked inflamed were totally healed.

Now for the cons:

It did have a tendency to make my mouth feel a little dry after using no matter how well I rinsed. To be expected with a natural astringent like Neem I suppose.

I was a little worried that the same thing that made it whiten immediately might make it a bit too abrasive for my horrifyingly expensive ,and therefore pampered, dental crowns. I have solved this by using this powder sparingly on those teeth.

I didn't love the bottle this came in. Instructions state to wet your brush and sprinkle the powder on the brush. I found that when you do that all the powder has a tendency to fall between and to remain at the bottom of the bristles. To fix this I put a portion of the powder in my dry hand and dipped my damp brush into the powder and that placed the powder on top of the bristles. At least until I hit the on switch on my electric toothbrush!

All in all I am very happy with this product and will be reordering it...soon since my husband keeps swiping it!

title: Support Hose for the Wild at Heart
text:
My friend gave me a pair of these (in a different pattern) for my 70th birthday. She called them psychedelic support hose. I loved the pattern and the support so I immediately looked to see if I could find them on Amazon. I have had varicose veins since I was in my 30s and these compare to the support in regular ugly compression hosiery. I will be ordering more of these I only wish there were more patterns eligible for Amazon Prime Shipping. I always receive compliments on them. I am hesitant to try the next level of compression since the 8-15 seems just right for me and are not overly tight at the top. In case it helps anyone decide on the compression level they want to try, I am 5 foot, 5.5 inches and 115 pounds.
UPDATE: As of now, I have about 5 pair of Celeste Stein stockings. They have all been good. The Austin Powers pattern is my favorite. I have worn them so much they have faded out some but are still quite attractive.

title: Worth Trying For Me
text:
I take so many different vitamins and supplements (nearly 10 or more...Vitamin C, B, E, D, magnesium, potassium, liver supplement, etc.) and I work out six days a week, so I can't say for sure what one specific pill is doing for me. I'm using all of this together and am extremely healthy. So that's why I can't for certain give 5 Stars, but a strong 4.

There isn't anything wrong with this product and I will continue taking it. I buy it here from Amazon because of this mix of L Carnitine with Tartrate.

I'm no scientist, but I'm copying and pasting the conclusion of a study I read on Bodybuilding (the website), and it put me over the top to give this a try. I won't go into all the details and studies they took their info from, but it wrapped up nicely by saying this...essentially L Carnitine L Tartrate (LCLT...and I'm hoping that is what L-Carnitine Tartrate is in this bottle) doesn't increase testosterone on its own, but works in tandem with it to produce results:

"In summary, research shows that:

Feeding after Resistance Exercise increased Androgen Receptor content, which may result in increased testosterone uptake, and thus enhanced luteinizing hormone secretion via feedback mechanisms.

L-carnitine supplementation can upregulate Androgen Receptor content, which may promote increased testosterone uptake and recovery from Resistance Exercise.

In layman's terms, such increases in anabolic hormones and with recovery being enhanced you can expect more muscle growth."

title: Perfect
text:
This is going to sound crazy, but I use these on my cat litter boxes in my house and have for years.

When I moved into my house a few years ago I decided I was going to exhaust my litter boxes out the side of my house. So I cut holes in the corners of a couple rooms near the floor, hooked up a dryer vent, and on the other end used these plastic docks on my litter boxes. I had to cut holes and put a screen over the hole / rig an undervolted (quiet) 80mm fan inside this dock, but for years now my litter boxes have quietly exhausted their smells right outside my house through this dock.

It works great and served my purpose well. When you clean a box you just twist to unhook these things and put them back on when done with a twist. Zero regrets and these suckers are durable as I've even replaced the boxes once and took the docks off and moved them to new boxes. Love it.

title: I wont buy Verilux again.  Ever.
text:
I want to mention up front I did NOT purchase my lamp from Amazon, so this review is strictly about the lamp. I purchased 2 Heritage Antique Gold/Bronze lamps from a store about 45 miles north of me - one for my wife's and my reading chair at $199 apiece. This is almost $400 I can not get back. I hope Verilux reads this, but even if they did it is highly unlikely they'd improve anything as long as they got their money.

Pros: the light, when it works, is excellent. Bright and not harsh at all even with the daylight bulbs. That's it.

Cons:

1. Look for something better. I failed to and got burned in the long run.

2. The original bulbs lasted about 4 and 6 months each. Replacement bulbs (Verilux brand) are expensive.

3. The transformer plug on one stopped working in the first 3 days. Verilux wouldn't replace it. Fortunately the store swapped one out of another unit at the store.

4. The unit is flimsy as hell. It wobbles and rocks on hardwood floor. Terrible engineering and design of the base. Must have been designed by monkeys.

5. After replacing bulbs the first time in each lamp, the tab holding the lens in snapped off. Now using large hair pony tail ties to hold them on; rubber bands melted.

6. I've only purchased Verilux brand replacement bulbs as Ive seen in a few other places, that other brand will not quite fit the socket base. If anyone can shed light on that Id be grateful. Id just as soon give money to another company with a product that works rather than Verilux, but for now, my hands are tied.

Someone out there has a better lamp. I'll find it. As for Verilux execs and engineers - I don't know how you can live with yourselves as you collect exorbitant money on pure garbage.

I was given a sample bottle of this product by Viva Labs for an honest and fair review. Ultra Strength Glucosamine Chondroitin MSM Combination- Guaranteed Joint Agony Relief capsules.

The textures, strength and elasticity of my hair, skin and nails also improved markedly since I have been using this product.

text:
I was pleasantly surprised by these slippers. Without the battery installed, the inside is super comfy and the L size fit a 9.5M shoe size fine. Once you insert the battery, the comfort level goes down a bit since you have a fairly object on top of your feet. The weight is manageable and didn't bother me after a while, but you can tell there is something resting on top of your foot. The batteries came charged and the dual charger cable is pretty handy. The batteries insert into the shoe and plug in without issue and each shoe is super easy to turn on. To fully test, I used one shoe without the battery and one shoe completely put together and turned on. You can start to feel the difference in a few minutes and on high, the shoe warms up fully in under 10 minutes. The bottom of your foot is the last zone to get fully heated. I found high or medium heat comfortable but low didn't really server a purpose.

These work well around the house and outside to the mailbox, but I wouldn't want to go long distances in the them. I enjoyed keeping my feet warm and look forward to these on the sub zero winter days to come.

title: Stains face and sheets, even after several washes.
text:
These masks are very comfortable and effective but, like other users have described, these masks will stain your face and your sheets, even after washing them several times. I strongly suggest that no one purchase these.
I read the reviews before purchasing and, seeing that many people complained about the staining, I purchased anyway and planned to wash them before use. Upon receiving them and before my first use, I washed them by hand in warm water with mild detergent and mild agitation, then rinsed them and let them air dry. Thinking this would remove any residual dye, I proceeded to use them. One morning I woke up with black stains on my face and my sheets. Strangely, it didn't stain on the first use, so I don't know what triggered it. Nonetheless, I decided that I would wash them again.
I washed them again by hand in hot water with Oxyclean and some serious agitation. I squeezed and squashed vigorously and over several minutes, letting out the water and refilling 3 additional times (adding more Oxyclean each time). When it seemed no more dye was coming out in the water, I rinsed them well and let them air dry. They still stained my face and sheets (though again, not on the first use after washing).
It seems that, even with washing, these masks will stain your face and sheets. I was very thorough in my washing - I actually broke the bottom seams on the outside covers of both masks due to my vigorous agitation - so I don't know what else to do to try to prevent them from staining. I suppose I could attempt to machine wash them, but since the bottom seams broke with hand washing and since they're still releasing dye, I'm afraid of destroying them in the washer and possibly ruining other clothes in the washer with them.
I was very hopeful that washing them would eliminate the problem that so many others had with these. Sadly, it seems that they will stain no matter what. There must be some problem in how they are made that this problem exists in so many of the products and persists even with washing. I must advise that no one purchase these.

title: Buyer Beware
text:
I've never purchased this, and I never will. The label is so blatantly incorrect that there's no guessing what you're really getting, and in what doses. For instance: 18 mg of iodine and calling it 100% of "Daily Value" is outlandish. 150 micrograms (not mgs) is considered the RDA. 18 mg would never occur in a multi. Magnesium, 150 mcg, and calling it 100% of "DV" is bizarre. 350 milligrams (not mcgs) is considered the RDA. 60 mg of zinc, and calling it 15% of "DV" is outrageous. That would make the "DV" 400 mg, which is a toxic dose. RDA is 11 mg for men and 8 mg for women. That might not be enough for some people, but it wouldn't be healthy to take 400 mg daily for any length of time, and for many people, the 60 mg daily that's alleged to be in this product would be too much, taken long term. I doubt there's 60 mg of zinc in the product. Selelnium, 15 mg daily would be an extremely toxic dose. The RDA is 55 micrograms, not mgs. Many multis have 200 mcg (2 mg), and that's considered a safe dose. This label says 15 mg of selenium is 100% of "DV." I'm sure this product has no such amount of selenium. With so many obvious errors on the label, there's no way to know what's in the product and at what doses.

Update: It appears that the "perpetrators" of this "product" attempted to copy another product's label and omitted a line. That slipped everything below the skipped line up to the next line for listed dosage. When "iron" is inserted above" iodine," and everything else is moved down a line, the dosages fall in line with more typical dosages for multis. I hope I'm not cueing the "perpetrators" on how to do a better scam, but it's more evidence that this is not at all a true label or a reliable product.

I did use the 'pro gentle' toothpaste that comes with the kit BEFORE I applied the trays -and to be sure I got all the gunk outta my teeth, I brushed again with the toothpaste AFTER. (Yuk!!!).

The insert states that results may be seen in as little as 3 days. If I do see considerable results in 3 days, I'm going to stop there. if not, I'll go another 3 days (for a total of 6).

Overall, it's not a bad system. I've tried Crest White Strips and they were HORRIBLY 'bleach' tasting. These aren't as bad.

title: What a lifesaver!
text:
UPDATE: So I've had my forearm crutches for a few years now, and I still couldn't be happier with them. Like I mentioned wanting to do in my original review (below), I have purchased a second pair. I noticed that the thickness of the soles of my shoes made a real difference in how I set the adjustable height of these crutches. I'm mostly barefoot in the house, but when I go outside I wear running shoes (for their thick impact-absorbing sole that makes walking easier on my back). Since the soles of the shoes are nearly an inch thick, it only made sense to adjust my crutches an extra inch every time I put my shoes on. And while these crutches can certain do that, I just found it more convenient to order a second pair, and keep them at that "higher" setting. So I use my original pair of crutches when I'm barefoot, and use my new pair when I'm wearing shoes. It really seems to make a difference for me. Plus, I like the piece of mind of having a second pair, in case anything happens to the first pair (not that I've had any trouble from my crutches, but when you're talking about your ability to walk, it's better to be safe than sorry). I still have no regrets about my purchase. And the next time I decide I need another pair of forearm crutches, I will return to this brand and model once again. The only complaint that I still have (as mentioned in my original review below), is it is almost impossible to find replacement rubber tips that are of the amazing quality that these crutches come with; at least at a price that doesn't rival just buying a whole new pair of crutches. So I've taken to just buying normal tips for my "around the house" pair of crutches, and I just plan on buying a whole new pair of crutches the next time my "outside" crutches need new tips. After all, these crutches really aren't very expensive at all.

I should also mention that I recently flew across country with these crutches, and they collapsed to a manageable size while in flight. Some airlines allowed me to keep them between my chair and the bulkhead, while others required that I put them in the overhead compartment. But regardless, I was very happy with how well they traveled.

And their durability is fantastic. They have never failed me in over three years.

I still whole-heartedly recommend this product!

ORIGINAL POST:

What a fantastic product!

After a car-accident-induced spinal injury, I've had varying mobility issues. After many spinal surgeries, I spent time going from a wheel chair, to a walker, then using a cane for quite some time. But lately, my condition has degraded, and I needed more support than a simple cane. But I also didn't feel I needed to go back to a walker quite yet.

Enter the forearm canes. My goodness, what a difference! They really allow me to take the weight off of my lower back when walking, and have drastically increased my ability to walk; allowing me to walk faster and farther than I've been able to in years. And the stability and reliability that these forearm canes provide (as opposed to a standard walking cane) cannot be measured. They really do make me feel more balanced and secure. By using two points of contact (a cuff around your forearm and the grip of your hand) your arm is locked into parallel with the cane, which means you don't have to "balance" your weight using only your wrist on top of a wobbly cane. This allows you to securely put more of your weight on the forearm cane than you could reasonably do with a standard walking cane. The stability factor of a forearm cane, as compared to a standard cane cannot be measured. I would say its stability is comparable to using crutches, only with much less awkward cumbersomeness that comes with full crutches.

Previously, I hadn't ever considered forearm canes, as they seemed too expensive. But as always, Amazon came to the rescue with prices that couldn't be beat.

This product has a long list of pros that have been covered by other reviewers nicely. So I will do my best to list the ones that are most important to me.
-This is a very well-made product. Strong and secure, I feel confident using this product. I am well over six feet tall, and weigh around 250lbs., and need these canes to hold my weight with each step I take. And they do not disappoint. They're one of the few things I don't have to worry about when I venture out my door.
-Unique to this product, the manufacturers have used nylon bushing-washers at all of the adjustment points. These serve to quiet the sqeaking sounds that are common with adjustable canes and crutches. At first, I didn't really think this was much of a big deal, but now able to compare, I find this idea to be one of life's little gifts. Kudos to the manufacturers!
-Unlike most forearm canes, these ones allow you to not only adjust the length of the cane, but also to adjust the distance between the handle and the forearm "cuff". Until I had the ability to make this adjustment, I never really knew how much of a difference this can make. And now, I would never use a forearm cane that didn't offer this ability.
-These canes came with a unique, large "footed" tip, that has improved traction substantially over other canes and crutches that I have used. The one downside (which I mention in greater detail in the "cons" section) is finding replacement tips. But after using these oversized tips, I won't go back to using "regular" tips.

The only cons I can come up with are negligible (at least to me).
-First off, these forearm canes are a bit on the heavy side. But I compare this to the weight of a regular cane. I'd say their weight is in the ballpark of regular crutches, probably a little less. However, noting my height/weight above, and needing these canes to hold my entire weight reliably with each step, I would expect them to have a "sturdy" weight/feel to them. Anything less and I would probably have my doubts as to their reliability. If you need something that can reliably take your weight with every step, this is your product. However, if we're talking about an 80 year old user (where the weight of the device is more important than its ability support weight), then you might want to look at a product that sacrifices stability/reliability in favor of being lighter and easier to maneuver. As with any product, always consider the target audience.
-Secondly, (and this is really a minor issue), the canes have a beautiful chrome looking finish to them (I believe it's actually nickel). But I've found that it's easily scratched; mostly from banging into each other when I put them down, or stow them when I get into the car. After many month's use, the finish on my canes is seriously marred, which detracts from the looks a little. But in reality, they should be a convenient medical assistive device first, and a fashion statement second (if even that). So I'm not really complaining. But if the manufacturers were looking for a way to improve their already great product, then I would recommend a more sturdy finish. Something that can really stand up to the rigors of life.
-Third (and also a minor issue), when I recieved my canes, one of the nuts that compresses the nylon washer (that in turn, cuts down on the squeaking noises) arrived stripped, making it uesless. This wasn't enough of an issue to write to the manufacturer to ask for a replacement. Although, the prodcut did come with a warranty card that suggested that this kind of issue would be covered by the warranty. I simply swapped the nut with one from the top of the forearm area (where it was less important), and that mostly took care of the issue.
-After many months of use, I'm finding that the rubber coating on the forearm "cuffs" is beginning to wear away at the edges, exposing the metal below it. I can't really fault the manufacturer for this. It's really just normal wear and tear. In other reviews, some people have mentioned that they use "after market" covers on their cuffs. I'm toying with the idea of buying a can of that liquid rubber substance that you use to apply a rubber coating to the handle of your shop tools. Perhaps that product can be used to apply a new coat of rubber to the cuffs of my canes.
-The canes can be a bit difficult to stow in your car while driving. Luckily, I drive a large SUV (mostly for the comfortable air-ride suspension that makes bumps easier on my back), and I've perfected a way of securing them between the passenger's seat and the center consol. But for folks with a smaller car, it may be difficult finding a place to safely stow forearm canes or crutches. Having been in a serious car accident, I'm always mindful of how objects can become flying missiles during a car accident. So be sure to find some place safe and secure to stow these guys while you're on the road.
-Even with the nylon bushings, there are still some ocassional sqeaks every now and then. I find that a little baby powder to the right places usually takes care of this. I wouldn't recommend WD-40 or any like lubricant, and it can react poorly with the nylon, plastic, and rubber parts of the product. (Plus, who wants to smell that all the time?)
-The only real issue of note, is that I'm having a difficult time finding replacement tips at a good price. These canes came with an unique tip that I've never seen before. It's quite large and very stable. But the only replacement tips even close to this style (that I can find online) are around $20 EACH. At that price, it would be near the same cost to just order another pair of canes here. I'll post an update if I find a better deal on replacement tips.

Some other reviewers have made mention of the handles being too hard. I haven't had an issue with this, and I've spent a lot of time on my forearm canes. So to each their own. Personally, I don't care for the soft rubberized handles that some canes and crutches come with, as I find it deteriorates quickly and over-all becomes more of a problem than a solution. I feel that it's a benefit that these forearm canes do not come with a soft rubber handle, and instead come with a hard plastic handle. This allows the option to add your own "after-market" rubberized grips, and the ability to replace them as they wear out; without makig it necessary to use the rubberized grips. After all, how horrible would it be if your soft rubber grip started tearing away at a time when you couldn't replace it, and all you were left with was a metal bar to grip until you could get a replacement? So I consider the hard plastic grips to be a benefit not a disadvantage.

At some point, I plan to purchase a second set of forearm crutches for two reasons.
1) To have a second pair around as a back up, just in case anything happens to my current pair.
2) So I have a set that still has a nice, un-scratched surface, for those ocassions when appearances matter.
I have every intention of purchasing this same product when that time presents itself.

Without any reservation I whole-heartedly recommend this product.

title: I don't understand how it works but it seems to work
text:
I don't get styes that often but when I do they last a while. I do the hot compresses but it's a slow process. I bought this because I had a single stye, plus a cluster of at least two styes near it that I feared was going to turn into a monster. The lymph node in front of my ear on that side was even a bit swollen and sore which has not happened before.
The Goodbye Styes started calming the visible styes after a day and "pulled" (?) to the surface two in the cluster that had not started coming to a head yet.
The reason I'm not sure exactly how it works is because I didn't ever see the pus ooze out but I would end up with little flakes of dried crusty stuff that I could pull off or wash off. I think was the pus somehow pulled out and dried out.
After just four days of treatment there's only one little spot left and it is almost gone (and the lymph node swelling faded as the swelling went down around my eye.)
You only need to put the tiniest drop on your clean finger and then on the stye. This bottle is small but should last the rest of my life!

title: Good results for me.....
text: I am not a great sleeper, one of those who tends to wake up easily when noise enters the room - a cat scratching on the door, one of the kids running up the steps, birds chirping at 5 AM in the summer when the windows are open.  If I have been asleep for more than 4-6 hours, I will end up not being able to get back to sleep.  I LOVE to run a box fan as I noticed that I sleep better with the noise and the gentle breeze.  But while researching white noise as a possible sleep aid I came to realize that is is likely not the breeze that I was enjoying, but the white noise created by the fan.  So in the endless quest for good nights' sleep, I decided to order this Dohm machine and see how it went.  I've been using it for several weeks now and, although it is very hard to quantify the benefit, I am convinced the machine is helping me sleep better.  It creates a nice noise zone which normal small household sounds cannot penetrate.  If you enjoy sleeping with a fan on, or other consistent background noise, I encourage you to give one of these a try.  I gave it 5 starts for the simple reason that ANYTHING that helps me sleep better, longer or deeper gets a top rating.  And I believe this is working well for me.

title: Simple install, none of the issues described due to 802.11b network interface.
text:
After reading the reviews on Amazon I was hesitant about the 802.11b Wifi connection supported by Aria and the potential disruption with our home network. We had none of the problems described in the feedback setting up the unit. We simply downloaded the app to our iMac, installed the SW and followed the instructions on setup. The Aria was "found" by our network and the installation took less than 10 minutes including adding other users fitbit accounts. The only suggestion I have is to be aware if you have multiple mobile Fitbit apps (we both have iPhones and iPads which we sync with our personal devices) that you can sometimes get conflicts when syncing. Simply remove the "extra" devices from the area (or power off those not involved in the sync process). This avoids any problems others seem to describe with syncing conflicts. I love that I can sync my fitbit with whatever device I am using at the time, and can then switch devices without interruption. Very pleased with all our fitbit products!

I can't attest yet to the long term use of the scale, but everything works as advertised and it is another great addition to my Charge HR and my wife's Fitbit One.

My hope was that these pendant chews would keep them from chewing their sleeves, fingers, toys, etc, and not got lost or end up dirty/on the floor.  I put them on long necklaces for the kids to wear.  My 4 year old promptly took off the necklace, swung it around in circles and ended up hitting his pre-k classmates with it.  My 6 year old threw it in the trash, and said chewing on his sleeve was more enjoyable because this didn't "feel good."  My 8 year old also used it to distract her classmates, swinging it around, etc.  So I bought these retractable pulleys that clipped to their belt loops.  My 4 year old broke the retractable pulley after 5 minutes and was banned from bringing his chewy to pre-school, and has not used it since.  My 8 year old took it off the clip and lost it.  Bottom line is, these pendants are very hard, and most kids are looking for something they can chew on for sensory input, but these are too solid/firm.  So for us, what sounded like a great solution did not work at all.  I wish I hadn't wasted my money.

title: Impossible to mold, doesn't stay in place, tough to breathe:(
text:
The molding process is an impossible joke. You're instructed to position the guard on the tines of a fork. I tried several different forks, and all my guard did was float off and swim around in the hot water. It was a molten lump of plastic each time, and I couldn't even get the slot for my teeth to open up. After four attempts, I got it properly molded up and onto my gums. No matter how thin it's pressed above my teeth/over my gums/onto my soft palette, it's still very easily removed and hasn't stayed in for more than an hour.

Also, I hope you don't have any need to breathe through your mouth at all, because you won't be able to with this mouthguard in. I have slight allergies and maybe 1 out of every 5 breaths happens through my mouth instead of my nose. This mouthguard is so obstructive to any mouth breathing tendencies you may have, it's actually caused me to panic and wake up because it's slipped out of place and completely blocked my mouth. I'll probably be lucky if I don't choke on it. It does stay in place for the most part, but one touch of the tongue or wiggle of the lips dislodges it, and no amount of re-molding has fixed that. I've had dentist-made appliances that have stayed put, and boxing mouthguards (for fighting) that have stayed suctioned on to an unpleasant degree, so I think it's the device, rather than some unique feature of my teeth (I've got very normal, straight, rather perfect looking teeth, and an otherwise unremarkable mouth and gum situation). This product just took my money when I was desperate for help. Well, I'm still desperate, but my wallet is a little lighter.

title: Perfect!
text:
I bought these for my mom who spend the last 5 months of her life confined to a bed and couldn't even sit up to watch TV. These glasses enabled her to watch TV and movies and, given her situation, they really helped her quality of life. She would panic if they were ever out of her reach!

They are well built and crystal clear. One of the prisms fell out of her first pair, but that's because she slept on them not because they were cheaply made. In fact, they are very well made and I would recommend them for anyone, not just those who are confined to bed.

Perhaps most importantly, the prisms are mounted "longways" instead of "shortways" (think landscape versus portrait) so that the wearer gets the maximum viewing area. The prisms are also mounted straight and even. We tried a different (cheaper) brand where the prisms were mounted "shortways" and were maybe not quite straight, which gave me and my mom a headache within a few minutes.

These glasses didn't have any sort of adverse effects such as headaches, eye fatigue, etc.

text: It has been a long bout with my 7 year old. We used to pee the bed everynight, and I have done the pull ups, changing sheets and yelling. I have begged and lost hope and gained the hope back all at the same time. I bought this alarm with that hope but strongly doubt. We have been pee free for 3 weeks already after starting the alarm. Within one week of using the alarm he started to forget to put it on, get up at night where as before he didn't and go to the bathroom. The concept of the alarm is one to two drops of urine starts off the alarm (it sounds like slomins alarm) and wakes the child up to understand what it feels like to have a full bladder and go to the bathroom. It is not the child being lazy, or the child doing it on purpose, when you think about it, at 7 who wants to be known to pee the bed. No one so don't doubt that your child has a small bladder, deep sleeper or maturity issues are the matter. This unit works for my son and I didn't believe but now I do. title: A lifesaver
text:
I suffer from chronic UTIs that develop very quickly into kidney infections. I was sick of going to the doctor for antibiotics, because those really mess up your body AND you will eventually develop immunity to them. D-mannose has kept me away from the doctor for years. But, you need to take it in a very specific way to make sure they work.

Wait til your bladder is empty. Take a spoonful with VERY little water or no water at all (the taste is sweet so it's easy to swallow it by alone). Wait 45 minutes before drinking water, then CHUG a LOT of water. This allows the d-mannose to attach itself to the bacteria in your bladder, and then the water will help you flush everything out.

They are currently all of our favorites, since they are perhaps the sweetest, delightful, and smooth way to gum out some precious vitamins and minerals, the latter in more ways than one.

Some of that should stick, in this form right?
While I couldn't remember that between the feedings and mommy mind, I do happen to always have these near, as they seem to always remember to take them everyday. All on account of the flavor - they are without a doubt some (if not the best) vitamins we have ever tried. Out of quite a few brands in my 3 decades of ingesting various forms, that's saying something. Not because I got them for testing purposes, which I did; but only for honest and unbiased feedback.

So the only thing I could find wrong with them was that it is hard to tell the flavors apart from each other. I will add a photo for reference, I certainly wouldn't want to place a bet on which one Orange and which one is Lemon.
At least I didn't think so, yet when I poured them out to try and discern 5 separate flavors I got it right. What part of that was luck and which part was an actual difference in color I cannot say. Looking at a pile of them I would have thought they were all the same or possibly 2 colors, so I ate one of each separately and surely enough they were not mixed but actually 5 different fruitls.
I like that there are 5 flavors but when you're only getting 3 out of 5 - if you wanted to be certain one was not Cherry or Grape you might be hard pressed to get it right the first time.

Still, not enough for me to take away a star over it since they are still by and large the best. We purchased another brand thinking they would be the same and the kids won't touch the others.

Which is ok by me.

Since most vitamin manufacturers put their bottle's expiration date in exactly this location, one might reasonably assume that the bottle has an expiration date of 09/2015. However, on closer inspection, there is a little sticker on the very bottom of the bottle that says "Expiration Date 08 2018"! The "DOM" apparently stands for "Date Of Manufacture". title: IT WORKS!
text: Our house was built in the 70's.  The floors upstair squeaked with every step, and it became unbearable.  A handyman told us he'd have to lift up the carpet to fix the squeaky floors, and gave us an expensive quote for the job.  We searched around and found a youtube video of this product.  We were skeptical at first, but at around $43, S & H included, we figured we should give it a try.  My husband struggled at first to find the joists, and ended up with some small holes in the carpet.  We thought the damage is permanent, but after some vacuuming and steaming, the carpet is whole again.  Though at some spots we could still hear a light squeak, overall it has improved 90% for us.  We ran out of the first pack and had to purchase another one.  The S & H fee is outrageous, but they ship fast and we received the product in less than 5 days after we purchased it.  Overall, we spent less than $100 for 2 kits, and we were able to fix the entire floor upstairs.  Our stairway is also squeaky, but we have no idea how to fix it.  Hopefully someone can give us some tips.

title: Great for daily meds, not great for vitamins or long trips
text: We bought this to manage prescriptions that need to be taken morning and evening.  It works really well for regular meds and helps with compliance.  However, there are a few drawbacks.  It does take up some room on the counter, but that works for us because the colors are pretty and we don't mind it being out.  Loading each of the days is a little tricky, because it's hard to hold open the little lids with one hand while putting the pills in with the other.  It is possible to take the hinged lid completely off to load them, but putting them back on again takes a steady hand. Large vitamins (like the Ester-C my husband takes) don't really fit with the other meds, but that's okay with us.  If we travel for a few days, it's nice to take those boxes out of the organizer and into a travel bag, but I don't think I would want to try to travel with the whole month organizer because it would be difficult to get them to stay in the tray.  Overall, this is exactly what we needed and it's worth the trouble of loading it.

title: They're ok, but they don't really work for me.
text:
I did not get these for snoring (I don't really know if I snore, but it doesn't matter as the only ones who would hear it are the dogs, and they don't care), but instead to see if it would make it easier for me to breathe through my nose. My nasal passages have been slowly narrowing for the last 10-15 years (probably related to old injuries, the cartilage has collapsed a little bit), and I just wanted something to help open them up a little. So I've been trying nasal dilators, but unfortunately not with much luck.

My nose is oddly bent at the tip. I haven't been able to use other nasal dilators because the width of the part that goes around the septum hasn't been wide enough to compensate for the curve at the end without being so wide that they won't fit into my nose at all. These are supposed to be soft and flexible, so I gave them a try. They are more comfortable than other nasal dilators I've tried, but they still don't really fit right, unfortunately.

I'm not sure how the blue ones are supposed to work anyway.. They seem to take up available space instead of creating more space. I think this is because my narrowing is further inside. These push inward on the septum instead out outward at the sides, and the balls at the ends (the magnets -- i don't understand why it has magnets) just end up plugging my nose right at its narrowest point.

The white ones are interesting, and much better for my type of nose. The instructions are unclear and it took me a while to figure out how they are supposed to go in, but I finally figured it out (I think). These stretch open the nostril without having to clip around the septum. There is a very thin and flexible piece that goes under/around the septum to keep the two sides from separating completely, but that's not the part holding it in - the design allows the nostrils themselves to hold these in. They're not too uncomfortable either, surprisingly. Unfortunately I still can't get them in far enough to make much of a difference, but these came pretty close to working at least.

For those whose septum isn't symmetrical, this design makes so much more sense. The dimensions aren't quite right for me though, I would need it to stretch my nostrils side-to-side more than back-to-front. So although I like the design and I think this is the closest I've come so far, they still don't really work for me.

title: For large or very stretchy socks only - not for small women's socks
text:
I ordered this because from time to time my back injury flares up and I'm unable to bend far enough to put socks on. I live alone, so there's no one to help when it gets bad, so I wanted something like this.

Well, I'm not really sure who they have in mind with these -- maybe people with giant feet only? The product images made it look so easy and it appeared to be a regular size. I thought that maybe it would be a little difficult but that I'd be able to get them on. I was wrong. My socks are not big or stretchy enough. I tried several pairs of socks -- the stretchiest ones will fit on the very bottom, but there's no way I could pull them all the way to the notch. If you can't get them to the notch, there's nothing to keep the sock from just sliding off the moment you try to put your foot in it.

I've attached a picture of this device with a pair of my stretchiest socks. I have average sized women's feet and wear the standard size for women's novelty socks. This device is huge next to my socks. I could not get a picture of me trying to pull the sock over the opening because as soon as I let go with one hand it just slips off the opposite side since I can't get it up far enough.

If you have very large feet or wear excessively stretchy socks, this might work for you. None of my socks would fit on it though.

Finally, this cushion really is portable. Because of the soft memory foam, I can easily fold it in half and place it in the carrying bag. It fits perfectly, and is easy to insert and remove. It’s especially nice for anyplace with hard, folding chairs like school auditoriums, church functions, or civic meetings. This eyelash curler works very well for me. The spring action is strong but easy to handle. Fits comfortably in the hand. The rubber cushion is sturdy but soft on the eyelashes. Comes with an eyelash brush and a replacement cushion. The brush is nothing special but a fun little bonus.

If you are having trouble getting good results with your eyelash curler, try these 2 tips:
-put the eyelash curler in your bra while you apply the first part of your makeup routine so it can warm up. It curls better while it is warm. You can also accomplish this by heating with a blow dryer for 5-10 seconds (but be careful not to burn your eyelid!).
-Curl your eyelashes before you apply your mascara. This will avoid build-up on your eyelash curler and extend the length of use.

Good luck! I have tried many brands of eyelash curlers and so far I am impressed with this one. Maybe my old one was getting too old, but I can really tell a difference. My lashes seem longer!

So I just received my heating pad. The cord and pad seem to be high quality and the cover is very soft. However, the description of this item was not accurate, and dishonest. I believe in honesty and integrity. Apparently this company does not.
This item has no digital controller as pictured but part of the cord has a controller (3x1 cm) that displays a 0.5 cm circle that changes color-- red, yellow, and blue. I am assuming they are heat settings but the instructions describe it as displaying numbers. The instructions and some of the reviews have such poor grammar that I am sure are probably translated using google translate or something,
The disclaimer on this item (tiny print) states: While we work to ensure that product information is correct, on occasion manufacturers may alter their ingredient lists. Actual product packaging and materials may contain more and/or different information than that shown on our Web site. We recommend that you do not solely rely on the information presented . So legally they are ok but morally?
I received a threatening email from seller that they were going to report me to amazon if i did not change my review.
I reported seller to amazon and now i continue to get multiple emails from them. One of them states:
Dear Dawn,
“This is Teddy from Amazon seller - Brigenius. Sorry for disturbing again, friend.
Regarding to the problem for the item, may I know if you receiving the previous emails about the solution？
As mentioned, we would like to arrange full refund or free replacement for you.
Your response would be highly appreciated.
We are not US seller, we sell on amazon and serve for you, and we need a good reputation, we need make money to feed kids and our family,
so please don't worry about the after-sale service, you can contact us at any time for any issue.
We are not the best, but we are trying our best to provide you the best service.
Regards,
Brigenius Customer Service”

I didn't make it a mission, but checked every once in a while and never really found a better deal, so I dropped the hammer. Easy enough to slip my fingertips under the end of the temples and lift them off my ears. I also thought they might be too tight, and they did feel that way at first, but not now... they're fine. All this being said, this is probably the swan song for my Ray Ban Outdoorsmans, and that's not due to these temples. title: Awesome little set of ear plugs!
text: I've been using these now for a couple of weeks and I really like these ear plugs.  I was looking for something to drown out the sound when I sleep at night.  These do the job very well.  They're small silicone inserts that are much different than regular foam ear plugs.  These do a much better job of sealing the ear canal keeping out sound.  There was a bit of a struggle at first to figure out how to get them to fit just right in the ear, at least for me, but once I did the quality was very apparent.  These were not necessarily designed for sleeping, so if you do get them for that, be aware if you move around a lot in your sleep like I do, they may fall out of your ears.  A couple of mornings I had to search the bed for one or both of them.  These are made well, but I do wonder how long they will last using them every night for roughly 8 hours.  Only time will tell, but now, and for the last couple of weeks the quality for me has been really great.  I really like the little aluminum storage tube that comes with them.  These little suckers would get lost really fast if you didn't have a decent place to store them, it was important to me to get ear plugs that came with some type of storage, so I was happy to see that these did.  All in all I'm very happy with these.  The do their job, they keep out the sound, and that helps me to sleep more peacefully which is what I was looking for.  I received these ear plugs for a discounted price in exchange for a fair an unbiased review.  I feel I have done just that.  I would definitely recommend these ear plugs.

title: Very soft brush
text:
I usually use an electric toothbrush, but I wanted to try one of these just because I was curious if it really was easier on gums. Yes, it absolutely is easy on the gums. In fact, I didn't even feel it on my gums at first. It wasn't until I tried really scrubbing with a lot of pressure that I could feel the brush. Even then, I didn't feel the bristles or the usual brushing sensation you have with a regular toothbrush. It was just a little pressure and that's it. If you're gums are so sensitive that even a regular soft toothbrush is too harsh for you, then these brushes will be great for you.

That being said, if you try to brush the same way you do with a regular toothbrush, it may not get your teeth clean. You will definitely have to floss before brushing your teeth in order to get food bits out of your mouth first. But, really, you should be doing that anyway. No toothbrush is really able to clean everything out from between your teeth all on its own. You may also have to kind of scrub a little harder to get the area just above your gums clean.

The only real complaint I have about this brush is the handle. Since it isn't textured my hand kept sliding up the brush.

text:
I've been wanting to try one of these for awhile so when I got the opportunity to buy one discounted to review, I jumped on it.

This was a very pleasant surprise. The brush is super good quality and the bristles are not rubber like I've seen on some. They are plastic and they don't pull your hair out! It heats up pretty fast but not as fast as a standard straightener. This also came with the heat glove and 2 hair clips. It's comfortable to hold too. The settings are great and you can't accidentally turn it off!

Using this is easy enough but it does not get your hair stick straight like a standard straightener does. This kept a little more volume which I liked. I did small sections at a time and did my ends a few times because it still looked kind of frizzy. I like that this does not cause frizz at the top of my head like my straightener can do sometimes. The hair goes through the bristles very easily and I would definitely suggest using the heat glove - it's amazing! I actually use that now when I'm using my regular straightener too.

Overall this gives you a different look than a standard straightener but it's a very nice tool to calm your hair down but still leave it having some volume. It didn't take long to do my whole head but I'd say it was longer than my regular straightener.

title: Scale doesn't work on Syncs but otherwise reports weight accurately.
text:
I'm being generous with a 3 star here. I've owned the Aria for a week now. I weigh on it daily at the same time, and it sits on a flat surface (not carpet).

The reason for the 3-star is that the scale setup fine on my wifi, but never successfully sync'ed any stats to the cloud.

I've gone through the following to troubleshoot the problem.

- Used Wifi with WPA
- Use Wifi with WPA2
- Used open Wifi
- In all the instance above, the scale was less than 15 ft from my router
- I've also done all of the above with two different wifi routers (both weren't turned on at the same time)
- I've setup on both 5ghz and 2.4ghz wifi networks

In looking at fitbit's help site, there are a ton of such issues reported, so I'm sure this is not a lemon I got, but a recurring theme.

I've just requested a replacement and will update my review AND rating based on it, but if that doesn't work, then I'll be returning this hardware. For now, its strictly a very expensive and fancy digital weight scale.

Update: got a replacement unit and it works perfectly

title: Heated Eyelash Curler
text:
Heated Eyelash Curler with 3 Heat Modes. C-Type Charging port.

Cordless, chargeable, heated eyelash curler. To switch between all three modes, simply press the button once for low, twice for medium, and three times for high.

The heat setting depends on the length of your lashes. I started out with low at first to be on the cautious side. I have an issue with my lashes curling inward, which scratches at my eyes. I was looking for something that would have a lasting effect, since I found regular, manual eyelash curlers to only last a few minutes at most. This is reminiscent of a curling iron, except it's for your eyelashes- I used mascara as my version of hairspray.

The heat softly curled my lashes up and away from the rim of my eyelid, keeping my lashes from curling under and scratching at my eyes.

I was overall pleased with the curler but found it somewhat oversized, bulky and clunky, while the handles were too thin to control well, which made it difficult to work with.

title: Super Soft Bristles
text:
Included are 4 toothbrushes with handles in black, pink, green, and white, perfect for the whole family, as you won't mix up whose brush is whose. Convenient and handy, each brush comes in its own protective travel tube.

Used to nylon bristles that tend to aggravate sensitive gums, I've never felt anything as soft as these toothbrushes. Feathery soft and gentle, with more bristles than the average brush, which truly cleans teeth, gums, and tongue. There are so many bristles that it almost looks solid- impressive.

The ergonomic handles aren't super shiny plastic, so they're not slippery when wet, so no worry over slipping out of your hand. I also appreciated the softer pastel colors of the handles, no loud designs that clash with my bathroom decor.

The travel tubes are an added bonus.

title: Easy to Use & Easy to Store
text:
Expandable Sitz bath with manual bidet.

The Sitz bath fit nicely on my toilet, a sturdy design. An attachable manual bidet was easy to install and use. The expandable bath was easy to open and close. The bowl is deep, which comes in handy with different body frames. The overflow holes ensured there was no mess.

A sitz bath is so much more convenient than taking a bath, especially if you need to soak several times per day for the healing process. Sprinkle in a few tablespoons of bath salts formulated for sitz baths, fill with warm water, and sit back and relax for 15 to 20 minutes.

The manual bidet feature was nice, but it only hits one spot, so you'll have to wiggle around until it hits where you're wishing it to aim.

Make sure the tub is thoroughly dry before collapsing to prevent mildew growth. Not only am I pleased with this sitz bath, I'm even more happy with how easy it is to collapse and store in a cupboard, not taking up much room.

I admit, I did buy a 3rd unit, simply because of their effectiveness, but I'm sure it won't last an entire year either...

Edit #2: As expected, the 3rd unit only lasted for 8 months, and then it completely died out too.

The Germ Guardian Pluggable Air Purifier and Sanitizer certainly does its job well, but also noisily.
My bathroom is always damp and smells like mildew, no matter how often I clean it. I recently had to replace a bathmat due to mold growing on it, and a hat I hung in the bathtub to dry had to be thrown away for the same reason. Already having breathing issues, that was a big problem for me. The replacement bathmat I purchased also had an awful odor. But then I added this product to the mix, and there was an immediate improvement.
After the air purifier was plugged in for only a short amount of time, the mildew smell and the bathmat smell were both gone. I have kept it plugged in the majority of the time, except when I won't be home for an extended amount of time, and the mildew smell has not come back. Regular bathroom smells dissipate quickly as well, making the ceiling mounted bathroom fan and spray air fresheners obsolete.
As far as space saving, this air purifier takes up very little space, and sits securely in the top socket of the wall outlet, without tilting sideways or forwards. It does not block the lower socket, and I have had no problems so far with using both outlets at the same time.
I don't feel secure taking the risk of leaving it plugged in when I will be away from home for an extended period of time, but I haven't smelled any smoke, or noticed any risk of fire so far. I won't know how much energy it is consuming, until I get my next electric bill.
All in all, the Germ Guardian Pluggable Air Purifier and Sanitizer is a great product, that does it job very effectively, and solved the problems I purchased it for.
The only drawback so far is the noise level. The air purifier is in the bathroom, which shares a wall with my bedroom. It is not plugged in on that shared wall, but near the corner of the adjoining wall. I can hear the fan running rather loudly all the time, especially when I am attempting to sleep, even with both doors closed. I expected to hear the sound in the same room, but not in another room. This is the only reason I did not give the product a 5-star rating, and the only reason why I won't be purchasing more of them to place in other rooms. If it ran quieter, it would be the perfect air purification product. Nevertheless, I will continue to use the product, due to its incredible effectiveness.

title: Accurate and reliable
text: It is an accurate and reliable daily weight scale. SO much more accurate than the digital because, being disabled, I need more time to get on the scale and balance my weight. This one allows me the time to do that. The digital scales I've tried decided my weight prematurely and I can repeat the procedure 5 different times in a row with 5 different weights varying by 10+ pounds. This scale I just step on and balance my weight, get the reading, and then step off. So easy. The display can be slightly difficult to read in low light (especially with my eye floaters and cataracts) so that's the only reason I gave it 4 stars not 5. It wouldn't be a problem with someone who has good vision. This is a vastly improved version of the "old fashion" analog scales they used to make.

When I wakeup on days when my under eyes circles are very noticeable I go to freezer and get the ice roller. The ice roller is very useful and can be use for multiple reasons. It can be use on the face and body and for all kinds of beneficial reasons. This is more convenient and cleaner then using a ice bag which drips water after the ice starts to melt. After usage, I just run it under the water and soap and wipe it with rubbing alcohol. I sometimes turn it to a hot roller by placing the roller into hot water for a minute or two and roll it on my face to massage and circulate the blood. The handle is very comfortable and the roller is detachable from the handle. I received this at a discounted price in exchange for my honest review.

text: Wow!  I have arthritis in my knee.  I bought this item after spending several weeks exploring exercise bikes and then pedal exercisers.  I found exercise bikes to either be loud or expensive, and all seemed to take up more room then I was willing to give up.  In addition, reasonably priced bikes were generally upright types that were hard on the glutes and created potential balance problems.  Recumbent bikes that offered magnetic resistance were very expensive.  When I first stumbled upon this product here, I was skeptical.  How could a magnetic pedal exerciser be worthwhile at such a low price.  As I read the reviews, I began to be more of a believer.  I have found Amazon reviews to be right on in the past.  Sure enough, this exerciser does everything it says it will do.  Very quiet and small enough to move around, yet perfect for my needs.  I can't say if this would be perfect for someone looking for a professional aerobic workout, but after 2 weeks, my knee feels much better already.

text:
I LOVE THIS PRODUCT! I had weight loss surgery and needed to find a protein supplement for after the procedure. I am very picky about my protein drinks because they're all so nasty!! Protein powder was a struggle - everything had terrible texture or flavor. I wasn't sure if I should take a gamble on this powder, being that it is kind of pricey, and I've hated every protein powder I've tried thus far. I bought it, I drank it, and it was pretty good! HOWEVER - what I've learned about the whey protein isolate is that IT NEEDS TO SET. It doesn't dissolve instantly, like stated. I've found that if you put some water in the bottle first, then add half the scoop and shake the bottle a bit..it'll start dissolving faster - then add more water and the rest of the scoop then SHAKE THE HELL OUT OF IT for a minute or so. Some people can drink it after that, but the little pieces of undissolved powder gross me out. So, I let the bottle sit for a few.. I go find something do to then come back to it. The handheld filter is about the size of a baseball and works extremely well to capture exhaled smoke by completely removing any smell. It is a bit more straining than simply exhaling to push the exhaled smoke through the filter, so be prepared for a bit of effort. While it does exactly what it is intended to, it cannot be used by a frequent smoker or long term. According to the Smoke Buddy website, the full-sized product will only last for about 300 uses. So, if you smoke a pack a day, you'll get about 6 weeks out of it. Unfortunately, this was not listed anywhere in the description for the product and I only discovered this after the device became nearly impossible to blow smoke through. text: Like other reviewers, I think this stuff is absolutely amazing. The instructions on the bottle and in the email I received from the seller were focused on getting odors and stains out of carpets, and my issue isn't really with carpets, because my two male cats spray, so I need to clean about 12" above the floor on the bottom of furniture and baseboards and such.  So I was kind of on my own with how to use Emmy's best on upholstered furniture, but I found it easy to use and extremely effective in removing odors and stains.  I just sprayed it on and rubbed it with a damp towel.  In fact, I had tried my regular product, Urine Off, on the same furniture recently, and afterwards, it almost seemed like the odor was worse, as if cleaning it had just diluted the spots and spread them over a wider area, so the whole house smelled like cats - yuk.  But after using Emmy's Best on the same furniture, the odor is gone!  I am amazed and excited to use this on other areas of the house.  I have tried it on the back of a leather chair and on walls and baseboards, and so far, it has worked on everything.  I do not think it smells like lavender, but the scent is quite pleasant, and ultimately, the clean smell after the scent of the product fades is wonderful.  Also, I was concerned that a 32 oz bottle would not be big enough but I find that Emmy's Best goes a long way.  I plan to buy more now though, because this stuff is so good that I don't think it will be long before some big company buys them up and starts selling a less effective version of the product for more money. title: The stuff to give the troops
text:
Anyone familiar with the Jeeves and Wooster books will recognize my title as an oft-recurring line. But it's literally true of this product. Operation Gratitude, Blue Star Mothers and other groups do a great job sending care packages to deployed US troops, but senders often wonder what to include.

This would be a great gift. Why? Usually there's a chow hall available that soldiers, sailors, Marines and airmen can at least sometimes get to. Generally you can get Gatorade to replenish electrolytes. But you wouldn't want to do that all the time, as it's all sugar, or rather, a blend of various sugars to avoid the sugar spike from a candy bar and provide a more gradual energy curve. Powerade, almost never available, is low sodium, using potassium instead for electrolytes.

Often troops cannot get potable (drinkable) water and instead use bottled water (supplied in abundance). One of these packets in a water bottle makes a great, refreshing, on-the-go drink. Best of all, it's sugar-free, providing a great balance to sodas, Gatorade and other high-sugar products. If you had an MRE (meal, ready-to-eat), this drink would make a great accompaniment. Stick a few of these packets in your pocket and you're ready to go. Seeing their faces light up upon finding these packets in a care package will convince you it's the stuff to give the troops.

title: Instant Home Hot Tub
text: I disagree with the negative reviews of this product. If anything, it works better than advertised. One complaint was that if you turn it on and leave it running, by the time you get in, the water's cold. Well, don't turn it on until you're ready to get in. Another complaint was the unit is surprisingly loud. It's also surprisingly bubbly --more like a gym hot tub than a home Jacuzzi. The instructions say not to use it with soap or shampoo (not to put it in the hose), but any shampoo or soap that spills in the tub instantly turns into a mountain of frothy foam. Is this thing fun or what? The leaflet also says to dry the mat and sanitize it now and then, but if you can, just disconnect the hose and leave the mat in the tub. It makes a great bath mat, and it's always ready to transform to hot tub mode. Suction cups hold it in place, so it's easy to remove the mat for cleaning. The unit plugs into the wall, but there's no danger since the hose is long enough to keep the unit away from the tub (and most bathrooms have GFI electrical outlets for backup protection). The only problem is that once your friends see your Bubble Spa, they'll want one too, and the tub will suddenly become a popular destination for your roommates or family.

It does not generate an excess of heat (though if you leave it on for hours upon hours the back gets warm) but casts the promised "full spectrum" - noticeably different from the dim yellow bulbs of the hotel or the nasty fluorescent beasts at work.
