title: Well worth the (low) cost! PLUS: INFO ON HOW TO USE THE TOOLS!!
text:
This blemish removal tool kit is a great value considering its quality, ease of use and low price. Each tool feels good and "weighty" in the hand, and each is strong and durable, being made of high-quality stainless steel--the very same metal of which dermatologists' tools are made. Despite the low price, I do not find these tools "cheap" at all; quite the contrary.

Concerning their ease of use: for the many people who've used such things as Bobby pins and safety pins--much less their fingers and nails--to remove blemishes, these five tools make removing blemishes much easier. Their length gives more leverage and their handles are all textured, giving the user much better control.

While it would be a good idea for the manufacturer to include a helpful set of instructions, my wife and I, as well as two of our teenage grandchildren, found them very easy and self-explanatory to use. And most importantly, we found them to be very effective.

To clean them between uses, a quick rinse could suffice. (Since they're stainless steel, no worries about rusting.) If you feel more cleaning is necessary, simply use an antiseptic disinfectant solution--many of which brands can be found quite cheaply on Amazon.

The zippered case that the tools come in is very soft to the touch. If it is indeed leather then it is very thin leather. But the case is otherwise well stitched and appears durable.

One last tidbit: one of my teenage grandchildren asked what a "comedo" is. Comedo (plural = comedones) is the medical term a doctor, like a dermatologist, might use to describe a clogged hair follicle (pore). Blackheads and whiteheads are common examples of comedones.

I received this kit at a discounted price in exchange for my HONEST review. My goal is to help prospective buyers make better informed decisions, and I will always "call 'em as I truly see 'em."

title: CHANGED... MY... LIFE...
text: Let's be clear. Buying supplements online, even on Amazon, is a big pain largely because of the industry's saturation with unethical companies, selling snake oil, who use shills to pad the 5 star reviews and give products that don't work a misleadingly high review rating. So understand that I am in no way affiliated with this company or any of its employees. I have not been paid or provided any free products in exchange for my review. I said all that just so say this, Zinc picolinate has changed. my. life. I have suffered from severe anxiety and premenstrual disorder for my entire life.  I had postpartum depression that destroyed my marriage. All my life I was put on anti-depressants, anti-anxiety meds, ADHD meds, etc. All the while, I knew I showed all the signs of elevated copper levels, I had been doing research, but since the medical community never really addressed it, I kept it on the back burner. One day I started researching how to combat elevated copper levels, zinc was the answer. But not all zinc supplements are created equal because some aren't readily absorbed in the body. So I further researched and found picolinate is the most absorbable form. I happened to choose this brand, no particular reason. Like I said, it. changed. my. life. I'm also doing Magnesium citrate, the kind that comes in powdered form that you mix with liquid. I'm shocked that all these years there was a way I could actually live life without feeling perpetually stressed and riddled with anxiety. I've only been taking it for a couple of weeks but the change has been pronounced. I'm not sure what it will do to my copper levels in the long term, I may end up needing a supplement that balances them, but just decreasing the effects of copper on my hormones and brain chemistry has been life-changing.

title: Fun to play with my 4 year old
text:
Very simple game, but definitely fun. It says ages 7 and up, but I'd say any child who can associate a picture with a word can handle it, but it being NHL obviously adds to that difficulty curve.

We have this and the original one (which is easier), but she still fairs by just making up her own words for the pictures on her card (e.g. Minnesota Wild is simply "bear").

Also, when I do play with her, I started by giving her a 3 second handicap per card before I would look at it too. That quickly dwindled to 2 seconds, and even then she was still keeping up.

Age requirement aside, it's a fun and kind of frantic game (think slapjack) that has many different very easy to pick up ways to play.

There are about 50 circle shaped cards each with an assortment of images on them. Any two cards will always have 1 matching image. Each player draws a starting card from the deck and they are to memorize the images on it. A dealer will place a card face up and you have to find the image on it that matches your card (hence "Spot it!"), the first to do so wins that card and the game continues with no stopping or turns. This can create a bit of riff raff on who touched the card first, so always have an appointed judge. As the game progresses you memorize them better and it gets increasingly competitive. The other methods of play keep the game fun and interesting.

title: Pretty pricey Protein for not so amazing toilet bennies
text:
I don't do many reviews, but I felt compelled on this one. I was really excited to get this and try it out. Most of the reviews previous to mine were people reviewing the protein before they had even used it for an extended period of time. I wanted to wait until I had exhausted the entire container. First things first: The Good
The protein is exactly what you would want from a plant based protein. I found it tasted like Vanilla Chai Tea (which wasn't too bad for me). Each scoop contains ~20G of protein which isn't too bad either. At times I have found protein powders to bloat me up a bit, and I didn't get that from this. Overall I felt that is was a great product and stood up to its claims so far.
The Bad
Unfortunately I have to write this part, I was really hoping that I wouldn't find anything wrong and I could keep buying this as my main source of protein! The most obvious 'bad' about this product is its price point of ~$60. I didn't pay close attention to the amount that they give you but for 20 scoops of Protein, $60 is way too much. That is roughly $3 per scoop. There is no other protein (plant based or otherwise) that costs this much. If I were to use this as my main Protein, I would have to buy at least 2 containers just to get through a single month. I was really disappointed to get such a small container. IsoPure which, is on the high end of the protein suppliment market is about $1 per scoop and give you 25 Grams of protein. Now I know Isopure is whey base, and this is not, but even Vega Protein (a competitor of this product) give you 25 grams per scoop at a cost of $1.50 per scoop. So for over double the price, I just didn't find that I got double the benefits..which I was disappointed about. If this were $35 or so (bringing my cost per scoop down to normal ranges) I wouldn't mind using this for a longer period to continue my trial and see if I realize other benefits, but it is simply too cost prohibitive.

Additionally, I found that everyday I used this protein, my bowel movements were hard as rocks...rather painful at times, and even more uncomfortable to write about. :) Each day during my trial that I substituted use of lentein with my regular IsoPure protein, everything was immediately back to normal. Go back to this protein, and back came the Rocks...I don't know what caused it but I know the only variable I had in my dieting was the use or non-use of this protein.

Bottomline, if you want an expensive plant based protein look no further. But for the price, I can't personally see benefits that equal the hole in my wallet. I honestly wish I could, because I wanted to love this product. Unfortunately it falls into the 'average' category for me.

title: More cruel than intended (or--at least--far more than this viewer was willing to accept)
text:
This may have been an instance of mismatched expectations. Perhaps I was expecting something gently nostalgic? Or more subtle than a Hollywood comedy (or a Hollywood film for kids). There are occasional and wonderful moments of observational humor. Mostly, though, this is broad farce.

What the writers considered to be funny: it's nearly always based on a familiar formula, one of which I'm admittedly weary: such that this will feel more like a pet peeve than an opinion. But nevertheless, the sort of thing where characters are repeatedly (and at times sadistically) tormented, for the sake of a few chuckles? Don't like it, never did: and this film relies on it. In ways both predictable and tiresome.

(Of course, some viewers will find it more to their liking. I wouldn't want to cast aspersions on someone else's enjoyment. This isn't an awful movie; it's simply not the sort of thing I particularly enjoy.)

The young actors do a fine job. Which could have been a challenge, given that most of the characters are little more than stereotypes: i.e. the kid who eats too much, the "dumb" kid, the "teacher's pet" who's a prissy tattletale, etc. Oh but they're somewhat affectionately portrayed, as cardboard cutouts go. (Except the obsessively-studious boy. Not a surprise that he's repeatedly bullied, but appalling how he's portrayed as fully deserving of every taunt and assault.) Nicolas is more well-rounded. Not terribly interesting: although--compared to his schoolmates--he's remarkably complex.

Despite being boxed-in by similarly stereotypical characteristics? The foibles of Nicolas' parents (and of the other kids' parents, and the teacher) are a highlight, and got the most enthusiastic laughs. I recognize I may feel this way because they're adults and "can take it." Whereas seeing winsome, endearing kids endure mind-numbing mistreatment? Before using the word "funny," I'd think of plenty of less-flattering ways to characterize their seemingly-unending woes.

Tone is everything. In Fargo many of the characters are tremendously engaging: including those who are loathsome. Even when they're placed in agonizing situations, it's hilarious.

Le Petit Nicolas, superficially, appears a charming story about a group of prepossesing (even adorable) schoolboys. Then, at length, we see them (metaphorically) put through the woodchipper. This is neither Fargo nor South Park. It doesn't feel wrong; it feels worse than wrong.

title: A fifth star for the zipper
text:
This eyeglass case handles my wraparound sunglasses, that also protect my dry eyes from the wind. NOTE: Otherwise, for all the other glasses that I mentioned in my review of the eyeglass repair kit, I put them in my pants pocked. For wraparound, wind-protective glasses, a case is needed. I was skeptical, because as I said, I don't usually use a glasses case for my off the shelf glasses, so I wasn't sure I would use this.

It turns out the it is !SO MUCH FUN! to put the sunglasses in this thing, often considering which side to put them in -- always with the hinge in your left and folding the glasses into the flatter looking part in your right hand -- or something different and opposite, I think, if you are left handed. Then the fun part is zipping up the case. The zipper works *so* well, and fast, zippy, even. The sound it makes is pleasant. I've done my day's work for a neater, more orderly world, and can put my other glasses in my pocket.

My head is pretty small, and I use children's sunglasses to keep the wind out of my eyes. The case therefore seems quite large to me.

title: careful
text:
Side Effects and Precautions

Methionine can cause allergic reactions and other side effects, regardless of the form its taken in. The most common side effects are nausea and vomiting. Some people feel drowsy after taking it. Emergency medical attention may be necessary if a person shows signs of a several allergic reaction such as difficulty breathing, chest tightness, and swelling.

Pregnant women or nursing mothers should not take methionine supplements without first consulting their healthcare provider, because it's not clear how they affect a postpartum body. Those who take oral contraceptives should also inform a medical professional before taking it, since it increases estrogen production. This amino acid can worsen existing conditions such as liver disease, acidosis, and schizophrenia. While it has no known negative interactions with other drugs, patients should tell their medical care provider about any other medications or supplements they are using prior to starting methionine.

text:
[[VIDEOID:922acaa26d5939f9d4b5a6dd554a0e9e]] I have back pain for a while now, probably because of the many hiking expeditions I did when I was young, carrying very heavy backpacks in the wilderness, with supplies to last for many days. And now, with my desk job, where I am staring at the computer for 8-10 hours every day, this doesn’t help. On the top of that, with all this “stay at home stuff” when I cannot go anywhere, I find myself spending even more time on my personal computer. All these things add up.
My wife, who is very concerned about this Coronavirus stuff and doesn’t want me to go to the chiropractor and spend several minutes in the waiting room with other people, she bought for me this back stretcher to try it. And the main reason she chose this over other similar models is because it comes with a sack where I can put away and store all the components.
On the top of that it comes with a nice massage ball, which can be used to massage your soles. It is very helpful for people that have bad blood circulation on the feet, or associated nerve pain (which unfortunately I have also).
And then, it has a strap which I use to attach the device to my home office chair and I have lumber support when I work.
The back stretcher has the same effect as the machine which my chiropractor is using on my treatment sessions, except that it doesn’t have moving parts. But the advantage is that I can do the treatment at home, whenever I want, and is free (of course, after the initial investment to purchase the beck stretcher).
In conclusion, I am using this device for two weeks now, I am very satisfied and I strongly recommend it to any person who has the same problems as I do (back pain and bad blood circulation in the feet).

text:
Please read the reviews. Many of the reviews are NOT for this product, the Vifycim Electric Razor. How can Amazon give this product a 4.8 rating based on reviews for other products. Amazon must fix this before I buy this item!

Here are just two reviews (there are more) supposedly for this product:

1. My cats love to jump on my desk and eat my brushes for some reason and bite chunks out of them so I needed something to keep them out. This is perfect. I only wish it were bigger cause I have too many brushes and they don’t all fit. I also need to push them away from the sides before I shut the lid or the bristles get caught in the lid and misshape them.

2. I needed a small reusable palette so I could stop wasting palette paper or little plastic cups everytime I wanted to mix just a small amount of a different color or when I am just experimenting. This silicone palette has worked perfectly for that purpose. It's a little hard to clean off when the paint residue is thin, but tape works well enough. When the paint is thick it's super easy to clean and peels right off. One bothersome quality is that dust and lint stick VERY easily to the palette and ends up getting mixed in with the paint sometimes. title: It's a push up people - this works as expected
text:
[[VIDEOID:45376213de93fe0b128beb0ccf9b966a]]I'm going to start by saying, that I think it is unfair to give this low stars because it is a push-up. A lot of reviewers are complaining about that, like they didn't know. I would suggest reading the description. It is stated in the description that this is a push-up and you should go into this understanding that.

That being said, this is a good product (thick plastic, well sized, and attractive), but it's not the worlds best push-up tube. When this comes out of the package, the plunger you push is very firm and sticky. I thought that this would be a good indicator that these would have some grip to them so that your product doesn't just fly out the top when you push the plunger. A common problem with push-ups. I was able to fill them with no leaking, and they held a really nice quantity of product. One ounce seems just perfect for about a month of body butter or natural deodorant. Imagine a tube a little bit larger than a quarter, and about the length of your pointer finger. This looked like a five star product, until I needed to push the tube up.

The oils in the body butter lubed the interior portion of the tube and the push-up piece slips right out of the tube. There's no lip to keep the gasket in and the product from falling out. As other reviewers have stated, you need to use your finger, on the product, to push this back down into the bottom of the tube again. You could probably get tricky with application and push it back while you're applying by creating resistance against your finger and pushing on the product at the same time.

I often times make mosquito repellent body butter bars or Shea butter bars for my son who has eczema. I don't think he could manage application without this becoming a huge problem. A twist-up tube would certainly be more appropriate in that situation as I don't think that a child could use this cautiously.

Bottom line, if you can use this cautiously and be careful with applying, you can avoid the product flying out of the tube and enjoy this attractive, and perfectly sized tube. If not, look into a twist tube.

title: Good product for the value, but with some quirks.
text:
I just received the product today and used it some this evening. I have used a similar (but more expensive) version of this product, so I was familiar with the process and instructions. I'm not sure if I was spoiled by the more expensive product, but I wasn't very happy with this curler upon first use, due to the following reasons:

1) Shorter pieces of hair curled much better than longer pieces (although width and thickness of selected strands were the same)

2) The third strand I curled got stuck upon release, and it took me a scary amount of time to get it un-stuck. I had to turn off the curler for fear it would burn through the strand before I could get it to release. It took me about 45 seconds to finally get it free.

3) If any small bit of pressure is released once you grip the pieces closed (and then several times when I held full pressure the entire time), the beeps stop and it doesn't count down for you. You just have to count the seconds off yourself and guess when you need to release

4) I have thin, fine hair, but it took the max heat setting and max time for the curls to hold

5) Immediately after turning the curler on, the product began to smell like burning plastic

However, I know sometimes it just takes some patience and practice to learn the quirks of some products and how they are on individual types of hair. I am still willing to try it again and see if I have the same issues.

Some features I like of this product compared to the more expensive versions were the value compared to its competition, the LCD display, the "alternating" setting for direction of curls, and the overall aesthetics of this curler.

Response from the seller:
Thank you for your time to write this email. Very appreciate.

1- May I know how long is your hair? Actually it does not work really well if you have really long hair (which is marked in the listing), such as all the way down back, almost to buttock, so only half the length of the hair could get curled. But that is not an issue if you have short to medium length hair.

2- Don't be afraid when hair is tangled, we always suggest you unplug the styler first and then use something sharp (like the tail of comb) to softly pull the hair out from the chamber.

3- As for the beep stopping issue, we would be glad to suggest you that the handle should be closed firmly. If there is any small bit of pressure is released, the beep will automatically stop. So after the hair is drawn in the curler makes spaced apart short, high pitched "beep" while the hair is being curled. After you hear a series of quick ‘beep-beep-beep-beep’ prompt, that's the time to loosen the handle. Be sure to listen to these, the timing is perfect.

[Below is the information for your reference]
- Setting 8 - 8 seconds, for slightly curls, 3 beeps, and finally ring 4 times to indicate the time is up.
- Setting 10 - 10 seconds, for soft curls, 4 beeps, and finally ring 4 times to indicate the time is up.
- Setting 12 - 12 seconds, for strong curls, 5 beeps, and finally ring 4 times to indicate the time is up.

4- Dear Allyson, if you have very thin, fine hair, we always suggest you don't use the highest temperature at the first time when you switch on the styler. As a honest seller, almost all we know that there is protein in our hair, if we choose the highest temperature at the first time (for example: 230C), then the hair is reached from the lowest temperature to the highest temperature within just a few seconds, the hair will be normally smelt like something plastic, but please note this will be damage your hair. So we always suggest our buyers should choose the lowest temperature first then gradually choose the high temperature, in order to let your hair adapt to the temperature better.

Dear Allyson, thank you for liking the feature of LCD Display and the Curl Direction. Actually this is the new version product in the market compared to those traditional automatic hair curlers. As an honest seller, we trust in our product and try our utmost to make every customer satisfactory. If you have any questions in the future, we very welcome your email and be happy to serve you :)

Thank you for reading my email dear Allyson.

My response after trying it again this morning:

Thank you for your response. My hair is only about 4 inches past my shoulders, so the length is within range. The smell came as soon as I plugged in the curler, before I even attempted to put hair in there. That smell did not come back when I tried it again this morning, so it must have just been the 1st time the plastic heated up.

I will continue practicing with this product and try to learn the best ways to make it work correctly. It has its quirks, but then, what electronic doesn't?
*****************************************************************

After using the product again this morning, I learned the following:

1) To get the best curl, use VERY small pieces of hair. My hair is thin already, but I still had to use very small pieces and brush them out really good to have the best success. Even then, with the longer strands, it still did not want to curl the entire strand.

2) Occasionally, the hair would not pull into the curler correctly, and it would just twist up the strand instead of actually curling it. I would have to repeat on the same strand until it pulled in properly.

3) In the 30 min it took me to curl all of my hair (again, I have thin, fine hair, and can usually curl it all with a curling iron in about 5 minutes or less), the strands got stuck in the curler about every 8th curl. Some of the times it stuck, I was able to get it out ok, but the curl was pulled out. Other times, the strand got really stuck and started smoking. This was scary, but I just unplugged the curler and worked my hair free.

Overall, this is a good curler for the value. It's just a matter of preference if you would be willing to deal with some of the quirks and hassle for a better value, or go with a higher end product that it a little more consistent. This curler may also work better with thick hair, but I cannot attest to that. I can say that with my thin hair, the higher-end curler handled larger strands and was a lot more consistent. It also never got stuck - not once. If it started to curl and the hair tangled at all, it would stop and release it.

title: One of the best household personal pharma items in the bathroom cabinet
text:
I've enjoyed using DMSO for myself, family, and patients since the mid 1990's. It's likely one of the best household personal pharma items in the bathroom cabinet.

Recently I noted some people saying you can use DMSO together with wintergreen oil as a local analgesic. Well, time for me to try it!

According to Wiki references, Thirty ml (about 1 fluid ounce) of oil of wintergreen is equivalent to 55.7 grams of aspirin, or about 171 adult aspirin tablets (US). This conversion illustrates the potency and potential toxicity of oil of wintergreen. [1]

Patients should definitely be aware that excessive use of DMSO together with Wintergreen oil applied to the skin could have an outcome similar to the excessive use of aspirin, (note: aspirin is not methyl salicylate, but rather acetylsalicylic acid), such as bleeding and so on. In other words, it might not be a very good idea for patients to relentlessly apply large combinations of DMSO and Wintergreen Oil, day in and day out, or over vast surfaces of the skin.

So on the one hand, it appears that DMSO together with Wintergreen oil is no more dangerous than aspirin; but on the other hand, it can be just as dangerous as aspirin for those that are relentless in its excessive application. I hope I haven’t scared anyone away. The fact is that DMSO used with other medicines is extremely powerful & useful. In some instances, such as the treatment of poisonous spider bites, the combo of DMSO with other meds is the best medicine available (per the empirical studies I have read). And like all powerful medicines, you have to be intelligent in its application. Thank God the corporate-sponsored US FDA was unable to bar its use!

Regarding safety: Is there a difference between taking aspirin pills and applying methyl salicylate transdermally (note: transdermally means DMSO carrying the medicine across the skin)? According to one peer-reviewed study, there is no difference; “No significant difference was detected between baseline and 6-hour thromboxane levels for either aspirin.” [2]

Does Wintergreen oil mix well with DMSO? I don’t know, but will give it a try. For DMSO to effectively carry medicine across the skin barrier, two conditions must be met:

1) The molecular weight of the medicine must about 350 moles or less, [Molecular weights of everything can be gleamed by online search or Merck index – If the medicine weighs more, then the chemical is just too big to pass through the skin barrier];

2) The medicine must be able to fully dissolve into the DMSO, [Vitamin C for instance does not dissolve well at all – wherein many hormones from testosterone, estrogen, to corticosteroids, dissolve and are carried across the skin very well by DMSO].

My personal experience has found a great deal of success in using DMSO to transdermally carry many antibiotic ointments and corticosteroids across the skin – Hence, vastly improving their effectiveness!

SUNBURN: I have never seen anything work nearly to the degree of DMSO (particularly with aloe gel) on preventing sunburn! I cannot begin to recall the innumerable successes of patient-use whose skin turned Beet Red under the Caribbean sun. I have never seen an instance of ‘sun burn’ occurring in a single patient provided they applied it soon and frequent! I am not endowed with a great deal of eloquence. Even if I had the skill, I do not believe I could adequately describe the remarkable achievements of this physician in using DMSO (and aloe gel) in preventing sunburn among over-exposed patients in the Caribbean.

The caution for people is to realize that DMSO has the ability to carry many chemicals across the skin and into the capillaries, and blood stream. Patients are advised to keep this in mind. It might be extremely harmful to apply DMSO and then work with poisonous chemicals you don’t want in your blood stream; [examples: gardening chemicals such as glycophosphates, insect killers (including mosquito spray), certain cleaning products, and maybe even sun screen]. The great news is that this is a wonderfully powerful & useful medicinal tool; and you are a grown adult that does not need some government bureaucrat to hold you by the hand, and do everything for you!

Power to the People!

[1] Johnson PN: Methyl salicylate/aspirin equivalence: Vet Hum Toxicol 1985; 26:317-318

[2] Tanen DA, et al., Comparison of oral aspirin versus topical applied methyl salicylate for platelet inhibition. Ann Pharmacother. 2008 Oct;42(10):1396-401. doi: 10.1345/aph.1L128. Epub 2008 Aug 12.

title: DO NOT FLUSH!
text:
Dear Pampers Kandoo Users:
Yes, I love(d) these just like every other mom with a little one in potty training or above. HOWEVER, and please pay attention to this: I strongly recommend you DO NOT FLUSH these wipes. Our home has a septic system and every two to three years we require a pump-out. Recently we found our system backed up outside of our normal pump-out range, and when our technician arrived he looked at our youngest and said "I bet you are at the stage of flushable wipes". This man does not have some sort of magical powers bestowed upon him, he simply has seen a boatload of septic issues cropping up with the introduction of 'flushable wipes' on the market. Sure enough we had a front row seat to look inside the tank and see a mass of these 'flushable' wipes blocking up our tank.
Save yourself the 'convenience' that you will pay for in the end. We are going back to that good ol' fashioned way of wipe well, wash your hands, and saving a 'load' of money!

title: Great Value with Certificate of Analysis
text:
Saw palmetto is widely promoted and used to treat the symptoms of benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), and some research studies have found it to be helpful in this regard. However, the webmd website characterizes the total scientific research on this issue as "conflicting and contradictory." Therefore, I would regard the claims made by Purely Holistic (and other supplement sellers) about the effectiveness of their Saw Palmetto product to be excessively optimistic.

When buying any supplement, I like to see that it is made in the United States adhering to Good Manufacturing Practice (GMPs), as is indicated in the Amazon item description for this product. In addition, I always look for a seal of approval from a third party laboratory (e.g., USP, NSF) certifying that the supplement really does contain what is claimed on the label.  In this case, I saw none. Therefore, I sent a message to Purely Holistic via their website asking whether they had third party testing or a Certificate of Analysis (COA) available for this product. I received a prompt reply that included a copy of a recent COA report conducted by Vitalabs Inc, a company located in Georgia. Their analysis found that the tested capsules did contain 500mg of Saw Palmetto powder (25% extract) as stated on the label and were free from common forms of microbial contamination. I have attached screenshots of this report.

The most outstanding feature of this Purely Holistic product Is it value. For the current price of $10.97, you receive 180 capsules each containing 500 mg of saw palmetto extract. I compared this to Amazon's current best selling saw palmetto supplement, [[ASIN:B00XUZCSPC Saw Palmetto Capsules For Prostate Health - Extract & Berry Powder Complex To Reduce Frequent Urination - DHT Blocker To Fight Hair Loss - 500mg Natural Supplement - 100% Money-Back Guarantee]], which provides only 100 capsules with the same stated potency for $15.99. This means that Purely Holistic provides about 62% more saw palmetto extract for your dollar!

I accepted an offer to purchase this Purely Holistic Saw Palmetto product with a promotional discount and review it after noticing that Purely Holistic sells a number of well-reviewed supplements on Amazon and that their product is manufactured in the United States; they also have a nice looking website. I try my best to write fair and useful reviews. I have given this supplement a four star rating due to its excellent value and ability to promptly provide a Certificate of Analysis. I deducted one star because saw palmetto may not be an effective treatment for BPH symptoms. I hope I have been helpful to you if you are deciding whether to purchase this supplement!

title: Pretty glasses, but painful to wear
text: I do a lot of computer work every day. My eyes need blue-light reading glasses to be comfortable. But for some reason, the plastic frames on the various glasses I bought kept breaking. I bought these thinking that the metal frames would last longer. However, the screw-on nose pads on these are excruciatingly painful. I've adjusted them, tried using foam pads, and padded my nose with bandages. I tried a couple of types of silicone nose pads, but they didn't work either.  Finally, I found larger oval silicone nose pads that offer some relief. Even with those nose pads, I can only wear these glasses for a couple of hours at a time before my nose is screaming in pain. That said, these are very attractive glasses and seem to filter blue-light well. Perhaps people with thinner nose bridges would find these glasses comfortable to wear. If the manufacturer would replace the small, hard plastic nose pads with larger, oval silicone nose pads, it would greatly improve these glasses.

If you're a wedding photog or other high consistent use off-camera flash shooter, then perhaps one of the high-output types is what you need.  But if you're a hobbyist who only pulls out their flash on the weekends, or even less, then it's all about the Eneloops.  I bought a brick of these things and I never worry about charging them. title: Great roller!
text:
2/9/2016

Received the Foam Roller from Spinal Labs today -- it was much bigger than I originally expected. I have some major long-term tendon problems from a condition known as Fluoroquinolone Toxicity Syndrome, so I constantly need work on my neck and back. However, because of some tendon degeneration, I can only handle so much before it ends up hurting me.

With that being said, I tried the foam roller and it was NOT for me -- it was too hard, and it began to hurt me (but not in a good way) almost immediately. So why the 4 stars, you ask?

My husband has some bad back problems due to his time in the military. He came home and tried the foam back roller and loved it. It was the perfect size and firmness for him. He said he could feel his vertebrae releasing as he slowly rolled it up and down. I informed him that the paper that came with the roller said there was some training information on their website.

However, when I looked for the training info, it wasn't there. I went to their YouTube channel and they haven't uploaded a video since December 2014. This is why I'm giving the product 4 stars instead of 5, as Spinal Labs indicated you could watch and learn how to better use the roller online.

This product was provided at a discounted price in exchange for my honest review. My review is based solely on personal experience and is my honest opinion.

UPDATE 3/17/2016 - Hubby is still using this almost daily. He loves this thing. It helps him stretch and adjust his back as he rolls along it.

title: Cute design, great value for the price
text:
For the price, this is a great diaper so far - we've only used it for a month or so, but so far we have had no leaks. The pattern is cute, and the outside of the diaper is incredibly soft. There are three rise settings, and the size seems comparable to other one size pocket diapers we have. The snaps for the waist adjustment are well-placed, with a row at the top, and another set of snaps below that to prevent wing-droop. The only thing that would make it better to me would be double gussets at the legs, but we have not yet had a leak, so the single leg elastic works fine so far.

You can get this a little cheaper ordering from the Alva Baby website, but you will only get one insert, and you will be waiting for several weeks to receive the diaper.

UPDATE (1-1-2014)
We've been using these for over eight months now, and they are one of our favorite daytime diapers. They have enough snaps to be able to get a good fit. We have not had any leaks or blowouts with any of our Alva Baby diapers (nor with any others, except for nighttime issues, but that is a whole different diapering adventure). We did end up buying extra inserts - our 19 month old needs two of the microfiber inserts to be able to go up to two hours without a diaper change (we haven't tried to go much longer - we like to change him at least every 1.5 to 2 hours). We dry the inserts on medium or medium-high heat, and hang the covers to dry, and after over eight months of washing every 2-3 days, all of the diapers still look new, all of the snaps still work the same as when we bought them, and we have no smell issues with the inserts or covers. Our wash routine is to rinse twice with just cold water (prewashcycle), wash once in hot water with Tide Ultra powder (no bleaches, fabric softeners, or extra scents), and then rinse twice with cold water.

The only possible negative I can think of is that we don't feel comfortable stuffing these with more than two microfiber inserts - the elastic around the legs is not quite as stretchy as our Bumgenius diapers, and I think if we tried to 'overstuff' these ones, we might risk leaks or a blowout, but this hasn't been an issue for us, because we tend to use the Bumgenius with a little extra stuffing when we need a little extra absorbency. We have used these with two microfiber inserts and one thin bamboo insert with no problems.

title: NOT DURABLE , failed days after warranty expired.
text:
If I had written this review a month ago it would have been 5 stars. I purchased this scale on Oct. 23 2014 and first used it Nov. 1 2014. On Dec. 4 2015 the scale died, 44 days after the warranty expired. Not a very durable product. So I figure, at $130, it cost me $11 a month for the convenience of my weight being recorded for me. I do not mind paying for quality things I want but I am a Veteran living on a small pension and every dollar counts. By contrast my Walmart, $20 , 10 year old digital scale, still works and I am quite capable of recording my weight manually. But with my now owning a Fitbit Charge HR I am hooked on the website and I promptly went to Best Buy (did not want to wait to get it from Amazon) and and bought a new scale (on credit). Then to my added dismay (according to my new scale) I had gained 3 lbs., and increased my body fat from 19% to 25% during my trip to the store. I know the body fat measurement is only meant to be a guiding/goal number and not a clinical , precise measurement. I do not think it is unreasonable to think that with the same make of 2 scales that the 2 measurements would have been closer to the same. Especially the weight.

In all fairness I loved this thing when it worked (5 stars) but being durable,long lasting is most important to me, not function. If you are willing to risk that it won't work a year from now and do not care, I would recommend you buy it. I love my Charge HR too, but have only had it 2 months. If it fails after 1 year, well I will be all done with Fitbit products.

title: Wonderful Quality and Well Worth the Price
text:
I cannot tell you how much I like this wig! I had really liked the color in the photo since it would coordinate with my costume, but it is less of the light golden brown that the photo shows and more of a dirty blonde (the reason for knocking off one star rating). I am not too disappointed, though. I didn't want white and a good quality brown one is hard to find. The quality is fantastic and it looked pretty good right out the package. It will, of course, need some touching up but I was impressed that it wasn't a tangled flat mess. The photos I have posted are of it right out of the package before even trying it on. I will post additional photos once I touch it up.

It stands up very high behind the head. What I did was shove some plastic grocery bags in the crown to round it back out as it was a tad flat. I will leave it that way until I am ready to use it. There are curls all around the side and hanging behind. Even the hanging curls were in very nice shape when I received it. The hair on the crown is flat and just combed back.

The inside has an elastic cross band that should make it more adjustable to different size heads (rather than a skull cap design). I will update my review on that once I use it.

I am also leaving a short review of the seller here since they are the only ones listed as sellers. At first I was shocked at the $20 shipping charge, but then remembered it was coming from Europe and their shipping costs are probably expensive like ours. Anyway, since I needed it quickly, I wrote the seller to ask if the $20 at least included fast shipping. They wrote back promptly and courteously and assured me that shipping is very fast. I decided to take a chance and am very glad I did. It arrived in only FIVE DAYS! I can't guarantee that service for others, but if you are on the fence about purchasing because of delivery time, go ahead and write the seller to ask what their current shipping times are.

UPDATE
I changed my review from 1 star to 4 stars because after contacting the company, they exchanged the small size for a Large size at no cost to me, so excellent customer service. However, other vendors which sell both sizes include instructions in their description to measure a couple of head dimensions to determine the correct size to order. The large size works great for me and does not slip off my head since the rear Velcro straps now correctly fit the shape of my head. This design of chin strap does not put concentrated pressure on any one part of your head, which means that your hair is not smashed down in one location, which can damage the hair follicles. The cap also does not make my head feel hot, I guess because of it's lightweight cotton material. All in all, when sized properly, this is a good product.

title: As comfortable as a $35 cushion, but I had a reaction to it--maybe toxic?
text:
So, I'll just say, I only used this for one day. I was interested in Purple, as their mattress commercials were intriguing, and when I needed a new butt cushion for my at-home office chair, I thought I'd go for broke and get the Purple chair cushion and lumbar support. They arrived quickly, and I put them both in their sleeves and set them up on my office chair. The next morning I was using them at my desk, when I noticed a weird burning/melting plastic smell. I thought maybe it was my computer, but I couldn't find the source of the smell. For what it's worth, the cushion and lumbar support were fine--my coccyx was still uncomfortable sitting on the 1-1/4" thing cushion, so it didn't seem any better than my previous ~$35 chair cushion, but YMMV.

Here's where things get weird: In addition to the weird burning smell, I also started feeling my throat kind of go numb, and needed to clear my throat a lot. It was weird, it was as if someone had sprayed a little bit of chloraseptic in the back of my throat; it felt a little swollen and kind of sensitive, and had the same feel as a chloraseptic. I thought maybe it was something I'd eaten, but my wife and I ate the same thing and she didn't feel anything. The smell would come and go.

About an hour into my morning at my desk, with the weird phantom smell and my throat acting up (I thought it was just in my head), I started to get a little light-headed and feel sick. I immediately got up and left the room, and felt better, which is when I started putting things together--the only new thing in my life was the Purple cushions. So I sniffed them, and sure enough, they smelled like the burning plastic smell. My wife suggested it might be temporary, so I turned a fan on and opened the office window, and had the fan blow on the chair with the cushions all night.

This morning I hoped everything would clear up, but after working at my desk for about 20 minutes I started feeling that weirdness in my throat again. So, I've only had them for about 24 hours in use, but they literally make me feel sick. I don't have any latex allergy, or really any other allergy I'm aware of, so I have no idea what could be causing it. It could just be me--YMMV--but I will not be buying any other Purple products.

Their website says everything is non-toxic and made from food-safe rubber, so I don't know what's going on, but between the smell and the effect on the back of my throat, I'm not keeping these in my house anymore. I'll reach out to Purple as well and report my experience, and will update this if I hear anything back.

title: Helps me feel better in the car immediately
text:
I bought this to use in my car while driving for rideshare. My car seat wasn't uncomfortable, but 5-9 hours not moving very much makes everything a little sore.
This cushion instantly made my bottom less tired and my legs not cramp at all. Previously, I could only make it about 3 hours before I had to take a 15 minute break. Now I can go at least double that before my bottom and legs need to stretch. It also does keep my back from getting tired.
The gel is nice and cool and is just wide enough to fit under my 38" waist - any bigger and I might need to go to another model. I also tried it on my old couch and it makes a big difference there too. DO NOT try the egg test on this model, it is not thin enough. The instructions suggest your keys instead and that is a good test.
The cover has a nice feel and fits very well, but I do not expect it to last more than a dozen washes. Hopefully they will sell just those. The only less positive thing is that the cover does not have very good grips on the bottom - the little rubber beads do not hold it in place when I get into or out of the car, but it does keep me planted while sitting on it.
Really like Purple products and I definitely recommend this one.

title: Nearly as good as GlassFloss filters
text:
I didn't want to pay nearly $30 for an air filter. I found these on line for $26 for a 2-pack.
I was slightly worried that I will get what I paid for.

Here are the measured differences. I took these measurements myself with the actual filters. Both brands claim to be 30" x 28" x 2" Merv 11 filters.

GlassFloss: 29 1/4" x 27 3/4" x 1 3/4"
Accumulair: 29 3/8" x 27 1/4" x 1 3/4"

They are slightly different sizes but the filter slot in my Tranquility 30 heat pump has enough margin to accept either one.

The Accumulair is built with less cardboard, making it slightly more flimsy (weighing in at 600 grams vs 900 grams for the stock GlassFloss filter). But since there is less cardboard and thinner cardboard supports, there is also better air flow.
The filter media in the Accumulair filters is slightly thinner too. The internal wire mesh in either filter is the same AWG of wire. The heat-pump air exhanger is directly in back of the filter slot so a more flimsy filter is still able to have sufficient support.

At only $13 per filter, The Accumulair is a good product at a great price.
Before, with the GlassFloss filter, I was hoping to vacuum it out and make it last 6-months to a year. After a few months, I tried vacuuming it out but with all the folds and crannies, it was very cumbersome and time consuming. Who knows if the vacuum was able to remove the small stuff like P 2.5 too.

With the less expensive Accumulair filters, I can justify swapping them out every 3 months like I should.

title: Awesome product. Works to relieve my anxiety
text:
This is the second time I've ordered ReMag, and I will continue to do so unless something else that is the same quality/purity/effectiveness comes along for a cheaper price.

Sometimes I'm a bit of a cheapskate when it comes to buying things for myself, so this product must actually work in order for me to pay full price for it - now twice!

I've been suffering from anxiety for the past...well, probably my whole life...but it's gotten pretty bad in the past couple years. The first time I ordered this was when I was having random muscle twitches in my arms and legs and slight muscle fatigue. I basically convinced myself I had some serious illness (I'm a slight hypochondriac), but when I googled my symptoms, I found out I might be magnesium deficient. Turns out anxiety can be a result of the same deficiency as well. I came across Dr. Carolyn Dean's website, and then ended up ordering a cheap brand of ionic magnesium from amazon (because, remember - I'm a cheapskate). That brand actually worked really well for relieving my anxiety, but some reviews stated that their bottles were expired. So I looked at the exp. date on my bottle, and sure enough, it had expired a year or two before. I also read some reviews about safety concerns about arsenic content in that brand. Concerned for my health/safety, I quit taking it, and sure enough, my anxiety came back full force, so I gave in and ordered ReMag.

Just so you know, the taste is absolutely horrible. Bitter and disgusting. Dr. Dean recommends mixing it with water and salt and sipping it throughout the day. I tried that and just couldn't keep doing that everyday. I loathed drinking it and eventually stopped taking it, which equaled the return of anxiety.

So now I put the dose of magnesium in a couple ounces of grape or orange juice and immediately guzzle a bunch of water after that to get rid of the residual bitter taste.

Anyways, this product is awesome, even if it is "expensive."

title: One of the best women's toys you can get for the money
text:
The bullet came on time and secure in it's packaging. As you can see from the pictures, it is small, but it was the size that I expected. From the get go, the plastic feels kind of light and cheap - until you turn it on. It's pretty damn powerful. My girlfriend has another toy, much bigger, and this almost gives that one a run for it's money. Anyways, make sure you use lube, but not too much because then the bullet will fall out of your fingers. I suggest not getting the lube on your hand. The sides of the bullet are lined with rubber so that who ever is holding it will have some extra grip to prevent it from slipping.

There are two buttons. The bottom button is On/Off, and the top button switches between the various modes. The first three modes are continuous vibration, at various speeds, but after that there are a multitude of different modes that are more like a heartbeat. Its fun to play around with the modes. But, the job will most likely be done at the fastest continuous mode. It only took about 10 minutes :) All in all, I am very please with this toy.

title: NOT a G-tube or PEG-tube holder!
text:
Whomever is hand sewing this did a decent job - but the product isn't what's advertised... Let me educate you:

G-tubes are "flush against skin". I can't imagine choosing to wear a belt to cover it? The G-tube is not a big deal. I doubt anyone wants to carry a feeding tube inside it - tubes go inside their feeding supply kit, which they have to carry to eat! And there are far more supplies than a tube (which is too long for the skinny pocket anyway!)

Second: These belts are for what's called a PEG-tube (also a feeding tube), but since most Amazon sellers are clueless, most advertise as a G-tube holder - not a big deal.

A PEG is NOT FLUSH to skin. It hangs an average of 5 inches from the stomach and is annoying. These types of belts are supposed to have a slit in back of pocket to insert this tube INTO THE POCKET, where it lays protected and the belt keeps it secure. To use for feeding, you simply open up the pouch to access tube and place tube back in pouch when done.

As far as for Dialysis? I am confused. Ports for Dialysis are secured into the upper chest under the skin; so the tubes are protruding from that area.

It's my fault for not looking at pictures - i only read description, and IMO, this is a useless piece of material except maybe as a child's hidden lunch money or, money card.
Bad products !

title: Great software, great design but it should tell you that your router must support 802.11b
text:
I started getting in shape using MyFitnessPal for my Windows Phone. After a bit I realized that it would be handy to have some automation so I bought my wife and me both Fitbit Flex's and the Fitbit aria.

So far it's a mostly positive experience. The scale is beautiful, just as simple as your normal scale once it's setup (more on that in the cons) and with Fitbits software which is a lot of what you're paying for when you get bands it's incredibly helpful for setting goals.

The only bad things so far were the setup. I started setting things up with my Time Capsule router (1st gen, using Wireless N). I kept getting errors while trying to connect the Fitbit and eventually decided to contact support. I work with computers (I'm a programmer) so this was a little disappointing and before I hit the send button I decided to do a little sleuthing. It turns out this only supports routers that are setup to work with 802.11b. My router was specifically setup to not work with some of the older standards since I don't have much legacy stuff on my network. Even my oldest stuff supports N. Anyway once I updated my router everything worked fine.

title: MhiL Collapsible Walking Cane with Light
text: This is a wonderful cane.  Safety, convenience, lightweight, portable, LED light all wrapped up in one. This cane comes folded and collapsed in a 14" long nylon storage bag which weights about 19 ounces total cane and bag. Flat enough and lightweight enough to easily fit into a suitcase for traveling. The lightweight metal cane expands up to 37 inches with 5 possible adjustable height slots. The handle is a silky smooth rubber comfortable to hold, there is a wrist strap and I love the built in LED flash light in the handle (2 AA batteries not included with purchase). A flash light in the handle is a great feature for dark or dimly lighted areas. The light is not adjustable and shines directly forward. It would be nice if there was the ability to adjust the light in a downward position. The tripod footing of the cane allows the cane to free stand yet will pivot and turn giving a more flexible natural function when in use. Three replacement rubber tips for the tripod foot were included. I would have appreciated the inclusion of instructions, recommendations, safety features, precautions when using a cane as well as what kind of batteries are needed, where and how they are applied. Even better if batteries were included. I like the lightweight flexible portability of this cane. I am submitting this evaluation freely and of my choosing.

title: Finger Toothbrushes for Your Dogs
text: The package contained 8 finger toothbrushes. Each finger toothbrush is a pliable plastic measuring approximately 2 1/4" high and approximately 1" diameter at the base. The "brush" surface part is about 3/4" x 7/16". The bristles are a rigid plastic, while the finger portion is a softer more pliable plastic. We have a large breed dog who did allow me to use the brush on her teeth. I was able to reach her back teeth, successfully brush each tooth and felt my finger was somewhat protected while in use. I had readjust the finger toothbrush a couple of times during the process since I had a little trouble keeping the finger toothbrush on my finger securely since my fingers were smaller in diameter and did not fit tightly on my finger. A man's finger may be more suitable for the size of this toothbrush. This toothbrush is a great addition to your dogs health if your dog allows you to put your finger in their mouth and move around. Suggestion for product improvement would be softer bristles and an option of Small finger toothbrushes for dog owners with smaller fingers.

title: Wildly inaccurate--"lost" 5.6 lb in just a few minutes...
text:
Updated 4/6/14.

The Aria scale initially weighed me at 6lb below my old scale. Took my old scale to my doctor's office yesterday and it compared at 1 lb below the doctor's scale. So the Aria is weighing me at 7 lb below my real weight--which could make for a nasty shock. I had previously tried to calibrate it with consecutive weighings, per FitBit support's instructions. Weights then varied by 5.6 lb one day, and 2.9 lb the next day.

Despite being able to see these weights in my account, FitBit Support insisted that the scale was weighing me within an acceptable 2 lb accuracy range. Very poor math skills! In this age of internet transparency--and yes, I got screen shots of my account--it's bizarre that they would insist against documented facts that the scale is on target. Either it's faulty or it's lousy. My guess is that FitBit is well aware that it proves inaccurate if you check it. They didn't even attempt to replace it.

If you're in a good place weight-wise, this might work OK, albeit expensively, to keep on track. Even 2 lb, let alone 5-6 lb, isn't an acceptable accuracy range for those of us who are trying to lose weight. My old scale never deviates more than .2 lb (yeah, I'll admit I'll occasionally check a couple of times if I'm extra-delighted or extra-horrified with my weight).

Also, don't even try to set this up on a computer. What a nightmare! When I switched to a smartphone, setup was a cinch.

So yep, it's going back. I was very excited to try this scale as I love my FitBit tracker, despite its shortcomings. Great idea, very disappointing execution and customer support. Perhaps the next generation scale will be better.

Here is my actual email exchange with Support (weights deleted to protect the not-so-innocent).

FitBit Support / Maria:

"After reviewing your account, it appears that your measurements fall within our expected accuracy range, which is plus or minus 2 pounds.

The Aria provides a unique measure at each weigh in. Moving while on the scale or standing differently (even slightly) can affect your reading.

We understand if what we consider an acceptable accuracy range does not meet your expectations. If you wish to return the scale, you can view our return policy by going to [...]. If your scale was purchased from a retailer, please see them for a refund.

We're apologize for the inconvenience. Thank you for your time and understanding.

Sincerely,
Maria S and the Fitbit Team"

Me:

You cannot be serious. I actually received a "You've lost 5 lbs!" notification from FitBit! In the space of an hour my weight ranged from xxx lbs to xxx lbs--a 5.6 lb variation. I did not change clothing, or eat or drink anything. The scale is on a hard floor and was not moved.

If you look at my account it clearly shows that between 8.24 AM and 8:51 AM I weighed myself 10 times--you had told me to "take five measurements one after the other to calibrate". I lost count, went to check my cellphone and found that I'd only weighed 4 times. So I tried again, and overshot.

The weights range from xxx lbs to xxx lbs during that time, a difference of 4.8 lbs. Then I decided to try again to see if it had re-calibrated. Between 9:20 AM and 9:22 AM I weighed myself 3 times and my weight ranged from xxx lbs to xxx lbs--a difference of 2.3 lbs right there.

Please look at my account instead of delivering a canned response.

Obviously I realize that I can return the Aria if it's completely useless, but I would have thought you would want an opportunity to make things right since the scale is apparently defective.

Please escalate this issue."

FirBit Support:

"Hello Maria, (That's the other customer support person, not me...oops)

We apologize for the frustration and disappointment you are having with your Aria.

The Aria was designed to be as accurate as possible. Something to keep in mind is that the Aria is extremely sensitive to input. A simple shift in stance while on the scale could trigger a fluctuation in weights and body fat measurements.

Your weight of xxx from the morning of April 2nd can best be explained by a possible shift in weight from one side to another (i.e. more weight from your left side now on your right side) or leaning forward/backward slightly unintentionally.

Looking at your measurements from today, the weights are within our accepted range of accuracy, which is plus or minus two pounds. Your body fat measurements are very close to each other as well, so we believe that your Aria scale is functioning properly.

If you deem that this is still unacceptable, we advise you to return your Aria to the retailer that you originally purchased it from.

We appreciate your patience while we better understand your experience with the Aria. Please feel free to contact us if we can assist you further.

Sincerely,
Ricky L and the Fitbit Team

Me:

"Dear Ricky,

Again--are you serious? The high weight this morning was xxx; the low weight was xxx. That's 2.9 lb, not 'within 2 lb.'

If the engineering dept. has the same math skills as customer support personnel, I'm not surprised I'm having this problem. I'm sorry to be rude but I've never seen such oblivious responses.

Yes, this is completely unacceptable and I will indeed return the scale and review it appropriately. What's the point of having it? My Healthometer digital scale never varies by more than .2 lb and weighs closer to my doctor's scales by about 6 lb. I can accept a consistently low weight, despite the shock when I see the real weight, but not a wildly fluctuating one.

This might work for people who are already at a good weight and just want to check in. However, people who are trying to lose weight--I would guess the majority of your customers--want to see that they're consistently going in the right direction, not wonder what the heck their true weight is.

(not Maria)

title: Wonderful and Amazing Gizmo!
text:
I am very happy with this straightener. I myself have long, very curly hair, it is about 6 inches below my bra strap. I don't often attempt at straightening my hair because of the amount of time involved and because of the often awkward positioning I have to use to accurately get the job done. It usually takes a good 45 minutes using a flat iron. Using this brush took only about 15 minutes and that was with a first time user.
The brush came with very easy to understand, comprehensive instructions. It explained what all the buttons and such were, the different setting styles and how to achieve the best result. I was very glad that is explained things so well. It recommended pitting product in your hair before use and drying thoroughly beforehand. I did not do this for my first test run and still came out with an amazing result. I have since, in later applications used product in my hair beforehand as recommended and the result was even better.
I was worried about burning either my scalp or my hair (having done both before using a flat iron) , but the teeth on the brush keep it a safe distance from my scalp and neck. I also found that the manner in which the hair is gathered at your starting point keep you from getting that "flat ridge starting point" that looks horrible. It was a smooth from start to finish. It sits in such a manner on the counter that it is not going to burn anything also. It also has a thermostat that is very accurate for different types of hair.
I am VERY pleased with this product. I highly recommend it, for both "first time" flatteners or "seasoned" flatteners. I did receive this product at a discount for my unbiased opinion. I will however be purchasing several more as gifts.

title: Yes It Helps - With Patience & Better Diet
text:
I had stopped taking this fish oil to my detriment, last year. My triglycerides went up and up. Finally I realized I needed to get back on fish oil and stay on it. So back onto Carlson Fish Oil I went starting Jan 2018. I take 1 tbsp per day (that's 3 teaspoons). That's the dose my body needs. Some may do well with 1 or 2 teaspoons, but if you have high triglycerides, start with 1 tablespoon/day.

Plus, and here's the reality: you *have to* modify your diet. Cut way back on butter, cream and reduce consumption of red meat to no more than one serving per week. Fish oil really helps, but it doesn't do enough without you doing some diet improvement.

Now, I just need to be consistent about 30 min or more of exercise at least 4 days a week.

My triglycerides went from nearly 250 down to about 140. Change doesn't happen immediately. For me it took several months, but taking fish oil *every day* is key, along with better diet.

As for the taste, I have no problem with this fish oil. The lemon flavor is quite subtle and I wouldn't mind if it were a bit more bold. I don't have any issues with burping or whatever. I take my fish oil one time -- in the morning. Easy Peasy.

title: Yes, It Really Does Work
text:
I'm going to give a huge tip to using the BedFan. Some of you won't want to hear this, but it makes all the difference. You MUST get some high thread count sheets, at least 400 tc and higher if you can afford it. I have a set of 400tc and then I purchased a set of 800tc sheets at Overstock.com and oh yes, the BedFan is divine. You need the tight weave of a higher thread count to help keep the air flowing. Also, make sure you get 100% cotton sheets. No poly!

Then, I position my BedFan slightly higher than what the company recommends. They suggest 2 inches. I do 3 - 3.5 inches. I'm using a temperpedic 2" topper and that thing is warm. The extra inch or so makes a difference in my bed.

Also, you must make sure to tuck the sheet under and around the BedFan very securely and also tuck it in on the sides of your bed, at least half way up. You should not have to run the BedFan on super high. If you do, that's a clue that the air is escaping out either at the bottom or on the sides, so double check the height of the fan, and check to make sure your top sheet is tucked in snugly at the bottom.

This is my 3rd summer with the BedFan and I could not sleep as comfortably without it. I don't have to run my AC as cold and having air flow between the sheet feels wonderful.

title: Meet my orthodontic needs, great value!
text:
I started my orthodontic treatment and spent hours every day to clean my teeth thoroughly with manual flossing. It's a nightmare - not only because of the time invested, but also the cold sores and damages resulting from the lengthy cleaning work. Then the water floss came to my attention. It's not until I first tried it did I realize it would save my life! Within just as short as a couple of minutes, I could achieve the cleanness goal.

Now, let's talk about how it works. When you first try this, do not look at the mirror (or keep your mouth closed). Otherwise, it's gonna spray everywhere. However, after a couple of tries, I managed it very well. I also like to add Listerine mouthwash to water to get hygiene.

Water tank is not big so that it's easy to run out of water. However, it's fairly straightforward to refill and not bothers me.

It has five modes which represents different pulse and strength. When my teeth are sensitive, I will use the sensitive mode. Bushfire works very well if I have a big meal.

I have not used it for travel. Based on the current battery states, it looks it will works fine with at least two days without charge.

Overall, the water floss saved my life with braces and makes the teeth cleaning super easy to manage now.

title: Did not work
text:
It's tough for me to write a review of the performance of the scale - because it did not work.

Setup was not as simple as it could have been...as some people state, there is a weird step where you have to connect the scale to your phone via a scale-based WIFI network - instead of just connecting the scale to your WiFi network directly (like the Nest Thermostat).

It failed on the first go around and I had to start from scratch.

Not the worst experience - but not as simple as it could be.

The problem is the scale didn't work.

I would try to use it once set up and connected to my FitBit account.
The Scale would give me an indication that it was sensing; tell me to get off; Then it would tell me it was "thinking" and then I would get "ERR".

This happened every time.

I contacted FitBit - via email - as no phone # was available on their site.

Their advice (24 hours later) was to not move the scale (I didn't) and to pull and reinsert the batteries. (Which I had done).

So - while this was probably just a defective unit, it was a poor experience with the scale and with customer service - so I returned it and did not order a replacement.

I have used both the FitBit Ultra and (continue to use) the Fitbit Flex with absolutely no issues and would recommend either.

title: It curls well, but...
text: The plates on this hair straightening device snags my medium-fine to fine naturally curly hair.  "3D Floating Plate for Smooth Hair: 3D floating ceramic coating heating plate is infused with nano silver, argan oil, tourmaline, and titanium."  Cannot entirely verify if seller's claim quoted here is true or not.  All I can offer is I've been using hair irons since the 90's and they've come a long way since.  This one straightens, snags hair, and does not smooth.  My curly fine hair is in very good condition and can be easily smoothed/straightened with other hair irons, like my reliable one I use sometimes to switch up hair style.  My usual hair dryer and hair iron (not this one reviewed here) have ions, ceramic,  and tourmaline to smooth hair, moisturize, even when I diffuse for curly days.  I can see how THIS specific hair iron straightens, and would do better at a higher temperature setting, but I am not willing to increase heat to do that and damage my hair.  It straightens, but does not smooth, nor moisturize.  The metal trim on this is rose gold BUT it is more yellow or orange than pink in the rose gold tone definition.  The cord on this is plentiful, the plug is good, the buttons to adjust heat setting are easy(but read the enclosed instructions).  Sadly, the metal heat plates on this flat iron do not glide effortlessly like we all know flat irons can and ought to.  And while it heats up quickly to use, it takes longer & a higher heat setting to straighten and smooth hair.  Really wanted this to not snag my hair and glide without resistance, but it did not.  I received this device in exchange for an honest review.  Like you, I have been burned with fake reviews and fake products that don't live up to basic expectations.  I give honest reviews.  This flat iron may work for your hair.  It did not work well enough for me.  I don't have time for hair breakage/damage.  The price is good though for what it is.  Did not want to be rude and give this device a 3 star, so I gave it 4 star.

text:

I tried this in an Emperor 1510 workstation, a Restoration hardware deep seat leather couch, and in a 2017 Toyota Tundra TRD Pro. It felt awkward in every seat.

In the Emperor 1510 workstation: I was raised up by a solid 2", making monitor placement and viewing angles uncomfortable.

In the truck: I felt like I was sitting on top of a phone book, my legs barely had any room under the steering wheel.

On the couch: It felt like I was sitting on top of a pool toy and it looked silly on a couch anyways.

It comes with a cushion cover. It is what you think it is. A cheap cover with a zipper. It has microdots on the bottom side of the cover. It does not perform an effective job at holding the cushion in place. It slides all over the place making it a danger in the vehicle, annoying in a computer chair, and overall ineffective at doing anything other than keeping the purple rubber cushion clean.

I'm going to try the smaller Purple chair cushion and see how it goes. I'll write a review when I do.

title: Remembering the many TV specials of Bob Hope, America's Goodwill Ambassador...
text:
“Thanks for the Memories: The Bob Hope Specials Deluxe Collection” is a DVD box set containing 39 TV specials on 19 discs, including 20 shows not seen since their original broadcast. The Bob Hope specials spanned five decades with Bob providing comedy, music, dancing and big-name guest stars. The shows are culled from over 250 network specials, several in support of the U.S. Armed Forces.

Bob Hope’s career in show business covered stage, radio, motion pictures and television. He made a series of popular “Road” pictures with Bing Crosby between 1940 and 1962, appeared regularly on radio beginning in 1934, was one of the first radio performers to embrace the new medium of television in 1950, and performed extensively for the troops at American army bases and those serving overseas.

This set features guest stars John Wayne, Bing Crosby, Raquel Welch, Desi Arnaz, Jack Benny, Don Rickles, Barbra Streisand, George Burns, Dean Martin, Ann-Margret, Lucille Ball, Steve McQueen, Lola Falana, Tom Jones, Carol Burnett, Angie Dickinson, Andy Williams, Lana Turner, Jayne Mansfield, Redd Foxx, Zsa Zsa Gabor, and many others.

Though there are other DVD releases featuring Bob Hope specials, this is the most complete collection available. A highlight of the shows is Bob’s memorable monologues, which often riffed on contemporary news and personalities, but never were overly political. Noel Coward once wrote in a song lyric about “a talent to amuse.” The phrase can aptly apply to Bob Hope.

title: Comparison with greenies hip and joint/ yucca makes me nervous/ serving size
text:
[[VIDEOID:fb3ad9c0a4b5eda2a6a106bf92b18160]] As I compare this with greenie hip and joint, I see that this contains 500 mg of Glucosamine (same as greenies), 400 mg of MSM (none in greenies) and 50 mg of Chondroitin Sulfate Porcine source (greenies has 400mg from chicken source).

I read up on Chondroitin and it’s widely used to help with osteoarthritis which happens when joints degenerate. It’s found in animal tissues rich in cartilage. I like that this is sourced from a pig (porcine) b/c many dogs have allergies to chicken (which is the source used in greenies). This has a lot less Chondroitin, but it’s also priced much more reasonable.

This is also loaded with fish oil, flaxseed, calcium (50 mg) and yucca schidigera (60 mg- controversial, but it seems like the extract helps to clear them out (and makes poops less stinky) so they can absorb more nutrients. I’m not seeing any of these ingredients in greenies.

If you have two medium/large dogs the bag will go fast. I have to give my big dog (60 pounds) 3 chews a day and a my medium dog (35 pounds) 2 chews a day. There are 60 chews in a bag. This means that the bag will only last me 12 days. The directions say to double the daily amount for the first week. I didn’t double the amount b/c it would have gone way too fast if I did. Plus, I wanted to see how my dogs respond to this first. I would have liked if this came in a larger bag of like 90 chews.

I like that this is made in the USA. The packaging is fun and “cool”. The chews however do have a strong, fishy smell. My medium sized dog likes the flavor, but my lab hesitated before trying it out .

Overall, I like the price and quality, I’m just nervous about the yucca and I think I would need to go through the bag way too quickly since I have two dogs.

text: This stay awake supplement is like No-Doze for the new millennium. Instead of just giving you a boost of caffeine (which you could get from drinking a cup of coffee), this product also adds some B vitamins to help prevent loss of the water soluble vitamins from the caffeine (caffeine can dehydrate you). Since there is such a large percentage of Vitamin B-12 in this product, I am not sure I would use it every day. I, personally, do not believe it is healthy to regularly take mega doses of vitamins (whether or not they are water soluble). The best recommendation I can give is that you should consult the medical practitioner of your choice before adding this supplement or any other to your daily regimen. I do like that this product uses Guarana seed extract, as I have used supplements with that ingredient in the past and I found that it will give you some pep and energy without the big crash, afterwards. title: Impressed with shave
text:
First off, I'm not an electric razor expert. I've always used the traditional razor blades since I'm not someone that grows facial hair very fast only shaving every 2 or 3 days. The only experience I've had with an electric razor was 15 years ago which was an entry level Norelco. I never felt like it gave me a very close shave and ended up using my razor blade anyway. I recently decided it may be time to try it again just to get those quick shaves without having to lather the face and rinse.

Kensen Electric Shaver was a nice surprise! This electric razor actually gives me a decent shave. I like the little battery meter that lets me know how much charge is left in the battery. The floating heads don't feel like it's ripping the hairs out of my face like my initial experience many years ago. I don't know how long these blades will last but it's nice that Kensen includes an extra head. The smaller form factor of the Kensen fits nicely in my hand with a nice matte feel to the body of the razor.

Overall the product seems of decent quality and will be something I use on a daily basis for the simplicity of shaving. Time will tell how long it lasts.

I've always worked out, since I was about 16 years old (25 now) and tried pretty much everything in terms of pre and post-workout sups (no steroids or anything inyected, only powders and pills). I've found that the perfect three products are ON's Creatine and Whey Protein, and Muscle Fuel's post workout. I take the creatine dissolved in my morning green tea, take the whey in the afternoon (usually 3 hors after lunch) get off work and hit the gym at around 6-7ish. After a hard workout, take the Muscle-Fuel sups and they have been doing great.

I used to use Jack3d but that only made me sweaty. Hydroxy-cut only made my heart beat faster and nauseous (got rid of that right away) but Muscle-Fuel's been doing great for me so far. Muscle swore is much MUCH less common and seem to be recovering faster (translating to working hard the next week, too, and pushing myself harder).

Anyways, buy this for your post workout. Totally worth it.

I found out " This marine oil, which is produced from shrimplike krill harvested from Antarctic waters, not only contains significant amounts of the omega-3 fatty acids EPA and DHA, but also phospholipids (which are integral to the building of cell membranes) and potent antioxidants, including astaxanthin, a carotenoid from the nutrient family that includes beta-carotene, lutein, and lycopene."

I got this gem because of the amount of krill oil and it's a lovely 30 day supply. Lots of bang for your buck!! Let me also add there isn't that nasty fish burp I would get while taking fish oil. Nothing worse than that I say!
