I definitely enjoy using this thing, I have watched my acne improve over the last month of using it. I have sensitive skin so I don't use it every day. Although as someone who has worked in the skincare business, unless your skin gets very very dirty everyday due to workspace or environment air pollution, I don't believe the skin needs to be scrubbed this deeply 2x/day every single day. The skin needs a chance to heal & grow new skin before doing a deep scrub. And your body's natural oils are important for balance. So a couple times a week is enough. But definitely still wash & moisturize your skin every day!
Also, it is great having a variety of bristles softness & lengths, so I can tend to what my skin needs. I haven't tried the foot scrubber yet but I'm excited to!
I saw a couple reviews showing pieces falling apart out of the box & poor quality. I definitely do not have that problem & do not notice it being cheaply made. I think there are bad eggs that occur just like with every other product out there & accidents happen. If your product is defective, I'd say try getting a replacement & try again.
The only thing I will warn you about, my box came crushed so I made sure to look everything over carefully & made sure the actual unit still worked. So if your box also arrives in bad condition, take pictures of both the shipping box it came in (if damaged) & the product box before opening it so you have evidence, then inspect everything and request a return/replacement if necessary. title: excellent pump, excellent customer service
text:
I actually began using this pump before my son was born because my membranes ruptured prematurely and in a last ditch effort to avoid medical induction I tried nipple stimulation using this pump to get my labor going. The design with the petals is supposed to be a close mimick to a baby suckling so it seemed like a good idea. My labor started within 4 hours! It may be a coincidence but it lasted less than 4 hours start to finish as well (and this was my first baby). Of course, always talk to your doctor before trying any induction method (I did), I am not a health professional.
I have used this pump exclusively since my son was born and he is seven months old now. I am a stay-at-home mom that pumps only for an occasional feeding, to stock the freezer for daytrips away from baby, and for milk for baby cereal (we have food allergy problems). So, I use it at least once a day, everyday, but not for large quantities of milk. I love the pump. I have always found it comfortable to use, it is small and travels well, and has suited my every need as a breastfeeding mother thus far.
Last month I managed to crack one of the plastic pieces because I was spacey and turned the pieces the wrong way when I dissembled to pump for cleaning. I called Isis Customer Service and they mailed a replacement part for free. I did not have to have my original receipt or tell them a date of purchase or anything. I was not expecting it to be so easy and was extremely grateful. I missed my pump immensely in the only 2 days it was out of service.
The only thing that worries me a bit about this disposable pump, is that I'm not sure Avent's bags are up to snuff for freezing milk. You definitely need to double bag if you are going to freeze your milk in the bags. I have had some single bags break before I realized this and the instructions with the pump actually specifically say that the plastic is not freezer grade and should be double bagged (boy did I feel stupid). From what I understand the Medela bags are much better for freezing (i do not know this from personal experience, but from word of mouth), but are not a good fit to use with this pump. I'm sure an organization like La Leche League could answer that question for sure.

title: Don't Last and Leave Residue; Won't Buy Again
text: I've used these for about 11 months and the most any have stayed on the glasses is about 2 weeks (and that was rare).  The silicone is about the right thickness and seems it would last indefinitely, but the pads stick on with double-sided adhesive tape.  The side to the glasses adheres well, but the adhesive quickly gives way on the pad side; then the pads go into the eyes or elsewhere on the face, without warning.  (This happens quicker the more frequently you clean the glasses.)  So you end up throwing away a perfectly good silicone pad because it no longer sticks.  And when you remove the sticky tape left on the glasses, it leaves residue that gets on the eyeglass lenses and is hard to remove because it gets on the cleaning cloth and smears.  Thankfully, 32 pairs is enough to last about a year, but they are messy and inconvenient to change so frequently.

There are two sides on mine, a light pink and a dark pink; the light pink side has shorter, thicker silicone bristles and the dark pink side has longer bristles that taper at the end. However, the bristles do work best against bare skin, so we will be back to using our hospital surgical brush in the winter when long sleeves and pants return as this brush is too soft to provide the needed input through a layer of clothing. title: Effectiveness justifies the price!
text: Over the past 10 years I have used various products for arthritis in my hands and knees. I have tried Voltaren prescription gel, emu oil, tiger balm, icy hot, capsaicin gel, etc. The only one that reduced my pain was the capsaicin cream. The problem with the capsaicin cream is that, if you cover over it with clothing, it burns your skin off. And it rubs off on anything you touch, and eventually gets into your (Or someone else's) eyes. I really did not expect Cool Azul to work, other than to make my skin feel cool. Was I ever surprised! I could tell within 20 minutes that 50% of my pain was gone, And within another 15 minutes my pain was reduced even more. I have also noticed that if I use it two or three times a day, I can even skip one day and not use it, and my pain remains alleviated until the following day. I make sure to not wash my hands for about 45 minutes after using to give the cream plenty of time to start working. It's not sticky or messy at all, and goes a long way away. It's a little pricey, but its effectiveness justifies its price!

title: Bye Bye Video Sickness
text:
I'm a huge gamer and always have been, but even though I do not suffer from motion sickness while traveling, I have never been able to play any games that are viewed from the first person vantage point. Any game that I played and could not see my entire character, I would develop a massive headache accompanied by severe nausea after 5-10 minutes of play time. I was able to research and find that I suffer from what is called video sickness. It is triggered by the same thing that causes motion sickness.

My daughter saw these glasses on Tik Tok and recommended them to me. I was hesitate to order them because they looked so goofy, but thought "oh well what the heck" and placed the order. Boy am I glad I did. I reinstalled a first person game today and played it for over an hour with video sickness. I felt completely normal when I stopped and took the glasses off. What makes it even better is they fit just fine over my reading/computer glasses so I don't have to try and play blind.

Highly recommend and would give more than 5 stars if I could! Awesome product especially for the price!

title: Just ok
text:
I am pregnant with twins and I have had back, hip, and pelvic pain since about 19 weeks of pregnancy. A support belt was recommended by various medical professionals and based on the other reviews, I had high hopes for this one. However, I have found it to be only somewhat helpful. I do appreciate that it provides some support for the weight of my belly while I'm walking around at home. However, it hasn't resulted in a noticeable reduction in pain or discomfort and definitely was not worth the price. This may be because I can't wear it all the time, for the following reasons:

First, I'm not sure why there are only three levels of adjustment. There are nearly four inches of space between each set of clasps and as a result, the belt is sometimes too tight or too loose while the size of my constantly growing belly is between clasps. It seems the company could have easily added five sets of clasps rather than three so that the belt would better adjust to the belly as it grows.

Second, even when the belt properly fits the size of my belly, I find it to be too tight when I sit down. It pulls on the base of my belly and is very uncomfortable. For that reason, I have to undo it every time I sit down and put it back in place when I stand up. This means that I can't wear it to work because I don't have a private office and I don't want my coworkers to watch me adjust this belt underneath my clothing at my cubicle every time I sit down or stand up.

Third, the belt is very apparent under even thick clothing. It shows under sweaters, so don't even think about wearing it under just a t-shirt. I agree with the many other reviewers who say that the straps by the neck show with all but the highest collars, but I didn't think that would be too much of a problem because I thought I could pin those straps aside a bit. However, even when that problem is resolved, the rest of the belt is very bulky under my clothes and looks very strange. I need to look professional at work and can't have weird bumps showing up all over the place under my clothing. title: Solid Energy, But Disappointing Flavor and Big Crash
text:
Although I typically subscribe to a "preworkouts are about performance, not flavor" mindset, I couldn't help myself in this case. The idea of a "Smarties" flavored preworkout just felt so awesomely fun and nostalgic. And since the formula looked decent (though neither as stim-heavy as some of the leading preworkouts nor as competitively priced since you only get 20 servings), I figured I'd give it a shot.

The flavor is unfortunately a big disappointment. It's simply pleasant and non-descript, which is frankly OK by preworkout standards, but a problem when you're expecting it to taste like a specific candy of which you have fond memories. Knowing that it's meant to taste like Smarties, I can MAYBE see what they're going for. But if I gave you this preworkout as part of a blind taste test, you would never in a million years guess the flavor.

Flavor commentary aside, it is solid as a preworkout. It's not legendary on the energy front, but the boost is on par with (if not better than) other products built around a 300mg caffeine blend. It also hits quickly.

That said, I've also been noticing a far harder "crash" than is typical of preworkouts in 2020. It's great if you workout at night since you can get a full-caliber energy boost without having trouble falling asleep, but it's a problem if you workout in the morning and need to be functional later in the day. Every time I've taken it early in the day, I've either had to take a nap that afternoon - or take another heavy dose of a preworkout/energy drink. Not ideal.

I have seen Dr. Pinkus being interviewed on TV several times. I have been interested in alternative therapies and how anyone can help themselves improve their health or the way they feel.

title: Mine looks tampered with.
text:
First I will start with saying that I did not taste it, due to it looking like it was tampered with.

Upon twisting the lid off, I noticed a line of nearly evenly spaced puncture holes running down the center of the seal that in most products is meant to show if the product was tampered with, or not. Usually when I order from Amazon, these seals look like they were not placed well onto the product, or a little damaged from the manufacturing process, and I don't like to, but would normally still consume the product anyway due to it being more often than not that I receive supplements with that seal in questionable condition. I am not doing that this time. This looks too suspicious for me.

As you can see in these photos, the seal was intentionally punctured by either a person, or the manufacturing process itself. I find it strange that the manufacturing process would be designed to intentionally puncture holes into the tamper seal.

I took a picture of the underside of the lid, to show that some of the protein dust did exit the tiny holes, which happened sometime before I took the lid off of it. There was no barrier between the food, and anyone who may have handled it, other than the twist-off lid. A person could have punctured the seal with a syringe filled with something that I am sure I would not want to ingest, for all I know, which I do not know. That's why the "seal" should be a seal.

I took a picture of the protein powder, because if you look closely, you can see brown specs. Those specs look a bit larger in real life, but I lack the HD camera to show them in full detail.I Those are globs that form when the protein powder comes into contact with liquid droplets. Liquid, of some type, clearly dropped through those punctures holes.

I was really looking forward to having a protein shake after doing some pushups earlier. This was the cheapest protein that I could find, and while I was not expecting to enjoy the taste, I was not expecting to receive something that I would suspect might be poisoned, which it might not be. I'm just having a hard time understanding why there are puntures in the seal, and why there are globs that formed with the protein powder, and liquid droplets. I'm not tasting it.

I'm sorry if these people who sell through Amazon send the containers to them without punctures in the seal. If they do, then they need to have a serious talk with Amazon about someone working at a warehouse tampering with food products. I do not like giving bad reviews, especially when I am the first to review a product. But I do not know what I am looking at here. If it is poison, then it might explain why I'm the first to review this, since I'm not even going to taste the stuff.

title: Not Very Accurate and Scale Must Be Reset After Any Movement!
text:
PROS:
-Sometimes it's nice and it'll tell you that you weigh a lot less than you actually do

CONS:
-The next day it'll say you weigh much more than you do.. :(
-Won't really ever tell you how much you actually weigh

Unfortunately the scale has seen better days. Like it's first one. The first day it worked, probably because I was so happy I finally had a scale so I didn't care if it was accurate. But as I tried using it for actual measurements, it failed both my boyfriend and I. One day it would say we had lost 5-7 lbs (yay!) and the next we had gained 20 (darn). So at the bottom (like most all other scales like these) there is a dial where you can reset the scale to zero when you're not standing on it.

Here lies the issue: step on it, *some number appears*, step off, the dial is no longer at zero. Reset scale with the dial, step on again, *some DIFFERENT number appears*, step off, dial is no longer at zero again.

This happens even if you bump the scale slightly after you set it to zero. This leaves it almost impossible to get a measurement that you can use for any purposeful reasons since one day you'll feel great for having lost false weight and another have a bad day cause you think your progress has gone backwards! I have actually kept the scale (hence 2 stars) because I trust it to tell me whether I'm at 150 or 100 but do not trust it to tell me whether I'm 120 or 110. My boyfriend keeps urging me to throw it out completely and when I do find a better scale it won't be hard to trash!

Initial Review:
Gradient intensity & 24 modes are comparable to many settings achieved using analog TENS/EMS. Not having to buy batteries & 4 individually controlled leads if desired are definitely an upgrade.

Despite the fact pads had not been moved, controls are locked & I was already enjoying simulation. The pads are easy to wash & frankly must be after/before each use. There is a small amount of residue from adhesion left on skin but easily removed. Failure to wash pads before/after each use will result in skin irritation, rash or worse. Blot pads dry to remove excess water. Clean area of clean skin with alcohol, peroxide etc not just soap & water before placing electrode.

title: The lamp failed after 7 months
text:
I bought this lamp on August 1, 2014, and it failed in early March 2015. So it was just over 7 months old at failure.

The light was fine when I turned it off for the last time, then the next time I turned it on it only had a very low-level pinkish glow. The glow didn't last long ... then it went to no light at all. Thinking it was the bulb (although it was nowhere near its expected lifetime), I ordered another one. When I installed it, it didn't work. So I thought it might be a defective bulb and ordered another one; it didn't work either.

I then contacted Verilux since it was still under warranty. They replied the next day and said it was probably the ballast, and I could send the lamp to them for repair, but I needed to enclose a check for $14.95 for return shipping. The ballast is not user-replaceable (presumably because the part is not available to the public). So the total would cost me about $30 just in shipping, and it would likely take several weeks to get it back. I didn't think the lamp was worth it, so I opted not to return it and will just trash the lamp. The Verilux warranty is essentially worthless.

Based on my experience, I do not recommend this lamp. If zero stars was an option, that's the rating I would give it.

title: Good for Sleeping Baby
text:
Our circa 1923 house has terrible squeaky wood floors, and all of our kids walk like elephants, so it is really tricky to keep a baby asleep. After reading reviews on several sleep-machine products, we decided the SleepMate 580A sounded like our best bet. We have been using it for about 3 weeks now, and we are very satisfied. It sounds a lot like a vaporizer running. I honestly expect to feel a cool mist when I walk past it. In our opinion, it is too loud to have right in our 12x12 bedroom, but the amount of noise it makes sitting right outside the door is perfect. You can still hear all of the other noises in the house (I still know when our teenage son gets home at night.), but the constant humming keeps other noises from being such a jolt to your system and waking you up. I really do think the baby is sleeping better. I would recommend this for anyone trying to sleep through noisy situations.

title: The best for cleaning, disinfection, etc, especially for allergies!
text:
The only contact lens solution I will use. I wear gas permeable (hard) lenses, and this means that they have to be cleaned and reused for up to a year or more. All the gunk needs to be cleaned and disinfected every night, and this is the most hygenic system of doing so-peroxide is what has been used to clean cuts for years, because it kills bacteria and viruses on contact. This does the same thing.

If people leave negative reviews of this product, THEY ARE USING IT WRONG. The product has explicit instructions, and every eye doctor will give you an explanation of how to use it. The red top and multiple warnings on the bottle say DO NOT PUT DIRECTLY IN EYES. This means dump the solution in the case, put the contacts in, and let them sit overnight. 6 hours later (no less), the solution is neutralized by the metal disc at the bottom and the solution will no longer burn. Where most people screw up is that they take the bottle with the red top and rinse the lens. NOOOOO. Use regular saline if you insist on doing this.

This is the best solution to get all the gunk off your lenses. Nobody is free of gunk-we all have it. Lenses will come out of this stuff squeaky clean, and since the solution requires you to use the neutralizing case, it will come with a new case every time you buy new bottles of solution. This is good because it reminds you to toss the old ones which get gross (and in the case of this, the metal disc gets old and loses its neutralizing power). I highly recommend this stuff as an eye doctor-nothing better works, especially if you have eye allergies, sensitivities, etc.

I'm not sure if this falls into the exact "official" plan rules, but I'm not too fussed about my sodium intake, I know any weight i gain from that is just temporary water weight.

title: Taking a while once started, but working!
text:
This is the first peeling foot product I've tried. I soaked my feet then used this for 1.5 hours and it mildly irritated the top of my feet while they were in the solution (they felt like they were burning, and were covered in small red, raised bumps, the burning stopped once I rinsed my feet off.) Some oral benadryl and a steroid cream applied before bed cleared up that reaction. I soaked my feet 2x per day for 3 days, and after almost no changes by the end of day 3 save for some dryness I was feeling disappointed and ordered the official babyfoot. Midday on day 4 I started developing small patches of peeling, and after a long, hot shower that night my feet were peeling! I'm on day 11 right now. Since day 4 I have been soaking my feet once a day (usually too busy to manage twice) and soaking definitely makes a difference.

Right now (day 11) the top of my feet are peeling, and the bottom are half done and half cracked and dry but not yet peeled skin. It's mostly peeling in small areas/spots and not large chunks. I am a compulsive skin picker so this could be that the skin detaches easier when it's attached to other detaching skin and picking it screwed up that process, or could be because I haven't soaked mine enough. I did rub my feet after soaking with a towel, and maybe that messed up the mass peeling instead of small bits as well. I'm definitely glad I ordered this product, and am excited to try the original babyfoot in 4-6 weeks to compare results (and knowing that they well come, hopefully I'll be able to resist picking my feet since I'll know they won't need helping along).

title: Great benefits for your skin!
text:
I have combination, acne-prone, and hyperpigmented skin. In an effort to help my skin tone even out, I have started adding Hyaluronic Acid and Vitamin C Serums to my everyday skincare routine. Twice a day, right after cleansing my face, I add a few drops of each into the palm of my hand. I then pat the serums onto my skin, focusing on darker areas under my eyes and where old pimples have come and gone.
Vitamin C Serum is a great product to add to your everyday routine. Vitamin C is a potent antioxidant that shields the skin from damaging free radicals that promote premature aging. Think sun damage, pollution, and oxygen! Vitamin C can reduce the appearance of dark spots, boosts collagen production, reduces inflammation/irritation, fade post-breakout red marks by improving the skin’s healing response, and boosts your skin’s defense against UV exposure.
My main expectation in using this product is to even out my hyperpigmentation or discoloration of the skin. Vitamin C does act as a natural bleaching agent to lighten the skin and even out your skin tone, and I look forward to seeing the results!
I did receive this product at a discount in exchange for an honest review, and I definitely encourage you to take a look at these benefits!.

I suppose it is meant for the bead to be pushed back into the hose to prevent air from escaping out of the bladder.  But I have found that just turning the metal knob on the pump valve to closed is all that is needed to prevent air escape.... just leave the little bead in that hose bubble or get it into that spot if not already there when purchased or you won't be able to pump it up.

title: Slow down the signs of aging by nourishing skin tissues
text:
I am not new to the use of essential and carrier oils, but using sea buckthorn oil was a new experience for me even though I had read about its use in nourishing the tissues in your skin and body and that it had a long history in regional folk medicines dating back thousands of years.

While I already have self made oil and lotion blends that I use for facial and body skin that I am very happy with, I am always open to learning new things and improving on what's there. So I was really curious and attracted to sea buckthorn due to its healing and rejuvenating effects on the skin and wanted to give it a try. I saw this product on Amazon and since US Organic Group wasn't a supplier that I was familiar with I had to research first before I was willing to purchase something that I was planning to use on my skin. I realize that reviews are not meant to be about manufacturer, but the manufacturer plays a key role for me in something like essential oils. One thing that swayed me in giving this manufacturer a try is not only because the product certified organic, but also that their products are 100% cruelty free. If you do a little further searching you will find that this company seems to have wellness in their DNA with affiliations to some other interesting organizations.

The oil itself has what I would call a deep amber or red orange color and viscous. It has a bit of a musky scent to it, although you can't really smell unless you hold it up directly to your nose. It can stain your skin, especially if you fail to dilute sufficiently. However, this is temporary and washes off easily.

It's a great exfoliator, skin cleanser and good for healing the skin. There have actually been studies done which show that daily use helps slow down the signs of aging by nourishing skin tissues. What's there not to love about that!

My facial skin is extremely sensitive and I have gotten to the point that I will know almost immediately if my skin likes what I am putting on it or not. I know some people may think that I am a little nuts, but it's true in my case. The reason I bring this up, is that when I used this product in my blend and apply it to my face, I can feel my skin reacting positively.

This is a very concentrated oil, and I recommend that you use sparingly. Also make sure that you dilute with a good carrier oil. There are a number of other essential oils that are good for your skin which you can add in your blend such as carrot seed, rose hip, lavender, frankincense, geranium and others. I can't tell you what blend works best in your particular case as everyone is unique. There are a lot of good articles that will help you get started. Whatever blend/s you come up with, I do recommend you include sea buckthorn given its ability to promote skin hydration, regeneration and elasticity, and even helps treat acne.

title: Nice concept for stinky dog breath
text:
I have four dogs, and toys in this house do NOT last long. I am always purchasing toys for them to just play with until I came across this. I have never purchased a toy that doubled as a toothbrush. I have a toothbrush for my dogs and they despise getting their teeth cleaned so this was a really good solution.
Quality:
This worked for my American Bullies, they have some serious jaw strength and at most the toy lasts like a day. This lasted well past that and it stayed intact. The rubber is very firm which allows them to bite hard on it to clean their teeth while the rubber is flexible enough that they don’t completely destroy it.
Uses:
Yes, my dogs actually used this. I have chicken flavored toothpaste that I put inside and they chomped away and it worked very well.
Things to note:
I would suggest using this in an area where there is no carpet or rugs if you put toothpaste or anything liquid in it. They are messy and it will get on your floor.
It actually does work to help their breath, I was surprised at how well it worked, but my dogs are on a raw food diet and have sardine breath which is repulsive. Giving them this after their mealtime made them bearable to be around.
Recommendations:
Some things that would improve the product would be if the bottom part was bigger so the dogs can have something to grasp while they chew and if it came with some type of flavored toothpaste to fill the product. A syringe to help place the paste into the toy would also be very helpful to keep your hands from getting nasty.
Bonus:
I placed this is the dishwasher to clean and had no problems. It sanitized it and washed it so the dogs could keep using it.
I’m really happy I purchased this and now that I know this is a solution, I will look for more in the future!

title: Good. But you need to commit
text:
So after a week of use, here is my review of the fancy, French baby butt creme: First of all, I'm convinced no baby craps more than Gigi. Chick crapped 5 times today, so we were needing something to keep her cleaner and put the protective shield up. This product does that.
Pros: you use it as a 2 in 1, so you squeeze the lotion onto a wipe and use it to clean up the poop and wipe her down. This also leaves a film (much thinner than Desitin) that protects for the next blowout. She has had zero rashes since starting. And this is coming from someone that uses diaper creme constantly.
Cons: not convenient. You have to have disposable cotton pads to use instead of reusable wipes. The company wants you to use reusable cotton cloths/wipes and just wash them afterwards. I'm not carrying around a crap covered wipe until I get home. Sorry. So just get cotton pads.
I found the solution: besides the cotton pads, I use a baby wipe to get the initial filth off her, then use the cremed pad for the additional cleaning, still leaving the film. This works best and she's not miserable from rash.
So ultimately, this stuff is great, but u need to commit to gross if you want to use it the way they intend it to be used.

title: A tool I RELY on!
text:
WORTH EVERY PENNY!

My husband and I have been using this product for a couple years now and it has seriously changed the way I look at headaches, migraines, neck and shoulder pain. It has provided me with relief at times I thought nothing else would help.

I have used this tool through a pregnancy to help with tension headaches, sciatica and hip pain from spreading. I have taken it on a cross country road trip to help me on the journey and I was glad I made that decision. My husband, who suffers from chronic migraines, will use this to help curb oncoming headaches and help relieve the end of a migraine hangover.

The cushions are soft, but still provide firm pressure on the points you adjust them to. It is easy to adjust for different areas you need it for and can be used a lot of different ways. It is comfortable to lay on and I can spend up to ten minutes on it and still feel comfortable. **I will mention that when I first started using it, I could only lay on it for a minute or two and built myself to this point.**

I've used it for migraines and shoulder tension, I've used it for hip pain as well as neck pain. Truly, I sometimes lay on it just to help me relax; it does that much for me. I have the privilege to see Dr. Westoby monthly for chiropractic care and he is always showing me new ways to use it (just recently he showed me how to use it for sinus relief!) This man is genuine and I love his practice and what he stands for.

This honestly is a tool I will share with anyone who says they need help with tension or headaches/migraines because it has made that big of a difference for me. WORTH EVERY PENNY!

title: Mini Humidifier
text:
This is a good humidifier. It's a good size, just good enough for a small office or bedroom. I got this because the air in my room gets so dry in the winter time and there is so much static produced from the dry air. So, it does a fair job at reducing the static in my room and it's great to sleep with.

It does make minimal sounds as the water level decreases in the tank, however, it's not enough to disturb you during sleep. It gives off a cool mist, and from what I can see it doesn't get anything else wet around it. Considering I have it placed on my dresser in my room right next to my cell phone charger. Essentially, it's a good buy. Good pricing and works really well. I've had zero problems with it. My only compliant is the little orange light that lights up when it's on. It's a bit bright at night when all the lights are off. So, I recommend tapping something dark over it, it you are sensitive to lighting when you're going to bed with the humidifier on.

title: Really good product, does the job well
text:
Really good product, does the job well.
I have straight lashes and most days can't be bothered to curl my eyelashes so after watching a few youtube videos I decided to buy this perming kit. first off it came earlier than expected which was great cause I was able to use it before I had to work. It didn't come with instructions in the kit, but when i was looking at the pictures I noticed that they have the instructions there so I just took a screenshot if it, it would be a lot better if the kit itself came with the physical instruction list.

My first attempt on perming my lashes was a little bit of a fail, I tried the pink reusable perming rod and it was a mess, I had such a hard time using it and my lashes wouldn't stay on the rod so I had to use more glue than i would like and after going through the steps my final results were not impressive at all.

Here is what worked from me my second attempt.
First I ditched the reusable perming rod and used one of the disposable ones that are already sticky and stuck it as close to my lash line as possible, and using my fingers I pressed as many of my lashes on the rod as I could since its already sticky then glued the rest of my lashes up. I still had to glue all my lashes to keep them on the rod, but since majority of my lashes were already stuck to the perming rod I didn't have to use as much glue.
Then using the spatula that was in the kit I covered my lashes in the perming solution "A" and waited 12 minutes, then cleaned the solution off and applied the eyelash treatment cream "B" and waited 10 minutes then took the glue off with the eyelash cleanser "C" at this point I also took the perming rod off and applied the eyelash restore "D" with the spoolie that was in the kit and waited 6 minutes. after I just took a baby wipe and gently wipe down my lashes.

I definitely had a better perm with the self adhering rods, but it will be different for everyone, I don't have really long lashes and that might be a reason that the pink rods didn't work for me. I would definitely purchase this product again.

title: 150 hours
text:
This bag ring has been used for 150 hours to pick up litter, and it has carried out 900 pounds of litter from the streets, trails, and parks, so far.

I use 13-gallon kitchen trash bags with this bag holder. Any larger trash bag will drag on the ground and will slip out of the holder when it goes over the weight limit. This holder comfortably holds weights up to around 11ish pounds (a 13-gallon kitchen bag is meant to hold around 8 pounds of garbage) and then the bag will very slowly begin to slip out of the holder. At around 15ish pounds the bag will fully come out of the holder, but at that much weight in a 13-gallon bag the bag will be ripping and disintegrating anyways unless you double-bagged. If you use drawstring bags, you can loop the drawstring around the handle and that adds extra security. Double-bagging is also possible, which increases the structural integrity of your bags if you're anticipating extra weight.

I haven't seen any evidence of damage to the ring, even though the edge is often whacked with a metal grabber in attempts to dislodge sticky bits of litter. There are still no cracks or anything. I bought a second one just in case, but I've not needed it yet.

Highly recommended.

It's possible that this is just a side effect of being on a Keto diet, but they deserve the benefit of the doubt, as the days before I started taking them (when I was just into Ketosis) were miserable.

They are cylindrical shaped capsules, that are clear, so you can actually see the clear fluid inside them. They are fairly fragile, and are packed with cotton, which brings up the only issue I've seen so far -- when my bottle arrive, one had broken open (and was stuck to the cotton), leaving the entire contents just slightly slick.

Would I buy them again? Sure; you take four at a shot, and they seem to help with the cravings that I otherwise experience in the mornings.

title: Mildly helpful
text: Ok, let me start off by saying I am a true marijuana connoisseur. I only smoke glass bongs. I own five bongs ranging from your basic straight tube to your fancy triple deca arm tree perc. I have been using Rez block in all five for about 2 months now. Does it work? Yes, for the most part. It definitely makes it easier to clean your bongs. But the downside is that the water gets dirty about twice as fast. So it actually causes you to have to change the water more. Now I don't believe in changing the water because I just completely clean the entire piece when the water gets dirty. So I'm cleaning about twice as much. Now the plus side of using Rez block is that when I do clean it's much much easier to get it 100% clean. One thing I did hear is that if you let the Rez block sit in a dirty bong for more than a few days it will actually start molding which I completely believe. I clean every one or two days so I've never seen any mold. One note I do have is that when you add Rez block to a clean bong it has a very faint citrus taste if you pull air through the piece. After your first hit it just taste like bong. You can't tast it when pulling weed through. Over all I don't think I will be buying again unless they lower the price.

title: Works exactly as it should. Almost superhuman. Futuristic. An Oracle?
text:
These rack ears work exactly as they are supposed to. You must remove (unscrew) the plastic sides from your Mackie mixer (pictured, disconnected and resting on top of rack ears) and then attach the ears in their place, using the threaded bolt holes left by the mixer plastic side guards. Perfect fit. No complaints. Ears attach within 1mm perfect spacing. Simple product, no moving or electronic parts to "break." What you see is what you get. A good tip is to wire up your mixer (with a patch panel) so you arent pulling and inserting cables into the mixer all day every day. The connections stay with the mixer, and are plugged at the other end in the patchbay. The gear plugs in and out of the patchbay, no harm- no foul to the mixer.

Pictured is my mixer on top of a rolling rack that has an adjustable, angled top- another ergonomical advantage. While I am at it, this rack was bought here on Amazon as well and is solid as a rock. If you need to move around your rack once in a while, this is the way to do it- in lieu of pulling your hair out when you unplug every connection, move your rig and either can't reach or can't remember where to plug in the myriad of cables. With a dozen inputs, a dozen inserts, 48 front patch positions, as well as 48 rear patch positions, audio interfaces, secondary and third level mixers, amplifiers, distribution amplifiers, humbuckers, effect pedals, power conditioners, two dozen pieces of vintage gear without all the modern amenities, MIDI spaghetti, MIDI interfaces, USB & USB3 running in and out of gear and the PC, perhaps a secondary PC just to record? Maybe even a PC to just record dry multitrack! Powered monitors, passive monitors feeding off amplifiers, casual entertainment from secondary and third level laptops, single board computers, refurbished PCs with a SSD, a GPU and massive memory dumped in to make it nothing more than a fancy HD internet streaming device. Possibly able to record with some big drives and a stripped down OS.

The short story is (TOO LATE!) the rack ears not only save space, they open up either the top or the vertical side of the mixer in order to make it more available for multiple uses by keeping the clutter behind, to the side, and generally out of the way- while you, the engineer, are trying to figure out a solution, not trying to get tangled in a spaghetti of wires and cables.

Sure, color coded cables help. Those little numbered decals at either end of cables near the jack can help. Not without a key of some sort though. If you've got all the codes on a piece of paper, it's hard to make mistakes. It's even harder to try to hold on to a cheat sheet, while holding tools, cables, balancing on your back, with a flashlight in your mouth.

Work smarter…. not harder!

title: Overall, Nerdwax works well. It’s easy and fast, you just rub it onto the nosepads and it works as advertised!
text:
I would like to start by saying that I wear glasses daily, and have quite greasy skin, so glasses sliding down my face is a real problem I face every single day. Nerdwax appealed to me in that it is advertised as being able to solve the very problem I suffer from.

A couple of things to note: I have to re-apply Nerdwax to my glasses at least twice a day for it to remain effective. Also, something with your glasses themselves could be causing the slipping, in my case the nosepads were too close together, so instead of hugging the sides of my nose, they kind of just sat toward the top of the bridge. I was able to just separate them a bit more, and it vastly improved how effective Nerdwax is for me, so that is something to keep in mind.

Overall, Nerdwax works well. It’s easy and fast, you just rub it onto the nosepads and it works as advertised!

title: Don’t Trust The Sizes From Unves
text:
I bought a different print design of “3 oz” bathroom cups from UNVES only a handful of weeks ago. Despite being advertised as 3 ounces, look at the picture… you can see that they are about 2/3 the size of a standard Bathroom Dixie Cup. Does that matter? It does if you have a dispenser for 3 oz. cups. In fact, a normal stream of water from our bathroom faucet causes the water to splash out of this tiny cup and onto the wall. Once you have to dry off your painted wall enough times, you might understand that the size DOES matter!
When I went to review the Unves 3 oz. cups that I bought, guess what?? They’re discontinued! I’ve experienced the same with other “Brand X” cups from Amazon as well.
* At this point, I’m reviewing the company that advertises their product with an incorrect size, not the printed design that could be discontinued tomorrow. I would advise you not to buy from UNVES unless you check reviews, and look out for complaints about the size.
These little cups look very nice and they hold enough water to take a couple of aspirin. If you don’t mind getting stuck with a pack of several hundred 2 ounce cups when paying for a pack of 3 ounce cups, then don’t sweat it… they’ll be OK. BUT, if you want a specific size, do your homework first.

title: Don’t Trust The Size
text:
What a shame!
These “3 oz.” cups by UNVES are much smaller than 3 oz., about 2/3 as big… the smaller cup in my photo is the UNVES. The larger is a standard 3 oz. bathroom cup from the grocery store. So what, right?? Well, many people use dispensers made for standard 3 oz. Dixie bathroom cups, and these 2 oz. cups are too small. Beside that fact, they are so small that an average stream of water out of most faucets swirls and splashes right out of the cup, onto my bathroom wall. After about 20 times of drying off your painted wall, you’ll get my point.
Of course, any review of MY otherwise attractive cups is useless, because one month after getting them, they’re discontinued! So- I’m not reviewing the printed design, I’m reviewing the UNVES brand. I have learned that this seems to be a common practice with these off-brand bathroom cups.
** If one style of cup isn’t what they claim, then beware ANY of them.
** SO- if you want to put up with a bathroom size cup that’s the same as what you get in a dentist’s chair for rinsing, then these cups are ok. But, if you need a 3 ounce cup, then look for a more honest, reputable brand. I’d be wary of any UNVES cup advertised as “3 ounce.”

title: Good in pinch but not for regular travel
text:
I thought this would be a good idea to cut down on the clothes packed for our 10 day trip to Italy. I think the sheets work fine for washing, it's more the entire process that is not good. First of all, you are supposed to remove the sheets with "dry hands", which is difficult unless you remember to remove them before putting the clothing in the sink or turning on the water. If your hands are the least bit damp you will mess up the paper-thin sheets in pack. :(

As for the washing ability of the sheets, I think it does fine with one to two sheets for an article of clothing (tshirt or two pairs of socks). It does not produce suds, but the clothes smell clean afterward (even socks).

Also, I bought the Rick Steves clothesline to dry the items. Well, it takes several days for the clothes to dry. Unless someone has a faster way to dry the clothes, then this isn't a really feasible way to travel.

title: It tastes terrible... but I never leave home without it!
text:
I've been using this remedy for leg cramps for about 5 years. It is amazing, and I always make sure I have a bottle ready for me. I keep mine in the kitchen, so I can quickly make it myself (or even have my kids or husband rush to the rescue).

I usually mix it with about 1-2 ounces of water, although I have also dumped it into whatever drink was quickly available, when I couldn't get to water quickly. This remedy is on my travel checklist, as leg cramps are common for me when I am sleeping away from home. I try to always keep a full bottle in the cupboard, so I never run out. I am glad to see this special deal for multiple bottles.

I am plaqued with terrifying leg cramps, unlike the "charlie horse" leg cramps I used to get as a teenager. They often wake me from sleep, but can also strike me when I am awake. My toes will seize up, and start curling backward, or there will be a burning cramp that rushes up the front of my calf and inside of my thigh. I have to jump up immediately, or they will paralyze me in my seat. There are times when I literally can not get my foot off the floor, to get to the kitchen for my "leg cramp stuff" (that's what my family calls it... LOL!)

It might be due to my varicose veins, but nothing my doctors have suggested has worked. I gave an empty bottle to the doctor who treats my varicose veins, and now he stocks it on his shelves at his office! Amazing stuff. My mother also relies on it, as it works for her similar issues.

The one thing I will warn you about, is the taste. It does have a yucky taste (like vinegar), and especially when you get down near the bottom of the bottle. Make sure you shake the bottle before use, and just don't pay attention to those strange floaty shadows in the bottle, as you are using the last of the formula.
I have tried drinking this straight from the bottle, but because I also suffer from peptic ulcers, it burned and made me double over in pain (while waiting for relief from the cramps). I am 41 years old and at a healthy weight.

These are so bad, even our teenage son - who eats 3,000 calories a day without blinking - would rather be hungry than put them in his mouth.

title: Should be renamed "Help, I Can't Stop Working Out".
text:
I've been a fan of Shatter for several years now. I tried SX-7 Neuro after about a year and a half of no use, and again I am pleased.

You know how you get mentally tired from a workout at a certain point? This stuff curtails or eliminates that. I was 40 minutes into a pretty strenuous workout this morning and I didn't feel like I wanted to stop. I felt like I could just keep going - there was no mental breakdown or resistance to doing more exercise.

I took this supplement about a year and a half ago and noticed the same sort of effect. I thought it was just a one-off, but it seems to be an effect of the powder. Pretty neat if you want a long workout without mental nagging.

Pros:

* As mentioned above, it seems to eliminate the "I want to stop working out now". It just gives more mental endurance
* Gives you more focus and sustained energy - leads to more lifts
* Lifts your mood somewhat, although the Shatter original formula seems to do this a lot more for me. That stuff is a big mood enhancer - you feel incredible!
* Doesn't taste bad
* Generous servings for the price (60)

Cons:

* Not much to complain about. This isn't really a con, but some people might not like it - there is a medium-strength niacin flush you get from ingesting it, especially on an empty stomach. It's like a warm, tingly, flushing feeling. Again, it doesn't bother me at all, but some folks may shy away from that.

Otherwise, this is really great stuff - a very potent addition to pre-workout regimens.

Other things:

If you want the most potent experience, I suggest taking it early in the morning on an empty stomach. Go workout about 15-20 minutes later. You'll feel the effects nicely.

text:
Despite of the fact that the author is not a nutritionist or a medical doctor, the topic is well researched and well presented.

As always, there are points that may be argues, such as consuming carbohydrates after a workout or training to the point of momentary failure (in the chapter on exercise, which is available on the author's website) and others. However, overall the book is very useful.

Rob Fagin elaborates on the topic of carbohydrate cycling. It is not new and has been advocated by other authors, Charles Poliquin, for instance. Fagin's approach is somewhat different and adds to options available to those who want to try it.

Other, neglected topics, such as sleep and water consumption, are also well researched and presented in the book.

The book is good. Well written and fun to read.

title: Krill oil supplement with astaxanthin
text:
VitaCause krill oil formulated with K*REAL* krill and contains astaxanthin. I am not sure what is special about the K*REAL* krill, but astaxanthin is a keto-carotenoid found in krill and other fish. In fact, it is this compound that gives shrimp and salmon flesh its red color. Astaxanthin has antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activity, so its use as a dietary supplement may be benefit those with cardiovascular, immune, inflammatory or neurodegenerative disease. There is also some preliminary evidence that astaxanthin has an anti-aging effect. This is in addition to the positive effects of EPA and DHA.

The krill oil was manufactured in the US in a GMP facility. A lot number and expiration date is stamped on the bottle. There are 60 capsules in the bottle. There is no mention as to whether the capsules are manufactured in a facility with soy, dairy, peanut and gluten, etc. The capsules contain shellfish [obviously] and gelatin. The recommend dose is 2 capsules which contains 1,000 mg krill oil, with 60mg EPA, 40mg DHA and 200mg astaxanthin. The capsules are the usual small peanut size for krill oil supplements and smell very fishy in the bottle. The smell doesn't bother me, it just means I am getting what I paid for. They are easy to swallow and I don't get fish burps from other supplements, so I can't say if these are better or worse in that regard.

Having done a lot of research on krill vs. fish oil, I have switched exclusively to krill oil to lower inflammation to help with my fibromyalgia. It is too hard to consume enough fatty fish regularly to get therapeutic doses of EPA/DHA. This krill oil touts the presence of astaxanthin, however, I think all krill oil supplements contain at least some astaxanthin, as evidenced by their red color.

I purchased this product at a discount for my honest opinion.

title: This size is great for small deep cuts, or small cuts that need held together.
text:
These are pretty great. They hold the wound together well, stick pretty well (see below), and are easy to use. This size is SMALL, for small cuts. My recent application is a small cut 1/2" long by 1/8" or so deep (razors are very sharp when they are new... who knew?!?). But, the backing they are attached onto is cut so you have a small 1/16" or 1/8" bit that stays on so it doesn't stick to your fingers when applying it, and the rest of the backing comes off so you can put THAT bit onto the site. Then you pull the stuck side across the wound to pull the cut closed and then press down the other side to hold it closed. Then you simply pull off the remaining backing. It is like how band aides have the white plastic backing split in half, so you leave one side covered until you position the bandage, then peel the other side off as you pull it over the wound.

You should probably buy multiple sizes. I did. These will not work for large cuts as you will need wider and longer strips, so find and order sizes to cover a wide array of wound sizes. Always be prepared!

They are not very 'stretchy' either, but they should not be. They are meant to hold the wound closed so it can knit together, not stretch so it opens back up. Maybe they should ask us to rate 'flexibility' instead. They are VERY flexible, like thin cloth tape, but also seem porous to allow the wound to drain if needed. you do NOT need to put on 50 of these to completely cover the wound from one side to another... there are videos that show proper usage. These are applied with spacing like stitches.

I have mixed feelings about the 'adhesion' rating. Current bandages using adhesives have to find some balance between 'it sticks on and does it's job' and 'it doesn't tear the wound back open when you try to remove the bandage'. This bandage seems to strike a good balance. I don't have much luck with them on a cut at the base of my pinky finger UNLESS I wrap the site with "Self Adherent Cohesive Wrap Bandages". If I don't wrap the site, the bandages will rub off in 5 min to 4 hours, depending on what I'm doing. If I wrap the site, then they will stay put for 4 to 6 hours. This is a double edged sword, as the wrap increases moisture retention, which in turn makes them come lose faster.

I think they all simply need to switch to a two step process. Make bandages stick like they are welded on is step one. Step two is you apply a sterile 'remover' agent to loosen/dissolve the adhesive to remove the bandage. Maybe some already do this? If so, then I haven't seen them.

title: Disgusted I turned them off and used my cheap practice ...
text:
I purchased this set of visual poi to use at a Bassnectar concert on New Years Eve.

Shipping too almost a month as it came from New Zealand, further there was no tracking available on the shipment, though it did come in a day or two early. Luckily I ordered them about 3 months out so no worries.

When I pulled them out New Years Eve I put in some fresh batteries as I didn't have a lot of faith in the "Home of Poi" batteries that come included and took off to see Bassnectar. About 5 minutes after turning them on, one of my poi turned off, so I go to turn it back on and nothing. Pulled the batteries out put them back in and they relit except the bottom most LEDs (Farthest from the tether), so I figured I had a short. Pulled them back apart and made sure all the wiring was connected, put them back together and miracle of miracles all the lights turned back on....for another 5 minutes...until the bottom LED's went out again....followed shortly by the rest of the LED's in that case. Disgusted I turned them off and used my cheap practice set.

When contacting customer service to see about an exchange, I was told to disassemble the poi and make sure all the wiring was tight. That was the end of the conversation, when paying over $100 dollars for a poi set I expect them to work as intended for more than 5 minutes. I turned around and bought some Podpoi from Flowtoys and have never been happier, they may very well be my most favored possession...and they come with a lifetime warranty.

Home of Poi your customer service is abysmal.

I needed this case for my fiance who is a nurse and travels often for work. When he travels, he needs to take his medication with him. I thought this would be perfect. It is definitely a great little case for the fact that it can hold so much, it is color coded, it has 4 compartments for each of the 7 days labeled (Morn, Noon, Eve, Bed) and that is great ,however after just a few uses the printing is coming off. I do think that it is a little rough sliding the clear plastic cover open to get meds out of a particular compartment (or add meds), the plastic is rather thin, it tends to get stuck, and feels like it could break eventually. If you do not need one of the medications in the middle, and you have to slide the clear plastic lid open past morn to get to "noon" , if there are meds in the morning part, and you have to dump meds out, they all fall out. I wish the lid had individual compartment lids. Otherwise, the case is good and can be a great case for the right person. I wish they would upgrade it a little by making a few adjustments. Better plastic on the lids would help, having lids for each compartment (Morn, Noon, Eve, Bed) even if it is just a lid to lift up, and the ability to label the compartments would be nice! Even if it just included stickers to label them. Overall, it is decent and my fiance is getting a lot of use out of it. Thank you.

title: Not that effective
text: Folks, this is basically a mild ben-gay. Sure, it smells better, but compare active ingredients. Did a blind test with Penetrex and both were ok. Neither provided more relief than the other, so go for the cheaper one. This is not a BAD product. It's just you're paying top dollar for a slightly reformulated ben-gay. You can buy over four times as much ben-gay, at a much higher concentration of active ingredients, for this price. Yes, this smells better and it's smell is noticeably less. Hat tip for that. But if anyone thinks this is "a miracle in a jar", they are reaping the benefits of the placebo effect. The mind is a powerful tool and it can do wonders to alleviate pain if it "believes". I suspect a lot of the 5 star reviews are written by people whose minds more responsible for their pain relief than this cream is. If you are leaving home for the day/night and need warmth to soothe your pain and no smell, I would recommended a thermacare. This product is very over priced for what it is and what it does.

title: and many marbles will etch easily from acids (certain cleaners
text: Most granite countertops are so dense they don't need sealing, especially black. Leave a few water drops on your granite counter top. If you come back in 30 minutes and they are still there, then you don't need to seal it. Marble and other types of stone are more porous and usually need to be sealed. That being said etching is what causes most peoples problems. Calcium in some granites, and many marbles will etch easily from acids (certain cleaners, citrus fruits, etc). Sealing doesn't prevent etching. The acids react with the calcium in the stone. All this information is easily available if you search google. Its not just my opinion. Search granite, etching, etc. You will find this information on many websites. This product works well when you have a more porous counter top. Remember Rock Doctor is in the business to make money. They aren't going to tell you that most granite counter tops don't need to be sealed, nor will they tell you that sealing won't prevent etching. Sealing also won't prevent hard water stains around your sink if you leave the water on the counter top to dry around the sink routinely. The minerals will build up over time as the water evaporates.

Yes, our Super Sweet blend is made from non GMO erythritol and our Organic Pure Stevia Extract Powder which is grown and processed in China.
Here is an excerpt from an article recently published by Trim Healthy Mama on the this subject:
"Serene's husband Sam recently returned from his second trip to where our Stevia is grown, harvested dried then extracted. While many companies are hush-hush about where they get their Stevia from (which in the world of Stevia is either from South America or China), we're so excited and proud of our source that we'll have a soon to be released documentary about it. There are many myths about the processing of Stevia, mostly put out by scare tactic bloggers who have never been to the countries where this plant is grown and extracted! So much of the speculation about processing is hearsay not fact. We want to show you the beautiful organic farms, the gentle processing methods used and some of the incredible landscape in this part of the country that has been dedicated to organic farming. We truly feel like God blessed us with the gift of being able to partner with organic farming communities who have been using the same growing methods for centuries without use of pesticides or other toxins.
People often get worried when they hear that a product comes from China. We felt the same way until we were able to send members from our own THM team to visit, not once but twice. They've been able to get to know the farmers and their families more and film the extraction from leaf to powder. Just like there are good and bad practices here in the United States, we've discovered that is the case in every country"

I will purchase again.

text: After a flood destroyed my workshop, most of my hand tools were covered with mud and began rusting. I bought ten pounds of All Natural Washing Soda - which is sodium carbonate - and followed the procedure.  It worked!  So far I have recovered 20 files and rasps with a minimal of manual effort. I have used up my ten pounds of the washing soda and plan to order another ten pounds so I can remove the rust from my stone and wood chisels. I recommend All Natural Washing Soda to anyone who wants to try electrolysis to remove rust from metal tools.

text:
It seems it takes several weeks for the affects to be felt. I am wrighting this review after 4 weeks of use and didn't notice any affects until about 3 weeks of continued use. I used them as directed, 2 pills, twice daily. I took them with & without food with no difference in stomach comfort or after taste. While taking these I didn't change my diet. My diet doesn't consist of Any fast food and contains Very Little processed foods. I eat mostly chicken meat, eggs, fish, beans, and brown or white rice. Those are my staple but I do eat vegetables, dairy, and breads, however not as much as the others, but like all diets it's a balance with time and is a work in progress.

4 - Stars for Ease of Swallowing as they may be hard for some to swallow.
5 - Stars for Flavor as there was None I could detect.

These pills don't have an after taste or cause burps. There is no jittery, weird, uneasy, or nauseous feeling after taking these. They are very light so that makes them a little harder to swallow as they float in your mouth. I found it best to have no air in my mouth with the water and pills and to swallow it quickly in order to make it easier. Thicker drinks, like protein shakes or smoothies, also help to swallow them as the more viscous liquid helps to hold the pills more still.

For me the affects are almost unnoticeable in some areas until I started thinking about it & focusing in on their benefits, however like all things, some may experience different results, quicker, slower, more intense, or less.

I have noticed less pain in joints where there was some pain.
They seemed to help prevent bloating as I seemed to have less of it although it's hard to really tell. I'm not sure that it helped keep me regular, as the ingredients are also known for, but I didn't have any issues with regularity.
I should note that my diet doesn't consist of enough fiber & vegetables so regularity is sometimes an issue but was not while taking these pills.

4 - Stars for Presentation because the inside of the bottle had a bit of herbal residue and I even got an empty smashed casing inside. In most of the supplements that I take or have taken I have never seen this much, if any at all, residue inside a bottle and this is the first time I have ever gotten a smashed and/or empty casing.

I believe more in taking care of your body naturally, with herbs, proper diet, etc. than with medications so I like these pills.
If you decide to take these I suggest using them, as recommended, for at least a full 3 weeks before you look for any changes in health or write a review. Most products take at least that long, or longer, to feel any affects.

title: Good for what it is
text:
What do you expect? It's a $12 mechanical scale.

If you are looking for 0.1 lb precision, don't buy this scale. If you are looking for something modern and stylish, buy something else. If you want to be able to step on this scale and just "get a number", you will be disappointed.

So why buy this scale?

You will be able to step on this scale and get a rough idea of what you actually weigh for years. No worries about batteries or sensor malfunctions in a few months.
If your weight is a bit off, this scale comes with a handy calibration wheel so you can adjust it. If your electronic scale gets out of calibration, well, too bad.
While internal friction may interfere the readings of any mechanical scale, if you think the number you get is odd, you can hop back on with no waiting!
You will not have to worry about the stylish glass surface breaking. The anti-slip rubber coated sheet metal surface is both safe and durable.

There are better scales out there, there are better mechanical scales out there, but this scale does a good enough job for its $12 price tag.

text:
I have used the mop once, and if my review changes after multiple uses I'll update. However, I've wanted a steamer since we moved into this house 7 months ago because our entire downstairs is tile. We have a swiffer but the wipes for that get crazy expensive when you try to do a whole house. I'm skeptical on how well it actually cleans since it's just hot steam, but after my first use I have to admit it does a good job! We have a dog and live in the desert so it's impossible to keep floors clean. I sweep & mop twice a week because of it.

Pros:
- Incredibly easy to assemble and use
- Comes with the carpet attachment. We have a carpet cleaner but this is nice for our area rug
- Seems to be doing a good job cleaning the floors without streaking
- Water container is small, but for our living room, family room, kitchen and dining area I only need to refill once halfway through which really isn't bad.

Cons:

- The cord needs to be longer. Whoever built this house didn't put in enough outlets where you'd expect there to be outlets, and it's hard to reach some parts of each room with this cord
- When moving the cord you have to turn it off, and then wait for it to heat back up. More of an annoyance than anything else, but a longer cord would also solve this problem
- I wish it had the option to do either continuous steam OR steam on demand, instead of only continuous steam. Now I either have to move things out of the way before I start or stop it completely (and then wait for it to heat back up) to move a piece of furniture. Maybe a pause button?

Overall, for the price, a great item. I'm sure my cons would be fixed with a more expensive steamer. Great value for the price and as long as it holds up for a long time, I will be happy with it.

One item that I'll be messaging the seller about is the part where the handle attaches to the rod is cracked, but I don't doubt they'll take care of that. If not, I'll update my review.

title: Great Replacement for Sonicare Toothbrush, with a Little Work
text:
I have an older Sonicare toothbrush from Costco. I wasn't able to find the exact model name of it. These batteries appeared to be the right size and layout for my toothbrush, so I gave it a try. Similar to another reviewer, I had a hard time getting all of the solder out of the holes to make room for the new battery. I spent a bit of time with a soldering iron, a desoldering braid, and finally some spare copper wire. Using the copper wire, I was able to get the holes cleared of old solder and make room for the new batteries. Then I was able to re-solder the new battery without running wires around the outside like the previous reviewer did.

Results:
Before the replacement, I had to charge my toothbrush every single day. Sometimes it would not even last through 2 brushings. With the new battery, I went a full week before the orange charge light came on. And it went another week before I really needed to charge it. So I'm now getting 1-2 weeks of battery life on these new batteries. I have been using them for about 2.5 months now, without any issues. I would highly recommend them, as long as you're not afraid of a soldering iron.

title: Cibavision discontinued Miraflow, but Walgreens makes an exact replacement
text:
I was a longtime user of Miraflow Daily Cleaner by Cibavision. It was the best lens cleaner I'd ever used. It made my lenses cleaner, more comfortable, and last longer than any of the other types I'd tried by Alcon, Bausch & Lomb, etc. When I shifted over to disposables, I still took them out at night and cleaned/disinfected them the same way as I had the old daily wear lenses.

At some point several years ago, Cibavision decided to discontinue Miraflow. All of us faithful users scrambled to eBay to buy remaining stock that had been snapped up by people who'd raided the shelves of the retail stores and cleared them out. Then it became known that CVS and Walgreens had their own versions of the Miraflow formula.

I don't think CVS makes their version anymore, but Walgreens is still available. And it works just as well as Miraflow did. If you tried Miraflow, you know how good it is. If you didn't, give this a shot. It really is that good.

title: I really wanted this to be great, but....it fell short
text:
I really wanted this to be great. I've had problems with falling glasses for months and thought this would be the solution. It works for about 15 minutes and then the glasses are back to sliding down my nose. I do have somewhat oily/combination skin so I don't know if that's contributing to it or not? I apply it liberally as per the instructions, but it doesn't work for long.

Also, because you have to apply it liberally, be prepared for it to somehow end up on the lenses. It's like syrup at a pancake house...somehow you always end up with it on the back of your arm even if you didn't eat pancakes. Good luck getting it off without washing your glasses in the sink, it just smears around.

Additionally because it's the same size as a chapstick, it doesn't really fit very well between my nose piece, they should make it narrower for people with smaller framed glasses.

title: Great Product - excellent nutrition - decent flavor
text:
I have tried a couple different "healthy" shakes, but none compare to Vega! Most shakes only contain whey protein, but your body needs so much more. Plus, whey protein does not agree with everyone (lactose intolerant, milk allergy, vegan), and it can be argued that whey protein is not good for anyone.
Vega's the only shake that doesn't upset my stomach and I feel good knowing that I'm getting a good dairy-free source of protein, vitamins & minerals from all of Vega's natural ingredients.

Now, on to the taste of Vega - I first tried the chocolate because I love chocolate. The chocolate flavor Vega in no way resembles the "chocolate" I know and love! My husband, however, didn't mind it while I could not even get through a glass of it. Next, I tried Berry and I found that with a banana & a handful of frozen blueberries it was quite good. I then tried the Vanilla Chai flavor and am pleased that I only need to add a banana to make it delicious! My favorite right now is Vanilla Chai because it's easier to mix up in the morning than the Berry with the extra blueberries.

A couple tips on Vega - mixing it with a banana helps hide the grittiness of the product. Also, mixing it with Almond Milk helps. I also like to blend up only 1 scoop (1/2 serving) with 8oz water, 1 banana, and 1 cup or so of ice and find it to be PLENTY for a fast healthy breakfast! Also, if you don't like the flavor at first try some different additions or try the other flavors and you should find one that you like. Even if you can only "tolerate" the flavor at first, after a few times of having it, you'll get used to it and it will taste better!

title: very little lotus root content
text:
not quite right. it *might* have some lotus root powder in it, but I think it's mostly some other kind of starch - cornstarch, or tapioca/arrowroot starch.
the color is off - lotus root starch is very pale grayish-yellow when dry, with maybe a tiny hint of pink. when you add hot water to thicken it should be dark translucent brown. this one is weirdly (artificially?) pale pink, with no yellow tinge, and the texture is too smooth. when you add hot water, it the color doesn't get as deep, and the texture is too elastic. By elastic I mean it is kind of stringy (like corn-starch) and sticky, whereas pure lotus root starch is a *little* sticky, but more on the gloppy side than the stretchy gluey side, if that makes any sense. This product also doesn't have a strong lotus smell like the old west lake brand. This is a shame, since i can't find the old west lake boxes (made in PRC) anywhere anymore, now all the west-lake style ones I can find are pre-sweetened mixes, flavored with osmanthus, which is way too sweet and sickly. Still this is better than nothing.

title: Staying Power and Cost Savings
text:
I stumbled upon the eneloop line through another website, and grew intrigued based on a multitude of solid reviews. I'm no engineer, but I can tell you this: these batteries last. I have a four-year old son who puts his electronic toys through their paces. Not only do I find myself hunting less often for a screwdriver to open plastic battery compartments, but also I'm saving tons of money. Seriously, I could track my spending on conventional batteries via my online banking account, I bought batteries so often. Now, no more runs to the local grocer amid a cold snap because Alfie the Robot lost his battery-powered mojo. With eneloops and a decent charger, fresh batteries are just a room away.

Pros:

Longer life than conventional batteries | huge savings over the long-term | long charge shelf-life (verified with charger) | environmental plus

Cons:

My sixteen pack order came with one storage case for four batteries--I wish they'd sent four cases.

I will purchase Sanyo eneloop batteries again, and would recommend to anyone.

title: LOVE MY ORGANIC EXTRA VIRGIN COCONUT OIL...
text:
Wow, where do I start lol? I have been using coconut oil for almost two years. I first started using it when I came across an article about how to clean and whiten your teeth naturally. I had become curious at that time, so I read as much as I could about cleaning and whitening teeth with organic extra virgin coconut oil. I couldn't get enough of reading the testimonials because I am curious like that. So once I got tired of reading, I decided I was sold on trying it. I have to admit, when I first tried it, it made me want to gag. But I reduced the tablespoon down to about a teaspoon for about a week until I got used to having it in my mouth. Long story short, it definitely works for me. After about two months of using, my teeth felt clean and I told a friend, who was asking about it, that at times when I rub my tongue across my teeth, I could feel a silent squeak. I know, but it's true.

My next experience was trying to figure out how to incorporate coconut oil into my diet. So off I was to research adding organic extra virgin coconut oil into my diet. I decided to start adding a tablespoon into my green smoothies that I drink each day or every other day because I read that it aids in dieting. I had already lost quite a bit of weight just with green smoothies, but wanted to incorporate this in for the health benefits. I just started doing that a about a week ago. Will see how that works for me.

And lastly, I have been mixing organic extra virgin coconut oil in my hair oils and body lotions. I've just started making my own body butters and this is one of my main ingredients.

I received this organic extra virgin coconut oil at a discount in exchange for my honest opinion. I can't say to much more about this oil. It's great and I can't see myself without it.

title: Game Changer for Problem Feet
text:
I have had problems with callused feet since I was in my early 20s. Despite taking great care of my feet, they would actually crack open if I was exercising/walking a lot. I have spent countless hours sawing away at my feet with various kinds of foot files and covering them in every cream known to man to help with the problem. A friend recommended I try this and it is AMAZING. I don't have anything magical to add to all of the other glowing reviews except to add my voice to those who say this thing WORKS. I like that it is corded and I don't have to worry about batteries dying on me (those first sessions lasted a while and I am pretty sure batteries would have died). I did overdo it on a spot the very first time I used it, so I do recommend tackling tough feet over several sessions. My feet needed coarser rollers than the blue, so it is worth trying one of those mixed sets to see what works for you.

Refills: I recommend sticking to the rollers that say they are genuine. There are some "compatible with" refills out there that are a waste of money (see my reviews for some to avoid and some that work well if you aren't sure what to buy).

I also HIGHLY recommend the O'Keefe's Healthy Feet foot cream. That stuff was helping before I found this wonderful device.

title: Holds air doesn't leak
text: [[VIDEOID:2d1754782a22b2c34cf0203b7ab2448e]] I have years of experience going to the physical therapist for my neck injury.  In the physical therapy session they usually put me in a traction device that stretched my neck, so I thought I would give this traction device a try since it is basically the same concept.  This device pumps up quickly and no air leaks, but my air release valve doesn't let all the air out quickly.  I do feel this traction device stretching my neck but after 3 weeks of continual use for 5 to 6 minutes per day I don't feel any difference in my neck pain.  I do not wear it longer because it does put quite a bit of pressure on your neck and jaw depending on how much you inflate it.  I'm going to continue to use though because I figure my neck injury has been there for 20 years so it is not going to get better in just 3 weeks.  I do think that anyone with serious neck pain should give it a try because it might help alleviate some pain.  Some relief is better than no relief.
