title: Easy candle lighting!
text:
I have been unable to find sturdy matches in the store lately. We have several old small boxes of matches, but it usually takes two or three to finally get one to light, and the striking area on the side of the box gets worn out before the matches are gone. So I sought out a refillable butane lighter, but I had concerns about safety, storage, etc. I looked into these rechargeable lighters, and decided to give it a go.

This one has been great! I am currently recovering from wrist surgery, and primarily have been using my non-dominant hand. I’m still able to easily light candles. The battery life indicator lets you know if this is running low, and so far it is held a charge for several weeks at a time before I need to charge it again. I light at least one candle a day. I do have concerns if the battery runs down while it’s in a drawer, that it might not work when you need it in an emergency. I hope to find some better matches to keep around for emergencies!

text:
I've been using this for awhile, it has always been the same - good at first, absolutely terrible halfway through. It clean the contacts well and it's really cool how it works. However this product comes with two bottles of the solution, and it is recommended that you leave the contacts in the device/solution for at least 6 hours. I've noticed it's best to check to make sure that the solution isn't still being neutralized by checking for moving bubbles (even the smallest ones) and is best to do it so you don't burn your eyes.

However once you get a little ways into the second bottle: you can leave the contacts in for 9 hours, I've left them in for 12 hours today and I thought that since this was 2x the recommended times that they might be ready, so I didn't check for the bubbles. The past few days, including today, every time I put my contacts in, I get to feel that burn really really badly, it doesn't matter how long they stay in the solution, it won't neutralize. I've actually been late to work twice this week because of it. I guess I will update this review with how long it's taking today but it's been 12.5 hours now and they're still working on it. So if you need your contacts in a timely manner and don't want your eyes to absolutely burn when you put them in, but will still follow the directions even though they're wrong and cause the exact undesired result it warns against in the directions, then these are for you. If you like comfort, simplicity, eyes not burning, your contacts when you need them, to be on time for work, directions that don't lie, these definitely aren't for you. I know they aren't for me anymore as this is the second time IN A ROW that I've purchased this product and the same thing happened. Why give people 2 bottles when the case only lasts for about 1.2 bottles. Insane

First of all, I’m very upset that L’Oréal has seen fit to discontinue the Clairasonic!
I have always used the Deep Pore brush on my face! I’ve actually used facial brushes of every type since I was 6 yrs. old! No joke! So when I found out these cleansing machines were discontinued, I figured I needed to buy more brushes! Bad idea! These brushes are not at all like the Deep Pore brushes that I use to buy! They are very very soft almost like a baby’s hair brush! It’s also fuzzy, like the bristles are all frayed! There’s just no way these brushes will really clean deep pores! I would send them back, but there is no other choice! I’ve had my brush for over 12 years & so far it’s still working great! I also know it won’t work forever, so I’m disappointed all the way around about these brushes! In my personal opinion, All the other brushes look totally & completely the same...soft & fuzzy! The brushes are way to soft so they more or less just flatten out on your face while using them! But you gotta do what you gotta do! I’m dreading the day my Clarisonic finally breaks down! There’s nothing else that’s comparable! I’ve looked at others but they are “cheesy”! I’ve had cheesy automatic face brushes that bog down when they touch your face & almost stop spinning! I’ve thrown several of that type, away! It’s sad that such a great product has been discontinued!

My issue with this is how SWEET it is. I’m not super fond of the taste of greens but this is like drinking sugar water. I was so confused upon first sip but when I took a closer look at the back, I saw that there was 95% of steviol glycoside in “other ingredients” list. It’s the same compound found in stevia. That’s a lot and explains so much why this is so sweet. Maybe it’ll be better in smoothies but it’s undrinkable on its own. I absolutely do not recommend this.

My only compliment for this is that it mixes in really smoothly. There’s no granules or weird textures, so in that regard, this was amazing. However, the sweetness (rather than the flavor) was what ruined it completely for me. I’ll have to try out PEScience greens powder instead next time.

text:
I am absolutely blown away by this Heated Eyelash Curler! It’s so easy to use and it does everything it says it’s supposed to do. It has by far exceeded my expectations! To be perfectly honest, I got the eyelash curler because I’m a lover of gadgets, and to me, this is a unique gadget that I have never seen before. Little did I know how much I would love it, and how much pain and suffering it would save me from during my makeup applying ritual. For decades, I’d been using metal eyelash curlers that pinched my eyelids and at times, pulled out my eyelashes (especially when using them with mascara on). Despite being happy with that curled eyelash look, it was painful to get them that way. Well, no more!

The Heated Eyelash Curler has four LED viewable heat settings with the highest being 85°. It heats up in about 10 seconds, and no batteries are required because it’s rechargeable. It comes with a Type-C fast charging cable, and even a cleaning brush. For safety, it has a 5-minute auto shutoff when not in use, and an anti-scalding comb teeth design. It’s lightweight and compact too! Since it’s about the size of a thicker tube of mascara, it’s really convenient to travel with, and so hassle-free to bring along for your everyday use.

The Heated Eyelash Curler is a big win!

text:
The concept of these are great. It’s cute and it is really easy on the skin. It’s too easy on the skin. It barely sticks for more than hour especially if the tape is being used on a child who is unaware that they aren’t supposed to be pulling on their tubing constantly. If you have an infant with a cannula or feeding tube through the nose, you need to pass on these because this tape can barely sustain the amount of pulling that infants do to their tubing. Instead, I would recommend this tape being used on children who are fully aware that they shouldn’t be messing with their tubing constantly mainly because it is super easy on the skin and it doesn’t leave adhesive residue like other medical tapes I’ve used.

UPDATE: I didn’t want to let these go to waste so instead I started using them to secure my 4mo old son’s G tube extensions when he’s being fed & these stickers come in handy more than I expected. Like I said previously, they’re very easy on the skin. Doesn’t leave excessive adhesive residue, and comes on pretty easy when taking them off. But they do keep a secure hold when placed in an area that isn’t tugged at all the time. So it’s a great thing my sons G Tube extensions are always under his onesies because he doesn’t tug and pull at them, ever.

title: Best Lip Balm EVER.
text:
I use lip balm on a daily basis. I've tried Chapstick, Bath & Body works products, lip butter from The Body Shop, Blistex, Neutrogena, Aquafina lip balm, and Aquaphor ointment. These products all did okay, but what I am really going for is a lip moisturizer, not a "lip protectant" with sunscreen. The Aquaphor ointment is good stuff, but a little to heavy for me to use during the day (sometimes I'll leave it on overnight). The Aquafina lip balm I bought in a 4 pack on a whim, but I really liked it and I used every stick to the end. It's very lightweight and not waxy (more like an oil), moisturizing and has a refreshing peppermint smell.
After I had used up the Aquafina lip balm, I went to the same store looking for more. They didn't have any, so I started looking at the ingredients of the other products because I remembered that the Aquafina labeled jojoba oil as one of the first ingredients.
I found this Green by Nature Lip Butter in a 3 pack, and after reading the ingredients (first 3: beeswax, jojoba oil, shea butter) I bought it. I love this stuff! I think the only reason I like it more than the Aquafina lip balm is because it's slightly thicker (from the shea butter?) and I only have to apply it 2 times in a day, and I've even started applying it before bed! It moisturizes so well that it makes exfoliating a breeze (I exfoliate with a washcloth once a week, after showering, to prevent peely cracked skin).
Take note, though, that it does not contain any sunscreen, if that makes a difference to you

title: Great for in between pedicures!!!!
text:
[[VIDEOID:cc5c53d69b593e1347ad63d9daf2af07]] Pedicures are my best friend and if I could get one every single week believe me I would. Not only do I not have time for that but it also gets a little pricy to get one all the time. My feet being in flip flops most of the days get dry and callused so I needed something for those between times.

CONTENTS: One foot file. This also comes with 2 extra files, a charger, cleaning brush and a cover.

BATTERY TYPE: Rechargeable device.

PERSONAL EXPERIENCE: My feet are not the worse feet in the world but I defiantly could use some help especially between my pedicures. The weather where I live is dry and really plays a huge part in the way that my feet look. I have a lot of dry skin and there are parts of my feet that are cracking due to them being so dry. One of the things that I liked about this file is that it was nice and easy to use. The foot file takes off dead skin without much effort. To do both feet it took me a maximum of 10 minutes total.

The machine itself does not make a lot of noise and is sort of a quieter hum. There are a couple of things that I recommend while doing this to your feet. The first one is that don’t put to much pressure down on your feet. This is powerful enough to take off the dry skin with little pressure. Also after you are done with taking off the skin of your feet, wash and dry your feet completely after you are done.

I love that this machine is rechargeable, this means no buying batteries which is always a pain. I usually charge the foot file an hour before using it and the charge lasts for the whole time that I am using the file. While I do not know how long a full charge lasts I can say for certainty that it lasts long enough for me to smooth both of my pedicure neglected footsies.

OVERALL: I like that I can keep my feet nice and smooth without having to pay the pedicure prices. I like that its nice and small and rechargeable therefore meaning that I don’t have buy batteries. Good machine to have especially if you are like me and like to do home pedis in between the salon ones.

title: Quality Stuff
text:
Truly the only Kava product that I have used that actually has some kind of affect. You really want an all root product like this. the reports of liver damage - in Europe - seem to be associated with capsule product that included bark, stems and leaves.

Also - I have been booze sober for over two years now - But I have read a great deal that suggests booze and kava do not play well together. Seeing that they are both processed thorough the liver this would make very good sense. A night of drinking is not a good night to "give kava a shot."

Start with just a couple large tablespoons the first time. See how you like that. Too much the first time can make you feel sick to your stomach. That isn't related to this product specifically - just kava in general. Forgo the capsules and such if you are looking for something that will have an immediate relaxing affect. Do t the way the islanders do it - make a proper drink from it. I have found the capsules to be a waste of time. Indeed - I have several bottles in my kitchen that have gone unused.

I have been buying this same product from this same company for over a year now and have never been disappointed.

Note - this will work as a mild to strong intoxicant depending on how much you take. You should treat this product just like any physical and mind altering substance (booze, pot, prescription drugs, Nyquil) and NOT DRIVE. Enjoy this in the comfort and safety of your own home.

I have read some say that there is no chance for a hangover. Not true. If you are feeling headachy or shaky the next day you have taken too much. I have been there. Adjust your dosage. Like anything - treat this with respect and you will come to join the many white folks like I who have come to enjoy this product.

Be sure and get yourself the kava strainer bag. DO NOT HEAT the product like a tea. Heat will break down the kavalactones in the product. You will be making a room temperature beverage - that will taste like mud.

title: I want to make the public aware of problem WE all have with this product.
text:
Problem: After applying the contact lens for several hours, I started to have cloudy vision and experience halo effect around streetlights. Very noticeable during the night time, car headlights made it difficult for me to drive. After I took the contact lens out, the cloudy vision and halo effect remained for hours.

The suffer: Because I have been using the Clear Care contact solution for years before having this problem. So naturally, it never occurred to me the contact solution is the problem. I thought I have a serious disease like cataracts etc and I am going blind. So I went to see both optometrist and ophthalmologist, spent money on all sorts of examinations just to find out why. None of the doctors are aware of this product can cause such a problem!
I put the contact lens in normal solution I used before clear care products for longer storage time. Just when I almost gave up on the contact lens, I tried it again. The problem it MAGICALLY went away! And you know how confused I was...(huh!???), and how happy I was. I thought I found the resolution of the problem. But it also occurred to me that I should let the other people know this. So I can help others to save time, energy, and money when they having the same problem.

Thoughts: This is not right! The newer Clear Care product clearly has something different other than the older clear care products. The company didn't make it obvious to the customers and I doubt the product has passed a legit medical trial. This kind of attitude is begging for a class-action lawsuit. I hope Clear Care pulls the product immediately.

title: Impressive ingredient list. GMP certified. Seems to be working.

I have a family history of hypothyroidism and have been tested... dozens... of times over my life but have always had normal lab values. Still I am the coldest person ever and go through seasons that I am convinced my thyroid is contributing to my mental and physical fatigue. This thyroid support supplement may be just what I need: I am happy to know that I am giving my thyroid the best chance of keeping me healthy. It is too early to say whether this supplement has made a difference in my overall well-being, but do believe the increased energy that I have been experiencing may be more that placebo. The capsules are not small, but they are easy to swallow, tasteless, and leave no bad after-taste. The list of ingredients means a lot to me too: I know vitamin b-12 and magnesium are often missing from my die and have benefited from l-tyrosine alone in the past. The rest is relatively new to me but seems to be a great combination. I also like that the dark green capsules are very distinct. And of course, I appreciate that this product is GMP certified.

I received this product at a discount for my unbiased review and am happy I can sincerely recommend it to all of you. Enjoy!

title: So much stronger than any other tea.
text:
I didn't realize just how amazing baetea was until I tried buying non-baetea loose leaf tea. The same tea routine would yield the lamest cup of tea. I first tried some that I got from target, of course, I should have known better, but while I used to fill up less than half of my tea infuser and use it for two consecutive large cups of tea, I found myself filling the tea infuser up to the max and seeping forever to get a tea with even close to enough flavor. Then I got some from a local restaurant in Minnesota for Christmas and had the same experience. Baetea clearly uses superior and stronger components that yield an obvious difference. I did buy some tea at a fancy and expensive tea store, and the tea was crazy expensive and targeted at the tastebuds rather than at the benefits, and this tea tasted a bit better and was equally as strong. So I offer that expensive tea to my guests and drink keep the brilliant of baetea for myself. Did the complexion tea make a difference for my complexion... it is so hard to say. I didn't drink the tea quite as frequently as instructed, and have a decent, but aging complexion... did my skin look healthier and like it was glowing a bit more, of course, but I'm a sucker for a placebo and can't promise with confidence that it was the tea that made a difference. I can promise, that a company that is willing to include the quality tea ingredients of this tea is a company I trust. So overall I think if you're looking for a tea to help with your complexion, baetea is the way to go.

This is my 2nd Tanita, the first was the UM-081 which I'm a big fan of. It calibrates consistently and it's accurate (I have a balanced doctors scale and access to expensive digital scales so I know when scales are accurate).

I wanted a 2nd scale, I wanted a Tanita since I was happy with the first one and figured this would be accurate like my other Tanita. It is not.

I get bad readings and I get inconsistent readings. If I move this scale and my other Tanita to other parts of the house and let them recalibrate and check my weight. I get different readings on this scale (and the same reading on my UM-081)

Unfortunately, at the same time I bought this scale a friend of mine asked me to recommend a scale, I said Tanita, he bought the same scale and he's also having the same issues that I mentioned.

So far my emails to Tanita have been ignored, I called them and then told me to call competitive edge who told me to call tanita again so this scale will be garbage. I asked if I could send this back in for another UM-081 (which costs the same)

title: Bath bubbler keeps bubble baths bubbly!
text:
I was looking for something to basically push the water around in my bathtub and maybe help the bubble bath stay bubbly. It doesn't say anywhere that I shouldn't use it in a bubble bath so I tried it. It moves the water around and is relatively quiet compared to an actually spa tub. Be warned though, this isn't a powerful jet that is going to massage your back or anything. It just bubbles the water around the tub in a gentle motion. For $40-$50 bucks, I love it.

One design flaw I found is that the suction cups are spaced too close together and are difficult to mount without them overlapping. One of them fell off but was easy to reattach. There is a push lock that holds the cups in place meaning in the future, I can probably replace the cups if they wear out.

My biggest concern was safety. I didn't want to electrocute myself in the bathtub with this thing so I read up on this product before trying it out. The device plugs into a transformer that reduces the voltage to only 12 volts so even if the entire device falls into the water, it isn't going to hurt you. Also, the device is capable of being submerged momentarily in case it falls into the water. The instructions say to pull it out and let the water drip out before remounting and turning back on. It's that simple. It suggests to hang the device out to dry for 24 hours if it gets submerged for longer than 5 minutes but since you aren't supposed to leave this item unattended, that shouldn't be an issue. I feel this product is very safe.

As I mentioned above, I used this to try and keep my bubble bath bubbly and it worked! I wondered how much it was helping and decided to test it by turning it on after letting the bubbles break down. Within a few minutes I saw impressive amounts of suds starting to mound up again.

Remember, it just pushes water around and makes bubbles. If you want real bath jets, you need a professional spa tub. As long as you manage your expectations, you will like this little spa jet.

title: AWESOME!
text:
I REALLY like these. They made it possible for me to extend the life of all my pants (including work trousers/slacks- but you have to tweak the way you use it for slacks: see below) until the end of my pregnancy. I have 6 weeks left, and the only snag I have found is that I may have needed one more extender that was longer than the longest one in the pack. It's getting just a little bit tight! I will probably utilize the longest one of the extenders with a hair tie through the hole and around the button. Kind of obnoxious, I know, but its worth it to me to not have to go out and buy maternity pants. I love my jeans and I know how to put outfits with them, so I want to try and use them as long as I can. I would have loved to have had an extra long denim extender, but the longest option is a black, faux-leather extender, which is fine. Oh, and you HAVE to make sure your tops are long enough to cover the zipper! Even if you pull up the zipper as far as it will go and then turn down the little handle to lock it, it will never fully close.

To wear with slacks: put the button through the hole on the side WITHOUT the little metal hook(s). Slip the most comfortable hook through the slit on the extender. Don't try to put the slit on the extender over the button on the side with the metal hook(s)- in the third trimester, it's just too dang tight and you'll be miserable. If your slacks have 3 hooks, then you have even more options/lengths for comfort!

Before the Sedaplus, I had trouble at various times: getting to sleep, being awake for hours in the middle of the night, or waking too early and not being able to sleep any more. Recently, this has changed. I rarely have problems in the middle of the night or early morning, but now just about every single night I have lots of trouble getting to sleep, no matter how tired I am. title: Work great and look great...makes the perfect gift!
text:
I admittedly didn't pay enough attention to this when I placed my order, so I was shocked when I opened my package and found FIFTY containers...for some reason, (because the price was so reasonable, I assume) I figured it was a package of 10, and I was still happy to find these. I have always wanted to make homemade lip balm but the only containers I could find at the craft stores were little tins, and plastic screw top lids where you have to use your finger to apply. I have a weird thing with touching my lips with my fingers when I can't wash them first, and I wanted to be able to throw my lip balms in my purse to use while I'm out and about so I found these and they were exactly what I had been looking for...Making the lip balm ended up being a lot of fun because I experimented with different stains and ingredients, and all came out great! I'm excited to give these out for Mother's Day presents now....Here's the recipe I used:

2 Tablespoons coconut oil
1 T raw honey
1 T shea butter
1 T jojoba oil
4 drops Peppermint oil (I also used sweet orange oil and lemon oil)
1-2 tsp. (depending on how much color you want) of Hibiscus powder (I also tried beet root powder and hibiscus powder - it's fun to play around with these!)
***Make sure your containers are ready to go as this solidifies quickly....!
Over very low heat, I melted the oils, honey and butter. As soon as it melted, I turned off the heat and stirred in the color and scented oils, then used an eye dropper to put into lip balm containers...voila!
Be sure to wipe down the sauce pan quickly, as it's easiest to get off while it's still liquidy

title: Firm and Dense Natural Scrubbers
text:
These are quite dense and very firm loofa. The "Luffa" gourd actually got it's name in Egypt. Here, the sponge gourd called “luf” in Arabic, came to be known as loofa from the name Luffa genus, Luffa Aegyptiaca.

When I ran a soap making operation, we had a three soap pack that included a native Philippine loofa. It was sometimes difficult to find the quantities that we needed. I would ride my motorcycle all around manila collecting loofa from different vendors and packing them into a gigantic clear bag.

I guess they grow them a little better in Egypt. All three loofa in the package were identical in size and density. Each has a loop of cotton rope tied to them so they can be hung in the shower. Water and use do soften them up a little bit but these are some tough little natural sponges.

One if my passions is long distance motorcycle riding. I'm a member of the Iron Butt Association, a world wide group of people who ride long distances. The shortest ride is 1,000 miles in 24 hours. Of course, there are much more challenging rides than this.

For me, the hardest part of endurance riding is a sore rump. I can stop up for days without sleep. I can ride through all sorts of weather and not bat an eye, but my butt starts hurting early and just gets worse and worse.

I've tried all sorts of air cushions and several different types of saddles over the years, but none have given me adequate relief, until I tried a Royal Purple cushion. It changed everything!

Where before I could only ride 1,500 miles max in 24 hours, with several days to recover, I can now ride much, much longer! My last ride a ride around Texas, where I rode around the entire circumference of Texas, 3,100 miles in less than three days. Most of this was on two lane black top, instead of the freeway. I was spending 16-20 hours a day in the saddle on an old Harley that didn't have much in the way of rear suspension.

Granted, I was still sore and tired, but I was no longer in agony. I've tried everything short of a Russell Day-Long Saddle, and nothing has helped until now. Truly a game changer.

title: Nice pillow for the car
text:
I purchased this pillow as well as the $19 "Adjust-Air Portable Lumbar Support by Mediflow." Both pillows are similar, but overall I think this one provides better lumbar support. However, if you're concerned about having the external hose/bulb arrangement, you might be happier with the $19 version.

I like this pillow best for the car. Once it's in place, having the external bulb makes it very easy to inflate/deflate even while driving. A downside is that it can catch on things if you're constantly moving it between the car and house/office.

The $19 version is pretty much the same pillow, however the bulb and release valve are just sewn into the pillow underneath "+" and "-" symbols. Being self-contained, it's definitely easier to move around and take with you. However, it can be hard to reach the bulb to inflate, and you can also accidentally lean against the air release valve when you don't intend to.

Overall, I'm happy with both pillows, but this version is probably slightly better. It'll give you a little better support in my opinion than the $19 version. I keep this one in the car, and carry around the self-contained pillow for the house and office.

title: Don't think about it, just get it.
text:
I had a hard time breastfeeding my baby so I made the decision to exclusively pump. It was fine at first but then got super difficult being attached to the wall for about 4 hours a day. I couldn't get anything done. Especially pumping at night was hard because being half asleep, feeding the baby and then pumping would take over an hour to do. I started using this and it has made my life easier.

Pros:
1. Super affordable compared to Elvie and Willow
2. Easy to clean the parts
3. Rechargeable!
4. Good suction
5. Got more output than with my Spectra

Cons:
1. Not enough size options
2. Replacement parts are pretty pricey, in my opinion
3. The plastic part got a bit warm on my breast, not sure why
4. Only goes up to level 9
5. Loud!

Overall, this is an excellent pump. I still can't believe I got more milk from this than I did with my Spectra. I only bought one but I just ordered a second one! Just buy it, it'll make your life way easier. Please be careful with transferring your milk from the container. I have spilled milk a few times. Basically you have to take off the motor and then SLOWLY pour the milk out of the spout. If you do it too quickly, the milk will come out of the hole your nipple goes into. Also when putting the pump parts together, make sure everything is tight and sealed. This will ensure no leaks happen while pumping.

Lastly, don't buy the spare parts for this. It will cost you almost as much as a new pump with motor. Instead, look for the same device under a different brand name. I bought 2 from this brand and 2 from another cheaper brand and it cost less. Now I have 4 pumps and 4 sets of dispensers.

title: Poor quality, convenient container -- UPDATED 10/2012
text:
**Original 12/2010**
This may be a tough rating (1-star), but I think that the quality of this product can be found in the dollar store. If it were $5 or under, I'd improve it's rating. (And if it were $1, I'd give it 5-stars.) As others have said, the threading is not high quality and the plastic is thin. It's definitely not worth $10. I was sent the all-clear variety instead of the colors, which I would have preferred. It would have been nice to be able to specify your preference!

There are pros to this product, though, and I'm not going to return it. It is definitely useful and convenient. It fits 8 vitamins (including big ones like my fish oil and calcium), and has room for more! You can probably fit two of those soft chewables in addition to fish oil, calcium, multi, and others. I probably could have gone a size smaller, but this will be great when I'm traveling and can double up on my days.

**UPDATE 10/2012**
I just improved my rating a little to 2-stars (If I could do 2.5, I would). I still don't think this product is worth more than $5.

However, I've been using it for a couple years now, and it has held up. I've dropped it on a ceramic tile floor, and while the container popped open and all of my vitamins spilled over the floor and under the fridge (ugh!), there were only cracks on the containers and chips off of the screw-top threading. The container now looks like it has a stained glass look since there are cracks ALL over it. So why would I improve the rating after this? Well, the containers still screw together and they didn't actually shatter. I suspect they will break, though, after another tumble or two, but I was pleasantly surprised! I should also add that the containers have become disconnected on other occasions... in my suitcase. Luckily at those times, they were contained. But it's still a less than ideal happening. The threads aren't high quality. You need to be extra careful that you have all of the threads alined and twist the container tightly -- but not too tightly (or it will crack). I think it might be an art.

One additional piece of advice... the containers are NOT WATERPROOF. I took it camping and threw it in the cooler on the drive up (thinking back, I don't know why did that!) and let's just say that it was rather disgusting cleaning out the vitamins. I will never do that again.

All of this said, I'm looking for another manufacturer of the stackable containers. I really like the convenience they offer. I can fill up the entire container for a week, but only take one with me daily instead of the entire stack. That, to me, is awesome. If I don't find a higher quality option or if the container breaks before I can find an alternative, I *might* buy another one. But I'm a little stubborn and will only do that if I absolutely have to! (And that is purely for the convenience [and size] it provides.)

title: I returned it but they wouldn't refund my money!
text:
The one I got did NOT have ANY brightness adjustment control, although note the description: "adjusts brightness to the equivalent of ordinary 75, 100, or 150 W bulbs."

The light was blindingly bright and because it uses a proprietary pin socket, you cannot replace the bulb with an ordinary lightbulb, and Verilux does not make a lower "wattage" bulb for this lamp.

I was told by the vendor Independent Living Technologies (Garner, NC) that an older model did have an adjustable switch but that the current model does not. They would not refund my money even after I returned it to them.

I note one reviewer says the light is too dim; perhaps they were sent the older model in which the adjustment control does not work properly.

Caveat emptor/buyer beware. Only buy this item if you can get a money back guarantee. It cost me $35 to ship it back.

title: Smells like cat food, tastes like salmon lox

I tried eating it straight from the can and the texture is not exactly pleasant. It’s extremely soft and spreads like whipped cream cheese, so I spread it on a sandwich along with a few other things, and it didn’t take long for me taste a familiar taste which is salmon lox. So now I pretend that that’s what I’m putting on instead of “liver” and it’s fantastic. I will say that what the scale says vs. total grams/can does not make a whole lot of sense to me. What I am looking at is roughly 28g or so if I divide up the chunks across 2 total servings in the can (57.5g/serving or half a can), but the scale reads a much smaller amount. That there is how much I use as a spread and what I log is not what the scale is telling me.

I always test the products for weeks prior to writing my reviews.

I run a detailing business and finding a good/great cleaning microfiber detergent has always been rough for me. I've tried many brands from CG, and lately I was using rags to riches. But I needed a detergent that would clean as well as restore the the microfiber.

That's where 3D towel Kleen comes in. I've found that 3D is one of the best out of the 10 I've tested to lift stains out of your towels while restoring your towels to it's natural softness. The only thing I do is add a little white vinegar to the load to help with the stains and waxes and sealants. 3D is a very viscous material, which I like, which helps attach itself to the towels in the machine.

In closing, with cost low, cleaning power high this is a detergent I would definitely buy for all of my microfiber.

title: TERRIBLE. NOT a new product.
text: ABSOLUTE WASTE OF MONEY.  TERRIBLE.  I DO NOT believe it was new. Received NOT in packaging, just loose in the box.  I used it once then recharged it and it was totally dead.  This has never happened to me before.  I bought a swivel sweeper more than 10 years ago and used it every day with no problems.  The battery was still good, but the bottom of the dust tray was accidentally thrown away.  I could not order a replacement part because on the sweepers today  the door on the dust compartment remains attached to the unit.  So I bought a new swivel sweeper which I used for several months, again with no problems.  Then the wall charger was lost so I ordered this replacement charger and battery, supposedly new.  It worked only once and then the "NEW"  battery went completely dead.  The battery that came with the new swivel sweeper still works.  When I contacted Amazon I was told that because I had received the replacement 34 days ago, that exceeded the 30 day warranty.  This is the first time in years of dealing with Amazon that they have not stood behind a defective product and allow a seller to sell old defective merchandise as new.  If you ignore this and other similar warnings and take a chance, be sure you use it and recharge it a couple of times as soon as you can so that if it dies you can get your money back within the first 30 days.

text: I absolutely love this wig, I've had it for almost two weeks now. This is my first "real" wig besides one that I got for a costume. It's honestly such a good quality wig that I definitely will be buying again from this company once I have the funds. Some of the complaints I saw before buying this wig was that it gets tangled too easily and it's too thick. My thoughts on that are this: it's a really long, curly wig. My hair was half as long as this and would get tangled all the time. That's just a hair thing, not a wig thing! It's not too hard to brush the tangles out as long as you know how to do it right and start at the ends instead of the roots. As for it being too thick, I don't see how that's a complaint at all, this seems like a positive to me. The lace was a bit dark for my pale skin color but I just dabbed a little bit of concealer on the "scalp" to make it look real. But overall, I'm really satisfied about this buy. text:
I used this for years. It's okay, but you will get tired of the drawbacks and want to just fix the glasses or get new ones.

The Drawbacks:

1. It is a wax, and you can't help but get it on the lenses, not easy to get off and it gets old removing it. You have to be extremely careful during
the day when when wipe off your lenses, touch the bridge of the glasses where this stupid wax is and you glasses are now hopeless fogged
with wax unless you give the a major cleaning. Wax on glass is NOT a good thing as you will soon learn.

2. Over time you realize your glasses slip because of oil from your face. To make this product work well you Must remove
any and all oil and old wax mixed with oil from your nose and glasses, this may be several times a day! Oil on you nose or glasses make this
product useless. I clean my glassed and nose with alcohol every time for best results.

3. Product is useless if you are sweeting in heat!
4. When product gets mixed with the oil from your face it becomes some thing more like Vaseline over the day, worse than nothing.

5. Product is best used for short durations in cool places.

I got sick and tired of having to keep cleaning and applying this stuff and had my glassed professionally modified to fit my face correctly.
Now the arms are spring loaded and pull inward where as before they were at right angles with no inward pull at all! I do not understand why all
glasses are not made this way to begin with. My glasses were fixed by adding a tiny wedge of white plastic in the hinge.

My advice is forget the wax as a solution, it is not a solution, just a short term fix with a lot of hassle. Get the right glasses for your face or get them customized so they fit right, it's worth it! Yes, you can wrap all kinds of crap on the arms of the glasses (part that goes over your ears), but the results are only so so for most people and look rather silly on a nice pair of glasses.

title: It's OK if you don't expect much
text:
I bought three of these after reading everyone's reviews. I figured I could send back if it really was awful, but I live in a super hot place and any little bit could help. My windows are not tinted and I have a lot of window visibility! It's absolutely true that the fans don't work if they are not in direct sun. If your windows are at an angle that won't tip the solar panel to the sun, it won't work. If you park in a spot that isn't directly east or west, it won't work. It won't work mid-day, because the sun isn't directly on the panel. I'm lucky, my windows are at a pretty good angle and my parking area at work is a north/south/east/west set up. I put one fan on the driver side, and one on the passenger side, and the little fans plug away most of the day. They don't create a lot of breeze, they don't "pull" any hot air out of the vehicle, but they do see to move the air around. For me, the difference these two fans make is whether, when I get in my car after work, I can touch my steering wheel with out it being too hot to grip. My air conditioner takes a while to get plugging away and without the fans it's awful, with the fans moving air around most of the day I don't feel suffocated by hot air until the car cools off. So, no the fans aren't great but they can make a difference if the situation is just right.

Also, nothing I read discussed that the fan comes with a rubber thing that fits on the window and takes up the gap between the top of the fan and the window's edge... in theory it should but it doesn't, so you need to drive with air whistling or put the rubber on the window with the fan each day.

I already broke one, I rolled up the window too tight on accident... so I guess you could say they're kinda cheap construction, but that shouldn't be a surprise for the price you pay.

First, I do want to say this is a great butt cushion in general. If you have a hard chair, this will work wonders! It's heavier than you expect but it feels solid and sturdy. If I were rating it for general butt cusion, it would get 5 stars.

That said, I bought this because they said it's unique design could provide support without pressure. I have a broken tailbone and hard chairs are agony to me. I know this isn't exactly a coccyx cushion, but Purple does't offer one of those. So I took the second thickest cushion they offered instead, figuring this would provide ample cushioning for my tailbone. Unfortunately that isn't the case.

It didn't matter how I sat or shifted, by the end of the day my tailbone still ached miserably. I tried it in conjunction with a donut, hoping to just ease the pressure in the one spot. I tried all sorts of variations in an attempt to make it work. TBH I've even thought about cutting out a section, but I'm afraid that would make it useless for anyone.

If you're looking for a good cushion for your bad tailbone, save your money. So far the $10 rubber donut is the best thing I've found. I would return this if I could because there's still too much pressure from the "no pressure" cushion.

title: Your hearing is important, invest in protection!
text:
You can't really appreciate silence until it's gone. A few years working in the live music industry has given me tinnitus, a ceaseless ringing of the ears, caused by long term exposure to THAT BASS. I deal with it well and still work with live music but believe me, if you have the choice, do not get tinnitus. Luckily, you do have the choice! Ear protection like DownBeats are no only affordable and low-profile, but will actually make shows sound better! DownBeats aren't kidding when they say "High Fidelity." I have pretty finely tuned ears and I can say with confidence that this product really does cancel pretty evenly across the spectrum unlike foam earplugs which will leave you wallowing in the bass and missing out on the crisp highs.

So please, do yourself a favor. If you truly love music, protect your ears and buy hearing protection. Silence truly is beautiful.

The brush came as ordered in 48 hours. (good). Sent it down the drain and it was immediately jammed after only 4-6 inches. Tried to pull it out and it was stuck (in spite of the no stick coating). Finally used needle nose pliers to get it moving out, then looked at brush - no dirt, just bent. I was planning to keep it for some other use (pack rat - never throw away a "tool" that might come in handy), but when re-coiling it, the brush fell off in my hands. If this had happened in the pipe, it would have been a disaster. the brush was crushed by the packaging and cheaply made - but "connecting it" to the coil wire seems to have been nothing more than shoving it down the coil and hoping for the best. I strongly advise staying away from this Chinese made product. (Not to say my Chinese Apple iPhone isn't great....just saying this item is very poor quality).

title: All Good...love it! Much better than a regular straight iron!
text:
I didn't receive a discount for the product or any incentive to write this review. The product is heavy duty, not flimsy. The bristles are thick and hard....they are similar to the wet tangle free brushes we buy. Anyway, my child has VERY frizzy super thick, coarse caucasian hair. We usually have to divide it into up to 8 sections and do each section at a time with my straightening iron.
Now if you want board straight hair this may not be for you but I wanted something to straighten frizzy corkscrew curls into smooth hair with a bit of a wave. This only took 5 minutes and I'm sure I could have achieved board straight if I had spent more time. But I am a 40 something work from home mom with no time for a 2 hour get ready routine....it has to work and be fast!
With this brush, I can brush it through each section without using clips and I don't have to worry so much about burning her because the bristles act as a small barrier.
The buttons are positioned well so it doesn't turn off accidentally. Heats quickly, straightens wisps close to forehead. I love it and will recommend to friends! Also, I love having the handle to hold onto...it doesn't get hot so I don't have to worry about my fingers like I do with my regular flat iron!

title: Seems to work good,but....
text:
i wanted to write about this, because i read reviews and maybe a lot of others do,too. This probably applies to all the products made like htis, with the straps you have to pull around and attach (velcro) on the shoulder straps in the front. i felt this would help me, I tend to slouch and my back is tired and aches. I received it yesterday, and took me awhile to figure it out, the directions are simple, but for some reason i thought the adjustment straps went around the waist. looking at the pictures I figured out they go up the shoulder straps in front. Then, i got it on but couldn't reach the straps in the back to pull it tighter. if i were thinner (my chest isn't over 50' it says it fits 50'hest) and did more yoga, i could probably reach the ends of the straps in back. There is no one else here to do it for me. i gave up last night and this morning took2 long strips of material and sewed them tightly to each end of the adjustment straps, (wrapped the thread around the material and strap tightly to hold it ) so i could pull it around and tie it in the front, instead. This worked fine, and as soon as I did it, the pain in my back started to fade. I am giving this 5 stars because it does work, and it looks like the more expensive ones, that work the same way, and it's me, I am not thin and flexible enough to grab the adjustment straps in back and pull them up on the shoulder straps like it's supposed to be used. Even if i got one that came around in the front, instead of on the shoulders, it still might not be easy to grab the straps in the back to pull them around. unless they were very long, like how i fixed this one. They seem like they are made for thin, flexible people, or for someone with help. (you can't put the adjustment straps on before putting it on, it has to open up to get the arms in). other than this, it has possibilities. i'm attempting to lose weight, and maybe when i do, i will be ble to use it the way it's meant to. Though i'm also hoping it will help m back and i won't need it at some point. it does make my back feel better.
[ I am editing this because after awhile how i had the pieces of material to tie around my waist attached to the straps, didn't stay on good. I then made a slip knot in the long strip of fabric, and put the strap of the brace in this, pulling it tight so it closed up on it and wouldn't slip off. On both sides. Now I can get hold of the straps in back of me (the material I attached) and pull them around in front and tie at my waist. As I said, I think a thinner more agile person wouldn't need to do this and could use it the way it is. as i lose weight do yoga,I hope I will be at that point sometime. But it does make my back feel much better and is soft and comfortable to wear]

title: Does what it says but cheapo quality makes it worth no more than $10 - seriously!
text:
Fit and function are great, this knee compression wrap does exactly what they claim. The workmanship (assembled in Taiwan) is pretty good, and in theory, you need this wrap to put the cold therapy just where you need it. Like most of the Active Ice system I bought at the same time, this compression wrap is made using cheapo materials - it is definitely NOT worth $30. I would feel much less ripped off if I'd paid $10 or maybe even $15 - but no more. Someone is making a killing on Polar Products - - top dollar for cheap products.

I'd guess there are about $5 worth of thin foam-backed polyester material, sewn-in velcro hook patches, and three decent elastic bands. Five sewn-in velcro patches attach to the hoop material on the universal chilling bladder that came with your system. The velcro sticks well and the elastic bands look like they will last longer than the cheapo material the body was made from. Overall, the whole thing weighs just a couple of ounces - very light duty. The thin foam/polyester material is exactly the same junk they used in the control box to "insulate" the cold water pipes. (which is still leaking condensation/water through every hole and crack in the control box)

I wore the universal bladder and my new knee compression wrap today for a few hours off and on. I can tell you that if you have fresh staples across your knee, any sensitivity in the knee area, or are easily chafed by rough things against your skin, the stiffness of this compression wrap, bladder, velcro, and elastic will cause you some additional soreness until you're used to it.

Bottom line - I would not buy it again unless they cut the price in half. Yes, it's really that over-priced. Best solution is really just to use the black universal strap with velcro ends to hold your chill bladder in place. If that's not enough, use another Ace bandage. You should be using one under the bladder also, since the bladder can't go against the skin.

title: Definitely not for those of us with chemical/perfume sensitivities!
text: I don't generally don't take the time to write reviews, though I sure enjoy the benefits of those who do (legitimate detailed reviews). Unfortunately, I feel that users like me need a review that details issues like mine with this product. As someone with chemical/fragrance sensitivities, this pet odor remover was far more nauseating than the cat spray/urine odors themselves. It was so horrifically strong that even the next day when I opened my bedroom a good 40 feet from the room I had sprayed the day before, the smell hit me like a tidal wave and will not go away. It has literally made me nauseous and given me a headache. Fortunately we will be out of town for about 3 weeks and I'm just hoping the smell will be gone by then! I'm not entirely sure if it might have gotten rid of any of the cat odors or simply overwhelmed my senses with more odors, as I think I was still getting whiffs of the cat breaking through the terrible perfume smell. A little side note that is far secondary in my review is that it came shrink wrapped and taped like Fort Knox, which was a royal pain to get open, yet it had still leaked a great deal in transit. To be fair, that may have had more to do with the altitude change in shipping, as we are in the Colorado mountains and it's not unusual to receive leaky liquids. All that being said, I'm afraid I'm going to have to go back to the ridiculously expensive Vetoquinol Equalizer Odor Eliminator, which does still have some chemical odor, but it does actually eliminate the pet odor and actually evaporates relatively quickly compared to this without the extremely strong perfume smell.

title: Save your money, save your time, save your sanity. Don't buy this scale.
text:
I received the scale yesterday. It took me hours to set up. Hours I will never get back. I thought it was finally set up, I got on it and saw the dreaded: "Sensing, Step Off, Thinking, ERR"! After some more fiddling nothing changed. I contacted Fitbit support and to their credit they got back to me pretty quickly. Their advice was, shall I say, a little flimsy:

Please make sure of the following:
1. You've removed the batteries for at least 10 seconds, and then reinserted them.
2. Your scale is placed on an even, hard surface such as tile or a hardwood floor.
3. You are standing still on the scale.

Needless to say that didn't work. I emailed again and again, quick response. They reviewed my case and have determined that my scale needs to be replaced. I decided I do not want another scale with a 75% chance that it won't work, and I would be better off with the $110 in my pocket. The scale is on its way back to amazon.com.

What I don't understand is that this issue seems to be prevalent and going on for a long time. Why are they still selling these things when they should be pulling them from the market and figuring out what is wrong with them? Save your money and your time, don't buy it.

title: Pricy but seems to work for me
text:
Update (6/25/2014): After using Yoder's for a few more weeks I have notice my weight has become stable again. I have found a slow decrease in weight which I think is from eating less. I definitely notice I am not always as hungry. I also have found a decreased appetite for sweet and fried foods. More importantly however I have found my blood pressure has dropped significantly. My diastolic (bottom) number measured at 62 this morning. I don't think I have seen that number so low since a physical 20 years ago. I have an appointment with my cardiologist next week and am excited to see how the blood work comes back for comparison.

When considering this product you need to seriously consider Yoder's slogan of "the cure for what ails you." I am not sure I would have given five stars had there not been aging issues I am dealing with in my mid 30's. In fact I am sure I would never buy this again if I didn't see any noticable differences. However, I have noticed a difference and pretty drastically after only four days that I feel the five stars are justified for me. I have tried taking apple cider vinegar from the store however have found a lot of what is out there tends to be labeled as "apple cider flavored vinegar." From what I can find this is nowhere near the same thing as true apple cider vinegar made from apples. I can notice the difference in the taste of Yoder's compared to the Heinz vinegar.

With all that said keep in mind these are the benefits I noticed and will likely not apply to anyone else since we are all unique. Since about 27 I have been diagnosed with hypertension. It may be military service based but it does run in my family and after a couple years of weight loss and testing my doctors were at a loss. As a result I am on lifetime medicine to manage my blood pressure, cholesterol medication (really low good numbers and normal bad), and some really expensive omega 3's to manage triglycerides. Unfortunately the blood pressure medication can affect cholesterol, the cholesterol medication can affect triglycerides, and the triglyceride medication hits the pocket book hard. Some of the other side affects I have encountered of these medications is weight gain even when I tightly monitor my diet and work out. I was running marathons for awhile and still continued to gain significant weight which I can only attribute to either aging or the medication; maybe both combined.

Fast forward eight years and now I am really only four days into trying Yoder's Good Health Recipe. I found my first purchase on a local store shelf so did not buy it from amazon. However here is a recap of my first four days and my experiences so far:

Day 1: A few hours after my first dose I found a pretty significant energy boost. This wasn't expected but definitely a welcome surprise. The initial taste is that tart/sour vinegar taste with some of the spice from the other ingredients mixed in to help smooth it out a little. No other side affects were noted.

Day 2: Unfortunately the high from day 1 had worn off and I was introduced to some pretty minor lows throughout day two. I did have some uncomfortable bowel movements which I can only equate to the onset of a flu. My stomach seemed to be rather upset most of the day and I didn't have much of an appetite. I did eat, but had to start each meal slowly to let my stomach turn around. I also found that I was extremely thirsty for water all the time. In fact I went from drinking about 2 X 34 ounces of water a day to 4-6 X 34 ounces of water a day. Not that I hate water, but it is a little rough wanting to drink water all day long. The 30 minute park and ride to work seemed almost too long to go without water.

Day 3: As a carryover from day 2 I still found I was extremely thirsty for water. Again I went through 5 - 34 ounce bottles today. The bowel movements were still present but not as bad nor as uncomfortable. I did find that I felt tired most of the day but could not seem to fall asleep for a nap when I got home. I also noticed a little more acne than normal.

Day 4: Today seems like maybe a breakthrough day. Although I still see a little more acne than normal it has decreased significantly from yesterday. Seems strange to have happened overnight. I also noticed my weight has dropped three pounds in the last three days. I suspect this may be because of the mix of bowel movements and increased water intake. One side effect of my medication is that it can cause water retention and I think the apple cider vinegar (or maybe one of the other ingredients) is helping to counter that issue. I also notice the bags under my eyes diminishing a bit. This would be one of those aging items I listed at the beginning. The item that truly pushed me to post about Yoder's though is that I just checked by blood pressure this morning. I generally check it every couple days and come in around 130/85 with the lowest in the past two years measuring 120/82. This morning I actually measured at 116/74. This to me is amazing and really what is prompting this post.

I know four days isn't long to try a product, but I am excited to see the changes which to me are significant. It is also nice to know they seem to have come about with a natural remedy rather than additional medications (my doctor has offered to perscribe diaretics for teh weight control which I have turned down). In a perfect world I would love to be able to reduce my medications and replace them with Yoder's. title: A Fine Razor With Issues
text:
The FaTip Gold "Testina Gentile" (Gentle Head) is a mild three-piece razor that provides a close and exceptionally smooth shave. It is well balance with a good grip and an excellent gold-effect finish. Of the razors I have, it is most comparable to the Edwin Jagger DE89L in its overall performance. And it has two pluses: The handle grip is far superior to the slippery DE89L and, best of all, it is made entirely of plated brass, including the head of the razor. Three-piece razors at this price point typically have a head (cap and plate) made of Zamak. Zamak (pot metal) is an inferior material subject to corrosion and breakage.

When I received this razor I wanted to like it, and I do. However, I would only recommend it with a proviso. The razor's cap and plate have loose tolerances, and blade alignment is consequently an issue. If this were a problem unique to only my particular razor, I would send it back. But from what I have since read on a number of forums, this is a characteristic typical of FaTip razors. When inserting a new blade, the user really should check the alignment and manually (and carefully) adjust the alignment of the blade as necessary. This problem is not yet a show stopper for me, but I could understand if others might find it too bothersome. So, despite its excellent shaving performance I can give this razor only three stars.

The EJ DE89L, at a similar cost, is noted for its precise blade alignment.

title: A MIRACLE of RELIEF
text:
I found this to be an excellent product with a loud piercing sound that you could not sleep through. Since I was the only other person in the house, this was ideal when I was either in my own bedroom on the other side of the wall, or downstairs and in another room, or even yet another level further downstairs, in other words this was audible from level 1 to level 3. This alert *is* going to wake up anyone else in the house, in my opinion, unless their door is closed, they are a very heavy sleeper, their bedroom is far away, and maybe even then. Other reviewers have discussed how it is possible to muffle the sound by wrapping it in a towel or something, so it can be muted, but that was the last thing I was interested in.

The battery also lasts an extremely long time, something like a year or more of 24x7 use, and there is a highly visible blinking light to assure you the battery is still working (the light is small, and won't keep anyone awake).

This was some of the best money I've ever spent, allowing me to actually sleep in my own bed with absolute confidence I would be awakened no matter how deeply I was sleeping, and as exhausted as I was, I had begun to sleep very deeply without wanting to.

The instructions are very clear, just put the batteries in, adjust the mat under the sleeper, and hang the device on their doorknob or wherever - the cord beyween the mat and the alarm device was plenty long enough to be convenient. You can place the mat under the other person's shoulders, so that it goes off if their shoulders come off the mat (which is about a yard wide, so just rolling over on top of it will not trigger it), or you can place it under them lower down, around the middle of their ribs, so it is triggered only if they actually sit up. The device is sensitive and works immediately with no dangerous time lag, when pressure contact on the mat is removed. It does not go off if someone just rolls back and forth on it or shifts position. I experimented with the proper placement by lying on top of it myself, and adjusting its location to be under my ribs, so that it would go off when my shoulders got about 8" off the bed, as I was in the process of sitting up. It worked perfectly EVERY TIME.

I did not actually *use* the feature of the magnetic tether for detecting when someone sitting, gets up from a chair, but I did *test* it, and found it unobtrusive and lightweight to the sitting person, and extremely effective.

I said out loud to myself and to others, repeatedly, that this was the best money I'd ever spent in my life. I no longer had to sleep on the floor by the bed so I'd be physically stepped on and awakened, or on the floor in the hallway just outside the open door in the hopes I would hear activity and wake up in time, and no longer did I have to attempt to stay awake all night at the foot of the bed, in an uncomfortable chair, in case something happened.

This product was a miracle of relief to me, I have absolutely NO complaints about it, and only the HIGHEST praise.

It's simple to use, it works brilliantly, there is a reassuring light visible from at least 60 feet away (probably farther) so you know it's on, the light lets you know when the battery finally *does* begin to get weak, but the sound is still very loud and the device still works strongly for WEEKS after the "weak battery" light alert comes on, so there is NO concern about being surprised by it suddenly stopping working. I have nothing but the highest praise - and my very deepest gratitude - for this product.

title: Effective device for lower back pain treatment
text:
Occasionally I have lower back pain. My kinesiologist treats me with a combination of ultrasound and infrared massages which alleviate the pain without recurring to pain killer drugs.
Infrared radiation (IR), sometimes referred to simply as infrared, is a region of the electromagnetic radiation spectrum where wavelengths range from about 700 nanometers (nm) to 1 millimeter (mm).
This device has an array of 63pcs 660nm red lights and 42pcs 850nm invisible infrared lights that can be selected with the controller. Also you can select the intensity (5 levels) of pulse massage.
You can set the timer in 5min increments up to 30 min.
You will experience a pleasant warmth that should alleviate your pain. I am using this with a portable USB power bank as to remain mobile and not be movement restricted by using the enclosed wall power supply.

title: Works but needed help to apply

These pain tapes, impregnated with lidocaine as the active ingredient, do work on various kinds of pain to provide some relief. The tape format, though, was a bit of a challenge for me to use. My pain is shoulder joint pain (caused by either osteoarthritis, carpal tunnel or both). Because the pain is deep within the joint and the area of my shoulder is relatively thick, perhaps application of the tape doesn't work as well as on other areas of the body. I think it would work great for knees, backs, ankles and lower arms but not quite as well for shoulders.

Application is easy on most of the body, but for shoulders, you really need to have someone else apply the tape for you. Doing it with one hand is just about impossible in that area.

With that said, the tapes did provide me with some restful nights either free of pain or with significantly reduced pain.

title: Comfortable, adjustable, useful, and great quality!
text:
This is, simply put, the best finger brace I have ever used. I have hEDS, a genetic condition that gives me very bad joints, so I've got an entire collection of assorted braces and splints, and this one is by far my favorite. I'm very prone to trigger finger, but I mostly get it in my pinkies and less often in my ring fingers, and most splints are designed for index fingers, since that's the "normal" finger to get it on. But this brace is comfortable on any finger with no modification required. It's also very lightweight and comfortable, and the removable second strap is a godsend.

The finger strap is very adjustable, and I am able to comfortably put it around two fingers at once. I have small hands though, so that might not work for everyone. The longer strap is very useful, I wrap it around my palm for stability while awake, and I can wrap it down to my wrist under my thumb at night, to keep the brace from slipping off while I sleep, which beats having to use a bulky hand brace like I did before. I ended up ordering a second one so I could have one for each hand for nights when they are both acting up.

So yes, I would definitely recommend this splint! Comfortable, adjustable, useful, and great quality for the price.

title: Good design and easy to use, but inconsistent and inaccurate readings
text:
I recently purchased this wrist type home automatic digital blood pressure monitor by Shuangjlshan. My husband already uses an upper arm cuff type blood pressure monitor, but I wanted to also have a wrist cuff. The writst cuff is desirable for those who have large bicepts or have an arm injury. This unit comes with a plastic storage case, it does not come with batteries (2 AAA batteries needed), and it is very compact.

Pros for this unit: easy to put on and to use. The display is clear and the hear rate seems to be consisten with other monitors we have

Cons for this unit: The top number is very inconsistent and is extremely high (about 25-30 points higher than our other recently calibrated upper arm blood pressure monitor). The lower number is more consistent but is about 10 points higher than our other monitor. The display screen is pretty small and doesn't look to be of high quality.

Overall, I like the design of this unit and ease of use. I'm not sure if the unit I received is flawed, but the inconsistency of this unit makes it hard to depend on. I had planned to give this unit to a relative, but I will look for something else. I am returning this item.

I was able to purchase this item at a reduced price in exchange for my honest and unbiased review.

title: No Miracles, But Definitely Does Help - Worth It
text:
Great product but the company is going through growing pains and is understaffed. Thus, the wait times for customer service or even updating an order or credit card number are long and frustrating. If you need to do either, I've learned through trial and error that calling them is the only way to get a quick response, but there really should be working options to make these and similar changes on their website... But to make it up to me they also upgraded me to 2-day shipping for free and gave me a nice discount. I'd say that makes it worth it. However, I'm curious how much it'd cost me to make my own Optimind. If I ordered the ingredients in bulk, or even just through a combination of cheaper products that have the same ingredients, I'm sure I could have the same thing for less than half the price, even with the discount. So what you're really paying for it the convenience of the all-in-one Energy and Focus pill.

The product works well for me, better than coffee and with fewer side-effects. Unlike coffee, Optimind (or anything with isolated caffeine) does not have a significant laxative effect. However, the caffine can produce a mild laxative effect for some people, especially those who are sensitive to it. The nootropic compounds won't work miracles, but for me they do seem to have a subtle positive effect on focus and mental clarity. There's varying amounts of research supporting how well they work, but no really strong scientific meta-analyses. I recommend research the individual ingredients with examine.com to learn more.

It's also important to note that we don't know how much of each ingredient (especially the nootropic ones) is present is Optimind. So the amounts they put in might not be enough to really produce a noticible or significant effect. It won't hurt to take them, unless you're alergic or have liver disease, but like I said - alone it won't work miracles either. If you want to strongly feel those effects consider making your own blend or supplementing with more of the nootropic compounds, or other ones.

TL;DR: It won't make you Limitless, but is definitely worth a try.

title: The cord is a swivel cord so I don't have to do the untwist when it gets all twisted up. :)
text:
I have been eyeing this type of hair straightener for a few months now and I am so glad that I finally purchased it because it is a daily use appliance for me!

I have medium length hair. It is somewhat fine but I have a lot of it! It's naturally wavy and even curly in some places. If I cut my hair short I'd have ringlets all over my head! This is the perfect mix for frizzy hair. It is healthy but if I don't style it, it looks horribly damaged. If I straighten my hair 100% it takes me 2 hours with most flat irons. If I do a quick straight it's about an hour. If I blow dry my hair it is a mess!

This brush works wonderfully in my hair. I brush my hair before using it and then slowly brush it through sections of hair. I usually just do a quick style with it, spending no more than 15 minutes on it and it looks great. This takes out the frizz and straightens my hair most of the way leaving a little bit of volume. I don't have to spend a lot of time on it but I can make my hair look great! I use leave in products to protect my hair from the heat and follow up with a leave in serum afterwards on the ends.

This brush is easy to use. It literally just brushes through your hair but you have to be careful around your ears. I learned that the hard way! It has the controls on the side of the handle. You can change the temperature depending on your hair. I don't like the location of the controls because I hit the buttons a lot. Thankfully you have to hold down the power button to turn it off but I change the temperature a lot. It appears to be made quite well. The cord is a swivel cord so I don't have to do the untwist when it gets all twisted up.

I don't think this is good for all hair types and I highly recommend reading reviews from people with your hair type to know if it will work for you. If you have a hard time getting a brush through your hair when it is dry then I definitely don't recommend this for you.

I received a discount for the straightening brush for inspection, testing, and reviewing purposes. My review is based solely on my personal experience with it.

title: Not bulky, perfect for under clothing or sleeping to relieve stiff joints
text:
I received my copper knee sleeve yesterday and immediately put them on. The first item I noticed was how cooling and comforting the sleeves felt. It's hot and humid here now, so the only part of me that actually feels comfortable is where the copper knee sleeves are. (Actually wish they made clothing out of this material - it's more cooling then the cooling towel) As long as I'm wearing the sleeves my knees actually seem to feel better.
The material is 88% copper nylon and 12% Spandex. Very light weight, like wearing a pair of spandex tights. The band areas at the top and bottom of the knee sleeves are thicker - and for anyone who's worn thigh high panty hose, it does have the rubber no-slip tops. Feels wonderful.
I did receive the copper knee sleeves for a free or discounted rate, but the opinions are strictly my own. I would recommend this for people with slight knee pain/irritation/stiffness or twitchy leg syndrome as I find that it does work for me. And I did try using this without using any other joint inflammation/pain vitamins - so would be able to tell the difference between what my normal joint pains are versus the difference in wearing the knee sleeve, because I wanted to see if it worked - and it did for me.

title: Ingenious design, exceedingly well-constructed
text:
SUMMARY: This clipper is a high-end tool. It's solid metal frame and truly beautiful built-in etched metal file are spot on. The unique blade design seems to work perfectly, too. They call it a "Feather Edge," and basically the upper blade is a tiny fraction of a millimeter INSIDE the lower blade. Not sure why, but it is crazy good.

Background: i bought both these Feather Co clippers and the a Kai "Seki-Magoroku", or "Swordsmith" medium clippers. Previously i also owned the Seki "Deluxe" clippers.

IN DETAIL: The Feather Co's Pareda clippers are the most unique, and the most heavyweight as well. The medium size is large, but not as large as this Kai model. The Pareda may be my top choice, though, because they have a patented under-bite on the jaws that create a truly feathered edge to the freshly-cut nail. Looking at it, I am still a bit stymied as to how - and WHY - this works... but it surely does. This means less filing, if any, is needed for a smooth finish. (Although, as it happens, the Pareda also has one of the nicest metal files i have EVER seen, even amongst my metalworking tools!. It is larger than the other brands' and built into the handle rather than the base.)

I have also bought the Kai deluxe medium size clippers , and previously owned the Seki "Deluxe Nail Clippers." the Seki are similar to this model, but they are smaller, more lightweight and have a hard plastic clippings catcher instead of elastomer. The Seki also feature a disappointingly small nail file built into the clippings catcher.

title: I was skeptical, but this really works!
text:
I saw a web ad for this shortly after a dental cleaning visit. As has been the case with recent visits, they were concerned about my gums, measuring many "3s" and some "4s". They said that if I didn't improve my dental hygiene, I was looking at more severe gum problems that might occur. I had also had some recent cavities.

Anyway, I got sucked into one of those 30 minute long Facebook ad videos on this product and I figured, why not run an experiment. So I ordered a set of bottles and faithfully took 2 capsules every day until my next visit, 6 months later. I was careful not to change anything else. Same diet (pretty healthy). Same brushing (once at bedtime). Same flossing (once in a blue moon when something was stuck in my teeth).

My teeth felt great heading to my next cleaning visit, but I was curious to see if anything changed. The hygienist was in shock, and she brought in the dentist to show him how my teeth were suddenly down to all "1s" and "2s". They were both intrigued and asked me what changed.

Since that visit, I went down to just one capsule, every few days. Yesterday I visited again (6 months later from above) and the hygienist didn't even do the usual thing of calling in an assistant and reading out numbers. She scanned over the gums with her probe and reported to the dentist that everything was great.

It's only anecdotal evidence; one experience of one person; it could be a fluke. Nonetheless, I'm here on Amazon buying more supply for me, and because my wife wants to start using them too.

I had pubic symphysis pain at around 5th month of my second pregnancy and my doctor recommended this belt. She said , the support might help ease the pain in walking. The belt is nice but weird. My only complaint is that I fit on the first sets of hooks initially. Once I started growing, the first set was too tight and the second set too loose rendering the belt useless. If you can work with adding your own sets of hooks in between, it would work great!
They could have a velcro. I had read someone's review before buying who suggested sewing a set of hooks and I thought I would do that but I just had so much going on in life, could never get around that. It supports your belly no doubt, just make sure it fits.

title: Product Great - Seller is NOT (AHealthShop)
text:
I realize this is to let others know whether a product is effective or not. Sovereign Silver is, so I gave 5 stars.

However, it is important to let the buyer beware when transactions go awry. I ordered what was clearly listed as a "multi-pack" from A Health Shop, but only received one. I sent the seller a message stating this: "Hello, My order says "multi pack" but I only received one. Thank you." This was the seller's response: "Jamie, That listing was incorrect, unfortunately. Our listing price for that item was for only one of them, since the retail price for one spray bottle is usually $14.99. That wasn't made clear, and I apologize. We have removed ourselves from that listing and created a new one to reflect the $11.99 price for one item. Thanks!"

Hmmm....Ok.

I am a business owner and let's just say that this is not how I would have handled the situation. I am not looking for something for nothing, because I realize that it costs money to run a business, but, if it were me, I would have rectified the problem (their mistake for an erroneously-worded listing) by providing the customer with what they believed they were ordering. Then, since I operate with integrity, would have immediately changed my listing so as not to continue advertising under false pretenses. I have made mistakes in business. I have also, at times, lost money because of those mistakes. However, I always correct the problem for the sake of my reputation and, most importantly, for the sake of my client.
