title: This is a good pill cutter. Do not slam down on it
text: I love the fact that this is transparent so you can see where you are placing the pill. Here's a little trick. If you have a pill that is partially split down the middle sometimes it can be a little tedious getting the split completely even with the blade on the pill cutter. So rather than try to line that up just turn the pillow over and don't use the guideline on the pill at all. Do not slam down on the pill cutter. Just press it firmly and it will do a good job. The reason I say turn it over is because sometimes it takes a while to line up the imprinted division on the pill with the blade and if you don't line it up it will not split the pill in a perfect manner. You have a better chance turning it over completely and splitting it gently

title: Easy to use, works with little to no effort! But watch out for the seams.
text:
This product is great. I have always suffered from extremely dried and cracked feet to the point of bleeding and where I can't walk on my feet without pain. Got these by suggestion of my partner, and was reluctant to try them at first. I used to use petroleum jelly and regular socks, but it was too squishy and messy. Upon buying these, I realized I liked them right off the bat. I hate wearing socks normally, as it makes my feet feel constricted, so having my toes exposed was a great idea for these. All I needed was something for my heels anyways, so it was perfect. The directions said to use a cream/lotion product for heels first then to put the socks on for a few hours or overnight. I chose overnight due to the dryness of my heels. The next morning I woke up, took the socks off and was shocked how smooth (compared to the previous day) they were. I repeated my routine for a week and I kid you not my heels are back to normal. Almost no cracks and they don't feel dry anymore. I also loved the gel like texture for the heels and honestly feels like walking on a cloud.

PROS:
non-constricting feeling (for people who dislike wearing socks)
Gel heels make walking around on them easy and cloud-like feeling
Machine washable and reusable!
Works over time with little to no effort!

CONS:
Watch out for the seams at both ends of the socks. After washing and using a couple weeks the seams start to fray and come apart.

title: Pretty good for the price, some issues.
text:
I bought this same model but with a different online seller.

Positives:

For the price you get a very good neck, butt and back massage, looks very sharp, heat on the lower back works well, you can tell in zero gravity mode that you get a better and more relaxed massage. The techniques mode lets you pinpoint problem areas, especially I like the kneading mode.

Negatives:

3 of the 4 types of 4 massage modes work as expected, the recovery mode has 3 glitches in the program where the shiatsu rollers only go up 1 side of my back, very uncomfortable, won't be using that mode again (I'm not going to pay $300 to send it back for repairs, I'll live with it, plus the other 3 modes are plenty.)

This thing beats up my upper back pelvic bone like I owe it money. I either have to arch my lower back when the rollers get close or put a thick towel in that area, unless you have extra padding naturally in that area be warned of possible bruising.

The arms and calves are just airbags that squeeze, feels nice but not really a massage. The foot massage is very good but like the arms and calves only activates sporadically through the cycle and even in manual mode (maybe I'm missing something, the directions are pretty useless).

The head cushion is pretty useless during a massage for anyone over 5'10" or so because it covers up a large part of the massage area, so I always throw it back over the back of the chair before starting, then put it back when done because it makes the chair look nicer.

Overall for the price I like it despite the problems described.

title: Excellent, sturdy tool for trigger point muscle tightness
text:
My back is always giving me grief. Whether it's knots between my shoulder blades from an injury-related scoliosis, or spasms in my lumbar vertebrae, I can count on having to deal with some kind of musculoskeletal back problem throughout the year.

I have resorted to all kinds of DIY self-torture to release knots. I've chewed ibuprofen like candy. I've rutted up against a door frame like a brown bear in the forest. I've even used a hammer to try and blindly pound knots into submission. Nothing really hit the spot in that "ahhhhh" way.

About a year ago a colleague mentioned muscle trigger points and how these goofy looking plastic hooks are great for releasing muscle tension. I did not believe it for a second, but she had a side business as a therapist and literally pulled one of these out of her trunk to show me. She showed me how to torque the hook over my shoulder and not to massage, but to press the knob on the tenderest, angriest spot of my muscle spasm (which it reached comfortably), and PULL. HARD. I saw stars. I saw liquid time flowing before my unshielded eyes. My brain slipped into a cool ether as phosphorescent nerves fired in beautiful agony, radiating the music of neurons from the hot core of taught muscle fibers beneath my shoulder blade. I knew no language. My reptile brain basked in the sun of suns. And at last, after eons of sorrow and wailing saints had slithered through the coils of my subconscious (which I guess took like 60 seconds), I eased up on the hook. I remembered my life. But the nagging ache was fading,ebbing like the rusty smear of a setting sun. Relief was a warm, drunken syrup drizzling down my spine. I felt a lightness, and a real release that no craftsman hammer ever provided. And it stayed.

I keep a MuscleHook behind the couch and use it whenever my back is even a little cranky. Nothing has ever hit the sweet spot like this tool. My lovely wife cannot, despite her best efforts, muster the raw brute force needed to beat my muscle knots in to submission, and now she is saved from the frustration of having to root out these issues with the muffled directions of her floor-prone husband: "higher...to the left...no, back...nnng...down...harder please....no- back the other way....left....", etc. are things of the past.

I'm not claiming this is a cure-all and I'm not giving medical advice here, but I am saying that this tool has so far been better for mitigating my back muscle issues than anything else I've tried at home, including:

- Hammers
- Door Frames
- Electric massage wands
- Foam rollers
- Stretching
- Contorted twisting and grunting
- Ibuprofen
- Ibubrofen with muscle relaxant
- Laying on tennis balls

This is a sturdily designed tool. It holds its shape and is tough enough to absorb the force of being wrenched, pulled, pressed, and twisted without giving. Worth every penny.

title: Lorre's Minor Masterpiece Is Finally Given A First Class Release.
text:
I first saw FACE BEHIND THE MASK on TV when I was 10 years old. That was back in 1963. The print wasn't very good even for that time and it was billed as a horror movie which it wasn't but still, even at that young age, I was moved by Peter Lorre's acting and the plight of his character. He plays a Hungarian immigrant, newly arrived in America, whose face is disfigured in a hotel fire. Although he possesses many skills, no one will hire him. On the verge of suicide he is rescued by a sickly thief (George E. Stone) and embarks on a life of crime until he meets a blind girl (Evelyn Keyes). He then tries to change his ways but Fate has other plans.

What makes this little 1941 film so remarkable is that it was shot in less than 2 weeks for around $100,000 and was planned as a B movie all the way. Based on a radio play, the screenplay was tailored specifically for Peter Lorre. who, although he disliked the script, gave a wonderful performance. The movie was directed by the undervalued French born director Robert Florey who had worked with Bela Lugosi on MURDERS IN THE RUE MORGUE (1932) and would work with Lorre again on THE BEAST WITH FIVE FINGERS (1946). Like the best B movie directors, Florey knew how to use lighting and camerawork to enhance his projects.

For all of its video life up until now, FACE has existed only in substandard public domain copies with poor sound and even poorer visual quality. I had a Region 2 VHS copy for years. It was all that was available for the longest time. The currently available download/streaming copies are just as bad. Sony Pictures, who own the Columbia Pictures library, have never released this one to home video. This Blu-Ray was issued by Imprint who specialize in collector's editions. It comes with two short features by film historians Alan K. Rode and Kim Newman plus a commentary track by Rode.

We brought this pack along with us on our 4 week around the world trip. We had all our stuff in just a carry-on sized backpack, so washing clothes in each city was required. We'd use a few sheets per sink load, and sometimes we'd also add some body wash that the hotel provided. I think we could have probably gotten away with only using the hotel body wash, but a few hotels didn't provide it so in those times it was handy.

The most important thing to remember is to have dry hands when you're removing sheets from the pack. If your fingers are wet you'll ruin the whole pack, so if your fingers are wet have someone else remove sheets from the pack.

Pros:
-Small, takes up minimal space in your bag
-Works fairly well when using several sheets per load

Cons:
-Fingers need to be absolutely dry to remove sheets

Turns out it works FAR better than alcohol, although I'm pretty sure the ingredients of the first bottle are just alcohol and d-limonene (orange oil), which makes sense because d-limonene is a fantastic and safe cleaner.  With the first bottle, you just put a few drops on the surface, wait about 30 seconds, and wipe the old thermal paste off.  This stuff eats the thermal paste away so there's really no scrubbing.  I do this twice just to make sure everything is off, but that's just me.  It's somewhat expensive, but it does work really well, although next time I need to clean a heatsink and CPU I'm going to mix some d-limonene in with some alcohol and see if it works the same. I disassembled the lamp to check whether I missed some thing. To my surprise, I found the brown wire from the base was out of the connector! I took a photo which you can see here:

http://ecx.images-amazon.com/images/I/51pMExPDRRL.jpg

I contacted their costumer service. The following is part of the conversation:

"""
Me: after i assembled it, i found the high power switch didn't work
Me: but the low power switch did work
Peggy: all right, do you have your order number? It sounds like the ballast, and I would be happy to exchange the lamp for you. I can send you a pre-paid label to return the defective unit to us and send you a new one.
.....
Me: you know what would happen if the wire touch the metal frame ... you put my life into risk just because of your poor quality control
Peggy: No, it would be fine, the wire is not connected to anything and wouldn't make a circuit. Thats why the lamp doesn't work.
Me: my body will be part the the circuit
Peggy: The wire was not connected to a power source.
Me: what if the red one were out?
Peggy: That would be the same thing. Thank you, I'll send the label asap.
"""

I know that they are doing their best to exchange the lamp for me. But personally I don't trust their quality control anymore.

I won't comment more. You can decide whether to buy it or not.

title: Not ready yet--consistent only in its inaccuracy
text:
Very sad to say I will be returning this. I bought a fitbit Charge HR previously and LOVE the product, and so I had thought that it made sense to purchase an Aria to complement and automatically track my weight and body fat. Despite having some hesitation based on the reviews here, I thought my experience might be different and so went ahead with the purchase (such a millennial). At first I was very pleased, as set-up was easy and the Aria easily connected with my WiFi network (**see note at the bottom as I did have some set up troubles independent of the scale itself). After setting up, I invited the other users who would be using the scale and it automatically detected them once they started using it.

After three weeks of use, i can confirm a few things: First, the readings are wildly inaccurate, even after the first few days of "break-in use". I followed all recommendations (storing flat, not moving the scale in between uses, measuring at the same time every day, etc, etc). The weight readings alone vary with each use (+/- 3 pounds on average). Literally stepping on the scale, taking a reading, stepping off, and repeating would yield large swings in weight, with NO OTHER CHANGES. Same was true with bodyfat %--swings of up to +/- 2% during the same measurement window. Now, I understand that body fat readings can vary with water weight, etc, but to have your actual measured weight vary that much on a digital scale is just unacceptable. Seriously, how did fitibit not get this right on a $120 scale? That's its basic, basic function. $15 scales from Target are more accurate.

Aside from inconsistent readings, the scale would also incorrectly categorize user readings. There are only 2 people using my scale--myself and my gf, and there are 50+ lbs separating us. On multiple occasions, I would get a notification on my phone from fitbit saying "congratulations on losing 50 lbs!". Fortunately it is easy to open the fitbit app, delete/re-categorize the inaccurate readings and have it resync, but the fact it would assume that I had lost 50 lbs in a day was frustrating. Note that when it miscategorized the user, it would then default into a mode where you would have to manually select the user for each use (until the readings were deleted), which again was frustrating.

The only things I can save to the positive are that 1) it had no problem connecting to my wifi; 2) the wifi range seems to be good (it was ~20 feet away from my router through a kitchen); 3) battery use is minimal; 4) the sync worked well, and 5) the integration with the fitbit app was nice.

Sadly, I cannot recommend this product and will be returning mine.

**Note on setup: Overall set up was relatively easy, but there is a problem with the user account set up for the Aria. Clearly, they have not integrated the back-ends. The issue is that I had set up my fitibit account with my facebook account, but when I tried to set up the Aria it asks for a fitbit username and password. Since I had used my fb account, I didn't have either, but obvi wanted to keep my prior data. I had to log on to the fitibit website using a computer, reset the password, create a new password, and then go through the Aria set up process again. This was additionally frustrating.

With the standard FF band, which is made of more rigid material, it can't absorb twisting motions as well and its clasp pops loose suddenly, thereby jeopardizing the FF to sudden loss. I've purposely put more stress on this WoCase band, twisted my wrist around in odd angles to see how easily it might release. All indications are that this will remain closed and secure better and therefore I shouldn't loose my second FF by a sudden release of the clasp which is what happened to my first FF and my first $100. I'm getting a little older. I've noticed my BP slowly going up. I hate pharmaceuticals. So with research I thought I would try the Hawthorn Berries supplement.

Now, I'm NO GENIUS but I have a few questions...
With 3 ingredients listed what EXACTLY are the carcinogens?
Better yet...WHY IN THE HECK ARE YOU ALLOWED TO SELL THIS?
If you know something in your product causes cancer why in the H*** wouldn't you remove them from the product & process????

Moral to the story; be aware of what you're putting into your body. ESPECIALLY with supplements that are NOT regulated by the FDA. Say what you will about the "system" but they did remove red die #40 which was also a carcinogen.

Frankly, I'm afraid to even try it. Are all the other companies doing the same? I feel like I wasted my money & time.

title: Outstanding edition of Heinlein's life's work!
text:
I first became acquainted with Robert A. Heinlein in 1956 with _Time for the Stars_. I had just turned 8, when my grandfather, who was a book buyer for A.C. McClurg, a publisher and then wholesaler, handed me the galley proofs. He said, "I want your opinion. I'm not a kid, and you are." From then through _Have Space Suit--Will Travel_, I got to read Heinlein's books from the galleys before they were published. Followed by an intensive Q-and-A with my grandfather, of course.

Since then, I've sought out and read all book-published Heinlein in paperbacks. I've probably bought everything twice: some books I lent and never got back, some got lost in moves, and some I read and reread to destruction. If you translate old dollars to 2014 dollars, I've easily spent more on paperbacks than I did for this set. And I've never had a lot of the short fiction, the letters, the screenplays, and the non-fiction. And all in authoritative versions, capably edited by the late Bill Patterson. By the way, the total shipping weight was 140 pounds.

What an utterly magnificent set this is! It is exactly as advertised, printed on excellent off-white book paper stock and stoutly bound with good, pebbly leather. Now I won't wear out paperbacks. And, no, you can't borrow any of my Virginia Edition volumes.

title: Okay, but old stock?
text:
I ordered 2lb of this powder in July 2014. Three weeks after it arrived I started using it and noticed that it didn't have a distinctive beet aroma. It didn't smell or taste bad, but it smelled different to the other beet powders I've tried. I then noticed that both bags were marked "RBF3-13A", which I guessed was a date code meaning Red Bunny Farms, March 2013. If that was correct then the date code was 16 months older than my order date, which could have accounted for the lack of a distinctive beet aroma.

Anyway, I provided feedback to Red Bunny Farms in August 2014 with the following question:

"The Lot Number on both 1lb packs I received three weeks ago is RBF3-13A. Does that mean they were packed in March 2013?"

That was nearly two months ago and they still haven't responded to the question, so I'm left with the assumption that the beet powder I received was over a year old.

To be clear, I still used the powder and apart from the lack of aroma it seems fine, and the price was good. However, I'm only giving it three stars because Red Bunny Farms appears to have shipped quite old stock, and they failed to respond to my question.

title: They do okay but aren't as good as the OEM
text:
I've shaved with these blades and heads several times. They are better than my really, really old ones, but they aren't up to the performance of the OEM blades. It just takes more passes to get the same shaving performance. The blades do fit the razor fine and don't cause any issues. I'm just not satisfied with the shaving performance.

Also, these would be better if they came with the plastic locks that hold the blades in place in the razor. One of the plastic locks I have is slightly deformed. Other replacement blades I've ordered have come with these circular plastic locks, but this set doesn't, even when ordered with the heads. It doesn't say it comes with it so it's no surprise, but from a practical perspective, it would make sense to replace these at the same time and include them with the full set that includes the heads.

At the time of this writing, these were significantly cheaper than the OEM blades. If you're willing to spend extra time to shave in exchange for a lower price, these might be a good option for you. In my opinion, the price difference spread over the number of shaves that will take longer, isn't worth the time/money trade-off.

text:
The Good: The fabric (excluding the scratchy/irritating tag at the top/front) was comfortable and soft. It provided nice warmth to the knee.
The Bad: Even though it did not feel uncomfortable initially, the device caused my lower limb to swell enormously.

I am an RN with orthopedic experience. I initially bought this to wear under a hinged brace I was wearing following a torn MCL from a ski injury. I felt the extra layer of warmth and support would be nice as well as adding a layer of protection from irritation from the hinged brace while working 12-14 hour shifts. The VIVE support sleeve felt firm but comfortable, warm, and soft (except for the awful scratchy tag at the top which I removed right away). I was very pleased until I got home and took off my scrubs to find a big, edematous balloon disguised as my leg. I don't have circulation issues, so I was a little freaked out.
Thinking I may still have too much swelling to the actual MCL injury and knee to use the VIVE support, I decided to put it in the drawer for a couple weeks and use one of my mom's TED hose instead, which worked very nicely. A couple of weeks later, I tried it again. Same results.
This support device may be suitable to use for short durations to aid some brief activity like a walk or a jog, but I needed it for marathon days at work on a busy medical/surgical unit, and it did not work well for me.

title: Well, maybe 4.5 stars...  good slim bmx seat w/ a bit of padding (not much)
text: I got this for a Redline MX24, which comes with a VERY light/slim hard plastic seat.  I wanted a bmx seat with a bit more size & padding.  This one was a decent price, and looked like it would fit bike's looks (it is the light blue MX24).  Initially, I was a bit concerned out of the box because the padding is very minimal, and it is not much larger than the original seat.  However, it fits the bike very well and is significantly more comfortable than the original seat.  Redline has a fat padded bmx seat, called the "Chubby" or something like that...just too big / too much padding.  However, it seems hard to find anything between those types of seats that are too big / too much padding, and these that are small with minimal padding.  While I might have preferred something a bit bigger and a bit more padding, I don't think that is the fault of this manufacturer, just personal preference, so I would not mark them off for that.  My suggestion of 4.5 stars is the lack of any directions.  There is a bolt down the middle of the seat you access through the top middle of the seat, and here there is a slit through the material at that point.  But it was not cut.  I was frankly concerned I might permanently mess it up just by jamming the wrench through there till it tore, and wondering if there might be some other solution like a way to remove the padding first to attach the plastic.  Near as I can tell, you are actually supposed to just shove the wrench through the slit, tearing it open as needed (or maybe get a slimmer tool like exacto first).  I don't think it said anywhere what size allen wrench to use, and I only knew what size because the bolt I removed from the old seat was exposed / easy to see.  If both seats had this sort of "slit" in the covering, I might have had to try trial & error.  A tiny bit of instruction would have saved me a few minutes of confusion / stress in attaching this.  Anyway, that's a minor issue.

title: Simple and effective deep tissue release
text: The last few years I’ve experimented with different myofascial release tools for tension and pain reduction. The SOMA  hard muscle roller is a winner for getting to hard to reach and deep spots in the back, hips and thighs effectively and quickly.  The dual rubber rollers are small and firm so can reach those tight spots, and they are adjustable.  I have been teaching Pilates for several years and all of my clients, and myself, have muscle tension in some part of our bodies.  Using the SOMA tools, like the SOMA muscle roller, before a workout helps relax the tension and allow us to move more freely and fully. I find that I can get a more effective and faster release on the upper leg (side, back and front) using the muscle roller than with a large foam roller or a ball.  The last few years, I’ve experienced back tightness and pain intermittently.  I’ve found the SOMA muscle roller to be very effective in helping me find and release the tight spots when I am lying on the floor and the roller is under my back.  My back felt relaxed and free feeling after using the muscle rollers for only a week.  Sometimes, I’ll use two muscle rollers under my back, one above the other. I have the slightly softer  SOMA muscle roller too (the orange one).  When using the rollers under the back, I lie on the floor with knees up and feet on the floor.  I start with the rollers under the low back, then move up the back.  First, I lie still over the rollers, then allow the torso to rock slightly forward and back and side to side, with pelvis down and then lifted slightly.  Sometimes I place the SOMA small foam roller under my head for support.  If I rock my torso forward and back, the head rocks on the foam roller and the neck gets a release too.  When I get to the upper back, I like to use both muscle rollers together, without head support, so that the exercise allows for both myofascial release and thoracic (upper back) extension.

I got this foot warmer to use as part of my foot care routine.

The foot warmer is a really pretty blue color and made out of really soft, velvety material. It has 6 heat levels, and 1/4/8 hour timers.

Level 5 feels very comfortable to me, and 6 is bearable, but a bit too hot.

I did notice that the heat seems to be the strongest in the middle, so be careful not to burn yourself. (I don't know if the wires are mostly there or some have shifted, etc, but it felt a good bit hotter.)

Every morning and every night (and sometimes in between), I slather lotion on my feet, put on plastic booties (disposable paraffin wax liners), and wear that for anywhere between 1 and 4-5 hours.

If I could stand to wear socks (which I sometimes suffer through, but I prefer not to), the added warmth would up my foot game. Instead, this foot warmer is taking me to a whole nother level.

I slather my feet with lotion, put on plastic booties, then stick my feet in this foot warmer for as long as possible (at least 2-4 hours). The warmth helps open up my pores and absorb the foot cream better.

I would recommend this foot warmer to anyone shopping for one, I don't think you'll regret it.

I am reviewing Glucosol here--it's pictured correctly as I leave this review and it's what you will get if you order this product. "Glucotrim" is not on the labeling.

I have been a borderline diabetic for years even while exercising regularly. When my blood sugar exceeded 125 and I broke out in a sweat after a meal, I knew things were changing. For two years I controlled my sugar level through diet and exercise. I measured my blood sugar regularly and mostly remained in a normal range. I started looking for herbs (and spices like cinnamon) that might also assist me. I came to Glucosol through reading articles on a diabetes board on lagerstroemia speciosa. Some users found that it helped mediate daytime blood sugar. I ordered a three month supply and measured my results. Simply put, I found no reaction in my overall blood glucose--certainly no discernible decrease that I'd relate to this product. But Glucsol also seemed benign--no negative reactions such a jitteriness, acid-reflux-like effects (took too much cinnamon for my digestion and paid...), or the like. I would sincerely have loved to have reported that it decreased my blood glucose by 5% or more, let alone possibly act like an herbal Glucophage. It did not.

title: Stable, but rust-prone.
text:
I use this stool to sit on whenever I take a shower. It is stable and doesn't tip at all. (That's why I wanted a four-legged stool instead of a three-legged stool; more stability.) My shower is extremely narrow, but this stool fits very well and leaves me enough room for a footstool I use to keep my feet out of the water. I like the choice of colors.

My only disappointment with this stool is that rust has formed underneath. I was hoping that by buying this product, I wouldn't have to deal with either rust or mold/mildew (I've learned that the hard way from using other healthcare bath seat products with many crevices that are impossible to clean and keep mold-free.) When the stool is tipped as I or my caregiver move it from one place to another, water leaks out from inside, and the water looks muddy due to the rust.

UPDATE 5/4/16
When I tipped the stool a bit while carrying it last night, black and rusty water spilled out. I quickly managed to get the stool into the tub and tipped out the rest of the watery contents which had collected in there for ???? long? (See picture.) It was kinda gross. So now I'm on the search for a rust-proof but easy to clean shower stool. It's really too bad that this rusts, as I've enjoyed it so much in the shower and must use a stool every time I shower due to a physical disability.

So if you just want a fun-looking stool that you never plan to get wet and only use indoors, this may be a good item for you.
If you're planning to use it in the shower, AVOID this one!

title: Works good when you figure out which setting you need.
text:
[[VIDEOID:2d4a267b18fcff6219c0df9e24562b80]] So at first I had no luck getting this thing to do much of anything with my eyelashes. It would warm up, and it didn't feel bad on my eyes (heat wise), however I wasn't getting any curl action; I even tried after applying mascara while it was a bit wet to see if that would help with the shaping and still nothing. Then I read the instructions (lol) and realized there was a higher heat setting and that fixed the problem. My stubborn lashes need more heat and thankfully the high setting on this was enough to get them to behave.

I was a bit nervous about having a heating tool on my lash line but there actually was never a point where it felt like I was going to burn myself and I know I was right at the lid at many points while testing this. I love that this is USB C chargeable, no specialty or outdated charging cables needed. It also will auto shut off after about 5 minutes so you can rest easy if you forget it on.

The ad does say this device has 4 heat settings which is inaccurate, it only has 2 (high=blue, low=green) - not sure if that's a misprint or an older model. The only real negative I can give the curlers is that the silicone/rubber bumper is not changeable so if it gets to where you feel you need to change it out you'll have to buy a whole new curler. All in all though I would recommend.

title: Tastes bad but is nicer to take than more pills.
text:
Got this for my dad who is struggling with split/cracking nails and general aging issues. He already takes a ton of pills for age related stuff so we though this would be a nice break from having to add more pills to his load already however his first reaction to taking a dropper full was a horrified face and an 'It taste like poo.' So not a fan of the flavor. The liquid does have some 'floaties' however based on the color and appearance I believe that is just the collagen as it does look like a powdered collagen supplement.

The bottle itself is a bit misleading at first glance with the claim of 15,000 mcg per serving however in reality its 5000 mcg of Biotin and 10,000 mcg (10 mg) of Collagen Peptide which is honestly a just average and actually less Biotin than he had been on previously with the extra strength pills. I wish the dropper actually had a 'fill' line as 'dropperful' is a bit subjective. We haven't notice a difference yet however we are still early on in the bottle and will update the rating if needed.

title: Weird handle, but they get the job done
text:
I have owned these brushes for four months now, and they are great! I use this brush on a weekly basis to clean my flower vase and taller water bottles. The bristles stand up to the abuse I put them through. I am still using the first brush that comes with this set, so it’s safe to say that one brush will last you more than four months.

PROS: stiff, long bristles maintain shape and get the hard-to-reach-crannies, delivers the necessary scrubbing power, metal rod shows no sign of rusting (yet), doesn’t hold onto food smells, dries quickly, and no discoloration of the bristles.

CONS: handle is hard to get a comfy grip on (not ergonomic), brushes have a strong plastic smell when new, and it’s awkward to store since bristles are so long.

Over all, I like these brushes and would recommend them if you’re looking for a cheap and effective bottle cleaning brush and don’t mind a skinny, flat, weird handle.

title: Be-aware of the side effects before you buy
text:
After reading lot of positive reviews and blogs, i thought this supplement would help me to solve my hair loss problem. I dont have any other health issues except this hair loss problem. Doctors said, it is hereditary. But wanted to give a try with this tablet.
I started to take the tablets as prescribed. But after taking it for about a week i started to feel so drowsy, sometimes it pushed me to sleep while i work itself. It made to feel so tired, and I always felt some kind pressure on my head. I thought these sudden changes could be because of something else. But i later realized i get these weird tiredness whenever i take this tablet only. I usually take minimum 3 liters of water per day and i always keep myself hydrated, and thats my habit. But even then i felt so tired and tight pressure on my head.
Later i came to know that this tablet is having high dosage of Vitamin A, and whatever changes i got are nothing but the symptoms of hypervitaminosis A. I stopped taking this tablet and i feel fine now, no sleepiness and i feel active at work as well.
I am glad if this tablet works fine for others without any side effects. But whomever consider to buy this tablet kindly do a small research on it and its possible side effects.

title: Complex
text:
I thought I’d be able to read the manual, then later use this thing. Nope. Had to bring the manual into the bathroom with me (actually, a blown-up copy of it) and keep referring to it. I’ve never used a water pick before, so maybe this is normal.

Anyway, I filled the tank as instructed. Then shot water all over the bathroom because I accidentally hit the power button while closing the water tank. And it took a while to turn off, because there is no intuitive way to tell the “M” button from the power button. No symbols. Not even an M. I got it by trial and error because that was faster than trying to read the manual while water was squirting everywhere.

I will say, once I got it working, it did seem to clean my teeth and gums well, but most of those settings are way too strong. Cue splashing water everywhere again, this time ricocheting off my teeth!

So, now I’ve basically had a shower, too. At least my shirt is drenched, as were my mirrors. Well, the mirrors needed a cleaning anyway because of the toothbrush (which I'd tried earlier) which vibrated toothpaste and water everywhere. I have another electric toothbrush, and have never had that problem before.

The brush heads for the toothbrush are rather small. I’ll stick to my previous toothbrush.

Maybe with practice I’ll get better at the water pick itself. I wish there were more information about the various modes, especially the intriguingly-named DIY mode.

text:
Updated review: had this for 4 months and I love it!

1) The sound it makes when powering on/off is loud and cannot be disabled. I’d planned to use this in our nursery, but this feature will likely wake the baby.

2) The light does NOT stay dimmed (or at whatever level you want it at) when you power the device on/off despite the fact that the manual says it does. I have to reset the brightness whenever I turn on the power. This creates a problem when I don’t want to stimulate or wake my baby for nighttime feedings as it automatically goes to the brightest setting when turned on.
The ONLY way to keep the brightness at the level you want is to keep the device turned on while separately turning the light on/off. This actually goes against what the manual advises. The manual says to power off the device when it’s not in use. I cannot do this without readjusting the light dimmer every time.

**4month update**
I was able to bypass the above issues by pausing the machine versus powering it on and off. I basically keep it paused whenever it’s not in use.

text:
I bought these to keep in my car because still, after all these months, I sometimes forget to grab a mask on the way out of the house. I wanted something cotton and soft, and these are. The workmanship is not superb but really, these masks are adequate and are comfortable. They are so thin that I had to check that there are actually 2 layers; there are. Not the best protection (no way to add extra layer or filter) but good to have in a pinch.

I washed these in the washer and air-dried them and they fit my adult woman probably average sized face fine. The1st mask in the photo shows what it looks like after air-drying. After wearing one of the masks for several hours (3rd mask is an example - as you can see, it stretched some after wearing), I washed it and dried it in the dryer (2nd mask). I wouldn't advise this. It shrank a lot. I put it on and it strained to fit my face, pulled on my ears. It will probably stretch out more if I wear it a bit but it's just much easier to air dry them in the future. These are inexpensive and comfortable and I would buy them again.

title: Solid and Reliable!
text:
We have used this for just over a season and have run more than 300 birds through. We have run the Cornish Cross as well as the Rangers and the KEY - to this or ANY plucker working effectively, IS the SCALD. ( more on that in a moment )

The company provides information on the product and you can look up the videos they have on unpacking, and setting up. You can choose to remove the protective plastic, or leave it on. I am fine with this level of instruction - as I have used the web to find most of our information on the various aspects of raising, cleaning and why we should be eating our own birds. =)

The Good -
Shipped and arrived faster than expected, and without damage.
Heavy duty construction seems durable, and after 1yr+ is still running like new
Worked as advertised
The Not So Good -
Switch is "encased" to be water proof, and the combined effect of a HEAVY DUTY switch and the water tight enclosure make it difficult to get it switched on and stay on. Requires a little practice, and wearing gloves for scalding make this more difficult. Good news is - that it is heavy duty and waterproof...
You need to be "Quick" on the water sprayer when you turn it on. So ONE person doing the scalding and operating of this machine is coordinating the chicken, off/on switch, and the hose. You can PURCHASE upgraded models that have sprayers built in, and for the money, to some it might be worth it.

I am giving this 5 stars because the value of what we paid, and the claims of what it can do are met or exceeded in all cases. The negatives I mention are necessary in my opinion to be offered at this price point and meet safety and reliability.

*SCALD*
In all cases I can trace back to "SCALDING" as being responsible for damage to our chickens when plucking. When we started using this, we used a flame and a thermometer, and had issues. The WIDE variance in temperature made it clear to me that SCALDING was responsible for the results through the plucker and not the plucker itself. When temps were right, for the entire scald - the pluck was perfect.

As we progressed through the year and into this year - we improved our scalding until we now have a 2 degree variance and run Reds slightly warmer than Crosses. Knowing that In Either case, use lots of flushing water during the pluck to wash away feathers and cool the bird. If the scald was correct, the feathers were released and the machine does the job of removing them and expelling them efficiently.

LAST IMPORTANT NOTE - Rinse and Clean this machine well after use. Feathers biodegrade, but not without their own stench. There are fingers pointed DOWN to expel feathers and stuff, but it will not get EVERYTHING. As with all your stuff, take care of it, and I would expect this to take care of you for as many years as you need!

title: Genuinely Fantastic; coming from me, that says a lot.
text:
We all have smelled them - those horribly stinky
, nasty air freshening [sic - as in sick smelling] agents that do far more vile olfactory offense than any odor they could’ve possibly been trying to cover up. This is not one of those. Quite the opposite.
I had forgotten actually that we had put one of these in our car, a car that routinely hauls our two big, outdoors loving dogs with all the - um - scents as evidence of the trouble they’ve been up to that day. Throw in a smoking husband, and, well... ..so I get in the car and drive the 20 miles to the nearest grocery store and just before I get out of the car I notice it. Cologne, just a hint of it. Smells good. I wonder to myself what new cologne he has bought, wanting some myself. Kid you not. Did my shopping, got back in the car and smelled it more clearly this time, unmistakably masculine, clean. It had to be cologne; it was that same light tinge of change in smell that you would get from something clean and fresh. Think rubbing alcohol - you catch a whiff and it carries with you for the moment but is light and clean enough that it does t smell sticky or nasty. Just what is this cologne I wonder again to myself. Right about then I realized I should plug my phone in and look down to grab my lightning cord, and then I see it. The new Glade car air freshener, plugged in to the car’s lighter assembly.
Needless to say I am a now a big fan. And you will be too, as soon as you listen to me and go click on this scent - the New Car smell - and nab the device that diffuses the smell. Ordered us a cigarette lighter adapter that gives you two USB ports and replicates the lighter port for use with the diffuser, about $9-10 here on Amazon. Recommend one of those if you charge your phone in the car (who doesn’t) and can’t afford to lose your charger.

title: A++
text:
This is a 5 Star Review:

How I determine a rating for my reviews

***** (5) Stars = I LOVE this item. This item arrived just as described in the listing. All items were in the package and it worked as the listing is stated with all working parts and fit the description perfectly. The instructinos were on par and I would rate the item A+++

**** (4) Stars = The items arrived almost as described but maybe didn't include an item that doesn't affect the way the items works or it's appearance. It's a little off from the website description. Maybe the color is off or not exact or directions aren't perfect.

*** (3) Stars - The item is not quite what was described and may vary in the color, style, or description of the item which may cause the item to function or look different than what was described in the listing. It may or may not work as I had intended, parts are missing, directions aren't complete or clear, or item is a little off. I would likely keep the item but may not re-order in the future.

** (2) Stars - The item is somewhat similar to the item described in the listing however it does not function or act like the items listing and/or major parts are missing or not functioning properly. Instructions may be missing or confusing to the point that makes the item unusable. I would most likely not keep the item or re-order this item in the future.

* (1) Star - The item is nothing like the description, or is not the item ordered. The item does not function or act like the item that was listed and I would never re-order the item. This item is a complete waste of my time.

Thank you!

title: Did not work well for me, I do not recommend.
text:
I used the product per the instructions as best I could. I first vacuumed the carpet. Then, working in 6x6 sections, I sprayed their pre-mist then used the sifter to dust the product over the area. I brushed it into the carpet. I let it stand for an hour and vacuumed. Most stains did not come up.

As far as the step to brush the product into the carpet, they tell you two options. One is to use their orbiter with their carpet brush attachment to brush the product into the carpet. To me, it seemed that this wasn't the best method for brushing the product into the carpet as the orbital is very powerful and it seemed to more scatter the product than brush it into the carpet. And I wasn't satisfied with how the sections I did that way came out. So, I actually went to my Oreck store and bought their hand carpet brush. I felt that it did a better job of brushing the product into the carpet. But, alas, still didn't really get my carpet clean.

I just saw on YouTube someone using a third method to brush the product into the carpet. They used the Oreck orbital, but used the fabric bonnet to push the product into the carpet instead of the carpet brush. I didn't try that method as I didn't think of it and hadn't seen the video yet. Perhaps that third method might work better. I don't know. But using the two methods I tried, not very good.

I do like the Oreck orbital machine. But, I'm going to use other cleaning products with it. I'm thinking of using the orbital with the bonnet but a commercial brand of encapsulation product.

And, the product isn't very cheap either. I spent a fair amount for their pre-mist, their dry carpet cleaner, and even the hand carpet brush, only to get unsatisfactory results.

I do like some Oreck products. I just bought an Oreck vacuum that I like very much and the orbital is a good machine. But I had poor results with the dry carpet cleaner.

title: So far, my menstrual cramps are DECREASING!
text:
UPDATE 07/14/2014: I've been taking Hyland's Magnesium Phosphorica (aka Mag Phos) 6X along with the Carlson fish oil and it is EXTREMELY helpful in reducing my cramps. In fact, for some women, I wouldn't be surprised if your cramps completely disappear as a result of this combination.

WARNING (12/30/2012): Before reading below, please keep in mind that, according to the National Institutes of Health, 3,000 mg of fish oil or less is considered the "likely safe" amount. When first trying the fish oil, I accidentally took a little over that amount a few times. So, try to stick with the "likely safe" amount. The link to the NIH's fish oil page: [...]

I have very, very, VERY uncomfortable menstrual cramps (to the point where, during my "bad day," I have an "incapacitating" period that can last up to 5 hours and I curse my existence). After hours of research, I decided to try Carlson's fish oil as a last resort. Since I ordered the fish oil "late" in my cycle, I was only able to take 1 teaspoon of it for 8 days before my expected "bad day." (I took 2 teaspoons on the "bad day.")

When my "bad day" started, I actually wasn't sure that it had started because I was only mildly uncomfortable and my "incapacitating" period never really started! I still had to take some Aleve, but I didn't feel like overdosing like I usually do. LOL. The next day, I happily realized that that *was* my "bad day."

It seems like the fish oil substantially minimized my cramps and I only took it for a few days! And I have a pretty bad diet/sleep schedule/exercise schedule.

About the product: It's extremely easy to pour (there's a little funnel inside of the bottle) and it tastes delicious (a very "pure" and simple taste that reminds me of "Fruity Pebbles" cereal a little bit because of the very light lemon flavor). All you have to do is refrigerate it, have a teaspoon handy, and make sure to take it immediately before or after you eat something.

I'm going to see how my next period turns out, but I think it'll be the same or even better because I'll have more time to take it and I'm slowly improving my diet. I'll update my review after my next period.

So far, I totally recommend this product for minimizing menstrual cramps. It definitely can't hurt to try it. Make sure to get the "Lemon" flavor because I'm not sure how the "Orange" flavor tastes. (Orange-flavored products are usually hit or miss with me)

UPDATE 10/14/2012: I was right on the money. My recent period was even BETTER than the first one!!! This time I took TWO teaspoons per day a week before and on the day of my "bad day." My diet/sleep schedule was about the same because I've been super busy. Still had a little bit of cramping but, like before, I could function. Very rarely have I had a period like this without birth control. Again, if you have horrible menstrual cramps, I would HIGHLY, HIGHLY, HIGHLY recommend this product.

If, for whatever reason, you can't buy this product, I also recommend eating sardines or salmon because, like this oil, they are high in omega-3 fatty acids. I like canned sardines in water. Leafy greens like spinach, collard greens, turnip greens, and mustard greens are also helpful.

title: Surprisingly bad
text:
I didn't realize that dental floss could be a hard thing to produce. Well, apparently it is.

1. The way this stuff is wrapped makes it impossible to pull out of the container without unscrewing the cap and taking the "ball" of floss out.

2. If you do manage to pull some out through the cap, the hole in the cap will cut the floss instead of the part that should cut the floss.

3. This floss is thick and ends up breaking frequently in my teeth. I end up using 2-3x as much as I would with normal floss.

4. Taste. Meh. No real taste.

5. So here's the thing, once you get past all those issues, the floss manages to get the gunk out from between my teeth but there's no way it's worth 2-4x what normal floss is. And, while this stuff is good for the fishies and dolphins and iguanas I'm not sure that having to buy it 2-3x more often is better for mama earth.

title: fine powder dissolved easily in room temperature water & tastes great like a slightly tart fruit + best C by far I've ever found
text:
I am so glad a reviewer of another product explained the many greater health & other benefits of finding a freeze-dried version which resulted in my finding this product as the ones produced by spray-drying require the addition of some maltodextrin to prevent it from caking. Maltodextrin is made from corn starch & I like many people nowadays are allergic to corn products to varying degrees because they are so over-used in so many products including at low enough levels that they don't always have to be shown in the ingredients list.

I HAD BEEN SCARED TO TRY THIS PRODUCT BECAUSE MANY REVIEWERS SAID it doesn't dissolve easily or can clump or tastes less sweet but none of this has been a problem for me.

IT IS THE FIRST FORM OF VITAMIN C (of many types I've tried over the years including all natural & food-based etc.) THAT I HAVE TAKEN THAT I TRULY LOVE & THAT DOESN'T FEEL ACIDIC OR BAD IN ANY WAY FOR MY TEETH OR MOUTH. With every other form of C I have felt the need to immediately then chew on a piece of xylitol gum ([[ASIN:B00ARABK20 PUR Gum Aspartame Free, Spearmint, 2.8 Ounce]] works great & has the purest ingredients with the least chemicals or additives of any of the many xylitol gums I've looked into) but not with this one. Instead it feels totally wonderful to drink & I love its slightly tart taste as some fruits have as that makes it feel like eating a piece of fruit or some fruit pudding if I have to rush while mixing the product & end up with a small clump of it in my mouth.

I FIND IT WORKS BEST TO ONLY USE 1/4 teaspoon at a time as then it's easy to sprinkle lightly over some room-temperature water which makes it easy & fast to dissolve simply by stirring with a teaspoon. C is best absorbed anyway when taken in small doses through the day because your body can't store it & only so much can be used at a time with the rest being excreted in your urine.

CHERRIES BRING SEVERAL KEY NUTRIENTS HELPFUL FOR ONE'S EYES & GENERAL HEALTH SO THIS HAS BEEN AN OUTSTANDING PRODUCT TO DISCOVER IN EVERY WAY INCLUDING BECAUSE good organic cherries are often not available or very pricey. ALSO, MOST FORMS OF C THESE DAYS ARE SYNTHETIC & THOSE HARM THE BENEFICIAL GUT BACTERIA CRITICAL TO MANY ASPECTS OF OUR HEALTH INCLUDING OUR IMMUNE SYSTEM & ABILITY TO ABSORB NUTRIENTS.

title: A Product Everyone Needs (And Should Own)
text:
I own multiple nail clippers of various sizes and have always found that quality does not always equate to the price paid. I one day came across a channel on YT (I am unsure if I can mention the site, but I am sure most know which video website I am referring to). The individual is a professional that goes above and beyond any pedicure, I have ever had. And they utilize tools similar to the ones found in this kit. Clipping, trimming, and filing your nails are not enough. There are tools in this kit most need but are unaware they do. I find the quality to be high, so much so my nails look the best they ever have after use. The only cons I can share are that the label/emblem on the case is highly sticky. We are talking to the point that I initially had to be very careful not to allow it to touch anything. Fortunately for me, it seems to have lost its adhesiveness over time.

The other things I will never use are the ear tools. While some might see them as a great bonus, you should never place anything (not even a cotton swab or washcloth) in your ear unless you want issues. Of course, you should clean your ears daily, but nothing should ever go inside any part other than the outer ear and pinna. Besides the above, this is a product that everyone who cares about their nails should own (even those who regularly get manicures and pedicures).

title: Great in Smoothies, Gross When Plain
text:
I usually drink the bottled Soylent 2.0, which I love. Taste is great and it's super convenient. The downside is that it costs almost twice as much per serving vs the powder (going off Soylent's website prices)
So I tried the powder. Not nearly as pleasant as 2.0. It tastes like if you put a scoop of flour into a cup of water. The mixed solution is thin, like water and there is not a noticeable texture like I've experienced with most protein powders.
I was upset that now I had many meals worth of powder left and didn't want it to go waste. So I started mixing it with different flavors.
Currently I eat one serving of Soylent blended with water, a banana, and a tablespoon of peanut butter and it's great! I will make 3 servings at a time and keep it in a pitcher to drink throughout the day.
It keeps me full and stops me from snacking. I also go out to eat less which has saved me a ton of money. I highly suggest this product if you have a busy lifestyle and are willing to blend up a batch once a day. If not, try out the bottled Soylent 2.0!

I went to Disneyland in February and was so sad that they no longer have them in the parks (Disney ears don’t stick around forever, and once they’re gone they’re gone) I regretted not buying them back in November and they’ve been haunting me. Now, as a true blue Disney fan I question if these are “genuine” or not. They are much fluffier then the typical ears sold at Disney and the tags are different as well. I actually like these ears a little bit better then my original ears (I have many) so I’m not complaining. The bow is also different then any bow I’ve seen on Disney ears. It has fluff on the inside which is unusual for the ears, plus when I almost bought these last year in the parks I don’t remember them having fluff on the inside. Nevertheless, I really love these ears. They look the same besides being a little more fluffy (which I like) and they feel comfortable. The sequins don’t seem as high of quality and the stitching is also not as good as my other ears. I missed out on them in the park and am super happy with these, even if they aren’t “genuine”. I will put in the pictures the tags from a couple of “genuine” ears and then the tags on these. I personally don’t care, but if you are an avid collector then you may not want these. If you are just a Disney fan needing some cute ears I would definitely get them.

title: This is my comparative review to Downbeats and Vibes at a Metallica concert
text:
We were taking our kids to their first concert (Metallica) so trying to appear to be a responsible parent we decided to buy earplugs for the entire family. I was torn between the Vibes and the DownBeats. (Vibes being an Amazon Choice and appearing to be more of a name brand, Downbeats having a 1/2 star better rating and a better price) I ended up ordering 3 sets of each for our family of 4 so we had 2 extra pairs to swap if needed.

At the house, a day before the concert, I gave my wife and I the Vibes (rated at less of a DB drop) and the kids the Downbeats (higher DB drop) Everyone liked what I got them except for me, Apparently I have small ear canals. (Im 6'4", this is the 1st time I have every had to go with the small in my life) Even with the smallest cushions they uncomfortable. I could just still feel the rigid plastic inside. . I tried keeping them in for about 10 minutes thinking I would get use to them but I couldn't take it. I then put in the Downbeats and loved them, they felt so much better.

So now that I had tainted both pairs with my earwax I figured id give both a try with my headphones hooked up to my computer. I could tell no difference at all in sound quality. The DownBeats did obviously block just a little more sound, like they were rated to do, but I was happy.

Fast forward to the concert and I put in my DownBeats and was really disappointed. This is not how a concert was supposed to sound! I know they say high fidelity but everything was just muddled. Frustrated I took them out, but wanting to be a good role model for my kids I thought I would try the Vibes to see if they were any better and they were! I kept them in for probably half of the concert. (Apparently concentrating on a concert made me forget they were uncomfortable vs just sitting at my computer) I will say the Vibes still made the concert less enjoyable, which is why I took them out depending on the song. But they were tolerable. I just didn't like the sound of the concert with the DownBeats at all. With the Vibes the concert sounded right, but you still didnt get that concert experience but they werent that bad. Im guessing my opiton would be the same for even higher priced earplugs as the Vibes. Quiet music at a concert just isnt the same.

Final Verdict Vibes = 4 Star and my loud Concert. They had great sound quality but their rigid nature made them uncomfortable. While I was able to completely ignore the comfort while concentrating on the rock concert in front of me they are also sold for Fitness classes, Riding a motor cycle and there is no way I could wear them long term for other purposes.

DownBeats = 4Star and my recommendation for anything but a rock concert. They sounded good in my headphones at my computer. They were super comfortable. Id have no problem wearing them all day for the other things they have listed like "Airshows and motorcycles"

title: This device appears to produce excessive EMFs (electromagnetic fields)
text:
My entire family has had 1-2 Dohm machines in their bedroom for years now. And recently, I started researching EMF's (electromagnetic fields) and a concept known as 'dirty electricity'. My interest was peaked because the new home we moved into has solar panels and 2 different Smart Meters. Both are known for their EMF and dirty electricity production, so I was concerned our exposure may have increased.

I ordered a $40 EMF reader from Amazon, and began checking the EMF levels in and around our home. Quite by accident, I discovered that the Dohm produces far more EMF's than anything else in or around our home. To put things in perspective, the Smart Meters generated up to 250uTs, and our running microwave produced anywhere from 50 to 80uTs. The Dohm completely maxed out my reader! I believe it goes to 300uTs, so obviously the Dohm produces more than that.

And even more disturbing is that it STAYED maxed out. On the Smart Meters, the value would spike in the 200's, but then drop down and jump all over the place. But not the Dohm, it pegged the reader right away and stayed there. Even on the low setting! I realize there are differing opinions regarding the safe levels of EMF's, but this seems way too high. Especially for something that you are likely sleeping next to, for many hours at a time.

I have retired all of our Dohm machines, and will not be using them again.

title: Makes awkward windows easier to clean
text:
I bought this item because I have several windows in my apartment that each have 9 panes of glass. The middle panes are wider than the panes on the left and right sides, but the middle panes to not open -- what a pain! lol
Anyway, even with my long arms, I could not reach from the left windows and the right windows to clean the centers of the middle windows. Adding to the complexity are the upper left and upper right windows that do open, that are about 12" high.
Anyway, I figured out the logistics and how to maneuver the telescopic pole out the small top windows without breaking them, and get to the right angle for cleaning the windows directly below, as well as turning the pole and flipping it about as needed to clean and squeegee.
Without this item, 1 window took me over 45 minutes to clean, and I could not reach the centers of the middle windows. With this item, I cleaned the windows in about 20 minutes and got nearly every part.
I would definitely recommend this item to anyone that has bizarre or awkward windows that their arms cannot reach easily to clean.

title: A good pendulum with insignificant problems.
text:
There are small usually insignificant problems with this particular pendulum. One detail is that the witness chamber is very very small. And if you used powder or fluid in the chamber it would be hard to clean such a small area. I never use a chamber so that doesn't matter to me but if you like a witness chamber then this isn't the pendulum for you. Something that you need to know is that there is a brass keychain style of chord from the inside of the top of the pendulum that isn't shown,. unless someone adds a different picture. The chain emerges from the top of the pendulum bob and cannot be swapped for another chain which for me is fine. The length of the chain from the top of the pendulum bob to the small ball at the end of the pendulum is exactly 5 1/2 inches long which is good for map and chart dowsing in particular. The pendulum bob itself is 2 inches long and is a slightly heavy pendulum. It is the weight of a very small fishing weight. Most people prefer a little weight to a pendulum. I do and so this is another matter of taste.
This is a good strong heavy duty professional quality pendulum which is what matters to most people and it looks great. It is a top of the line quality pendulum.
Here is my primary problems, and it's with the descriptions on this page that is used for this pendulum,. and to a degree with other pendulums that are labeled Xeonix pendulums on Amazon. First one very important point is that this style of pendulum is known as an "Isis pendulum" which is a style of Egyptian pendulum. People looking for either Egyptian pendulums or for an Isis pendulum can't find this pendulum unless they really really know where to look. And Xeonix isn't a pendulum supplier not a manufacturer because there are many other styles of pendulums could be mislabeled a brand of pendulums. They supply other metal pendulum and wooden pendulums and over 50 styles of crystal pendulums and a lot more so most pendulums could be mislabeled as being Xeonix pendulums. If the page labeling is changed soon then I will revise this part of the review.

title: Finally! A Precision-Made, Durable, and Affordable Oral B Replacement Brush Head!
text: Everybody seems to agree that brand Oral B replacements are over-the-top expensive, and I have joined many in relying on the less expensive generics sold on Amazon.  This is my fourth order, but the first time I have tried Oliver James brush replacements.  Although these are slightly more expensive than other generic offerings, I decided to try them because of shortcomings in the generics I have previously purchased: (1) large tolerances in brush fit and rotation that led to sloppy operation and painful pinches of cheeks and lips, and (2) poor bristle durability and brushes that I felt were entirely too soft.  When my first order of Oliver James brushes arrived, the brush heads looked for all the world like they might have been repackaged versions of those I had purchased previously.  Upon opening the package and examining the Oliver James brushes, the differences were striking!  The moving brushes on these fit more tightly and made brushing much more precise.  Although the bristles of both my old and new brush heads felt comparable to my fingers, the Oliver James brushes felt twice as firm on my teeth.  I now am getting perhaps three times as many brushings from each brush head as I did in the past.  Indeed, some people with sensitive teeth and gums may find the Oliver James brushes to be TOO firm, but I love them!

title: Speeds up straightening time
text:
[[VIDEOID:3ad9784b29a27fead3e0767b05945d34]] I’ve tried many, many straighteners. None are perfect, but this is the closest. Usually it takes me an hour to straighten my hair. With this brush, it took me just 10 minutes!! I didn’t even have to divide my hair into parts before straightening! I also didn’t have to detangle or comb my hair before ironing. This brush just brushed easily through my hair.

My hair is normally between wavy and curly. Medium density. Also very dry with split ends. After straightening, some split ends still showed, but my hair felt much softer!

I’m surprised some people didn’t have a great experience with this. It had by far been my best straightening brush. I guess different things work differently for different people.

I found that when hair is stuck in the brush, there’s a bit of smoke coming out (like with a blow dryer or straightener.) Removing the hair from the brush helps with that.

The brush heats up extremely quickly, as you can see in my video. I also didn’t have to use the glove. The brush isn’t hot to the touch.

Overall, for me this brush worked really really well, as you can see in my pictures.

title: Not Sure Forskolin Works
text:
I was really interested in trying Forskolin as a weight loss supplement because I had read some article about Dr. Oz promoting it as the next big break-through. I honestly am not sure what all the hype is about, and haven't really had the results that I am looking for.

First, I am taking Forskolin in conjunction with the Atkins diet, in hopes that it would help to speed the process. I have lost weight, but I'm not losing any more weight (in my opinion) than what I would be losing anyway on this diet. I have been consuming about 1800 calories per day for the last month, and have lost a total of 8 pounds, as well as taking this supplement. I'm a 33 year old male, and was undoubtedly consuming more than 2500 calories per day, which is what made me gain weight in the first place, but at around 8 pounds for the last 4 weeks, that is what can be expected on cutting calories down to 1800 per day - which is what I have done.

That leads me to believe that the weight loss has been purely diet related, and not because of this Forskolin supplement.

When taking, I don't feel any noticeable effect on my metabolism, and I don't gain any more energy than what I already have. I don't necessarily feel any appetite suppression, and I honestly can't say that I feel any effect from this product at all.

I will say that I have noticed that my body's fat composition has improved (meaning it looks better than what I think a normal 8 pound weight loss would have provided, but that doesn't translate into more weight loss, it simply means that I think that my fat distribution has been improved.)

I don't think that this is the magic go-to pill for weightloss that it is touted to be, unfortunately. I did read that reports after having been taking this product for a month that indicate that it increases blood testosterone levels in men, which is why it improves body composition. I didn't have any blood-work done to prove that one way or the other, but at the end of the day, I would say that it hasn't improved or hindered the weight loss that I have achieved from my normal low calorie diet.

I hope you found this review helpful. It may work for some differently than it worked for me, but since I depend on the reviews of others when purchasing products online, I wanted to provide my feedback as well. I did receive this product at a slight discount in exchange for my honest review.

This can lead to damage if I don't use the right kind of hair tools, so I am very careful to pick items that state that they are anti-static, smoothing, or anti-frizz.  My last hair straightener was a Remington S-2004, it had some kind of fabric on the plates, worked great, left my hair super shiny, and lasted me for many years.  I wanted to purchase the same model, but it wasn't available anymore so I initially bought a Remington S9520 as a replacement.  Unfortunately, the Remington didn't work out, so after searching for something with fabric on the plates decided to purchase this ProCabello nano fiber non-stick straightener for $47.50, and an Apalus fiberglass fabric straightener for $21.  They both work much better on my hair type, lower heat setting (360`) for super straight hair, no pulling, and my hair is shiny after straightening, even at lower heat settings.  However, for half the price, the Apalus is an awesome deal, has fabric on the plates like my old Remington S-2004 straightener, and works every bit as well as this more expensive ProCabello (which doesn't have fabric on the plates even though the description makes it sound like it does), I'm not sure if there is a quality difference that will become apparent long-term, but because a couple of reviews on the Apalus said it stopped working after only a couple of months, I will probably keep them both so I have a backup.

title: Know your numbers
text:
I have been on a ketogenic diet for 2 years. One of the problems is knowing what foods might throw you out of ketosis. There is so much conflicting information and of course each body is different. I have tried keto sticks but they are next to worthless. Although there is nothing better than a blood test to determine the level of ketones, the Ketone Breath Meter is the next best thing. You can't always believe the nutrients that are listed on a package. There are no regulations as to what constitutes net carbs. The only way that you can tell if the food you are eating is throwing you out of ketosis is by testing your ketone level about a half hour after you eat it. The Ketone Breath Meter is an easy, accurate way to do this. In that way you will know for sure.

This little device is easy to use and seems to be consistent and accurate. Press a button to turn it on and wait for the 20 second countdown then blow into it for between 5 and 10 seconds. There is an audible beep which tells you when to begin blowing and another audible beep which tells you when to stop. It then displays your ketone level. A reading between .5 and 3.0 indicates that you are in ketosis. The first time that I used it I registered 2.30. To me this seems to be very accurate since I rarely have more than 12g of carbs each day.

If you have cheat day or days then you probably will be thrown out of ketosis because of the carbs that you ate. The Ketone Breath Meter will let you know how many days it took to bring you back into ketosis. In this way you can judge whether the cheat days are worth it.

The readings on the meter are large and unambiguous. It comes with 10 attachable mouthpieces and everything can be stored in a small convenient pouch. If you are serious about a keto diet you need to know your numbers and have the proper information about the foods that you eat. And the Ketone Breath Meter is an economic and convenient way to track your ketone level.

title: Simply Amazing
text:
I have always suffered from rashes and bumps after shaving, especially when it came to my thighs. I've tried a few products and while some of them helped to minimize these reactions, they were never completely eliminated.

I'd long heard of the wondrous success of Coochy Shaving cream but it had never been a convenient time to buy it and I was a little put off by the price tag. Fortunately, I stumbled across a selection of Coochy Shaving cream at a local adult bookstore and decided to pick it up. It certainly helped that both the employees there were users of it and personally recommended it.

I am so glad I picked up this product. I can say that I am now completely irritation free. I also had a much easier time shaving; areas which might need several strokes of the razor in the past needed only one or two with this cream. To top it off, Coochy Shaving cream left me with the closest shave I've ever had and my skin remains smooth and silky after shaving with this product.

I must admit, none of the scents are all that great but the performance far outranks and cons to this product! If you suffer from rashes, bumps or irritation when shaving any body part, you should invest in Coochy Shaving cream!

Unlike many, it's taste it not overpowering, probably because the taste is gone a few seconds after you start brushing - like cheap bubblegum. title: Nice Size
text:
Just got this set to replace the numerous little containers in my daily bag. Each slot easily fits basic pills and gel caps (in abundance, for those who go through a lot) as well as larger pills like 12hr Mucinex and a row of Tums. The cases are very smooth, are easy to use, and they were exactly the size I imagined from the images provided.

Latches are very easy to open, but could be considered TOO easy depending on where it’s stored.

Due to internal sizing, a non-divided case can only hold 3 AA batteries; AAA fit more. Standard bobby-pins require two slots and must be diagonal (mini ones would fit well). A US standard house key can fit diagonally in 2 slots. My Cruzor Blade flash drive (not retractable) fits in a slot well; you can fit probably 3 in a single slot at once.

PROS:
As sturdy as plastic (or more so, depending on the thickness of regular pill cases)
Latch is easy to open
Removable parts are very easy to remove and replace and feel secured when returned

CONS:
Purchased “biodegradable” plastic, yet the whole set comes in a plastic bag and each case is individually wrapped again inside of that bag. (These are sturdy, a thin cardboard box would work just as well!)
Latch opens easily, which may come off too easily
Limited color options

text: Pure acai is delicious! I've had it in store-bought smoothies and acai blueberry drinks, but I've never had it on it's own. I always thought it would be tart, but it's not at all. It's subtle and sweet and so good! The powder is a very dark blackish-purple color. I added a teaspoon to a vanilla milkshake, expecting to get a deep purple milkshake, but that's not what happened. The powder didn't dissolve completely, so it wound up looking like a light purple cookies and cream milkshake. I was expecting it to be gritty, but it surprised me once again! I don't really understand how, but it wasn't gritty at all! The majority of the particles stayed suspended in the shake, and the ones that sunk to the bottom easily mixed back in when I stirred it. It tasted like a light, sweet berry milkshake with just a hint of chocolate...definitely a new favorite! I can't wait to try this in my berry smoothies and to see what else I can do with this purple goodness! I also love that it's an excellent source of iron. I try to give blood as often as I can, but my hemoglobin levels are always very low (sometimes so low that the meter won't even read my blood). I don't eat a lot of red meat, so I'm always looking for other foods that are high in iron. This will be a great booster for the days leading up to my appointment! It tastes amazing, and it's great for my body...I couldn't ask for anything better!

text: Outstanding service from this company and the product is excellent. During our physicals we did a comparison of the results of her product against the results of tests done in the MD office and the results were pretty much exactly the same. My husband and I are both using the ketone strips as he adjusts to a serious change in his diet and though we aren't currently monitoring ph, it was good that there is a sample of those monitoring strips as well in the kit, and when tested against the test done during our physicals, they proved accurate. This company has been attentive in making sure we received additional infirmational charts and such through email and has checked on us a few times to make sure we were satisfied and understood what we are about in using this product. I bought two kits. My husband and I are sharing and only check ketones and weight on Monday and Friday. This is to make sure we stayed on track during the week and didn't get silly over a weekend.  The ketogenic way of eating and living isn't for everyone. But I found over 30 years ago that I am at my healthiest and best when I stay within these parameters and my husband, who was a big time bread eater and fairly new to this way of eating has seen a decrease in high blood pressure to within normal ranges,  we're watching his cholesterol levels starting to make a turn in the right direction and in general he just feels better and stronger.  As you add more foods into your diet these monitoring strips help to ensure that you are aware of how your body is or isn't dealing with the changes.  We ate some Honey Baked Ham and while we still saw ourselves in Ketosis when we checked, we saw clearly that the strips registered the small amount of sugar we had consumed. I have added somethings to my own diet that I have pretty much never eaten much of in the past. So these strips are helping me see how my body acts towards them. If we still require monitoring by the time we use up our supply I will be reordering from this source.
