title: True sound, protects hearing
text: I go to a lot of concerts and I want to keep my hearing so I can continue being able to enjoy them, haha.  Normally I just wear the cheap purple foam plugs which work fine.  But I wanted more specialized earplugs to improve the sound quality.  I looked at several and tried these.  I like the long stem- it makes them easy to get in/out.  The carrying case is also nice.  Sound-wise, I compared them to my foam ones and the sounds is better and less muted.  It is still pretty loud when wearing these.  There is a small hole that the sound passes through.  There is no filter (my brother has a similar pair that has different filters you can put into the hole).  I would describe these as just "taking the top off of the sound". I.e. they keep it from being unbearable and protect your hearing without limiting any of the sound quality or muting certain frequencies.  The concert sounds loud and true but afterwards when I leave and remove the earplugs my ears are not ringing and everything outside sounds completely normal.  Thus I would highly recommend these as allowing you to enjoy a concert while helping to protect your hearing.

title: Very potent and pure product
text:
I've been a coffee drinker all my life, and I drink the strong stuff (black as night, never diluted with cream or sugar) but this stuff is above and beyond anything coffee has done for me.

At first I giggled at the name "God's speed", assuming it was just a little joke. Be certain that this is no joke, this stuff feels very much like a powerful stimulant. On that note I urge those with heart problems or caffeine sensitivity to be careful with this product, it is seriously that effective.

There are much cheaper caffeine pills on the market but most of them are processed very cheaply and packed with filler. I want to assure whoever is reading this review that these capsules are absolutely pure and very strong. When I take these it enhances my performance on multiple levels. I lift more at the gym, I focus more on tasks at hand, I don't slow down or get tired after hours of studying like I would without it.

I want to make another note about caffeine though, it is a receptor agonist which means that daily usage will reduce its effectiveness (tolerance buildup). I use this product every other day at most and strongly recommend others to do the same. If you drink coffee a lot you will be less sensitive to caffeine already so cut out the coffee if you want the full "God's speed" experience from these capsules.

All in all, this product has been consistently effective (an understatement honestly) and provides me with enormous amounts of energy whenever I need. Give it a try before you waste your money on cheap chinese caffeine pills.

title: Very pleased with these plugs. A musician's shield against hearing loss...
text:
Awesome plugs for noise of any kind. Personally, loud instruments have caused many a problem with my hearing. I think these are a fantastic product, especially for the price, when it comes to saving your precious hearing. The product arrived in standard cardboard and plastic packaging, with the instructions printed on the back of the box.

I really enjoyed the fact that there are two levels of protection included in this package. The BLUE plugs are perfect for me, because they allow me to hear my instrument clearly, without allowing too much noise in. The WHITE plugs, in my opinion would be better suited for shooting or construction work as they filter out a greater level of sound. They are very easy to clean with warm water and mild dish soap (please do this! As a healthcare provider, I could go on and on about the risk of infection/hearing damage should you not clean your earpieces)... The only thing I did not like about these plugs, is the carrying case. I think they meant well, but the case is a little too small to easily store the plugs. Well, I should say you can get the plugs in, but they are incredibly hard to remove from the case once you get them in, but it does serve it's purpose... Overall, these are the best reusable earplugs I've ever used, and will definitely use them daily and purchase them again if they should fail. I recommend these to musicians, laborers, marksman, husbands/wives of loud snorers, and anyone looking to cut out the noise in their lives. Keep your ears safe with these things, you won't regret the buy.

text:
I really like this whey protein. I was looking for one that was minimally processed and had no nasty additives or stevia, and this seemed like the best option.
I've mixed it into protein balls, yogurt, and even plain water. Every time it mixes easily and smoothly, with no chalky texture.
My favorite way to eat it is just in yogurt with chia, fruit, and a little honey, it needs to sit overnight for the chia to soak but the result is a very creamy pudding-like high protein breakfast!

I do wish I could try the flavored options, but because they have stevia I cannot; stevia tastes repulsive to me and gives me a horrible stomachache. So I'll have to settle for flavoring it myself.

This stuff is pretty expensive, especially if you use it every day. But you get what you pay for and it's well worth it in my opinion.

title: No more daily dehydration headaches!
text:
THIS THING IS AMAZING. I've had it 1 month now and not had a single dehydration headache!!

MY BACKSTORY:
I carry a water bottle everywhere and would sit with one on my desk at work daily, but I rarely would drink out of it. I simply carried it because I would suddenly feel thirsty if I didn't have it. I get a headache around 2-3pm daily like clockwork. I suspected it was dehydration since the rare occasion that I did manage to drink enough, I didn't get a headache, but I couldn't keep up with it. I tried various tracking systems, including the ones with the time printed on it to pace myself. None of it worked because I physically needed a reminder. I thought about setting a timer, but that would be cumbersome, disruptive, and not dynamic enough to shift with daily life. I found this reminder and was hesitant to pay $25. But, it was a lot cheaper than "smart" water bottles and I knew taking Motrin and/or Tylenol daily was not healthy. The cost was worth it after feeling this headache-free relief!!

SIZE:
It has a silicone band that fits well on my water bottle, which is about 3 inches in diameter. It definitely has enough stretch to fit on a 1L Nalgene, for example. The device itself is about 1.5" tall, 1" wide, and 3/8" thick.

HOW IT WORKS:
I timed it when I first got it to see how the cycling works. Every ~35 minutes it strobes for ~5 seconds, then is off for ~5 seconds, alternating that cycle for about a minute before it resets the 35 second clock. I usually grab it within those first 5 seconds, but if you're not around and it does 2 full cycles of 35 min/1 min flashing, it turns off until you drink again. It also resets the clock every time you drink and has a light that blinks whenever it registers you taking a drink. It's gotten to the point that my body has internalized the clock a bit; on many occasions it started strobing as I was reaching for a drink on my own!

MY CONCERNS DIDN'T END UP BEING ISSUES:
- I thought the "just drank" light would get set off a lot carrying my water bottle around, but that hasn't been an issue.
- It also has a light sensor, because it doesn't go off in the dark. I can keep it on my nightstand with no issues
- My water bottle has a straw, so every once in a while my sip is a little too still for it to register, but that's been only maybe 5 times in the last month.
- It's also perfect everyday use outside of the office - I don't have to deal with alarms and it dynamically updates as I drink.
- I keep it on all the time, and haven't worried about it falling off. I did take it off twice when I want on a day-long outing where I knew I'm going to be drinking a lot on my own and didn't want it to interfere with the frequent in and out of my backpack.

title: I also like our thermometers to be able to take both oral ...
text:
We have a 5-yr old and a 3 week old, so I need a thermometer that is both accurate and quick. I also like our thermometers to be able to take both oral and axillary temps.

PROS:

Consistent reading. I took my temp orally multiple times and all of them were within 0.2 degrees of each other. Having young kids, this is especially important to me. I also took an axillary temp and both methods produced the same temp so it's accurate across different temping methods.

Quick-ish. Depending on how you're taking the temperature, it is close to the 16-second mark. When I took my temp (oral), it took about 16 seconds to get a reading. When I took our 3 week olds temp (axillary), it took almost 30 seconds to get a reading. I then tried an axillary temp on myself with an 18-22 second result. We have not tried a rectal temp.

Quick one-push on/off button. Nothing to fiddle with or hold down.

Automatic shut-off. I'm a sleep deprived parent. I'd like to say that I remember to turn everything that I use off, but I'm sure that's not the case. The GearDistrict thermometer has an auto shut-off after 10 minutes.

Comes with a case. I can disinfect it and then put it back in its case and place it back in our changing table drawer. I don't have to worry about it getting all germy (although we always wipe it down before using it orally anyway) or broken in there.

Flexible tip. Having squirmy children means that the thermometer up doesn't always stay in the same place. I didn't think that I'd like flexible tip when I read about it, but after trying it on my wriggling 3-week old, I'm in love.

CONS:

Inconsistent (and not 10-second) times. The only reason that I'm docking this product 1 star is because the result times were inconsistent and none of them were 10-second times. It is still a fairly quick product at 16 seconds, but 30 seconds with a screaming baby can seem like forever. We have a thermometer that is truly an 8-second thermometer, so if she was really sick, we would reach for that one before this one. For myself and the rest of our family, it's not as big of a deal, but I wish that it were noted in the product description.

Overall, it's a good basic thermometer. I wouldn't necessarily recommend it if you're looking for a super quick thermometer for young children, but aside from that, it's an accurate thermometer that gets the job done and I would recommend.

I did receive this product at a discount in exchange for my honest review.

title: Works about as long as Juicy Fruit gum lasts...
text:
At first read of the product description and no-frills advertising, I assumed that this product would be pf a much better quality. The idea behind it is actually quite clever and works wonders - on paper. If you follow the guidelines they give you on their Amazon page; however, it seems to cause more harm than good. I am not saying that it will ruin your glasses by any means, but if you use any sort of cleaning cloth that has been anywhere near the Nerdwax, you will be disappointed time and time again with smudged lenses. I purchased the HD super quality blah blah set of lenses to combat complaints later down the road due to hindsight wishing I had gotten the higher grade lenses. This particular lens option is supposedly easier to clean and wont scratch as easily etc etc. Nerdwax proved them wrong.

If you expose any of your cleaning (cloth) options to this tiny tube, it is almost immediately spread across the whole lens, forcing you to clean more and more and barely get a result. I am always careful and extremely meticulous when it comes to taking care of my personal effects and I found the amount of time I was most recently taking to clean my glasses was entirely too long.

I am also halfway convinced that the company took Burt's Bees products and crammed them into their own packaging. The stuff smells like it would make a great chapstick - peppermint and whatever the other scents are make it nicely refreshing as you put your glasses on. This is when the fun ends and the stupidity begins. Once you find yourself smelling your tube of Nerdwax and trying to apply it like chapstick, you know then it is time to move on and just keep pushing up your glasses like everyone else.

I have only used it for about a week, but I haven't noticed any adverse effects since application. I assumed with having rather sensitive skin, this may be irritating but it is actually showing zero signs of angry skin. Aside from getting wax all over your fingers, frames, lenses, cleaning cloths, etc, I would have to say it wasn't a bad trip at all.

text: This product really works. I have tried memory foam mattresses (the worse for sagging of all), those expensive air mattresses that they advertise on tv and plain old inner spring mattresses. In desperation, I ordered the 1" No Sags inserts for my latest 1 year old innerspring mattress. This hardened up the mattress slightly, but took the sag almost out. I added the 1" extension piece right in the center of the main insert and completely eliminated the sag. I don't know how long this will last before the mattress sags further, but since it stiffened it up a bit, I have great expectations that this may very well be a long term answer to my problem. I wish I had the thousands of dollars back that I have wasted on new mattress replacements over the past few years & had simply bought this product. Remember, this product works on innerspring mattresses only (they claim also latex, but I have never had one of this type). Highly recommended product.

For some reason, the delivery was delayed but Amazon responded with a $100 discount, which I felt was very reasonable. The chair was delivered today. Be aware that the shipper will not help bring it in the house. Fortunately, I had some help. It was very well packaged and came on a wooden palate which was left in our garage. It was quite easy to remove from the carton and only minor assembly was required which was very easy. The chair easily fits through a standard door. and is very attractive and appears very well made.

Now for the good part. Having tired a number of massage chairs, This relatively inexpensive model provides as good a massage as I have felt in a chair. I have tried most of the functions and they all feel great. There is a good selection, but the menu is not overwhelming as it seems to be in some models.

All in all, I'm sorry I waited so long. I did purchase the square trade 3 year warrantee, but based on my past experience with a Panasonic chair, I doubt I will need it. Since we live pretty far from a major city, I thought it worthwhile.

In summary, if your looking for a massage chair, I recommend you look no farther and I certainly would recommend Amazon for the purchase. Just be aware of the shipping limitation. I don't know if they offer a higher level of shipping but you might inquire if you feel it would be difficult to get it unpacked and into your house.

title: EXCELLENT with pigmented ink
text:
I use this with my Canon Pro9500 pigmented ink printer with excellent results. I'm picky about papers becasue I sell my prints in a gallery. I expect my printed colors to match my calibrated screen precisely. Using the print profile supplied by Ilford for my printer, color rendition, as well as shadow and highlight rendidion is as true as with Canon papers (which are of course outstanding).

The texture is exactly what I want for my wildlife prints. The term "pearl" describes it well. Not matte, and not quite semi-gloss, it is somewhere in between. The texture is like a very fine matte, but with a sheen that is more lively, much like a pearl. Canon does not have a comparable paper, so I am quite pleased this works so well.

This is the only third party paper I have used that gives comparable results to proprietary paper when used with a vendor-supplied printer profile. I can't say it would work with other printers, but with Canon Lucia pigmented inks, I have only praise.

title: Make sure to understand they are molds
text:
So…I got the product and read on how to mix the glue that came with it. Talks about placing the glue into the mold, etc. did that. Places the mold to my tooth and loved them! They stayed in place all night, I couldn’t believe how strong the glue was since originally I was afraid of it not holding.

Hours later I get home and I wiggle the tooth back and forth to release the glue from my actual tooth and it lets lose fairly easily. I automatically realize how weird my tooth feels…realizing that all that glue was left behind to stick to my tooth. All night I tried to get this glue off my teeth. I can’t even close my mouth right to eat or anything!! Desperate, I get online to the reviews of the order and slowly realize that these are molds!! The glue it comes with is what goes inside these molds to “form” the fake vampire teeth that you then have to buy your own glue for to place the formed vampire tooth to your tooth. You DO NOT glue the fake mold to your tooth!

I am in tears bc this will not come off my teeth and I have great teeth! 5,000 dollar mouth that is now probably ruined because of this product! Nowhere did it explain this! The directions make it sound like you place the mold to your tooth! Wtf?! I’m so mad right now and so uncomfortable!

Make sure you read the product reviews fully before ordering!!!

title: There is something addictive about this gummy vitamin, but I like it.
text:
Let me start off by saying my immune system is pretty great even without these gummies. But I like sugar and I like Vitamin C. Throw in "2020" and I figured why not inhale some Zinc.

Anyway, here are my takeaways:

Taste: Delicious. That almost too good but intriguing taste that makes you want to keep eating them, but you know you can't. It's a cross between jam, jelly, and purple (lol) gummy bears.

Scent: Reminds me of my childhood. It's sunny, the rain just subsided, but I'm leaving my doctor's office? The scent is confusing but nostalgic. If I had to sum it up, I would say it's a mix of lolly pops from the doctor and hard candy on a spring afternoon.

Touch: Feels... like a cloud? I don't know. If you care about how it feels, just ask it. But I promise it won't answer back.

Appearance: Purple.

Sound: The gummies didn't answer me back. I tried.

It might be the pandemic isolation getting to me, but I think my experience with this gummy vitamin is the same as everybody else. A love like no other. A generational romance. A moving encounter. Genuine. Funny. Tasteful.

That's all I have to say. If you found my review helpful, please let me know.

title: Thick presssure-relieving cushion.
text:
I purchased the extra-large purple double seat cushion directly from the company. The extra-large version is wider and longer, but is otherwise the same. This is a very good pressure-relieving seat cushion. Anyone who sits for a long time and has noticed numbness or pain spots on their bum would do well to use one of these cushions. The cushion is reversible, with a soft side make with larger squares, and a firmer side made with a more dense pattern of smaller squares. I have been using the cushion for several days and it has definitely eliminated pressure points on my bum. Time will tell how long the cushion will last, but given its construction, I would say likely a long time. It comes with a cover of thin, flexible material for optional use. One side has thicker material with small bumps to reduce slippage, but I have used the cushion on both sides and the material feels fine either way.

I give this cushion 4 stars instead of 5 because 1) It is very thick which will change how a chair will fit your body. I had to lower my chair, raise the back and add a lumbar support pillow. Used on my recliner, it raises the seat position high enough that the built-in chair headrest feels a bit too low. 2) The front edge of the cushion, unlike other versions, has no contour, so there is some pressure on the bottom of your thighs at the edge of the cushion. This might be improved by just cutting some of the pad with scissors to create a contoured front, but it would have been better if that was a feature.

Because of the thickness and absence of contouring, I am thinking of getting the Royal purple pad version: less thickness and contoured.

I don't know how this compares with other cushions, but it does do an excellent job of relieving pressure points, and anyone having issues with that should get a pressure-relieving cushion such as this one. I tried a couple of different conventional chair pads with poor results.

11/29/2020: I've increased the rating to 5 stars because this cushion still works so well. One end of the cushion is mildly thinner. I tried this toward the front and the back. I like it towards the front since it eliminates pressure on the bottom of my thighs. I no longer use a lumbar support. I think simply adjusting the back height of my chair fixed any issues there. The cushion hasn't shown any signs of flattening or wear, which is surprising since I use it a LOT. Even the covering, which seems thin and maybe a bit fragile, hasn't failed nor does it look worn. So, I am really glad I bought this extra-large deluxe version and it is holding up amazingly well. It works far better than any other pad I have ever tried.

My hair is angled (longer on one side, shorter on the other), and when I cut the extensions to match, they looked like they were my real hair. I didn't cut them too short, I just layered them. I've straightened them and they didn't get damaged at all.

Now yesterday, I decided to dye my hair aqua, and because the extensions were a bit too dark to dye, I bleached them. They aren't damaged at all. I was very surprised. No hair fell out and they didn't think out either. They took the dye extremely well too.

I've see reviews of people saying the hair is too thin. Yes, they are thin. But because my hair is already thin, and for my haircut they need to be thinner at the bottom, they looked extremely natural.

The seller was very nice too. They sent a letter with my package saying they hope I'm happy with the product, and to email them if I had any problems. I appreciated that.

The only thing I wasn't really happy about was when I got them, they were so bent up. I had to turn my straightener to the highest setting and they still took a while to straighten out. We've been using these energy drinks for a few years now to give us a boost at the mid-point of our long-distance runs. We find the small bottles are easy to carry in our running clothes, and two of us can share a single bottle to give us just enough of a boost to finish strong. Somewhat surprisingly, these drinks don't seem to make us at all jittery.

Occasionally, if the taste seems a little strong, we dilute the drink with a little water. And we'd caution others to be careful about consuming these drinks if engaging in very intense exercise on a completely empty stomach as they can sometimes cause a little queasiness.

Still, when it comes to 5-Hour Energy, on big running days, we don't leave home without it!

I will continue looking for a reliable source at a reasonable price. Or I may try simply taking pure ground psyllium husks with water. title: This helps with more than just balance problems. well designed.
text:
Just what I needed. This review is for the style #2. I have bone on bone hip pain. I am scheduled for first hip surgery in 4 weeks. My problem is putting my full weight on my hips (230 lbs). not just balance. It looks to me that most walkers/rollators appear to be for addressing only balance problems. I searched for a rollator built sturdy and a design where you walk between the rear wheels, not behind them. THIS IS IT. This unit is well designed, it will fit thru doors 25" wide. The main connections are welded aluminum alloy, not plastic like I saw on other models. Sturdy enough that it will take some weight off my hips. I can use the inside wheel break to turn corners on a dime. The seat us also useful to carry something (like a laundry basket). In the event you need to go thru a doorway less than 25" you can just pull up on the folding strap and the walker gets more narrow with the wheels still on the floor. Attention to detail. there is even a reflector on the front wheels. Rated for 300 lbs and is MORE STURDY than my previous 2 wheel walker rated for 500 lbs.
You will not be disappointed.

title: Works better than advertised
text:
I have used this product twice now, one month apart, on my car and my wife’s car. It contains both car wash and sealant, so I don't have to wax after washing (this is why I purchased it). The gloss and feel of the paint after washing is amazing. Repeat washings are much easier. I also wash the wheels with it and repeat washings of them are also so much easier.

CarPros’ website emphasizes rinsing this product off within 30 seconds of application to reduce the risk of streaking, and I have followed their advice religiously with no streaking issues. Also, based on a YouTube video recommendation, I only use 6 ounces of product per gallon of water to reduce the risk of streaking instead of 14 ounces per gallon, which is the 1:9 ratio of product to water that is recommended.

Before I began using this product I sealed the outside glass with Adam’s glass sealant. Now after washing the car and windows with Hydrofoam, I just use Adam’s glass boost to clean/add sealant between car washings.

Another YouTube video showed that pH-neutral products like Hydrofoam really don't work as a prewash to lift dirt off the car before actually contact-washing the car (i.e. using a mitt). Therefore, I don't bother with presoaking the car with this product; I just give the car a good rinse with water before washing.

I like Hydrofoam so much that after using up my initial 16-ounce purchase, I bought a one-gallon container of it.

title: Lovely Lashes Eyelash Curler Review
text:
I was thrilled to receive the Lovely Lashes Eyelash Curler in the mail! As I opened the pink box, I found the eyelash curler and an extra pad. I have always curled my eyelashes be applying mascara and, sometimes, even if I’m not wearing makeup. I find it makes my eyes look bigger and I look more awake than I sometimes feel!
I have used some curlers that are hard to open and close. Some have pulled my eyelashes out of my lid and pinched my lid. I am very picky on what I use now after learning my lesson the hard way.
The first thing I noticed when I opened the box was the inscription Lovely Lashes on the eyelash curler. I know, you’re thinking that not important but I thought it was cute. The handles are outlined with black rubber so your fingers can fit comfortably. That’s important too! You don’t want fingers slipping and sliding or you may be getting eyelash removal instead of curl.
I tested the eyelash curler by opening and closing the curling tool. The movements were smooth with no hitches. I placed my lashes in the curler and closed. I was able to get the tool to the base of my lashes and squeezed for 10 seconds. The directions say 5-10 seconds and my lashes can be stubborn! There was no tugging, no pulling, and no pinching! When I opened and removed the tool, my lashes were gorgeous, if I do say so myself! They had the perfect curl and I immediately looked more alert and wide eyed.
The only thing I wish could have been different with this product is something to place the extra pad in. I have a place to put it but am always afraid of losing tiny pieces. My answer to that problem is possibly placing the eyelash curler and extra pad in a small pouch or container that I could put in on my vanity. I do feel like this eyelash curler will last for a very long time, as I can replace the pad when the first one displays wear. My verdict is five stars. I recommend this product but only if you love your lashes!

title: Great foot stool for people who play string instruments:)
text: As someone who is new to playing instruments, this guitar foot stool is awesome because it allows me to rest my foot without the strain.  I do not know if there is a weight limit to this stool but since you are only putting one foot on it, you should be okay.  As a violin player, your body can take on the effects of  sitting and leaning for a long time and can cause pain after years of playing. The guitar stool is used mainly for sitting and playing instruments as I am currently using it to practice my violin at home. The design of this foot stool is to  to elevate the leg your leg a  bit so your body is not in a hunched over position while playing, which can become painful after a while of playing. The foot stool has several different height positions to choose from so whether your short or tall, there is a setting for just about anyone. The adjustable levels are made by moving one of the legs on the bottom and selecting one of the groove positions. The material used to produce this product are sturdy and seem to be of good quality so I don't have to worry about it breaking after the initial use. Again, you are just resting your foot on the stool instead of applying your entire weight.  It features a padded surface for the foot rest part, which allows for a more comfortable foot position and it has a slip resistant surface so your foot is not moving around. As someone who tends to wear shoes that has horrible traction, this foot stool allows me to rest comfortable with slipping. Upon initial usage, it will take some getting used to and might feel uncomfortable  for the first two times because your muscles are getting used to the resting stage instead of flat.  The great thing about this feature is that each foot rests has a protective piece attached to prevent any scratches to your floor or surface. This is the added bonus because I can literally use this foot stool anywhere without worrying about it damaging my floor especially if they are tile or wooden.  This guitar foot stool can easily put in your tool bag and easy to carry around since it is lightweight and folds up easily for storage. I don;t have anything negative to say about this item because it does the job that it was made to do which is to support your foot. title: Quiet and Efficient
text:
For many years I'd used foil shavers to get a close shave; they worked well but were noisy and needed expensive replacements for the foils and cutters, so I decided to try a rotary shaver. The first one I tried was inexpensive, worked well for a while, didn't hold a charge well, and totally died after six months. I've had the Dynabliss just a short time, but at this point it works very well.
This shaver costs much less than the replacement parts for a foil razor. It's quiet, shaves close, and keeps a charge very well. It is easy to clean without a brush--just run water through the cutters. The shape and size of this shaver is the same as that of the failed rotary shaver, but the cutting blades on this one seem stronger to me.The body of this shaver--like the body of the previous shaver-- seems slippery when wet; it would help to have something rough or rubbery to make the shaver feel more secure in my hand.
The shaver does a good job on the neck, cutting close with no irritation when shaving wet. In fact, my experience tells me to use electric shavers wet--never dry--and using shave cream or gel (not foam).
I don't expect to return to foil shaving again. Incidentally, this shaver is so quiet that I can listen to music while shaving.

title: Best shaker. It has all the features I need except for one.
text:
This shaker would be perfect except for one flaw (more below), but it was still the best shaker I was able to find.

Features needed:
1) Triggers quickly on phone ring (my phone system ringers are unreliable for technical reasons that won't change anytime soon).
2) Does not trigger on extraneous signals and/or background noise.
3) Stays buzzing (for at least a minute) even if/after the ringing stops.
4) Has a backup battery in addition to the AC supply.
5) Does not keep buzzing forever if no one is home to reset it. (Should auto reset after 1 or 2 minutes. Or this delay might be user adjustable.)

Surprisingly, I wasn't able to find these features in any other unit.
The KBS300RX satisfies the first 4 requirements nicely when used in conjunction with the KA300 transmitter (required).

Alas, the shaker, once triggered will keep going forever until the reset button is pushed. This is great for heavy sleepers but bad for the many calls when no one is home. It greatly increases wear on the shaker motor and, potentially, could drain the backup battery excessively in a power outage.

title: Decent Flashlight, Bad packaging
text:
I bought this flashlight to replace my old Makita swivel head flashlight that had recently died because I dropped it from 3ft. The Energizer flashlight has 4 bright LEDs for decent lighting and a nice solid case. The head swivels nicely and it does feel like I can drop it from 15 feet and it will survive. I bought it for the sole purpose of working under the car. The flashlight itself is probably a 4 star, but I'm giving it 2 because:

The name of this product also describes the packaging. The packaging on this product is one of those packages that you will want to wear safety glasses and gloves to open. Getting the flashlight out took the use of a razor blade and wire cutter. I hate using razor blades for hard packaging because it's easy to slip and take the tip of your finger off like I have done many times. Getting the the batteries out is another monster. I hacked one side up with aviator snips and wire cutters, damaging the batteries in the process and used a small hack saw for the other side. I don't usually have such issues with product packaging but this was over the top and very hard plastic. If you can manage to get a utility to cleanly cut those two tabs off the back you may be better off, wire cutters and scissors do not fit. I managed to stumble across how to put in the batteries in while playing around with it but many people have issues with it (Search google if you don't believe me). You simply turn the bottom counter clockwise to open, remove that awkward battery holster, and insert the batteries.

While other DNA tests like National Geographic tell you your Neanderthal percentage, Insitome goes a step further - it actually goes in-depth into 10 traits that you have inherited either from Neanderthals or Homo Sapiens. I have 1.4% overall percentage, with 5 from Neanderthals and 5 from Homo Sapiens. Incredibly interesting and I routinely bring this app now at dinners with friends to show them.

My Neanderthal traits: pigmentation, sun damage repair, cognition, fat storage, and pathogen recognition.
My Homo Sapiens traits: Torso shape, high altitude adaptation, interpreting immune signals, viral immune response, and muscle growth and development.

Each trait had a lot of information to learn what it meant and how scientists know where it came from. Incredible!

title: It's a feature for some but a bug for me.
text:
The compartments are roomy enough for all the medications I require on a daily basis. The organizer allows for a full month rather than 28 days. Those are the pluses.

They are not, for me, enough to outweigh the minuses.

The compartments pop open a little too easily. I respect that as a feature for people with arthritis or other joint difficulties but I suffer anxiety and oh, this feature is a bug for me. I had a day's dosage fly all over my room because it popped open on its own when I picked the organizer up.

Also, while the compartments are removable, again, they come out a little too easily. I picked up the organizer and my fingertip knocked a day compartment out. They don't slot or click into place.

So summing up: size of compartments is good. Number of compartments is excellent. But the compartments open and fall out too easily.

title: VERY EFFECTIVE AT WORKING OUT THE KINKS
text:
This Yosager Shiatsu Shoulder Massager is very effective at applying deep pressure on localized areas of the shoulder, neck and back. (I took some close up photos. Let me know if you find this helpful.)

There are two sets of massaging balls. Each set has two small balls and two medium sized balls which rotate. They spin smoothly when applied to the back and you can control the direction of the spin as well as choose two different speeds. You can select a button to have it slightly warmed. The buttons are easy to operate. I love that I could decide how much pressure to apply by putting my forearms through the hand holds and letting my forearms rest in it. It’s easy to slide the whole device up and down the back and to use it on the neck with the use of the hand holds. I was able to use it for my hamstrings and did a great job of helping to loosen it up and decrease muscle soreness.

It’s a lot better than the handheld massager because it’s a lot easier to reach all areas of your back. It also covers twice the area and is a ton more effective with more intense massaging.

It does an incredible job and actually does a better job than my spouse. It allows you to get a great massage when you don’t have someone to give you a massage. It plugs into the wall with an AC adapter and isn’t able to be recharged. This was definitely money well spent.

title: 3rd Generation E.T.
text:
MY BACKGROUND:
I’ve had essential tremors in my hands since I was in my early 30’s. I’m now in my mid-40’s. I'm 3rd generation of essential tremors. (I don't know if it goes back even further than that.) My father also has the same symptoms. My grandmother has it more severely, but also involves head shaking side to side and her voice has tremors worse than Katherine Hepburn.

I was interested in the ingredients and thought I would post some very basic information about them. I really appreciate the combination of these quality ingredients backed by research. It’s aimed at treating tremors and prevention of further deterioration. (Because of the ingredients, I would give it 5 stars. However, read on and I’ll tell you why I docked stars.)

*Methylcobalamin (methyl b-12) 1 mg
---It’s a form of Vitamin B-12.
*Magnesium citrate 100mg
--There is evidence that some people with hypo-magnesium may have symptoms of essential tremors.
*Acetyl L - Carnitine 100mg
*Curcumin extract 100mg
--This is turmeric, which is very beneficial to health in myriad of ways, has also been found to protect nerves.
*Gamma-Aminobutyric acid 100mg
--There is some research that suggests there is GABA dysfunction with tremors.
*L-Tyrosine 100mg
*N-Acetyl Cysteine 150mg
--This has reportedly been found to be very effective in preventing further damage to some nerves due to oxidative stress.
*Skullcap 20mg
--This is a mild relaxant which is also used for anxiety. It has reportedly been found to ease tremors.

I didn’t experience any change in the tremors. However, I only took this for a month. Perhaps after a few months there may be results. I feel like this should be taken over a longer period of time to see if it makes an improvement. And of course I can’t vouch for preventative measures. At the moment, I can’t afford to continue taking it. If I had the financial means, I would take it for the possibility of preventing it from becoming worse. This concoction of ingredients at least gives some hope. And hopefully over time more studies will accumulate to further address essential tremors. At least essential tremors are now being recognized and understood by the medical and science community more than they had 20 years ago! So, although I love the ingredients and the possibility that it may prevent further deterioration, I felt like I had to dock it 2 stars because I couldn’t vouch that it would work, since I only took it for 1 month.

I value credible, informative, and candid Amazon reviews by other Amazon buyers and hope this review helps you. Although I received this product at a discount in exchange for my honest and unbiased review, I don’t spend all this time and energy to post non-truthful reviews. My time is worth more than saving a couple of bucks. I’m posting for your benefit. Please click “HELPFUL” if you appreciate the effort.

title: Hey, these are pretty good!
text: I have yet to compare these to HearDrops or HearSafe ear plugs, which are slightly more expensive, which is why I bought these, but these are pretty good. I've been a professional musician for some 20 years and I've worn a lot of different ear protection in a lot of different situations. I prefer wearing nothing in or over my ears, but sometimes that's just not a good idea. The problem with most ear plugs, especially the cheaper ones, is that they totally kill the higher frequencies because those short frequency waves cannot get through while the larger and longer low frequencies are still audible; so you end up with low, rumbling, unclear sound. You need the high frequencies for clarity and to understand a conversation. These DownBeats manage to let in some of the highs that you lose with most plugs. They're not perfect, but they're good, especially if you get used to their sound. Frankly, that they let those highs in at all is a big plus. I have yet to try them as an audience member. Perhaps I'll update this when I do. There's definitely not much of a handle on them, so some users will find them difficult to handle, but I have no trouble.

title: "ultimate" food sensitivity test
text:
Yank a few chest hairs, throw it in their pre-addressed (but not postage-paid) envelope, find a stamp, send it in, wait over a week before getting an email acknowledgement that the sample was received (I don't think it takes a week for first class mail to get from AZ to TX, but, okay....), and then wait a few weeks more for the actual results.

the .pdf report that I was sent was extremely detailed, but with questionable results. My test results claimed I have extensive dairy sensitivities including sensitivities to other foods which I seem to tolerate just fine and have never had any difficulty with. I am tempted to get a 2nd kit and send it in to see if I get the same results.

There is no information included about the actual science behind the testing, it's all smoke/mirrors, "we test DNA", ok, that's great, but a link to a scientific study actually backing this testing would be nice (and would be expected from my perspective as a healthcare professional).

Questionable accuracy, extended wait for test results. Expensive. The report looks nice but I have my (serious) doubts. Would not recommend.

title: Quality book, cute yet classy, and simple to fill out
text:
I'm picky about styles and materials and I liked this book by far the best of those I saw in person (for a boy, in this price range, and amount of effort you'd have to put into filling it out). It's a very simple book with a cute yet classy design and includes good prompts to record your little guy's babyhood. I'm not a scrapbooker and don't have the know-how/time to put together a completely personalized book but this one was really cute with the letter on the cover to individualize the child's name. Also, I really hate how some books are either WAY too general so you don't get very much detail on the kid, or WAY too specific about the parents or religious ceremonies, etc. (i.e., I DON'T have a doctorate degree and don't want pages that deal with each parents' career highlights and advanced degrees. Yes, I've seen books like that at Target and Walmart, where I don't think those types of people would shop anyway because those books weren't great quality either.) This book had several pages that you could do whatever you wanted with. Like a page for a "Special Day" instead of a specific type of religious ceremony, then you can use it for a ceremony OR whatever else you want. There are cute pockets for saving hair, etc. and a few extra page protectors if you want to add documents. And of course, it has plenty of pages with the classic questions that apply to every baby and that every parent wants to remember :)

And best of all, it's easy to fill out! I kept an extra fine point sharpie marker in the box for the first year of my son's life and my husband and I took just a few minutes once every few months to update it and that's all it took! Anyone can do this, even people like me who start projects and never finish them! (I'm pregnant with a baby girl now and we're buying the girl version for her without actually seeing the book because I trust it's a good product.)

title: Amazing product, can't live without them now
text:
Before I found Silver Linings, I could never really go sockless. Its such an embarrassing problem, and I am a stickler for anti-bacterial, anti-germs, and cleanliness in general. Every time I bough a cute new pair of ballet flats, they'd inevitably end up in the trash a couple weeks later because the stink would start to get out of control. No amount of daily foot scrubbing with anti-bac soap, powders, etc would keep it at bay, and my feet would slide around from moisture in my shoes after several hours in them. You see, I live in a city where a LOT of walking and being on my feet is done. And ballet flats or sneakers are pretty much my only option - I can't wear open heels for 10 hours a day. This problem really got me down and made me feel icky. I never understood it when I'd see girls sockless in super expensive flats.

I was skeptical when I first tried Silver Linings as I just didn't get how they could ever work. But they do! Like magic! Not only are my feet daisy fresh all day, but they're completely dry too. I finally have the confidence to take my shoes off around others. I think this product is truly a miracle, and has really solved a nuisance problem for me. I've been using these for years now and I'll continue to buy them as long as they're offered and I'm at the point where I don't use anything else.

A few things to be aware of --

- they don't adhere the greatest to shoes that are fabric on the inside. I have to stop and adjust them because they sometimes shift around in my shoes. Though I love that they don't have an adhesive and won't ruin my shoes, I sometimes wish they did just do they'd stay put. This is mentioned in a LOT of other reviews and it's true - with certain types of fabric insoles they will slide around. This is easily remedied with a touch of superglue. Vinyl, Plastic, or Foam insoles? They stick and stay put just fine.

- Also, for those particularly tight and un-breathable shoes, I wish they'd come out with a full foot version. The half is sufficient (at least for me) in most shoes, but I do have a couple that I have to be careful with because the heel isn't protected.
- They're a bit expensive, and you have to replace them every couple weeks. (Or sooner, depending on how frequently you wear the shoes). I think ChuShu may be alienating certain consumers by not offering a product that lasts longer and has a bit of a high price tag. I was so thankful for the 5-pair value pack they were offering.

Reminder that you CANT just stick these into already stinky shoes and hope they eliminate the odor. They work best on clean shoes as a preventative. I've ordered 2 pairs of my favorite ballet flats and the second pair have wayyyy outlasted the first pair with the use of Silver Linings.

Overall, I LOVE this product and know a ton more women would too if they knew about them and had easy accessibility to them. I really think they should be in every walgreens, walmart, and CVS around the block, much more than that Dr. Sholls garbage.

title: I loved the scale when it was working
text: I will begin by saying that I am not  a computer savvy person.  I loved the scale when it was working.  I got it set up after quite a bit of work but was satisfied once it was on line.  Then we upgraded our router and got a faster DSL speed.  There was no way that I could get the Aria set up again either through the desk top or mobile phone.  I spent hours on this.  Finally Fitbit customer support told me to contact our internet provider and  have them change the protocol.  Our internet provider, Fairpoint,  said that this was a very unusual request and that it would slow our internet back down.  I called Fitbit again and got a representative who told me that the Aria's technology would not work with the new, faster routers.  She said that they were working on improving the technology.  I now have an expensive scale that does exactly the same thing as my old, offline scale does.  I am going to send it back.  If you are thinking of purchasing one I would check out what your protocol number is.  I believe that the Aria works on 802.11b.  I would love to hear that there is some work around so that I could get the scale  back on line.

title: ... started sharing pictures of these brushes or a brush like this. (Note
text:
****Attention**** To all of you women that have been eyeballing one of these when FB started sharing pictures of these brushes or a brush like this. (Note: after doing my research, the one being sold on FB is an expensive piece of crap. Never buy anything without reviews!)

With all that being said, I'm not a reviewer but if I were I would totally give the Apalus Straightener Brush a thumbs up and a 4-4.5 star rating. It does exactly what it says it will do.

•It straightens your hair.

•It has a power button and two temperature control button settings that go up and down in temperature.

•It can go as high as 450 degrees.
Being my hair is so damaged from this last go around trying to get my hair lightened to go grey. I started at 390 and quickly set it down on 360. I still think this is too high. I have seen the review videos on YouTube and did my research before I purchased this. The ratings on Amazon where phenomenal. I don't purchase anything without a 4 star or above rating usually.

•out of 1835 reviews, it rated 3.7 out of 4 stars. That was good enough for me out of that many reviews.

•It comes in two colors pink/ black and black/ teal (picture below).

•it has a swivel cord so no tangled cords and the cord is long.

•it is definitely made for all types of hair. I watch several videos on all sorts of hair textures and ethnicities and actually thought "this might be too hot for my hair" because I'm Caucasian and have fine, damaged hair. But with the temperature control it works just fine.

Cons or possible cons:
•it doesn't straighten your hair like a flat iron because it doesn't flatten the hair. It still gives you body and makes your hair feel full not flat but It gives you that straight look that you are looking. If you are wanting the flat iron straight look this isn't for you. But for the price of 29.99 it was totally worth adding to my collection for those days I don't want to curl my hair or straighten it.

•in order to get the results that you want you will have to section off the hair. When you do this, it gets pretty darn close to the skin/ root without burning your skin because the rubber nobs don't get hot.

•straighten the hair first from underneath the strand for a fuller look and for the brush to come in contact with all strands of hair. It won't come in contact with all of the hair if you use it like a regular brush.

•it's kind of heavy, but my arm didn't get tired of using it. Although, it's easy to clonk yourself upside the head with so be careful.

• my biggest con with this is that the back of the brush gets extremely hot. I usually put my pointer finger on the back of my brush or curling iron to guide it but quickly learned to grab somewhere else. 😉

• the little rubber nobs on the ends of the "bristles" of the brush does pull a little but not to the point where it kept me from using it. (We will see how this works out).

If this thing carried a bit more oomph power wise it would be awesome with the other attachments. But alas it just doesn't measure up. Save your dollars as it will cost you more in the long run having to find a better products for the jobs this is supposedly intended to do.

Edit: so within 24 hours of my review going live the company reached out to me to express their regret of this product not working for me and issued a full refund with no other requirements from myself. Although my review stands on this product, I appreciate it greatly that a company would care so much about customer satisfaction and customer service, that they would reach out like they have. This is why I am a loyal Amazon member and customer as I have always received top notch customer service. title: CARLSON'S FISH OIL HAS BEEN LIKE A MIRACLE IN A BOTTLE FOR ME!
text:
Of all the supplements I take, and that's at least a dozen, this is the one I will never give up! I had a thumb that was locked up for a year, I assume from arthritis, which I have in both hands. 3 weeks after I started Carlson's Fish Oil, my thumb unlocked and was perfectly normal again. I have had no problems with my hands since I started taking it, which has been 5-6 years now. While that is so great, it's not even the best part. I was in my 50s when I started this (and if you're over 40 you'll relate), and I had brain fog...that wonderful thing that happens with age, where you just aren't thinking as fast and clear as you did in your youth. I like to say that Carlson's gave me back my 20 year old brain! I was most impressed with how sharp my thinking was after about a month! So exciting!

I do take one medication for my arthritis, but I think a large amount of credit goes to my fish oil for keeping me pain free. As a side note, I took fish oil capsules for years, with no noticeable effect.

I love the lemon flavor and I drink it straight. I think it tastes just fine and leaves no fishy aftertaste.

The place I'd always bought this from jumped up several dollars in price, so I thought I'd give my favorite shopping site a look, not really expecting to find my beloved fish oil on Amazon, and what a surprise - there it was, cheaper than I'd ever seen it anywhere!

No matter what your age is, you owe it to yourself to give this amazing product a try! I'm so thankful I did!

title: Slightly less symptons but not quite my solution.
text: About 3 months ago I had thorough allergy tests done: blood and skin prick, for over 300 different allergens including the most popular, gluten, milk (dairy), peanuts, etc.  All came out normal.  The Doctor prescribed Zyrtec, of which I have been taking now for nearly 2 months on an as needed basis (about every 4 - 7 days).  I researched my symptoms and being that Zyrtec helps alleviate my symptoms, severe itchyness all over and some slight burning sensations, I believe I have Histamine Intolerance (HIT).  It got really bad one day I ate Bologna which is considered a "high histamine" producer.  Anyway, I have been taking Vitamin C complex 2000mg (Vitaminshoppe), Vitamin B-6 (Solgar) & Copper (Multi-Vitamin w/ 2mg), which supposedly helps boost Diamine Oxydase production -the main enzyme that breaks down Histamine- but its not working fast enough.  I bought a bottle of DAOSin about 2 weeks ago and have been taking it too.  I have felt diminished symptoms, but not enough to be tolerable and still find myself having to take a Zyrtec when it gets unbearable.  I recently read about taking Black Seed Oil (Nigella Sativa) & Quercetin which I recommend you research.  Black Seed Oil includes a natural anti-histamine and many other incredible benefits.  Quercetin also prevents certain histamine(s) from producing and helps boost enzyme production, maybe DAO?, so I am trying this too.  My symptoms, other than severe itchyness, burning sensation in my feet (mostly), and slight indigestion are transparent, meaning not physically noticeable.  I can't say that DAOSin has been my "cure" but I also feel I can't say it's working, so I am just relaying information and you decide.  I don't think I'll continue to buy it if after a month if I still have to take Zyrtec when I get a reaction.  To everyone I encourage, do your research and try the natural way as best you can.

title: Probably works. Works counting steps anyhow.
text:
Tried to set up the pedometer and it's far more complicated than a mere mortal can figure out. It's so complicated that I can't keep track of where I am in the setup process long enough for it to keep it's current setting to know what the next step is I have to take. It keeps going back to ground zero after a mere 5 seconds or so. You have to have a photographic memory to avoid starting all over again in the sequence of setup steps. It took me about 45 minutes to set up the basic parameters.

I haven't the faintest idea what the strap that goes in the strap holder is for because it's way to small to put around your neck and it's a joke that the instructions suggest you do that. If I drape it around my arm it doesn't register anything when I move around. If I put it in my pocket it increases the step count on average of 2 steps for every step I take. My brain was exhausted by the time I got to the part that supposed to tell you things like activity time, checking your ongoing achievements, and using the memory function, and view stored data in memory mode.

I took it jogging with me in my front left pocket and took over 7,000 steps in 4 miles. I registered just over 2,800 steps. Oddly, when I trudged downstairs after the jog, it registered one step per step down. So if I did all my exercise climbing steps maybe it would work. But for my exercise I jog 4 miles per day, and so it just doesn't work for what I do. 2/5/16 It seems to count steps okay now. That's all I really need it for. The rest is too complicated for the satisfaction it brings to come to grips with it. But my 4 mile jog is the same every day except for my speed. The step count is an indication of my speed: the longer my stride, the faster I jog and the fewer strides I take.

title: Reliable product - seems effective
text:
I had twin premature babies born in 2010. At that time, with the RSV scare and all, I was looking for products that would help keep them safe and sick-free. After a lot of research, and assuming some risk, I bought a bunch of Germ Guardian products, including a GG-1000 air sanitizer. When I got the product in hand, I knew that the application for this neat little thing will be limited and specific. Since I wanted an air purifier in the babies room, I did not choose to use this for the room.

The GG-1000 is a small, great looking product that sanitizes the air in a closed environment using UV-C. Because of its size and airflow it is best suited for small spaces like the bathroom or a small study, or as in my case, in a vehicle. I chose to plug in the GG-1000 in my car, which has a low enough air volume to justify using this small device. Its size and plug-prong configurations make it convenient to use in the limited in-car space too. Since the plug socket in my car is connected to the ignition key, I have left the device in there permanently connected; and it comes on when I start the car and turns off when I shut off the car.

My babies turned 1 a month ago, and the air sanitizer has been with us for the same duration, and its been there since then. It continues to work and continues to have no issues - although my usage pattern is not 24x7, which might be the case if you are plugging it in a room in the house.

Once in a while, the fan does start whining, but this seems to be sporadic and temporary - and seems to happen only as it starts. The whining, when it does come up, does stop within 5-10 minutes of starting and is not loud at all (sounds like a desktop PC when turned on).

On long trips, when the device has had chance to cycle the air in the car atleast once, it did seem to give a "sanitized" smell/feel to the air.

Unfortunately, I have no other way of measuring the sanitizer's effectiveness, except through the perceived comfort to mind it provides. I had purchased the GG-1000 as a refurbished product on clearance directly from Germ Guardian, and the price I paid then (@ less than 20), continues to justify the risk I took of trying an unknown product.

Given my experience with the GG-1000, if I wanted another one for a second vehicle then I would be happy to spend the full price to purchase it again (that is if it were not still available in clearance for the reduced price).

title: Highly Effective Brand
text:
This is the best tea tree oil (Melaleuca) product that I have ever used and I highly recommend it to anyone who is looking to try it!

I have lupus and it primarily affects my skin. I have been trying various essential oils and recipes to address my skin problems in a natural way because I do not like using steroid creams. After reading up on how good tea tree oil is for use as a first aid product, acne treatment and eczema treatment, I started using the oils at my local shopping center. The products there were okay, but I did not find the high level of success that others had documented so I started experimenting with the different brands of essential oils. By far, the New York Biology brand has been the best product that I have tried to date.

The first thing to note is that it smells stronger than most other brands I have tried. Tea tree oil has a very unique smell that is difficult to describe and not everyone will like it. It has a spicy, medicinal tone that I do like so it does not bother me. Because this product is so strong, as soon as I opened the bottle and took a sniff, it opened up my sinuses! Big plus! The good thing is that the scent can be adjusted by diluting the tea tree oil if you find the scent not to your liking. I also liked that this product has a dropper that allows me to be very accurate with the placement of the product when used alone or when mixing it with other products. Usually, it is suggested that you need to use a specific number of drops for various purposes and it is difficult to get the mixes exactly right when you do not use a dropper.

Next, the uses of tea tree oil are many. I have read several books and websites to discover which uses I was most interested in trying. I first tried it as aromatherapy using my diffuser. That worked great as a way to freshen the air. Then I used it in my vaporizer to help with congestion and stuffy sinuses and it decreased the amount of time it took for me to feel relief to about 10 minutes. I read that it could be used to keep cuticles healthy so I tried that this time and it did work. I developed a small pimple during the time I was testing the oil and so I was able to apply it at night before I went to sleep and when I woke up the pimple was gone. (Please note that it is recommended that you perform a skin test to determine if you can use the oil directly on your skin or if you need to mix it with a carrier oil. I do not mix mine unless I have a specific recipe that requires mixing.) I got a paper cut while going through my mail so I tried the tea tree oil on that and it quickly took away the stinging. I used the oil in my bath and it did help relax my muscles, but I found that if I combined tea tree oil, epsom salt and lavender in a really warm bath, I got the biggest bang for my buck: Open sinuses, relaxed muscles and calmed mind!

Finally, I thought that it was an interesting fun fact that it is believed that the Aborigines of Australia have been using this product for centuries and the New York Biology brand specifies that its product originates in Australia on the bottle. They know what their doing and it shows in this high quality product. They offer a money back guarantee that you will love their product, or they will provide you with a refund.

I was provided with a free sample to test and critique. #NewYorkBiology

title: Will see how well this supplement works for our aching joints
text:
(Disclaimer - My wife and I were invited by the seller to try and review their products. We only agree to these requests when it's something we would actually use. The fact we received them for free has no bearing on our review, and we have written negative reviews in the past for products we were sent for free. But we tend to accept more review invitations for quality products, so that's why many of these invited reviews have high ratings. Also, for this type of invited review, we always begin with a disclaimer.)

Neither my wife or have have tried glucosamine before, but as we entered middle-age, our joints and skin are starting to show significant wear. For the past few summers after we both turned 40, we've been getting a lot of problems with our joints--mostly in our wrists, fingers, and shoulders. And being a beautiful woman, my wife is willing to try anything to keep her skin looking young (as long as it's safe). So even though we never tried glucosamine before, we have tried other Viva Labs products before and trust the brand. And this being a combination of three different ingredients seems like a good idea.

We just started taking this supplement so it's hard to tell if it's doing anything yet, but so far, it's at least easy to swallow and has no strange smell of taste (I can't stand the smell of some supplements--they make me gag). We'll continue to take it and see if it really improves the health of our joints and skin, and if so, we'll update this review.

title: Look nice and work well
text:
Sometimes I am at events where I really want to wear earplugs, but it just wouldn't "look nice" or "be appropriate." These do the trick! I ordered the rose gold ones, as they don't stand out significantly against my skin tone. They came with 3 sizes each of silicone and foam tips, and I really appreciated being able to try them all and having both types to use based on what I need the plugs for. The foam ones seem to block more sound.

These are a little uncomfortable to sleep on, but not the end of the world. If you need total sound blocking for sleep, these are not it, nor are they designed to be.

I appreciated the sturdy little storage bag which was included. It's just large enough to hold the loop, a set of foam plugs, and a set of silicone plugs. I keep it in my bag at all times.

The silicone tips have a bit of a seam around the circumference as part of production. Parts of the seam aren't trimmed as well and cut the inside of my ears--not enough to bleed, but they do hurt. Unfortunately, it's not sticking out enough that I would be able to trim it myself without cutting the plug. I just put up with it for the few hours I have to wear them. Honestly, I'm a little surprised that the skin on that part of my ear is so fussy. Looking at it, it doesn't look like it would be an issue. Who knew?

Also, these are, hands down, the easiest, fastest earplugs to insert I've ever tried. I can discretely slip them in, rather than engaging in the calisthenics usually involved with fitting earplugs.

I do recommend these for volume reduction with retained general clarity of sound (musicians may have other opinions!)

title: These are key to making a  mask work for various sized faces.
text: I wish I could draw a diagram of how I use these toggles.  I will try to explain it.  First you need to have a seam on the ends of the masks or if you are making them yourself, overlap the material to make a narrow channel for the elastic cord to slide through.  Then I take a hair "PIN" not a bobbie pin. and slide the pin over the elastic with the curved back of the pin towards you. The narrow ends of the pin will fit nicely into the holes of the toggle. push the pin through the toggle bringing the elastic cord with it and slide the toggle down the elastic. Pull the toggle up and down to tighten/ loosen the elastic.  It will make your mask perfectly adjustable and comfortable. When I make masks for my family I send extra toggles and a hair pin with them.  It is much safer with the new virus variants to have a secure fitting mask.

title: Product is mislabeled with incorrect serving size -- only provides 24 servings, not 34!
text:
UPDATE!!! (4/5/22)

Okay... I can't believe they actually did this. This seller is sleazy.

Instead of simply increasing the amount of blueberry powder you get -- which would have been the normal and decent thing to do IMO -- or decreasing the number of servings listed on the package (to make it accurate to what you're getting), they instead opted (after I complained in my review below, apparently) to REDUCE the total amount of blueberry powder you get (from 3.5g down to 2.5g) AND cut in HALF the recommended serving size from 2tsp. down to 1tsp., and are now claiming that by reducing the volume of actual blueberry powder you're getting by almost a third, they are MAGICALLY increasing the number of "apparent" servings you are getting by almost 30%, which is now claimed to be 48 servings versus the original 34 claimed servings (which was actually 24 servings). So, basically, by cutting the serving size in half, and reducing the powder weight by 29%, you're now getting 2x the actual previous number of servings (see my original review below).

I cannot believe people are this unethical in business on Amazon! Amazon needs to hold sellers like this accountable for their misleading advertising. Stop playing games and just deliver a good product at a fair and *straightforward* price and quit playing games with your amounts, serving sizes, and number of servings. It's very misleading -- and I believe this has been done very much intentionally.

/rant

------------------

Original review:

The packaging claims there are 34 servings. One serving is shown as being 2 tsp.

It was running out very fast, so I decided to measure how much a serving size weighed.

1 tsp weighs approximately 3.5 grams (averaged across a couple of teaspoons), thus a 2 tsp serving is 7 grams.

There are 6 ounces (allegedly -- I should have weighed it when I received the bag). Thus, the bag provides only 24 servings, not 34. Big difference! So, I was not imagining things. It really did run out fast (30% faster than it should have).

It is mislabeled as providing more servings than it actually does.

I'm annoyed because A) It's expensive, B) It ran out long before all the other smoothie ingredients I bought, which *will* last at least a month, as I expected this to do.

I wish I could get a refund. Not happy when products are mislabeled like this. I don't know if it's careless or deliberate to make it seem like you're getting more servings than you actually are in order to try to compete better with other products, as no, I would *not* have spent that much money for only 24 servings.

title: Mouth Slime Galore!!!
text: I gave this toothpaste two stars only because it does clean your mouth, but also creates mouth slime galore! I had been using the toothpaste for about two months. About a month ago, I noticed I started getting this slimy substance inside my mouth. It would occur all day long, and I could gather/pull out huge gobs of slime!!! It was embarrassing. The inside of my mouth never hurt. No sores of any kind, just alot of white slime. One day my fiance noticed some on the outside corner of my mouth that had somehow escaped from the inside! That's when I realized I needed to research the cause. I was worried it might be thrush or something serious, but didn't think so because I didn't have any pain or sores. I'm not on any medication, so I knew it couldn't be the result of a side effect. Searching the internet I found lots of people with the same condition, and we all had something in common. We used Crest Pro Health toothpaste!!! Interestingly enough, my fiance uses it also and has never had a problem with it. But I'm going to stop using it immediately, and see what happens. I have to assume this is the cause since it only started after I changed from my old toothpaste (Aquafresh) to Crest Pro Health.

title: Functional, but not great
text: I ordered the large Darco toe guard to fit in my men's large Darco square-toed surgical shoe after toe surgery to provide some additional protection during recovery. As far as the primary goal of the product: it absolutely covers and protects the toe. However, I have a few complaints: first, it is enormous and looks fairly ridiculous hanging way off the front of the shoe. It is in no way mold-able by hand as advertised. I would recommend other buyers to be sure you get the smallest size you think you can get away with. It also does not fit into the square-toed shoe well at all; the insole won't go back down into the shoe with the toe-guard in place. I just put the guard in when I'm around the house to protect from the dog and my little ones, and not when I'm in public because it is uncomfortable and unsightly. I would probably buy the product again just because it is functional and fits the Darco shoe, but would try a smaller size (perhaps the women's size?) if I thought I could make it fit.

title: Can't Connect
text:
I love my Fitbit -- but this scale is going to be returned.

Actually... it looks nice, but I can't get it to connect and it should NOT be this hard.

First... the instructions that came with it don't work. Other reviews which love the scale even frequently concede this fact. They say, "just use your phone, it's much easier." Some people may not have a smart phone. I do, and I tried it and indeed I got farther. I could connect to the scale, but the scale still did not connect to my Router. I replaced the batteries and set everything 2 feet from my router. Still no luck. I've determined it must be a compatibility issue with my Belkin 300N router, but I've already wasted too much time and don't wish to go in and try tweaking my router just for this scale. Truth is... the more I've thought about it while working on the problem... I can manually plug in my weight and fat % from a another scale and save some money (and stress!)

Based on other reviews, many people don't have problems via their home set-ups -- good for them! I wasn't so lucky.

title: It works, but I have safety concerns.
text:
I am a bit conflicted as I write this review.

From a functionality standpoint, this item works very well. The QR code to load the app worked. The app itself is quite functional and I immediately found the camera on the tool once I connected to its custom WiFi. The LED in the tool is plenty bright and the camera itself is quite sharp and the image was very detailed. The various rubber tips that come with the tool also look like they would be quite able to remove earwax, especially the little scoop.

My issues with it are from a safety standpoint: specifically the tool end, which is very thin, stiff metal that you cover with a rubber tip. If you were to make the slightest mistake or push too hard, it would be VERY easy to push this right into your eardrum. If the tips were broader or the tool had a more flexible end, I would not be nearly as nervous about using it.

As is, it might be ok for a medical professional to use, but I would not personally want to use it on myself.

title: It is fairly easy to use and it works.
text:
This is not a product that I would normally order on a regular basis, but my wife sort of suggested it (lol), and, as I get older, it has become a bit more necessary. As Jeff Foxworthy once commented, it's not that we lose our hair as we get older, it just pulls in off the top and grows out other places instead!

Overall, it works and does the job. It comes with multiple attachments, including one for nose/ear hair, one for eyebrows, and one for general shaving. It also includes a cleaning brush and a cover. A USB cable is included for charging, but no charger. As is becoming fairly typical these days, you will need to provide your own. Personally, I would have preferred it came with one. When it came, it had at least some charge, but I charged it for about 2 hours before using.

For ear hair, it works nicely. For nose hair, it works, but it feels a little odd. According to the instructions and the notes from the manufacturer, you are supposed to use using a bit of a rotating motion while using it. This seems to work, but has a bit of tendency to catch and pull longer/thicker hairs rather than just immediately cutting them (which is a bit uncomfortable). Sharper blades might help on this. The eyebrow trimmer also works well, although you may want to go gently and be VERY careful of the angle at which you hold it until you get a good feel for how it works...otherwise you may end up trimming a bit more than you intended! The general shaving attachment I have not tried. I looks like it would work for simple touchups to whiskers and such, but is not really intended for giving you a full shave.

Long term reliability is yet to be seen, but it is compact, easy to use, and does what it is supposed to, though it would be nice if it came with its own charger.

title: Lotta Protein! Tastes great.
text:
1st, a WARNING for those taking Warfarin (Coumadin) or other blood thinners. This protein does have "Black Pepper Extract" or "Bioperine" in it. Some studies have shown this can increase the effects of Warfarin & blood thinning medications. In fact it can cause greater absorption of a LOT of different medicines etc. ...So those using such medicines should really be aware of this & watch your levels (INR etc.) when using this or any Black Pepper Extract containing product. ...That being said: -

This stuff has 31.5 grams of protein in it & actually tastes great.

Only has 2 grams of carbs & zero fat in each serving. That is a little hard to believe but OK. That's what it says.

It mixes really well & dissolves in water nicely.
I usually beat mine up (Mix) with a fork to get the chunks out with most protein. I did that with this but I doubt it's really necessary. It dissolved very smoothly in the water but still had a nice texture to it.

I just used a "solo" type cup to mix it in filled about 2/3rds up with water & that's fine for me. I like it a bit on the thicker side. Just mix to your own taste though I would say.

It may be a bit of a treasure hunt to find the scoop down in there, but it IS in there. May have to dig deep down in that powder though! lol

The specs of the ingredients look great & it tastes very good to me. 5 stars!
