title: Typical Multilevel marketing...Jim Jones juice...
text:
Gonna have to agree with the other reviewer. Monavie is a typical MLM product...they took a good product that few people really understand or will understand(in this case a rich antioxident berry) overpriced it, and put the Jim Jones pyramid cult glasses on all their distributors/suckers.

The price of 100% Acai berry juice at Wholefoods is just shy of what you pay for the same quantity of Mona Vie. The problem is that the amount of the very expensive Acai juice in Mona Vie remains a secret and is probably not much. Acai in Mona Vie is mixed with cheap juices like grape and others. You'd probably do better regarding antioxidants to simply mix half Acai and half (purple)grape juice, and take a good multivitamin. If sugar is a problem, then just dilute the Acai and drink that. You'd definitely save much money if you did this. Top commonly attainable antioxidant rich foods per weight in order 1-10, blackberries, walnuts, strawberries, artichokes(cooked), cranberries, rasberries, blueberries, ground cloves, grape juice, cranberry juice. Acai is the best so far for ORAC value(the potency grading system for antioxidants) per weight, but is not considered a common food so it isn't on the list. A great way to get Acai is freeze dried powder, which you can order online at Amazon or get through a few major retailers(maybe Costco).

I give it two stars because you should be taking antioxidents, and the Acai berry is excellent for that, but I've looked and have yet to find any legitimate science identifying any benefit to the "patented freeze dried" Monavie process over the freeze dried Acai packets at groceries like Whole Foods. I asked my brother(a biochem Phd) about Monavie, and he generally said he couldn't imagine that Monivie's process has any benefit. Also, fruits/veges aren't the only source for antioxidents, so for the Monavites to espouse that "Monavie juice has everything" is wrong and neglects noting the key anticancer benefit of the antioxidant Selenium(found in meat, garlic, and seafood). In fact, just recently, the Mayo clinic identified that beta carotine(antioxidant) can cause cancer in smokers!...

(Jan 08), Selenium has been identified by the Mayo Clinic to reduce cancer rates by 23% in men, with no effect on women. Some sources of Selenium: fish & shellfish, red meat, grains, eggs, chicken and garlic.

'While antioxidants have been touted for cancer prevention, different antioxidants have different effects, and their effects may also vary depending on the part of the body involved, Dr. Aditya Bardia of the Mayo Clinic in Rochester, Minnesota and colleagues note in their report.'
'In fact, the researchers found, smokers who take beta carotene supplements could be increasing their risk of smoking-related cancer and death. title: Great for Travel
text:
I put one of these on my Amazon wish list to replace my old one in case it ever dies on me. I bought mine probably 10 years ago from another website, and it cost a LOT more ($27.99, I think). I really don't like showers, but when traveling, especially in Mexico, bathtubs are few and far between. And even in a nice hotel bathtub, I like to have the handheld to wash my hair and rinse off.
The first few times I installed it in a hotel room, I was nervous that the maid would be upset, but, no, they LOVE it. It makes cleaning the shower or bathtub much easier for them.
I like the plastic hose: it's much lighter, and I think the TSA doesn't scrutinize it as much as they would a metal one.
I travel with a small pair of channel locks and Teflon tape. The channel locks are to remove sometimes badly stuck showerheads, not to tighten this unit. You want to finger tighten so as not to crack the plastic. And I use the Teflon tape everytime or it will leak.
I was very happy to find this on Amazon, as the hose on my old one is kinking from being coiled in my carryon. I'm worried that it might give up the ghost someday, so I'll pull the trigger on this one at that time.

title: High Quality Omega-3 Fish Oil Improved Cognitive Function & Mood and Eased My Arthritis Pain
text:
Omega-3 fatty acids are essential to human health and can only be obtained through one's diet. Fatty fish like cod, tuna and salmon are the best sources, but you have to be careful because these foods can be contaminated with mercury and other pollutants. You can also get Omega-3 in flaxseed, walnuts and soybeans, but who is really going to eat enough of these on a daily basis to get an adequate amount? I know I'm not since I hate the bitter taste of walnuts and really don't like dried soybeans. Higher blood levels of Omega-3 essential fatty acids including EPA and DHA are associated with improved cognitive function and mood, protective properties for the heart, and possibly a positive impact on joints and flexibility for people with arthritis.

Taking a supplement may be beneficial, but a lot of the cheaper ones may contain traces of dioxin, mercury, PCBs and other contaminants from the environment. Not to mention the fact that you burp up the taste for hours. After trying several inexpensive brands including a free full-size bottle I received at a health fair, I decided that not all Omega-3 fish oil supplements are created equal. This one is as pure as you can get, has really helped with my cognitive function and mood, and most importantly - eased the chronic pain from arthritis. I am really happy that I switched to this high quality product from TruFormula.

title: Helpful pain relief device
text:
I'm an individual who deals with a lot of back pain. I have retrolithesis of L4 and L4, and spinal stenosis. There are days where I'm completely immobile due to lower back pain. I'm always down for something to help my back, especially on days where I am in excruciating pain. I found this awesome red light therapy belt, and thought it could be beneficial to my situation.

So far, my experience is good. I'm using the plug in version, even though you can plug it into a battery pack for portable use. It's very simple to put the belt on, select your options from the control unit, and enjoy the benefits. I really love how the massage and warmth feels on my tender back. There are 3 light modes. You can opt for 660nm, 850nm or both 660nm+850nm together. The days where I'm in severe pain, so I just use the 850nm. There are 5 brightness levels. I believe I'm feeling the warmth from the highest setting. There are also 5 massage levels. I like putting mine on the highest massage intensity. It's like a vibration massage, but it brings relief. Oh, and it has the option to pulsate. I love all the choices with this belt.

Another very nice thing about this belt is its timer. This is nice for me, since I have fallen asleep with it on. The recommended amount of time to use it is 20 minutes per day. The timer gives you the choice of 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, and 30 minutes. I run mine for about 30 minutes. I'm always sad when my session is over. It feels so nice while it's on.

Overall, this is a wonderful therapy belt. It has helped me tremendously and I hope it can do the same for others.

title: Works. I wish I tried this hair removal method sooner.
text:
I grew the hair out for 10 days to ensure that the device would be able to grip it. Yes, I was prepared for the immense pain, BUT i was not prepared that i would have to do the same area over and over and over for minutes to get it all off. There are many hairs the first time you do it, so it hurts for a sustained time. It felt like it was cutting me everywhere, but it wasn't. With each pass, there are fewer hairs left behind, so it gets better after the first couple minutes in one spot.

I have not used this hair removal method previously, so I can't compare this to other models. I don't know if it's normal to need so many passes over the same area, but it says it has 18 tweezers, so I guess it can't get a lot of hairs at the same time. After doing one leg for at least 5 minutes, I couldn't see hair anymore, but it still felt slightly stubbly. I realized this is probably because some of the hairs were still very short and blunt from when I had last shaved, and not long enough to get grasped yet by the epilator. Each time you use the device, this is less of a problem as all old hairs grow out enough to get pulled out.

After the first time, i used it a week later, and then another week later to catch more hairs as they grew out, and it is not terrible after the first time because of much fewer hairs. I think now I'll only need it about twice a month, and there won't be many hairs grown out each time. If you HATE shaving, this is a good alternative and long lasting. Lasts much longer than depilatory creams, too.

If you want smooth armpits, it is VERY challenging to get all the hairs with the epilator head due to the curves and also because the hairs grow in all different directions. It is worth it if you have the patience to just keep going over it with many passes in all directions, it feels smooth for many days.

It came well-charged right out of the box, and a small amount of charging lasts long. When you change the head, the gears inside are small and plastic, and don't appear durable. The alternate head says it is a shaver for finer hair, but it feels like it's pulling hair. The result is not as long-lasting as the epilating and leaves a blunt hair end.

UPDATE: I have used the product about 5 times, and each time it is less effective because you have to go over the same hair many times, i think the tweezers are losing their grippy-ness. I still think this is a good hair-removal method, but i will look for another brand that is more efficient. It still holds a charge for a long time.

title: Amazing, if Unexpected Results
text: I've been working with a wide variety of nootropics for a few years now.  This is not my first time with lion's mane.  That this experience has been unique is perhaps a coincidence, as I had never previously tried lion's mane before bed, but the results have been amazing.  When it comes to the day to day benefits of lion's mane, it is always long term and subtle at best--it is not psychoactive, but restorative over time.  However, as someone who has always had sleep issues, wherein no matter how long I sleep it feels like no time has passed and I always wake up more tired than I was when I went to bed, this product (and I am inclined to suspect specifically this product) has changed all that.  There is something different about this lion's mane than others I've tried, though I can't say for sure exactly what it is.  When taken before bed it has consistently had an effect on my sleep like very few things I have ever found in my life (and none of which have been consistent).  After taking this, my sleep feels like I can account for time, meaning, it feels like I have slept for hours rather than a single instant of nothing.  More than that, a small amount of time sleeping feels considerably longer (e.g. a couple hours of sleep often feels like 5 or more).  It is entirely possible that I have a condition whereby others who do not may not see the same results with this product as I have (as is common with psychiatric medicines).  But if what I have described sounds like an issue you deal with, give this product a try.  And what's more, the price simply can't be beat, so it isn't a huge investment.

title: Not 100% effective, but it does help!
text:
There is somewhat of a design flaw with this product which makes it a less-than-perfect solution for containing smoke. The issue is that the mouthpiece, or the end where you blow the smoke into, is not directly connected to the filter itself. This empty space between your mouth and the filter fills up with smoke (obviously) but that smoke never reaches the filter so when you move the device away from your mouth, the smoke just escapes from the device without ever having been filtered. It isn’t a lot of smoke, but it’s enough smoke to be detectable, especially if you are using it multiple times in one sitting. I tried to blow as hard as I could into the device to “force” that last bit of smoke into the filter, but it didn’t work. This actually made things messy because apparently when I was exhaling as hard as I could, I was also blowing saliva into the device or something, because it eventually became so filled with drool that it was leaking out the other end. Gross!
Anyways, this product is pretty useful for the most part, it definitely helped immensely to keep the room somewhat free of smoke, but I’d sit next to an open window just to be sure. If you’re looking for something 100% effective, this isn’t it. But if 98% effective is sufficient enough for your needs, buy it.

title: Ozone Gas Health Hazard & Not Loud
text:
I have no idea how this idea got such great reviews.

1) INSUFFICIENT NOISE: First, it's not loud enough even in the highest possible setting. It might work if you like white noise as an ADDITIONAL noise but don't purchase this to block out noise. It's clearly not loud enough for that.

2) OZONE GAS: Second, it might even be harmful to run this. Every time I turn it on, it generates an "ozone" gas type smell. I know this device is causing it because as I stick my nose closer to it, the ozone smells gets stronger. The ozone smell goes away when I turn it off.

Ozone gas is generated sparks by some electric motors, such as the one used in this. My blender also generates that smell but I run that for less than 1 minute. I am concerned for the long-term health risks of using this item since one obviously runs this for more than 1 minute. Regardless of health risks, the ozone smell is very unpleasant and in itself enough not to use this.

I returned it.

I seriously recommend an electronic/digital "nature sounds" sound conditioner instead of this. I saw one in an office and really wished I had bought that instead.

text:
The Promeko products are sold in almost every local, privately-owned pharmacy in Puerto Rico. They're very economical but sell well because they work good even if the ingredients list is sparse. This Bear Oil smells really good, like a really expensive product. The bottle's label seems cheap and "budgety" but the product is as good as anything ten times the price. Lots of elderly people use this oil, and their skin is admirable. So this can help a younger person, too. It makes my beard really soft and shiny.

Because it's a REALLY thin oil, unlike anything I've ever tried, I foundby accident that it is fantastic to clean and shine my cellphone's black cover and other plastic electronics like my speakers, camera, etc. that get dull with handling and dust and stuff, because it's really, really thin and silky oil. So the pores of the plastic kind of absorbs the oil superficially and it creates a thin, shiny layer of protection. I'm not endorsing it to treat your black plastic items, because some plastics or rubber might not like any oil on them, but in my case, it makes them look like brand new without leaving residue. title: Braun's new best razor
text:
I'm going to approach this review primarily as a comparison between the 7 series and 9 series. I assume that anyone looking at this razor is in the market for something very high end and therefore the real question in mind is "is it worth the upcharge to go from a 7 series to a 9?"

In all of the images I've attached, the 9 series is on the left and the 7 series is on the right.
I've been using a Braun 790-cc exclusively for the last year, so I am pretty familiar with the Braun shaver head style. I've always preferred the foil razors over rotary shavers.

Footprint of Clean and Charge station

For each of these two units the Clean and Charge station takes up about the same amount of space. The 9 series is a little bulkier, but not significantly enough that it would cause a problem. The main difference is that for the 7 series the razor is tilted, which I suppose allows better draining after running the clean cycle.
In the 7 series unit, the cleaning cartridge loads from the front. I thought this made a lot of sense as once the cap is off it can slosh around a little bit and potentially spill on the counter if you have to do too much handling. This was not carried over into the newer 9 series. The 9 series loads the cleaning solution from the back, which I did not appreciate at all. This means the entire unit has to be moved in order to put in a new cartridge. To me, this is a major design flaw, as most people will place their charger right back up against the mirror and the area in front of it will eventually fill with odds and ends. The end result is that changing the cleaning cartridge in the 9 series is not good (and given that the whole top pops up on springs to change it there's no reason they couldn't have front loaded).

Size and handling of unit

The 9 series razor is definitely chunkier. It's still ergonomic enough to fit well in the hand. Both units have pivoting heads. The head locking mechanism (to prevent it from changing angle to hit hard to reach spots) is more convenient on the 9 series, being the large button on the handle of the unit. The head lock for the 790 is on the head of the unit and pretty easily snaps to new orientations when engaged, although I haven't found a whole lot of need for it. The head of the 9 series unit is also significantly bigger, meaning being able to lock it is a bigger deal.
The battery life on both shavers is excellent. I haven't seen the 9 series lose a bar over a couple days use and I have taken my 7 on business trips for a week or more at a time and never had to plug them it in.
One other big big difference between the two units is the longer hair trimmer. I've attached an image with the review of each of them extended. The 9 series comes straight up from the back parallel to the handle of the unit, which I consider to be the traditional conformation for foil razors. The 7 series sticks out perpendicular from the back of the unit and is much harder to use, as it lead to awkward hand placement in order to see what you were cutting in the mirror. This was one of the main complaints for last year's model and I'm glad to see they fixed it.
Last but not least, the unit power for the 9 series is automatically controlled by the unit. The 7 series you dial it in yourself. This could be a selling point for some, but I didn't really find much difference either way. I usually left the 7 dialed all the way up anyways.

Visual Appeal

I can't deny that the 9 series is a very attractive razor. All of the blue lights that hide behind the black plastic on the base unit look really nice next to the blue power readings on the handle of the unit itself. It looks like something straight out of the future. However, some of the information is lost in presenting it this way. The 7 series had a battery and hygiene gauge on the back of the handle which was very intuitive, although less attractive. The battery indicator for the 9 is still just as easy to read, but the hygiene indicator has changed to just be the cleaning drops, indicating how long it will clean for. I liked how everything was presented on the 7, but I understand why they changed it.

Shave quality

Perhaps the most important part of the review - how well do they stack up? The 9 definitely delivers a better shave in less time. The first time I used it I was caught off guard because it felt like it was catching a lot using the amount of pressure I usually do with the 7 series. It was a little off-putting until I felt the results afterwards. Wow. It was almost as good as a straight razor, which is quite a step up from where foil razors typically live. In comparison, the 790 was more like straight razor plus 4 hours in terms of shave quality. You could always feel a little bit left if you were willing to look for it. The 9 also took less passes.
The 9 series also is a wet/dry shaver, which means you can use shaving cream with it for that little extra boost. I didn't try it with shaving cream, as my old razor was dry only. Both shavers are waterproof, so you can use them in the shower if you want.
Upkeep

Both units use the same cleaning cartridges, which is great, but have different heads. The razor cartridge should be changed every 18 months for each per Braun's instructions. The price of the 9 series head is ~ double that of the 7 series.

Overall verdict

The 9 is definitely a better razor, both visually and performance-wise, but the price tag is double that of the other high end Braun models. If money is less of a concern and you really just want the best performance the 9290 is where it's at. If money is somewhat of a concern and you want something that still does a really good job, go with a 7.

text:

With a seat cushion you want something that will not instantly deflate while being supportive, the problem with this cushion is it is too supportive. The areas that you feel the purple cushion on are getting pressure, so instead of getting pressure on one area without the cushion with it is spread out, I wish the cushion had more give to it. title: Instructions are horrible, so that's the only reason why I'm giving ...
text:
Instructions are horrible, so that's the only reason why I'm giving this 4/5.

My 60 gallon planted tank got planaria infestation -- we are talking about hundreds of them crawling on the tank's glass. Funny thing is I have few Discus, tetras, and platys in the tank that supposed to eat these worms! I've tried many things to get rid of them and nothing works other than I managed to kill my Nerite snails with other medications. On Day 1, I decided to put whole packet #1 (250mg) into the 60 gallon tank. I waited for few hours and no changes. But on Day 2, I noticed that the planaria seemed less than the day before, but not much. So feeling frustrated, I dumped full packet #2, WITHOUT changing any water. 12 hours later, I finally noticed that >50% of them started to shrivel up. on Day 3, I put half of the packet #3, and within hours, the planarias were all shriveled up.. So I think it's working. Day 4, all i see is hundreds of dead planarias on the gravel. All the fish and shrimps are alive and kicking. They dont seem to be affected by the meds, but the discus were showing signs of stress. So I changed 25% of water on Day 4, and they looked better on Day 5.

This thing supposed to kill Nerite snails, but NOT all snails. I still see few Malaysian Trumpet Snails alive in my tank.

title: Finally, a USB shaver!
text:
This shaver is replacing my Panasonic shaver of 21 years. I have only had this item just over a week, so I might have to come back to this later. What drew me to this razor first and foremost was that fact that it is charged with a USB cable. I have searched hi and low, and it was difficult to find a USB rechargable razor. The ones made by the major companies use a USB cable but still connect to a giant dock. What a terrible waste. Isn't this the 21st century? I use my razor for travel. I grew tired of having to carry more and more cables every device. Many of the USB shavers had a USB on one end, but still used an odd old style razor charging connector on the other end, which defeats the purpose. I you were to lose that cable if would be even harder to replace than the average charging cable for most razors.

I was concerned at first at how light this unit was. It felt like a toy. If I didn't actually see the metal parts on it, I would have sworn there was no metal anywhere in it because it was so light, and has a very plastic feel to it. But the shave is surprisingly clean. I tried the flip up clippers and they worked well on my side burns with no issues. It has shaved me for a week straight without needing a charge yet. I was worried that being such a low cost razor that it would be junk, but it has held it's own up to this point. More razors need to follow this route and go full USB. This has been a great razor.

title: Nice that it links to fitbit, but there may be more accurate options out there
text:
So, I want to start off by saying that while I really like this scale, it's not always very accurate. The weight reading is OK, but the body fat reading jumps around a bit. I can sometimes get two different readings just by stepping off and then back on the scale.I pretty much assume that since there are a million different factors that can affect a body fat % reading, that I'll probably never get a truly accurate reading on any scale. I'm mostly using this to see if, on average, my body fat % is dropping as I get in better shape, so I'm not too concerned if it's not super accurate.

Overall, the scale does a pretty good identifying who is on the scale, but it does have some problems when guests use it. My boyfriend and sister weigh about the same, but their body fat % is way different (male vs. female, so it's a pretty big gap). When my sister was visiting me and used my scale, it automatically assigned her stats to my boyfriend's account. It would be better if the scale could look at the body fat as well as the weight to determine who the person is. The nice thing about the fitbit app, though, is that it's easy to reassign the data if it was assigned to the wrong person.

A feature that I really like is the ability to sync the fitbit data over to myfitnesspal (this is more of an app feature than scale, but whatever). I have my account set up so that when I weigh myself, the data gets pushed from fitbit to myfitnesspal. This makes it easy for me to log my weight changes with my exercise and food intake.

Setting up the scale wasn't too big of a deal. It did take 3 or 4 tries before it worked, but that still only amounted to about 10 minutes total. It was a little bit annoying, but not something that would impact my decision to buy it.

Overall, I am pretty happy with this purchase, though this scale could use some improvements. I would probably buy this again due to the ease of syncing data across different apps. This scale has made me a lot more accountable for logging my weight, since it does it for me every time I step on it. I am giving it 4 stars due to the body fat inaccuracies and high cost.

title: Good spacers, but some effort to work in some devices
text:
These Eneloop spacers are decent quality, unlike some of the other battery adapter brands. However, they may not work for your application with out some messing around.

First, when you slide the AA battery in, the positive end slides inside four little arms to make contact with the positive terminal of the adapter. On a couple of these spacers that I have, you need to use a little screwdriver to move one of the arms back so that the battery will slide in - no big deal.

The bottom, negative end of the spacer is just open, so that the AA battery will slip out if it is not firmly retained by a spring or terminal inside your device.

Another potential problem is that some of the springs designed to hold D batteries will have an inner coil that is too big to hold the AA battery base (as in many flashlights). The solution to this is to use a 50 cent (half-dollar) coin or similar sized 1-1/4" diameter, thin, round metal disk on the bottom of the adapter to make electrical contact. You can tape it on with a small piece of masking tape if necessary. (Obviously, just tape the outer edges of the coin/disk to the adapter, so you still get electrical contact with the spring). Note that a quarter may work in a pinch, but since it is smaller in diameter it may tilt and fail to make contact.

UPDATE: I had previously suggested using a metal washer, but most washers have a hole that is too large to make electrical contact with the base of the battery.

title: Excellent product, exemplary customer service!!
text:
After seeing nerdwax (a.k.a. The Nerds!) on Shark Tank, I knew I had to purchase it for my constantly-slipping eyeglasses, which had already been adjusted several times, to no avail. The problem is that my nose hasn't much of a bridge for the glasses to rest on, nose pads or not!

Nerdwax works super well for me with considerable adhesion -- very tacky, as desired! No more *incessant* need to shove my glasses up my face anymore, which is especially annoying while trying to focus on my computer work (I've a computer job). However, an occasional push-up is still needed. Though it must transfer to the skin over time, I don't feel gunky residue on my nose ... it dissipates quite nicely!

As you'd find on nerdwax.com (FAQ section), the product naturally wears off by the oils produced by your skin, including sweat, so if these conditions are present (e.g., during intense exercise), you should expect to apply it more frequently. The product is designed to be reapplied every hour or two, or once a day, depending on your activity, skin conditions, and even environmental climate (I live in the arid desert!). Also, the shelf life of the product is about two years, after which it "loses its mojo".

But a TOUR DE FORCE of this company is their EXEMPLARY customer service. After receiving the product, I wrote to the owner, Don, that I just received the 3-pack of nerdwax tubes purchased on their website, had been happily using it, and planned to give a couple to family members with similar slippage issues...

Then for giggles, I told what I deemed an amusing story of how one tube got into the jaws of one of my pups, while my husband and I were out one night. (Must have rolled off my desk onto the dog bed.) She had the cap in her mouth when we got home, and so I searched the house for the rest of it, which was in our spare bedroom. I told Don that I managed to salvage the product by extracting it from the mangled tube -- and that it was in a plastic container so I could apply the product by finger... it's a great product, so how could I let it be wasted??

Don wrote back, like within the hour, assuring there is nothing in the product that would hurt my little pup, and then offered -- without my asking -- to send a replacement tube in the mail, as he couldn't let me get it all over my fingers during each application. (As I said, the product is very tacky!) He has the friendliest personality, is wonderful to communicate with, and cares passionately about ensuring customer satisfaction.

A couple of days later, I received an entire 3-pack in the mail... this was a pleasant surprise, as only one tube of the three I purchased was damaged. So I vowed to Don to give the extra two replacements to co-workers/friends/family who want to try the product. So happy with their customer service (and extra tubes), I want to pay it back somehow. THANKS DON!!

title: Just what I need for pre-night-time use
text:
The lenses are light in weight and the clip allows then to flip up and down quickly & easily. This is an important feature when deciding when to use them. Or not. So far, the clip has been secure and the lenses do not fall off in a dangerous way when lightly flipped with the thumb.

NOTE: These are NOT for use in the lowest light situations. When used with care, they are acceptable in the range of ordinary visual accommodation to different light levels, even *moderately* low levels. I suggest strongly that they be tried out in three or four different low-light environments before they are worn while driving. Look for detail edging and definition of dim objects.

Further, I suggest that they be flipped up and down often in a *variety* of low-light driving situations before anyone settles upon a low-light-driving pattern. Constantly re-examine your low-light usage until you get a good feel for when you can actually see better without them! Low-light driving with these is NOT for the lazy. If you use them, you must be ready at any time to flip them up and out of the way. Seriously.

title: 2015 (Reusable Portable Male Comfort Fit Advantage Urinal System with Spill Proof Collection Bag from Advantage Urinal Systems)
text: Maybe the design has changed or maybe different sellers have different suppliers or models, but this urinal I bought for my 92-year-old dad in November, 2015 (Reusable Portable Male Comfort Fit Advantage Urinal System with Spill Proof Collection Bag from Advantage Urinal Systems) wasn't as good as the first one I got back in May, 2015 (Reusable Portable Male Comfort Fit Advantage Urinal System with Spill Proof Collection Bag Sold through Amazon by PSA DEALS).  Specifically, the opening at the top of the most recent purchase is smaller.  I would think the Advantage name means I bought an authentic, current model, but the smaller opening in the new(?) version, makes it more difficult to use for my aged father (who really liked the first one we got for him since it saved him trips to the bathroom at night).  We bought the second to keep by his chairside (with one for the bed).  The tubing, bag, and padding at top inevitably pick up stains over time (even with daily rinsing), but they remain functional.  I just wonder why the opening at the top (and the collection cup) is now smaller.  I could follow up wiith diameter measurements but I am not currently at his home.  Most likely the production costs are slightly less, but I hope that's not the only reason for the design change.  All in all, it's a very good product that can help a lot of men.  Maybe the diameter was decreased to make a better seal for other users?

title: Disappointing
text:
I've actually got three of these, and had a few more over the years. This one is the older model, I guess, but I wanted the art cover because I'm superficial like that (and the plain black really shows scratches). It's a premium product, and the filter replacement are not cheap. They also do not last the cited 18 months, if you live anywhere the air actually needs filtering. Keeping that in mind, Rabbit Air products are generally great.

However, I guess I got a lemon this time. The unit does not work on auto mode. There is no increase in suction/fan speed if it detects a disturbance in the force. It seems to have a defunct computer, because it gets stuck in permanent off/sleep mode. So to check the air quality and manually increase the power to match, I physically click it on (to check the indicator light). It really defeats the entire of purpose of being energy-efficient. This is NOT typical of Rabbit Air products in my experience. If they hadn't sent it in a damaged box, I would have already returned it. I'm annoyed that they'd even sell/ship a subpar product.

In short, I would not recommend buying the 700A model at all for any reason.

title: Nice for the price
text:
It's not going to give you the best shave of your life, but it is compact and surprisingly well built for the price. The cap is held on by a magnet and cleverly has a mirror hidden inside it so you can see what you're doing even if you're somewhere without a mirror.

It's not the most powerful razor, but even with a couple of days of stubble it worked pretty well. The only issue was that it did grab a couple of long whiskers on my chin. Best to use it regularly so you don't have to worry about that.

Battery life seems decent. I expect you could go about a week of shaving every day with this before it needs a recharge. It actually came with its own wall wart, which considering the low price was a pleasant surprise to me.

I'm sure you could find a nicer travel razor if you spent more money, but for the price I doubt you can beat this one.

title: Misleadingly EXTREMLY EXPENSIVE and SCRATCHES throat rather than soothes it
text:
Perhaps my worst purchase yet. I thought I was careful … I didn’t really know what this product was like, but I was willing to take a chance. I was almost certain that when I purchased this, it showed 2.5 oz for $6.99; though, now it’s showing 0.25 oz (I think I’ll take a screenshot of my purchases from now on). It seemed like a decent deal, since other brands were selling for about $8 to $10 per ounce. As it turned out, when I got the bottle, it was a tiny 0.25 ounce container! That’s right – a quarter ounce. If you do the math, this is equivalent to $27.96 per ounce – ouch!

I went back online to see what it was that I actually purchased. Let’s assume that I was wrong and my eyesite is just not the same as it used to be, and it really did show 0.25 oz. Even with this, the webpage is misleading. Right after the price is shown for $6.99, in parenthesis there is an amount showing $4.37/oz. At the time, I didn’t pull out my calculator, but it seemed to make sense that the unit cost per ounce would be less (if I was buying 2.5 ounces for $6.99). But I should have checked this closer ... the two figures are completely contradictory –especially at the 0.25 oz rate. How can an item cost $6.99 for 0.25 ounces (ie. $27.96 per oz) and at the same time cost $4.37 per ounce? It just doesn't add up either way. This is completely misleading, and makes me wonder if I should be checking these discrepancies with other purchases on Amazon. This is FALSE ADVERTISEMENT. And to add to this, if you scroll down to the “Product Details”, it shows an item weight of 1.6 ounces. Granted, this includes the container, but when one looks at a product like this, they are mostly interested in how much liquid it holds. Again – misleading.

Once I got the spray, I decided I’d still try it, since I was curious about what it would do. I can honestly say that I would NEVER buy this product again, solely based on the taste and how it’s supposed to help. I can’t really describe it, other than it being a completely disagreeable taste that seems to scratch my throat more than soothe it.

Do NOT buy this product. It doesn’t work, and it’s misleadingly EXTREMELY expensive - $27.96 per ounce. Totally not worth it.

title: Best massager I've ever purchased.
text:
My husband has back and neck issues and pain after being in a car accident. It has been over a year but he still struggles with the stiffness and pain up and down his whole spine. I have purchased other massagers and they work pretty well but they can be either too large, bulky and heavy or they just don't have the power behind them to actually work effectively. So, when I had the opportunity to purchase this massager at a reduced price so we could try it out, and then give an honest opinion I wasn't really expecting anything different but boy was I wrong.
This is the coolest Shiatsu back massager we've ever tried. First off, it is made of great quality leather, the massager itself is very powerful. It has a very nice and quality on/off button with heat or no heat. The best part is it has straps that you can wrap around your arms and hold this massager anywhere you want up and down your spine. So, my husband can just sit comfortably and move it on his back and neck wherever he feels stress and pain. It's a cool concept and works exceptionally well. He really loves it and I like that I don't have to stand there using the old back massager on him. I would recommend this to anyone experiencing muscle soreness.

title: Great quality Milk Thistle
text:
I've never used Milk Thistle before as I take many supplements I really didn't want to have to take another one. But, my mum died of a liver disease and in the back of my mind I knew I should be proactive in the care of my liver. I started reading about the most natural and best way to help the liver detoxify the body and to help with the liver function and I kept coming up with the same thing..... Milk Thistle.
So, when I had the opportunity to purchase this Earth Star Milk Thistle at a reduced price for me to try it and then give my opinion of the product I was pretty happy but still unsure as to the effectiveness of it.
I've been using it for a few weeks now and am pretty impressed with the quality of this brand, first of it's a large bottle of 120 capsules. It's GMO and gluten free and the price is great.
I've noticed an increase in energy which I didn't think was something that Milk Thistle would do, I've just had my blood work done at the Dr. a few days before starting taking this product and my liver enzymes were elevated, I have a follow up in 6 weeks and will report my findings.
I'm hoping it does what it says it will do and protect and help my liver.

Serious gear for your rear! Sitting on it right now as I write this review.. Epic levels of comfort. If you are at a coffee shop and need to be there for a while to get some work done, this will allow you to sit for hours without discomfort. I think there is an even deeper, cushier version, I am curious to try it out.

The seat works exactly as advertised. Helps a lot with reducing pressure on the thighs where the edge of a wooden seat might dig in. I'm pretty fit, so no extra chub on me for cushioning. I'm also used to the hard seat on my Bianchi road bicycle, so I'm not particularly spoiled when it comes to cush for my tush. But I couldn't resist this seat cushion, even at this steep price.

With that said, there are three things to be concerned about:

1. It weighs a fair amount. I wish I could take it with me to work in my messenger bag, but it is like an anchor. Definitely more than 5 pounds. You won't really be able to take this with you everywhere, so I leave it in the car.

2. It can slide a bit on your seat, despite the grippy mesh underside of the slip cover. So you might readjust it every once in a while, no big deal. That said, with with all the force from sitting and inadvertently sliding on it, the slipcover has shown very little sign of wear and tear. That's a sign of solid quality. WonderGel, please stick with this quality level of slipcover for your seats; it's the small things like this that make for good reviews and recommendations of products to friends!

3. The other thing: I removed the black slip cover once and touched it with my hands. A few minutes later, my fingers and palms were itching quite a bit. I washed may hands very thoroughly and the itching stopped. Not sure what that was about. Hopefully whatever it was didn't get absorbed into my skin, but who knows. Just leave the slipcover on, and maybe don't sit on it with your bare legs (i.e. your shorts/pants/skirt should be between the cushion and your rear) and you will be fine.

Haven't had it make my rear itch, so we should be good! Maybe from the heat exposure when I leave it in my car did something to the cushion? It's still the same shape and size, no warping from heat. I only took off one star for the above issues because they pretty easily mitigated, and the itch thing only happened once.

title: Good Quality Gel - Works Well!
text:
I bought this Virgo Active Performance Gel for my husband who uses gel everyday. I'm always looking for great gel for him. His hair grows pretty fast and so the length of his hair varies and he needs something with good hold whether he's just had a haircut or it has been a few weeks.

-This gel works very well and the hold lasted him all day

-It is a firm hold but did not make his hair stiff and crunchy or annoyingly shiny (if you've used a gel that does those things you know what I mean)

-It does not flake off at all or leave white residue which is an absolute must for good gel

-The one thing he commented on was "This stuff dries fast - you have to move quick" and only after that did we notice that the directions are: "Apply to damp or dry hair and move fast and furious!" This is not a negative but just something to keep in mind

-It has a strong and distinct scent. If I had to name it I would say it is ocean scented. That's not to say that I actually think it smells like the ocean but rather like products I've used before that are called things like "Sea Breeze" or "Ocean Rain" - you get the picture.

He was nice enough to let me take a picture of his hair just after using it. This gives you some frame of reference for what type of hair it was used on and how it looks right after being applied. I was going to take an after picture of his hair at the end of the day but, honestly, it pretty much looks the same. It held very well! I also included a picture of the gel next to a gallon water jug for a universal reference of size.

I, like you, rely on heavily on Amazon reviews when deciding what to purchase. I received this gel at a discounted price in exchange for my honest review. However, these are my own opinions and experience which are not influenced by the seller. I do my best to describe it thoroughly and include pictures whenever possible so that you can make a confident and educated purchase.

It also has multiple programs with varying opening sizes that changes the amount of skin that is exposed to the vacuum. It also comes with a cleaning brush and replacement screens, making it fairly easy to clean and maintain. Overall I found that it does a very good job of removing the excess oil/gunk from my pores rather than squeezing it as I always have done in the past.

Put some socks on over the booties. They really hold the liquid on your foot.
Leave it on for at LEAST 2 hours.
After using the baby foot, your feet will not peel for (most likely) 3 to 4 days. Don't get discouraged.
Soak your feet. If you only have enough time to do it once, make sure it is 3 to 4 days after the application of the peel.

title: This is a great bundle package for blackhead and blemishes and cleaning for your face!
text:
What a great idea to place all you would need in a bundle… This Blackhead and Blemish Remover Bundle - includes a 5 piece stainless steel Comedone extractor kit, deep cleansing peel off mask, and a charcoal Konjac sponge. The kit contains a spoon shaped extractor, a lancet, a thin angled curette (looped shape) extractor, a curve angled curette (looped shape) extractor, and other angled curette extractors of different shapes and sizes for hard to reach and delicate areas. It also comes with clear instructions on how to use each piece. Before using the kit your face should be really clean and I used the deep cleansing peel off black mud face mask the night before. I applied the mask and left it on for about 30 minutes and then peeled it off. My skin has a little tingle sensation and felt cleaner and I also applied toner afterwards. This bundle pack also comes with a charcoal Konjac sponge which is extremely hard, but once it is wet is softens and you use it to exfoliate the oily areas on your skin. It’s hard to describe but my face felt completely fresh and clean after this treatment and I did have a little redness but it didn’t last long. I did not use all of the extractors but tried some. It will take a little practice getting use to using tools to extract blackheads and blemishes. I think this is a great bundle pack at a very reasonable price and I will purchase more of the black mud face mask and more of the Konjac sponges.

I took a pic of my two favorite attachments and the one that is for massage is great and I'll tell you why in a second. First I need to mention that this is NOT A/C it runs on 2 double A batteries so you might have to steal the ones out of your tv remote when you want to use this! lol It's a little bit of a trick to get the lid off of the battery compartment but, that's about it and I think that's my only problem with it as far as from a reviewers stand point which I need to mention I did get this product at a steep discount to help you decide if you want to try the DBPOWER 6 IN 1 brush but, please believe me that in no way has any bearing on my honest opinion of this neat little gadget. Well I decide to read about it a bit before finishing this review and this is what I found out  that lymphatic drainage is a medical procedure. When the body has a hard time removing lymph, it causes swelling, water retention, and discomfort. Lymph nodes are powerhouses of the body, regulating fats, sending out white blood cells to heal, and disposing of bacteria. Sometimes, the body needs a bit of help to get this system moving optimally. Exercise is the easiest way to stimulate lymph flow, but you can add a few minutes of light manipulation to the face to really see a difference in swelling, headaches, or sinus congestion. So with all that said I decided to use it for that purpose and at low speed it's gentle enough to just close your eyes and go over that area, then next to your nose, your temples neck etc. it was an awesome feeling instantly relaxed me and I am sure with continued use I will really reap the benefits. The other attachment head that I was instantly fond of is the gritty one. Now you don't want to use this on your face or nails because it's really super coarse but, put that head on and attach the long handle and you can go to town on your feet any rough spots or calluses this thing is going to make short work of them. The other attachments are all also great and perform their functions perfectly. I just wanted to expand on the two I like most. title: It really feels like zoom but...
text:
Ok here's the deal. These insoles actually feel like full length zoom air from Nike.

It has a real springy and bouncy feel,it's not a lot but you can definitely feel it. The yellow part of the insole is more firm than soft and it's not too thin or too thick,but thicker than your original insoles. It fits good in my Kyrie 7 after removing original insoles.

The Insoles are not ridged or very stiff but it does add more support than the Factory NIke insoles in my shoes.

Now the reason why I give it 3 stars is this:

1. The discoloration is due to the insoles melting probably in the factory process. It's all over the actual white zoom part which I think may hinder it's performance. It's also just looks gross!

2. After trimming it with scissors the right insole fits and feels perfect. The zoom is amazing. However,the left fit but zoom feels dead it feels like a regular insole not a huge difference from the original insoles inside the shoe.

Overall, when it works it's amazing. Unfortunately ,only one of the insoles really works, Fast shipping and a good fit.

This is good for people who are Fans of ZOOM technology, people who want something a little better than their Factory insoles, and athletes especially basketball players who want a little more bounce in their step.

I recommend at least given it a try and returning if it doesn't work.

title: Absolutely LOVE this, especially the scent!
text:
I received this product as part of a promotion at no cost to myself...and I wish I could continue to! It's fantastic but a bit pricey.
Sunscreen is absolutely necessary year round, even though it’s not commonly thought of during this chilly season. Did you know that the sun is actually closer to the earth during the winter while, at the same time, the ozone layer is actually at it’s thinnest? It’s true! The National Science Foundation Polar Programs UV Monitoring Network will tell you as much- so we’re actually at an increased risk for UV exposure, especially if you’re a winter sports enthusiast. According to skincancer.org, anyone hitting the slopes may want to remember; “Higher altitude means increased risk of sun-induced skin damage, since UV radiation exposure increases 4 to 5 percent with every 1,000 feet above sea level. At an altitude of 9,000 to 10,000 feet, UV radiation may be 35 to 45 percent more intense than at sea level. In addition, snow reflects up to 80 percent of the UV light from the sun, meaning that you are often hit by the same rays twice. This only increases the risk for damage.”
When heading out skiing or beaching, the above pictured is a new favourite for our skincare. The Sun ‘N’ Fun description reads that this;
Chemical free, non toxic, not greasy, no white cast, EWG Rating 1.
Natural with Organic ingredients, Zinc 20%
Contains fresh and inviting (natural) scent of marshmallow & chocolate, that kids love
Can be used by kids and adults alike
moisturizing with antioxidants
suncreen sun protection.
The 1 rating means that this sunscreen has the lowest hazard rating possible, and when seventy-five percent of sunscreens and 90 percent of SPF moisturizers tested in the Environmental Working Group’s “2013 Guide to Safer Sunscreens” were found unsafe or ineffective, that’s a major plus. We typically use my homemade sunscreen for that reason but this one does appear to contain a fairly comprehensive ingredient list. It also includes the antioxidant tocopherol (from soy), which enhances sun damage protection.
When they say that it smells of marshmallow and chocolate, it smells EXACTLY like that and my daughter loved it. My husband loathes sunscreen and hates wearing it but he readily agreed to where this one whenever asked as a result of the scent. He said, “I would be a walking dessert” and then make innuendo regarding as much. Men. Heh.

title: Fell apart in my hand the very first time I used it
text:
I bought this jade roller to use on the odd day when I am retaining fluid in my face and looking particularly puffy. Well, such a day didn't arrive until about a month after my jade roller was delivered. When I went to use it, I couldn't keep the larger roller attached at all. Even using the absolutely lightest pressure, barely even touching my face, the roller would fall off. Trying to keep the roller in place for just long enough to use it, I held the roller at the two arms which hold the roller. When I did this, one of the arms immediately broke off and could not be put back in place. This jade roller was poorly-made and incredibly flimsy. Of course, the first time I used it, when it fell apart in my hand, it was just after the return window closed. Well, although I don't have a useable jade roller, at least I got a lesson out of this purchase - try out everything you order at least once
as soon as it's delivered!

title: This is a great massage chair. Looks nice, strong motors - very happy.
text:
I'm 6'5" tall, and yes, I'm about 3-4 inches too tall for the foot massage. My feet fit fine, but the fact that my knees are up higher means my legs don't fit in the calf air bags. It's really not a big deal - they end up squeezing me in the middle of my leg instead of engulfing my calf. The foot rest does extend about 5 inches - but it's not enough - and even if it was, my thighs are longer than the seat so my calves still would not fit right.

But I didn't want pay $3-5K for chair that fit someone like me, so this works just fine - The rollers move from my butt to the top of my shoulders and it's amazing. I don't know why anyone would buy a chair without an L track. I could probably stand about 10-15% more strength on the shoulders, but this chair delivers slightly more than I can take on my lower back and butt - I literally find myself lifting up a bit, it's so strong - which is good, my concern was that it'd be too weak. (Disclaimer, it might seem stronger to me because I'm a skinny guy)

The foot rollers are so strong, I wear slippers. - It'd be nice if they moved up and down my foot (maybe they do, and I haven't noticed) but you can sorta move your foot around to the right point.

It has 4 programs and also allows you to manually position the rollers anywhere and pick any massage technique. It's a great chair. I'm sure there are much better ones out there, but I'm considering the price when I give it 5 stars.

title: Nice unit. Not for my windows.
text:
Despite having an adjustable magnetic intensity, I could not get this to work on my 1993 double pane with aluminum between the glass channel windows. It just kept falling out. The adjustable feature pushes magnets inside closer together so, I assume, they contact each other. The adjustable screw does not stay at any of the settings, it flips back to #1. I found it hard to hold the outside scrubby part, the inside scrubby and adjust the gear at the same time to try to get this to all stick together, which it never did. My windows must be too thick. In the description, it does state what thickness this works with, but I did not know how thick my windows were., They are obviously beyond the stated tolerance.
I think this would work quite well on the right windows. It is one of the less expensive magnetic cleaners and is a nice size to manipulate. Plus it came with all the extra parts. Try to determine your glass thickness ahead of time.
The extra pads, extra squeegee strips and locking gadgets for the pads is a great feature and one of the reasons that I ordered this cleaner. I was disappointed that it wouldn't work on my windows. I am not giving it 5 stars, because it doesn't work with all windows.

text:
Good evening fellow Amazonians.

I had originally ordered these for myself, as I have been wearing extra insole thingys in my shoes for the past year, and it has REALLY helped my foot pain. I am a preschool teacher, so I am on my feet from about 7am until around 1pm every single day.

Not wanting to disappoint the review readers, I gave them to my husband. Generally during the day he wears shoes with good insole support, but he does have some flat loafer type shoes that he also wears. He has never tried any extra support in these kinds of shoes prior to this.

After wearing them a few days, he said he DID notice a significant reduction in foot fatigue, and he also reported having less back and hip discomfort as well.

My husband has never been diagnosed with any sort of problem, but he really liked these after a few days and is for sure going to keep using them. He did say they made athletic shoes too tight, but for "flat" type shoes they were fantastic.

I can say these helped my husband out, and he was not even looking for anything in the pain relief area!!!

I received this product at a discount in exchange for an honest and unbiased review.

title: Testing Vivitar MB-D12 with a Nikon D800 - Mechanical and Battery Life in Video Mode
text:
I bought this product mainly to increase the run time of a D800 camera. It performs this task well. With one third party battery, tested at 89 minutes continuous video runtime in the camera body and a second third party battery, tested at 80 minutes continuous video runtime, in this product, the continuous video runtime was measured to be 159 minutes.

As a point of reference a single standard Nikon EN-EL15 will power the D800 video mode recording for 120 minutes.

The downside of the product is its construction quality, mainly materials. The unit is constructed of plastic, perhaps a durable plastic, we will see. Mounted on a tripod without this product directly to the D800 tripod socket, with the camera equipped with a Tamron f2.8 70-200mm zoom, the end of the lens depressed 2mm when a force of 34oz was applied at the end of the lens. Under the same conditions but with this product attached to the body and to the tripod, the deflection was 6mm. The lack of stiffness is a bit of a concern but it is not completely clear that this product is worse in this regard than the D800 with an equivalent Nikon product.

And finally, here is the reason for the five stars:
The product comes with two battery adapters, one for a standard EN-EL15 battery and a second to run the camera on 8 AA batteries. I tested the longevity of the video mode using 8 Panasonic eneloop AA batteries (available from Amazon). The D800 recorded video continuously for 200 minutes on only the 8 AA batteries

title: Decent product, but have realistic expectations.
text:
To put it simply, this product is nothing more than an aluminum tube with a UV light inside of it, and a small fan to blow air through the tube. It will not clean the air, remove dust or dander, remove odors, or anything else that people expect "air cleaners" to do.

This product has one single purpose: to kill any living micro-organisms that happen to be in the air. This means that, realistically speaking, you may never know if it's actually doing anything. The science behind UV-C sterilization is solid, and the product does seem built well. However, the fan is needlessly loud, and and the unit is too small to handle the air volume in even a large bathroom.

I am using this product in a small bathroom for the benefit of someone recovering from serious illness. Again, I will have no idea whether it will do anything, but it theoretically might, which is good enough for my purposes. For any space larger than a closet/bathroom, I'd suggest getting a proper air purifier with built-in UV light. There are many models that will filter dust, dirt, and odors AND contain the same UV lights as this unit. However, if you have a small space and need ONLY a sterilizer and not a filter, this product will do fine.

title: Good value, need one like this in a different size.
text:
I am only reviewing these for ice pack use. I use them for neck and shoulder pain. I ordered 3 of them. There are pros and cons to these ice packs. Here they are.

Pros -
Once these sit out for a few minutes, they loosen up, and become nice and flexible.
They stay cold for a long time.
They have a cold/warm option, but I've only used the cold.
They seem well made, with thick outer plastic and plenty of 'filling'.
The price is right! Best value, I'd say.

Cons-
Once frozen, you have to leave this sit out for a bit to become flexible.
They're not quite the right size. They need to be a few inches longer, especially to go around the neck, and an inch or so narrower.
No sleeve to put them in. It would have been nice, but for the price It's understandable.

Bottom line. They're a good value for the price, and length of time they stay cold. I'll use them until I can find a lighter weight one like it, that's a little a few inches longer.
They're bulky large size makes them too heavy for the neck and shoulders which is a real disappointment.

title: This is one of my favorite purchases. I waited impatiently to receive this one
text: This is one of my favorite purchases. I waited impatiently to receive this one. I have been looking  for a bathroom scale that was not only beautiful, absolutely  accurate and a great tool to track my ongoing weight management. I bet many of you remember those old clunky, absolutely ugly bathroom scales we all grew up with in the 60's and 70's. They had to be continually adjusted , and that tiny little knob that had to be turned to make sure you were getting an accurate read and still the results were questionable.  I spent all those years wondering just how much I did weigh because even the Dr's scale read a different weight depending on the office you were in. Well, those days are long gone thank goodness. This beautiful black digital scale not only is attractive in your bathroom it reads a very accurate weight each and every time. No more guessing about those few pounds difference you would get even when stepping on it multiple times. The red digital numbers are not visible until you step on it and go dark within seconds of stepping off. On the bottom of the scale, there is a button that is pushed to change the units of measure from kgs to lbs, to st. Whichever unit of measure you want to use or are used to using it is there at the push of a button. It measures 12inches by 12 inches square and sits off the ground at a very thin 1/2 inch. The cutout handle in the  upper right corner can accommodate a normal size had with ease. Included in this box were the scale, two AAA batteries that were inside of the scale as well as an additional set of batteries and a tape measure. The scale itself it lightweight and easy to move when needed. I would definitely recommend this scale as a purchase if you are looking for beauty as well as accuracy. title: I've Owned at Least Three and Will Be Ordering a Fourth
text:
I've owned at least three of these Epipen holsters. They're well-made, secure, and the synthetic cloth looks like new even two years on. I think they look good, too. Very functional. I recommend getting a good matching carabiner to more securely hook it to your belt. The holster has a loop at the top designed for this.

Far better than the branded Epipen holsters I used to have. Those things looked bad after six months.

However, after about two years, I've found the clip snaps off. It's still functional with the carabiner, but it doesn't ride as high and tends to bounce around. Prior to the clip snapping off, the faux leather material they use around the clip wears off. Again, still functional, but it might be a little rough on your dress pants if you wear it a lot.

I'm about to order another because of the clip issue. If they could fix that problem, this would be the ideal solution and would deserve five stars.

Also... sometimes people mistake it for a multitool, knife, or even a gun. But hey, it's a holster, so... just make sure to be open with security about what it is. I've probably been asked about it by security maybe three times, and it's never been a problem. In fact, under certain circumstances, I don't mind if people wonder what it is!

title: Even more EPA and DHA than what our "Family Member Nurse" personally takes, at a better price
text:
Over at least a dozen years, every one of the few times I've gone to the doctor, they have consistently recommended taking Omega 3 ... so I just take it. I also used to work in a Family Practice Medical office, and the docs there also suggested taking it.

Nutrition and supplements are not my specialty, and I mostly don't believe in them ... unless, of course, the doctors in my life consistently recommend them. So I consulted our "Family Member Nurse" about the Nordic Wellness Omega-3 Fish Oil tablets to get more information.

Our "Family Member Nurse" pulled her own personal Omega 3 out of her refrigerator and explained to me that it is the amounts of EPA and the DHA that are important. In comparing the Nordic Wellness with the nurse's Omega 3's, the Nordic Wellness had slightly more of both the EPA and DHA than her own personal brand, and at better price.

I noticed that these Nordic Wellness Omega 3's are also manufactured in the United States, which, as I understand it, has generally more reliable control of the actual ingredients, product labeling and product distribution than the pharmaceuticals from some other countries. The lot number (30693), manufacturing date (03-13) and Expiration Date (03-15) are clearly marked on the bottom of the bottle.

There are 120 softgel tablets in my bottle, each with 1,000 mg of fish oil, 400 mg of EPA, and 300 mg of DHA. I definitely prefer the softgel tablets to dry, "scratchy" tablets, as they are quite easy to swallow. And the top is "sealed for your protection" with plastic shrink wrap.

title: Painful learning curve
text:
I used to buy "crystal skin polishing mitts (for hair removal)" years ago but they got expensive and then I couldn't find them any more. I thought this would be a comparable, less expensive (in the long run) and less wasteful alternative. This left me disappointed.

The main body is like holding an old laptop mouse, everything is very rigid. Even using a constant light pressure circular pattern, the hair removal was sporadic in the same area- there would still be long hairs in areas that the skin was already at irritation point. Press too hard and your skin is red and itchy, too soft and it just twists the longer hairs until the knot up and pull off. EVERYTIME my brain glitched and I went at a straight line, it sliced into the skin. Also cut the skin in bony areas where the hard bone and hard surface of the buffer creates too much friction.

There is not enough pliability to the buffer for me, forget nooks and crannies and bony parts, add in the areas that it doesn't remove the hair at all and the pain and irritation while learning the right amount of pressure, it's just not worth it.

LSS, it only worked as expected on pudgy areas of my body that had enough skin movement and fat to counteract the stiff structure of the sanding block.

title: Worth it!!! especially if you have to do any physical work
text:
I had a lot of amniotic fluid and my belly was huge! I work outside on weekends and have to lift boxes, tables etc up to 50 pounds -- my back and legs were killing me. Quitting work was not an option because I have to pay my own bills!!

So in desperation I ordered this and it really really helped with the belly burden. I'm a larg-ish lady (about size 18) and it fit comfortably and offered great support. Definitely relieved both back and leg pain and strain in general.

Couldn't give it 5 stars for two reasons. The top band is too narrow so after a couple weeks of wear it began to bunch and ravel up the way elastic does on a tight skirt.

Then, because the Velcro was the same width as the top band, as the band rolled up the Velcro stuck out past it and REALLY itched because it was in direct contact with my skin. I combated this by buying a sheet of felt at a craft store and stuffing it under the Velcro. Really helped, but still a bit itchy.

Still, it was worth it 100 percent. If the manufacturer would widen the upper band this would be a 5 star item.

BTW I tried one other support belt (don't remember which brand) and this was far better.

title: One more satisfied user...
text:
Love the product. Have been using a fan for years, then tried my iPhone for sound, but just didn't seem to hit the spot. Nothing can truly duplicate a fan unless its mechanical. The fan is a little silly when its 20 degrees outside, so I broke down and tried the tried and true Dohm. It's older than dirt and mechanical. A small high speed fan draws air in a series of slots and holes allowing you to fine tune the white noise. You can not increase the volume, just the texture of the sound. Well, it simply works, and works great. I have it next to my bed so I can turn it on/off easily, but some find it annoying being so close. I didn't have any trouble getting used to the sound as I have been using fans for years. It will also be much more convenient to take on trips than a small fan! Didn't hear a single firework during the new year!
The only improvement I can think of would be a speed rheostat. They offer a 2 speed version, but for $10 more it didn't make sense, since once you get used to a speed you would never change it.
Good job Dohm.

title: My fellow loofah snobs, look no further!
text:
I'm not totally sure at what age I became so critical of loofah quality, but I'm here now and there's no turning back. Truly a blessing and a curse, because finding good loofahs on Amazon is like searching for a needle in a haystack. Thousands of different options, many of which claim to be high-quality but ultimately can't deliver. Recently I took a chance on this loofah 4-pack with hardly any reviews, and I'm so glad I did! Now I had never heard of Tobyan before until I came across this product, but it doesn't even matter. They make one hell of a loofah! The texture is soft, the mesh is dense, and they are all tightly packed with sturdy knots. Best part is, the quality is carried through the entire 4-pack, not just 1 or 2 good ones. The last time I found a good loofah multi-pack on Amazon (Novosun brand), the product quality was totally different when it came time to re-purchase them. Due to my paranoia, I promptly ordered a second Tobyan 4-pack and they're just as awesome as the first pack. I am still currently on my first loofah and there are zero signs of it coming apart after a week+ of usage. Now one thing that many reviewers here on Amazon don't seem to grasp is that it is recommended that you replace your loofah once every month-or-so. Even though we are covering these in soap they still retain bacteria. Any more than a month-and-a-half of usage and you're just going to end up covering yourself in your own grime. If you can make your loofah last a year, good for you! You just admitted to everyone reading your review that you have questionable standards in cleanliness.

Bottom line: Buy this 4-pack. They are soft, dense, sturdy, and look awesome! The price-to-quality value here is excellent and you will not be disappointed :)

title: Great focus and energy. A shot that finally works as advertised!
text:
UPDATE: 3/4/21 - It had been quite a while since I ordered these energy shots from Neu, and WOW was it a totally different (and terrible) experience than what I had come to know from my past purchases. I'm not certain if they changed their formula or added new ingredients, but they totally wreaked havoc on my stomach. I lost count of how many trips I made to the bathroom over the 3-4 day period that the effects lasted. Sometimes I'd be on the toilet for 20+ minutes with cramping and bowel movements of varying consistencies. It was so unpleasant, that I returned what drinks I hadn't consumed and came back to update my review and drop my rating down FROM 5 TO 2 STARS! I don't think I've ever done that before in my nearly 2 decade history of being an Amazon customer. Absolutely disappointed in these Neu shots now, and I don't plan on re-ordering them in the future :(

ORIGINAL: I am very impressed with these energy shots! The taste is kinda bad but the result was very pleasing. I drank the recommended half bottle before work and I noticed improvements in my motivation, energy, and my mood. It wasn't a euphoric feeling, but I was feeling noticeably "happier". Usually energy shots like 5-Hour, etc., just give me the jitters and make me sweat. This was a more mellow type of energy and the focus I experienced was a definite plus. The only negative side effect I've experienced so far is that, even after drinking on a full stomach, I started to feel hungry and my stomach churned a little bit about 1-2 hours after having the shot. All-in-all I'm very happy I came across this product. It's a little pricey in my opinion, but the fact that it actually works as advertised makes it well worth the cost. If you're skeptical on how these will effect you, I'd recommend trying the 3 quantity variety pack. That's what I started off with.

So I of course wanted to experience the renowned comfort and pressure relief Purple has been touting, even if I couldn't experience the bed yet.

I suffer from some kind of tailbone fracture that has been making it painful for me to sit longer than 5 minutes at a time, and if I over-sit my stay, my tailbone will continue to throb, making it painful to walk as well. I sat this cushion down on my office chair (where I depressingly spend most of my time) and gave it an honest try. My initial thoughts were disappointment: "This is so much hype for what? It doesn't feel like I'm sitting on anything." I was expecting a squishy feeling, or a sinking sensation, or a jelly-like hug that would encase my butt cheeks like jello. But no, it didn't feel like I was sitting on anything.

And then five minutes later it dawned on me...it DOESN'T FEEL LIKE I'M SITTING ON ANYTHING! I can feel the surface my butt is sitting on, but that's the extent of the sensation. No pain, no pressure, no nothing. It feels like I'm sitting on a regular chair, just minus the pain and discomfort. I definitely recommend the seat cushion. Stay tuned for my mattress review in a couple weeks when my bed arrives!

I've tried side to side comparison tests on multiple surfaces like rusted metal, tub soap scum & moldy grout. In every test both this product and my everyday cleaner did the exact same thing. There is no perk to using this over anything else. The down side to using this product is that it leaves everything feeling gritty, chalky and has to be rinsed off in excess with water. If not the item your cleaning looks dingy. Since there's things (like an oven range top) that you can't spray down excessive with water to remove the product, it is not worth it to use. This product did nothing on objects like rusty knives. I'm not sure what everyone is so impressed with. I haven't tried the spray cleaner yet and maybe that's better then the paste but for now I'm not very impressed.

This stuff should be carried pink magic. It's as though it immediately removes grease. COMPLETELY. Despite my original review of not liking this product I now give it 5 stars. title: Won't Fit Ettore 15ft Pole, ONLY Certain Poles Not Listed
text:
While this adapter is beautifully machined and is much more sturdy than other alternatives, the one I received two days ago will not work with a 15ft Ettore pole. It works fine with another pole I have, a painter's pole, but the threads don't quite match the much longer Ettore product. This may be an issue only with the individual product sent to me and not with the general run of product, but it is a big disappointment for me. Putting a camera 15ft above the floor is a great technique for all sorts of situations and if there were a 20ft option, I'd try that, too. Extremely high build quality otherwise, and it might work perfectly with all other poles...but it is not compatible with the Ettore 15ft model I have. I am going to keep it and try other poles.

UPDATE: I went to the Kacey Enterprises site and discovered that this is designed to work ONLY with 3/4 X 5 threads and that there are poles out there with variations on this that may look the same but that have a different thread pitch. I am downgrading from three to two stars because of the Adorama listing, not the quality of the product directly. Leaving out this essential information is misleading and deceptive.

title: Had to return—would never sync reliably
text:
This is a nice scale, but like so many others, I just couldn't get it to work consistently.

When I first tried out the scale after first setting it up, it synced immediately. But the next morning when I weighed, it failed to sync. I tried weighing several times, and got the Wifi symbol with an"x" display. I looked on my Fitbit dashboard display and it had not synced. But several hours later when I looked again, it had mysteriously synced all those attempted weighings. After that it would not sync anymore.

I headed online to the "My scale is not syncing consistently" page and checked the suggestions for this situation. No, I had not make any changes to the network. Yes, the scale was within a short distance of the main router in an area where other computers and devices connect up fine. No, I didn't have any indication that there is any interference or too much traffic on the network. I do have a network with MAC filtering, but I had put the scale's wifi number into my router, granting it permission to connect, and restarted. I'm pretty sure that wasn’t the problem, since the scale did sync a time or two. If it were blocked out, then it would have failed to ever sync.

I then followed the instructions online of resetting the scale by removing the battery, pressing down the corners, and going through the setup routine again. This time it crashed my router for some reason—and, to make a long story short, again failed to produce consistent syncing.

After working with it further, I saw that there was little chance of ever getting it to sync reliably, and just decided to give up.
