title: Wonderful. Replaces bandages, and feels futuristic.
text:
I'm very prone to minor injuries, due to silly mistakes or doing stupid things with hand tools, and as such my hands usually look like I went to war with said hand, against a housecat.

If you're at all like me, you tried regular super glue on cuts and wounds. Regular super glue is not meant for use on human skin, or really any skin at all. It emits noxious and irritating fumes that make your eyes water, and can burn harshly when put on fresh cuts. No bueno. Plus it's also non flexible, which is important when used on the very much flexible skin we all have.
This stuff is different, but similar, super glue. It has a different chemical group on the molecule, and as such acts a lil different. Still dries quickly, but emits no irritating smells. Just a faint ... chemically smell, it's almost floral in a weird way. Also does not burn as nearly as much as regular super glue on fresh cuts. Probably like a .... 90% reduction in pain vs regular. It's also a little flexible, which is fantastic and helps it last a bit longer. On very busy or active areas, you'll probably still need to reapply every day or so, since it flakes away. But the wonderful thing is, you still maintain near full mobility of whatever you used the glue on. Touchscreens still work. Etc etc.

The little applicators are nice, sorta. I say sorta, because I feel like a dropper type tip would be better and less finicky.
Make sure when you're done using one, it's facing right side up so the glue inside settles on the bottom, and not at the cap. This'll help stop it from clogging up.

I'm pretty pleased. I definitely use this a lot more than bandages now, since it's just convienent, and also stops bleeding nearly right away when used properly.

title: Did it's job!
text:
I bought this a few years ago, in order to secure my wedding set (which was sautered together) to my anniversary bands, which I wear on top & bottom. In order to get multiple rings like this sautered together, you must resizing at times & if you have an eternity band, it can be costly & could end up damaging them. Additionally, I like to interchange my bridal set with different sets of bands, so I didn't want a permanent situation.

That being said, lol, here are my thoughts on the product, which I use to temporarily 'glue' the bands together, providing both stability (no rolling around) and security (I always fear the top band will just slide off since it is close to my knuckle, and, especially in the Winter, my finger contracts, making them all loose.) Oh, I also just recently used them to fix two 'fashion' type rings-they were flower shaped, 2 had multiple metal layers, one of which had fallen off, the glue secured these, and has stayed that way for a few weeks. One had a faux pearl fall off, I glued it back, all good.
Cons:
My husband applied the 'glue'...btw. I say glue, but the consistency is more like...like a thin grout for the bathtub, you know-it can dry and is kind of stretchy or gives, and can be pulled up in on layer? It's more like this, but obviously, much thinner, due to the tube & product formulation.
1. The gel, at least mine, did not dry clear-it dried white, so if it's spread on thickly, or the glue oozes out the front (visible) part of the rings, it can be seen, and it did get onto my diamonds & in nooks/crannies, due to band style. It came off without damaging the ring or diamonds by cleaning them in a solution safe for jewelry. A light brushing with the brush or cloth included with your cleaner, or a very, very soft toothbrush, will get it completely off, safely.
2. If it does ooze and leave clumps, they cannot usually just be spot removed, you'll end up taking the rest of the 'glue' with it, since it's one long piece.
3. Smooth application can be difficult, especially on rings that thin out in the back-since it's applied on top of the band, which can be difficult.
4. It does take a few tries to get it on well enough, or to whatever look you're ok with. I never got mine to perfection, but I did get it to a 'happy place' lol. Also, white gold/platinum rings and white diamonds hide any small bits of glue.

Pro's
1. I wear my rings every day, but I don't work (outside the home). I didn't wear them, or wore gloves while doing housekeeping, but I usually did not remove them while washing my hands, they were removed for showers/baths. Once we got the application down, they stayed together until I separated them myself. The only times they didn't last, was when the 'glue' was spread too thin in places. I was very happy with the staying power.
2. Really did keep my rings together, all lined up beautifully, and prevented them shifting on my finger, (ladies know, the heavier the ring, the more likely that it's going to end up with the pretty front part towards your palm, and not on top, were it's supposed to be!) While my main idea was not to size my rings up and down, it was effective in doing so to the extent that the rings felt secure, I did not fear one just sliding off. The 'texture' kept everything in place.
3. The tube is great, the product does come out in a small line (although, be prepared to take a pin to the top if it dries in the application part, no biggie) . It also has quite a few applications in it, and doesn't dry out quickly (if you keep the cap on!) I'm buying my 2nd tube just now, at least 2-3 years after the initial tube. My 1st isn't completely empty, and is still working.
4. Practice makes perfect. We found that by squeezing a little glob on, then taking either the thin side of a wooden kitchen skewer, or a toothpick, you can gently smooth it on, then put your ring(s) together (in the case of taking 3 rings like we did, we'd do the top band+wedding set, let it dry securely, then the next evening/hours later, 'glue' the secured/dried top band+bridal set to the bottom band). We'd secure the rings with a wooden clothes pin-they have a few openings that accommodate various sizes-in order to complete the drying process. But, wait until the rings have dried a bit, if they're clipped too soon, they will shift.

So, while I didn't use it in all the ways possible, it most certainly worked in the capacity I needed it to. I would recommend it to friends, and actually, have.

title: Testing definitely shows lower pressure vs OEM product
text: I needed a replacement hose/handle assembly for my Waterpik WP-100 due to a broken hose.  I considered the OEM from Waterpik and the WyFun from Amazon and decided on the WyFun because of the lower price.  Actually, the Waterpik model is only about $3 more but Waterpik charges $5.95 for shipping so there’s a $9+ difference.  Many of the reviews say the pressure from the WyFun is lower than the original Waterpik but I thought I’d give it a try anyway.  I definitely noticed a reduction in pressure when I first tried it and over time, decided that it wasn’t enough so I bit the bullet and ordered the OEM from Waterpik.  One of the first things I noticed in comparing the two was that the intake hole in the fitting that connects to the main unit was smaller on the WyFun unit vs the Waterpik by about 1mm. I then decided to give the two a somewhat scientific pressure test.  I timed how long it took to transfer 12 oz. of water from the Waterpik unit (set on “10”) to a measuring cup.  I did three tests for each hose/handle assembly.  The WyFun averaged slightly over 1:20 (one minute, 20 seconds) for the transfer, the Waterpik was under 1:05.  This tells me that the Waterpik hose/handle moves water about 23% faster than the WyFun.  I’m not hydraulics engineer but I think this equates to 23% more pressure from the Waterpik OEM hose/handle.  The WyFun unit otherwise worked OK for me and if you normally run at a lower pressure, it’s probably suitable, but if you want full pressure, the Waterpik OEM is the way to go.  As a note, I did this testing during the covid-19 crisis under the stay-at-home orders so it gave me something to do.

text:

As for negative reviews I've read about this product: anyone with any kind of experience buying Monoi de Tahiti will recognize the "homemade" nature of the packaging of this one. The packaging itself makes it that much more authentic, and any "texture" or material found within the bottle upon receiving the package is a byproduct of the natural process of making Monoi de Tahiti. In fact, the style of the packaging is what convinced me that this is a far superior product to the other makers of Monoi de Tahiti who make theirs with all sorts of nasty additives (albeit much fancier labels on cheap plastic bottles).

This Monoi de Tahiti comes in a nice glass bottle with a small plastic pump for dispensing and has quickly replaced the need for me to ever try any other Monoi de Tahiti ever again. title: At best it appears to get mildly warm and just wasn't ...
text:
Needed a dual voltage flat iron for trip to Europe and the U.K.
Pros-
It's dual voltage and compact enough to travel with.
Came with 4 alligator style clips.
Included heat protective zip bag to pack if it's still hot.
Cons-
On/Off switch is located in very difficult spot to reach, on the inside just below the bottom plate. Was hard to reach so never bothered switching it off, just unplugged it.
The plates are very small. Granted, this is a travel/compact flat iron so I guess that's to be expected but unfortunate.
There is no heat setting. It's on or it's off. In my opinion, this iron doesn't get hot enough. At best it appears to get mildly warm and just wasn't hot enough for my hair.
Conclusion? Although compact, pretty and packaged nicely, I'd rather take my everyday iron with me and take more room in the suitcase to have something that heats up better, has bigger plates and doesn't take me 5 times longer to do my hair. As far as dual voltage, I won't need that feature often so I'd investigate other options if needed again.

title: Best dry shampoo says this non-dude!
text:
You don’t have to be a dude to make great use of this product! I’m female and don’t use it for what it’s intended for, and it’s become one of my favorite products. I use it as a dry shampoo. I have oily hair, but it’s also thick and takes forever to dry so I wash it every other day. On the days when I don’t wash it, I need a product to keep the oilies away. I’ve tried dry shampoos in aerosol cans but they are so heavily perfumed that I can’t stand them. They also leave a noticeable haze in my dark brunette hair, especially near the scalp and part line. I’ve also tried baby powder, but again the fragrance is too overwhelming and I don’t care to smell like a baby who just had her diaper changed! For awhile I was just using plain old cornstarch but it was messy to apply and also left a white haze near my scalp.

I ordered Fromonda because it’s one of the only unscented body powders I could find. And the verdict? I finally found my go-to dry shampoo! It really is unscented, the shaker bottle makes it really easy to apply close to my scalp and roots, and it is very, very blendable! Meaning that I can easily rub it into my dark hair and it seems to disappear without leaving a noticeable white haze like other powders do. This powder seems to be finer than other powders which makes it easier for my hair to absorb. But also finer as in... hey girl, your hair is so fine and non-oily. How ‘bout a date?

I also started using this powder as a primer before applying deodorant as it ensures my pits are dry first. I couldn’t get away with using it as a deodorant alone though, but I also think my pits are swampier than most! 😝

title: Great unit. Shop for best price.
text:
First off, this package was put together solely for COSTCO, so its availability on Amazon is from enterprising resellers.
There seems to be some confusion among reviewers as to its functionality. Reviewers have commented on the fact that the pressure in the cuff is raised, rather than lowered after pumping the cuff up to a pressure that’s above any possible systolic pressure, as other sphygmomanometers employ. The technique of lowering the cuff pressure while listening with a stethoscope or microphone for the Korotkoff sounds (those tapping and squishing sounds in the brachial artery) suffers from serious imprecision. Nurses have a lot of practice listening to those sounds as they lower the cuff pressure, but unfortunately they often practice an irreproducible technique, even after years of experience, and they often rush the measurement, knowing that they will only be able to get a ball park reading anyhow. To avoid those inaccuracies, a newer measurement technique has been developed in which oscillations in cuff pressure are measured and analyzed algorithmically. The amplitude of these oscillations is only a few mmHg, so they’re insensible. The problem is that the algorithms are proprietary and secret (although there is at least one that is open source). Using this measurement method, the cuff pressure trend can either be falling or rising, it only has to span the mean arterial pressure between systolic and diastolic, but a combination of Korotkoff sounds and pressure oscillations can also be incorporated in the algorithm. Microlife seems to think that they can produce less annoying pressure of the cuff by their method of raising the pressure in small increments and using oscillometric measurement; in my experience it’s not a big comfort difference, but the results are accurate.
So how do I like the unit? It’s great. It’s easy to use; it’s portable or can run off the included wall wart; and it can keep the last 99 measurements with time and date for two people. It can report either a single routine or take three measurements and average them (the preferred option and the one most researchers use). It can report but not analyze irregular heart beats. And it exactly matches the unit in my cardiologist’s office; he thinks it may actually be better.

I have extremely sensitive teeth that causes me to experience severe sensitivity pain to cold air or cold liquid. This is not from cavities. I have been examined by a dentist. Normally, if I have not used my prescription toothpaste and use non-prescription toothpaste, the sensitivity pain comes back with a vengeance within three days. I mean the kind of pain that brings you to your knees.

After using Crest Pro-Health gel toothpaste for five days, I have not experienced any sensitivity pain whatsoever. Plus, the taste is a refreshing cool mint. It is nice and foamy which I like. My teeth are clean after brushing. I don't see any whitening effects at this time, but it has only been five days.

I primarily like this product for controlling my sensitive teeth. The mint taste, foam and whitening (I guess if used long enough) are added bonuses. I give it four stars because I don't see any whitening effects at this time.

title: Great, no-hassle, blood pressure monitor!
text:
At first, I used the stethoscope, upper-arm-sleeve blood pressure monitor. I wasn’t fond of that, so I got a digital reader with the upper-arm sleeve. I still wasn’t fond of the hose that always got tangled up—and probably raised my blood pressure—when I was trying to get everything in place. And the hand pump virtually wore out my forearm when trying to pump it up through three readings. And with the upper-arm wrap, I wasn’t too good at tightening it at just the right spot to get a good reading. I had to fiddle with that all of the time.

Then I got this KEDSUM wrist monitor, which you can set to display the date and time. No hoses. No hand pumping. No worries about proper placement of the wrist wrap. I just wrap it around my wrist as shown in the manual, put my elbow on the table, raise the monitor to heart level, and push a button—and write down the results, although it does keep a digital record for “60 groups of measurement data” for two people. The manual isn’t the greatest in the world and was probably written by someone who doesn’t know English very well, but I stumbled through it and got the monitor going in quick time. Now I no longer dread the hassle of taking my blood pressure. It even detects my a-fib. I’ve used my last upper-arm-sleeve blood pressure monitor. The box it comes in is very compact and measures 3-3/4” by 3-3/4” by 3-3/4,” and inside that is the manual and a plastic case that holds the monitor.

Works great for me!

title: Remains Soft yet Firm when Frozen
text:
I have had several different gel / stay-soft ice packs. I have always liked the comfort gel packs. With a husband and child that have Ehlers Danlos and are accident prone, we have a lot of bumps, bruises, and twisted ankles, etc. in our house. These freeze soft yet firm, so it is easy to wrap around a knee or ankle or other parts. I have also used them for back pain. We will sometimes use them in coolers (especially when traveling) and they easily wrap around bottles of soda/water or other containers in the cooler.

I have never tried them for heat. We tend to use heating pads for that instead.

We unfortunately left some of ours in a hotel freezeer not long ago so I am back replenishing our stock. I have not had one break on me (though it is used frequently) and we had our old ones for several years.

At the time of purchasing I got 5 for ~$25 with tax. So at ~$5 per ice pack I am very happy with the price.

title: Pleasant but not profound
text:
This does provide gentle warmth at the top of three levels. This uses a magnetic attachment to a USB-A power cord. I'd have liked a somewhat longer cord-- but you could add your own USB extension cord if you want more slack between you and the power source / charger (not included).

PROS:
- Mask is light and comfortable.

- Magnetic connection is easy to establish and maintains a tight connection.

- Unobtrusive enough to be used in conjunction with a variety of earphones, headphones and ear buds.

CONS:
- Heat is gentle at the top setting. I'd would have preferred that the scale was bumped up so that the lowest level started higher than it does and that the top level might be somewhat higher for occasional, short term use.

I cannot imagine using this for overnight use. Not because it'd be dangerous-- it would not be at all. But because it's probably not going to work well with anyone who tosses and turns. The ideal usage scenario is in your easy chair or on the couch while listening to pleasant music.

I have had the benefit of testing more massive "eye massager" devices that augment warmth with massage of the temples and around the eyes. I don't want to exaggerate but they come a lot closer to a spa visit than this warmth-only mask. Their prices hover anywhere from slightly higher than this product to twice the price. Any one of those provided me a more profound sense of calm and relaxation. And with my occasional mild migraines, the massage helped me while I waited for painkillers to take effect.

This product might provide some modest relaxation benefits if the purchase price isn't too much of a dent in your budget but I would not hype expectations. It's pleasant but not transformational.

Value:

title: Old stock - not as pictured.  No idea if this is indeed antibacterial or antiviral.
text:
The seller used a photo of newer packaging in the listing which is misleading. The product I received appears to be unused old stock. See photos attached - very similar packaging, EXCEPT the yellow arrow that states 'kills 99% of bacteria and viruses' only states CLEANS & FRESHENS! Always in Reach.

According to the label, the product I received does contain Alkyl Dimethylbenzyl Ammonium Chloride (which will kill a few germs according to Wikipedia), however it does not call it an 'active ingredient' nor list the percentage of this chemical in relation to the overall volume of liquid. Who knows - maybe this stuff is better than the new version?

Pump operation works fine, cardboard shipping boxes are heavy duty and product arrived in good condition. One caveat - this stuff is so heavily scented that there's probably enough perfume in the bottle to kill the germs if indeed the 'active ingredient' isn't so active. So if you're sensitive to perfumes, look for something else.

Normally due to the listing error, I'd give a one star review and send the product back to Amazon for a refund. However given the craziness that is our world this week, I'm going to keep the product and use it hoping it works.

title: Protein "milkshake"...........Made a mistake and thought I'd try something different
text:
I buy tubs of protein pretty much on a bi-weekly basis, so was getting tired of teh same old flavors. Saw the new flavors, chocolate hazelnut flavor oatmeal cookie, and even though they were Plant Based Proteins powder I figured what the hell - and gave them a shot. While teh flavors are good, the powders themselves are just two much. I'm used to just putting two scoops of protein powder in a 12oz smart shaker, adding some water and taking it on the go.

This doesn't work for these proteins; two scoops and 8-12 oz of water and you get a clump of powder. I've needed to use at least 3x the amount of water to even get it to a form that's drinkable, and even then it's like drinking pancake batter. I can't even imagine using milk or almond milk.

Granted it is smooth, but there's just way too much to drink. It's similar when you order a milkshake from silver diner, and they bring you the "leftover" shake in another cup, which is basically the equivalent of having to drink two shakes.

Probably turned me off to all plant based proteins in the future. Guess it's back to my go to Fudge Brownie flavor.....

title: Great BP Monitor
text: I love this BP Monitor.  It is so simple to use.  So, you are probably wondering why the 4 instead of 5 stars.  Well, truth be told, I would give it a 4.5 if we were able to give half stars.  The deduction is really a nitpick. IT is about the voice and the directions.  It is obvious that it is manufactured and the directions were printed by a company where english is not the primary language.  I don't have any issue with that.  It's a big world.  However, it does make it a bit more challenging during setup of any device you get from manufacturers outside of the states.  The voice is just not a pleasing tone and due to the vernacular and inflections, it is just not useful.  You can read the screen 10X faster than the voice prompt reads the screen info to you.  With that said, the screen is terrific.  It is so clear with the black screen and lit data projection.  It is already set to read in mmHg, which is millimeters of mercury.  The menu also is defaulted to a 24-hour clock, which I also appreciate as all of my clocks and watches are set to 24-hour time.  It can also store 2 different users' readings, but if you want to delete them the command is not intuitive.  The menu allows you to set something called PA but nowhere in the menu does it say what that is.  Maybe that is the alternative to mmHG, I don't know.  It comes with a USB c cord as well.  It is not for recharging, but the cord is very short if it is meant to be a power source.  It does come with 4 AAA batteries, so just use those for convenience.  Overall, I love this monitor and its ease of use will have me checking my BP way more often and tracking my health in a more meaningful way.  Hope this helps.

title: Messy but Effective
text:
I own the Sonicare Water Flosser. I'm guessing that's my baseline for this review. It's not perfect. If we could fuse the Sonicare with this Water Dental Flosser Oral Irrigator, it would be the perfect machine for the task at hand.
Now, let's discuss this Dental Flosser Oral Irrigator. It's rather large, standing almost a foot tall without the nozzle attached. About half is the water reservoir and the other half is the handle with the controls and digital display. There's 2 buttons, the top is the power and it starts the water flow. The bottom button toggles thru options and changes the water pressure. There's a hidden lid on the top that lifts up and allows you to store two nozzles. That is a nice bonus feature for storage or travel.

The instructions are rather simple. Rotate the water reservoir a few degrees to remove it from the handle, fill with water and reattach to handle. Press the top button for power then press it again to start the water flow. This is the messy part. You should have the nozzle in your mouth or you're going to get wet. Once that water jet starts, it's shooting a lot of water. So, you have to just open your mouth and let it drain all over the handle and your hand. Not to worry, the MFG says it's rated IPX7, which means it can survive being fully submerged, so drool and water dripping on it shouldn't be an issue.
This thing is pretty powerful. It caused a part of my gum to bleed. That's not a criticism. I like to keep my dentist employed so I haven't flossed in 5 days, so I definitely need to resume the daily floss. Anyway, particles of the Greek salad I had for dinner littered the sink, so this flosser did its job very well.
"So, Mister gross no floss guy, why only 3 stars?? It sounds like this water flosser did its job"
Well, yes it does seem to floss very well. However, I believe some improvements are needed before you'll pry those remaining 2-stars from my wet drool and food particle covered hand. There needs to be a trigger or additional button to allow control of the water. Currently, you start the water and it comes out non-stop leading to the drooling mess. If you could control the water, you could control the drool. They could also preprogram the water to come out in bursts. I was initially impressed with the larger water tank, but it turns out that larger reservoir is needed due to the amount of water this thing spits out.

In summary, it does floss well, but it is fairly messy from my experience. If I figure out a way to make it a little less wet, I'll definitely edit my review with my suggestions.

title: Cleaning, yes.  Remineralizing, not so sure.
text:
I bought this because I've been exploring non-fluoride remineralizing tooth powders.* I started with Frau Fowler's Mouth Medic, which I liked (see review there for more detail) but was disappointed to realize that 'supports remineralizing' doesn't seem to mean it actually has any remineralizing agents in it. I moved on to Simply Sooney. I'm like it to use, but I'm not so sure about the long-term benefits. I haven't found any way to do my personal research into remineralizing yet.

Pros: Cleans well. That's the big one! It isn't too sweet, isn't so salty it makes me drool, and I like the orange flavor. It's all-natural. It's affordable.

Cons: there doesn't actually seem to be much research on whether bentonite actually helps remineralize teeth. There are minerals in the clay. You put the clay on your teeth. Whether they're minerals that are useful to your teeth in preventing/fighting tooth decay is not clear. Basically, it appears to be guess-work and it-sounds-reasonable thinking. That doesn't mean it's wrong, but I'd like to see some solid research backing it up. Another con is that it doesn't have a lingering alkalinizing effect, which I like, especially at night, to slow down the effect of naturally-produced destructive acids in the mouth. Finally, the flavor isn't strong enough for me.

Neutral: the consistency is a little weird, but I think I could get used to it easily. It leaves a bit of a residue in the sink, but it's easily rinsed or wiped away.

I may add some stuff to it to help with some of the cons, if I can find the right ingredients in a fine powder. Otherwise, I'll probably keep looking after I use up this (generously sized) container. But if I can't find anything with more research-supported ingredients, I'll probably come back to this one, because I do like it.

Three stars because it advertises 'remineralizing' without satisfactory support, and that was the main thing I chose it for. If it weren't for that (or if I found research supporting it after all), I'd give it a 4 or a 5.

*I am not anti-fluoride. I use a natural fluoride mouth rinse in the mornings. I want an *additional* remineralizing agent, not a substitute. However, if you are anti-fluoride, this will apply as well.

title: Somewhat relaxing with an okay flavor.
text:
After drinking this for over 3 weeks, I did notice it relaxed me a bit on the nights I took it. While I did not notice any effect on falling asleep sooner or staying asleep, I did notice that falling back asleep after waking up in the middle of the night was easier. I did not drink this nightly, and have just been trying it every now and then to see the effectiveness/side effects. Maybe about 3 or 4 days a week.

The taste is okay for me. It has a touch of sweetness, slightly bitter, and a coffee-like taste. I do taste the peppermint and wished it had more, but thats just a personal preference.

Now everyone is different, but I ended up getting a headache after drinking it. They weren't bad headaches, but just enough to know it's there. I have taken most of the ingredients listed without side effects, but I don't want to blame specific ingredients without knowing for sure which is the culprit.

In the end, I wouldn't purchase this product. The ingredients listed are great and it may help you, but it unfortunately gave me headaches. I have tried another Reishi nighttime drink and preferred the taste of it. Im not a big fan of coffee though, so it all comes down to personal preference. The other product I tried was Four Sigmatic Mushroom Hot Cacao with Reishi. It doesn't have as much of the beneficial ingredients the FreshCap mushroom tea does, but I enjoyed the flavor and still noticed a relaxed feeling when taking it(without headaches).
I do believe that reishi mushrooms help calm, so this FreshCap product may be worth a shot if you enjoy a coffee tea taste.

title: Thoughtful Design & Excellent Value
text:
I'm pretty impressed with this product and wish I'd gotten one sooner!

I've been doing vaginal steams for about 5 years now since first learning about them from an herbal practitioner. I love them - they're so relaxing, beneficial and an easy way to practice self-care. At the time of first learning about them, it was suggested that if I wanted to do them at home it would be least expensive to get a 5-gal bucket from Lowe's and order a camp toilet seat (for portable/compostable toilets). This was efficient and cost only about $15, which at the time was less than what I was seeing for better ones, like this.

This sitz bath is fantastic and at the time of writing this review it's going for just under $19. Here's what I like:
- Collapsible: it takes up so little space when stored.
- Quality Feel: it feels well-made and sturdy.
- Easy to Clean: I have had no trouble scrubbing it after use.
- The holes in the back make it super easy to empty without making a mess.
- Fits my standard-sized toilet
- Excellent price point.

Only con - it's a little tough to close the toilet seat for the water/herbs to steep. It's just too thick for it to properly close (and therefore properly steep herbs). Because of this, I may steep them first then pour it in. Small change in my process, but something to note if that was your current process too.

All in all, I highly recommend it. I'm very pleased!!

title: Unexpected jarring blue light at bedtime, but otherwise effective. If you can follow the instructions.
text:
Good: this light wakes me up gently and within a few minutes of the beginning of its sunrise mode.

Bad: I have become adept at turning off yet another form of alarm in my sleep, and this one isn't unpleasant enough to wake me up sufficiently that I remain awake for long.

Most jarring thing: the sunset simulator goes from full daylight and fades over a half-hour. This sounds great. In practice, this means if you are using the lamp on automatic light temperature cycle mode and initiate sunset after 9pm (when the lamp switches to "night" warm-white mode), there's a slight delay, and then all six LEDs turn on full blast. That means a jump in illumination and a strong shot of blue light, although the ramp-down of the light is nice and smooth and helps me go to sleep a little more quickly than I otherwise might. Minus one star.

The people who complain about the user interface are not wrong. It's amazing, and I say that with astonishment and fear. The icons are tiny. You do need the manual. This would be minus two stars on its own. There were some details in the manual that were slightly inaccurate (exact button sequences to save/escape), but I managed to puzzle through with some trial and error and button-mashing.

You can tell that you have the feature enabled if the relevant icon is blinking. If the icon isn't blinking, go back through and try again.

If you want to test the light alarm to see how it turns on, don't set the alarm for 1 minute from now, set it for 31+ minutes from now. It's not programmed to realize that a newly set light alarm less than 30 minutes away should turn the light on immediately and bring it quickly to full intensity, it will only activate at the 30 minutes before alarm time mark.

The lamp will shut itself off after a while when it's turned on as an alarm.

title: I don't understand this scale at all
text:
Update: After a ton of exercise and barely any fattening food at the Relay for Life this weekend, my weight went up 5 pounds and my body fat % went up 4%. Wait, what?? A minute later I reweighed and was back to what I expected. I sent the scale back. I love my fitbit Ultra but HATE this scale. I can't trust anything it says. Thanks to Amazon's great service, I got my money back in two days!! I bought the EatSmart scale instead for less than half the price. It has MUCH better reviews. Hopefully it works better. It can't possibly be worse. As an aside, I posted another question on the FitBit forum and not only did I not get an answer, I think my question was deleted.

--original review--

My husband and I are around the same weight. When I step on the scale in the morning it weighs me around 180 then asks me to tell which person I am. It uploads the info to fitbit. Then if I step on the scale again, it says "hi" which it doesn't the first time. Then it says "sensing", which it also never does the first time. Then it comes back with 176. This has been going on pretty consistently for a week. Four pounds difference between the first weigh and the second a minute later. I tried posting to the boards at fitbit, twice in fact since this wasn't my first problem. No answers. If a scale is going to be as frustrating and not dependable as this one, I'm sure you can get one for much less money.

There is virtually no documentation and really no help. I will update if I ever figure this out. Right now I'm very unhappy with this purchase.

title: An okay massager, not strong enough for my needs
text:
[[VIDEOID:ac0bfbe8e22d4968e421edd03535bc80]] The H2OMO back massager is a decent device for its price range. While it's not my favorite tool so far, it does provide some subtle relief and is helpful to have strapped to my desk chair (even when off), to help me maintain better posture.

My chronic illnesses cause pain and discomfort, with my back and neck being pretty unbearable most days. I've been trying to find a variety of tools that may at least temporarily provide relief. I will admit, I prefer stronger massage pressure than the H2OMO provides. The heat function, however, is pleasant and doesn't seem to get too hot compared to similar products. It does hold a little heat after your 15 minute session and post unplugging the device.

Inside the handled box, you receive the massager, a manual, car adaptor, and regular power plug.

**I also want to note: a card from the company with an outlook email address was included, advising to contact them to activate a warranty card...and offering a gift card after reviewing. Please keep that in mind when reading reviews. I find it odd and kind of bribe-y, honestly.**

The device isn't too loud, just a low thrumming sound. Its cover can zip off for washing, and features an elastic strap on the back for placement. Keep in mind, shiatsu "pillows" are firm and have some heft to them.The button placement is on the back, which is slightly easier to reach and adjust when in use. The power button also cycles through the subtle mode differences. Long press to power on the device and start at the lower intensity with heat, another press for higher intensity, another press to turn off heat, etc. The other button is to switch directions, but I prefer a device that does that on its own during use.

Overall, this is an okay device, but I feel it's pricey at its current $51.99 (at the time of this review). I'm leery of companies that offer a reward after emailing a non business sounding contact email proof of your review.

title: Updated: Soothing after you get accustomed to the sensation
text:
[[VIDEOID:28b41da2dec2d1153a4fb0e3d8f14dab]] **TLDR pros/cons at the end of this review**

I have a lot of hand/wrist pain and weakness from my chronic illnesses and am constantly looking for tools to provide some relief. This will be a nice aid when I'm in flares or am unable to manipulate manual tools.

First impression aesthetically: The massager is a bit bulky and looks like something out of a "futuristic" cartoon. It will take up some space for storage, particularly since the instructions advise keeping it in the original box.

Practicality: This item has very specific and limited usage, which makes the current price feel a little high. Additionally, the charger form factor is a bit limiting and you'll need an adapter if you don't have USB specific charging ports available.

Usage: The instructions are simple to follow and describe the three modes, although the names for each aren't too helpful in understanding their effects. It would be more practical if they described what function they serve. If you have small to averagely large hands, there's enough space to rest them comfortably, with room for your thumb on either side. The inner lining is smooth and feels nice against your skin. It's simple to select the mode you'd like or to add heat.

Sensory: This may take some getting used to, depending on your sensory needs. I experience discomfort when things press stop my cuticles/nails, so I may not use the refresh mode as much. The compressive aspect is a bit bizarre initially and made me internally squirm a bit, but after a few minutes you get accustomed to the feeling and it becomes relaxing. I was able to close my eyes and enjoy the pressure and heat as the little nodes did their thing. I particularly enjoy the feeling on my wrists, as their norm is to feel loose and pained. This provided at least some temporary relief from finger stiffness.

My doughy EDS skin takes on texture impressions (so don't worry, you probably won't see the pattern of the nodes when you remove your hand), but I figured I'd include a photo to give you a better idea of the internal workings. The size of each massager remind me of the side of an small pony bead.

Overall, I can see this having some positive benefits regarding relaxation and relief from general discomfort. It's a good tool to make hand massage more accessible for those of us with mobility/grip issues and/or disabilities. I'll be sure to update this review if further usage causes concerns or additional benefits.

Pros:
-Different modes and levels, plus heat
-Helps enliven stiff/cold fingers.
-Easy to operate, can fit variety of users
-Relaxing, good self care to add to your routine
-More accessible hand/wrist relief option for the chronically ill or disabled
-Fairly quiet when running

Cons:
-Bulky
-Cost may be tough to budget for
-Charging form factor is limiting
-Specific usage
-May trigger sensory issues or initial flight reaction due to compression sensation (start at the low setting, you may adjust quickly and find it relaxing)

Update: Originally 4/5, now 3(3.5)/5. I've used the hand massager for 45 minutes to an hour total after fully charging it when it arrived. While it's convenient to not be tethered to an outlet, it's disappointing that the unit turned off just now when I tried using it. For the current price, I thought the battery would last longer before needing a recharge. Also, I usually use this with headphones on and my eyes closed, so I didn't see the warning light flashes when the battery died during use. It doesn't seem that the nodes are repositioned prior to shutting down (the machine just stopped during a compression cycle).

title: Excellent tool and great value

title: Such a soft brush - no gum discomfort
text:
Wow!! What a soft brush! When brushing my teeth, it feels so smooth - like getting a polish from the dentist. I didn’t feel any gum discomfort but yet I did feel like my teeth and gums were getting clean. Even if I push hard, these brushes cushion the pressure so that I continued to feel soft brushing.

Now, I just wish these had some sort of approval from the ADA. While I would assume my teeth are getting the brushing they need, I can’t be so sure. Some parts of the product page don’t instill a lot of confidence (for example, the picture in the product page of the before and after teeth - the woman’s teeth become several shades writer after using these brushes - makes no sense, so can I really trust some of the other claims about my teeth getting a good clean with these soft bristles?) Also these came in some traveling toothbrush cases, that didn’t give the brushes a lot of protection from possible dirt and grime within the package, so if you get these, I suggest giving them a good wash - I did so in baking soda and water.

Assuming that these work to clean your teeth the way a toothbrush should, I really do like them!

title: Kind of bulky
text:
This water flosser is quite a bit larger than I would have preferred for a portable model. The tank is not removable. There is an easy-to-lose rubber cap for the charging connector which isn't a 'captured' component (think of how a gas cap doesn't fall on the ground when you unscrew it). So you have to set it down and remember where it was put. Also, the toothbrush and flosser don't use the same means for charging, which means you'll have to remember two cables if you plan to go on an extended vacation.

The flosser itself works well, although the tank doesn't seem to be removable. It has enough oomph to get out those annoying pieces of corn kernels that get stuck between the teeth. I tend to leave my flosser on the 'DIY' setting, as it lets me control the level with plenty of precision. However, I probably would have preferred a dial or better designed interface for that mode, as there is no way to lower the level after it is at a certain point. +/- buttons would have been a big improvement here.

The toothbrush is nice and compact, although its buzz seems more annoying than I would prefer.

title: first-time miswak user and I'm pleased with these
text:
Disclosure: I've never used these before, and so my review is from the perspective of a first encounter. I wanted to look into these as a backpacking option that would reduce the need for one or two things to pack.

Overall, I'm pleased. They have a scent and flavor I wasn't prepared for, and will take some time getting used to, but it's not revolting. In fact, it has already grown on me a little in a couple uses. It's just unfamiliar to my palate. To my understanding, this is partly because of some bittering compounds in the bark.

A little about miswak for newbies like me: Miswak comes from the Arak tree. It has antibacterial properties, and the bitter compounds stimulate saliva production. The chemical composition of the tree includes a number of natural cavity-fighting compounds. It is purported to strengthen enamel--I have no idea if that claim is accurate. Used properly, however, many peer-reviewed studies suggest this to be equally effective to toothbrushes and toothpaste (select studies suggest possibly more effective). The Arak also has mild analgesic properties.

To use this stick you chew or cut about 1/2 inch of the end off, then chew the inner part until bristles form (it only takes a few seconds), and then brush in an up and down motion on your teeth. Every so often you cut off the bristle portion and slice off a bit more bark, rinse and repeat.

In terms of flavor, I found it a little indescribable. I was trying to find someone else's description online, and someone on reddit said they taste like the crystalline form of the white powder drug. I have zero experience with that and can only take their word for it.

The packaging for these seems to pretty universally involve vacuum packaging. These are no exception. In terms of price, these were much cheaper than the Middle Eastern grocer in my town, and cheaper than a lot of bourgeois rebrands of miswak as a conscientious lifestyle choice for eco-hippies.

As for effectiveness, I've only used it a couple times so far, but it has been shockingly effective at removing the day's tartar from my teeth, and much quicker than my usual (standard nylon bristle) toothbrush. For the first couple uses I ended up with bits of the bark in my mouth that I had cut off improperly, but they're easy to get out and they're soft and not stabby.

In spite of not being accustomed to the flavor, I like it enough that I may even carry one around regularly for on-the-go toothbrushing. If you like clean teeth and also enjoy chewing on toothpicks and straws and such, this may be a great option for you to try out.

title: Does the job!
text:
This water flosser is a bit awkward in design, but it does clean teeth well. The build materials are somewhat robust. I already dropped this on the floor by accident, and it still works fine. The replaceable plastic tip did break off with a piece still inside the connecting part, but it was easy to remove and replace. It comes with replaceable tips.

The flosser comes with a plastic reservoir to fill with water. There's a plastic tube that reaches into it to pump out the water. It holds plenty of water.

The spray from the water flosser is powerful. It really blasts away through the crevices and gaps. It takes a little getting used to, and I accidentally sprayed water on the wall. Guess I should be more careful where I aim this thing. It can be a bit awkward trying to turn it on and off. Not a huge issue.

You can change the pulse patterns of the spray or leave it on a steady stream. It doesn't hurt teeth. However, if you have sensitive teeth, pay special attention to the temp of the water. Personally, I have cold sensitivity, so I use warm water.

It's not a bad product. It works just fine. However, my issue is with the design. It can be hard to maneuver inside your mouth because of the bulky design. It can fall over easily if there's no water in the reservoir, because it's a little top heavy. I recommend removing the reservoir after use or store it in an organizer or something.

But, yeah, I like this way better than using dental floss.

title: The keys don't fold into the handle, so they're gonna stab everything.
text:
Sure, it has a wide handle with a nice ergonomic shape, but without the ability to fold the keys into the large space inside the handle, what's the point? The key teeth will rip through purse linings, poke your thigh from the inside of your pants pocket, or scrape little bloody lines into your chest, if you were to wear it on a lanyard or ball-joint necklace or something.

There IS a horizontal hole in the handle, if you turn it sideways to look at why the frack the keys can't fold into the handle, despite there being plenty of room. So it's plausible to run a necklace-like-thing thru that hole and wear your keys around your neck. But, if you were going to do that anyway, just put the keys on the necklace directly. There are much better "wing nut" shaped silicone key-head covers that will give the weak of grip more, well, grip. Without being so tremendously difficult to set up and switch out.

Plus, this product is intended for those with low dexterity, to HELP them hold small objects, right? So why is it designed so that, to put the keys into the holder, you have to crank a tiny handle to unscrew the central metal screw-threaded rod, causing you to immediately drop other side's tiny hexagonal nut, which you didn't notice earlier, that really SHOULD have been glued into place - like, why leave that thing loose?? AND THEN you have to hold each of your keys, to be inserted, verrryyyy carefully, in the upper part of the handle. And continue to hold the other side's nut in place - at least they designed the plastic handle to have a correctly-sized hexagonal hole to HOLD the nut, at that spot! - while trying to poke the threaded rod thru the tiny holes in the tops of your keys, and then also successfully thru the tiny holes in the top of this key-holder??? Or, my favorite silly maneuver, hold the handle sideways, resting the nut in its little cut-out with gravity's help, feeling like you've finally figured out the correct way to use this mysterious object. And THEN, you immediately miss with the threaded rod, shoving the nut out of its cut-out and back onto the floor. Where you just picked it up from. :P If someone needs their ego deflated or brought down a peg, seriously, buy them this thing as a gag gift, and watch them curse your birth.

So once you've placed all the keys into their slots, is that it? Have you succeeded against this formidable puzzle? Not at all! You have to go through this rigamarole every time you want to change a key! And what about if you want to USE a key? Ho-ho! Well! You've fallen right into its trap! Because if you want to make just ONE key stick out forward, and the others not in its way? Ya know, to place it into a lock? You have to unscrew the central rod, juuuust a teeny bit, to decrease the pressure of the plastic sides on each key, making them all fall limp and perfectly lined up. Now! NOW, you have to pick one, and hold it between your fingers, to point it straight forward so you can actually poke it into a lock, and THEN, you have to RE-tighten the little crank! And hope you don't drop the tiny nut on the backside again! And if you have to use two keys in quick succession? As in the situation of having a storm door locked, and a solid door behind it? Then you have to REPEAT that process! Just... why. Did nobody stress-test this design? This is nearly useless, even for someone WITH good hand strength!

That's my second complaint - someone with really good fine motor control like myself struggled to get this thing set up. Someone with weak hands trying to buy this thing for themselves would have a much harder time. And not every person with disabilities has access to an able-bodied person who can do the difficult things for them! That's important to keep in mind when designing accessibility products.

The only reason I didn't give this product one star is because the metal bits are actually very well machined, and it turns very nicely. Perhaps it can find new life as a fidget toy for a middle schooler, to spin the crank back and forth. I sure won't be giving this to my grandmother to try to struggle with, with her arthritic hands! :/

title: ETL-Listed ALCI Plug; CE-marked brush; Oval shape and decent performance
text:
The Kinga hair dryer brush is a very sleek-looking, lightweight, and ergonomic brush with three heat settings. The brush has ceramic coating, which protects the hair while drying and the bristles are tangle-free.

The brush with the oval head takes time getting used to when you have used a round brush all along, but I can see how the oval brush works better. The low setting did not dry my hair. I have soft straight wavy shoulder length hair, and had to use the high setting to dry my hair and style. The brush did not add much volume, but helped to straighten out the soft waves in my hair. Did not lose much hair in the brush as the bristles did not tangle my hair which was a definite plus.

Overall pleased, with the ease of use and the results.

From a safety standpoint, the unit comes with an ALCI plug (prevents electrocution if dropped in water) that is ETL-Listed, which is good. However, there is no UL or ETL listing mark on the dryer brush itself – instead there is a CE marking on it. This is not nearly as good as UL or ETL listing, but it is better than nothing.

title: Works well; readings match another existing unit we have
text:
I got the Antrolife AES-Ui121 for daily measurement of daily blood for my mom. It came with everything one needs to get started right out of the box. The box came with detailed instructions along with how to use guiding pictures on the box. It contained a sleek rectangular white unit, with a large display that rests nicely on a flat surface at 45 degree angle. The box also comes with 4 AAA batteries and a USB cord to power the unit, a large high quality blood pressure cuff with a guide steel rod for circling the cuff around the arm, and a nice pouch to easily carry the unit.

The blood pressure cuff is large and made up of quality material and it can fit most arms without difficulty. Once my mom learned how to wear the cuff, start and turn off the unit, it was easy for her to use it by herself without needing a help from someone else. The unit has very large, senior-citizen-friendly display screen with just 3 buttons – one for setup, one for start/stop, and one for memory.

I really appreciated that it came with 4 AAA batteries, and it was made in USA. In addition, a note by the company in the box says they are part of campaign to plant several billion trees in USA and part of their revenue is donated for that purpose.

My mom has used other machines but found this to be nicer, sharper to read, and easy to operate, and easy carry in the pouch while visiting her friends.

title: 5 day supply overpriced, full of cadmium, thorium, strontium, sugar??
text:
EDIT: I had to update my review towards the negative because I didn't like being slandered, called a liar, ridiculed, and having comment and review-stuffing of what sounds like PR company written propaganda doing ad hominem attacks against me. I got mad at being attacked and now am responding to save other users the trouble.

Since I posted my review, there are a bunch of "positive reviews" that sound like they were written by a PR company, or attacks on me calling me a liar when the label itself tells you everything. I am doubting the positive reviews are legit. Do a general search of the internet yourself and read about the doubts people have had about this product. This has been discussed in forums multiple times. I don't want to link offsite but you can use google.

I have revised my 2 star down to 1 star after learning of health DANGERS. Another user (as well as forum discussions elsewhere on the internet - use google) pointed out that "plant mineral powder" contains cadmium, thorium, and strontium.

I've also been attacked as "not being able to do math" (i'm about 300lbs due to type 2 insulin resistance yet I eat very healthy 85% of the time, the directions say 1-2 scoops per 100lbs bodyweight, the radio host clearly pushed best weight loss benefits at the higher 2 scoops level, and under that math one canister lasts about 5 days) and attacked for claiming its' not organic yet there is no organic certification on the label, it is not advertised as organic anywhere, etc. I cannot for a moment believe that a "true customer" (as opposed to say, the apparent Multi Level Marketing manufacturer of this product sockpuppeting a response??) would spread lies talking you into buying it for things provably untrue on the label, which you can't even see here on amazon until you actually order the product and read it yourself.

If there are multiple, personal responses all attacking me for telling the truth that is right on the label, there must be multiple, fraudulent positive reviews as well for this junk. I wasted hundreds of dollars to find out it wouldn't help at all. A product with ingredients seeming to be this cheap only needs to scam you into trying it once though.

There are truly dumb positive reviews saying how much cheaper this is than buying vitamins to match the doses yourself, I don't know what planet they are coming from, probably manufacturer PR again (who writes reviews like that??), the powder form vitamins used in megadoses here like C and B complexes are available in large bulk versions from anywhere, so is bulk E and A in high doses, and you can compare the costs to the cheapest made in china vitamin powders because there is no organic certification and no statements about the origin or forms of the vitamins to differentiate them in any way from the cheapest, which means they are almost definately the cheapest or they'd be trumpeting it from the rooftops. There are much healthier forms of vitamin C (rose hips for instance) which don't seem to be those used here because they are more expensive yet more bioavailable. The only thing "special" about this product differentiating it from a general vitamin megadosing plan is the "plant mineral powder", which my experience shows it has no magic weight loss at lower or high doses. If you are ultra deficient in vitamins you'll probably have benefit, but you can get those benefits for alot lower cost.

This product has so much sugar in it it will prevent you from doing Atkins or Protein Power type diets and could even be a risk for diabetics or require alot more insulin. What other health products do you know that are more than half corn sugar and fructose? The energy boost is probably from the sugar alone like those energy drinks, one scoop made 12oz water taste like Kool Aid yet my recommended dose for 300lbs was six scoops twice per day according to the label itself.

======
My full original review, even though I no longer stand behind it being a 'good product', where i ranked it 2 stars, titled: 5 day supply phenomenally overpriced
-------
I'm not sure if i'm supposed to compare something to a different product, especially if the other product is praised more. I have no affiliation with either company, financial incentive, reward or anything else from them to give a positive or negative review for anyone.

Does this seem to be a good product? Yes for the most part.

Is it worth the money? Only if it brings you ongoing miracles not obtainable elsewhere.

I heard about this on a popular alternative news radio show which used to really push a different product for years (Enerfood) which as far as I know used to be sold here as well although maybe they stopped being an advertiser and so stopped being pushed on the radio show. Said radio host has a solid reputation for news but a possible conflict of interest pushing otherwise good quality but often substantially overpriced (from double to far worse like $12 solar panels for $80) products. For that previous product I tried it, based upon the hosts recommendations and DID have what I could almost call a miracle - an undeniable boost of energy, alertness, clarity, and reduced hunger because my body something it needed that I assume I wasn't getting before. I had tried other algae supplements and nothing was even close to what I experienced on Enerfood, which i'm GUESSING was because my body was utterly starved from whatever it happened to supply despite trying or taking various multivitamins and similar or the extra stuff they threw in really made a difference.

FYI I try many health products including expensive ones, always looking for a "new edge". Some other health products pushed by the host actually turned out meeting their expectations so I was optimistic.

This is a different type of product, basically a megadose vitamin powder instead of a superfood. It's ingredients are nonspectacular however, not much different than what you find in other good quality vitamins or if so no attempt has been made to document why they are better. They don't seem to be organic or any extraordinary source, it's mostly a vitamin powder with an adequate covering tangerine taste plus some other plant extracts and such added in along with recommended dosages that will probably put the typical american male using 5-6 containers per month costing $300(or over $400 "at retail") at which point it is extraordinarily expensive for a multivitamin.

Now make no mistake I DID feel an energy boost taking it, not a mega one but an undeniably noticible one, one I did not get taking general multivitamins, mega-B vitamins and similar. But it was not life-altering extraordinary and it requires the "full recommended dose" to get at which point one container lasts me 5 days, and at which point its so far beyond any megavitamin levels i've ever even attempted (ie vitamin B12 being about 50,000% the US RDA at that level) it could be due to that alone. At more sedate levels (like half that) it just seems to be a solid mega multivitamin. There was no "reduction of food cravings" past about the 4 hours water soluable vitamins seem to last in your body. Now it's possible that because I already take Enerfood that i'm already getting a high quality of nutrition although it is not a megavitamin product. Other people report taking Enerfood and having no miracles yet I did, and i'm guessing this product is probably similar YMMV. Others taking this product have reported weight loss at levels I have to assume was at least $300+/month perhaps because their body has been vitamin starved or they have only had low quality vitamins. I was hoping it might fill some mineral hole or something due to not being totally sure what was in it, just going off word off mouth. For some it will be exactly what you are missing and for others it will be a boost but not a huge one.

Since i'm not feeling a difference in say food desires past about 4 hours I don't see how it will have a weight loss benefit superior to "superfoods", although superfoods in general seem to have a benefit. Note it's not sold as a weight loss supplement just others report benefits like that and that seems to be the word of mouth reason pushed by the radio host in question to give it a try.

I ordered 3 of them without reading more on the dosage, thinking a 1lb container might last around a month, as it is a full evaluation at recommended doses will equal my house payment. Until the price starts to approach something resembling reality or some explanation of what is so special about the ingredients that justifies a cost probably 10 times higher than other things i've seen (not to beat a dead horse but the Enerfood is organic, specially cold processed, its vitamin sources are from food sources which digest FAR better for bioavailability and I get the mental high from it at a fraction of the dose while it costs less than this.. What most bothers me is for this premium price it just seems to contain common forms of vitamin powders that are in every other vitamin, and the mysteriously named not even organic "fruit and vegetable powder" and "planet derived mineral powder" could mean absolutely anything and they refuse to divulge even a theory of why it should be so good, plus it contains things that don't usually appear in top tier health supplements like xanthan gum... is it because of this filler that a single container only lasts about 5 days?)

So what do I think so far? It's getting 2 stars for the price alone, it would have originally gotten 3 stars until I realized one $50 container wont even last a week. It seems like a good product, of good quality. Not miraculous, just good. I say good instead of decent simply because of having the mental clarity spike after my first serving so i'm being optimistic it has something that at least is not in absolutely everything else. I would happily add it to my daily regimen at maybe $30/month, maybe even $40-45. But not when I need 6 of these to last a month. Not when it's not even organic, not food source vitamins, lacks documentation for other ingredients and similar and mostly is relying upon testimonials instead of even an attempt to document scientifically why it would contain anything more special than other multivitamins using exactly the same "ascorbic acid" for vitamin C (not the more readily absorbed Ester-C, not rose hips) for instance.

title: Don't believe it
text:
Don't use Zetaclear to treat nail fungus. It's a scam.

To start with, just look at the ingredients in ZetaClear Clear Nails Solution as mentioned on their website (in order of prevalence).

Undecylenic Acid - a moderately good topical antifungal. Buy a lifetime supply for a few bucks at your local pharmacy. And can be found in other products for much less. For example: FungiCure, Fungi-Nail, Tinecide. Read more by searching Lee dot org for "Zetaclear".

Tea Tree Oil - It's an OK natural anti-bacterial and anti-fungal. It might help with your nail fungus but it costs $5 for 8 oz, not $30 for 0.5 oz plus shipping!

Clove Oil - smells nice. Kills fungus? Not so much.

Almond Oil - nice oil for back rubs...

Jojoba Oil - wha?

Vitamin E Oil - Good for lots of things. But not for fungus.

Lemongrass Oil - Smells nice on Thai food. Not so much help with fungus.

Some other reviews recommend not buying Zetaclear from Amazon. Those are fake reviews (just look at how many other reviews those "people" have written. Hint: 0) trying to get you to buy the product from the private website where they'll charge you and arm for shipping and a leg for returning the product when you realize it doesn't work.

title: Good but too flimsy. Not worth it for only three days use.
text:
I work at a job where I'm on my feet all day and the stress on my feet has caused calluses that just won't heal. I thought these might help, and they seemed as though they had started to help a little. But after only three days the material broke and it could no longer be worn. They are just too expensive to be going through a new pair twice a week.

Anyhow, general notes:

They are made of a thin, cushiony silicone, so when you first put them on they feel kind of similar to how gel shoe inserts would feel if you put them at the front instead of under your heel.
The first day I wore them it felt as though it was hard to stand and they affected my balance (just a little). After only one day though, I got used to it and could forget they were even there.
When putting them on it's a bit of a fuss to get them situated without bunching up or stretching too tight. The silicone tends to stay right where it's placed so you can't slide them on like socks. It takes some time but it's probably a good thing because it also keeps them in place through the day — well, mostly... There's a nasty tendency of the bottom to roll itself up away from the ball of the foot. But you can feel when it does and stop and readjust it.

So, the second day warring them, they did help relieve the discomfort of the calluses.. The downside was that the silicon rubbed against my toes and caused an abrasion on the top of my right middle toe. I didn't yet xx but knew I was going to have to bandage it to prevent it getting worse. At the moment it was just a red, tender patch, but continued use would certainly aggravate it further. But in spite of this I was impressed with the progress in relieving the calluses. I would estimate that wearing these for a month or two would have allowed them to heal completely.
But unfortunately these are too flimsy to be worn anywhere close to that long. On the third day the one on my left foot broke. I didn't notice until I took my sock of at the end of the day, but it is now completely un-useable. So it didn't last long enough to be worth it.

Beating all this in mind I might still day that if you weigh less than 150 lbs and aren't exceptionally active during the day then they might still be okay for you. For me though, far too disposable.

The new mat smelled divine, there is no "slippiness", and I am one happy yogi. My old mat is rolled up in the corner for when my sis comes to visit and we do yoga together. She'll love the smell!

I am so glad I found the Yoga Mat Cleaner -- it truly ads an element to my practice that enhances my sense of well-being. I'm sure most of you experienced yogi's already know how pleasant aroma therapy is, but if you're new -- add this aroma and cleanliness to your practice for that extra umph!

title: Not what I thought it was...
text:
I usually have no complaints with Vive products. They are quality made, this being no exception and I still use the shoehorn from them daily. But this is the first one I do have a complaint with.

This says it's supposed to help put on socks, the one bane to my independence with dressing. However, there are NO instructions with it. I seriously have NO clue how I am supposed to use this to put my socks on. I tried using the S-shaped hook and I couldn't figure out how to get my foot into the 'leghole' of the sock. The sock wouldn't even stay on the C-hook on the other end of the stick.

The one upswing to this stick is it does help to remove the socks and/or shoes, but my individual problem is putting these clothing items ON, not taking them off.

If a disabled person has trouble with any other article of clothing, this will be a god-send to them. But if your only trouble is socks, order an actual sock aid.

I'll gladly edit this review if I figure out how to use this to put on socks.

FINAL THOUGHTS
Great for any type of clothing... except socks.

WOULD RECOMMEND: Not really

I have had my glove for two weeks and found I do get some relief from the pain. There is an instant lessening of pain as soon as I put it on due to the compression of the glove.

I used to wear those braces with the metal plate and was restricted in what I could do, then at night I would take them off in my sleep because they were so uncomfortable. With Copper Compression I am able to do my daily chores (excluding anything with water) and find I never take them off in my sleep.

My biggest recommendation is to consider swelling in your wrist if you don't plan on wearing them 24/7. I bought two, one medium and one large because I have trouble with both wrists and one was slightly larger than the other. The benefit I wasn't expecting is when my smallest wrist swells, it is nice to have the large size till the swelling goes down and I can comfortably wear the medium again. So in a nut shell take the time to measure your wrist before you order.

I highly recommend these sleeves/gloves to anyone suffering from pain due to repetitive movement. They are comfortable, pain relieving and don't restrict your daily action.

Saw palmetto is an extract derived from the deep purple berries of the saw palmetto fan palm (Serenoa repens), a plant indigenous to the coastal regions of the southern United States and southern California.

Health benefits

Saw palmetto is a remarkable herb for both men and women and is used by natural health practitioners to treat a variety of ailments such as testicular inflammation, urinary tract inflammation, coughs and respiratory congestion. It is also used to strengthen the thyroid gland, balance the metabolism, stimulate appetite and aid digestion. This wonderful herb is becoming famous for its uses in hair restoration, prostate health, sexual vigour, breast enhancement and as a nutritive tonic.

Saw palmetto berry also tones the urethra and it may be used to uphold the healthy function of the thyroid gland and urinary system.

Historical use

In the United States, its medicinal uses were first documented in 1879 by Dr. J.B. Read, a physician in Savannah, Georgia, who published a paper on the medicinal benefits of the herb in the April 1879 issue of American Journal of Pharmacy. He found the herb useful in treating a wide range of conditions. He wrote,"By its peculiar soothing power on the mucous membrane it induces sleep, relieves the most troublesome coughs, promotes expectoration, improves digestion and increases fat, flesh and strength. Its sedative and diuretic properties are remarkable".

Benign Prostate Hyperplasia

There is much scientific documentation outlining the effectiveness of the herb in treating irritable bladder and urinary problems in men with benign prostate hyperplasia (BPH), an enlargement of the prostate gland. BPH results in a swelling of the prostate gland that obstructs the urethra. This causes painful urination, reduced urine flow, difficulty starting or stopping the flow, dribbling after urination and more frequent nighttime urination. In addition to causing pain and embarrassment, BPH can lead to serious kidney problems if undiagnosed and left untreated. It is a common problem in men over the age of 40. Estimates are that 50-60% of all men will develop BPH in their lifetimes.

Saw palmetto does not reduce prostate enlargement. Instead, it is thought to work in a variety of ways. First, it inhibits the conversion of testosterone into dihydrotestosterone (DHT). BPH is thought to be caused by an increase in testosterone to DHT. Secondly, saw palmetto is believed to interfere with the production of estrogen and progesterone, hormones associated with DHT production.

Clinical trials

Since the 1960s, extensive clinical studies of saw palmetto have been done in Europe. A review of 24 European trials appeared in the November 1998 issue of the Journal of the American Medical Association. The trials involved nearly 3,000 men, some taking saw palmetto, others taking Proscar and a third group taking a placebo.

The men taking saw palmetto had a 28% improvement in urinary tract symptoms, a 24% improvement in peak urine flow and 43% improvement in overall urine flow. The results were nearly comparable to the group taking Proscar and superior to the men taking a placebo.

In a controlled clinical trial with patients with enlarged prostate glands, 50 patients who received saw palmetto (320 mg per day - 4 tablets taken in two separate doses with meals) were compared to 44 patients receiving placebo. Patients treated with saw palmetto urinated less frequently, produced a better flow rate and amount of urine and had less pain and discomfort in urinating than control subjects. title: Horrible Network Security, Mixed Messages about Safety, but works.
text:
GOOD: this collects a weight and syncs that weight to fitbit’s dashboard as I expected. The weight is quick.

BAD: Wi-fi range is poor (despite being 2.4 Ghz [and only 2.4Ghz]). It’s slow to do the BF % measurement. I’ve found the BF measurements to have very low test-retest reliability.

INEXCUSABLE: The setup experience on this scale is horrible and I cannot see any way for a typical consumer to do the setup OR operate the scale in a secure fashion. The UX is just bad project management the security issues are the deal breaker that prompted the rating.

User “mrgunn” in the FitBit forum thread titled “Aria Wifi ERR solution for new routers which support 802.11ac” gave an amusing tongue-in-cheek flavor for what is required to setup this scale up in the least insecure way possible. Before you buy please read “mrgunn’s” post and be sure you are prepared for a 50 step setup adventure.

Even once you are done with “mrgunn” you are worse off: the low-complexity key that this scale requires to connect is no way to operate a network. The biggest problem isn’t the UX, it isn’t even that your best case is less secure, it’s that the path to worse off is so complex that many people won’t get to minimally worse off and will instead operate dramatically less secure networks out of a frustrated desire to have their glossy new scale working and limited understanding of the risk. Someone will be victimized needlessly as a result of this “wide open is all that works”. For me this was a fun weekend project and chance to feel pleased about having RJ45 in the bathroom*. For most people this is an early adoption laserdisc moment. For someone this could be the entry point to a crippling identity theft.

UNTESTED: I don’t need multi-user. I could imagine this being a nice feature feature and a trivial problem (e.x. a highly diamoprhic couple) to solve. I could also imagine it being nearly intractable (say men’s lightweight rowers living together). Given the security and the BF issues I question their ability to execute in the face of complexity.

FYI: I read a bit about this scale before buying it and was surprised to open it and find a big warning label about pacemakers, kids, and pregnancy on the scale. Neither is relevant to me so I assumed I’d just glossed over them. Quick re-read suggest they are hiding in the fine print and Googling yields inconsistent information on fitbit.com. This is poor form. The safety info should be front and center and the evidence / risk should go with it (in this case I’d wager this is a lack of evidence not evidence of harm).

TL;DR – nice “weigh you and save it” function, horrible consumer protection / security practice. Why the extra star? It can be used safely. It’s just a lot of work.

*HOW TO USE: Knowing what I know now setup for this could actually be easy…
- You’ll have to have a dedicated ultra low power 2.4ghz AP for the scale (and only the scale) to connect to. I used an old router running dd-wrt and turned transmit power down until the signal didn’t escape my bathroom. The limit case value here is reduced interference with my real signal but piratically speaking this does really change the physicality of exploitation.
- Granting that “just whisper rarely” isn’t security you’ll have to treat this AP’s back-haul as insecure. For me it was easiest just to put the bathroom network drop’s port (you’ve got gigabit to your toilet right?) on an isolated vlan for the reduced power AP’s back-haul.
- Now that you’ve planned to mitigate the harm of this scale you can setup a burner Linux VM and use it to do the wi-fi dance with your custom lower power minimal security AP in your walk in Faraday cage from a burner VM.
