title: Nice If You Don't Get a Lemon
text: This is a aesthetically pleasing scale and it's great the way you can keep track of your weight on the Fitbit dashboard.  I would give it 2-1/2 stars because all of that is very nice *if* you don't get a lemon (something that would earn four to five stars) but if you get a scale that drains batteries every few weeks, one star is generous.  I have gone through two (or is it three?) scales so far and am so demoralized by it all that I haven't followed up on the tedious process of trying to get it fixed.  There is no one to call; you have to go through a drawn out process of sending emails, answering a lot of questions and then wait for a replacement (and I can't help but wonder, based on my experience, if you're likely to get a scale someone else returned) and then pack your old one up and send it back.  Then, you have to go through a tedious process of setting up the scale which always seems to have a glitch that needs more emails.  My current scale drained the batteries in a little over a month a while back and although I started the emailing process to replace it, I decided I couldn't bear to go through it again just to get another scale that didn't work so I bought new batteries and replaced them.  But, you see, you can't just replace the batteries and expect the scale to work.  It tells me I have to set up a new device, which involves unplugging cables in my computer and going through a whole process which will likely not work anyway until I send an email.  Seriously?  You make a scale that drains the batteries and then don't have a way for the scale to just start working again when the batteries are replaced.  Bottom line:  Fitbit has nice (and actually rather addictive) products but the Aria is a crap shoot (I've heard I am not at all alone in my problems) and their customer service just sucks. Customers of a company this successful should be able to get a customer service person on the phone to resolve problems.

title: Strong fundamentals, poor details
text:
I bought this centrifuge for educational use, so I didn't have overly specific needs in terms of functionality. I think it will fulfill that role reasonably well. The motor is well-powered (although it is a brushed motor, rather than brush-less, so it probably will wear out faster), reasonably quiet, and the operation simple. There are three details which are less than ideal, however: the speed indicator is unreliable, the lid latch isn't well-engineered, and the centrifuge tubes which fit in this machine are not common.

Focusing on the criticism, the analog speed indicator seems to be simply a measure of the resistance of the speed adjustment potentiometer. This would need to be calibrated pretty carefully to be meaningful, but I see no evidence it was. The speed indicator does not even immediately return to zero when the unit is turned off. While it is not important for my use, if I were using this in a clinical or lab setting, I might need to know the speed is constant. This might pose a problem for those uses.

The safety latch is a important feature, but in my centrifuge specifically, it seems to be slightly off of alignment. This makes the lid difficult to open, and a little bit of jiggling is needed.

The most important criticism of this unit for my use is that the centrifuge tubes needed are non-standard. The common 120mm conical tubes are too large for the unit. I think the best fit for the unit are 100mm by 17mm diameter round bottom tubes, which do exist, but in my experience are less common than the longer conical tubes.

On the other hand, for the price, you can hardly go wrong. The motor and balance of the unit are good and it is basically functional.

title: Brutally Slow Shipping, and Quite Small for the price.
text:
I used to be a Head-On user. I used it for tension headaches I would get in my forehead. That product was a combination of homeopathic ingredients and menthol/mint. I don't know which aspect was effective, but it was helpful. I was glad to find a replacement for the product - I've been making due with Bio Freeze or Ben-Gay spray on the back of my neck for neck tension headaches, and the feel is similar.

This product delivers the same cooling effects as Head-On, but the format is different. Head-On was a clear/translucent stick. Not greasy. Not really waxy either. This product comes in a white stick which feels similar to a cocoa butter stick, without feeling greasy. There is a concern about it melting in hot weather, and the instructions included indicate that it might do so (melt) in extreme weather.

That said, this stick is tiny. Fully extended, the full product extends a smidgen over 1/2 (.5) inch and is about 3/4 (.75) inch in diameter. I'm not sure about the value at this price point.

It's also worth noting that it took 30 days to receive, so don't be in a hurry for it.

title: No more holes in sheets and socks from dry hard cracked heels.
text:
Not powerful and stops? No
I’ve seen reviews that say it stops when it’s pushed down to hard, this can be misleading. Several other units I’ve bought over the years are literally just a motor spinning some piece of sandpaper. This one is geared down; meaning that it spins slowly but with more power. If you do press too hard then it will stop; but I haven’t found a reason to press it that hard.

Size: Great
The size is perfect for not only doing your heel, but it’s small size let’s you do the bottom of your foot too.

Adhesive on Sandpaper:
Is strong and great, It hasn’t slipped or felt like it’s going to come off. After sanding both my feet the sandpaper still feels new. Although it white from dead skin it still works like it’s new.

Handle: The handle is small and easy to maneuver it is smooth which gives it a professional feel, but a rubber sleeve over the middle would of given me a better grip. But I’m just being picky it’s fine.

The only thing better but not as convenient is a small wood detailing orbital sander; However being designed for wood it can take too much off if you’re not attentive; So I don’t recommend that.

If your foot is really really bad then get a new rasp type sander and use that to get it under control then use this to keep it soft and normal. I don’t know how this wood work on “concrete hard” heels since I used a new rasp first. Btw: Rasps don’t last forever and eventually get dull; I just threw several away.

Following up with a good Urea type Creme should help maintain you new baby soft feet.

I’m going to buy another one just in case, because I don’t ever want to be without one.

title: Eneloop AA Bulk Pack
text:
These 16 batteries came packed in reusable eight cell holders rather than the throw-away retail pack shown. Additionally a pair of four cell holders were enclosed. The total package included:
16 AA batteries
2 eight cell holders
2 four cell holders
The cell holders are not the fancy ones but are a big improvement over having the cells roll around loose. I tested all the batteries using the break-in function of the MAHA MH-C9000 analyzer and they all exceeded the minimum specified capacity of 1900mah.
For the record, you can use the batteries right out of the package. I used the discharge function of the MAHA MH-C9000 at 100ma to fully drain all the batteries prior running the break-in function. All the batteries had around 1350mah right out of the box which equates to about 70% of the rated minimum capacity. In other words, if you're not obsessed with testing batteries like I am, you can take them right out of the box and use them.
My past experiences with rechargeable batteries were disappointing. They discharged quickly so that whenever I needed a battery I had to plan ahead and charge the batteries the day before I needed to use them. You could forget using them in something like a clock or an emergency flashlight because they would self-discharge to nothing in about three months.
These eneloops have changed all that. They will hold a useful charge for years and can be recharged 1500 times. They make the investment in rechargeable batteries pay off in a big way as well a making it convenient.
This is the rare opportunity to go green and save money without a big hassle.
I would recommend these for low and high drain applications.

title: Simple, Affordable Creatine Powder
text:
One thing a lot of folks don't seem to realize is that you don't need a complicated, expensive product to take advantage of the wonders of Creatine. It's a simple compound, and all you need is that simple compound - you don't need it to be a serum, mixed with a bunch of flavoring, or mixed with various ingredients that will supposedly make it absorb better. Just buy a simple powder and take it with something heavy in fast-acting carbs for an insulin spike (like grape juice) or add it to your protein powder.

Optimum Nutrition excels at giving us simple products at affordable prices without a bunch of glitz and extra junk we don't need, and this is more of the same. Get a big size and this stuff will last you an incredibly long time. I do 2 months on, 1 month off, and I'm halfway through my second phase without being even close to finishing off the 2000g bottle I bought.

But I was confused for a bit because they included instructions that said it was "Stainless Steel".  I'm very happy with it, but the company should be more careful.  I almost returned it.  I use it in the shower, and contrary to what people think, stainless steel rusts in a year or so.  Titanium takes many, many years to show oxidation.  So why does it matter?  Because the titanium version is $25, versus $8 for the stainless.  I got the correct model, but the instructions almost made think I was deceived.

title: Best sound protection ever
text:
I am autistic and have strong sound reactivity. Noisy spaces disorient me and reduce my ability to function. Quietly noisy spaces make it difficult for me to focus on a task.

These "foamies," as we call them in my family, are FANTASTIC. This style of ear plug is the BEST I've used, and while I'd love it if it reduced even more sound, there's only so much sound that can be reduced. They are even better when coupled with hearing protecting ear muffs if you want double protection (like for shooting firearms).

I carry a set of foamies everywhere at all times, and they are lifesavers when I end up in a crowd. I can still hear people talking directly to me, but these kind of foamies dim out MOST of the background noise, and GREATLY extend the amount of time I can stay at, for example, a party. Entirely worth it. I love this big carton so I have plenty on hand.

They are also re-usable, though they do get dirty. It is super important to roll them very thin and insert them all the way into the ear canal so there is over a centimeter of noise blocking in effect. Without using this system, they are FAR less effective, if not entirely ineffective.

I find them quiet comfortable and can wear them for many hours. I do know people who find them uncomfortable to wear for more than a short time. If you're not sure which camp you fall in, it's worthy buying 2-3 pair to give them a test....but make sure to use them properly, and decide if it's a comfort level you can work with.

The women who would receive these napkins rely on a pad that does its job so it's easier to maintain their hygiene during menstruation. I can go home, clean up, and change. title: Like a forcefield against mosquitoes!
text:
After seeing glowing recommendations online and hearing praise from coworkers who are also moms and grandmothers, I went ahead and got the Avon Skin-So-Soft Bug Guard. We were going to the in-laws for a birthday party, it was late summer, and the skeeters out where they are are VICIOUS. I know Zika hasn't really hit our part of the woods yet, but there are plenty of other diseases that mosquitoes are a vector for, and I get super itchy even with normal mosquito bites. I didn't want to find out how our 6 month old baby would react to the bites, either. So I slathered both myself and the baby with the lotion before we set foot outside for the party, and had a great time watching mosquitoes dive-bombing my daughter and bouncing off like a millimeter away as though there was a force field. I don't have the chemistry chops to know how this lotion works, but it does work! The only place I got bit was on my ring finger where--silly me--I hadn't taken off my wedding ring before applying the lotion, so there was a tiny chink in my armor. The baby got off bite-free. My husband, who usually never gets bitten, was getting eaten alive and finally caved and let me put lotion on his arms and neck too, after which the mosquitoes just flew around him.

tl;dr: This stuff smells great, works great, and is gentle enough for even delicate baby skin. Highly recommended!

title: So far so good
text:
I received two different laser hair IPL devices and my sister is trying out one and I'm trying out this one. Overall I will say I really like how easy this one is to use and to hold. I have a pretty good pain tolerance and am doing it on level 2/5. Without the cooling part. It doesn't hurt or pinch or burn me on level 2. I've done it for four weeks and am starting the second phase where you do it every other week instead of once a week.

So far my armpits have shown the most change. I used to shave them every day to every other day and by week three I was shaving maybe 1-2 times per week. I'm really excited about the changes I see there. My lower legs are so so. I almost feel like I need to increase the level to 3 because while the hair is definitely thinner, there is still a bit of it. Overall though I feel like I'm going to be really happy with the legs as well. Finally my bikini line, I'm just doing a 'clean up' not a Brazilian and honestly I haven't noticed a difference in that hair, it's still thick, growing, and hasn't changed at all. I plan on increasing the intensity this week and seeing if that will make a difference (I also plan on still doing the bikini area once a week with a higher intensity to see if that helps). I will update when I've reached the final phase and how it goes, but this is the four-week update, using it once a week.

(if you're interested in hair how often we actually grow hair I'd recommend googling it as it's fascinating and you begin to understand the thirty day hair growth phase and why you have to do so many treatments in office and at home as well as how hair changes the older we get and with our hormones)

title: Confusing brand labeling but they work
text:
I have prescription lenses with a treatment for antifog cloths. The retailer charges $12.95 per cloth and shipping and handling, so I figured I'd give these a try since they're $4.99/6 as of this writing. When I received my order, it was packaged in a small box and each cloth is in a Mingdai brand resealable packet. This isn't what was advertised, but they work so I'm going to keep them. I saw reviews saying these don't work, but they're working for me. The trick is you have to follow the instructions and exhale onto your glasses so there's some moisture. Then wipe the cloth around a bit and the antifog will activate. It's not going to give you 100% antifog, but works well enough when you're transitioning from the cold outside into a grocery store, or similar (i.e. you might get a little fog, but can see well enough to not need to wipe the condensation away).

So while the brand labeling is off, these are performing like the retail brand cloths at a fraction of the price, so I'm happy with my purchase.

title: Quick way to get the benefits of bone broth
text:
I like to make my own bone broth. Needless to say, doing so isn't always feasible, so having bone broth in this easy-to-make, powdered form is a really great product to have on hand for a quick afternoon pick-me-up. In addition, I have friends who drink bone broth while doing intermittent fasting and I think this would probably be very handy to have around for that as well.

If you make your own unsalted stock (or bone broth) then you'll have a pretty good idea of what this tastes like. It's not as beefy as what I make for myself, but I think that's a matter of taste as well as what ratio of powder to water you use. Unfortunately, the product itself gives no indication of what amount of water to use.

So why four stars instead of five?
Unfortunately, there are no guidelines for how much water to use with this powder. I guess it's supposed to be to taste, but it would be nice to have a baseline amount from which to make personal tweaks.
The other reason is the "organic beef type flavor." I'm not sure what "beef type" is and it would be nice to know.
The cost at $3/serving is also a bit steep, but that may be worth the convenience for some.

It is my understanding that the jury is still out regarding the research being done on the benefits of collagen, however, my personal experience tells me that it works, at least for me. The thickness of my hair and nails is better and I believe I see benefits in my skin as well when I am using some form of collagen supplementation. But it works better with consistent use and having it in quick form like this powder is great.

Spray 'n Wash has removed even set-in stains like this, but I really liked the idea of this product's natural ingredients so I wanted to try it. I'm disappointed that it did not work. Perhaps it is more effective on non-oil stains.

title: Works well and is fully controllable
text:
Wanted a TENS unit that could be left in my camping equipment. That meant that it had to use batteries as recharging is not always an option while out camping. This is the perfect fit for that job. Being of advanced years pain from things like hiking and such are the expected norm so one of these is a good addition.

This one is larger than my other TENS units. It is about the size of a regular TV remote and feels about the same in hand. It has the controls on the sides for two channels. There are a number of buttons on the front that allow you to choose between 5 different pre-programed events. Below these are three settings so that you can change between the pre-programed settings and custom set your own. You can also increase or decrease the speeds of each setting by using a rocker switch on the face of the unit. Something that my other two devices do not allow. Intensity is controlled but rotating two knobs/wheels on each side.

Using the device was easy and quite effective. I do, however, feel that the intensity is a bit weak compared to my other devices and the three buttons that let you select the type of pulses really seem to be only two selections. The message and knead modes seem to be the same and there is little difference between them.

Comes with the device, 4 AAA batteries, two leads and 4 pads. The pads are quite sticky, as they should be, but there really should be more included with the device. You are going to need more so order them along with this. You will eventually need to replace the pads on any device, just sooner on this because there are not many included. Also included is a well written and readable manual.

All-in-all it is a battery powered unit and is quite nice for a battery unit.

title: Absolutely wonderful walker
text:
When I ordered this I had no idea what to expect as I have never had a need for one, so had nothing to compare it to. My Father-In-Law needs the help of a walker to get around so decided to give this a try. He has been using one of those walkers with 2 wheels up front and you just drag the back legs. He didn't do a lot of walking with it. Once we gave this to him he has been out and about every day, even in the rain!! The seat is so hndy as he does get tired during his walkabouts. This is so easy for him to use that he has started investigating a lot more of the neighborhood. And... best of all, he is meeting the neighbors and making new friends.

It comes in a tripple boxed state. Yep, 3 sturdy boxes which actuall are heavier than the walker itself. The walker is very light but is strong and very well made. It includes the walker which folds down for transporting in a small space. There is a drink cup which slides right into the supplied bracket. A small cup snaps in place and one can take their cane along while walking. The wheels are large 10 inchers up front with smaller trailing wheels. Tires are rubber and mounted on some snazzy looking wheels. There is a black bag that hangs up front and zips open or closed. It also has a larger bag so that you can fold the walker up and slip it into the bag for traveling. They have thought of everything on this one. We are now calling my Father-In-Law Hot Rod.

Assembly was easy as it was already assembled with the exception of the cup holder, the cane holder and the bag. Everythng was in perfect working order with one exception. The zipper on the hanging bag has 2 zipper heads. One of the zipper head pulls broke off when I tried to zip it shut. I am going to remove the broken one as well as the second and install a small rope type pull that would be easier for some people with hand issues to operate. The maker of this might want to do the same. The pull will hang down about 2 inches and is easier to handle and will be a contrasting colour for easy visibility. I had considered a 4 star rating because of this zipper issue but it is such a sweet walker that I just cannot bring myself to downrating it for the zipper pull. Yes, it is that nice!!

If you are looking for something like this and want the best, you might do yourself a favour and get one of these.. This is going to last for a very long time.

In case you're like me and can't figure out by looking at the photo how these straps could possibly be adjustable, I can assure you they totally are. title: Additional information to the first review
text:
The white residue left behind inside the boiling chamber is not polishing compound, it is mineral scale. If you left it there, you would find that it builds up over time to a rather thick hard coating, which sometimes will chip off.

You may remember Sears used to sell these units for $89-$99, until they went to a new design and then stopped carrying them altogether. Sears also sold a cleaner for these units, which they may still do (although the previous commenter's suggestion about using 9% vinegar plus some table salt sounds like a fine one).

You do not actually have to clean these after every use. In fact, unless you get an unwieldy amount of scale build-up, you don't have to clean them at all; merely rinse the inside before adding more water to start another cycle. If you don't rinse, that can affect the taste of the finished product (we never bothered with the charcoal "after filter"; just threw it away and never replaced it). And if you don't clean, that supposedly will make it a little less efficient, although I've not really found that to be the case.

If I remember correctly--and if this uses the same components--these units take 5-6 hours to distill a full gallon. What makes this design superior (there are several other brands with this same design) is its ease of cleaning. The kind of distiller which uses an internal float mechanism is a bear to clean and I don't recommend them for that reason.

The weak point for this type of distiller, with the thermal cut-off, is the cut-off itself. That will die after a number of cycles and then you will end up throwing the whole unit out. I've been distilling water at home for 25 years and got so tired of this with the Sears units that I figured out where the cut-off was, and how to replace it, and never had to buy a new one after that. I'm not particularly mechanically adept, so that tells you how easy it was to do.

In my opinion, the brush would have been better if it came with a handle, but this is not a big deal. The scissors are quite sharp and work well for hair trimming. The set comes with a storage bag and can be taken on the road when traveling. Overall, this would make a nice useful gift and made my husband happy.

title: No Ability to Charge and Only Comes With USB Cable
text: This sound machine is fairly nice. My husband is a very light sleeper and will turn on a fan every night just for the noise to help him sleep. We always have issues when staying at hotels, as he is unable to bring his large fan with him for a noise maker. Now we have this compact unit that can be easily taken on trips. I like the variety of sounds the machine offers. Some are a bit obnoxious, and I am not sure who would want to sleep to a cuckoo noise or a seagull squawking, but there are plenty of other choices. I also like the option of the night light, as well as the option to either set the timer for the sounds or have the unit on a continuous playback. I think an addition of an alarm clock with LED display would have been a great idea. I do wish the machine would have come with the option of a wall plug versus just a USB cable. I was able to plug the cable that came with the machine into my phone charger plug and it seems to work fine that way. The charging instructions are non-existent, simply because the device has no ability to be charged. No matter how long it stays plugged in, the minute you pull the cable, the power is gone. For this reason, I really think a wall plug would have been a much better option. Overall, not a bad device but has some room for improvement.

title: The Best Elderberry Product I Have Tried So Far
text:
I have been taking elderberry products since the beginning of this Fall season for immune support. This is my first year of trying this based on the recommendation of one of the physicians I know who swears by it and takes it every season. I usually get frequent colds and sinus infections during the colder winter days, however this season I have been staying healthy so far, while everyone around me at work is coughing and sneezing.
I have tried elderberry syrup and capsules in the past. The syrup was too sweet and the capsules were large and at 2 per serving were difficult to swallow. This gummy elderberry product is amazing! It is only one chew per serving and packs the same amount of elderberry as the competitive products, with the addition of vitamin C and Zinc for extra boost. It is so easy to take and does not taste very sweet as was the case with the syrup. The price is also very affordable compared with similar products. I am definitely hooked on this version of elderberry and will be getting more. Great product to have on hand during the COVID times for the once a day supplement. So worth it!

text: I got this mostly for my boyfriend, who does more strenuous outdoor exercising than I do and manages sugar better as well. That, however, was before we both got the stomach bug. When you've been throwing up, and now you're feeling queasy but thirsty, an electrolyte preparation seems to help things settle even better than my go-to tummy beverage, cola. This one tastes pretty good, can be diluted as much as you like, and doesn't seem to have that nasty greeny-yellow fake coloring like many lemon-lime sports drinks. If, like I did, you suddenly decide to mix it into ice water, let it sit a few minutes after the initial stir so the powder can dissolve and it will be fine. That works a lot better than stirring frantically and tossing patience out the window. Another small hint: when you try to poke the scoop back into the canister, go for the handle-first option. The scoop part is a lot more difficult to insert into the powder.

title: Brunos hearing aid review
text: These hearing aids arrived well packaged with an egg-shaped container and charging bay, two manuals, a micro-USB cable and wall plug as well as replacement earpieces and cleaning brushes. The hearing aids took less than one hour to fully charge which is indicated by the orange and green LED lights on the charging/storage container. The hearing aids are small enough to keep their use unnoticeable while still being large enough to handle easily. Being rechargeable, you don't have to mess with small replacement batteries that are difficult to install. The hearing aids work well and are easy to operate which is assisted by the quick instruction booklet provided. These are a little pricy but compared to others that I've tried I would say that these are worth the extra cost. I would recommend these hearing aids.

title: MASS pre-workout supplement
text: I've tried many pre-workout supplements previously. Most of them contain caffeine or large amounts of B12 but this one does not. The container arrived double sealed and has 240 capsules in the container which are gold in color. This provides only 30 servings per container at the recommended serving size which is 8 capsules! The directions state to use 30 minutes prior to your workout and that new users may want to start with only 4 capsules. I'm not a fan of taking pills and having to take 8 capsules prior to my workout isn't appealing by any means. The capsules are average in size but I'd prefer this to be in a powder format instead. You could open up each of the capsules and put them into a shake instead but I have no idea if that would cause any issues. There are a good mix of ingredients in the supplement which does contain some salt and black pepper. The supplement does work for its intended purpose but I had to lower the rating because of the 8 capsule serving size.

title: Alpha Evolve supplement review
text: This supplement arrived in a double sealed container. There are 180 capsules in the container and the suggested serving size is 3 capsules per day which is a 2 month supply at the suggested serving size. The capsules are of average size and there was no strange odor from the container upon opening. This supplement combines several ingredients that aren't typically found together in a single supplement. Those ingredients are DIM and DHEA. The other ingredients are comparable to most competitive products and what you would expect to find in a testosterone supplement. I found the supplement to be well tolerated with no noticeable side effects. I like the combination of ingredients which allows me to take fewer supplements overall but the requirement to take 3 capsules sort of makes up the difference. The price is comparable to other competitive products but you get 2 months instead of 1 month which most of the competitive products provide. Overall I like the ingredient list and I think that this supplement is worth taking.

title: Vitpro supplement review
text: I looked at a lot of supplements prior to this one but the Vitpro supplement seemed to have the best ingredient list and the most reasonable cost. The bottle arrived double sealed and with 180 capsules that are average in size. The suggested serving is 3 capsules which provides 60 servings per container at that level. I had no unwanted side effects from taking this supplement. I would suggest starting with a single capsule and working your way up to the suggested serving size to ensure that it doesn't cause any issues for you. I had a great workout and I believe that the quality ingredients will help with stamina, endurance and energy. I can't say that it affected my libido but I wasn't having any issues in that department previously so I probably wouldn't notice any difference. There are many of these types of supplements that include "proprietary blends" or other unnecessary ingredients and this supplement was one of the few that didn't which I liked. I would definitely recommend this supplement.

title: Pill organizer review
text: Now that I'm older I find that I need to take more supplements and medication than before. I also find that I sometimes forget if I've taken my meds and supplements already, especially when I'm tired. This organizer fixes that problem because it has separate day and night containers for each day of the week. The organizer is easy to use and well made. There was no strange odor upon removing from the packaging and the containers are all clearly marked. The containers are large enough to store a decent amount of pills and since there are separate containers for day and night it should have plenty of room even if you take a large number of pills each day. I would definitely recommend this pill organizer.

title: grip strength exerciser review
text: I already have the metal and far more challenging hand grip strength exerciser but I wanted something that didn't cause as much discomfort for my hands. These D-shaped exercisers seemed like a good alternative. For what they are they work very well. The D-shape fits nicely in the hand and you can comfortably use them for extended periods. They come in three different levels of difficulty (30, 40 and 50 lbs). This isn't nearly as much as the metal ones that I have which start at 100 lbs. but you can use these for a longer period without hurting your hands. These would be good for someone with limited grip strength, rehabilitation or for seniors. They seem to be well made and should last for a long time. I would recommend these for the above mentioned purposes.

title: Pimple popper kit review
text: So this is a gross subject but there are times that you just have to do what you have to do and this kit helps to minimize the damage. The kit arrived well packaged in an included storage tin. The tools were wrapped in a sealed bag and are all well made. They look like a small dental tool kit but they actually work well and are easy to use and clean. For those that suffer from persistent acne these tools help to avoid excess swelling from trying to use you hands. There are a number of different tools included so that you can use the one that is most effective for your condition. I would definitely recommend this kit.

title: Apple Cider Vinegar gummie review
text: I wanted the benefits of apple cider vinegar without the bad taste or smell and these gummies seemed to be a good solution. I'm also not a fan of swallowing pills and having to measure out liquid for each dose also wasn't appealing. These gummies arrived sealed and you get a decent amount in the bottle. There was only a slight odor to the gummies but it wasn't overpowering. The gummies actually taste good with only a very slight bitter taste. They contain a good amount of apple cider vinegar with only a small amount of sugar. I had no digestive issues with these gummies or other side effects. I would definitely recommend this apple cider vinegar supplement.

title: Aggressive Labz Creatine Review
text: This creatine supplement arrived in a double sealed container. I was easily able to find the scoop at the top of the container. With a flavor named "Lion's Blood" I was expecting the taste to either be really bad or be somewhat close to blood orange flavor. I used 24oz of water instead of the 8oz suggested and the taste is actually pretty good. It has a light orange taste (because it is watered down from adding more water). There are no extra unnecessary ingredients and no "proprietary blends" in the powder. There is a higher than average amount of creatine in this powder which is reflected in the additional warnings on the label regarding its use. This supplement is targeted toward the serious athlete or body builder and not the casual gym user. I would recommend this supplement for those that need the additional creatine for their sport but it's probably an excessive amount of creatine for the average person. I would recommend this supplement for its intended audience.

title: Dr.Pedi Tape Review
text: I've used most of the major brands of athletic tape previously and I use athletic tape on a daily basis. This tape is slightly thinner than some of the top brands that I've used previously. The tape did stay on for several days with only one piece that started to roll the edges prior. I had trimmed the corners round to prevent corner rolling but how much the corners roll is really dependent on how much friction the tape gets based on where you place it. I was able to shower without the tape coming off and there was no residue or skin reactions upon removing the tape. With three rolls you get a decent amount for the cost compared to most brands where you get a single roll. The tape has a good amount of elasticity to it but it still manages to provide some support. I would recommend this tape.

title: Massage Tool review
text: This tool arrived well packaged but it is smaller and thinner than it appears in the picture. The tool shape does lend itself to using slight pressure and there are no sharp or unfinished edges on the tool. The tool has a small hole near the top for a lanyard which isn't a bad idea incase it slips out of your hand. If you use too much pressure then it does feel like it is scraping against the skin so it takes some practice to get the hang of it. The tool also came with a small instruction pamphlet. Overall it does work well for its intended purpose.

title: Electrolyte pill review
text: I've taken a number of electrolyte supplements previously. This one comes in a capsule format with 120 capsules in the container which arrived sealed. The suggested serving size is one capsule which contains a good amount of ingredients as well as 200mg of salt per capsule. This compares quite favorably to competitive products in the same form factor. The ingredient list does not contain fillers or unnecessary additives and you get a good amount in the container for the price. I would recommend this electrolyte supplement.

title: Oasser breathalyzer review
text:
This product arrived with a USB cord and re-chargeable battery. The battery looks to be the same size as an AAA battery but AAA batteries won't work as the voltage is different. The battery arrived without a charge and the device took some time to fully charge. Once charged it did work but the instructions aren't that clear. I'm not convinced that the window breaker attachment would work as the device is fairly light and small so it would be difficult to ese effectively. The device won't function when plugged in with the USB cord so it has to be charged. The device will also not function with a low battery so you have to keep it charged. In my non-scientific tests the device will get you in the ball park (once you change the settings to read BAC %). I wouldn't count on the results
that you receive to make a driving decision if you were close to the limit for your state as I doubt that its as accurate as the professional ones. It will give you a general idea of where you are at to make a better decision than just guessing.

title: Mamlyn face mask review
text: These face masks are well made and comfortable. They have pockets for filters and the elastic ear pieces are adjustable. They come with a carrying case as well as a laundry bag to keep the masks from getting lost in the wash. They provide a good amount of coverage and are thick enough to provide a good amount of filtering even without the filter. There was no odor to the masks upon removing from the packaging and they fit well. I would definitely recommend these face masks.

title: Mask Extender review
text: These mask extender pack comes with 6 extenders which is a good value. I found that the best way to use these is to try them on with the different adjustments and determine which one works best. Once you know which one works best you can trim the excess off of each side. Unless you tie each strap around the round part you will have to re-adjust your mask each time you put it on which I didn't like. Other mask extenders have a method to hold the ear loops so that you don't need to re-adjust each time. The extenders are flexible and comfortable to wear. They stay in place while wearing once adjusted properly. Overall I like these extenders but there are a few minor issues to be aware of with this style.

title: Notebook journal review
text: This is a very nice notebook/journal. I use it to track my workouts so that I can see my progress over time. The notebook is hardback with plenty of pages that have a date and page entry areas at the top right corner of each page. The pages are double sided and the lines are spaced far enough apart to allow easy entry and reading. The pages are off-white or light tan which is easy to look at and the notebook comes with an attached ribbon page marker. The size of this notebook is compact which would make carrying or transporting it very convenient and easy. The only thing that I would have liked to see would be stickers or divider tabs which most notebooks come with. Other than that minor issue it's a very nice notebook that is well made and should last for a long time. I would definitely recommend this notebook.

title: It Definitely Helps
text:
I am allergic to dust mites, which are everywhere in almost all homes. They make me sneeze and stuff up my sinuses. A good air purifier can make life a lot more pleasurable because it can remove many if not all of the microscopic little dust-mite body parts that float in the air and end up being inhaled.

Unfortunately, one air purifier is not enough for a house. If you have the same allergy as I do, you might want an air purifier in the bedroom, another in the living room, another in your home office, etc.

This AMEIFU is efficient, if perhaps a bit overpriced, and it works very well in my home office, where I spend a lot of time. I used to go into sneezing jags while sitting there because dust mites feed on human skin cells and dander that everybody sheds. Wherever you spend a lot of time (bed, TV room, office), dust mites will thrive.

I have three different brands of air purifiers in my house, one in each of my most-used rooms, and my sneezing has been significantly eased.

I know of no cure for the dust-mite allergy, but this purifier effectively mitigates the sneezing.

title: Better Design Than Other Brands
text:
I've owned electric toothbrushes from Philips Sonicare, Oral-B, LeBond and now this new HIEIE model. The reason I've had so many is because they do not last forever. Whether it's the dripping of water and toothpaste into the connections of the casing or just plain electronic natural death, they all seem to die. I liked my first Sonicare a lot, it did a great job on my teeth, but it died after about a year. I replaced it with another Sonicare, and then it too passed away. The Oral-B still works, but it runs on an AA battery and doesn't have the cleaning power of Sonicare. The LeBond and Sonicare share a design flaw in that they placed power and mode buttons low on the handle, which means your fingers will accidentally change the mode or speed while using the brush.

This HIEIE model solved that problem by putting the power and mode buttons higher up the handle, so no more unwanted power and mode changes (see my posted photo). I like almost everything about the HIEIE brush ... low price, high-speed brushing, relatively soft bristles, five different brushing modes, it comes with a replacement brush head, and the recharging pad is smaller and easier to use than the one that came with my LeBond brush.

I only have one minor quibble with the HIEIE -- the little instruction manual has perhaps the worst Chinese-to-English translations I've ever seen. It's actually kind of funny. Examples: "Do not pull brushing of your toothbrush to avoid deformation and falling off ... we suggest you brushing your tooth twice a day ... we suggest you changing the head of your toothbrushevery three months."

I got the black HIEIE toothbrush, after always having white models previously. I now wish I had gotten white again. You're trying to have white teeth, and although the brush color doesn't make a whit of difference in functionality, black just seems to send the wrong message to your mouth. I know, it's silly.

If the HIEIE lasts two years or more, it will rank as my favorite electric toothbrush ever.

title: It’s a great little machine!
text: I’m using it as I type this review. I have had it for longer than 2 months now. It still works (yay!) and I would say this is a pretty decent device for the price. A super fancy massage chair would be better, but most of us can’t justify the price! I read a lot of the reviews on many of these portable massagers sold here on Amazon. I lean up against it with all my weight on my couch and just let it dig deep into my lower back and middle back area. It didn’t work for me in my car but I’m fairly short and it was just a weird angle for me. What I can say is that I think eventually the gears inside will wear out and it will need to be replaced. However it’s very affordable so that’s okay with me. If it lasts longer than 6 months I will be very pleased. Longer than that - even better! It is on a timer that I believe lasts 15 minutes. It has heat (you can turn it off also) and it has three speed settings. I think it is great for self-care OR a gift!  If you do what I did and use it for 40 minutes in the same spot letting it get deep into your tissues you will be sore the next day but I got used to it after a few days of use and the soreness subsided. That only happens now if I go a week or so without using it. I highly recommended trying it!

title: I've used better sleep masks
text:
First off, let's get the "100% natural" claim out of the way - unless that's the brand name, it's false. It's got polyester straps and plastic pieces, plus some sort of fill which may or may not be silk. So while the silk may be a "natural" fabric, nothing else about this mask is "natural."

That aside, it's soft and the fabric is smooth. I find the fit to be very tight, even on the loosest setting, but I assume the thin, inexpensive polyester elastic will relax over time. The double straps give more adjustment options if you need that, but I find myself adjusting them to fit on top of one another so they're actually fitting like a single strap. Maybe because that's what I'm used to?

Where it really fails is in light blocking. The cut and style are very basic and old-school, which means plenty of light comes through around the nose. I agree with another reviewer that this is very much like the airline eye masks they hand out for free, with the exception of the silk covering (but the airlines use a very soft polyester, so the feel is the same).

Overall, there's nothing to really recommend here. I'll keep using my Lewis N. Clark eye mask, which is both cheaper and much better at blocking light, while still being extremely comfortable.

title: Just What's Needed To Clean And Prepare For A New CPU Installation....
text: I have always used denatured alcohol to remove excess thermal paste from CPUs and heat sink and I still do when that's all that is available. However, after trying out the thermal cleaner in this kit, I find it does a much better job of getting rid of the left over paste that's left when one swaps out a CPU or changes a heat sink setup. I had an older Prescott Pentium 4 that had dried up compound on it and it was really caked on. I was able to get a good bit of it off with denatured alcohol but there was a residue left so I deiced to try the clean from this kit. I didn't think there was much left on the CPU, but when I cleaned it with the cleaner I was pleasantly surprised to see more paste come off. I have tended to use this cleaner as a "as clean as possible" solution when I want as much old paste off the CPU for a fresh install. And BTW the purifier does help when getting ready to apply fresh paste for the new installation. Well worth the having...

title: My thoughts on the DownBeats vs. Etymotics
text:
Huge improvement over cheap foam ear plugs - if you want to hear more music, step up to the DownBeats.

I also ordered the Etymotic Research ER20 ear plugs at the same time for comparison...so the rest of my comments is a comparison between the two...

To my ears -- the DownBeats and Etymotic ER20s provided equal sound quality at reduced volumes. So for me, the choice comes down to their physical traits:

DownBeats:
Nice rigid hard Blue case
Smaller white Plugs
Harder to remove because they are so small
Less visible when inserted
No neck strap

Etymotic Research ER20:
Soft/small semi-clear plastic case
Larger/colorful plugs
Easy to remove
More visible
Comes with a Cord to connect the plugs

Summary:
Pick the Downbeats if you want to be discrete when wearing ear plugs
Pick the Etymotic if you want larger colorful plugs with a cord (easier to find if they drop)

title: Mixed Feelings
text:
There are good aspects and not so good aspects to this scalp massager. First, the good aspects: The ergonomic shape of this head massager distinguishes it from any others I have used. It fits perfectly into one's hand, and stays comfortably lodged there while in use. The ergonomic design is fantastic, and it is super easy to handle. The soft rubber is pleasant to hold, much nicer than the harder plastic of other massager I have used.

The wide teeth, made out of soft rubber, are excellent for not pulling or harming the hair. I don't think this massager will do damage to the hair, which is always a problem with the more traditional massagers made out of harder plastic with smaller teeth.

The downside of the thick soft rubber teeth is that they don't produce as satisfying a scalp massage as the harder plastic versions. So, this massager essentially involves a trade off - easier to hold and use, safer for hair, but not the penetrating scalp scratching sensation some other types produce. I will keep using it, and may occasionally resort to one of the other types when I really want to scrub my scalp hard.

title: Beneficial, dangerous or ineffective?
text:
One reviewer states fenugreek causes cancer. One medical center does make this general statement regarding in vitro breast cancer cells, however, if you read actual experimental data most studies found it causes cancer cell death, but not in normal cells. This includes prostate, breasf and other cancer cells in vitro and in animal experiments. Of greater concern is that it is the entire seed powder, and not the individual chemical components that provide this benefit. Extracts standardized for certain components were not found to be effective. This product was not tested, so we don’t know if this extract helps or not. What is removed and what remains? It is thought that the fenugreek fiber plays a part. The most common sought after benefit is in blood sugar regulation.

It would be extremely difficult to take enough fenugreek seeds, whole, ground or in capsules, to make a difference. In the past I was never able to choke down enough regular powder to make a difference. Thus the appeal of this 20:1 extract. Due to infections, my A1c will be high regardless of anything I do right now. Perhaps later I would see a benefit. So someone really needs to test this extract. At least it is reasonable in cost per dose.

By the way, do not confuse seed extract with fruit extract, which is used to encourage female lactation.

title: Here's What Worked For Me
text:
This device looks great on paper. My wife saws logs while sleeping and I honestly don't know how she doesn't constantly fall asleep all day long. She tried this Anti Snore Chin Strap, youmotu [Upgraded 2022] Snoring Solution Effective Anti Snore Device. Unfortunately, it didn't work for us.

Even with it tightened down on her head, she still snored constantly. For her, I think it might be a "surgery required" thing like the uvula surgery her dad had done. If you're interested in trying different things to stop snoring, here's what worked for me.

Step 1: I suffered a detached retina 5 years ago and recovery (after surgery) meant I needed to sleep on my back at a 45-degree angle for weeks. Specifically, I stacked 4 queen-size pillows under my head. This may sound uncomfortable, but I've slept like that now for 5 years. Your results may vary, maybe start with 2 or 3 instead of 4.

Step 2 was to start using nasal strips across my nose at night. The additional pillows plus the nasal strips have given me the best sleep I can remember. I get the Clear Passage Large Tan nasal strips here on Amazon. They also make a black extra-strength strip that sticks extremely well. The important thing is to clean your nose well (I use rubbing alcohol), then dry the bridge and sides well (I press a toilet paper square against my skin). When applying the strip, be sure to press the ends against the sides of your nose for 30 seconds to help it stick.

Hopefully, the addition of nasal strips will help you breathe better at night too. In fact, I'm going to suggest to my wife that she try a couple of nights using this anti-snore chin strap combined with my nasal strips and see if that helps her snoring. Maybe that will be the right combination for her.

It is very easy. These are perfect for anyone that sits a lot to keep feet warm, but they are comfortable enough to wear for long periods of time.

My only slight criticism is that I have small feet and wear a size 5 and these slippers in size small are for women sizes 5-81/2. There is a big difference between a size 5 and a size 8. title: Initial impressions
text:
I have herniated discs in my lumbar and sacral regions of my spine, slight herniation in my neck, plus MCLs that give when pressure is exerted. I've done physiotherapy and been exposed to TENS machines there. Then after my Mom had a stroke I got acquainted with EMS machines which are used in her therapy. I've bought various brands of TENS and a Balego EMS. This EMS has a large display unlike the TENS and Balego machines and seems fairly easy to figure out. The other TENS and EMS seem to have better ports for connecting the electrode wires, somehow this seems frail. The electrodes that come with the kit have good adhesion but seem much thinner than the ones that I've bought. The ends where you push in the wires are very thin and frail, they literally seemed to be wrapped with shrink wrap tape which suggests that you have to be very careful pushing in the wires and removing. The other electrodes that I've used are thicker and have plastic ends. I'm using it on my knee and went through all the EMS settings but really never felt anything. I finally settled on program 4 and increased the individual channels using the CH+ buttons to increase to 3 bars which is when I felt some sort of electrical stimulation.

My Mom's physiotherapist examined this and said that it was easy to use and was actually better than the one that they use at the hospital on stroke patients. She says that one is very complicated and not easy to use.

The manual which I skimmed over has a weird setting for knees - all negatives on one knee and all positives on the other knee. Can't figure out how that is supposed to work, and the physio was of the opinion that it wouldn't work. She recommended that I use the electrodes on the sides of the knee or over the top. I'm using it with one set over and under the knee cap and the other on either side of the knee.

The settings for the back seem to skip out a placement in the lumbar region. There is one for hip pain. When I did physiotherapy for my back, the placement of the electrodes for TENS was on either side of the lumbar region, and when the SI joint was involved the placement was by the spine and close to the hip if I recall correctly.

I will update later after more use on knees, back and abdomen.

title: Perfect for taking powdered herbs
text: The Pip Oblate bags do exactly what I need. They are much easier to use than the circles I have used in the past.  They are the perfect solution for taking a supplement whose dose would require too many capsules. Fill the bag no more than 2/3 of the way full.  Fold the top in at the sides and down to form a flap.  Moisten the end of the flap slightly, fold it over to hold the powder in, and seal the flap to the bag.  Be sure take a drink of some liquid before you try to swallow the bag.  It's best if you hold some liquid in the back of your throat so the bag will slip right down.  Then tilt your head back and put the filled bag at the back of your throat.  Swallow (don't breathe in!!!) and quickly take another drink. If the bag gets stuck in your throat and not swallowed, the bag will dissolve and you might inhale some of your medicinal powder.  That's pretty awful, so swallow quickly!  As long as you don't have a strong gag reflex, these are great. I love them.The grape taste is subtle but nice.

title: I've been using the same bottle for over 12 years :-)
text: Ax Wax is the perfect fretboard conditioner. I've been using it for over 12 years (same bottle). Unlike the rest of the instrument, most fretboards are not lacquered; it is exposed wood that requires conditioning. My fretboards are either ebony or rosewood. Periodic conditioning goes a long way to preserve the frets and to clean them from any grime buildup as well as to protect the fretwire from oxidation. Once or twice a year is all my guitars (frets) need. A little ax wax goes a long way. I apply it with a piece of folded paper towel, leave it for about 5 min, then buff it ff microfiber cloth. Regarding using the product on the entire guitar, I would not recommend that as a regular practice. Ax Wax is the "marvel mystery oil" (whatever it is, it is light mineral oil) and contains no wax or silicone. It will not damage a guitar but a regular, non-oil based cleaner would be my 1st choice for a guitar that is well kept and is looked after, however irregularly. I've only used ax wax on the body once and that was to condition an instrument that had tons of buildup and wear and tear and it worked beautifully.

title: The Dirt on... The Dirt
text: After a lot of research, I decided to try this product because it is one of the only toothpastes (well, it's not really a paste at all but you get my point) that doesn't contain sucralose which I am allergic to. Cinnamon, btw, is the only flavor of Dirt that doesn't contain any sweetener at all (the other two contain Stevia extract just FYI). To use it, you wet your toothbrush and dip it into the glass jar and then brush your teeth. It doesn't foam and it turns your teeth brown -- until you rinse. Then your teeth are nice and white and feel smooth. After using it for a week, I decided to brush once with regular toothpaste again to see if I could sense a difference in how my teeth felt. The difference was negligible-- if regular toothpaste is a 10 in that category, The Dirt would be a 9. BUT... I noticed that I had fresher breath for longer after using The Dirt than I did after regular toothpaste. The Dirt never felt overly abrasive and I like the fact that I'm no longer putting a myriad of chemicals in my mouth twice a day. The little glass jar isn't ideal if you're someone who spills stuff a lot (this stuff ain't cheap!). Over time, my teeth may not be as white as before simply because it doesn't contain whitening agents, so we'll see. But overall, it's worth trying. I'm going to continue to use it.

title: Great manual grinder
text:
I am very excited to have this little grinder. I have recently started drinking coffee out of a french press, and that requires grounds more coarse than already ground coffee or that my electric grinder will produce.

I first have to say that this grinder is very pretty! I don't mind having it out on my counter, but I do appreciate the storage bag to make it easy to travel with. (I still have to drink coffee when away from home!) There were no instructions included so I had to study it for a bit to figure it out. I wanted coarse grounds so I adjusted the dial under the top part counterclockwise. The fact that it is a dial lets you get your grounds to the perfect size! It ranges from very fine to very coarse. Everyone should be able to find the right size for whatever they are grinding.

I like that there is a window at the bottom to check your progress. The handle is easy to attach and then you just crank. It took a little more muscle than I was expecting, but it was still very easy to use. It didn't get stuck at all and was very smooth to crank. I poured the grounds right into my french press and had perfect coffee! This was much easier to clean than my electric one, also.

Now that I have used this grinder I can't imagine any reason to go back to my electric one. I received this product at a discount in exchange for an honest review.

title: Impressive, but you might find something better for your situation
text:
This is about the fourth or fifth set of clippers and kits I have tried as an amateur. I have been surprised to learn there can be much variation regarding the reaction of dogs as well as with the actual functioning of clippers you might otherwise assume to be “equal” just by looking at them. I have also read some of the other reviews, and have slight disagreement with some.

If this is the first set of clippers you have ever tried, yes, you will be impressed, especially if your pet is not frightened by them. It is very nice to have the rotating fine-tuning adjustment, as that can be much more important than one might think. If your pet is receptive, you should be happy.

Having said that, there are a few observations I would submit. Other reviewers seem to hail this as relatively “quiet.” I disagree. I’ve seen quieter. And this can make MUCH difference to the pet. It may be “quiet” enough, but I think my dogs are reacting more to the vibration as opposed to the noise level. The vibration here is as strong as I’ve seen.

Another observation is that not much emphasis is placed on the importance of oiling the blades regularly. In VERY SMALL PRINT, the instructions do note that oiling is needed for maintenance. Apparently, some manufacturers assume the user will know this. But some amateurs will think it’s no big deal; but it is a BIG deal. Here, the manufacturer informs that due to delivery restrictions they could not include oil, so you must buy your own. Oiling is CRITICAL to the proper functioning of this.

My limited use of this so far seems to suggest some extra effort may be needed for long-haired dogs with heavy coats, but I allow that may just be something I need to learn more about. Charging has not been a big issue for me. This is nice, but know that what YOU and YOUR PET need and like may be found either by investing in a more elaborate set of clippers OR by even finding out that a lower cost set might provide the ideal situation – including an even more quiet level.

As a separate issue, I will say this to the manufacturers, which applies to MANY products on the market today: PLEASE CONSIDER USING LARGER PRINT FOR INSTRUCTIONS! Older people - and even some younger people struggle with such small print. (I do not deduct for this, but it is tempting!).

title: Long enough to reach all of your back (but not as huge as the picture shows)
text:
You can think of this as a curved oversized model of one of those "safety razors" like people used to use before they came out with cartridge / disposable razors. It's long enough where I can reach to the middle of my lower back using it over-the-shoulder, but to get lower I have to come from the side. But there you'd be able to reach with a standard razor anyway.

It's large, but not quite as huge as that last picture shows. I think they had a midget pose for the photo! It's a good thing it's not as huge as the picture because that would be unwieldy.

Before mine arrived (I hadn't read the description well enough) I was thinking how in the world am I gonna find blades that long? The trick is they use 3 standard blades aligned side-by-side in the shaving head. These are just the standard paper-thin blades that you can buy anywhere for cheap. And no, there's no "seam" between the blades because you overlap them when you install them. It's kinda clever, and works fine since the blades are so thin.

There are plastic protective teeth on the head around the blade so you don't cut yourself. This makes it very safe, but it does mean that you have to hold the razor at a certain angle to your skin or it won't shave properly.

Changing the blades _would_ be very quick and easy, except for the fact that you have to undo 4 rather small screws first. Yeah, it comes with a little screwdriver, but it's really tedious undoing those screws. Maybe they could improve with a tool-less design. I don't think this would be suitable for an elderly individual or anyone else who lacks fine motor skills due to a medical condition. They do give you 2 extra screws because they figure you're gonna lose some. Nice of them, but I'd rather not have to screw with screws anyway.

When it comes time to change the blades, turn them around and use the _other_ side of the blade. So you can use each set of blades twice. It comes with 10 extra blades (in addition to the 3 pre-installed blades). Basically 4 sets of blades which can be flipped around once each.

When I went to change the blades on mine the first time, hidden inside the head and molded into the plastic was a message: "BE CAREFUL CUTTING HAND". Haha that made my day! Apparently there's a Chinese product design guy with a sense of humor who likes to play jokes. I just hope he stays away from my Coca Cola.

The handle can be disassembled so that it fits in the small travel bag they give you. But in order to do that you have to... you guessed it, undo more screws. Fortunately these screws are much larger than the other ones though. Still, no way in heck am I gonna go through all that each time I want to put it away, so I just store it as-is in one big piece.

title: Doesn't burn at all, just like they claim
text:
I had never heard of low melting point candles before, but I'm certainly no stranger to wax play. I didn't know this until just recently, but regular pillar candles normally use some of the hottest melting wax. So I thought being burned was just part of the game! (I still do, in fact.)

But these really do exactly what they say they do: There's no burning sensation at all. Just a little heat, but not uncomfortable in the least. You can drip these all over even the most sensitive areas without any danger of getting burned. Honestly that kind of takes the fun out of it, but I can see where these would have their uses.

Melting point says 50C on the box, which is 122F. Rather cooler than regular candles.

My candles did become flattened/deformed before I opened them. I don't know if that was due to sitting in a hot UPS truck, or maybe I left my bag of toys in the car one day. They weren't flattened too badly though.

I think these are a bit on the overpriced side, for what they are. I mean it's not like there's any special additives in these. If you're serious about wax play, and want the low melt temperature, I'd just pick up some paraffin wax in bulk like they use for canning. You can even buy colorants if you want.

title: Doesn't lose loft and resiliency
text:
I was given one of these pillows about three years ago that had been purchased as a 2-pack from a warehouse store and I liked it so much that I went to the same store and bought an additional 2-pack.

I prefer a firm pillow that provides more loft and support without collapsing, as I tend to sleep on my side. This pillow fills the bill perfectly. It weighs considerably more than a down-filled or polyester fiber-filled pillow, but that isn't an issue. From a thermal standpoint, it feels about the same as down and polyester fiber pillows I've used in the past. All considered, I don't think I'll go back to those earlier technologies.

There are some quirks about this pillow. The fill material doesn't shift as easily as down or feathers would, and with abuse the pillow tends to compact into a lump after a while. This can be corrected with some vigorous shaking and kneading. Conversely, the material doesn't seem to break down and lose loft and resiliency, whereas after a couple of years of use a polyester fiber pillow would have been ready to toss out.

My pillow 2-pack says they were Made in China, even though the description above says they're made in USA. Further, I recently discovered that the inner spun-bonded (non-woven) polyester bag that contained the foam bits was disintegrating and leaking. The filler consisted of random bits of memory foam ranging from off-white to pale blue in color, and appeared to be shredded remnants from mattress manufacturing. I solved the problem by cutting the bag open, dumping the filler contents into a large plastic tub, then stuffing the filler into a new Standard/Queen microfiber pillow protector that I had obtained inexpensively from a local department store. Thus, I managed to recover 99% of the filler. I then put my reconstituted pillow into the original protector. It was an easy fix that cost about $2 and 20 minutes of my time.

title: By far the best deal on Amazon for light output per Dollar 1/6th the cost of a Joovv per watt.
text:
I’ve bought two of these so far. By far the best deal on Amazon for light output per $. The actual energy draw is 98-99 Watts from the wall. The RED LEDS draw about 65Watts and the IR 33 Watts. These LEDS are BRIGHT, efficient and the beam is tightly focused as each light uses 60 Lenses with 120 total LEDS . You could mount two of these from a 8 foot ceiling and each beam would be a about 2 feet by 3.5 feet at beam height so you could make 2 x 7 foot pattern on your bed to lay under with almost no spillover. The beam is very collimated compared to my other RED/IR lights.

These units come with a nice stainless door holder, a rope and pulley and a 4 point stainless steel wire that allows it to be hung vertically from the celling. They do have a very quite fan, they do get nice and warm but not too hot. The only time they would get too hot is if you block the fan opening! The temp is perfect for me as I place these against my skin and they warm you up without getting too hot even after 30 minutes of use. These have digital timers that can be set from 5-30 minutes. The construction is pretty solid. The electronics layout is VERY good.

The only fault I found is the grounding isolation. It works perfectly if you use the Grounded 3 wire plug. If you use two units and don’t have a properly grounded extension cord about 50 volts will flow between the two units and it’s enough to feel it if your touching both units at the same time. The cases of these are grounded so as long as you have a grounded outlet the voltage will be zero.

If you're curious how these stack up to the high end Joovv Red Light Therapy devices. The Joovv mini draws 105Watts from the wall and Costs $895. This one draws 98 Watts and is 1/6th the price. The LEDS are actually lightly brighter than the Joovv mini. I own a integrating photometric sphere and some lux meters that are capable of measuring RED and IR wavelengths. I would say these are the perfect alternatives to the Joovv’s if your on a budget as they are about 6 times cheaper per lumen of light.

title: compare with the Toto and other new technology that is better
text:
I've owned my Toto Washlet Portable Bidet for three years, and used it daily at home and travel. When comparing the Bio Bidet, consider the warranty, the issues with batteries and electrical connections, and the general mechanics of the system inside compared with the Toto. Essentially, and I am sure that Bio Bidet will agree with this - is that the Bio Bidet intended on copying the unique features of the Toto Washlet Portable Bidet, and offer it at a lower cost. title: Great tool for rehab and fitness.
text:
I have been a physical therapist for 17 years and the Bodyblade has been an important part of my practice as well as my fitness program. I remember that I was impressed with the Bodyblade when it came out and I am still just as impressed. I have two Lites and a Classic at home. I came on line today to purchase another for home and more for our new rehab clinic. The Bodyblade was in the top portion of my equipment list for the new clinic. I use it for lots of orthopedic patients but it can be good for neuro patients as well such as paraplegics and more. It is light, portable, fun and effective.

Sure, I do get some people who can't figure out how to make it work but many do figure it out, some faster than others. The people that "get it" are impressed with it's effectiveness and have fun doing it. Some purchase their own for home.

Regarding sizes: The Lite is fantastic for rehab of the shoulder, especially for single-armed exercises. I use them at home for straight armed exercises as well since the straight armed exercises are more challenging. The CXT is great for beginner core strength and for progressing shoulder rehab. I personally think that lots of folks could get by with a CXT for some of the more difficult core exercises. I am a pretty fit guy (but only 155#) and find that I have to decrease the intensity of my oscillations of the Classic quite a bit to last very long on some of the core exercises. That's why I'm purchasing a CXT for home. If a person can get two blades for fitness, I would recommend the CXT and the Classic. I can't imagine how difficult the Pro model must feel. I would recommend that for big, strong college and professional athletes.

The blades are so easy to store and you can take them with you to exercise on vacation or outdoors, etc. They are very durable as well.

The videos are educational and the workouts are good. A person can be so creative with these, so "the sky is the limit" as to what you can do with these.

I still believe that Bruce helped revolutionize rehabilitation and fitness with the invention of the Bodyblade. Thanks, Bruce.

I have an eye disease called Keratoconus and must wear sclera lenses to help support my corneas and allow me to see. Here is my rank for lens solution, based off comfort and value.
1. Purilens
2. Sclerafill
3. Lacripure
4.Addipak
Although good, not quite as good as other brands.
Comfort 7 / 10
Clarity 6 / 10 (protein attacks my lenses sooner with this solution)
Longevity 6 / 10
Dry eye support 5 / 10

Edit: I want to help out my fellow Keratoconus patients, only use UNIQUE PH to clean lenses, don't use Clear Care or anything else as it can strip the coating and hurt your lenses. title: Too expensive for what it is.
text:
This is one of several foot massagers on Amazon that, while they are sold by different manufacturers, are actually identical products.

It has a rolling piece under your foot that massages your sole, and two pads on either side of your foot that squeeze it. It does squeeze pretty hard so it can hurt.

It claims to have 3 modes: auto, custom, and manual. Auto has 4 settings, custom has 3 settings, and manual has speed and directional adjustment buttons. In reality, there is no difference between any of the auto settings or any of the custom settings; they all function exactly the same. If you pick manual, you can adjust between 3 speeds, and the rotational direction of the wheel under your sole.

Based on the weird, broken English in the operational manual, this was probably made in a Chinese on the cheap.

Despite only actually having two settings this works fine, so if you want it you should save your money and by whichever manufacturer is selling it for the cheapest.

title: Waste of money.
text:
First of all, I got a used one. The box had old tape that was already cut open.I am guessing it was returned by someone else because it is incredibly painful to use.

I got this for my daughter who has an inflammatory condition. Foot massages help her with pain. She has small feet, only womens size 6, and right away she said it hurt. She pulled her foot out, and took her socks off, and there were actually red marks where the top massagers were squeezing way to tight. I put my hand in it and that was enough to tell me it was squeezing way to tight.

We checked the ridiculously bad manual, but it was no help. It is so badly translated, it was actually laughable. It gives very little actually operating instructions, and fails to even say how it is best to place your feet. The adjustments are a joke. The description makes it sound as if you have all these options, you don't. You have auto mode, and the other 2 modes just do they same thing. All they do is allow you to pick between the 3 speeds, and change the direction of the bottom massagers. There is no way to adjust how tightly it squeezes your feet, not that we could find anyway.

My daughter did some research on them online and found several videos. We noticed that in all the videos, the amount that the top massagers squeezed was different in all of them, but could find no info on if that is just due to poor manufacturing, or because there is actually some way to adjust it. She tried to find a manufactures website to try and get a better manual, but could only find a Facebook page for Orion Motor Tech, but they specialized in car parts and upgrades, not massagers.

All in all, this is the worst experience I have ever had with anything I have bought off Amazon. It was back in the box and ready to be returned within hours of it being delivered.

I want to add that I am not affiliated with this company, this is not a paid review or anything like that. I am just a person who found out about this water on youtube and researched it out and bought some of it. I have tried other waters in the past few years and truthfully, they did tasted smoother than normal bottled water but I did not really feel different from there use. So whether this Kaqun water is helping me or not...at 4 days you don't know, but I do know that I am more alert not that dragging feeling and I do feel better in 4 days.
