title: An acceptable scale, imporved options for linking to network ...
text:
Review update (Sept 2015) ---
After a frustrating attempt to reconnect my scale several months ago, I had a few minutes the this morning and decide to try again. I thought something might have changed since Windows 10. I loaded the Fitbit app and then downloaded and ran the Fitbit connection utility. Fitbit has added the option not to use a router password so I can reconnect to my Guest network. I realize I may leave my scale open to be hacked but the link up went fine. I am glad that Fitbit has returned the link with no password to allow connection to my guest access point. I moved it up two stars for the ability to link and the nice Win 10 app. Fat measurements on scales seem to be difficult. I prefer the hand held models. The Fitbit scale's fat measurement doesn't seem to be reproducible or has a high standard error. Nevertheless you can get an indication of fat loss if plotted over time.

When I first got the scale the setup did not seem too difficult, but once the scale stopped syncing that was it. I have spent hours try to reconnect the scale and exchanging emails with tech support. This seems to be a company that is going backwards in product quality and design. It maybe that if you have the correct router (not an Apple Airport Extreme) this scale is no problem to link up, but I have not found that to be the case. Compared to the network capabilities of similarly functioning devices this is the worst product I have encountered. My Honeywell thermostat was a breeze to connect and reconnect. Fitbit did not think to design a direct connect with a USB cable to aid in setup, yet another example of poor product design. I recently returned my wrist monitor, after I got my first case of contact dermatitis from contact with the metal of that device.

Even if the scale can't connect, at least I have a scale that measures body fat and weight, right? The scale does not perform either of those functions at a level in line with its price. The % body fat measurement is inconsistent and rarely agrees with a hand held body fat measurement. The weight measurement is also inconsistent and appears to differ from other scales. I have not attempted a calibration weight on it but it is certainly not worth the price I paid for it. I have seen another wifi scale on the market and I think I will give it a try.

title: Good, useful humidor addition
text:
This was a bear to get set up, largely due to a weak wifi signal. Make certain you have a really strong signai where you plan to put your humidor. I was forced to get a Netgear signal booster. Once that problem was solved, setup was fairly straightforward.

Couple of things...you must use a mobile device to set it up. You first have to connect to the module's wifi network (it has the module number--the MAC ID--as a name). Once there you go to an IP number and identify your home network and put in your network password so the device can connect to it. You then RECONNECT TO YOU HOME NETWORK (I missed this, at first), go to the Cigar Oasis wifi site and add you device.

Follow the instructions carefully, make sure you have a good wifi signal where the module is, and you will succeed.

Works great only updates hourly. But a great luxury.

I picked this up after having a particularly bad experience with a foldable bather. Yes, it's hard to dry .... cause it's a stuffed fabric bather! Duh.
I drain the bathtub itself as I'm pulling my daughter out, prop the Hug Tub up against the interior side of the tub to let gravity work, give it 10 to 15 minutes, then shake, squeeze and hang on the shower curtain rod to drip dry onto my 'kneeler' towel. Oh what a hassle .... not.
This product just makes sense. Non-slip bottom, soft and comfy for baby, designed for them to lounge as little ones and then sit up supported as they get bigger and stronger.
Oh and for everyone complaining about how it starts to smell from being wet: there's a great invention called the washing machine. Every few weeks I pop mine in the washer by itself with 2 rinse cycles, and extra spin and poof - good as new.

text: I rarely write reviews. But after eating a helping of this...low carbers have to try this!  I read some reviews of this and other products made by the same company and almost ordered a case.  Common sense prevailed  and I decided to try one package of this and the black bean spagetti since both are low in net carbs. I was going to prepare it one night with low carb tomato sauce and meatballs but was afraid my husband wouldn't care for it as so many soy products have this taste that is hard to forget, so I didn't serve it that night. I saved some sauce so I could try it by myself.  I cooked it in boiling salted water for 7 minutes, strained it and added it to my preheated sauce.  While cooking it smelled like a kitchen when you are frying chicken (something I haven't smelled in a long time) so my mouth was watering.  I plunked the noodles in the sauce and dove in.  I like the taste and the texture wasn't so off either.  The texture is like eating shredded mozerella cheese.  The noodles didn't absorb the sauce but held it well so that you aren't biting into a glob of noodles with no sauce.  No gastric disturbances afterwards. Blood sugar didn't rise although I would like to check was it does when I'm in ketosis. I ate another portion today, just as yummy.  One package has four servings, 17g Carbs minus 11g fiber = 6g net Carbs.  One serving filled me up.  I ate it at lunch and was not hungry until dinner.  A winner for me and I'm ordering a case.

title: Great toothbrush heads but wish they came with a cover.
text:
My husband and I have Philips sonicare toothbrushes and seem to be always in need of replacement toothbrush heads. The problem is that the replacement heads usually come in 3 packs (so there aren’t enough for each of us to replace our brush heads at the same time) and they are really expensive at most retail or online stores. These E-Cron® toothbrush heads got great reviews and came in a set of 4 so we decided to give them a shot.

The first thing I noticed when I received them is that they do not come with toothbrush covers. I guess this isn’t that big of a deal, but I really do prefer to keep my toothbrush from being exposed to all of the germs in a bathroom, not to mention the hairspray and cleaning products that are regularly used around the bathroom countertop. Also, the lack of a cover makes travelling with my toothbrush a little difficult.

The replacement brush heads were easy to install onto my toothbrush handle and fit snugly and securely on the base. The contoured bristles are firm and clean just as well as any of the more expensive brush heads that I have tried in the past. This is our first experience with a mini brush head and although the product description claims that the “small brush head size helps you focus in tight places and maximizes sonic motion,” it will take a little getting used to.

FYI: I received a discount on this product in exchange for my honest review. Overall, they appear to be a good quality brush head and the price is much better than the cost of replacement heads that I have purchased in the past. They would probably have received a 5 star rating from me if they came with a cover.

title: Good workmanship, poor performance
text: I searched for a nice looking eyeglass holder, because I had recently had cataract surgery and was having to put on my reading glasses and then take them off over and over again.  I remember having seen people, (especially it seems, librarians for some reason), using them.  I liked the looks of the Holdies.  Unfortunately after I got them, they did not measure up.  the material was fine, the look was great, however, the attachment mechanism, failed the test.  there is some sort of silcon or other material elastic band that you slip over the earpiece and then stretch it and slide a wire tube up close to the earpiece. when you let it go the wire tube prevents, (or is supposed to prevent the Holdie from sliding off the glasses as they hang around your neck.  Frustrating was my  experience.  As I went about my day, I was continually having to re-attach the end to the earpiece as they would slide off, with the result that a number of times my glasses fell to the floor. I would recommend the attachment be changed, not so it won't come off, (glue would do that with negative results), but so that with normal use the Holdies would keep the glasses where needed.  I don't like giving a bad report, but for me they don't do what I purchased them for.  One more thing I discovered, glasses hanging on your chest make great debris catchers!  When you can't see out of the glasses, it defeats the purpose of having them.

title: 1st new razor in 20 years and I love it
text:
I received this item free through the Amazon Vine program and these are my honest opinions about this product.

I've been using the same Philips Norelco razor for over the last 20 years. It works, but this Kensen razor is so much nicer. My old razor was good for maybe 6-8 shaves before needing to be recharged. Its 20+ years old, so the battery is probably not as strong as it used to be.

I also found that this razor is compatible with my Norelco heads and blades, so finding replacements will be super easy when the time comes. The shaver has a very strong motor and is very quiet. Push button start/stop with a lock feature to prevent accidental startup.

Pros:
- Cordless wet and dry performance (my old razor was not rated for wet use)
- LCD Battery status indicator
- Lock feature to prevent accidental start
- Includes a complete set of extra spare head and blades. It's actually the entire top assembly
- Compatible with Norelco SH90 head/blades

I included a side-by-side comparison of the Kensen heads & blades against the Norelco ones. The Norelco ones have a much more aggressive head design and far more cutting blades. I don't have a ton of facial hair, but do appreciate a tool that can do the job faster. So once the original blades start to feel dull, I will switch over to use the Norelco blades instead.

title: Finally replaced my dull blades.
text:
I received this item free through the Amazon Vine program and these are my honest opinions about this product.

The product description says "blades only" but it does in fact include the heads as well.

I like the addition of the v-grooves in the heads as it makes it more versatile. The extra v-grooves make it easier for the shaver to pick up longer hair, whether you haven't shaved your beard in a couple days or weeks, it makes easier work with these bigger grooves.

Extra cutting blades inside make for quicker shaves. Nothing quite like fresh razor blades for a smooth shave.

It also makes it easy to shave your legs. Yes, I sometimes shave my legs for cycling and this works much better than my original heads without the big v-grooves in the head.

title: Bodybugg is better than both Jawbone and Fitbit
text:
I used a Bodybugg for two years. COMPLETELY satisfied with its accuracy, user interface, functionality for calorie measure, ability to isolate calorie use for specific activities, easy recording of calorie intake (i.e., food). But mostly I TRUST IT to measure my energy output. I validated its results against many different calorie measurement devices.
But for my 2011-2013 Bodybugg experience there was no "app" to connect the Bodybugg to my smartphone. Instead, to capture the Bodybugg data I had to use a USB cable connected to my computer, download the Bodybugg data for the day, recharge the device, then upload the data to an Internet provider app ($7/month) for all of the (excellent) analysis of my daily activity - including sleep patterns.
Then I tried Jawbone's UP3 ($190). It did not work as advertised. The sleep analysis was superb - I miss that and wish all fitness devices had the same functionality as Jawbone's. The "double-tap" feature only worked randomly, it was not "waterproof", and I could not adapt the device to my specific needs. I returned it for a refund - now 6 weeks later have not received that refund.
Then I tried Fitbit Charge HR. I've documented my frustrations with their device on Fitbit's blog for all to read. Briefly, it is so inaccurate that I recommend only the novice to buy this device. Not only that, but the "Fitbit" people decided to send me a new "replacement" device after telling them how dissatisfied I was with their product. I'm selling their replacement device on Craig's list. Can you believe how insane they are!
Worst news I heard lately - Jawbone bought out Bodybugg. Damn - now the best device will be "dumbed-down" to Jawbones inferior device.
For the record: I'm a lifetime fitness enthusiast. Although 73 years old, I still maintain 18% bodyfat, trim physique, 3+ hours active per day, push-to-the-limit interval training, and active in Karate, golf, and softball. I know a lot about fitness. My experience with these three "fitness" measurement devices should be taken seriously if you are "jock" like me.

title: I’m convinced this is a great product!
text:
Honestly, I see where you’re coming from with the toilet paper roll/dryer sheet setup. If it’s working, cool, but this doesn’t just filter the smoke thru a dryer sheet and make it smell like Downey. It literally traps the smoke, the smell, the actual smoke goes into this thing and nothing but clean air comes out. It’s not disguised toxins that your kids and animals still will take in their bodies secondhand. I don’t know about others, but when I’m mislead into thinking something is … say healthy, but it’s really not… I’m not cool with it. I don’t care to be mislead at all, ever really. I can only assume to treat others with the same regard, even if they happen to be naive to the fact. This filter actually keeps the toxins out of the air, hence off your walls and furniture, and away from your loved ones who may not care to inhale smoke by choice. A joint isn’t a great candidate for this thing because it continues to emit smoke, neither is a cigarette. A pipe or a bong is probably what your aim would be here. Idk just have some respect for people and pets. just because you choose to smoke doesn’t mean you need to force feed others your choice smoking habits. It’s toxic and it leaves residue on everything in the room you smoke in. I’m sure smoking once isn’t going to produce much buildup, but maybe you smoke oftentimes somewhere. The residue doesn’t miraculously change once it’s put thru your lungs, it still has toxic properties. Ask your old bong with the nasty buildup, go ahead and scrape off the resin or whatever, and eat it if you think it’s so untoxic. Your cats lick their paws and clean themselves. Your kids put their hands in their mouths and that much won’t change because you smoke. I’d really recommend this filter in particular. I’ve tried other brands of filters but they don’t seem to work nearly as well as this one does for some reason.

That said, The only thing I’ve found it that It’s hard to impose on people to use this sometimes, Ive struggled with that. It’s a little obtrusive. 100% worth it for me, 10% recommended by my guests.

text:
I've had this apparatus for a year now, It's ok. While it does help with keeping good posture, it's uncomfortable mostly on account of the velcro straps that are allowed to attach just about anywhere on the mid or upper shoulders at any off angle. Allowing the material / flexible nylon strap, to dig into the shoulder if not lined up perfectly. But the straps are free to move about left and or right.
**Why not put the straps in fabric channels, three of them. One at the very bottom of the beginning of the hard stitched shoulder pad, another at three and six inches.

And also, why not make the straps that you pull 'up' on to adjust easier to reach and operate?? Especially when putting it on. Perhaps make the end a little bit longer, or even make the end a detachable plastic pull strap. I dislike the action of pulling the strap out of it's single plastic loop on either the left or right shoulder. Why not make the ends with wings, preventing loop pull-outs. Lots of options for improving this product a bit more. All in all a promising pain relieving apparatus.

title: Don't buy this!
text:
**PLEASE be warned when purchasing a Fitbit Aria scale!** It becomes defective and Fitbit refuses to take responsibility.

The company does not stand by their defective scales. If their scale decides to be defective after the 1 year warrantee they do not offer any solutions to the problem. No fix, repair, or replacement. They tell you "Sorry, there is nothing we can do." Please see the photos of the customer service transcription telling me their item IS defective yet there is nothing they will do because it is "outside of the 1 year warrantee".

There is a forum thread in their online community that is 21 pages long of people with this same issue, yet they still refuse to take responsibility for it.

I purchased this scale in 2014 and hardly used it. By hardly used it, I mean that I hardly ever used it. I purchased a Salter scale years before this one that was far more accurate, by the way. The Fitbit Aria was always at least 7-10lbs off and the measurement varied every single time anyone weighed themselves. This left me using the Salter every time I weighed myself, which was every morning for about two years. The only time I used the Aria was when I wanted to log my weight in the app which was maybe bi-monthly for about a year. I ended up getting an Apple watch and no longer used the Fitbit. From that point on the Aria was used maybe a few times a year. The scale had VERY LITTLE USE. I wouldn't be as upset if it had actually taken a beating and/or been a workhorse.

Fast forward to yesterday (June 2018) and I decide to weigh myself on my very expensive Aria so I can keep a visual of my weight because I'm starting a workout program in hopes to 'tighten up' a bit. Well, that's a no-go! I get "measuring">"step off">"thinking">Err" every single time! So naturally I refer to Dr. Google to see if there is something I can fix. I land on Fitbit's 21 page community thread about this exact issue and follow the recommended advice; remove batteries, wait 15 sec, etc - which mind you worked for no one in this thread. It didn't help, still the same "err" message.

I decide to start a live chat, as mentioned above, and I am informed that they won't help me because I'm out of my one year warrantee and they don't offer to repair/fix this defect within their item. So here I am with a $129 dollar decoration piece. Because it's defective it. Because the company refuses to take responsibility for their defective item. Because I was stupid enough to buy it.

One could argue that I could have chosen to use it heavily for the years I owned it so I shouldn't complain. Either way a company should recognize a common defect with their item and at least offer to repair it. And if I pay $129 for a scale I do expect it to LAST and be good QUALITY. I mean sheesh, I paid $39 for the Salter weight/water/body fat scale that has taken a whooping and is still going strong after 7+ years. How could I not expect to spend $129 and get a better longer lasting product?

To recap:
-I purchased a Fitbit Aria scale in 2014
-It was HARDLY used (proof was seen by CS rep in my account)
-In 2019 I'm told by a CS rep my scale is now defective (it did work for 3+ years)
-Fitbit refuses to offer even a fix/repair for it
-I have to throw it out - goody bye $129

Please consider your purchasing options wisely, don't throw your money away like I did. I had to leave this review because if I had know 5 years down the road the scale would become defective I would have never purchased it. I don't think anyone buys a scale to use for just a few years, usually it's for a lifestyle change and will be used for many years to come. Not the Aria, get all your exercise and dieting in within 4-5 years before the defects happen. And make sure you don't decide after 4 years to start a new exercise program and have the Aria log your weight...cuz it will be defective at that point and Fitbit doesn't care.

title: Great DVD about Jewish artists and High Holiday visual art
text:
The Jewish Art Education organization produced a wonderfully informative DVD about visual art that relates to the Jewish High Holidays. Myrna Teck, Ph.D., narrates the DVD, providing information about 60 works of art dating from the 6th century to the present. She describes the print "Creation," 1985, by Judy Chicago, a sculpture "The Prayer," 1943, by Jacques Lipchitz, as well as a stained glass window from the Chicago Loop Synagogue by Abraham Rattner. There is also an ancient, 6th-century mosaic floor depicting the binding of Isaac from Bet Alpha in Israel.

Dr. Teck also includes completely non-objective paintings by artists such as Barnett Newman, including "The Name I," 1949 and explains them so that anyone can understand their meaning. There are images of many different kinds of shofars, and she describes why they are used, as well as why they are so diverse. Paintings depict the use of the shofar, as in "Blowing the Shofar," by folk artist Malcah Zeldis.

The impressive array of images, along with an explanatory narrative, makes this original DVD a great learning experience, and would be a wonderful addition to the High Holiday curriculum for any grade of a religious school or for an adult education class.

title: Shows some promise, needs more experimenting
text:
One day while perusing items for sale on Amazon, as one often does, I happened upon Tesla Purple Plates and thought - hmmm, interesting. But then I discovered some long-standing feud over which company sells the REAL original ones, because there's 2 companies, of course, with "yay this is IT!" and " no this is NOT it! " reviews on both sides - and my brain went into freeze mode.
But Amazon is always kind enough to supply you with any number of alternatives to whatever it is you are looking at, whether or not they're even remotely in the same category. That's how I came upon this tachyon plate. It sounded interesting so I decided to try it out. (And there's no competing sellers claiming the other is a fake)
This tachyon plate isn't really a "plate", per se, as one might think of a plate: dinner plate; electrical plate; license plate. This is 4" square and 1 /8" thick, and has the appearance of thick cardboard or the like, with some type of fibrous -looking coating on one side that has a texture similar to woven grass wallpaper, at least in my estimation. (When I am able to take a photo, I will upload to this review). It does not appear to be metallic, and feels as though it would bend, crease, or even break if attempted. (The above is just my attempt at describing its appearance and has no bearing on its actual composition, of which I have no clue.)
Generally, I am a person who is able to feel energy from things that put out energy, such as crystals, for example. But sometimes I get in a slump (or whatever it is) and can't feel that energy like I usually do. Yep, slump time - can't feel a thing right now. So if this thing's cranking it out, I'm not picking up on it.
So "feeling" an energy emanating from it is not working right now. How about results of said energy? Well, I've had mixed results so far, hence the 4 stars. I've been setting my
1 gallon jugs of water on top of it for at least 15 minutes or more. The water seems to taste fresher, but I'm already starting out with Water Mill RO ultra filtered water rather than trying to improve on the disgusting chloramine-laden tap water that's available here. But still - there seems to be a subtle taste difference.
Next topic: pain relief. I've been experiencing some pain and swelling in both my legs recently. So one night I tucked this tachyon plate under my left leg when I went to bed. The next day, that leg felt better all day. That night, I tried it on the right leg. The next day - no difference at all in my right leg. Tried twice on right leg with same outcome.
I have also been experiencing screamer pain in the sole of my left foot that can come out of the blue when I'm not even standing on it, but that can hurt for hours when I'm on my feet. So I tried resting my left foot on the tachyon plate, painful part on the plate, for about 15 minutes. The pain went away and didn't come back all day. The next time it hurt I did the same, but the pain did not go away. Like I said: mixed results.
I've always been a truly open minded person, willing to give the benefit of the doubt until proven otherwise. And I have some years of experience with various things that are not necessarily main-stream, as I am well aware that there are many many more valuable things out there than can be accounted for in common circumstances. So I'm not done experimenting with this thing yet, might even go so far as to re-read the instruction leaflet, maybe do a web search even. I've only had it since July 15 so I still have time to return it if that's what it comes to. Naturally I'd prefer it if this tachyon plate performed as promised - partly because I really dislike having to drive to the UPS store to return things, but mostly because this pain stuff really sucks and I'm beyond ready to be done with it!
Two more weeks to experiment with this - better get moving...

Even the good toilet tissue will feel like rough-grain sandpaper. At some point you will stop caring if you're actually clean or not, you'll just want to go back to bed, to die in peace. And then you'll remember that you bought this item, pull it out from under the sink, knock the cobwebs off, and use it. And you too will cry in relief. Pro tip: warm water to get you clean, then cool/cold water for relief. You're welcome.

---

Ok, I'm not sure how to write a review about an item that sprays water up your butt, and not be totally gross, but I'm going to try.

First of all, the big question: DOES IT WORK? Answer? Eh... Ish. If you lived through the great toilet tissue shortage of 2020, and you were hoping for an item that would completely replace the need for toilet tissue, you're going to be sorely disappointed. HOWEVER! It does greatly reduce the amount of toilet tissue that you'll need. Also, if you think that one bottle will be enough, you're going to be even more disappointed.

I read a lot of reviews of people complaining about the air-hole at the bottom leaking. Either those people got defective bottles, or they've improved the design, because I don't even put a finger over the hole, and mine has never leaked a single drop of water. I did once accidentally knock the arm (with the sprayer head), back into the bottle, and ended up with water EVERYWHERE... soaked my shirt, the floor, pants, everything. At least it was warm water!

My main issue is that it doesn't spray hard enough to actually get you clean. What I end up doing is use the bidet, then wipe, and repeat about 3 times, until the tissue is clean. I get pretty much the same results from using wet wipes, but at least the bidet is cheaper than wipes and tissue, and doesn't clog the pipes like wipes do.

Because of damaged nerves in my back, the motion of twisting around to wipe is incredibly painful for me, so I appreciate that I don't have to wipe as much. And it's convenient for me to use multiple times, because the sink is right next to me. So it works for what I need. Whether it works for you or not, you'll have to decide. Hope this was helpful. Y'all be blessed.

title: Handy, useful foot soaker
text:
I wanted to be able to soak one or both feet. The fancier, more pedicure-oriented foot spas seemed to take up a lot of space and not perform particularly well from what I read. I tried a dishpan and it was too shallow and the wrong shape; also, it was awkward to fill, carry and empty. My local Japanese dollar store sold this green bucket for about $15, so I got one there. The bottom has little bumps and also a raised section for the arch of the foot. These additions were unremarkable. I'll probably add a layer of little round stones to rub my feet across to get more of a massage action.

The handle is reasonably sturdy. I have US size 8.5 feet and had to fill the bucket a little more than 1/4 full to get a soak that would cover the top of my foot (about 1.5 gallon; the bucket can hold a lot more than that). Using that amount of water, the bucket was quick and easy to fill, carry and empty. It does force foot placement somewhat close together, which could be an issue for some heavier/bigger people. For people in that situation, I would say check out a 5 gallon square Rubbermaid dishpan, which may work better.

I like this bucket for the depth, which is really good for soaking feet and ankles; the handle, which makes it easier to carry and empty; and the fact that it's a dedicated foot bucket which I can keep clean and disinfected.

I weighed myself several times on the scale and got similar (+-5lbs) results each time, until I realized that I was accidentally changing position each time I stepped onto the scale. My other scale wasn't quite as finicky, for whatever reason. I would suggest using some sort of sticker or glass paint to paint "toe spots" on the scale. The lines on the side help, but vertical foot placement is as important as horizontal. I did place the scale on a hard floor, not carpet, so that isn't the reason for the different readings.

If you have a small bathroom like I do, you'll be pleased to know that this scale is thin and lightweight so that you can pick it up and store it elsewhere when not in use.

title: Now this is a great item!
text: It's funny, I hadn't heard anything about red light therapy until about a year ago when I was at a local spa. They encouraged me to try a red light pod machine that they had basically for free. I didn't know anything about it, but after 15 minutes in that space age machine, my chronically painful body felt better, lighter, energized, I don't know...I just felt good. I went back a few more times and actually shed a couple of stubborn pounds that no amount of diet or exercise would help to move. I figured it had to be a fluke. Since those in-spa red light treatments are ridiculously expensive, I didn't continue going, but then decided to try it a couple more times, several months later. The same thing happened, I lost a couple of pounds and felt really relaxed and good after doing it. So, when I saw that there are red light belts and wraps that can be worn at home, I wondered if it is the same basic technology as what they were offering in the spa. I am not completely sure on the science and don't fully understand why this works, but this wrap seems to offer pretty similar benefits to the professional treatment I received. I feel very relaxed and a lot less pain after using this wrap so I am excited to have access to this at home. This belt is so easy to use, just wrap it around your mid-section, your legs or the upper back and chest as well. It feels so relaxing and seems like it might be doing something to get the sluggish lymphatic system to wake up a little bit. I think this would make a fantastic gift for someone because it is so unique and really has a lot to offer in the way of pain relief with the slight possibility of helping someone to lose maybe a pound or two. I know that seems pretty far-fetched, but I don't know, I figure it can't hurt to try if nothing else is working and/or in conjunction with a great diet/exercise regimen, etc...why not give it a try? I think it is working for me and will definitely update if I change my opinion!

title: Incredibly deep tissue massager
text: I suffer from chronic neck pain and have a whole host of pain relief contraptions that I rotate through on the regular. I actually didn't like this initially, at all. It was truly just too painful to try to relax into and felt like it was going to injure me further. I waited a few days to try it again and surprisingly, I changed my mind. This is very far from being a pillow of any sort in the sense that it is hard and painful and doesn't feel supportive at all. It is quite tricky to figure out exactly how to situate yourself on this device and you need to be careful when doing so. This digs deep into the back of the neck, so deep that it is incredibly painful...initially. I wish they had included a little more info about precisely where I was aiming to try to rest on this thing, but eventually, I could just feel that I had it in the right place. Then, I took several deep breaths and kept my knees bent instead of laying completely flat on the floor in case this truly was too much pressure for me, and I felt was this is supposed to do. Wow, super intense, but really gets in there and does induce some good muscle relaxation that I don't get with any of my other contraptions. This won't be a go-to, every day pain relief tool for me, but I am glad to have it in the rotation. I just need to get onto it with caution and ease, but it does serve a good purpose in relaxing my upper cervical region.

title: High quality probiotics
text: I am a huge fan of probiotics and tell everyone I know to try to incorporate them into their daily regimen because they have helped me so much. They say that 70-80% of your immune system is located in your gut so it is crucial to keep your gut biome balanced with the right types and amounts of bacteria at all times. I have been using little probiotic drinks recently that I love, but the problem with those is that they have to be refrigerated. If you are traveling or don't have access to a fridge for a long stretch of time in a day, then of course a capsule is a lot more convenient. I found that these perform just as well as the drink I was taking. They help to appease bloating and really to encourage a stronger sense of energy and well-being in me. I am not sure what specifically is in the formula that is uniquely designed for women, but either which way, the variety and quality of probiotic strains seems to be top-notch. This is a very nice torch lighter. Do not let the price or the negative reveiws turn you away from this great bargain! With three jets you only need a fraction of the time other torches need, trust me for I had to learn that lesson too and since having learned that I rarely have to refill this bad boy!

Complaints have been made that this is "only" a torch lighter and that they sacrificed having a cigar punch, cigar cutter or something else. Listen, this is a torch lighter not a swiss army knife that replaces all of your cigar contraband. If you want a cutter to buy an Xikar, if you want a punch go get one but don't complain that a great torch lighter is nothing more than a lighter!

Long story short: buy this and buy this now for it will be the last torch lighter that you need and will fufill every lighting need you will ever encounter. oh and buy it from amazon since the shipping is free (for now) and cheaper than on the seller's own website!

I had a bit of an unusual purchase experience. With the letter, they included 2 additional free rollers to apologize for the inconvenience, which I appreciated. I patiently waited, and waited, and waited.. And finally after about another month to a month and a half, I finally received the product. So after receiving the product I had already waited nearly 2 months. I know that this was not a typical experience for most buyers and I don't want to judge too harshly because the seller was friendly, apologetic, and offered the free rollers. However I did mention this because it's important to know that this item is shipping from another country and will take a couple of weeks (minimum) to arrive. I just wanted to mention that and now I will continue with my product review:

Pros:
- Comes with 2 "extra coarse" rolling heads, which are very easy to clean and replace
- Comes with a traveling pouch to carry your items in, if desired
- Comfortable design to hold and very easy to use
- Roller is not too harsh on your skin. When rolling over your skin, it feels nice and smooth almost as if you are getting a foot massage.

Cons:
- Slow shipping due to international shipment

I plan to purchase the higher grade coarse roller heads in the future to see if those help.

Though the price was little high for my taste, all in all, I like this device and it is probably one of the best options for removing calluses painlessly and effortlessly. Before purchasing this device, I used a PedEgg for smoothing out my calluses, but decided to buy this before the PedEgg is just awful. The PedEgg blades dull out quickly, it hurt my feet when trying to remove tough callus marks, required a lot of manual effort, and just did an all around worse job than this device does.

title: Independent testing for the naysayers
text:
Having previously owned a different UV Duct lamp in my last house, I know that typically these lamps all produce at least some Ozone. My last unit in particular made quite a bit as the smell of O3 was noticeable every time the AC kicked on. I decided to purchase an O3 meter before installing this particular UV lamp. To test I placed the lamp with one bulb connected in an open box (you need O2 to be circulating in order for O3 to be produced by the UV light). I left the meter running for 10 minutes and as you can see the ozone levels never went passed .02ppm (which I think is just the ambient ozone level, as it remained the same for 10 mins after removing from the box). Be warned that you may not have the same results if you buy replacement bulbs with a different part number. These bulbs are made of doped quartz which blocks the wavelength of light needed to make ozone. If you replace with non-doped bulbs, you WILL make ozone. Lastly pay attention when changing bulbs, do not just pull or slide the bulb from the base. You must press the black elector button on the base to release the bulb. Likewise when installing it you slide it into the socket HORIZONTALLY not vertically (see the last pic, red is slide direction, blue is the eject button).
Final thoughts: this lamp presents the best value for the money on Amazon and seems way better constructed than the 99.00 model I had previously. Will update on longevity when the first change of bulbs happens.

title: Oversensitive Ears? Maybe Not What You Want For Everyday Use.
text:
These earplugs definitely deliver "quiet sound," however I have found them to be much more noise-blocking than sound-reducing. Sometimes conversations come through relatively clearly, but usually music, TV, and movies are so muted that they can't be enjoyed. (This, of course, depends on the external volume. I suspect if you're someplace where it's really really loud, these earplugs will protect your hearing and you'll still be able to stay in the loop.) I've found myself removing one earplug to make sure I'm not missing out— only to find that I often am. I don't want to risk damaging my hearing, so I think I'll be searching for another pair.

I have chronic illness and very sensitive ears, a lot of migraines, and am often overstimulated. I need earplugs that I can wear in restaurants, out shopping, at movie theatres, and even at home when someone else has the TV on too loud for me to handle. I like my earplugs corded because I use them so much and don't want to lose them, especially when out and about.

I was very disappointed that once connected to the included cord, these no longer fit in the case! Please fix this, Quiet Sound. Silicone earplugs will grab lint like nobody's business so they certainly need to be kept in a case. And that also makes sense for reusable earplugs like these. It's pointless if the case isn't usable.

Update: I was in the car with family and they had some music blasting. It was so loud that my ears were quite literally hurting. I am sure that hearing damage was occurring for everyone in that vehicle. I was so happy to have these ear plugs in my purse. I put them in, and for the first time, they didn't block *enough* sound (rather than the "too much" I'd previously experienced). While my head throbbed, I am seriously grateful I had these with me for that unplanned moment. They did, however, hurt my ears to be wearing for such an extended period of time. I had to keep readjusting them to try to stay relatively comfortable. But they did the job of protecting my hearing.

Moral of the story? Invest in multiple ear plugs in various decibel reduction levels if you, like me, have sensitivity to everyday sounds and sometimes are caught in situations where you just can't alter the volume or escape the noise.

text:
Footinsole Massage Heel Liner Gel Pads to Prevent New Shoes Blisters, 2 Pairs - Provides Extra Cushion

I love the idea of these but they miss the mark a bit. Overall they are ok but you have to kind of adjust them. First if your shoes are already tight, they won’t fit. I mean you can put them into your shoes… but then your foot won’t fit. I got these to use inside of normal everyday flats. When I get new shoes (normally flats) they always irritate the back of my foot. (That is probably because they are cheap shoes and aren’t well made… but that’s not the point.) Anyway so you put these into your shoes (that fit or are a bit loose. And they feel great… until you start walking around in them. They start to move around and slide. I realize that there is serious friction going on in the back of your shoe. The pads come right off. You can throw them away or… you can glue and sew them on. (Again I put them in cheap shoes so I didn’t mind the holes). Once they are attached, they are great!

Star Rating: When I do a review I always start out with 5 stars. Then if there is something wrong I will deduct one star and explain why. This way I’m not just arbitrarily picking a number. I gave these liner pads 4 stars. I would give them a 3 but once they are attached, they feel really good. So if you are willing to sew them in (or have them sewn in) they are great. If not… maybe you should pass on these.

title: The Network Issue
text:
I've been using this scale a while now and when it works, its very smooth. No hiccups. Both my wife and I are using it and it is properly uploading our weights and body fat percentage calculations as expected.

However, if you are struggling to get this connected to the internet I can tell you from extensive diagnostics exactly what the problem is.

The Network Issue:

The Aria does not respond to ARP requests on the network. If your DHCP server does not remember the IP-MAC association when it hands out the IP address, this scale will likely not work. From what I can tell, most routers do remember this. However, some routers, such as those by Zyxel, do an ARP request after they serve up the IP address with DHCP. Since the Aria ignores the ARP request, the router will have no idea how to contact the Aria. Thus, you will never get it to work.

The only workaround is to get another router. I had another router lying around and put it on my network. The end result is the Aria is getting a double NAT address. Still, it all works.

Aria technical support was very helpful and worked with me for months trying to diagnose the issue. In the end I figured it out myself. I sent an email to them explaining the issue, but I got the impression nobody exists at Fitbit capable of comprehending this. They probably contracted the software out and have no way to fix it anymore.

title: Good for light to medium tile floor cleaning
text:
Disclaimer: I received this product courtesy of Amazon Vine's review program. This review is my own opinion. Beware: At first, I thought this was a whole floor cleaning system; it is just the soap wafers that you put into your own bucket and use your own mop. This is just a small box of soap wafers. Just wanted you to know, since I was confused by the advertising photos. I thought I was getting a whole mopping system along with these wafers.

Directions: You put a little over a gallon of water in your bucket, depending on how much dirt you need to remove. Drop in a wafer to dissolve about a minute, and then clean your floor.

Info:
-As advertised, the wafers are easy to carry around if you have a lot of areas you need to clean, instead of carrying around bottles of cleaner.
-Wafers means no danger of spilling your floor cleaning soap.
-The cleansing wafers are about the thickness of a few sheets of good paper, and feels almost sponge-like, so they are very lightweight
-Vegan
-Cleans your tile floors sufficiently

Pros:
They are lightweight, thin, and easy to use.
I used one wafer to about 1.3 gallons of water, and it suds up nicely. The suds were still there when I was done.
Since it is not liquid, there are no spills from a bottle container.
-Pleasant and very light scent.

Cons:
-I have really dirty floors. If you plan on doing heavy-duty cleaning, you might need something else.

Recommendations for the company:
I wish these wafers came in a reclosable bag. The bag is open on one end, without a way to close the plastic bag after each use, to make sure to keep the product dry between uses. It may help keep the product more efficient between cleanings.

Overall, I enjoyed using this product. I think it is a brilliant idea to put soap into a sheet, kind of like some of the dryer sheets that we use for drying laundry. I only gave it four stars because it did not really clean the difficult stains. I do recommend it for lighter stains and general tile floor cleaning.

title: Didn't receive what was advertised
text:
This isn't necessarily a review of the product (because I can't really use it), but a review of the supplier.

Firstly, It is supposed to come with a male and female part so that it can connect and make an S shape.

I received two female parts. As someone else had reviewed the product, they got two male parts. I cannot put it together to use as intended.

Secondly, per the information listed on this Amazon item. The product is advertised using the manufacturers information and says "each Backnobber II comes with a 36 page 4 color fully illustrated educational User Guide"

The user manual I received is "the original Backnobber User guide". It is a blue manual that is only about 8 pages, and not the illustrated 36 page booklet as advertised.

First photo is the product advertised with the manual, second photo is of what I received.

I don't think a supplier should advertise what a manufacturer provides with a product, and then the supplier does not provide that which is advertised.

Plus, every time I sprayed bathroom or tile cleaner, she avoided the box until the smell was completely gone (which just isn't nice for an older cat). I sprayed on the Emmy's Best and let it sit for the 15 minutes suggested. Right after the first application, it was like night and day. The stain was gone, the smell was completely gone. title: Excellent for acid reflux
text:
I have acid reflux and cannot tolerate eating acidic foods. I used to eat a lot of yogurt, but these days, I can't even eat Greek yogurt without it hurting my stomach. This supplement provides all those active organisms to be found in yogurt and then some, without irritating my stomach.

One capsule of the supplement contains 13 billion organisms, consisting of L. Rhamnosus, L. Casei, L. Acidophilus, L. Plantarum, L. Bulgaricus, L. Salvarius, Enterococcus Faecium, S. Themophilus, B. Longum, and B. Breve. These organisms are being studied for their possible beneficial effect on diarrhea, lactose intolerance, colon cancer, cholesterol, and blood pressure.

It also contains 300 mg of Fructo-Oliogosaccharides (FOS), which functions as a prebiotic. Prebiotics are what the probiotic organisms eat, so it's supposed to stimulate the growth of all those good organisms in the capsule.

In fact, since I started this supplement, I've stopped taking Prevacid. I definitely would recomment this supplement as "Worth A Try" to anyone with acid reflux. title: Noise machine with quality, bass, and plenty of natural sounds to choose from
text:
[[VIDEOID:ab51364ebfc2968fc1377709022d10ab]] As a doctorate student, I am frequently stressed and thoughts are rushing through my mind while I am trying to go to sleep. When I was younger, I always wanted one of these noise machines that played the 4 sounds of rain, thunder, heart, and waves. This sound machine by Renpho has 15 nature sounds along with fan and white noise sounds. One of the biggest features that drew me to this machine was the nature sounds are non-repeating. The previous sound machine I had, contained only a wave, rain, and thunder sound that had a very short loop. It would actually prevent me from sleeping because I was focusing on the pattern of the sounds. However, I can't find patterns with this noise machine and allows me to clear my head and meditate. Although I purchased this towards the end of my semester, I also used it several times while studying and helped me to relax and focus. I like to have something on in the background while studying or writing a paper. Usually, I'd put the TV on in the background, but would end up distracting me.

It has a variety of noises for everyone including lullabies for younger kids. I occasionally sleep with the light on and the LED allows me to set it at my own ambient comfort level. Just know that it can go super bright if you want it to. The base sounds 9/10 for such a compact device and the sound seems to fill the room which makes it feel quite real. When I close my eyes, it's easy to forget the thunder and rain is coming from the device rather than outside my windows. I always like to test out sounds before I buy something so I figured I'd record 10 seconds of the thunderstorm sound for others to hear. The only con that I have to say for this machine is there is one sound that is unusual and I can't figure out what it is supposed to be. Maybe it's supposed to be the wind or cicadas during the summer time?

title: Spiru-Tein not very spiruteied
text:
I was looking for a powdered Egg Nog drink to wash down fruitcake with. When I came across Spiru-Tein, I thought that is was just Egg Nog drink mix. Normally I don't use any soy protein supplements, because I once read an article about nutrient blockers, and don't trust unfermented soy products. When I opened the container, the scoop was buried in the powder, and I wound up digging it out with a measuring cup. The first time that I used it I put it on top of water with powdered milk, and had a problem mixing. The second time, I put the water on top of the mix and had no problems mixing. As I was looking for a beverage mix (not a protein shake), my opinion might not be very helpful for people evaluating protein shake mixes.

The consistency was less than great. I didn't hate it, but it was disappointing. The flavor was lackluster at best. Mixing was difficult for someone who has to make the product from water with powdered milk. In conclusion, Spiru-Tein is a beverage for when nothing else is available, when Egg Nog is concerned.

title: I Use Daily
text:
Nice presentation/packaging. My cats were ALL OVER this from start to finish, but I generally try to keep them away since some essential oils are proven toxic to pets. Plastic spray bottles, not glass. Ingredients listed and clearly dated for expiration, nice touch. Must shake before use as the solution does separate. I don't know about sellers instructions or any other customers' preferences, but I use Uncrossing to clear first, then Dragons Blood to empower, and lock it with the Fiery Wall. Uncrossing has a sweet, mentholated mint fragrance while Dragons Blood is kind of soapy floral (my husband says dusty bubblegum) and Fiery Wall is masculine, musky sandalwood (hubby's fave.) Layered altogether makes for a light, clean incense fragrance. I presented these as tools onto my ancestral altar and recited certain psalms to activate; I apply these once daily before going out. At first I was a little leery because for the first couple of days suddenly and inexplicably I was fixating on my problems with a vengeance, but that has subsided.

After a year or so I've demoted these to basic air fresheners in my office space and knocked it down a star on the ratings. I'm not convinced they're quality and there are better, more effective products and techniques available.

title: I'm genuinely surprised how well this works!
text:
Not to be negative, but I didn't believe this would work and mostly wanted to serve my curiosity. I've tried whitening treatments in the past and those never worked. Also my dentist has said due to the texture of my teeth, I'd never get much from whitening. My dentist clearly doesn't know about this product! After the first treatment I actually noticed a slight change in the color of my teeth. Multiple uses amplifies this effect. The treatments are easy to apply and stick really well without being uncomfortable. The instructions, which are extremely clear and very helpful, suggest wearing the strips for 30 minutes or up to an hour. I wear them about 40-45 minutes based on what I'm doing around the house. Upon removing them, they come off pretty easily but leave a bit of stickiness that comes off with a gentle rinse or brush. I haven't even had to use the desensitizing brush because I've had zero sensitivity as of yet, which surprises me because I have naturally sensitive teeth. I suspect it's because this is a cruelty-free and natural product with no aggressive ingredients. The powder that is supplied for dipping your toothbrush in for brushing is really wonderful and has a good taste. I use toothpaste and just dunk my brush in the powder. My mouth feels especially clean after brushing with it. And an extra perk: all this comes with a bamboo toothbrush! I love how eco-friendly and ethically-conscious this company is!

I for sure recommend this product. I don't know anyone whose insurance covers professional whitening so that makes this price point more than fair and especially so considering the results.

title: A Cookbook that delights all the senses
text:
This is a beautiful book that wonderfully evokes the mood and beauty of Umbria. This is simple, honest Italian cooking that relies on fresh ingredients and solid technique, which Letizia explains in a manner understandable to cooks and non-cooks alike. The instructions for making fresh pasta are clear, explicit and guarantee success. Competent home chefs will find new techniques to delight in as well as recipes that are traditional but with an added twist that make them worth trying.

The well-written sections on the history of the region are lovely to read, as are the explanations on the processing of olive oil and balsamic vinegar. While I have other Italian cookbooks, I find myself reaching for this one as it promises light, fresh recipes while transporting me to a beautiful place.

All over my sheets!! I thought there was no way it would last until the next day and sure enough it’s day two and my feet feel better than what any $66 dollar pedicure out there could do!! And I spent $7 dollars!! $7!!

So YASSSS this was an amazing investment and now hopefully I can keep them this way! No more breaking bricks like I’m Jackie Chan - woop woop 🙌🏽

The one thing I would say- before you go all crazy on yourself is to put a few days in between you and your new buff daddy.. so that new skin can regenerate! Or you can buff out too many layers making the skin tender (and even feel some what raw). Just a little advice for all the crusty toe jam out there!! FIVE ⭐️ ⭐️ ⭐️ ⭐️ ⭐️

title: Super Sucker!
text:
Works great, but use as directed!

I’m an oily monster with giant pores. It’s sad, but true. I decided to finally try out a face vacuum and see if it did anything for me. It did, it really did! But I have learned I need to follow directions.

The first time I used it, I was a bit skeptical and thinking it might work like those nose peel strips, you know, where it pulls up the gunk so it’s sticking out all over and your nose looks like a hedgehog? Yeah, that. So I casually reviewed the instructions, set them aside, and went to town sucking face.

Real talk, I was going to post some gunk pics, but they were just too funky. But trust me when I say I ended up with about half a pea sized pile of nose goo. It wasn’t pretty, but it was pretty satisfying. Also a bit horrifying- that was in my face?! Gross.

It worked so well that I decided to try it out again the next day. This is where I should have read the directions, which clearly state that you shouldn’t really do that. The vacuum worked, it sucked out some more blackheads, but not nearly as much as before, hallelujah. Buuuuut. My nose felt a little sting afterwards, like it was lightly sunburned. I figured no big deal, it will go away. It did go away, but you know when you get a little sunburned your skin gets rough and then peeely? Yeah, that happened. I got a bit of flaky-nose.

To be clear, this was MY FAULT, I should have followed instructions! So I’m just saying, when you get this, you should follow the instructions, okay? Learn from my mistake. I also gave myself a little accidental face hickey, because I didn’t pay attention when the instructions say to keep moving. Lesson learned, no more flaky nose or face hickeys!

I found the best way to clean the cones is with a qtip to get the gunk, and some rubbing alcohol for an all over wipe down.

This little machine really sucks, no pun intended, and it does a great job. The price is very reasonable, and as of now, there’s a discount you can click on, so it’s even more value for money, woot! I really like this, and I’ve already recommended it to my friend.

Bottom Line - two gunk-free thumbs up, read the directions, recommend buy

I suppose if you only drank one of these when you needed to work out they would be fine as they are a pre workout. I did not.

I decided to give it a go to have some energy to play with my kids and be super dad after I pulled a 10 hour shift.
I got home started eating dinner broke out in a sweat felt so energetic. Classic pre work out symptoms. This is when I realized what I had just done. I was up for 29 more hours. I loved it and hated it. So I immediately order this whole pack. I drank one every morning until they were gone. I quit cold turkey. Had to go buy 3 more from the gas station to feel normal like I did before I even started these drinks. Finally quit the stuff and started falling asleep doing normal every day things. title: Feels great! Only wish for a little more cushioning.
text:
Got these recently to add to my collection, which mostly consists of Zensah Tech+. I've used these a couple of times, and they're an excellent choice for those looking for a lightweight option. They fit comfortably with a perfect amount of compression. The quality of fabric used feels soft and flexible. The lightweight design also makes them more breathable than the Tech+ socks.

My ONLY complaint is that the cushioning is minimal, but that's just the tradeoff for a lightweight pair of compression socks. I've used these a couple times while on a recumbent bike session that lasted for 2 hours, and while the lack of cushioning was somewhat noticeable (compared to the Tech+) they were still plenty comfortable to get through the workout. I just wish there was just a little more cushioning to wear for everyday use.

My recommendation is this: If you prefer a lightweight design for socks, or if you want something lightweight to wear for raceday or workout, go with these. If you want more cushioning for everyday use like I do, go with the Tech+.

title: Wow this stuff is weird!
text:
This is absolutely the strangest stuff I have ever brushed my teeth with. This tooth powder is a very, very fine powder. I usually wet my toothbrush, dip it in the powder, and the put some regular tooth paste on top. Merely using the powder does not create a foam, so it's weird to use it alone. It feels like brushing your teeth with dirt, and it has a very unusual, powerful antiseptic taste. Also, it smells like an old man's breath. It really takes some getting used to, but I tell you what, it gets the job done. My teeth are definitely getting brighter the more I use it, and it does a great job battling the worst morning breath. When I receive this in that mail I had never used tooth powder before, and don't know anyone who has either. I got it just as a little experiment, and for a new experience. The company gives some incredibly vague directions for use. It seriously only says, "use brushing teeth, morning and evening". So, yeah, no help there. In the ingredients list, the ingredient camphor is listed twice. The product comes from Thailand, and the bad Engrish is strong on this label. Reading this label during toilet time is quite entertaining. My husband has been very amused with it on more that one trip.
The product its self is weird, it's weird to use, it tastes weird, and the label weird. It's weird, and it works. I'm having a serious problem getting over the weird though. I don't think I would buy this again, it will be fun to tell friends about though. They can use it at their own discretion. I obtained this product at a discounted rate in exchange for my honest and unbiased review.

title: This is Magic!
text:
Turmeric is all over the headlines. Everywhere you turn, someone is touting the health benefits of turmeric. However, when you research a little more there is very little evidence, actual, scientific evidence, that it does much of anything at all. So when I embarked on my turmeric guest, I was a little skeptical. Could turmeric really ease joint pain, relieve headaches, cure illnesses quicker, etc?

And the answer is... a resounding yes! I didn't start with this brand, but found it to be a great quality, affordable brand. One actually needs to consume quite a bit of turmeric for it to be effective. At least, I did. The recommended dose of 3g is great. Trying to get that in organic capsules would cost quite a bit.

When I began using turmeric I used it only in cooking. Some believe that it could be the heat, fat and other spices used in Indian cooking that creates the greatest health benefits of turmeric (pepper and fat are what activates it, but there is a theory about the cooking too). However, I did not cook with it enough, with a high enough dose, and never really noticed a difference in my health, joint pain, etc.

When I received this large supply of it, I was able to use it properly. That is, in a dose that would actually be effective and handle the issues I was having trouble with, i.e. knee pain, headaches and some rare colds. I cannot say that the turmeric got rid of the pains completely, but it majorly reduced them. As soon as a headache comes on I take a small teaspoon of turmeric and the headache never develops to migraine, which is has many times in the past. After vigorous exercise I take a good amount of it and the next day I do not feel creaky and the pain in my knees has almost completely gone away.

This is one supplement that, if taken correctly, will change your life. I highly recommend it!

title: Newer Doesn't Mean Improved in the 5 oz Pump Version of Ancient Minerals Magnesium Lotion
text:
UPDATE DEC 2019: Ridiculously weak 'pump' system in the new bottles that easily break. Like other reviewers, the last bottle I got has a defect. It was my only bottle and full, and definitely not in my budget to toss out and try another. Fortunately I had not yet tossed my empty bottle that had consistently worked. So I used a thin flat screwdriver to pry off the top and discovered that the 'pump' system is a recipe for breakdowns.

In that test, I got my answer to my earlier review down below why, oh why did they now not let us open up the tops. The reason is we would have discovered there is no 'pump' as we know it and have destroyed the super delicate plastic cone the size of a small crouton that now is part of the 'pump,' which actually is a 2 part process of suctioning, where the suction lifts the bottom by so much, which then pushes out so much lotion.

So there is no straw or pipe as a regular hand lotion, but just a narrow hole where there is this delicate plastic cone loosely fitted into that hole at the bottom, the cone only a delicate lattice of plastic, and the larger end of the cone then sits loosely inside the top part that we depress. With that cone only a weak lattice of delicate plastic, it is easy for something to break or go wrong, but it wasn't ultimately the cone that was my problem, but the internal bottom floor was not perfect, but off. So the suction was null and void.

Wow...give me an old fashioned pipe hand-lotion pump any day, especially at this price of this lotion, for this means taking scissors and transferring the thick lotion to another bottle or jar of any kind. I did try using the old parts of my empty bottle on the new full one, but it worked partially until it stopped, and that is what led me to figure out it is the bottom piece that is hidden by a pry-able cap on the bottom, which is defective. So be warned and have on hand empty jar or bottle which you can transfer the contents to if even shaking does not bring out anything. As I experienced, the top does pop off with a thin flathead screwdriver.

This was my original review:

I'm a praying woman and you can believe that I am praying they will bring back the original 8 oz version of Ancient Minerals Magnesium Lotion after having no recourse but to buy the new smaller 5 oz by said name and company. Well it never makes me happy to have to pay the same for almost half of the product, and this proved no different as I need a certain quantity of the lotion, and not a certain ml per ounce in that I will change the amount I use as if it is a prescription drug of which I only need x-dosage of. I have found the original lotion a God-send working much needed aid for muscles aches, arthristis aches knees, ankles, back etc.

And to cover that area means so much lotion. So here I got almost half the size for same price, and it didn't transform into less usage because they are touting now it carries an extra 7 mg per 1 ml, because it still takes x-amount whatever that is, to treat the areas I need. Plus another very needed ability the old bottle gave has been removed! And that is the ability to unscrew the top and take out to the last dollop as this isn't cheap. Instead they've made it a sealed bottle so you can't get out the last bit, or open it to just get a tiny bit. What this has meant is I find myself going through this smaller bottle at an alarming rate for its cost, and thus using much less in effort to make it last the same time as my budget can't afford replacing this more often that I could before with the 8 oz.

Plus get this, despite what someone else has said here, it is quite a lot thinner than the previous version, which is a negative to me. People new to the product expect a easy thin lotion like a handlotion and so the thickness I could see often would get complaints; but when you realize this is normal, it ends a bonus because it spreads more, reaches more. But now the consistency IS like a thin handlotion and so not only do you have 5 ounces instead of 8, but a thinner lotion about 1/8th the thickness of before, I suppose so it can flow through this pump. I haven't found it to be 'better' working than the 33 mg 8 ounce, and so have found no justification for paying more for less, and having a bottle that no longer opens. What is up with that for all of my handlotion bottles can twist open, so why the move to seal it off---I can only rationalize so a customer is forced to dispense a full amount, and hence go faster through the bottle to the math of 150 pumps. Well, people can just pump in microcosmic presses to get near the same, but even so, I like to open a bottle to get the last amount. I still have bottles 2 years old that came to almost empty I can still get amounts from that are good for little things that have not expired.

At $20+ dollar a bottle, if the product is still potent I want to get the final use of it. Of course one can take scissors to this new plastic bottle, but it will just be more of a mess, and I guarantee with this thinner amount, the option to get months worth or even a year plus won't be there, since there was half there to begin with. I wish Ancient Minerals would produce both versions, so those who want a pump bottle lotion-thin version can have this one, and those of us who want the original thicker larger bottle can stick with that. Maybe that is the company's plan, I hope, but if not, if this has superceded the older 8 ounce, I can't give it 5 stars; I only give 2 because the product still works, but it has been at the price of a lot of valuable removals of the older original lotion that I find a grief.

**UPDATE October 24 2017***
After having gone through 5 of the new pump bottles since my this review, I learned there is no way one can expect to find even a drop of lotion left over once the last pump has been reached. I DID take scissors to the first pump bottle I went through (less than a month lasted) and found it utterly clean inside. I could see that as the pump innards (not technical) pushed the lotion upwards, it has been designed to totally fit the inside so that absolutely NOTHING is left at the last pump. After 5 bottles in a frame of time I would have gone through 1.5 of the old larger size, when you knew the lotion from the larger 8 ounce squeeze bottle, this is a tremendous disappointment and ripoff as each time I haven't been able to make one of these 5-ounce bottles even get to the end of 1 month. As I'm on a fixed income, I can't afford to buy 2 of these $24 bottles per month; I could just swing the larger size as for sure I could at least get 2 months out at the rate I need to use it. Plus, the fact the older bottle wasn't by a pump mechanism like some of those toothpaste pumps that have a floor that climbs up pushing the toothpaste and fills the inside, and instead required one to squeeze the bottle to get some of the thicker lotion out, that combination of the lotion being twice as thick minimally, and it was free of any progressive rising tightly-fitting cylinder, always, always meant I could count on another couple of months of getting use out of the lotion while I also made use of a new 8 ounce, so it was affordable.

Even now I STILL have @ 4 bottles of the old larger one still useful with enough dollops yet on the inside walls that I keep them as reserve so that when I am inbetween a bottle I just finished and waiting for a new one to come in the mail, I have a supply to keep using that hitting the bottle on my fist or using my finger to swipe the inside walls gets me a useful amount.

Having had the larger bottles left me experiencing the painful difference: there is no way around it, when I pick up a brand new smaller 5 oz, it literally feels like half and even less the amount of the older 8 ounce, and it even makes me wonder if there is less than 5 ounces. And, being thinner the new formula, one is indeed getting almost half the same in the 5 ounce of the new compared to the older one, as the older formula was so thick you couldn't pour it out, but had to hit the bottle a little on your palm, or just open the top and dab a little out.

This has left me considering getting the still reasonably priced oil, and testing if first putting hand lotion on my palm, then the amount of ancient minieral oil will result in the same advantage I found with the lotion, in that the lotion never burned my skin, as $48 a month for the right number of the newer bottles does not fit into my budget. The newer formula has its conveniences, but this isn't a product I buy to use like hand lotion to soften my hands or a small area like that as elbows. It is a product I use to aid against muscle aches, prevent cramps at night, on my back, feet, knees, calves and whatever my senior body decides to throw at me. Now if you have never had the use of the 8 ounce, it's like the adage you don't miss what you never knew, and if you only have a small area to cover like knees, or fingers, the smaller size might last you a long time. My own mother uses it just when she has a headache, and at that rate of use and amount it will last her more than a year because she only uses a pea size once a month or less. In this journey the down-sizing and formula thinning started me on, I did give a try to other brands, not all, but of the ones I tried, I haven't found one that has worked as well for me. You know on the old bottle, some complained about the thickness, and some complained that it was hard to get out, but there were others like me who found that a plus because it it wasn't designed to be a hand lotion but more like a medicinal ointment/cream of which we are all used to getting a dab out on our fingers and spreading on what ails us. Maybe that led to Ancient Minerals thinking it would be all love from the people by thinning the formula and making it an easy pump. Well, to a point, IF they had kept the same size 8 ounce or even more 12 ounce to make up for the thinner formula so that save value was there for what actually is $4 to $6 more a bottle for there were times I could get the older formula at $18 a bottle, free deliver. If they decide to make this a larger size pump bottle at a good price for larger size so one bottle would last me the same as the older formula, then my complaint would be over. But since this is the only choice, a down-sized bottle at a rich-person's price to spend a month on lotion, it stays at 2-stars because it is too costly now. Because of the cost I know my mother would benefit from this lotion on her other aches and pains, but I see her refusing to use it except for the smallest rare times as if it is to her like turning to luxury liquid gold and her thriftiness makes her unwilling to use it more, even if it has meant she just suffers the pain. Now then what is the use of such a product change if it results in a price too high for those on a fixed income to bring themselves to use it? Then it becomes another display item on the cupboard shelves much like high priced perfume. I am sure her one bottle will still be there until it expires 2 years from now; at least I use my own, but I feel the monetary pain when each new one ends unpractically before 30 days.

title: Great product & easy set up
text:
I bought this product the day after receiving the Fitbit One as a gift. I'd been eyeing it for quite a while and thought that it was time to give it a shot. I ordered on Friday and it was at my doorstep by Monday afternoon so I was very pleased.

I found the setup to be extremely easy. I took my laptop into the bathroom and logged into my Fitbit account, pulled out the tab on the scale, and clicked "add device". Within a few minutes I was ready to weigh for the first time. I weighed on this scale and then on my old scale and there was a 4/10 lb difference, BUT my old scale only weighs by the 1/2 pound. Since it was so close to the old scale I didn't find the need to step on more than once, so I honestly don't know if it fluctuates much like other reviews have mentioned. I also put it in one spot on the bathroom floor and haven't moved it since.

If anything negative happens with this product, I'll be sure to update my review, but as of now, I love it!

PS - It does not come with a user guide/manual, but the Fitbit website has one. It can be found under this link, https://help.fitbit.com/#product_aria.

Even my husband noticed the difference between this water and the water that comes from our refrigerator and sink filters.  I use this water to fill a carafe for my fridge, give our dogs fresh water, cooking, coffee, tea, ferments, etc.  I refill it just before retiring for the night and it's ready to go the next morning.  We are very happy with the recommendation and our purchase.  Worth every penny!

title: What are you really getting ? Mercury, Lead, Arsenic, Cadmium, Bromium, Chlorine, Fluorine, the list goes on!
text:
Ok so, my father-in-law ordered this stuff in a "Healthy Start Pak" from one of the distributors.(In the kit was a 420g jar of Beyond Tangy Tangerine, Osteo-fx Plus,and Ultimate EFA Plus.) He listens to Alex Jones and when Alex said it was good for you, he wanted to try it. My father in law dropped $160 on this kit, just for me to find out later that day, that it IS NOT GOOD FOR YOU!!

Here's why..

The true source of the ingredients is unknown. The label says Fruit and Vegetable Powder, and Plant Derived Mineral powder. What fruits, vegetables, and plants does it come from? I was reading somewhere on one of the websites that the mineral powder comes from a mine in Utah and that is why there are all of these heavy metals in it. The effect that 'organic heavy metals' (as Youngevity says) has on the human body is unknown. I spend a lot of time researching what we should and shouldn't be doing to ourselves whether it is eating habits, excersice etc. And I have not found any supporting evidence that there are no negative side effects of 'organic heavy metals'. I have 6 mercury fillings and I feel the toxicity of it (physical and mental) so heavy metals are really a concern for me. I also had a two year old daughter who tried this and guzzled a full glass so I am a little uspet about that. Anyways, back to what's in it..

This is the list of the other ingredients: Maltodextrin, citric acid, natural flavor and color, xanthan gum, CitriSweet (inulin, fructose, citrus peel extract), stevia.

Maltodextrin is known to contain MSG. It has been known to cause so many health problems. citric acid's source is unknown, so is natural flavor and color. xanthan gum is a filler in the product and the inulin in the CitriSweet has been known to cause digestive problems. Stevia is so-so, I haven't done much research into it to tell you what the deal is.

I can say off-hand that a lot of the vitamins are synthetic, which means that the body will use very little, if any of each synthetic vitamin.

Some of the amino acids are also from questionable sources. Lysine has been known to be genetically modified and I don't see GMO Free or Non-GMO anywhere on the label.

I would contact the company to express my concerns if I had the time to do it, but my two year old is already eating dinner by herself as I write this in hopes that it can help someone. If anyone needs more information about anything, comment and I will help you as best as possible.

I gave two stars instead of one because you are getting something out of it instead of nothing.

I hope this helps!!

P.S. I recommend using a whole food or superfood supplement if you feel you need it. I use basic organic whole food vitamins in addition to my organic plant based diet and I have no health concerns at all.
