title: Buy it for the can
text:
A generic energy drink with the iconic "Flaming Moe" logo. The cans are, well, cans. The logo is done well, and it's sure to illicit a giggle from any fan of The Simpsons series, especially those who were around during the third season in which the "Flaming Moe's" episode aired. The drink itself is as generic as they come. Tastes sort of like Red Bull, but leans more towards the Monster energy drinks, being sweeter and having flavorings. It certainly doesn't taste bad, but the point of these cans isn't really to drink them, but to have them as collector's items. So, in that respect, I guess it doesn't really matter what they taste like.

Bottom line: if you have the money to spend on a superfluous collector's item and you love The Simpsons and/or have a few friends that are fans, then this is a decent buy.

title: Done getting ripped off by overpriced SAM-e vendors (Edit: You get what you pay for)
text:
Edit: The below was written at the end of the first week of taking the product, shortly after that, the product fell off sharply and started deteriorating. The aroma towards the end of the bottle smells strong of vinegar, which is likely part of a biochemical breakdown of the product and may very well be related to the lack of coating, I think I spoke too soon. What's worse is I attempted to contact the company several times about this and I received no responses, which gives me a bad feeling about continuing to purchase this product or keeping this 5-star review up here. Wanted to share. Overall, the product did work, but I'm not impressed with it like I was in the first week.

Don't listen to the haters regarding this product, it just goes to show how expectation can affect the impact of taking something.

This supplement is on-par, if not slightly better, than all of the other brands I have tried.

The fact that it's not "enteric coated" or in individual blister packs has zero bearing on the product quality, there is absolutely no science behind that and it just became the trend once one company started doing it and getting all braggadocio about how that made the product better. It doesn't.

Put it this way, for any brand buffs out there, go look at Douglas or Pure Encapsulations, yes they are acid-resistant capsules, but they are still capsules. You don't need blister packs or tablets for SAM-e to be effective.

This company is no bull, this product works, I don't write a lot of reviews but after reading some of the stuff on here I felt it was the right thing to do, don't get ripped off paying 300% more for the same thing!

title: Good for DRY eyes
text: I got contacts about a couple months back and my boyfriend had insisted to get the big bottles of these because he had a condition that was related to dry eyes. This solution really helps to clean out the gunk and extra protein that builds up for your contacts. I guess for my boyfriend, it was because the extra protein would rub against the little bumps behind his eyelids (again from the dry eye condition). For me, I actually felt the wonders of it after I tried it. I was wondering what all the hype was about, but it really does a deep cleaning of your contacts and make it feel new again. However, I would advise to ALWAYS ALWAYS use the container that they give you. I read on reddit that a girl burned her eyes from using the regular  contacts container. This is because the titanium in the container that they give you reacts with the solution. After 6 hours or so, or whatever the solution container advises, the solution becomes docile and pretty much is like water to you, making it safe for you to put your contacts in.

title: Pretty stationery set, but the envelopes are weird
text:
This stationery sets comes nicely packaged in a sturdy cardboard box with an attached lid. Included are a package of folded note cards in an attractive abstract graphic, a package of square one-page note papers (the bottom of the box calls these "message sheets" -- they are smaller than the notecards -- ivory in color and sized about three-and-one-half inches square) -- and a package of envelopes. There is also a silver-colored retractable ink pen which writes in black ink. The quality of the paper is a little above average, but not heavyweight. For the money, it's not a bad set.

What I did not like about the set is the design of the envelopes. The envelopes are plain ivory, sized to fit the notecards. But they are not like a regular envelope where you insert the notecard at the top of the envelope. These envelopes are "end-loaders". They remind me of the little envelopes you get from the bank when you ask for cash back at the drive-in. I think they are weird, and for me the unusual design of the envelope spoiled the function to which I was going to put these note cards. I don't want to give my friend a thank you note for inviting me to her nice dinner party and have her think I'm handing her a pay envelope.

These are going to Goodwill, minus the pen. I'm keeping that.

title: Hoping this scale gets better with use
text:
I have had the Mosiso scale a bit over a week now. For the past 15 or 20 years, I have been using an electronic scale I was given for a gift and it was purchased through "Sharper Image" and had their name on the thick glass covering the scale. That scale was one that had to be tapped to start and wait for the numerals to read "00" before getting on. My presumption was the scale was accurate. But, every time I went to the doctor's office, and weighing in seems to be an obsession for the doctor's nurses, I'd wear the thinnest and lightest clothes I own and still come up over 6 pounds heavier than I weighed at home. The difference in weight was fluffed off as different scales come up with different readings. One doctor has the old weight balance type scale and I could easily see the weight was balanced at "0" pounds. Another has a fancier standing electronic scale.

As the difference between scales increased, I began to suspect that maybe my Sharper Image scale wasn't accurate. That led to my looking at a number of different scales on Amazon.com and thinking maybe the sensors in my scale or whatever mechanism in that scale that measures weight were failing. The last doctor visit I had I ended up weighing over 4 pounds more than I weighed at home and I knew my clothing didn't weigh 4 pounds. It was much less. So, I researched the scales from Amazon and thought Mosiso would be more accurate than the others. What I found out in using it is the doctor's scale was close to correct. There was nearly 4 pound difference in weight between the Sharper Image scale and the Mosiso scale.

I am also finding there may be some variability in weight based on floor surfaces. Each floor is level, but on a composite floor that looks like ceramic tile and one that is hard, flat ceramic tile, my weight can vary up to 2 pounds on the Mosiso. I'm also finding that the initial 4 pound differential between the Sharper Image scale and Mosiso has become anywhere between 1.4 and 2.8 pounds and can't account for the difference. At my heaviest, I was 330 pounds and carried it well. Losing weight over the past 10 years and keeping it off, I am somewhere between 262 and 266 pounds.

I do like the Mosiso scale's looks and like the final weight flashing on the scale. I usually weigh myself 3 times and by just tapping the back edge of the scale, it resets to "00" pounds. I then consider my weight to be whatever 2 of the 3 readings match. I guess the only way to get the most accurate weight on myself is to own a scale exactly like those in doctor's offices. However, I do get closer to an accurate measure on the Mosiso scale and the price certainly can't be beat. I'm hoping that as the scale gets more accustomed to being used, perhaps the readings will become more consistent or accurate.

If you know a proper diet for building mass coupled with the right lifting regiment (there are several for different effects) you will get the results you are looking for. All in all, the only miracle muscle builder is anabolic steroids which we all know are illegal and dangerous. I have personally looked through dozens of so called mass builder supliments and I have come to 1 conclusion, they are all junk. If you want a nice physique you have to learn what foods add more mass, ie proteins, carbs for energy, amino acids, etc. and research the right lifting for what you wish to accomplish. Hint, professional power lifters and body builders use max weight with low reps and overload their muscle groups with several days rebuild time in between workouts. I have lifted since I was 15 (35 now) and I found to get more mass max out to muscle failure then rest 2 days in between your sessions, some recommend more but this worked for me.

title: First ever fun scale
text:
My first impression of this scale is that it weighed me at one pound lighter than my old scale, so how can I not love it?

For the past several years, I would weigh myself several times per week, and then once in a while I would follow through and update my weight in my various fitness tools (e.g., Fitbit, Garmin Connect, Nike+, etc.).

This scale makes it so easy. You just step on, and everything is magically updated. There's even a third party tool (free) that will sync your weight from Fitbit to Garmin Connect.

If you don't like the price tag, don't forget that the scale also measures your body fat, and it similarly sends this data to the Fitbit web site.

The display has a nice backlight and is easy to read. It makes weighing yourself fun, and it adds a little extra motivation to keep yourself accountable for your weight every day.

I am very happy I got this scale to supplement my Fitbit Force and Garmin Forerunner 610.

title: Good Profile, Too Many Pills in a Serving
text: The [[ASIN:B00THEPUCI Athletic Greens - Pure Branch Chain Amino Acids (BCAA) - 390 Capsules (312 grams)]] have a good profile, but way too many pills. It states to take two servings a day; however, one serving is sixteen (16) pills! I got this product for my husband who uses BCAA products all the time because he is a bodybuilder. BCAAs are important to have included in your supplement regimen. The profile of these BCAAs are good, it is just too bad you have to take so many pills to get the benefit of them. My husband hates taking so many pills, but was doing so to get the benefits of the BCAAs. It would take him several minutes to consume the pills because you can't just take sixteen pills all at once. You have to do a few at a time. So the daily serving amount is a total of thirty-two (32) pills! That is a lot of pills to take with just one supplement. Not to mention taking a multivitamin and other supplements as well. If this supplement profile was in a smaller number of pills, my review would be a higher rating, but I do not know anyone who would want to take so many pills at once. I received a discount on these BCAA pills in exchange for my honest and unbiased review.

I was pumping 2-4 ounces per breast every two hours for the remainder of my time at the hospital, and the nipple shield on the Isis did not further inflame the scabs I had from the electric pump. title: First day impression and details and manual
text:
Hi just received my order of style 1 chair, the black “space tub egg escape pod” bestmassage chair.
Seems a day or two after ordering I got a text with a phone number to call and they found a date I’d be home and gave me like a 2 hour delivery window.
The chair sat on 2 wood strips in a bag and padding inside a heavy cardboard box.
It chair looks just like the amazon ad even though I believe the model number is a bit different, the manual is correct.
The imitation leather textured vinyl looks better than in the ad I think because I wasn't sure it was upholstered on the sides and it is there too.
The chair is solid, nothing feels of flimsy cardboard at all but I don't let anyone sit on the arms or abuse it.
I’m glad it’s not high maintenance real expensive leather.
I’ve uploaded the main pages of the manual for your viewing, the simple assembly info is in the last pages.
I believe others have said the side arms can be easily removed if needed although the manual does not say this and I just barely got it through the door sideways out of the box with 3 people without having to remove anything. We did risk damaging the upholstery because it was pretty tight, so I'd advise to remove the arms if you can if it's pretty tight don't force it.
It looks just like the picture and I’ll try to give an update after some time.
I have a kill a watt meter and it shows the stand by watts used is 1.7 which isn’t bad although i have read ideal is under 1 watt. In use it consumes around 50 watts with heat selected as well although the manual says 100 watts so any outlet can power this chair.

It has a small outlet 24v transformer so the chair electric system can’t shock a user as our skin can resist that low so that is safe too.
The Bluetooth speakers on each outside are satisfactory and very basic simple with no control on the chair or wire or jack to attach to, you just find it in your phone’s search and it pairs. My phone volume turned all the way up can fill the room alright with music, this could perhaps really serve someone in a small room so they don't need a stereo system for their music needs.
All you have to have is the chair plugged in.
It fills the room with the sound of a small stereo with some alright base even and no distortion to say.
It’s odd the speakers face outside instead of inside the chair but it works and can double as music for the room anytime desired seems to be the concept.
I can't say the bluetooth connection will work all the time you get in the chair because I don't use the speakers much and I did have an occasion where I had to turn the main power stitch off at the back and back on to get the bluetooth to connect to my phone so I haven't played around with it to learn it's ins and outs.
The build in left panel controls on the chair are basic and display the run time up to 30 min and also A1 through A6 when the auto button is pressed. The manual says to not run it more than 30 min continuously, then you just need to give it 15 min off to let the motors cool/rest is what it says. So if you get it, don't let too many people line up and try it out without a rest.

The right side wired remote control is large and much more elaborate and includes a colorful detailed digital display and options like being able to raise or lower the legs unit by themselves to about 45 degrees, this is done by an airbag between the leg unit and chair.
In fact you can move the leg unit and or the chair back without turning on the chair massage functions.
Also when the chair is off, it can be sat in a bit like a regular chair because the rollers part at the top under the flip in place when desired head pad.
Although you may want more padding if sitting for a while stationary just add a lounge chair pad etc
Although your legs movement is a bit restricted as well as your body might make long sits odd.
The leg foot rest can not be slid out of the way although I suppose you could completely remove or leave it off and plug the air lines if you wanted to....but then you should perhaps buy a lessor chair.

The control buttons are not illuminated, it would be nice if they were but just a minor complaint when using in a dark room and very sensitive to touch as if they were a touch pad and there is always a beep sound when a button is pressed unless the button is not effective for that auto program mode you may be enjoying as some buttons only pertain to manual mode.
Assembly was easy, the foot rest attachment pins now have pull spring instead of the removable clip some complained about figuring out.
There is a plug and 2 air line tubes to plug together under the leg foot rest.
Everything is shipped in one large box.
The chair can recline just a bit more than zero gravity or you can leave it up while enjoying the massages.
There are Velcro and also zippers for some of the pieces which is nice in that you can get access to and also add more foam if you ever so desired like in the head pad or under the main back seat panel.
The main back seat area has a Velcro pad and under that is a zippered fabric panel and under that is a center hammock like strap that serves as support, you can see the 3 motors and 4 rollers exposed at this point and looks reasonably simple and roomy inside where the tract runs the rollers.
So far this is a great chair for $800 and it’s very obvious that the chairs selling for many many thousands of dollars are well over priced for rich cats to throw their money at it seems other companies have really cornered the market and are stubborn on the price.

I’ve read reviews on very expensive chairs and the reliability and satisfaction is no better than the reviews for this chair is what I got out of all the reading from others.
Yes the 6000 dollar chair may have a better warranty but when the warranty is over how much are they going to want for parts when they charge so much for the chair to begin with?
This chair is the real deal I’d say not for frail people it’s not a stationary vibrating motors points similar priced chairs that look kind of like this one, no this one does actually have the S track that the rollers move on up and down your body as they do the different options and it really is nice that it goes down past your ass is a real pleasure.
Vibrating chair pads can be very nice and all some people want and that is great but this is more deep and pressing for those that want that.
If you don't want the legs massage, I did see, I believe this same company, makes a like gaming chair that has the shiatsu S track but no legs but it might not fit large people but it is even less in price.

The foot roller is strong but you can move your feet so that it’s not on the sensitive area or put heavy socks on.
The extend stretch setting is very interesting as it grabs your legs and with the air bags and then draws the legs down while moving the body up, I like this setting for new users to surprise them LOL.

Update after a 3 months:
We still like it and it does impress adult friends who enjoy sitting in it and you can chat with them as they enjoy it.
I am surprised that none of these rollers on a track chair companies, even the super expensive ones, seem to install the stationary vibrating motors from those inexpensive massage throw on a regular chair pads that are sold in common local stores to go with the shiatsu moving track so that we would get the massage rollers with it's actions and the little cheap stationary motors vibrating could really up the game and the happy sighs and moaning of the user whole body at once LOL. Perhaps I will try putting the affordable vibrating pad on top of the massage chair and sitting in them and turning them both on and see! LOL
It's important to destress our bodies and treat our body to give it the space and time it needs to rejuvenate and unfortunately we aren't yet taught how to quiet our obsessive internal thinking that is causing a lot of our stress to begin with in our daily lives, massage devices of whatever type you buy might help and there's so few pleasures in the adult world so why not.

Well I feel empty of anything else to say, that’s it for now.
Take care of yourself!
Xo

title: We love them! But modified how we use them due to previous reviews!
text:
We bought these for our 5 1/2 yr old severaly non-verbal autistic son while potty training this past month. I agree with previous reviewers that these are definitely smaller & thinner (will tear easy) than the pampers sensative throw away wipes. We have never used the prior version Kandoo sensative flushable wipes so we can't compare the new version with the old. I do believe the reason for making them smaller/thinner is so it will not clog your toilet..I am guessing maybe the previous version did so they had to make this change. Makes sense to me.

We still need these wipes for him since his bottom is so very sensative & like the idea of flushing them after use. So how we work around the issues of these wipes is by getting a wad of toiler paper if you will then putting 1 sheet of the flushable wipe on top of it so it helps with a messy clean up without tearing or having to use the entire pack. We do this each time as we are wiping his bottom (get wad of toilet paper with 1 sheet of flushable wipe on top). This has worked extremely well for us! We love the idea of no longer having to carry around sensative throw away wipes & disposable diaper throw away bags to contain the odor. And we do not have to go through a lot of the actual flushable wipes since we use it along with a wad of toilet paper.

Hope this helps!

title: Not A Fan
text:
I ordered a multi pack of this product a while ago and I’m still trying to find a way to use them......because their intended purpose of wipes for potty training is useless. I realize some reviewers were very pleased with theirs. But my from experience, I found the following things to be true : 1) each wipe is very small. 2) the individual wipes rip as they are pulled out of the package. 3) it is often difficult to pull out just one wipe as multiple come out even tho you’ve grabbed only the top one in the container. Remember, they frequently rip as you pull them out so now you have multiple torn pieces. 4) They really aren’t that moist and if you aren’t going to finish the package soon, by the time you get towards the bottom of the container, the product feels very dried out.

Now imagine them being used as potty training wipes. You have small, not so agile fingers trying to remove a wipe. The wipe is small, one or more come out in shreds as they pull on it, little pieces fall from tiny hands. By the time they are actually going to wipe, they may now only have a partial section of a wipe in their hand. If they are aiming for a messy target, the user will likely have some stuff on their hands as well as the little section of the wipe. Now you have two things to clean up and this product becomes a waste of time and money. You might as well hand your toddler a sugar packet and tell them to wipe with that.

I didn’t give them one star because I can still use the clean shreds to wipe a spot of sticky juice off my tile kitchen floor or wipe a speck of pudding off a small chin. But, it’s very infrequent and I am about to throw the remainder of what I purchased away. You may like the price of this product, but if it doesn’t work as designed then you have wasted your money. Hope this review saves you time, money, and an opportunity to avoid getting really irritated. Lastly, google photos of wipes that have been flushed and what they do to sewer systems. Ultimately just not a good idea.

title: BUYER BEWARE! Not as flushable as you think
text:
Yeah these were flushable for about 8 months until our entire sewage line was clogged and it wasn’t just some toilet clog you could just unclog yourself. We had to call a plumber out who had to access our sewage drain from outside because that’s how deep the clog was and all he pulled out were these wipes that haven’t broken down for the past 8 months since we’ve been using them.
It was a $500 plumbing bill and the plumber had to get permission from the city before he could even start the job because of how far out on the sewage drain he was going to have to work on. It was so far out into the sewage system that it wasn’t even on our property anymore. The build up of 8 months of baby wipes in the sewage system went all the way out to the sidewalk which is public property hence the reason the plumber had to get permission so that was a hassle as we had to inconveniently wait for the plumber to get permission from the city to finally fix the sewage line while I held in my crap I had to take.
I’ve recently learned that NO FLUSHABLE WIPES are actually flushable no matter what brand. They just don’t break down in water like how toilet paper does. It says to just flush 2 at a time but all that’s gonna do is extend the time before you need to call a plumber to fix your sewage drain. It’s not worth the plumbing bill.

title: Game changer
text:
UPDATE: After using this product for a few weeks I stand by most of my initial review (below). Some notable differences are as follows...

-You CAN just use the straightener to dry and style the beard, but the best results are when you still use the hair drier as it gets 100% of the water out and allows the hair to straighten. The brush leaves some residual moisture which can kink stubborn hair like mine.
-Make sure you use a charging brick that is sufficient enough. Using my small Apple charger was frustrating as the charge would take a full day/night to complete! Once I read the battery requirements I realized I needed a more powerful charging brick. TIP: if the screen flashes while charging, the unit is not receiving enough power to charge in a reasonable time. You should see the display fully lit, not flashing, and the charge increasing fairly quickly before your eyes.
-Battery life on this thing leaves much to be desired. That being said, I'm only charging it about once a week as results for me can last a few days at a time if I'm not getting the beard soaked every night in the shower. If I used it daily, I may have to increase to charging 2x a week.
-Heat up time is also a small issue. It gets to 200F pretty quickly, but 200-365F takes a bit. If I turn it on right out of the shower it still needs a minute or so by the time I'm ready to use it. Not a deal-breaker though.

Pros:
-easy to follow manual
-the battery came with a mostly full charge
-the packaging was nice and high-end
-instruction manual was clear and easy to read
-comes with charging cable
-lightweight
-bristles aren’t too tall for shorter beard lengths
-easy to lock the desired temperature
-easy to adjust the temperature
-can be used to charge other devices (this will be really useful for me when camping or traveling!)
-straightened out kinks and ripples easily on hair that hadn’t been washed or straightened in 2 days

Cons:
-the box had a pink unit pictured but was black inside (I didn’t recall a color choice at the time of purchase)
-charging cable is short and doesn't come with a power brick to plug the USB end into (read power requirements in manual)
-it is possible to burn yourself on the heating element if you press down too much, although it is somewhat uncommon

Original Review:

Overall this is a great product! The biggest point is that it can eliminate the need to blow dry and then straighten your beard. I haven't washed my beard since getting this product so I still haven't tested it fully, but my best results came the day I got the product. I had washed my beard the night before, blew dry, and straightened with a brush (I have very curly/kinky dark hair).

The next day the product arrived and I used my round brush to raise the hair and then brushed it out with the straightening iron- it worked amazingly- stick straight, no water or washing. That night, I got it all soaked and used the straightener by itself... the results were really good, not as good as the first time, but maybe with more finesse.

The next morning, I untangled using a wide-tooth comb, raised the hair with my round brush, and used the straightener... I was able to achieve a nice result using the brush and straightener together and it definitely saved me time over my normal routine.

title: From 5 Stars to 1 Star
text:
August 2017: 5 Stars. Then the price was $13.99 for 5 pairs, they were ok considering the price, lightweight and didn't break as easily as you would think as they are not exactly sturdy. I often fall asleep with them on and even then they help up. Of course after a while the lenses become scratched with use but that's to be expected.

March 2019: 1 Star. The new price is $14.99. Moving forward and after the 5 previous ones gave out I clicked on "Buy It Again" without a thought but what I got was NOT the same item as last time. Sure, they are glasses, they are lightweight, they are sold by the same seller and the box still comes all the way from China. Except... The new "design" must be the work of some kind of genius (sarcasm intended).

The old glasses had the traditional nose bridge supports, a piece of plastic attached to each lens to comfortably rest on your nose. In the new glasses instead of having the traditional nose bridge support there is a thin... I don't even know what to call it... but it looks and feels more like a blade that cuts and digs into your nose leaving some serious ridges or indentations that make wearing them all day almost impossible unless the skin of your nose is made out of a material similar to the skin of an elephant.

Once again we get proof that "new and improved" is no such thing, I ended up paying more money for a lesser product, now I have to buy something else form another seller.

title: Best supplement I've ever taken
text:
I"d never heard of rhodiola until this summer. One of the health & fitness bloggers I follow, recommended it for decreased pain and increased energy.

Well, he certainly knew what he was talking about! This rhodiola rose organic extract powder is the best supplement I've taken -- and I've taken plenty, especially following two back surgeries and a persistent TMJ issue. Fish oil, magnesium, turmeric, vitamins, etc. -- all good for what they are, but nothing seems to compare with this rhodiola.

My morning ritual now is to take 1/6 of a teaspoon of this powder and mix it into my morning hot coffee. It takes some persistent mixing to get it to dissolve, and to tell the truth some of it never actually does dissolve, but I drink the whole cup down.

About 30 minutes after drinking it, the rhodiola does its thing.

What happens? First, I get more energy. Yes, I just had the coffee, but this is a different kind of energy than what I get from caffeine. Peaceful & productive energy, not too much, just right.

Second, I get some focus. I'm as ADD-addled as the next person (maybe more so), and have a lot I want to accomplish. The increased focus (for work, for working out, for playing the piano) is more than welcome.

Finally, I feel a LOT better. The TMJ (mostly jaw & neck clicking) settles way, way down. No back pain. No headache.

Someone wrote recently that you can build up a tolerance to rhodiola, and it stops being effective. I've been using this for three months and that hasn't begun to happen. I pray that it doesn't, because I really plan to keep using this. Maybe forever.

The computer lenses are great for reducing monitor brightness while reading text , but I set them aside when editing photos because they interfere with accurate color rendering.  The frames have spring hinges which give them added flexibility which reduces (not eliminates) the odds of them snapping off when accidental pressure is placed on them.  Both the right and left lenses are balanced (closed one eye and then the other and both were in good focus).  The focal strength seems to be precise for the power level I need.  Cosmetically, they are very attractive frames.  They are lightweight, yet sturdy.  And they are comfortable to wear for extended periods of time.

title: Metal sensitive? Beware.
text:
I used this product for ten years and had no complaints other than how skimpy they are with the cleaning containers. However since surgical staples were left in my neck (without my knowledge nor consent) following a surgery, My pre-existing nickel allergy has broadened and I am even more metal sensitive. When my eyes starting drying out six months ago, I initially worried it was Sjogrens Syndrome. They were so dry my eye lids would stick to my eye balls and I had to wake up in the middle of the night to apply drops.
I eventually discovered that the platinum disc that causes the bubbling is indeed platinum, the metal. When I switched contact lens solution, the dry eye problem went away (as long as I now also avoid iron oxides, which are in most cosmetics —sigh). I wish they’d label the box to indicate metal is used. Stars given reflect that.

title: A stimulating and awakening effect on the mind and body
text:
A great product, with definite noticeable effects. I created an eye drop solution to work with the undulata in the way that it is worked with by hunters in the Amazon.
I placed 30ml of contact lens saline solution into a microwave-safe cup and nuked it for 30 seconds. Afterwards, I mixed in the T Undulata extract with a butter knife. It took roughly 5 minutes of stirring the tarry extract into the hot saline before it was fully diluted.
Afterwards I used eye droppers to place a single drop in each eye. The effects are immediate, and stimulating, in a way that is not quite like caffeine. It feels cleaner, and more awakening. Rather cerebral, yet peaceful.
I have been using the solution each morning before putting my contacts on, with consistent effects.
I'm very much enjoying working with this plant, and am super thankful for the man who doesn't exist for providing this service to other incarnations of his lack of self.

title: This is 2nd one of these I bought. The exact same bag cost me $40 more from a medical supply store in Manhattan
text: I first got this exact same model number EZ Access Walker Bag in January when I went to a medical supply store in Manhattan located near my doctor's office to buy an immediately needed walker. The bag cost me $59.95. It turned out to be much more useful than I thought it would be, particularly at my job. With the bag on the side of the walker, and with the zipper on the large pocket open, I am able to put a ream of paper in the bag to carry it  to our copier. I am able to put a gallon size bottle of water in the same large pocket to carry it from the refrigerator to my office. Tonight we had a lecture presentation and I was able to fill the large pockets (having bought a 2nd bag thru Amazon.com which arrived yesterday) with spoons, a container of milk, a bottle of Coffee Mate, Sugar, foam cups, all to bring to the refreshment table in the room for the presentation. It feels good to be able to do these relatively simple chores again, and not depend upon others to do them,  as I have had to do since 9 months ago when i first came down with a series of physical injuries which coincidentally led to a relapse of a plasma cell cancer which had been in remission for 14 years. I do only use the pockets for carrying items at work and at home. I use the walker outdoors only to walk from my house or from my office, or from one of my many medical appointments, to a waiting car service. The bag's zippered pocket stays closed and flat while outside, keeping the bag nice and flat and unobtrusive, as I feel I must be while outdoors. At 4'6", having lost over 5 inches in the past decade due to my illness, it had become very hard walking around the city's sidewalks filled with people so much taller, who it seemed were always walking into me, having not noticed me down there while talking on their cellphone. At home I add a removable tray to the walker, and now with two pockets, it has become so easy to transport things all over my house. So, I really love this walker bag for helping me feel so much less helpless than I did 2 months ago. And, as I stated up above, the 2nd bag that I bought thru amazon.com was 19.99, whereas the 1st bag cost me $59.95, which is a whopping $40 more, from a medical supply store in Manhattan. Oh, and I should mention how much less I saw the exact same Drive folding walker model on amazon.com selling for, than what I paid for it in the same medical supply store. Too upsetting, so I remind myself that I had no choice as I needed the walker immediately, and that was the price I paid for immediate.

title: Cute but pricey
text:
Ultimately, I will be returning this bag. There were several things I really liked. The design is cute and the color combo is gorgeous. I love the idea behind it. The special touches, like the photo windows and insulated pockets, are really neat. Also, it is obvious that the company really has a passion for what they do for moms.

The reason I am returning this bag has everything to do with the relatively expensive price tag, which I do not feel is justified by the structure and materials of the bag. Had the bag been half the price, I would keep it no problem. I wanted a bag that would carry everything I need for pumping and work, but I could tell that once my pump and pumping supplies were packed, there would not be a lot of room for much else. Adding only my laptop made the bag super heavy, and as I mentioned earlier, the structure is not sturdy enough to really support much in the bag. Also, the interior of the bag is floppy and I could tell I would spend a lot of time digging around for items I needed. I know the zippers have been updated, but they still seem a little difficult to maneuver.

I really love the idea of this bag, and I wanted to love it! It just didn't meet my personal needs when considering the price.

title: Fits ankle perfectly, but only stays ice cold for 10-20 min.
text:
I have tendinitis in my Achilles, and I've been using it for a couple weeks before leaving this review.

Pros:
-Perfectly conforms to all the areas of my ankle that are swollen from tendinitis
-Very soft and comfortable
-Lightweight, easy to walk in
-I don't feel embarrassed to wear it in public because it is well designed and discreet

Cons:
-I noticed it takes longer that my other more traditional ice packs to freeze; about 2-3 hours
-It only stays at peak coldness for 10 minutes, and only stays cold at all for about 20 minutes. After that it is room temperature. (I think this is the sacrifice for having such a lightweight and formfitting shape. It just doesn't have as much fluid in it as a traditional ice pack.)

Overall, I find myself reaching for this particular ice pack over my others when I want something to gently ice down all the swollen areas of my ankle for 20 minutes or less. When I want something for deeper tissues or that stays very cold the whole time it is on, I reach for my traditional ice packs instead. Also, the price is totally worth it for the quality.

title: Grew on me!
text:
I tried to base these on whether or not I would recommend to a friend more so than personal opinion.

Personally, I decided to get the Naturals because I work out 2-3 times a day and always drink a whey shake after... ingesting that much artificial sweetener every day will probably add up to cancer one day. The Natural Nectars use stevia, which has actually been shown to have positive effects such as regulating blood sugar.

Flavors:

Apple Ecstasy - 4/5 - I normally like apple-flavored anything, but this did not impress me. It's a little too sour. However, there was no aftertaste or anything, so I'm sure someone out there might like it.

Caribbean Cooler - 5/5 - I must say I was impressed with how the coconut aspect of this coconut/pineapple flavor concoction really captures the taste and texture of real coconut milk. Would I want to drink 2 lbs. of this stuff? Eh, IDK. But if you like coconut...

Crystal Sky - 2/5 - Tastes like ground up Sweet-Tarts mixed with water. It's a very, very synthetic berry taste of some sort. It has so much blue coloring that my poo was bright green!

Fuzzy Navel - 5/5 - This is the flavor that made Nectar famous. It's a nice blend of peach and orange and tastes like a glass of juice; I could not detect any protein, and the aftertaste was mostly just peach flavor.

Lemon Tea - 3/5 - I really wanted to dislike this one, and although I'm still not a fan of iced tea protein (lol), I can see why some people would like it. I can clearly detect an underlying protein taste, but ignore that and it's just like Arizona iced tea.

Roadside Lemonade - 1/5 - This one is nasty, I could barely get it down! The obvious protein taste gives it a gelatin-like quality. So, yeah, (synthetic) lemon-flavored liquid Jell-O is how I'd describe it.

Strawberry Kiwi - 3/5 As soon as I smelled it, I knew this was going to be another Jell-O flavor. Honestly it's not that bad (no kind of protein taste or aftertaste), but most of us have had strawberry kiwi Jell-O, and so drinking it in liquid form is rather unappealing.

Twisted Cherry - 2/5 - Extremely synthetic cherry Kool-Aid flavor (just like children's medicine) with way too much red color.

Strawberry Mousse - 5/5 - Tastes like the pink Yoohoo or strawberry milk. Slight bitter aftertaste, but not a big deal.

Vanilla Bean Torte - 5/5 - I normally don't like vanilla, but this is just like frosting (yummmm)! There is a slight "metallic" aftertaste (Acesulfame K can do that), but not as bad as the weird Chocolate Truffle aftertaste.

Chocolate Truffle - 4/5 - It's like watered down chocolate mousse. I'm not a big chocolate fan, but someone who likes that kind of thing would probably enjoy this flavor. I took a point off because it had a strange aftertaste.

Cappuccino - 5/5 - Personally, it's way too sweet for me (but I really don't have much of a sweet tooth). I like my coffee black, but someone who is into those Starbucks shakes would probably like this. It actually reminds me a lot of a mocha flavored chocolate bar Lindt sells called "Milk Mocha."

Natural Peach - 5/5 - The best of the "naturals." It's kind of orangey-peachy, but in a more toned down way than Fuzzy Navel.

Natural Orange - 3/5 - My least favorite of the "naturals," but it's okay.

Natural Fruit Punch - 5/5 - Didn't like this one at 1st, but it grew on me. It's not like a Hawaiian Punch kind of taste, but more like fruit-flavored Tums.

title: Not for every banana!
text:
I bought one of these a while ago and was pretty pleased with it and would have happily given it a 5 star review. It protects your banana, comes in colors, and has "pleasure ridges." The ridges do take some getting used to, but are very useful in teaching a beginner how to hold and eat a banana. To properly hold and eat a banana you need a fairly loose grip; you should be able to slide your hand up and down the banana with only a little effort while still feeling a little friction. If you squeeze too tight you may bruise the banana or end up with a cramped hand. The ridges make it too painful to grasp the banana too hard, so you get that perfect grip every time.

So why only 3 stars? I returned from the store recently and to my shock, not one of the bananas I bought will fit. All the bananas curve to the right, and unfortunately, the banana bunker curves to the left. Now I know to only buy left curving bananas, but sometimes the store doesn't have any. They should really sell these in a 2 pack with one right and one left.

title: They do the job.
text:
Height adjusts, cuffs pivot so you can use your hands while standing, they do the job.... they're crutches, can't imagine anyone waxing rhapsodic about such. Let's face it, this is not an item anyone wants to need.

Forearm crutches are far better than the armpit version as far as convenience and mobility -- particularly for we women. The under the arm versions squash and bruise areas that should never be squashed or bruised. The E/R I landed in when I broke my ankle only had the arm pit crutchs -- clearly such "standardization" was done by a man who didn't have to worry about bruising and squashing "side boobs".... for women that's not workable. Having used crutches before, I asked for the forearm ones, when they didn't have them I was pretty stunned, and was on Amazon looking for the forearm variety as soon as I got home from the E/R and got 1 day delivery. It makes a world of difference. I was already bruised from the hospital issue ones when these arrived just from going back and forth to the bathroom a few times and getting to the door to take delivery of these.

These are also much better for getting in and out of a car. Because they're so much shorter than the arm pit crutches, they are just plain easier to maneuver all the way around. Having used both at various times over the years, I simply don't understand why anyone would use the other type at all. The big ones are more cumbersome, heavier, and smash sensitive areas. No crutch is a joy to use, but why make it harder?

My only problem is that with the hot weather this summer, the rubberized coating on the cuffs sticks to my forearm and can be a pain -- the flip side of that is that it makes it easier to use my hands because my forearm isn't sliding out through the cuffs if they're effectively glued to me.

Notice to all those making decisions on what to stock at hospitals -- STOCK FOREARM CRUTCHES FOR FEMALE PATIENTS PLEASE!

title: Does not fit tiny ear holes = EarSad
text: I bought these almost a year ago as a last ditch effort to maintain the tenuous grip on sanity that comes with extended sleep deprivation. As I'm writing this at 1:47AM from the resentful position of my couch, I can report this purchase was made in vain. For reference, I purchased these based on the high reviews, reviews which mentioned their capability to fit even the tiniest ear holes, the number of options in the box and finally, cost. After multiple attempts to use these to block out the variety of snores emanting from the other side of the bed, including my personal favorite - the ventilator inhale/kuzo exhale combo - these are not the solution for me. However, I can impart some pros and cons. The packaging is very nice, the quality of the ear plugs is very good and the storage containers are well made. That said I still gave each one a go. All were terribly uncomfortable (again, freakishly small ear holes) and had to be jammed pretty far into the canal to get them to stay but would eventually pop and/or fall out. The "pulls" on all stuck out really far, preventing me from sleeping on my side. After trimming them back, this was remedied, but their inability to stay put was still a problem as was how painful they were to wear. I can say for the brief time they stayed put, they did greatly diminish even the loudest wildlife impressions produced by my husband.

title: Pads lasted about 1-2 weeks for me on average - they lasted best when I swiped with alcohol before application
text:
I read a lot of reviews prior to purchasing these and was excited to receive them. I used them for about 3 months while losing weight to lift my frames off of my cheeks. Now they're not necessary.
These pads can be used whole (a butterfly shape where one side folds over, to provide a longer-lasting fit) or cut to a half-moon shape for a more streamlined but shorter-lasting adhesion. Pads lasted about 1-2 weeks for me on average - they lasted best when I swiped with alcohol before application, kept my nose as oil-free as possible and kept the area near the pads clean without pushing them around. The height was just right to lift them off my nose. Removal wasn't too difficult - any adhesive residue peels off easily.
I had been hoping these would help more with slippage. They helped a bit as I have a narrow bridge and my glasses are wider, but were just as susceptible to sweat/oil as the frames themselves. I cycle for fitness and cook frequently, and hate when my glasses slip off my nose. If you need to lift your frames off your face, these will likely do the trick. I'd suggest measuring to see if 2.5 mm is appropriate for you.

title: Wonderful massage chair!
text: This massage chair is an excellent product.  I spent several weeks researching and trying name-brand massage chairs.  The features on this chair match the features on other chairs selling for 3 times the price.  It massages from my scalp to the bottoms of my feet, with preset massages or custom-made massages.  It scans the person in the chair and then adjusts to their size.  My 6'5" son used it and had rave reviews, and my 5'1" friend also loved it; it adjusted to each of them.  It is becoming the perfect way to unwind at the end of a work day, loosening my tight shoulders, as well as a great way to stimulate circulation in my feet and hands.  I have no regrets and would recommend this chair to anyone.

title: Simple and works better than expected!
text: Following recent knee surgery, I needed some way to get socks on my feet with limited flex of my knees. I saw the gizmo shown on TV, but decided to look on Amazon to see what else was out there. I spotted this device, did a quick browse through the reviews and placed my order. This device is simple, yet 100% effective. Simply pull your sock over the 'scoop', slide your foot into the scoop, then pull up the two padded handles. The grip material on the rear of the scoop holds the sock material in place until the sock is completely pulled up. Due to the size of the scoop, I can see where smaller sock sizes may not stretch enough to fit on the device. I wear men's size 9 to 12 socks, and had no issues. Perhaps the manufacturer should make a smaller device for folks with smaller feet? In any case, I am VERY pleased with my purchase.

title: The Very Finest
text:
Normal fish oil pills contain 18% EPA and 12% DHA. DHA is the important part. So I did a DHA per dollar analysis of a lot of different fish oil pills, and the best one had a 719 DHA/$ ratio (though this didn't have your standard 18/12 split; it has a 12/28 EPA/DHA split). However, when I started entertaining the idea of a liquid fish oil, I was very surprised to see a 2159 DHA/$ ratio. Like 3x more efficiency. That's huge, obviously. For comparison, the best performing 18/12 pill on Amazon only has a 302 DHA/$ ratio. The fish oil is 7 times more efficient/cheaper than the pills. To put it in perspective, to get the same amount of DHA as I get in this product from a standard 18/12 pill, I would need to spend about $160.

When this fish oil arrived, I was kind of expecting it to be a little nasty, but it wasn't at all. It had a kind of pleasant, subdued lemon scent. I had some straight and it was fine (if a little oily =p), and then added some to a blended drink psyllium fiber drink this morning. While I imagine it bound the drink together a little better, it also yielded a mild lemon flavor to it I found pleasing. I think it may even be good incorporated into a salad dressing.

If you're open to the idea of a liquid fish oil, I think this one is great. It's a very cost effective means to get your daily DHA.

title: Great features, iffy construction
text:
Love the features of this scale: body-fat measurement, weight, and Wi-Fi. No issue whatsoever with the features. There are two problems with mine that might be indicative of overall design or build quality issues however:

1) The device rarely powers down on inactivity, and as a result burns through batteries. I've tried everything -- checking that it's on a completely level surface, and making sure the surface is clean in case detritus of any kind is activating the electrodes. No joy. Hour upon hour of LED display, 24 hrs a day. 4 alkaline AAs last less than two weeks, and I only weigh myself once a week.

2) The metal ring around the LED display came loose within about two days. I keep it in place, but I'm afraid to glue it back on because it seems to serve some conductive function for the electrodes. Not sure if gluing it would defeat that function.

It works well enough, and I like the features enough to keep the scale (and keep my Fitbit app, for scale syncing) even though I'm no longer using a Fitbit wristband. My experience dealing the Fitbit customer service on my Flex was so negative, I have not contacted them about the scale.

title: Good price for lemon oil. It has a very "clean" scent.
text:
Overall I am quite impressed with this lemon oil. I love the price. A 15ml Young Living Lavender oil is $11.25 wholesale. This bottle is 120ml for less than $11. I have read that the dark blue bottle is important in protecting the oil from degradation from light. It also comes with a high quality dropper that is essential to using the oil. The dropper screws onto the top of the bottle, so I threw out the original top and just leave the dropper screwed on top.

This oil is cold pressed, which is the best method of extracting oils - or so I've read - and country of origin is Italy. The oil is very fragrant and has a very clean smell. I have heard that lemon oil can be used as an aromatic disinfectant simply by putting a few drops into a cotton ball and sitting the cotton ball on your desk. I have been using this method to *hopefully* keep my wife from catching the cold that I have right now.

I received this product at discount for review purposes. I will continue to test and experiment with this oil and update my review if I learn anything new or change my mind on anything I have stated above.

Note: This oil is labeled "For external use only."

title: Works Well, Impossible to Apply Without Getting On Your Lenses
text:
Interesting concept. It actually works as advertised but is impossible to apply without getting on your lenses. Then you have to clean your lenses, which becomes a major headache because Nerdwax is a mild abrasive designed to stick. So it's tough to remove from your lenses without scratching your lenses. And then you have Nerdwax on the cloth you use to clean your lenses, which ruins the cloth because if you use it again guess what? You'll smear Nerdwax on your lenses. So keep a stack of lens cloths handy.

It really is effective and much less painful than nose pads. But the Chapstick-style applicator is poorly thought out, should be a needle-nose style applicator for more surgical precision when applying. Gooping this stuff from the way-too-large Chapstick applicator just makes a mess and I spend more time cleaning my glasses than worrying about them slipping.

Hopeful they'll get it right with a second swing.

title: Big Crack Down the Middle. Too Bad, So Sad
text:
I hate to be the spoiler of so many glowing reviews, but here goes. Reason I bought this toothbrush in the first place was to replace a different previous brand, albeit not one of the expensive name brands, that had begun to fall apart. What happened was after about 10 months, the outside/exterior housing of my earlier model had begun to disintegrate/crack/fall apart, and I wanted to replace it. So, after reading all the glowing reviews about this brand, plus they threw a discount coupon at me, I bought this.

Welllll, guess what! After 5 weeks, yes that's right, 5 WEEKS, not months, the outside housing on this one cracked - a big crack right down the middle of the body from the switch on down the side. This was one week after the return/refund/replacement period had expired. Looks like I'm stuck.

Soooo, I did what any conscientious consumer would do -- I emailed the manufacturer's Customer Support. The email address is right on the toothbrush case. Gave it a few days. What did I hear back? "Crickets. Chirp. Chirp." Nothing. Utter waste of time.

Yes, the toothbrush is still functional. Works as well as any other electric toothbrush I've used. But, the cracked case is problematic. Even more problematic is the lack of Customer Support.

So, in the future, I'll take my wifey advice: " Buy the name brand." She's had a name brand for over two years with no cracking, no problems.

Bottom line: Yuse pays yer money, yuse takes yer chances. Buy a name brand electric toothbrush and save yourself time and trouble. Thanks for reading and heeding. :-))

title: Different readings from my other BP monitor
text:
[[VIDEOID:746cebf4b319b8873db16f14daa745ca]] It seems like a nice blood pressure monitor but I am getting different readings from my other BP monitor I bought from the pharmacy at my local hospital and I’m not sure which one is accurate. I took my BP with this monitor and got a 139/89 reading. Then took it with my old monitor and got a 125/73 reading. Then took it with this one again and got 134/80. That was all within minutes of each other on the same arm. So… ? I think I might bring both to my next doctors appointment and test it against theirs. So far this one is consistently giving higher readings than my old one.

I like that it takes the readings relatively quickly. It’s a bit faster than my other monitor.

I also like that this comes with a USB power cord. My old one runs strictly on batteries. I like having the option to also plug it into a wall outlet. That’s a nice feature.

And I really like that this detects an irregular heartbeat. My old one didn’t do that.

I just need to figure out which BP monitor is accurate. I tried to see if this is Antrolife BP monitor has been validated for accuracy using the online registries at MedEval and Stride BP (the 2 most well known international registries) but I couldn’t find any BP monitors manufactured by Antrolife listed on either registry. I also checked the British and Irish hypertension society registry, European society of hypertension (they use the stride BP registry) and the American medical association registry with no luck. None had any Antrolife products listed. I searched by both manufacturer and model number.
Maybe they are manufactured and tested under a different brand name? Or maybe I’m just not searching the registries properly? I’ve never done a search of BP monitor registries before today so it could just be user error on my end. It says it’s certified by European ISO but I was unable to find a way to search for European ISO certified BP monitors. I thought they were supposed to be listed on the Stride BP registry but I may be wrong.

I’ll try to update this review in the future if I ever figure out which one is accurate.

title: 2nd defective product in a row and it’s less than 2 months old. And I’m stuck with it
text:
Edit - I now have the same issue with this new hair straightening iron. The temperature gauge is not accurate and it keeps getting way hotter than the temperature I set it to. I was using it today and set it to 200 degrees (near the lowest heat setting) and it actually melted/burned my hair right off. It’s obviously getting WAY hotter than it should be. There’s no way it should melt my hair when set to 200 deg. It really shouldn’t even melt my hair if it was set at the highest heat setting of 350. Not with a quick press. So I would guess that it was getting much hotter than that (which should obviously never happen).

This is the 2nd unit in a row that had this problem. This one isn’t flashing the “Err” message like the last one. At least with that one it would start flashing an error message when it overheated. This time it was reading the correct temperature so there was no way to know it was was hotter than it should have been until I used it and it very quickly started to melt my hair.

There seems to be some type of manufacturer defect. I would avoid buying this hair straightening iron.

I had an issue with the first 1-3/5 inch hair straightener I ordered. It kept getting way hotter than what I set the temperature at and then it would start flashing an “Err” message. So I contacted amazon that night. They got back to me hours later and had already shipped the new hair straightener by the quickest means possible. It arrived the next day. Very impressive!

So far so good with the new hair straightener. I had this same model for years and loved it but unfortunately it got broken in a move. So when I came across the same model I ordered it immediately. I’m guessing the first one I got was just a rare defect. As I said, the replacement is working perfectly so far and the previous one I had worked great (and would probably still be working if it hasn’t been broken). title: Nice hearing protection for concerts
text:
I purchased these a while ago but only just used them recently. Attending three rock concerts in three nights, I wore "regular" workplace industrial earplugs the first two shows (3M 1100 Foam inserted halfway through the first show, Howard Leight Max-1 for the second), and these for the third. My preferred hearing protection for work is the Howard Leight Laser Lite as I have smaller ears.
These ear plugs worked great in a concert environment. I was able to hear the music more clearly than with the foam ear plugs, but they took the edge off the pain-inducing loudness. The short stems can be a bit tricky to grab, so for larger-fingered and larger-eared people, this may be a deal breaker; however, the short stems also mean that they are fairly inconspicuous.

title: Low quality limited use scooter
text:
In full disclosure, I purchased this exact scooter elsewhere and this rating doesn’t reflect on any particular seller.

The GOOD: comes with better than average options, if you are going to purchase a Ventura, the DLX worth the upgrade. The hi-back seat is heavy but fully adjustable and among the best I’ve seen on a scooter.

The BAD: 1) this is strictly an outdoor scooter, the huge 53” turning radius is larger than many 4-wheel scooters and is of little value in a home, or even a store or shop. 2) Dismantling this scooter for transport is a pain, regardless of what the manufacturer indicates, so unless it can be transported in one piece you can assume it isn’t going anywhere. 3) Parts for this scooter are beyond ridiculous and can take weeks/months to arrive from overseas. For example, $87 for a plastic basket, $145 for a wheel, $620 for a seat, $125 for a seat pedestal (broken on every Ventura I’ve ever seen)...you get the picture. 4) Drive’s description of the the dual-hand tiller control is VERY misleading, it is just a simple right hand control that is not mirrored on the left side. To go forward, the user pulls down on the right tiller handle and pushes up for reverse. However, for those users who must use their left hand, those controls are the opposite which is extremely uncomfortable at any distance. Drive customer service, which is poor at best, states the scooter must be taken to a particular service center for reprogramming (at the customer’s expense) and suggested 2 centers that were within 50 miles: however, neither was aware of that particular programming. 5) documentation is very poor, not detailed and not always accurate. After several wasted hours I finally called Drive CS who had an updated bulletin they were able to send me, but why does a customer have waste their time because Drive chooses not to include valuable updated information with the original documentation....or update the owner’s manual? 6) the overall quality, except for the seat, is average at best and does not support the exaggerated price. Unless a person is looking for a dedicated outdoor scooter that doesn’t need to be dismantled, look elsewhere. If so, look carefully.

The product itself feels solid and matte. Doesn't feel like cheap plastic at all, which I highly appreciate as I am particular with those kinds of things. The songs played and the sound quality are run-of-the-mill. They are of similar quality to the phone apps I've used before. title: Very comfortable and does the job.
text: I have rheumatoid arthritis which causes fluid and pain in both knees. They swell so badly, the kneecap moves around and makes the joint lock up. I have tried many other knee braces but can only wear them a few hours before they slid down or wrinkle and become too uncomfortable to continue wearing. These compression sleeves work extremely well and I sometimes wear them for a couple days without taking them off to reduce swelling. When my knees swell at night, I can hardly get them to support me when I get out of bed until I put on the sleeves but, then I can instantly walk nearly normally. They seldom have to even be pulled up at all and cause me no welting at all. Long lasting quality construction. They don't feel hot, well ventilated and stay put. I can't live without them.

title: These are super comfortable! Inflate them just a little for best ...
text:
These are super comfortable! Inflate them just a little for best results. I have owned several and they fold and transport easily, even in a hip pocket. The downside is the valve which is like a beach balls and becomes very difficult to remove and adjust the amount of air. The small strap attaching the plug to the valve is what breaks over time. To fill once and continue to use it this wouldn't be a problem, but to travel where you need to fill and deflate it's difficult to adjust to the optimum amount of air.
I now use mostly Therm-a-rest cushions of which there are many sizes and styles and they have screw valves which are much easier to use! The Therm-a-rests are also very comfortable but are not as portable as this cushion. When I sit - car, plane, or computer I always use one or the other of these to avoid a sore butt.

title: Almost perfect ... almost
text:
I do my computing from my rocker-recliner and needed a flat surface for my laptop mouse and it works perfectly for that. I also wanted to get my four remotes off my side table. At least it takes care of three on one side and one on the other. I just wish they had made four pockets on one side instead; there is enough room for four side by side if it had another pocket.

The pockets are just 5.5" deep, which lets the remotes lean outward. I wish they were a little deeper and not so loose. Remotes are not nearly as thick as the room these pockets have.

I like that it doesn't have raised edges so I don't have to rest my arm on something protruding. I have stabilized it with a single twist pin in the middle of each side and it stays nicely in place.

I like the look of the suede-like material and the cafe color. It doesn't look cheap and the flat surface is very comfortable.

I couldn't find another product that came as close to meeting my requirements and after a week of use am glad I have it. I would have given five stars if only it had four pockets for remotes, and deeper.

***

After about a month of use I can say that I like it a lot. As an afterthought, the smooth leather like version might have been a better choice--easier to wipe clean--but this suede one looks nicer.

title: Gets the job done
text:
A lot of reviewers complained that it didn't work, that it was shoddy, or that they couldn't sit as close as it said they should. Pshaw.

I get dreary when we go through a couple of days with no hint of sun, the kind of winter days where you have to have your inside lights turned on all day. From what I can tell, this takes care of it. I'm a little more energetic, a little less droopy when I use the light.
Is it made of solid gold? No. It's pieces of plastic with a lightbulb, just like most other things out there. It's fairly solid and not unattractive. Even better, when I dropped it, the pieces seperated but I was easily able to click them back into place.

Some people complaining about prices implied that any light would do this. The FDA doesn't regulate this, but Mayo Clinic suggests brighter lights, white (as opposed to blue), and having the UV rays filtered out. This does all of that.

As for its use: I just plug it in next to my computer on dreary mornings. It's about a foot and a half away. I just leave it on in the morning hours. One person said the instructions tell you to knit while using it. There's a whole list of activities they say you can do while using it; the point is that you can continue on with your life and just use it during activities that normally keep you in one place for an hour or so. Anyone who has such an active lifestyle that they don't have an hour of stationary time due to their obligations is probably so healthy that they don't even get seasonal affective disorder.

The brightness is great, they warm up quick, out of a box of 24 I've got 9 left (lots of spot lights in my 4 storie house) and out of the 15 I've screwed in, only 1 has been a dud when powered. I.e., it never worked at all. That's decent odds for me.

So about 2 weeks ago or so I decided to get my hair chopped and when I say chopped I mean it was above my butt and I got it cut to my shoulders but because of the perm that was still left in my hair I wasn't able to recreate the style that the cut demanded, so I got Amazon and looked around for straighteners and I came across this beauty and read some reviews for this and a few other brands and this one just called to me.

On this model there is a LCD screen and it heats up pretty quickly, the back part of the brush gets warm but not hot but the bristled part gets very hot so don't let children use it. It can straighten up to 2" inches of hair at a time and is suitable for all hair types.

title: Nothing Better Than A Warm Bed On A Cold Day
text:
We moved to Massachusetts from Arizona so that I could attend graduate school and we'd never experienced a real winter before. Goodness gracious you people live with this kind of cold?! I bought us heated blankets, but you're not supposed to bring those into bed. I found this heated mattress pad and bought it even though I initially thought it was kind of expensive. Oh my goodness it is Worth It. 100% Worth It. Nothing is better than turning it on to pre-heat the bed while you get ready to go to sleep and then coming to bed and sliding between the nice, toasty covers, warming your freezing, weary bones before you turn the temperature down to something you can sleep the night through without being too warm. The biggest challenge is finding the motivation to slide out of the nice, still heated bed in the morning and face the crisp bedroom air to start your day.

The other comments are correct, the place that the power cord attaches to the mattress pad is at the same level as your feet. Just scootch more towards the middle of the bed and it won't be a problem, or pull the mattress pad farther down on your bed so it curves around it a little bit. It's really not that big a deal to me. The power cord is plenty long, so even though it attaches at the foot of the bed, the cord will reach all the way up to the head of the bed to plug in if that's where your outlet is located.

It does take a while to heat up, so I would definitely recommend pre-heating it before you climb into bed, but once it's preheated it's delightful. It is a more gentle heat than the heated blankets that we use, so bear that in mind.

Oh, I guess I should also add, the only downside is that the display light is really bright blue and a little blinding in the middle of the night, and the white lights for each of the three buttons are really bright, but we keep them covered up with a cloth so that they don't bother us and that works just fine.

I don't know if this heated mattress pad is the best ever because it's the only one that I've owned, but we're starting our second winter in Massachusetts and I can definitely say that I'm one happy customer knowing that I get to go to a nice warm bed every night.

title: I love Linux
text:
Background: I have been using Rebecca 17.1 for many months and am quite happy with it! IT WORKS GREAT!! Then came along some new hardware, and Mint is very accommodating to it, so the next pc was with this newer recently released Rosa 17.3 version. I am primarily using Mint for LibreOffice which is included, or free elsewhere, and the internet. This version has proved to be even better than 17.1. Open source means its made by us, and this version seems to be perfected, intuitive, and easy to use to me.

Disk Use: As soon as you begin to boot up change the boot device to cd-rom in your bios, this is started with pressing the F2 and/or Delete key on some MBs. Next it will boot directly from this disc. Test and play with the program while it is held in RAM memory. Install it to your drive from an icon on the home screen. It will erase the drive disk first & install, OR install alongside your current op-sys which I would recommend you may want to do (if your current op-sys is working ok) at first.

Why pay $11 for this disk?: Because thats peanuts compared to around $100, and it will boot right up without errors in my experience. I tried downloading my own as I have done before, and it did not want to boot for some reason. I wanted a "perfect" copy like this disc that I can use again whenever I want, and I hope to, a few times!

Conclusion: It may not need all the extra security & drive conditioning attention "Smoke & Mirrors" does, or run games, or S&M Office, but I have one version of that old system still around, which I think will get used for Turbo Tax again. And don't blame me for the name either, I did not tell them to put both of those things on the first screen! Does anyone remember the older sky-blue "chemtrail" screen with the sun hazed out, and the white lines all over on it? Hummm? I haven't been on the "other system" for months, believe it or not. Some programs I use my phone for, where Android is powered by.....Linux.

I cannot recommend this op-sys more highly. It works for all my daily needs, and I have been puttering around with hardware & software for some time. Its pretty easy to learn, you probably wont ever need to use the command line, as I dont.

title: I'm hoping this will be my miracle
text:
I just started taking it. I know it is too early to tell, but I really need help, I don't know what to do. I was diagnosed with De Quervain's syndrome in my right wrist (inside of wrist) last January, I have horrible inflammation/tenderness on the thumb side of the wrist and burning pain at the base of my right thumb when I extend the fingers. My doctor said to get a cortisone shot but I refuse to do that, I have been trying to find other things to get rid of it. For about the last 2 months the pain has also been in the right hand about a 1/2 inch to the right of the thumb and stays in about a 1/2 inch area, it is the most painful when I wake up and is the level of crying pain. Someone told me last March that it is thumb tendonitis and might be from mineral deficiency and suggested that I take high dose magnesium and Vitamin D3. I worked up to 1,200 mg. a day taking magnesium malate and was taking about 10,000 IU Vitamin D3. One day I took 3,000 mg. magnesium but did not get relief. I got tested for magnesium and Vitamin D deficiency and my levels are low and I stopped taking the Vitamin D as my calcium levels are really high. The D level was coming up but when I stopped taking it, it dropped. I have taken a lot of things to get improvement but nothing has helped: B6 P-5-P, methyl B12, ice, heat, infrared light therapy, self-massage, acupuncture, castor oil packs, olive oil packs, bromelain, high dose serrapeptase, homeopathic remedies/creams, colostrum, chondroitin sulfate/glucosamine, msm, copper bracelets, borax, baking soda, tart cherry juice concentrate, alfalfa, essential oils. I got an xray done but my doctor says it is normal.

I have a very high level of stress, I moved in with my dad a year ago to take care of him, he has alzheimers. I suspect that I have Leaky Gut, I am severely gluten intolerant, a mild intolerance to casein and sensitive to the nightshade vegetables. I am also hypothyroid. I have been gluten free a lot of times but more recently about 6 weeks, no dairy, cutting out rice and trying to eat healthy. I've done the Whole30 diet, the last time was in February but it didn't help the tendonitis. I don't know why the magnesium isn't helping or anything else that I have taken. As I said, I don't know what to do, I am not working and I don't have money to spend on more tests to see what is happening. I don't know if this product will work.

title: Essential Companion!  Excellent kit!
text:
UPDATE 4/4/17: This Key Chain has been hanging on the outside of my purse/bag every day since I purchased it back in August 2015! (It currently holds 7-2ml and 2-1ml bottles. See pics of well-loved pouch.) I still absolutely love it. It has held up well, no busted seams or over-stretched elastic.

I see where some reviewers are not happy. I wonder if this is due to a product change or purchased from a different seller than I did. Mine came from Everything Essential [[ASIN:B013GKMF7G Stylish Essential Oil Key Chain with 8 5/8 Dram (2 ml) Vials and Blank Labels - Fits Easily in a Purse or Makeup Bag - Carry Your Favorite Essential Oils Everywhere You Go! (Black/White Windsor)]]

Of note, my order contained only the case and eight 2ml brown bottles. No pipettes, labels, or removal tool... AND YET! I would buy it again for the current $12.95 price. I am in no way related to the seller - I just love this product.

ORIGINAL: Dang, I love this thing!
It comes with eight amber 2ml (5/8ths) dram glass bottles with black lids. Each with a small white lid label that can be applied.

Outside:
The outside is made of cloth and has a soft canvas feel. I received the blue/white windsor colored case. It is a very dark blue, nearly black.
A smooth-gliding black zipper wraps around three sides. It is attached to an approx 2" silver carabiner hook. The set up feels very sturdy.

Inside:
The inside has a dark blue background with white polka dots. Very cute! This is where there is eight black elastic loops for securing oil vials. Each 3/4" width elastic loop easily holds from 1ml (1/4 dram, 7/8") bottles *up to* 5ml (1.5"), too!
(Dram = 3.7ml, but a dram bottle is often called a 5ml.)
Further, the vials are protected from the zipper with a piece of soft piping that runs the full zipper length! This is a really nice extra feature!

I currently have this stocked with my favorite go-to oils and have it clipped to my bag. It is lightweight and much easier to haul around than a baggie or small satchel. I love that my bottles are secured, but still easy to access.

***Note: One trick I have found is to slide the bottles into the case elastic lid first. This prevents the elastic from hanging on the bottle lid.***

It is made in China.

title: Comparison between 2 Amazon 31 day pill organizers
text:
Pro's & Con's:

I am comparing this with the [[ASIN:B000RZPL0M MedCenter (70265) 31 Day Pill Organizer with Reminder System]]. I am a transplant recipient, so I really, really need a monthly pill case that is going to work for me. I cannot mess around--I take about 16 pills in the am and about 12 at night every day. My survival and that of my transplant depend on me getting my meds right, and consistent. I previously have used the 70265 31 Day Pill Organizer for the last several years, but it was getting a little old, so I tried to mix things up. Here is how they compare:

Pro's: This one is much more compact
All of my pills fit in there (barely!) and 16 pills is a lot!
Nice pill splitter & pill crusher, though I currently don't need it--still nice to have
Does not take up much space on a counter and very lightweight when full
Daily pill cases open easily
MUCH less expensive than the other one

Con's: The pill cases are much smaller than the other one-- makes it precarious to fit all pills
Filling each pill case is a bit hard, because the individual day cases do NOT stand up by themselves, unlike the picture
Bottom is uneven and angled, so case wobbles and falls over unless leaned against something
Looks in the picture like it is a lazy susan you can spin, but it is not
Lids are so loose that I am worried they will pop open on their own--one did so while empty the first day (see picture)

I've attached several photos so you can see for yourself. If you look at the bottom left hand side of the last picture, you can see where one of the boxes popped open by itself just sitting in the carrier. It was empty, but that would suck if it does that when it is full of pills. Overall, I like this one, but if I had it to do over again, I'd try a different one or re-buy the larger box.
