title: Good for acneic/mature skin/and cold sores
text:
Update 9/16/2021:
Still repurchasing this oil because it is the best geranium oil I've tried; however, I bought the biggest bottle available last December and it was more sweet smelling than normal. I didn't love it. I'm not sure if it was just that particular batch, but I went back to purchasing the smaller $18.99 bottle because the scent has historically been a bit more sultry.

On a funny note, I was staying with one of my friends and she 'borrowed' some of this oil before bedtime. She used WAY too much and applied it directly to her face and body. The scent was so powerful that her fiance and dog didn't want to be in the same room with her! Always dilute with a carrier oil. A little goes a long way :)
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Update 10/5/2019:
I am still loving this oil. It is my HG forever. I moved overseas last year and stocked up on this geranium oil. Now that I live in Ireland, I’m subjected to far more cold/windy/rainy days. Introducing cold sores - hooray! Anyway, this stuff works wonders on them. I dilute with my Argan oil or dab a bit on a qtip before using a gentle lip balm, and it really helps minimize swelling and oozing. Cold sores didn’t really even get big enough to be noticeable! Just be sure to moisturize the EFF out of your lips after applying geranium as it has a slight drying effect. So not only has this oil completely obliterated my acne, it also keeps the cold sores in check.

_____________________________________
Dang, y'all. This oil is boss. I put a drop or two onto a cotton ball with a bit of safflower oil each night and use it to cleanse my face. My skin has never looked better! I've been struggling with acne for over 20 years, so that's really saying something. Cystic acne off an on for the last 5-6 years. This stuff seriously balances me out and keeps breakouts at bay. My scars are also (slowly) starting to fade.

--------------
Update: February 2019

I stopped using this at some point after feeling like I had my skin under control and slowly my problems returned. I am always trying new things, so I'm positive I also changed other things about my skin care routine during this time. I was using safflower oil as cleanser and ACV toner and that cleared things up somewhat, but my skin was a little dried out. I also moved to Ireland recently and the cold weather made things worse. text:
Pros:
These crutches feel really sturdy and unlike other crutches, they are quiet when you walk with them. The handles feel strong and the rubber tips have held up with quite a bit of use, even when walking on asphalt roads. Forearm crutches tend to be very pricey so finding a pair under $50 is an amazing deal.

Cons:
I bought these in the youth size and while they were shorter than adult crutches, they didn't seem particularity catered to smaller people. I'm 5'0 tall and have to have the cuff to handle length adjusted to the smallest setting and it's still a bit too long, I could see this being a major problem for someone even smaller than me. The other part that seemed inappropriately sized were the cuffs. They're no smaller than the cuffs on the adult size crutches and my arms easily slip right out the front. For me, this personally isn't a huge deal but for others, I know that's a bit more of a problem. The only other complaint is that the handles could be a more comfortable material/shape but you can't expect much when you go for the cheapest model. And they're not the worst handles ever either.

Overall, I do like these and will continue to use them as long as they hold up for me. They're not the fanciest crutches you'll ever use but they will help you get from point A to point B with confidence.

title: A make-over from  Cold/Sterile to Soft/Decorative in a quick 5 minutes
text:
I'm really glad I selected the leaf motive with its variegated pattern. The SoClean container has rounded corners. The decals were really well thought out to match up the flat pieces without gaps that were not planned for. I recommend planning out your project steps before beginning. I was unsure which side was considered left and which one was considered right. By starting with a piece that was was symmetrical, it made for an enjoyable and quick project. I started with the piece labeled Front. It had a notched out space for the control panel. After attaching it, I continued with another piece that was not questionable: the top. I made sure the decal was aligned with the edge and well centered. The print of the decal reminded me of wallpaper. The alignment is especially important anywhere there will be an adjacent piece. The right side and the left side were those adjacent pieces. In the end, my idea of right & left was not what the manufacturer had intended. Starting with front and top kept my misconception from becoming a mistake. The decals come off well, and remained intact, not tearing or peeling. Like wallpaper and large decals, air gets trapped underneath. To avoid that, I aligned an edge, then pushed outward from the middle of the decal and smoothing outward pushing out air along the way. The 5 main pieces were easy to apply and only a little air was trapped. It came out easily by either pushing the bubble toward the closest edge, or lifting the decal and smoothing it again.

The last of the pieces to apply were the small strips around the sides of the lid, the skinny strips. To my delight, the print matched up really well. It was not perfect, but it didn't matter. I only had one spot that ended up with a little bit of wrinkles. It didn't bother me becuase of the busy pattern, and the fact that the SoClean has a rounded body being wrapped in a flat decal. It was bound to happen. I call that a WIN!

The leaf print is a nice crisp green leafy pattern over a stark white background. It dresses up the bedside "equipment" and makes it look like a decorative item. And with the green and white, it should be extremely versatile, just like a plant in a white container would be. I know I made the perfect choice for me. I highly recommend it!

title: Took some getting used to but now I love it!
text:
It took me a little while to get used to this(like a couple days) but now I can't imagine going back to a regular non-powered toothbrush!!
My first couple day I wasn't a fan of this, of course I reaally wanted to be, but the vibrating had me flinching away from it! However I finally figured out that part of was that I kept turning it on before putting it in my mouth and having it in position first seemed to help me. Of course part of it is also just getting used to the vibrating I did find the massage setting the easiest to get used to.

The toothbrush came in a very pretty white with a blue inner box that I really liked. Inside was the toothbrush fit into it's spot with the cup was on top as well and the charger base directly below.

Set up was beyond simple as all you do is connect the toothbrush head to the base, plug in charger, put the cup on top(optional) and set the toothbrush on that. Once it's set on top you see the red light come on. I'm still amazed it's really that simple, and that it actually charges like that!!
I did leave it on the charger for a day but that's mainly cause I didn't realize it had finished already!

I really love this toothbrush, it feels good on my gums and it helps me make sure I split my brushing up equally. I was surprised to find I normally brush for about a minute and a half already as I always worry I don't take long enough!
Now that i'm used to this toothbrush I don't think i'll ever go back to a normal one!
One other tip i've found is to just let the brush do the work for you(which is hard for me still), go slowly and you don't need to press very much(it will harshly buzz against your teeth when you press to hard). I have the hardest time with this when moving from the different surfaces(front, inbetween and inside).

I received this for free or at a discount for my honest and unbiased review. I write reviews in the hope that mine can be helpful to someone else. If you did find this helpful please click that little button below, it helps sellers know you like what I have to say!

title: I love essential oils
text:
I love essential oils. I use them a lot, but often, especially buying them online, I am not sure of what I am buying. The only thing I can do to know if an essential oil is good is doing the paper test, and of course I did this test on Radha Lemon Essential Oil 100% pure and natural, and it passed the test greatly (I posted the photos of the test). If an oil is synthetic or it is cut with other vegetables carrier oils the stain on the paper stays there long and it leaves an oily stain for more than a day. The pure essential oil instead evaporates after a while leaving the paper almost totally clean (but the odor lasts). This test, however, does not tell us all we need to know, and we need also other information that are usually reported on the bottle like how the oil is being extracted for example.
As known, citrus oils extraction is cold pressed, and it is not steam distilled: indeed, the oil is extracted from the vesicles peel. Radha lemon oil is cold pressed.
Also, a pure essential oil is really strong, and it must be used diluted in a carrier oil. If on the bottle you find this indication, you are pretty sure you are using a good essential oil. This oil is only for external use.

I would like to add that citrus oils are phototoxic, so do not take sun for 12 hours after using this oil on your skin, and better using a sun protection when you are in the sun.

I used this oil for aromatherapy and to make a perfume: in both cases I was satisfied.
Even if this oil is bottled in US, the country of origin is Italy. As known, citrus from Italy are very high quality.
I received this product for free in exchange of a honest and unbiased review.

Just took this on a trip to Argentina/Peru. We had to double mask a few times and the structure made it really functional as the outer mask.

title: I was super excited to try this straightening brush out this morning
text:
I was super excited to try this straightening brush out this morning. I love the look of straight hair but the process of showering, blow drying, and then using a flat iron took too much time from this nursing student. I was looking for a product that would allow me to shower at night, air dry my hair while sleeping, and then straighten it in the morning and so far, I think I've found it.

I have very fine hair, but a lot of it. The apalus brush did a good job straightening my hair. It took a couple of passes to figure out what I was doing but once I got the hang of it, everything was great. Instead of using my fingers to hold the section of hair I was going to straighten, I used my brush which ensured no tangles and it worked well for me.

My only complaint so far is towards the end, the brush kept shutting off. I don't know if I was accidentally pushing the power button or if it was the auto shut off feature the brush comes with. Whatever it was, it got frustrating and kind of annoying to have to keep Turing the brush back on and waiting for it to return to the selected heat setting. Other than that, I am very pleased with this straightening brush.

title: COULDN'T SURVIVE WITHOUT IT.
text:
I needed to place a cold ice on my knee as long a period as possible because II had total knee replacement and need to keep swelling down. Well Ice from the freezer placed in a freezer bag did not cut the muster because the ice could not be distributed over the entire area and I had to hold the ice on because it would slip off because the ice would melt and turn to water then warm up from my hot knee. So to was a constant trek between the freezer and the sink to pour the water out of the bag and replenish the ice in the bag. There was wasted time doing other things when I should be cooling my knee.
So this Aqua Relief System had eliminated all of the wasted time above. You put as much ice inside the unit and fill it with water to the maximum fill line, attach your pad to the hose, wrap around knee, turn the unit on and set to the cooling time, then relax , it will auto shut off according to the set time. No more running to the freezer during treatment for ice.. After one hour the unit still had cold ice in it.

The only problem I had was the small cooling/heating pad that came with it , so I ordered a larger one.
This unit is very light to carry around , It has holes for attaching a shoulder strap. It is also very quiet to operate. In fact the low hum of the motor caused me to fall asleep.
I recommend to anyone needing cold therapy or heating therapy that needs continuous treatment for at least an hour without interruptions.

title: Nice and easy, but short on functionality
text:
This scale was a breeze to set up with my existing home WiFi, synced easily to the Fitbit app, and is pleasing to look at. BUT. Compared to the Withings (available for about $10 more if you look around) it's short on functionality. First, the only readings you get are weight and body fat percent. NOT BMI. Some other reviewers have mentioned BMI, but it's not. It's body fat percent, which is not the same.

Then there's the issue of compatibility with various fitness apps. Maybe because it's so new, but it just didn't deliver in terms of talking to various apps. I like Lose It for my meal tracking (it syncs to Fitbit, and is WAY friendlier to use with barcode scans etc) but the Aria doesn't talk to it, and the Withings does.

So if you're in the market for a high-end fitness scale that looks like a sleek piece of white or black glass on your bathroom floor -- compare features and functionality carefully between this and the Withings. Look carefully at the lists of compatible apps and data tracking. Both work well with Fitbit, but I think for the price you'll get more bang for your buck with Withings.

That being said ... the 3rd party seller (Brookstone) were **awesome** in the customer service zone for my return. Very smooth.

title: One of these is not like the others
text:
This does not smell like real lemon essential oil. I have DoTerra and Eden's Garden lemon oil and compared the scent to these. While the Doterra and Eden's Garden both smell like a fresh cut lemon, Radha does not.It smells like lemon scented cleaner. It is lemony, but not the fresh cut lemon like the more trusted brands.

Also I like to add a drop of lemon oil to a glass of water. The doterra and Edens Garden diffuse through and the water tastes like I squeezed a fresh lemon in it.The Rhadha does not diffuse or taste correct.

I see that it passes the paper test. That only shows that whatever it is, it isn't diluted with a carrier oil. I am not sure what it is. Perhaps it is lemon oil stored or extracted poorly. Perhaps it is something else.

There is a group of people on FB who group fund 3rd party testing. Perhaps if there is enough interest Radha can be tested. As there is no real regulation for Essential Oils, we often find oils labeled pure and therapeutic which are something other than what they claim to be.

title: Once you start using this bottle, you will have a hard time sleeping without it!
text:
Got this after receiving a recommendation for an external warming device for camping in near 20 degree weather. I tried it out at home first and learned several very important things: Your bed retains warmth even after your spouse moves it, it stays warm over 24 hours if buried in a heavy down comforter, if the water is scalding hot then it generates an amazing amount of heat for many hours, and it is the best camp buddy.

Well camping in 20° weather recently, I filled this up with 140° water and threw it in my 20° sleeping bag. I normally use a Reactor liner, wool socks and a knit cap plus fleece PJs. At 2 AM, It was way too hot. I sleep cold and this was literally the first time I had to remove the liner, my socks and air the sleeping bag out. I actually thought I was suffocating from the heat.

Does it work? Will you kick yourself for forgetting it when you go on a business trip and have to stay in a hotel for several days? Will you wonder how you got along without it all these years? Will your spouse complain it is too warm in the bed? Will your child ask for his own bottle because it is so nice in bed? Will your spouse laugh that you were giving a five star review for a hot water bottle?

Absolutely.

I never give five stars unless it is really useful. It is really really really useful.

One minor issue, I noticed that the knit sleeve is starting to tear. It is only been two months so not sure how long it will last before I have to sew it or try some repairs.

title: Decent For A Season w/ Care...
text:
This item was purchased to replace a Braun Series 7 that broke after many, many years of use. With that said, here's my review of the Sonax Pro 5 In 1.

It took considerably longer to achieve the same results as my former Braun. It took multiple passes to trim up an area (to my desired length), which became frustrating after some time.

PROs:
-Its super light weight.
-Comfortably fits in my hand. (I've got really small hands).
-Multiple attachments for multiple areas.
-USB Charging (Lasts me 2 full pelvic trimmings - 50 min).
-Able to use eyebrow trimmer attachment (without guide) to trim up men's pesky ear hair.
-Wet / Dry use.
-Great for travel.

CONs:
-Body is made of plastic.
-Flimsy - doesn't feel like it would hold up to accidental drops.
-Nose trimmer blades are loose. Must insert blades into head casing, which may be a safety hazard (if not careful you can cut your fingers).
-Takes 6-8 hours of charging to get full use of the battery.
-Doesn't come with a storage case.
-Takes long to achieve desired results.

In conclusion, you get what you pay for. It gets the job done, but not as efficiently as better-grade equipment (like my former Braun). You may get a season or two out of this item, but I wouldn't count on years-long use.

title: Quick and easy miracle for thick hair!
text: This thing is a miracle for my long, super thick, wavy/frizzy hair. Initially, I ordered the "other" cheaper straightening brush (the one you see everywhere available in pink or white). There is no way to use it without turning it off or changing the temperature since the controls are on the side of the handle....duh! Not to mention, it is smaller and doesn't heat up nor get as hot as this one. I promptly returned it and ordered this one. I have a great flatiron but with all my hair it takes forever so I rarely use it. Most of the time when I wash my hair, I use a ton of conditioner and after rinsing use a bit more conditioner and comb it through my hair and leave it in and let dry naturally. The way, it is curly but if I brush, it stands out about a foot all around. I had resigned myself to just letting it dry curly and usually put it in a ponytail. With this, after it's dry, I just brush through slowly, layer by layer and it looks amazing. Even with my thick hair, I am done in about 10 minutes. I have let a few friends try it and they were so impressed, they ordered one too. If you are looking for perfection in straightening and don't mind spending half a day to get it, stick with your flatiron but I run a dog rescue and don't have the time. If you are considering a straightening brush, don't hesitate...this one ROCKS!

And while the brush gets really hot, the barrel is almost too smooth, as your hair gets really smoothed out as well - this can make your hairstyle look flat and droopy though:/ The method I've figured out that seems to work the best, is to use as small a grouping of hair as possible, and to leave it curled for at least 20 seconds. Unfortunately this can make curling your hair take longer than expected...sigh! And I thought the wide barrel at 1 1/2 inches would produce more natural curls, which it does, but the larger size seems to be harder for your hair to hold the curl, 1 1/4 inches would have been better. Would I buy this brush again? Absolutely, as it works as promised for the most part; perhaps it's my expectations that need to be revised as I hoped I could have used a larger section of hair while curling, instead it just takes longer to achieve the desired effect. One point to note, my hair is really porous and on the frizzy side, so it might work better on hair that's not as unruly as mine.

title: Decent Product--Time will tell.
text: I used this for 12-in ceramic tile.  I only had 3 spare tiles from the tile installation, and had already used those.  I noticed grout breaking up at a corner and found a total of 10 tiles, roughly in a square, that sounded hollow.  I drilled one hole on each side initially.  My one little tube did not do the job.  It is only 10 oz. and there is significant waste with adhesive exiting the holes.  I had trouble getting the product to easily flow under the tile as shown in the video.  I wound up drilling more holes until I got what seemed adequate coverage underneath.  After 24 hrs, about half of the tiles still had spots that sounded hollow.  I drilled 32 holes total.  I used a 1/4-in. masonry bit which jammed frequently when trying to drill.  (The tiles are set with those little spacers which are not exactly 1/4 inch. )  A 3/16-in. bit MIGHT work better, but I did not have this size. The tiles are down much better than before.  Hope they last.  Expect one tube to treat 3-4 tiles.  My job took 3 tubes.  The adhesive seems a lot like Elmer's glue in flow characteristics and tackiness.  Cutting the applicator tip is important.  It needs to fit snug inside the drilled hole without bottoming out.  Start with a narrow tip and shave off slices until you get it right.

title: Works on fingers and toes! Game changer.
text:
[[VIDEOID:60113d9fe849cfe6248fa74dfed0bdc1]] Summary: As a person who bites their nails, plays with knives, and regularly cuts their toenails too short these are a game changer. They keep a bandaid on easily, keep water out, and reduce pain from an injured finger.

Background: I cut off a chunk of my middle finger two days ago at work, and they gave me a bandaid and a blue "finger condom" as they called it. It immediately made my life easier. I had painful cuts on two other fingers from a woodworking project and cut one of my toenails too short (causing slight pain to walk lol), so I figured these would come in handy.

Shipping: I ordered them at around 3 am on nov 9 with 2 day shipping, they came nov 10 (1 day early. That was nice!) They came in a white box (pictured) sealed in plastic.

Sizing: they are a little over two inches long, so they don't make it all the way to the base of my longest finger but do on the others. They snugly fit on all my fingers and toes, but are a bit tight on my thumb and big toe. At work I use medium sized vinyl glove. For further size reference, I am female with average sized hands and abnormally long toes. I cut one of the cots shorter for my thumb (see last photo) and it is no longer too tight.

Material/durability: these are made of latex, and seem to be about as thick as a typical latex glove. They seem pretty durable. I tested it by both slicing and poking it with a knife (seen in video). It is obviously not cut proof but it took a fair amount of pressure with a knife to slice through it, and I dragged it across the serrated edge and it did not break. It took a relatively hard poke to make a hole. For the price, they are much more durable than I expected. The latex has a pretty good grip on everything, but that may go down with longer use. They do not roll up my finger at all. Even the one I cut short is staying on my thumb with no problem. With no bandaid they work with a touch screen, but with a band aid on underneath it it is harder to use the touch screen.

All in all, pretty amazing for the price. If you are bigger than a size medium in gloves/id you are a grown man I'd recommend getting these ones in a larger size.

title: Treating Gill Flukes, Bath Method
text:
I read on a couple internet forums that this product can be used to treat Praziquantel resistant Gill Flukes.

These forums quoted a book called
Fish Disease: Diagnosis and Treatment 2nd Edition
By: Edward J. Noga

I downloaded this 500+ page book. The picture I've included with this review is directly from that book showing the treatment methods and correct dosing using Fenbendazole.

I reached out to Thomas Labs to ask if they'd heard about this bath method, about its safety, and if they recommend it.
They did not respond.

After 21 days of Seachem Paragaurd (WCs every other day) and 10 days of Prazipro (WCs every three days and redosing) didnt work I started looking for some serious help. I will clarify that both medications did help temporarily relieve symptoms only to have them come back almost immediately after treatment.

I used the 12 hour bath treatment on my Betta fish. I will do a second bath treatment 7 days later to be sure they're all gone.

I was extremely nervous about doing this bath as I had limited knowledge of others using this treatment safely.

My Betta showed no serious signs of stress. I did observe some yawning, a couple of deep breaths where her gills went out slightly further than a normal breath and she did dart about (flashed) very briefly 4/5 hours in. She swam about like she normally does and readily accepted food 5 hours in. Some of the medication settled in the tank and I did have to stir it up again every hour or so.

"Fenbendazole works by binding to the beta-tubulin within the microtubules and inhibiting their formation, resulting in disruption of cell division. This potent disruption blocks the parasite's ability to produce energy, starving the parasite until it dies.
What makes fenbendazole unique is that it is more attracted to parasite beta-tubulin than that of the animal being treated. " Merck Animal Health Oct 2018

When medicating your fish make sure to have a separate clean tank set up to transfer the fish into if there are adverse reactions to the medication and for when you've finished treatment.
To get rid of Flukes in your aquarium, let your display tank run for a minimum of three weeks, heated and filtered normally before reintroducing your fish.

title: They really work!
text:
I bought these as my feet are often cold. I am a professional athlete and have a very low blood pressure and a resting heart rate of below 40. So when I need to sit still in front of the computer, cold feet are almost inevitable. In addition, for health reasons I keep the temperature in my house below 70 F. I was looking for a solution to cold feet for some time, and best I found so far were woolen socks and a yoga mat under my table.
I was quite skeptical when I got these slippers, but from the first moment they were really convincing. First off, the slippers themselves are well made. The material they are made of is sturdy and yet soft and comfortable. On the inside, the fabric is even softer, slightly padded. They have an adjustable opening that doesn’t open too far (I am a size 12) so that you have to slip in first until your toes touch the front, then pull up the part that covers your heels. Once done, they fit nicely and sit snugly on your feet.
The energy for the heating comes from two standard charging batteries, as you would also get to charge your phone on the go. They come with a dual USB-C cable so that you can charge both batteries using only one USB outlet. The charging time is about 1 h. Then you have to connect the batteries via a cable and put them in a small pocket for each slipper that sits on top. of it. They are rather easy to insert in the pocket. I was surprised how comfortable the slippers were even after inserting the batteries; they just add a light weight on top of your foot, which you very soon forget about.
The slippers have a button on the outside that you push to switch them on. They have three settings indicated by three different colors. I kept them on the highest level and had them on for an hour a day. The batteries lasted for three days. That is good enough for me as already after ten minutes my feet began to be nice and warm. The good thing is, when you are physically fit as I am, it’s enough to get your feet warm. Once they are warmed up, and the arteries are widened, they manage to stay warm without any additional help.
If you suffer from cold feet, I can recommend these slippers. They are well made, they work, the batteries are ok, and they absolutely do the job they promised to do.

title: Effective for controlling histaminic reactions to foods
text:
This product works well for me to counteract unpleasant reactions I have to certain foods. With DAOsin I can usually eat them with little problem. I'm histadelic and thus have a low tolerance for known high-histamine foods (avocado, lemon, tomato, eggplant, banana, vinegar, red wine, cheese, sardines, etc.), especially during allergy season (when my histamine levels can already be sky-high). Previously, even with anti-histamines and methionine, I had to limit my diet very carefully to minimize burning eyes, a stinging tongue, sinus headaches, itchy skin, sneezing fits, nausea, and insomnia. However, I've learned that DAO (diamine oxydase) doesn't just block histamine receptors in the body like antihistamines or break it down after it's already gotten into your bloodstream like methionine; DAO actually helps digest and break down excess histamine in your GI tract BEFORE it can be absorbed and released into the blood stream and cause unpleasant reactions.

DAOsin even works fairly well for me if I forget and take it AFTER eating. Using it along with methionine (an essential amino acid) and an OTC antihistamine, I can actually sleep soundly and allergy-free when the pollen counts are high. I would have given DAOsin five stars, but it is expensive and has lots of excipients (extra inactive ingredients). It makes allergy-free meals pretty costly, and I'm a little concerned about all the added chemicals that I can't even pronounce - the company says these extra ingredients are in very small quantities and serve as binders and slow the release of the DAO so that it reaches your small intestine. I have not found any other high-potency DAO products that don't have a similar number of extra ingredients.

The deciding factor for me was that it is clearly stated on the label that DAOsin is "Made in Austria", whereas other potent DAO products often don't state their actual origin - "manufactured by", (worse) "manufactured for", and (the worst) "distributed by" do NOT indicate WHERE the product was actually MADE. For example, a nutrient corporate office in North America may own a factory in Asia, where their products are made by cheap labor without any assurance of quality control, but they can still label the product "Manufactered by" this American company. The question remains: "Manufactured by you WHERE?" That can be guaranteed only with "MADE IN..."

Histame, another DAO product, lists very few excipients on its label, but it also contains MUCH less DAO than DAOsin, forcing me to take three to four times as many of Histame's larger capsules (why are they so big then?) to get the same results as one or two very small DAOsin capsules. In the long run, this makes Histame just as expensive or more than DAOsin. I haven't done the calculations yet, but a bottle of 30 Histames runs out a lot faster on me than a bottle of 30 DAOsin capsules.

I hope this helps! And no, I don't work for or know anyone at Swanson in the US or the DAOsin company in Austria.

title: Handy Device But With a Price Tag
text:
First up I wanted to state that I don't personally have trouble with my hearing. So I had to get some other people to help me with the review. Think we came up with some good points. And here is what we found.
First up, this isn't an item intended to replace a hearing aid. It's more for people who are in the in between stage of still hearing alright, but could use a boost because of minor issues.
Setup is easy. You find a channel on your TV. Only takes a matter of minutes. The device has four modes: Relax, Talk, Listen, and Watch.

Relax is a mode where you listen to relaxing sounds. Nothing special. And not worth buying the device for. You can get a free app like this on any smart phone.
Talk mode is when you're trying to have a conversation in a loud environment. Like a crowded room. I had a couple people help me test this. Worked fine.
Listen mode is for talking on a cell phone. It's got an annoying latency issue. But that was probably made worse by the fact I could hear the other person in the other room anyway. Still it does increase volume like it was made for.
Watch mode is for watching television in a loud environment. Here is where it really shines. It amplifies the TV volume really nicely.

All in all a good device. A bit pricey, but how can you put a price tag on your hearing? Recommended.

Another thing that stood out was how quiet the toy was.  I was expecting it to be loud  like my fiances massager but it was fairly quiet. I dont regret buying this whatsoever or any of their other products. Its nice having such a variety of textures within their male massagers too. text: I like these sensory bracelets.  They're extremely stretchy and will be easy to get on and off.  The bright colors are appealing and the spikey protrusions offer good sensory interaction. title: Not Great
text: This Vonexx trimmer works, but not all that well.  The unit is fairly lightweight, with a lot of plastic in the construction, and it feels to be of average quality.  With the attachments on, it seems to do okay.  I trimmed my beard without any real issues using the 9mm attachment.  It doesn't snag and trims effectively.  The biggest problem is that it doesn't trim well without attachments.  When I use the trimmer alone (no attachments) to try to shape the edge of my beard and to clean up loose whiskers, it snags and doesn't cut cleanly.  It can't really get a good clean line around my beard with it.  Overall, for this reason,  it's not great and not recommended.

title: Good But Too Expensive
text: My sister-in-law is a physician and has recommended to our family that we take NAC daily as a precaution in case anyone gets Covid.  She believes that it will help to keep symptoms milder and enable our bodies to fare better if we get it.  I'm happy with this NAC supplement, but ultimately wonder if it's worth the very high price.  The capsules are moderately sized and are easy to swallow.  They also have significantly less odor that other brands of NAC I've used - and this is a supplement that can have a really off-putting smell.  These appear to be of good quality and are made to high standards, but the price is really high compared to most other brands.  It's hard to recommend these due to the high price unless you have an allergy to some certain ingredient common to other less-expensive brands.  Very good but very pricey.

title: Good C
text: My physician sister-in-law suggested to our family that we take vitamin C daily as a preventative to combat covid - not that it will keep us from getting it, but she said she thinks it's helpful in maintaining a healthy system to fight it.  I decided to get liposomal C over traditional regular C after reading about it's much better absorption.  Happy with this brand.  The 2 capsule dose is easy to take, with the capsules being of average size and without any noticeable odor.  Haven't experienced any aftertaste or ill effects.  The ingredients seem to be of good quality: vegan, gmo & gluten free, GMP certified, no artificial ingredients, etc.  I also appreciate that it's made in the USA.  Good C!

title: Good but You Need to Order Smaller Thank Suggested
text: These ankle compression sleeves are of good quality, but to get them tight enough for my liking you'll need to order a size or two smaller than they suggest.  Based on their measurement chart, I needed the large ankle sleeve.  I ordered medium, and even it is not as tight as I want it to be.  I have bad ankles that are very prone to sprains, so I'm especially careful to try and have maximum support.  If you're just looking for some moderate compression, you make be okay with one size smaller.  Either way I'd down-size at least a bit.  The material is nice and stretchy, has good thickness, and is breathable.  I'm happy with them despite wishing I'd gone another size lower.

title: Good Ingredients, Not So Good Taste
text: I like the ingredient combination in this liquid.  I've taken various blends of glucosamine, chondroitin, etc. for quite awhile for moderated age-related arthritis and found it helpful.  Though this is a good formula, unfortunately I am not a fan of the flavor.  It's sickly sweet with a medicinal flavor that's just not very palatable.  I will finish the bottle since I've got it, but I won't be getting it again based strictly on the taste.

title: Okay
text: I like these Zilly ear plugs okay.  They do a good job of making painfully loud events bearable and not painful.  I got them after going to a concert several months ago that was so loud I couldn't enjoy it.  These will be effective to avoid that situation next time.  As far as fidelity and clarity, they're so-so.  They are better than a pair of foam earplugs that just muffle and dampen everything, but they're not noticeably great on clarity and the claims of high fidelity seem exaggerated to me.  Overall they're good for sound reduction but only fair on sound quality.

title: Pretty Good
text: This was my first foray into a keto creamer and I like it pretty well.  I was expecting something that actually seemed like creamer, but this really just feels more like putting oil in your coffee at first.  I have found with repeated uses, however, that it does accomplish what creamer does to a degree.  It makes the coffee a little smoother and less pungent.  It also adds a bit of sweetness, and I'm grateful it's not overly sweet.  One packet seems about as sweet as perhaps a half packet of stevia.  The french vanilla flavor I got is also pleasant.  Ultimately you won't mistake this for heavy cream in your coffee, but it's a pretty decent substitute if you want a non-dairy option that's good for keto.

title: Great Taste & Nutrition
text: I like the keto bars a lot.  They have a very natural taste thanks to the quality ingredients - lots of seeds, nuts, and other such natural items.  The fact that they use monk fruit instead of erythritol or stevia gives them a much more natural tasting sweetness.  The texture is chewy and nutty and the flavors are really good.  Good healthy keto snack!

title: Okay But Could Be Better
text:
I've used breathe-right strips in the past to help get better airflow through my nose while sleeping. They work well but the cost becomes a burden since they're disposable. Decided to try a nasal dilator and got this. I see the potential and it work somewhat, but it needs improvement.
The first issue is the little tab that holds the two dilators together. It's super short and keeps me from being able to insert the pieces far enough into my nostrils. I ended up cutting the strip and separating the dilators, which helped a bit. The second problem is that the tubes need to be a little longer for my nose. They don't reach quite far enough into my nose to completely open up the airways. Thirdly, I find the blue filter inserts to be counter productive. They reduce airflow, which is already the issue they seek to fix. I got rid of them immediately. The last thing is that these don't always stay in my nose overnight. The extra-big ends that remain outside of the nostrils keep them from getting a good tight seal for me.
Despite the above complaints, these still help. They might work better for someone with a smaller nose. Ideally the tubes would come with plenty of length and could be trimmed to size to fit the users nose more suitably. These are okay, but could be better.

title: Good Quality Household Gloves
text: I'm very happy with these household gloves.  I got them for use doing house cleaning and for changing my car's oil (where they keep my hands clean and give me good grip).  These are of good quality, with sturdy durable material that has a nice bit of flex and good grip.  I like that two pair are thinner with a little more tactile response and two pair are lined for added comfort, protection, and/or warmth.  The length is long enough to cover beyond the wrist and to go over long sleeves.  The sizing is also accurate: I have medium-large male hands and the mediums in these fit me snugly  and also work well for my wife and her smaller hands.  Very happy with these all around.

title: Excellent Cleansing and Wonderful Aroma
text: This organic shampoo goes on easily, with a thick, rich feel that lathers up nicely.  It rinses clean, leaving none of the tacky residue that some shampoos do.  I love the fragrance.  It's a strong herbal blend of patchouli, frankincense, balsam, cucumber, and other oils that give it a very natural and unique aroma.  Though strong, once rinsed it doesn't leave behind too much of a scent but just a pleasant hint.  It leaves my hair feeling very clean and manageable without drying it out.  Overall, I like it a lot, and particularly appreciate the organic ingredients that forgo the usual laundry list of chemical ingredients.

text: I broke my left foot three years ago and ever since it's needed a wide shoe. These heel grips are absolutely wonderful! Finally my heel stays in place and I can walk around very comfortably knowing I'm not going to walk out of my own shoes. The grips are not very padded, so the actual shoe size doesn't change. It has this ridge of padding at the top that secures the heel into the shoes. I've tried all types of thick heel grips which shorten the length of the shoes causing my toes to be jammed into the toe bed of the shoes, making it extremely uncomfortable and my heels still would slip out. I highly recommend these grips if your foot tends to be wider than your heel and your heel slips in and out of your shoes. It's been magical wearing my beautiful pumps again!

title: Decent Mask
text:
This is a pretty decent sleep mask. It fits my head well and the strap and mask are pretty comfortable. It does press on the bridge of my nose a bit, but it's not that bad. It blocks out all light through the mask but it does stick out just a bit around my nose and let's a little bit of light in. I don't feel any pressure around my eyes with this mask on and I have slept with it comfortable multiple nights.

I have noticed a difference while wearing this as quite a bit of light comes into my bedroom in the mornings and I usually wake up a couple times after dawn before I actually want to get up. With this mask, I have been sleeping a couple hours past first light every time so it's definitely helpful. The earplugs are pretty basic but do work well to block out a lot of sound, however, I don't need, and don't like to sleep with, earplugs in so I'm not sure how comfortable they are over long periods of time.

Overall, this is a good sleep set. The mask also folds up nicely and is very small when folded. For the price, if you're looking to try out a sleep mask, I would definitely recommend this.

title: Small Business Maid Compared to Regular Microfiber Cloths
text:
I splurged on these because I wanted to see if they were worth the hype - because if they were, I was going to buy a lot more for my cleaning business. They are plenty-thick, good-quality microfiber cloths - but, they are not much different than more affordable brands, even just the 'Rubbermaid' brand in most department stores, etc. I also tried the e-cloth brand. My opinion is the same regarding them.

Apparently, these cloths are treated so that they don't mildew up and smell - but, I don't leave my wet microfiber cloths in a heap for that to happen to begin with. I wash & dry them - and if I can't get to that right away, I rinse them out by hand and hang them to dry until I have time to wash them. My other cheaper, but still just-as-good-quality microfiber cloths don't stink. The 'special treatment' these cloths receive are not worth the extra money, in my opinion.

Also there is no on/off switch, so only plug/unplug.
Nevertheless, if it had been quieter, I would probably leave it on at all times.

It only eliminates odors and probably also germs, so don't expect it to filter air all-around -- dusts, mites, and other allergens will still be in the air.

I am no stranger to enjoying healthy and earthly tastes that lack the high-spike pleasure, being satisfied with the health benefits and immediate effect on my internal system. When I first tried Kombucha, it was an acquired taste that I did not care for at first, but it had given me an immediate euphoric feeling of well-being, and the way it invigorated my intestines and esophagus was very delightful. Over a short period of time, the taste of Kombucha grew on me, as I learned to enjoy the uniqueness of the taste alongside of the great health benefits.

This schisandra product is my first schisandra product that I have ever tried. And right away, I experienced its strength and potency working on my internal system, telling me by its immediacy, that this has to be an effective product. Though I don't think the taste will grow on me in the long run like Kombucha, I know I will continue to take it for its health benefits, and that the taste really is not something that bad; a lack of satisfying pleasure as to its taste, yes; but the taste itself is not horrible or unbearable.

I took my watch to a local jeweler, who wanted $100 to send the watch off to a repair facility to have the battery replaced.  I instead ordered a watch repair kit and this battery and did the job myself saving over 50 bucks and now I have a nice repair kit for future use also. title: Just what I needed to relieve the metatarsal pain on my left foot!
text:
Not sure what i did to cause it, but I started to experience immense discomfort on my right foot, around the 2nd and 3rd largest toes. before heading to the podiatrist, I did some research and found that strategically placed pad could help take the pressure off of these toes, so i could walk with relatively less pain. This products came with a right and left side slip on ace bandage like sleeve with a gel insert sewn in and also 2 gel pads that I am assuming could be affixed inside a shoe as well.

I wanted something that i could just slip on under my sock, put on my shoe and go without a lot of shifting and that is what this product did for me. I would slide on the left pad; there was a hole for my big toe and then another for the rest of them.

There was some occasional discomfort felt at the stitching between my big toe and the next largest toe, but it was a tolerable give for the relieve the pad gave me! I was able to go out walking around and shopping again with considerable less pain. It took about a month or so but I just noticed the other day that my metatarsal pain has all but subsided. For the money, I would recommend this as something to try.

title: I think it tastes good
text:
I recently found out that I need to go on a anti-inflammation diet, and most of the protein mixes out there have ingredients that cause my inflammation to act up in not so great ways. Despite the reviews that hurled down curses on this mix for its sweetness, I went ahead and ordered it, and I haven't been disappointed. In fact, I've re-ordered it many times. When I was first looking into the anti-inflammation diets, especially the Whole 30, I came across some people who approached it with a near religious fervor, ranting about their epic battles with their sugar dragons. My dudes...relax. You ain't battling dragons. You're putting down the Twix bar for once. Just because this tastes a little sweet from the monkfruit doesn't mean you've committed a mortal sin.

I haven't noticed any skin or hair benefits from the collagen like many people report, but that might be because I'm freakin' old. My skin and hair have pretty much thrown in the towel.

Bottom line: if you're looking for a protein mix that won't make your dairy, gluten, chemical sensitivities flare up, order this. Drink up.

title: Better than Cisco consumer and small business VoIP devices.
text: I dare say it may be even better than Cisco's enterprise devices but since I never tested Cisco enterprise devices I can't rightly make that statement. Mediatrix the 4102 and the 4102s are extremely stable and reliable. I never had an issue with calls not going out quickly and properly due to the device itself having issues. In fact Mediatrix 4102 and the 4102s holds well under some pretty nasty conditions. Now to clarify the word "conditions" I mean packet loss, jitter, and some VoIP server issues. Both the 4102 and 4102s use a Texas Instruments chip as the main processor for VoIP. However, the 4102s has a quicker chip and more memory to deal with the extra security features it contains but also adds a wealth of other features not related to security. I'm impressed with the Mediatrix devices and highly recommend them over Cisco offerings.

title: Thoughts from an exercise-induced asthma patient
text: A bit of history:  in the late 80's, I was diagnosed with exercise-induced asthma.  I was put on two prescription inhalers by my pulmonologist.  I was able to keep going with my exercise, but the side-effects of the drug gave me upper-respiratory infections several times a year which pretty much knocked me out until I recovered. Many years later, I was being treated by a doctor who specializes in metabolic medicine, and he mentioned that several of his patients were on Oralmat and were doing so well they were no longer using their inhalers.  I was skeptical, so I weaned myself off slowly to ensure my symptoms didn't return, and the rest, as they say, is history.  I have experienced NO side-effects at all during all the years I've been using this product.  For several years it disappeared from the U.S. and I had to track it down in Australia from the gentleman who produces it.  He is elderly, and I'm concerned what will happen to the product after he passes.  Fortunately, it's now being sold again in the States.  It's made from the rye plant, so unless you're allergic to grain, it's virtually harmless.  Unlike the "suggested use" instructions, I treat it like a homeopathic remedy and place the 3 drops under my tongue and wiggle it vigorously to absorb it.  All the blood vessels there help.  Then I don't eat or drink 30 minutes before or after I ingest it to give it plenty of undisturbed space.

title: High Quality and Effective Digestive Enzymes, Though Frankly Too Costly For Me
text:
These have been very effective digestive enzymes for me thus far.

Positive:
-Vegan (therefore Vegetarian, of course)
-Fairly High Potency
-No junk fillers and binders and garbage additives that impede health
-Non-proprietary formulation, meaning you know what dosage of each enzyme it contains,
-They really seem to be effective and work for me, which is saying something as, despite eating well most of my adult life, I have Crohn's and other autoimmune issues due to too many rounds of antibiotics and other medical bungling as a child, so I have a lot to contend with and sometimes I really need the extra help of supplemental enzymes to digest food and have bowel movements

Negatives:
-Very expensive, even compared to other high end enzymes (both proprietary and non-proprietary; by the likes of Enzymedica and a few others I have used over the years)... The cost of this has had me skimping on digestive enzymes more than I should, which really doesn't help me

Although these are working well with me, I am probably going to test out a different company (Allegany Nutrition) when I go to reorder digestive enzymes (very soon), as I have found the Allegany Nutrition HP270V product contains higher doses of many of the enzymes (though a slightly different profile) and it also a lot cheaper too, it is less than half the cost of Baseline's per capsule/ dose, when ordering the larger bottle (although the upfront cost is a good bit more). The cost of Baseline's product is about 70 cents a cap (shipping factored in, about 60 cents without shipping), while the ones from Allegany Nutrition are about 30 cents a cap, when purchasing the 270 count bottle for $79.95 on amazon. Both are vegan and do not contain fillers and useless garbage, both are high potency, both are not proprietary formulas. If the other product doesn't work out for me, I am still uncertain what I will use next,as the cost of this one is prohibitively high for me, unfortunately, for the amount I need to take.

title: security hole
text:
It works okay if you have 1 user for the scale or if you dont mind the other people you share the scale with knowing your weight. You can add multiple users to the scale, and set the privacy settings so that only you can see your weight, but other users can change who that weigh in belongs to. for instance, 2 people connected. User A and User B. user A weights in, then User B. User A cannot see Users B's weight and vice versa. But, now User A logs in to the website. User A can change User B's weigh in so that it belongs to User A. Then user A logs out and logs back in. User A can now see user B's Weight. User B can do the same to User A.
It is then possible to change it back so that you never knew the other users viewed it.

Otherwise it is a good scale with an easy setup and seems fairly accurate. Beware, the directions say to store it flat otherwise it takes a few uses to get it accurate again. This is a major pain to me as i need to store it vertically to save space. They really really need to fix the security hole i've mentioned. then it would get 4 stars, not 2.

title: Good Product for the cost
text:
I have been using a competitors electrolyte powder for some time now and was looking for something a bit less expensive. The concern one has when you are looking for something less expensive are you giving up quality for less cost. I had read the reviews on Amazon and found there was a 70% rating with five stars and saw many good compliments and comments about the product so I thought what do I have to lose.

First of all I was very happy with the price and the quantity it purchased! The prior product I was using would have cost me almost double for the same number of servings.

Second, I thought I am going to compare my current electrolyte powder grape to Junp and see how it compares. Junp grape has a great flavor but it is a bit weak in the flavor. (The company informed me they had customers who had requested to make the flavor weaker so each to his own.) I would love to have more grape like the competitor but it was still pleasant to drink. I was very impressed with how it dissolved in the water and how I had very little residual amount of the powder at the bottom of my glass.

Third, I was tickled pink when I opened the jar and found the long handled scoop. The scoop makes it so much easier to carefully scoop out my needed powder and then carefully put it back with absolutely no mess. Win!!

Finally I was impressed with how the company is truly interested to hear candid comments from its customers. This is the way to make a product your customer likes and keeps them coming back.

Thanks to Junp for making a great product.

title: Taste takes me back to my childhood
text: I look forward to drinking my electrolyte twice a day as it takes me back to my childhood.  Even though the drink has lots of good vitamins you really don't taste them but instead you taste the delightful lemonade flavor. The razor comes with its travel pouch/bag; which makes it very convenient to take everywhere and it does not take a lot of space. I like the comfortable grip and feel when I hold it.

Overall, I would use this razor only in times when I do not have better options. I would use it as a last resource and maybe only to remove excess hairs but not if I want my legs and armpits to look and feel smooth.

title: (2) Just Out of the Box Comments
text:
Wikipedia.org says "Shiatsu techniques include massages with fingers, thumbs, feet and palms; assisted stretching; and joint manipulation and mobilization." I don't think this means that these cushions are meant to be soft and comforting. And this device meets the definition, as it should. So expect some discomfort!

Secondly, there a many reviews with comments or questions about the massage (not) reaching the neck and/or the lower back. I don't think you should expect the device, out of the box, to fit your body dimensions without some experimentation with extra cushion size and placement experimentation. I am about 6 feet tall yet the neck setting massaged above my ears !!??. And the lower setting did not reach my lower back where I wanted/needed it most. Ten minutes of messing around with a couple different sized pillows on the lower cushion and I found a combination that raised me up to massage the lower back as well as the pressure point on my shoulder.

Getting the body elevation adjusted properly also eliminated a big mechanical jolt that was very disconcerting. The jolt had been happening previously when the cushion's massage elements transitioned from the shoulder area to the back area.

This "body altitude" change turned my initial reaction from a 1-star to a 5-star. However, I am always leery of a product that gets at, or above,10% of its ratings with only 1-star. I am keeping my fingers crossed that these two realizations cover a good portion of the 1-star complaints.

In seriousness, these bottles were easy to fill and put together. There is no mess and no leakage. They work like a charm and will prolong the life of our essential oils, which are NOT cheap. I imagine we will order again so that everyone in the house has multiple single and combination oil blends.

title: Ease of use is worth it, even if body fat % isn't that accurate
text:
The automatic logging of daily weight on the Fitbit site is a real convenience. Yes, I know you can remember or write down the number and enter is manually, but what gets put off often doesn't get done, so I can't complain about the convenience. The weight also seems to be pretty accurate if you keep the scale in the same place on a hard surface and step on it the same way each time. Different foot placement or leaning a bit can give inconsistent weight, but that's true for an extent on any digital scale so you just do it the same way each time and i doesn't vary more than one would expect from normal daily weight fluctuations.

The body fat % is not an exact science on these monitors regardless of brand. It only measures the path up and down your legs and through your hips and not your entire body. Legs tends to have more lean mass (bones, connective tissue, etc...) so the formulas have to make some assumptions based on height and weight to extrapolate that measurement. The sales are also very prone to hydration and how well your feet conduct electrically, but that's the nature of the beast. Most people have different body fat percentages on different parts of their bodies, so it's all just an average estimate anyway. Compared to skin fold calipers, the scale reads mine as a few percent higher than the calipers. As with most things, the truth is somewhere in the middle and based on comparisons to photos of people at different body fat percentages, the calipers seem more accurate, so the scale is measuring mine a couple percent too high. Your mileage may vary.

What's been frustrating lately is that because I've been gaining muscle mostly in my upper body, the scale is correctly measuring as weight gain, but since it's using the same amount of lean mass in my legs which hasn't changed much at all, it seems to be calculating the extra weight as fat so my body fat % number is increasing, but I know visually and from clothes being looser that I'm getting leaner. I tried setting the scale to the "lean" setting, but that reading is way off the other way being far too low.

I wish there was some way to enter in your own personal adjustment somewhere in between lean and regular or at least have Fitbit do the adjustment after the fact based on your profile, but there isn't. If there was, I'd give it five stars. I'm giving it four because its a great product within the limitation of what it does. Digital scales do need flat hard surfaces and standing the same way and electrical body fat measurements are estimates based on lots of varying factors. It doers what it does well. WIFI uploads are fast and trouble free and the batteries last at least six months, so it's pretty much a set and forget device which is what I wanted.

title: Some flavors
text:
Stick with the chocolate Lava. Have not tried all of the flavors, but the ginger snap alone is worth the loss of at LEAST 2 stars, and I am being magnanimous here. The Sunflower Butter is oily as is the chocolate lava, though unlike the chocolate lava, it is almost flavorless, and the cinnamon raisin roll is OK.

Conversely, the recipe for the Ginger Snap should be burned, it's ashes mixed into cement, and the resulting block shot into space...

I sincerely hope the person who formulated that flavor reads this, because I have quite a bit to tell them. First off, what, exactly, WERE YOU THINKING? Calling this flavor hideous and unpalatable is an insult to all hideous and unpalatable foods everywhere. If this flavor were a sentient being, you would euthanize it to put it out of its misery. Were it served in prisons, it would be considered cruel and unusual punishment, and all inmates who (forcibly, no doubt) consumed it would be immediately released for time served. I am guessing that the ONLY reason this flavor is produced is that someone in the supply chain of this company lost a substantial bet...

It tastes like clove oil, and actually has a numbing effect on your mouth. I read the ingredient list expecting to find it there, and was shocked that not only clove oil, but both "pure, unadulterated malevolence" and "malicious intent to do bodily harm" were also suspiciously missing from the ingredient list. Cinnamon oil is present though, so perhaps it has some of the same properties.

All exaggeration aside, the Quest bars are far superior, and nutritionally equal if you are not vegan, though I will still buy the chocolate lava, even though they are a bit oily (you really could cut the fat content down a bit on those).

title: soylent, huel, or ka'chava?
text: I've been into this meal replacement thing for about three years now, started with soylent, and then tried huel. and finally kachava. i typically make a smoothie every morning with one of these meal replacements. it consists of the vanilla flavor on all different brands. with water and a tablespoon of powdered Hershey's chocolate. (the chocolate flavor of all these brands just kinda sucks IMO). and I've been doing this for about 3 years every morning. i will break down each brand briefly. Soylent: smooth and soft texture. has the most neutral and adaptable flavor. it is also the cheapest, but taste kinda synthetic, and not quite confident it's "healthy". but soylent takes a 4.5/5... soylent is about 1.90 a serving. Huel: kinda grainy texture, and has a plan and plant taste (not perceptively appealing, although, I can enjoy this taste much more in the long run compared to soylent and kachava), but i feel this is much healthier than soylent. (on par with kachava as far as health) 4/5. hule is about 2.30 cents a serving. ka'chava: sadly i got this hoping i could explore it more and incorporate it with the other two. the texture is very similar to huel, but it's been loaded with some sweetener that just overwhelms anything you do to make a tame drink. (i can't do this flavor every day compared to the other two.) but this is somewhat a bias on my part because I don't like sweet things very much. so if you like sweet smoothies, godspeed. also, kachava is the most expensive for the least amount of food. at about 3$ a serving. 3/5. 4/5 if you like sweets, and can afford them. i typically do a 2/1 ratio of soylent(2) heul(1). with chocolate and water in my smoothies. I have tried putting kachava into this portioning, but it almost obstructs the taste at any level. kachava has to be about 1/7th of the ratio for it to be neutral enough of a flavor without it disturbing the flavor with excessive sweetness. anyway hope this helps with your decision-making with these meal supplements. :)

title: Luxurious and not overbearing. . .
text:
These Herbal Essentuality Bath Bombs are lovely. Immediately upon receiving the box, the faint smell permeated the packaging. The box itself is very pretty and the six bombs are individually wrapped in simple brown paper with an attractive label on each one. The brown wrapping is over a plastic covering, keeping the bombs completely free of moisture or humidity.

I love taking baths and have a large tub in my bathroom. After my children went to bed, I ran the tub and dropped the "balancing" bomb in. It immediately began fizzing and a faint blue tinged the water. I normally don't like coloring, but this was very mild and not overbearing.

It took about ten minutes for the bomb to completely disintegrate, and it continued fizzing until it was gone. The smell was present, but not pungent, just as I like it. My skin felt moisturized and supple, but not slippery as sometimes occurs with oils, like coconut oil.

This was a great addition to my bath. It felt luxurious, but was mild and not offensive to my allergies. I'd highly recommend this as a gift for yourself or someone else who enjoys taking baths.

I received these bath bombs at a discount in exchange for my honest and unbiased review. I'm enjoying them and think these would be appreciated by anyone who enjoys baths.

title: Price to move so I trust it!
text: I have been in the hobby for 20+ yrs. After reading all the reviews I elected to purchase the product and edit the product to suit my needs, as I do ALL my products in this hobby! If you have boxed products for your tank that you’ve never had to alter in some way, give it time! You’ll certainly find different uses and ways to use the same products. I would recommend this product because the suction power is good as long as your water level is high enough for the tub to catch enough water to pump. I use this for emptying this nano tank of 12” high sitting on my nightstand, and a few 3.5g nano tanks in high places, and several others at different levels. I have a sump under my 200g and it fits under there well! I have to take off the extra tubs and tilt the device so the water can catch (suck) after the water gets too low. DO NOT SUBMERGE ENTIRE PRODUCT! But the product WORKS WELL! I purchased TWO! I have a lot of tanks. I do not know how long the batteries last, because I have not had to change the batteries after I changed my sump (3 tubs at the bottom of my tank with about a 10” clearing to get inside the tubs, at least 25g each) and all my nano tanks (4). It cleans well, but the sock it comes with is EXTREMELY small! It would be more helpful if it were longer. It is. Not like the filtration sock on my sump, and it gets dirty FAST! It’s safe to use with all sorts of fish because the bag can catch and release anything you accidentally catch (ie fry you didn’t notice were there), because the bag is easy to manually dislodge without accidentally coming off during use. I use a hose in the sock position (it is an interchangeable part that comes with the product) to do quick changes to expel waste really fast without a long drawn out water change, and a fast refill from a lower bucket to a higher sitting tank to slow the water flow back into the tank without a lot of pressure, or stress to the fry/fish. The water level never gets up to the battery, so hopefully this product will never fail me! The best part was the price! $8.89 was in my budget. When a product is priced to move, its a good product and the company knows people will buy more of them. Priced with the hobbyist in mind! Get 2!

title: I like the idea, but...
text: I've been using the Boie brush for about 10 days now. There were several things I really liked about this brush when I first got it: The dense bristles did a terrific job with gum massage as well as scouring between teeth and in tight places. It took a little time getting accustomed to the new feel rubbery "fingers" instead of fiber bristles. The bristle area is larger than my old brush, so the way it fit in my mouth felt different. I'm usually on autopilot when I am brushing my teeth, but with this, I had to concentrate on what I was doing to get a good cleaning. Still, even with that, I thought the brush did a good job of cleaning my teeth. It rinsed out nicely with no residue on the brush, and after 10 days' use, there is no bristle deformation. The reason I am giving it one star is that it has a design flaw that makes me uncomfortable to use it. The brush is in two pieces: a stiff plastic handle and a the head which is a sleeve with the soft rubber-like "bristles". The head slips onto the handle like a tight sleeve. The trouble is that the bristle head does not seal on to the handle and after a few days of use, moisture, saliva, and toothpaste gunk seeps into that area between the handle and the head, and makes the whole thing a funky mess. It looks like a good bacterial breeding place. Yes, it can be cleaned, but that is just another step in my daily dental hygiene ritual. Who needs that? Overall, this is a good idea, but IMO it is not ready for prime time.

text:
A friend of mine got a set of these, and I tried them out & I ordered a set that day. I'm a musician and recording engineer, and I struggle with chronic back and shoulder issues (probably related to all the music I play and computer work I do, plus driving a ton and sleeping in weird places on tour).

The Myssage balls have been a total godsend. It's such a simple idea, but they are so well-designed - they stay where you want them to, and the nubs really get deep into the tissue. I feel like I can do more with the balls and my own body weight than someone could do with their hands when giving a massage. When I get ambitious, sometimes I do the entire book of exercises in one session...I can get those normally tight muscles to feel rubbery and smooth. It's crazy. I also brought them (and the book) to show a physical therapist I was going to months back for an ulnar nerve issue, and he was impressed - I got the thumbs up to use them alongside my PT exercises, and he wrote down the website to explore further on his own.

As a musician, I've carried them on tour with me around the US and through Germany, Austria, and Switzerland. The portability is a huge factor! I often bring them with me to the studio or just throw them in my backpack when I'm out and about. Always good to have nearby. Just bought a second set as a backup.

Definitely get the book - the exercises are key. There are also videos on their website and YouTube.

title: A cool and unique wax, just know what you're getting into
text:
Its a neat wax. I applied after buffing my paint to a high shine. I found the wax fairly hard to work with. Not the worst ever but make sure you put it on thinnn and take it off in a reasonable amount of time. My truck seemed to be no problem, but I have experienced streaking on other cars. Make sure that paint surface is as cool as you can possibly get it, within reason. I'm not sure if that caused the streaks or not but its the only thing I can think of. The streaks don't come out easy so be careful as you might end up having to polish if it streaks on you.

Gloss was OK but not great. My truck is black with metallic flake. The truck looks shiny and nice, but it just doesn't have that same "pop" that other nice waxes have. The metal flake doesn't glisten like I was used to with other waxes.

Durability so far has been great. The truck beads water like crazy even 2 months later. I love seeing it run off the hood like mad when I drive in the rain. It certainly lives up to its reputation there.

I was hoping it would make for a great glass wax (rain x alternative if you will) and its pretty good. I've used A TON of products on my windshield to help sheet off rain. I would rate this as very good but it hasn't beaten my go to for the past several years which is turtle wax ice paste. We will see if this out lasts the TWI. I suspect it will, but thats not a huge benefit to me as the TWI lasts a very long time already. I have noticed that it takes a quite a bit more speed to get the water sheeting off the windshield vs the Ice, and it doesn't do as well with fine misty rain as the Ice either. If its pouring or you're driving at a pretty quick speed though you'll have no problem so use this product on your glass and you'll be happy.

I am also experimenting with it on my jet ski. Didn't seem to last even one whole trip on there (when it was working it was great though). I did a very quick job though, so it could easily be on me. I'll take a little more time next time before I make my final call on that.

title: Great for sore fingers
text:
I don't have arthritis or any other problem, so I can't speak to its effectiveness for that, but I have a bad habit of keeping tension with my index finger in a way that places severe strain on it. I was getting to the point where I was going to have to switch to mostly knitting, as I wrap the yarn around my wrist and finger for that without strain, until I found this device. I don't use it exactly the way they recommend, but the way I use it solves my problem, and I am able to keep my index finger straight. I place the yarn under the velcro bracelet, and under the main part of the ring against my finger (not the little ring on top like they suggest). The combination of these provides perfect tension and I'm able to crochet faster and without pain.

You do need to make sure that your yarn doesn't get caught by the velcro, and if you use the ring the way I do, it occasionally slips out, but these are very minor problems. You also have to keep the ring from small children for both safety reasons and because they find it fascinating. My daughter thinks she's found a treasure if she gets ahold of it, and hides it from me with great amusement. She has also stretched it out some by opening the ring too much (i think it's silicone) and it isn't as tight as it was. As far as safety goes, I think the entire ring is too big for a baby to choke on, but I would worry about the attached little ring being the part that goes in first. I don't know if it would be enough to choke on, but it is a concern.

title: Not As Advertised in the Picture, but Actually Better!
text:
I'm a little conflicted on how to rate this item. I ordered it because the lancing device that came with my meter kit was defective and the manufacturer was taking way too long to get me a replacement. The device I received with this order was NOT the one pictured. The image showed the longer, pen-like black and gray device, just like the one that came with my kit. Instead, I received the more rectangular two toned blue device.

This actually turned out to be a very good thing, though I'm still a little annoyed at the misrepresentation. The black and gray device pictured doesn't work very well. The one that came with my meter kit was defective. The replacement that the manufacturer sent wasn't much better. Even at a setting of 5, it barely pierces my skin and sometimes takes multiple attempts. It also falls out of the meter case because the elastic band that's supposed to hold it is too loose.

The smaller, rectangular blue one that came in this order, however, works great. I started it at a 3 and got a good sample with no problem. I'm going to try it at a 2 next time, since the 3 actually bled more than I would like. The device also fits snugly into my meter case and doesn't fall out like the other kind. The lancets I received are a different brand than shown in the photo. I haven't used them yet, so no comment there, but I'm sure they'll work fine.

So overall I'm a happy customer, but the seller should more accurately represent the product they're selling.

title: As promised, really facilitates the process of making suppositories for naturopathic HPV treatment
text:
These suppository molds are exactly as described. I have started making green tea vaginal suppositories to combat HPV in a coconut oil base about a week ago. To make 12 suppositories, I use a couple tablespoons of coconut oil, melted and dissolve a teaspoon of matcha within, as well as some liquid green tea extract, some pure aloe gel (1 tsp) and two small drops of tea tree oil. After the trays have been filled with the pipettes, you can put the suppositories in the freezer and when you're ready to use them, run the tray under lukewarm water to dislodge the "suppository bullets" as my boyfriend and I call them. I use the smaller end of a chopstick to push each one through after removing the mold cap and it pops right out. I then use a suppository applicator which I also purchased on Amazon to place the "bullet" right up against my cervix (I place on foot on the toilet and the other on the ground to get it all the way up... TMI, I know). The shape of the suppository is compatible with the applicators and it inserts fairly easily. After I've inserted one, I put the mold back in the fridge. The pipettes are nice because they help in getting the right amount into the molds without making a mess though they're a bit tricky to wash and remove the oil from (you'll need to rinse them out in a bowl of warm, soapy water several times, filling them up and emptying them out repeatedly).

Some advice: The formula I use feels good (cooling, soothing) and doesn't seem to cause me any discomfort. Wear a pad or a liner with it as it will leak as it dissolves. Also remember that anything oil based will be incompatible with latex condoms for at least a day. I believe you can also douche the next day to remove the oily residue (using vinegar and water, or simply water, nothing unnatural I would think).

text:
I purchased this so I could easily track my progress while I lose weight and build some muscle. I was previously using a soft sewing measuring tape, which worked but was a bit of a hassle when trying to measure different areas (ex: shoulders). All I have to do now is pull out some of the tape, fit the end piece into the hole, put the tape around whatever part of my body I want to check, and press the button so the tape constricts down around it and tells me the measurement. It's easy to do your shoulders, bust, bicep, or anything else you may have trouble measuring when you're having to hold the two pieces together with a manual measuring tape. I haven't had any issues with quality and I've used it several times, but I will update if I do have a problem. If the end piece happens to pop off, I can just glue it back on.
Also, to anyone complaining that the tape is not accurate because it doesn't start at 0... Please turn your brain back on. It is accurate, and it's pretty easy to figure out why it's made that way.
